Its limits: little good-quality research exists, and methods make comparing autistic and non-autistic people difficult, so it does not describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska närstående kommer i kontakt med polis eller domstol kan det hjälpa att förbereda ett kort eller en lapp som förklarar hur personen kommunicerar, sensoriska behov och vem man ska ringa. Be om anpassningar och om en trygg stödperson vid förhör. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 47 studier publicerade sedan 2013 om autistiska personer i rättsväsendet; den tyder på att autistiska personer kan ha särskilda sårbarheter och motiv som förtjänar förståelse. Begränsningar: det finns lite forskning av god kvalitet, och metoderna gör jämförelser mellan autistiska och icke-autistiska personer svåra, så den beskriver inte varje individ.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder and Gender Dysphoria/Incongruence. A systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Kallitsounaki A, Williams DM
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The suggested overlap between autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and gender dysphoria/incongruence (GD/GI) has been much disputed. This review showed a relationship between ASD traits and GD feelings in the general population and a high prevalence of GD/GI in ASD. Our meta-analyses revealed that the pooled estimate of the prevalence of ASD diagnoses in GD/GI people was 11% (p < .001) and the overall effect size of the difference in ASD traits between GD/GI and control people was significant (g = 0.67, p < .001). Heterogeneity was high in both meta-analyses. We demonstrated that the chances that there is not a link between ASD and GD/GI are negligible, yet the size of it needs further investigation.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista, es útil saber que las preguntas sobre la identidad de género aparecen con más frecuencia de lo esperado. Puedes escuchar con calma, sin presionar ni descartar lo que comparta, y buscar profesionales que conozcan tanto el autismo como la diversidad de género. Este metaanálisis reunió estudios previos: en personas con disforia o incongruencia de género, alrededor del 11 % tenía diagnóstico de autismo, y también mostraban más rasgos autistas que los grupos de comparación. Sus límites: los estudios eran muy diferentes entre sí, por lo que el tamaño real de esta relación sigue sin estar claro y no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it helps to know that questions about gender identity come up more often than many expect. You can listen calmly, without pushing or dismissing what they share, and look for professionals who understand both autism and gender diversity. This meta-analysis pooled earlier studies: among people with gender dysphoria or incongruence, about 11% had an autism diagnosis, and they also showed more autistic traits than comparison groups. Its limits: the included studies varied widely, so the true size of this link remains unclear, and it does not describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det vara bra att veta att frågor om könsidentitet förekommer oftare än många tror. Du kan lyssna lugnt, utan att pressa eller avfärda det personen berättar, och söka professionella som förstår både autism och könsmångfald. Den här metaanalysen sammanställde tidigare studier: bland personer med könsdysfori eller könsinkongruens hade omkring 11 % en autismdiagnos, och de visade också fler autistiska drag än jämförelsegrupper. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, så hur stort sambandet verkligen är är fortfarande oklart, och resultatet beskriver inte varje enskild person.

title: Mental health in autistic adults: A rapid review of prevalence of psychiatric disorders and umbrella review of the effectiveness of interventions within a neurodiversity informed perspective.
authors: Curnow E, Rutherford M, Maciver D, Johnston L, Prior S, Boilson M, Shah P, Jenkins N, Meff T
abstract: Background Autistic adults have high risk of mental ill-health and some available interventions have been associated with increased psychiatric diagnoses. Understanding prevalence of psychiatric diagnoses is important to inform the development of individualised treatment and support for autistic adults which have been identified as a research priority by the autistic community. Interventions require to be evaluated both in terms of effectiveness and regarding their acceptability to the autistic community. Objective This rapid review identified the prevalence of psychiatric disorders in autistic adults, then systematic reviews of interventions aimed at supporting autistic adults were examined. A rapid review of prevalence studies was completed concurrently with an umbrella review of interventions. Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) guidelines were followed, including protocol registration (PROSPERO#CRD42021283570). Data sources MEDLINE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. Study eligibility criteria English language; published 2011-2022; primary studies describing prevalence of psychiatric conditions in autistic adults; or systematic reviews evaluating interventions for autistic adults. Appraisal and synthesis Bias was assessed using the Prevalence Critical Appraisal Instrument and AMSTAR2. Prevalence was grouped according to psychiatric diagnosis. Interventions were grouped into pharmacological, employment, psychological or mixed therapies. Strength of evidence for interventions was assessed using GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation). Autistic researchers within the team supported interpretation. Results Twenty prevalence studies were identified. Many included small sample sizes or failed to compare their sample group with the general population reducing validity. Prevalence of psychiatric diagnoses was variable with prevalence of any psychiatric diagnosis ranging from 15.4% to 79%. Heterogeneity was associated with age, diagnosis method, sampling methods, and country. Thirty-two systematic reviews of interventions were identified. Four reviews were high quality, four were moderate, five were low and nineteen critically low, indicating bias. Following synthesis, no intervention was rated as 'evidence based.' Acceptability of interventions to autistic adults and priorities of autistic adults were often not considered. Conclusions There is some understanding of the scope of mental ill-health in autism, but interventions are not tailored to the needs of autistic adults, not evidence based, and may focus on promoting neurotypical behaviours rather than the priorities of autistic people.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un adulto autista, toma en serio su salud mental: es frecuente que aparezcan dificultades como ansiedad o depresión. Al buscar apoyo, pregunta si la intervención está adaptada a personas autistas y si respeta sus prioridades, no si busca que parezca neurotípico. Su opinión sobre lo que le ayuda importa tanto como la del profesional. Esta revisión rápida y paraguas analizó 20 estudios de prevalencia y 32 revisiones sistemáticas de intervenciones, con investigadores autistas en el equipo. Sus límites: muchos estudios eran pequeños o de baja calidad, las cifras variaron mucho (15–79 %) y ninguna intervención alcanzó el nivel de 'basada en evidencia'.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, take their mental health seriously: difficulties such as anxiety or depression are common. When looking for support, ask whether an approach is adapted for autistic people and respects their own priorities, rather than aiming to make them appear neurotypical. Their view of what helps matters as much as the professional's. This rapid and umbrella review examined 20 prevalence studies and 32 systematic reviews of interventions, with autistic researchers on the team. Its limits: many studies were small or low quality, rates varied widely (15–79%), and no intervention reached the level of 'evidence based'.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, ta hens psykiska hälsa på allvar: svårigheter som ångest eller depression är vanliga. När ni söker stöd, fråga om insatsen är anpassad för autistiska personer och utgår från hens egna prioriteringar, inte från att hen ska verka neurotypisk. Hens bild av vad som hjälper väger lika tungt som professionellas. Denna snabb- och paraplyöversikt granskade 20 förekomststudier och 32 systematiska översikter av insatser, med autistiska forskare i teamet. Begränsningar: många studier var små eller av låg kvalitet, siffrorna varierade kraftigt (15–79 %) och ingen insats nådde nivån 'evidensbaserad'.

title: The effect of physical exercise on disordered social communication in individuals with autism Spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authors: Jia S, Guo C, Li S, Zhou X, Wang X, Wang Q
abstract: Objective The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to systematically investigate the intervention effect of physical exercise on disordered social communication in patients with autism spectrum disorders. Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis used the PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase electronic databases to conduct a systematic search of literature describing randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the effect of physical exercise on disordered social communication in autistic patients from the first year of inclusion to 21 January 2023. Results A total of 14 RCTs including 460 autistic patients were analyzed. A meta-analysis showed that physical exercise had a positive effect on social communication disorder (SMD = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.15, 0.74, p P P P P Conclusion Physical exercise can improve disordered social communication in patients with autism spectrum disorders. Specifically, early intervention, multi-component exercise, a moderate period, moderate and high frequency, long duration, and multi-participant programs were most effective. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ RecordID= CRD42023422482.

sheet.es: Moverse juntos puede ser una buena puerta a la conexión. Si a tu hijo o hija le gusta, prueba actividades físicas variadas y regulares, quizá en pequeño grupo, como juegos de pelota, natación o circuitos, eligiendo lo que disfrute y respetando su ritmo sensorial. El objetivo no es cambiar quién es, sino ofrecer espacios agradables para compartir. Este metaanálisis reunió 14 ensayos controlados aleatorizados con 460 personas autistas y encontró una mejora moderada en la comunicación social con el ejercicio. Los estudios eran pequeños y diferentes entre sí, medían la comunicación desde una mirada no autista y los resultados no se aplican a todas las personas.
sheet.en: Moving together can be a gentle doorway to connection. If your child enjoys it, try varied, regular physical activities, perhaps in a small group, such as ball games, swimming or obstacle courses, choosing what they like and respecting their sensory needs. The aim is not to change who they are, but to offer enjoyable shared spaces. This meta-analysis pooled 14 randomized controlled trials with 460 autistic participants and found a moderate improvement in social communication with exercise. The studies were small and varied, measured communication from a largely non-autistic perspective, and the results will not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Att röra sig tillsammans kan bli en mjuk väg till kontakt. Om ditt barn tycker om det, prova varierad och regelbunden fysisk aktivitet, gärna i liten grupp, som bollekar, simning eller hinderbanor. Välj det barnet gillar och respektera sensoriska behov. Målet är inte att förändra vem barnet är, utan att erbjuda roliga gemensamma stunder. Denna metaanalys sammanställde 14 randomiserade kontrollerade studier med 460 autistiska deltagare och fann en måttlig förbättring av social kommunikation vid träning. Studierna var små och olika, mätte kommunikation främst ur ett icke-autistiskt perspektiv, och resultaten passar inte alla.

title: Access to employment: A comparison of autistic, neurodivergent and neurotypical adults' experiences of hiring processes in the United Kingdom.
authors: Davies J, Heasman B, Livesey A, Walker A, Pellicano E, Remington A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are less likely to have a job than non-autistic people. One reason for this may be that hiring processes (e.g. job applications, interviews) can be challenging for autistic people. To better understand the experiences of hiring processes in the United Kingdom, we asked 225 autistic, 64 neurodivergent (but not autistic) and 64 adults with no reported area of neurodivergence questions about their experiences using an online survey. We found a range of similarities and differences in responses. For example, participants in all three groups were frustrated with the focus on social skills in recruitment and said they wanted more practical methods (e.g. work trials) that help them show their skills and abilities. Autistic and otherwise neurodivergent participants discussed the importance of the environment (e.g. the interview/assessment room) in improving experiences. Participants also discussed how employers can impact whether somebody decides to disclose their diagnosis or needs - or not. Autistic people experienced some barriers to successful recruitment that non-autistic people did not. For example, autistic people felt they had to hide their autistic traits to gain employment and many autistic people were worried about being discriminated against if they disclosed that they were autistic during the hiring process. To make experiences better, our participants said that employers should offer candidates different recruitment methods and give them more information about the hiring process. They also said employers should improve their understanding of autism and other hidden disabilities so they know the challenges that people might face during recruitment.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una persona autista que busca empleo, puede ayudar pedir al empleador información detallada sobre el proceso, preguntar por alternativas a la entrevista (como una prueba práctica de trabajo) y por ajustes del entorno (luz, ruido, sala). Decidir si comunicar el diagnóstico es una elección personal; hablarlo juntos con calma puede reducir la preocupación. Evidencia: encuesta en línea en Reino Unido con 225 adultos autistas, 64 neurodivergentes no autistas y 64 neurotípicos, que compartieron sus experiencias. Límites: se basa en respuestas autoinformadas de voluntarios de un solo país, así que no refleja a todas las personas ni prueba qué método funciona mejor.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person looking for work, it may help to ask employers for detailed information about the hiring process, whether there are alternatives to interviews (such as a practical work trial), and adjustments to the setting (lighting, noise, room). Deciding whether to disclose is a personal choice; talking it through calmly together can ease worry. Evidence: an online survey in the United Kingdom of 225 autistic adults, 64 non-autistic neurodivergent adults and 64 neurotypical adults sharing their experiences. Limits: it relies on self-reported answers from volunteers in one country, so it does not reflect everyone or prove which method works best.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som söker jobb kan det hjälpa att be arbetsgivaren om tydlig information om rekryteringen, fråga om alternativ till intervju (till exempel en praktisk arbetsprövning) och om anpassningar av miljön (ljus, ljud, rum). Att berätta om sin diagnos eller inte är ett personligt val; att prata igenom det lugnt tillsammans kan minska oro. Evidens: en webbenkät i Storbritannien där 225 autistiska vuxna, 64 neurodivergenta men inte autistiska vuxna och 64 neurotypiska vuxna delade sina erfarenheter. Begränsningar: svaren är självrapporterade från frivilliga i ett land, så de speglar inte alla och visar inte vilken metod som fungerar bäst.

title: Psychological strengths and well-being: Strengths use predicts quality of life, well-being and mental health in autism.
authors: Taylor EC, Livingston LA, Clutterbuck RA, Callan MJ, Shah P
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract It is often suggested that supporting autistic people to identify and use their strengths will lead to positive outcomes. However, little research has explored if this is true. To date, no research has explored whether autistic people already have knowledge of and use their strengths, nor whether increased strengths knowledge and use is linked to good outcomes, such as a better quality of life, well-being and improved mental health. Comparing large samples of autistic and non-autistic people, this study tested these unanswered questions. We found that autistic and non-autistic people reported similar strengths, but autistic people reported less knowledge and use of their strengths compared to non-autistic people. Importantly however, autistic people who reported using their strengths often had better quality of life, well-being and mental health than autistic people who reported using their strengths less frequently. We, therefore, propose that supporting autistic people to use their strengths more often may be a valuable way to boost well-being in this population.

sheet.es: Mañana puedes ayudar a la persona autista a notar qué se le da bien y buscar ocasiones concretas para usarlo en su día: su memoria, su honestidad, su curiosidad o su atención al detalle. Nombrar esa fortaleza en voz alta y dejarle espacio para practicarla puede sumar bienestar. Este estudio comparó grandes grupos de personas autistas y no autistas mediante cuestionarios: tenían fortalezas parecidas, pero las personas autistas las conocían y usaban menos, y quienes las usaban más a menudo referían mejor calidad de vida y salud mental. Limitación: muestra asociación, no causa; no prueba que aumentar su uso mejore el bienestar de cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, you could help the autistic person notice what they are good at and look for concrete moments to use it in their day: their memory, honesty, curiosity or eye for detail. Naming that strength out loud and making room to practise it may support well-being. This study compared large groups of autistic and non-autistic people using questionnaires: strengths were similar, but autistic people knew and used theirs less, and those who used them more often reported better quality of life, well-being and mental health. Limitation: it shows a link, not cause and effect; it does not prove that using strengths more will improve well-being for every person.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du hjälpa den autistiska personen att lägga märke till vad hen är bra på och hitta konkreta tillfällen att använda det under dagen: minnet, ärligheten, nyfikenheten eller blicken för detaljer. Att sätta ord på styrkan och ge utrymme att använda den kan stärka välbefinnandet. Studien jämförde stora grupper autistiska och icke-autistiska personer med enkäter: styrkorna var likartade, men autistiska personer kände till och använde sina mindre, och de som använde dem ofta rapporterade bättre livskvalitet, välbefinnande och psykisk hälsa. Begränsning: studien visar samband, inte orsak, och bevisar inte att mer styrkeanvändning hjälper varje person.

title: The experiences of autistic doctors: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Shaw SCK, Fossi A, Carravallah LA, Rabenstein K, Ross W, Doherty M
abstract: Introduction Medicine may select for autistic characteristics. As awareness and diagnosis of autism are growing, more medical students and doctors may be discovering they are autistic. No studies have explored the experiences of autistic doctors. This study aimed to fill that gap. Methods This is a cross-sectional study. A participatory approach was used to identify the need for the project and to modify a pre-existing survey for use exploring the experiences of autistic doctors. Results We received 225 responses. 64% had a formal diagnosis of autism. The mean age of receiving a formal diagnosis was 36 (range 3-61). Most were currently working as doctors (82%). The most common specialties were general practice / family medicine (31%), psychiatry (18%), and anesthesia (11%). Almost half of those working had completed specialty training (46%) and 40% were current trainees. 29% had not disclosed being autistic to anyone at work. 46% had requested adjustments in the workplace but of these, only half had them implemented.Three quarters had considered suicide (77%), one quarter had attempted suicide (24%) and half had engaged in self-harm (49%). 80% reported having worked with another doctor they suspected was autistic, but only 22% reported having worked with another doctor they knew was autistic. Having never worked with a potentially autistic colleague was associated with having considered suicide.Most preferred to be called "autistic doctors" (64%). Most considered autism to be a difference (83%). Considering autism to be a disorder was associated with preference for the term "doctors with autism," and with having attempted suicide. Conclusion Autistic doctors reported many challenges in the workplace. This may have contributed to a culture of nondisclosure. Mental health was poor with high rates of suicidal ideation, self-harm, and prior suicide attempts. Despite inhospitable environments, most were persevering and working successfully. Viewing autism as a disorder was associated with prior suicide attempts and a preference for person-first language. A neurodiversity-affirmative approach to autism may lead to a more positive self-identity and improved mental health. Furthermore, providing adequate supports and improving awareness of autistic medical professionals may promote inclusion in the medical workforce.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que estudia o trabaja en un campo exigente, sabe que es posible: muchos médicos autistas trabajan con éxito. Ayuda hablar del autismo como una diferencia, preguntar qué adaptaciones necesita y conocer a otras personas autistas en su profesión. Estate atento a su bienestar emocional y pregunta con calma cómo se siente; si aparecen ideas de autolesión o suicidio, busca apoyo profesional. Evidencia: encuesta transversal, diseñada con participación autista, respondida por 225 médicos autistas. Límites: es una muestra autoseleccionada en un solo momento; muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person studying or working in a demanding field, know it is possible: many autistic doctors work successfully. It helps to talk about autism as a difference, ask which workplace adjustments they need, and connect them with other autistic people in their profession. Keep an eye on emotional wellbeing and ask calmly how they are doing; if thoughts of self-harm or suicide come up, seek professional support. Evidence: a cross-sectional survey, shaped with autistic input, answered by 225 autistic doctors. Limits: a self-selected sample at one point in time; it shows associations, not causes, and does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som studerar eller arbetar inom ett krävande yrke: det går, många autistiska läkare arbetar framgångsrikt. Det hjälper att prata om autism som en olikhet, fråga vilka anpassningar personen behöver och skapa kontakt med andra autistiska i samma yrke. Var uppmärksam på det psykiska måendet och fråga lugnt hur personen har det; om tankar på självskada eller självmord dyker upp, sök professionellt stöd. Evidens: en tvärsnittsenkät, utformad med autistisk medverkan, besvarad av 225 autistiska läkare. Begränsningar: ett självvalt urval vid ett tillfälle; den visar samband, inte orsaker, och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Self-Harm Events and Suicide Deaths Among Autistic Individuals in Ontario, Canada.
authors: Lai MC, Saunders NR, Huang A, Artani A, Wilton AS, Zaheer J, Ameis SH, Brown HK, Lunsky Y
abstract: Importance Reasons for elevated suicide risks among autistic people are unclear, with insufficient population-based research on sex-specific patterns to inform tailored prevention and intervention. Objectives To examine sex-stratified rates of self-harm events and suicide death among autistic individuals compared with nonautistic individuals, as well as the associated sociodemographic and clinical risk factors. Design, setting, and participants This population-based matched-cohort study using linked health administrative databases in Ontario, Canada included all individuals with physician-recorded autism diagnoses from April 1, 1988, to March 31, 2018, each matched on age and sex to 4 nonautistic individuals from the general population. Self-harm events resulting in emergency health care from April 1, 2005, to December 31, 2020, were examined for one cohort, and death by suicide and other causes from April 1, 1993, to December 31, 2018, were examined for another cohort. Statistical analyses were conducted between October 2021 and June 2023. Exposure Physician-recorded autism diagnoses from 1988 to 2018 from health administrative databases. Main outcomes and measures Autistic and nonautistic individuals who were sex stratified a priori were compared using Andersen-Gill recurrent event models on self-harm events, and cause-specific competing risk models on death by suicide or other causes. Neighborhood-level income and rurality indices, and individual-level broad diagnostic categories of intellectual disabilities, mood and anxiety disorders, schizophrenia spectrum disorders, substance use disorders, and personality disorders were covariates. Results For self-harm events (cohort, 379 630 individuals; median age at maximum follow-up, 20 years [IQR, 15-28 years]; median age of first autism diagnosis claim for autistic individuals, 9 years [IQR, 4-15 years]; 19 800 autistic females, 56 126 autistic males 79 200 nonautistic females, and 224 504 nonautistic males), among both sexes, autism diagnoses had independent associations with self-harm events (females: relative rate, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.61-2.08; males: relative rate, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.28-1.69) after accounting for income, rurality, intellectual disabilities, and psychiatric diagnoses. For suicide death (cohort, 334 690 individuals; median age at maximum follow-up, 19 years [IQR, 14-27 years]; median age of first autism diagnosis claim for autistic individuals, 10 years [IQR, 5-16 years]; 17 982 autistic females, 48 956 autistic males, 71 928 nonautistic females, 195 824 nonautistic males), there was a significantly higher crude hazard ratio among autistic females (1.98; 95% CI, 1.11-3.56) and a nonsignificantly higher crude hazard ratio among autistic males (1.34; 95% CI, 0.99-1.82); the increased risks were associated with psychiatric diagnoses. Conclusions and relevance This cohort study suggests that autistic individuals experienced increased risks of self-harm events and suicide death. Psychiatric diagnoses were significantly associated with the increased risks among both sexes, especially for suicide death, and in partially sex-unique ways. Autism-tailored and autism-informed clinical and social support to reduce suicide risks should consider multifactorial mechanisms, with a particular focus on the prevention and timely treatment of psychiatric illnesses.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, presta atención a su salud mental de forma tranquila y continua: cambios de ánimo, ansiedad o retraimiento merecen hablarse y, si es necesario, consultar pronto con profesionales que conozcan el autismo. Preguntar directamente por pensamientos de hacerse daño no aumenta el riesgo y puede abrir la puerta a pedir ayuda. Ante un peligro inmediato, llama a emergencias. Evidencia: estudio poblacional en Ontario, Canadá, con registros sanitarios de unas 380 000 personas, autistas y no autistas; las personas autistas, sobre todo las mujeres, tuvieron más autolesiones atendidas en urgencias y más muertes por suicidio, en parte ligadas a diagnósticos psiquiátricos. Límites: solo incluye diagnósticos registrados y eventos que llegaron a urgencias; no explica causas ni predice el riesgo de cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, keep a calm, ongoing eye on their mental health: changes in mood, anxiety or withdrawal are worth talking about and, when needed, raising early with professionals who understand autism. Asking directly about thoughts of self-harm does not increase risk and can open the door to getting help. In immediate danger, call emergency services. Evidence: a population study in Ontario, Canada, using health records of about 380,000 autistic and non-autistic people; autistic people, especially females, had more self-harm events needing emergency care and more suicide deaths, partly linked to psychiatric diagnoses. Limits: it only captures recorded diagnoses and events reaching emergency care, and cannot explain causes or predict any individual's risk.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person, håll ett lugnt och kontinuerligt öga på den psykiska hälsan: förändrat mående, ångest eller tillbakadragande är värt att prata om och vid behov ta upp tidigt med vårdpersonal som förstår autism. Att fråga rakt ut om tankar på att skada sig ökar inte risken och kan öppna för att söka hjälp. Vid akut fara, ring 112. Evidens: en befolkningsstudie i Ontario, Kanada, med hälsoregister för cirka 380 000 autistiska och icke-autistiska personer; autistiska personer, särskilt kvinnor, hade fler självskador som krävde akutvård och fler dödsfall i suicid, delvis kopplat till psykiatriska diagnoser. Begränsningar: studien fångar bara registrerade diagnoser och händelser som nådde akutvården, och kan inte förklara orsaker eller förutsäga enskildas risk.

title: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids and/or vitamin D in autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Jiang Y, Dang W, Nie H, Kong X, Jiang Z, Guo J
abstract: This systematic review aims to offer an updated understanding of the relationship between omega-3 supplementation and/or vitamin D and autism spectrum disorders (ASD). The databases PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, EMBASE, CINAHL, Vip, CNKI, Wanfang, China Biomedical Database databases were searched using keywords, and relevant literature was hand-searched. Papers ( n = 1,151) were systematically screened and deemed eligible since 2002. Twenty clinical controlled studies were included in the final review. The findings were analyzed for intervention effects focusing on the core symptoms of ASD, included social functioning, behavioral functioning, speech function and biomarkers changes. The review found that the effects of omega-3 supplementation on ASD were too weak to conclude that core symptoms were alleviated. Vitamin D supplementation improved core symptoms, particularly behavioral functioning, however, the results of the literatures included in this study were slightly mixed, we cannot directly conclude that vitamin D supplementation has a beneficial effect on a specific symptom of ASD, but the overall conclusion is that vitamin D supplementation has a positive effect on behavioral functioning in ASD. Omega-3 and vitamin D combination supplementation has a good combined effect on social and behavioral outcomes in patients with ASD.

sheet.es: Si te planteas dar omega-3 o vitamina D a tu hijo o hija autista, no esperes cambios claros: la evidencia sobre omega-3 es débil, y la de vitamina D apunta a posibles efectos en la conducta, pero con resultados mixtos. Antes de empezar cualquier suplemento, habla con su médico, que puede valorar si hay una carencia real, y observa con calma qué necesita la persona en su día a día. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 20 estudios controlados con personas autistas. Sus límites: los estudios eran pocos, variados y con resultados poco consistentes, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are thinking about giving omega-3 or vitamin D to your autistic child, don't expect clear changes: the evidence for omega-3 is weak, and for vitamin D it points to possible effects on behaviour, but results are mixed. Before starting any supplement, talk with their doctor, who can check whether there is a real deficiency, and keep calmly noticing what the person needs day to day. This systematic review pooled 20 controlled studies with autistic people. Its limits: the studies were few, varied and not very consistent, so it cannot be a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på att ge omega-3 eller D-vitamin till ditt autistiska barn, förvänta dig inga tydliga förändringar: stödet för omega-3 är svagt, och för D-vitamin pekar det mot möjliga effekter på beteende, men resultaten är blandade. Innan du börjar med något tillskott, prata med barnets läkare, som kan undersöka om det finns en verklig brist, och fortsätt lugnt att lägga märke till vad personen behöver i vardagen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 20 kontrollerade studier med autistiska personer. Begränsningar: studierna var få, olika och inte särskilt samstämmiga, så resultatet kan inte gälla som regel för alla.

title: The workplace masking experiences of autistic, non-autistic neurodivergent and neurotypical adults in the UK.
authors: Pryke-Hobbes A, Davies J, Heasman B, Livesey A, Walker A, Pellicano E, Remington A
abstract: Masking entails hiding or concealing one's traits during social interactions. Research suggests that masking is particularly common for autistic people, though many non-autistic people also conceal aspects of their identity. Existing research has identified the key motivations and consequences of masking. No research to date, however, has considered how this might be affected by the social context in which masking is employed. This study compared the masking experiences of 285 autistic, 88 non-autistic neurodivergent and 99 neurotypical adults within a context in which masking is expected to be highly prevalent, namely the workplace. We used reflexive thematic analysis to explore the motivations, consequences, and contextual differences of workplace masking compared to other social contexts. Workplace masking was considered by participants in all three groups to be an adaptive response to a range of socially grounded workplace challenges and was usually employed as a strategy to safeguard against the threat of negative social and employment outcomes. Our non-autistic neurodivergent and autistic participants, however, reported experiencing unique pressures to mask, given the limited understanding of neurodiversity in workplaces and society more broadly. These findings have important implications for the wider masking literature and for workplace practice.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a la que apoyas parece agotada después del trabajo, el enmascaramiento puede ser parte de la razón. Podéis hablar con calma sobre en qué momentos siente que debe ocultar sus rasgos, qué le cuesta más y qué ajustes o espacios seguros podrían ayudar, sin presionarla a revelar su diagnóstico. Este estudio cualitativo recogió experiencias de 285 adultos autistas, 88 neurodivergentes no autistas y 99 neurotípicos en Reino Unido; todos enmascaraban en el trabajo para protegerse, pero las personas neurodivergentes sentían presiones extra por la falta de comprensión. Límites: se basa en relatos de personas de un solo país y no mide efectos ni prueba soluciones.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support seems drained after work, masking may be part of the reason. You could talk calmly about when they feel they must hide their traits, what costs them most, and which adjustments or safe spaces might help, without pushing them to disclose. This qualitative study gathered experiences from 285 autistic, 88 non-autistic neurodivergent and 99 neurotypical adults in the UK; all groups masked at work to protect themselves, but neurodivergent people described extra pressure because workplaces understand neurodiversity poorly. Limits: it relies on self-reports from one country and does not measure outcomes or test solutions.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar verkar slutkörd efter jobbet kan maskering vara en del av förklaringen. Ni kan lugnt prata om när hen känner att hen måste dölja sina drag, vad som kostar mest och vilka anpassningar eller trygga platser som kan hjälpa, utan att pressa hen att berätta om sin diagnos. Denna kvalitativa studie samlade erfarenheter från 285 autistiska, 88 icke-autistiska neurodivergenta och 99 neurotypiska vuxna i Storbritannien; alla maskerade på jobbet för att skydda sig, men neurodivergenta beskrev extra press på grund av bristande förståelse för neurodiversitet. Begränsningar: studien bygger på egna berättelser från ett land och mäter inte effekter eller testar lösningar.

title: Neurological and psychiatric disorders among autistic adults: a population healthcare record study.
authors: Underwood JFG, DelPozo-Banos M, Frizzati A, Rai D, John A, Hall J
abstract: Background Co-occurring psychiatric disorders are common in autism, with previous studies suggesting 54-94% of autistic individuals develop a mental health condition in their lifetime. Most studies have looked at clinically-recruited cohorts, or paediatric cohorts followed into adulthood, with less known about the autistic community at a population level. We therefore studied the prevalence of co-occurring psychiatric and neurological conditions in autistic individuals in a national sample. Methods This retrospective case-control study utilised the SAIL Databank to examine anonymised whole population electronic health record data from 2001 to 2016 in Wales, UK ( N = 3.6 million). We investigated the prevalence of co-occurring psychiatric and selected neurological diagnoses in autistic adults' records during the study period using International Classification of Diseases-10 and Read v2 clinical codes compared to general population controls matched for age, sex and deprivation. Results All psychiatric conditions examined were more common amongst adults with autism after adjusting for age, sex and deprivation. Prevalence of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (7.00%), bipolar disorder (2.50%), obsessive-compulsive disorder (3.02%), psychosis (18.30%) and schizophrenia (5.20%) were markedly elevated in those with autism, with corresponding odds ratios 8.24-10.74 times the general population. Depression (25.90%) and anxiety (22.40%) were also more prevalent, with epilepsy 9.21 times more common in autism. Conclusions We found that a range of psychiatric conditions were more frequently recorded in autistic individuals. We add to understanding of under-reporting and diagnostic overshadowing in autism. With increasing awareness of autism, services should be cognisant of the psychiatric conditions that frequently co-occur in this population.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, conviene estar atento a señales de ansiedad, depresión, TDAH o epilepsia, y no atribuir automáticamente todo cambio al autismo. Si notas cambios en el sueño, el ánimo, la energía o episodios extraños, coméntalo con su médico y pide que se valoren por separado. Llevar un registro breve puede ayudar. Este estudio revisó historias clínicas anónimas de toda la población de Gales (3,6 millones de personas, 2001-2016), comparando adultos autistas con personas similares en edad, sexo y nivel socioeconómico. Sus límites: solo refleja diagnósticos registrados, que pueden ser erróneos o incompletos, y no describe a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it helps to stay alert to signs of anxiety, depression, ADHD or epilepsy, rather than assuming every change is simply part of being autistic. If you notice shifts in sleep, mood, energy or unusual episodes, mention them to their doctor and ask for them to be looked at on their own terms. A short written log can help. This study reviewed anonymised health records for the whole population of Wales (3.6 million people, 2001–2016), comparing autistic adults with people matched for age, sex and deprivation. Its limits: it only captures recorded diagnoses, which may be wrong or incomplete, and it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen är det bra att vara uppmärksam på tecken på ångest, depression, ADHD eller epilepsi, i stället för att anta att varje förändring bara hör till autismen. Märker du förändringar i sömn, stämning, energi eller ovanliga episoder, ta upp det med läkaren och be att de bedöms för sig. En kort anteckningsbok kan hjälpa. Studien granskade anonymiserade journaler för hela Wales befolkning (3,6 miljoner personer, 2001–2016) och jämförde autistiska vuxna med personer av samma ålder, kön och socioekonomiska situation. Begränsningar: den visar bara registrerade diagnoser, som kan vara felaktiga eller ofullständiga, och beskriver inte varje autistisk person.

title: Prevalence of Victimisation in Autistic Individuals: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Trundle G, Jones KA, Ropar D, Egan V
abstract: Autistic individuals are at an increased risk of experiencing victimisation. Previous reviews have focussed specific types of victimisation. Thus, a clearer picture considering the range of victimisation experiences autistic people face is required. This systematic review aims to identify the prevalence of victimisation in autistic individuals considering a variety of victimisation types (e.g., bulling, sexual victimisation, and crime) in both adults and children from clinical and community settings. Through systematic searches of relevant databases, 291 studies met the criteria for review. Of those, 34 studies met the inclusion criteria: a) quantitative studies, b) involving autistic individuals, c) reporting prevalence rates of victimisation. Meta-analysis found a pooled prevalence rate of victimisation of 44% in autistic individuals. Subgroup analysis examined moderating factors as high heterogeneity was present. This found the pooled prevalence rates for bullying to be 47%, 16% for child abuse, 40% for sexual victimisation, 13% for cyberbullying, and 84% for multiple forms of victimisation in autistic individuals, though heterogeneity remained. Correction for participants' age, reporter used, and the population which the sample was recruited from did not reduce heterogeneity. Although heterogeneity impedes the definitive interpretation of the findings, this review illustrates the need for strategies and interventions to reduce the incidence of victimisation.

sheet.es: Vale la pena preguntar con calma y de forma regular a tu hijo, hija o familiar autista cómo le tratan en la escuela, el trabajo, en internet y en otros lugares, usando la forma de comunicación que le resulte más cómoda. Creerle, anotar lo que cuenta y contar con adultos de confianza puede ayudar a detectar el acoso o el abuso a tiempo. Esta revisión sistemática con metaanálisis reunió 34 estudios con niños y adultos autistas y encontró que alrededor del 44 % había sufrido algún tipo de victimización, como acoso escolar o violencia sexual. Las cifras variaron mucho entre estudios, así que no predicen lo que vivirá cada persona.
sheet.en: It is worth gently and regularly checking in with your autistic child or family member about how they are treated at school, work, online and elsewhere, using whatever way of communicating suits them best. Believing them, keeping notes and having trusted adults around can help spot bullying or abuse early. This systematic review and meta-analysis combined 34 studies of autistic children and adults and found that about 44% had experienced some form of victimisation, such as bullying or sexual victimisation. Results varied widely between studies, so the figures cannot predict what any one person will experience.
sheet.sv: Det kan vara klokt att lugnt och regelbundet fråga ditt autistiska barn eller din autistiska anhörige hur hen blir bemött i skolan, på jobbet, på nätet och på andra ställen, på det sätt att kommunicera som passar hen bäst. Att tro på det hen berättar, anteckna och ha trygga vuxna runt omkring kan hjälpa till att upptäcka mobbning eller övergrepp tidigt. Denna systematiska översikt med metaanalys sammanställde 34 studier med autistiska barn och vuxna och fann att ungefär 44 % hade utsatts för någon form av utsatthet, till exempel mobbning eller sexuella övergrepp. Resultaten skilde sig mycket mellan studierna, så siffrorna kan inte förutsäga vad en enskild person kommer att uppleva.

title: A realist review of health passports for Autistic adults.
authors: Ellis R, Williams K, Brown A, Healer E, Grant A
abstract: Background Autism is a normal part of cognitive diversity, resulting in communication and sensory processing differences, which can become disabling in a neurotypical world. Autistic people have an increased likelihood of physical and mental co-occurring conditions and die earlier than neurotypical peers. Inaccessible healthcare may contribute to this. Autism Health Passports (AHPs) are paper-based or digital tools which can be used to describe healthcare accessibility needs; they are recommended in UK clinical guidance. However, questions remained as to the theoretical underpinnings and effectiveness of AHPs. Methods We undertook a systematic literature search identifying studies focused on AHPs for adults (aged over 16 years) from five databases. Included literature was subjected to realist evaluation. Data were extracted using a standardised form, developed by the research team, which considered research design, study quality for realist review and the Context, Mechanisms and Outcomes (CMOs) associated with each AHP tool. Findings 162 unique records were identified, and 13 items were included in the review. Only one item was considered high quality. Contextual factors focused on the inaccessibility of healthcare to Autistic patients and staff lack of confidence and training in supporting Autistic needs. Interventions were heterogeneous, with most sources reporting few details as to how they had been developed. The most frequently included contents were communication preferences. Mechanisms were often not stated or were inferred by the reviewers and lacked specificity. Outcomes were included in four studies and were primarily focused on AHP uptake, rather than Outcomes which measured impact. Conclusion There is insufficient evidence to conclude that AHPs reduce the health inequalities experienced by Autistic people. Using an AHP tool alone in a healthcare Context that does not meet Autistic needs, without the inclusion of the local Autistic community developing the tool, and a wider intervention to reduce known barriers to health inequality, may mean that AHPs do not trigger any Mechanisms, and thus cannot affect Outcomes.

sheet.es: Un pasaporte de salud autista (un documento en papel o digital que explica cómo comunicarse con la persona, qué sensibilidades sensoriales tiene y qué ajustes necesita) puede ser útil, pero no basta por sí solo. Si lo usas, complétalo junto con la persona autista, llévalo a las citas y pide al personal que lo lea y aplique los ajustes. Pregunta también qué formación tiene el centro. Esta revisión realista analizó 13 trabajos sobre pasaportes de salud para adultos autistas mayores de 16 años. Solo uno era de alta calidad y casi ninguno midió si mejoraban la salud, así que aún no sabemos si reducen las desigualdades sanitarias.
sheet.en: An autism health passport (a paper or digital document describing how someone prefers to communicate, their sensory needs and the adjustments they need) may help, but it is unlikely to be enough on its own. If you use one, fill it in together with the autistic person, bring it to appointments, and ask staff to read it and act on it. It is also fair to ask what autism training the service has. This realist review looked at 13 sources on health passports for autistic adults over 16. Only one was high quality and few measured real health effects, so we do not yet know whether passports reduce health inequalities.
sheet.sv: Ett autismhälsopass (ett papper eller digitalt dokument som beskriver hur personen vill kommunicera, sensoriska behov och vilka anpassningar som behövs) kan vara till hjälp, men räcker sannolikt inte ensamt. Om ni använder ett, fyll i det tillsammans med den autistiska personen, ta med det till besök och be personalen läsa det och göra anpassningarna. Det är också rimligt att fråga vilken autismkunskap vårdenheten har. Denna realistiska översikt granskade 13 källor om hälsopass för autistiska vuxna över 16 år. Bara en höll hög kvalitet och få mätte faktiska hälsoeffekter, så vi vet ännu inte om passen minskar ojämlikheten i hälsa.

title: Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Review and Analysis of the Risks and Benefits.
authors: Okoye C, Obialo-Ibeawuchi CM, Obajeun OA, Sarwar S, Tawfik C, Waleed MS, Wasim AU, Mohamoud I, Afolayan AY, Mbaezue RN
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition made up of enduring challenges in social communication and interaction and the presence of repetitive and restricted behavior patterns. Early diagnosis of autism is crucial for timely intervention and improved long-term outcomes. This review aims to explore some of its signs and symptoms, look into some diagnostic tools, and analyze the benefits and risks associated with an early diagnosis of autism. The symptoms of ASD vary from child to child, some of which are: avoidance of eye contact, lack of response to names, excessive fear, and lack of interactive and pretend play. Early identification of these symptoms by caregivers and healthcare providers facilitates the need for diagnosis and appropriate interventions. Some screening and diagnostic tools that have been found to help make the diagnosis are the Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, Revised with Follow-Up (M-CHAT-R/F), the Social Communication Questionnaire (SCQ), the Parents' Evaluation of Developmental Status (PEDS), and the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), amongst others. The benefits of early diagnosis include the opportunity for early intervention, which has been shown to enhance developmental outcomes and improve adaptive skills. Early identification allows for the implementation of specialized interventions tailored to the specific needs of individuals with autism, targeting social communication, language development, and behavioral challenges. Furthermore, early diagnosis enables families to access appropriate support services, educational resources, and community programs, facilitating better coping mechanisms, reducing parental stress, and increasing adult independence. However, early diagnosis of autism also entails certain risks. One significant concern is the potential for labeling and stigmatization, which can impact the child's self-esteem and social interactions. There is a risk of overdiagnosis or misdiagnosis, leading to unnecessary interventions and treatments. Additionally, the diagnostic process can be lengthy, complex, and emotionally challenging for families, requiring comprehensive assessments by multidisciplinary teams. This review highlights the importance of a balanced approach when considering the benefits and risks of early diagnosis. Early identification allows for timely interventions that significantly improve developmental outcomes and quality of life for individuals with autism. To mitigate the risks, it is crucial to ensure accurate and reliable diagnostic procedures, support families throughout the process, and promote societal awareness and acceptance. We also highlighted some future directions in the management of autism, including the use of biomarkers and the use of artificial intelligence and learning for diagnosing ASD.

sheet.es: Si notas diferencias en cómo tu hijo o hija se comunica, juega o responde a su nombre, puedes comentarlo con el pediatra y preguntar por herramientas de cribado como el M-CHAT-R/F. Una evaluación temprana puede abrir la puerta a apoyos, recursos educativos y redes para la familia. Pide que el proceso sea cuidadoso, pregunta todo lo que necesites y busca apoyo emocional para ti; un diagnóstico describe una forma de ser, no define el valor de tu hijo. Esta es una revisión narrativa de estudios previos, sin participantes propios. Su limitación: no analiza datos de forma sistemática y usa un lenguaje centrado en déficits; cada niño y familia es distinto.
sheet.en: If you notice differences in how your child communicates, plays or responds to their name, you can raise it with your doctor and ask about screening tools such as the M-CHAT-R/F. An early assessment can open doors to support, educational resources and family networks. Ask for a careful process, ask every question you have, and look for emotional support for yourself; a diagnosis describes a way of being, it does not define your child's worth. This is a narrative review of earlier research, with no participants of its own. Its limits: it does not analyse data systematically and uses deficit-focused language; every child and family is different.
sheet.sv: Om du märker skillnader i hur ditt barn kommunicerar, leker eller reagerar på sitt namn kan du ta upp det med BVC eller läkare och fråga om screeningverktyg som M-CHAT-R/F. En tidig utredning kan öppna dörrar till stöd, pedagogiska resurser och nätverk för familjen. Be om en noggrann process, ställ alla frågor du har och sök känslomässigt stöd för din egen del; en diagnos beskriver ett sätt att vara, den avgör inte ditt barns värde. Detta är en narrativ översikt av tidigare forskning, utan egna deltagare. Begränsningar: den analyserar inte data systematiskt och använder bristfokuserat språk; varje barn och familj är olika.

title: The Foundations of Autistic Flourishing.
authors: Pellicano E, Heyworth M
abstract: Purpose of review All people-including Autistic people-deserve to live flourishing lives. But what does a flourishing life look like for Autistic people? We suggest that the hidden biases, methodological errors, and key assumptions of autism science have obscured answers to this question. Here, we seek to initiate a broader discussion about what the foundations for a good Autistic life might be and how this discussion might be framed. Recent findings We identify five ways in which autism science can help us all to secure those foundations, including by (1) giving Autistic well-being prominence in research, (2) amplifying Autistic autonomy, (3) attending better to everyday experiences, (4) acknowledging context, and (5) working in partnership with Autistic people and their families and allies to ensure that they are at the heart of research decision-making. Such an approach would direct the focus of autism research to help shape good Autistic lives.

sheet.es: Una idea práctica para mañana: pregunte a la persona autista qué hace que su día vaya bien, y deje que esa respuesta guíe las decisiones. Fíjese en lo cotidiano (descanso, intereses, entorno sensorial, relaciones) más que en corregir rasgos, respete su autonomía y ajuste el contexto antes de pedirle que cambie. Planifique junto a ella, no por ella. Se trata de una revisión escrita con personas autistas que propone cinco prioridades para la investigación: bienestar, autonomía, experiencias diarias, contexto y colaboración. Su límite: es un análisis y una propuesta, no un estudio con participantes que mida resultados, y cada persona definirá su bienestar a su manera.
sheet.en: A practical idea for tomorrow: ask the autistic person what makes a day go well for them, and let that answer guide decisions. Pay attention to everyday life (rest, interests, sensory surroundings, relationships) rather than correcting traits, respect their autonomy, and adjust the context before asking them to change. Plan with them, not for them. This is a review written with autistic people that proposes five research priorities: well-being, autonomy, daily experiences, context and partnership. Its limit: it is an analysis and a proposal, not a study with participants measuring outcomes, and each person will define flourishing in their own way.
sheet.sv: En praktisk idé för i morgon: fråga den autistiska personen vad som gör att en dag fungerar bra, och låt svaret styra besluten. Uppmärksamma vardagen (vila, intressen, sensorisk miljö, relationer) snarare än att rätta till drag, respektera personens självbestämmande och anpassa sammanhanget innan du ber hen att ändra sig. Planera tillsammans med hen, inte åt hen. Detta är en översikt skriven tillsammans med autistiska personer som föreslår fem forskningsprioriteringar: välmående, autonomi, vardagserfarenheter, sammanhang och samarbete. Begränsning: det är en analys och ett förslag, inte en studie med deltagare som mäter resultat, och varje person definierar sitt välmående på sitt eget sätt.

title: Increased rates of chronic physical health conditions across all organ systems in autistic adolescents and adults.
authors: Ward JH, Weir E, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background The poorer physical health of autistic adults compared to non-autistic adults has been highlighted by several epidemiological studies. However, research has so far been limited to specific geographical areas and has primarily focused on young autistic individuals (aged 35 years and younger). Recent studies indicate a higher rate of mortality in autistic people, as well as poorer quality of self-reported healthcare interactions. This study aims to determine, first, whether autistic people experience greater levels of non-communicable health conditions and second, whether these are explained by differences in demographics (i.e. sex, country of residence, ethnicity, education level), alcohol use, smoking, body mass index (BMI), or family history of medical conditions. Method We employed a cross-sectional, convenience-sampling study via an anonymous, online survey of autistic and non-autistic adults (n = 2305, mean age = 41.6, 65.9% female, 49% autistic). The survey asked participants to self-report information about their demographics, autism diagnosis, diet, exercise, sleep, sexual health, substance use, personal medical history, and family medical history (for all first-degree, biological relatives). Binomial logistic regression across four iterative models of increasing complexity was applied to assess rates of physical health conditions. The Benjamini-Hochberg correction was used to account for multiple testing, and only physical health conditions that achieved at least 1% endorsement within the overall sample (n > 22) were included in the analysis to reduce risk of Type I errors. We also used novel network analysis methods to test whether there are increased levels of multimorbidity between autistic and non-autistic people. Results There were significantly elevated rates of non-communicable conditions across all organ systems in autistic people, including gastrointestinal, neurological, endocrine, visual, ear/nose/throat, skin, liver and kidney, and haematological conditions. We confirmed previous findings by showing highly significant differences in rates of neurological and gastrointestinal symptoms (p Limitations Our study is biased towards females, white individuals, highly educated people, and UK residents, likely due to sampling biases. Our self-report study design may also exclude those who lack access to computers, or those with intellectual disability. Our network analysis is also limited in size. Conclusions This study provides evidence of widespread, physical health comorbidity that spans nearly all major organ systems in autistic adults compared to non-autistic adults, using both binary logistic regression and network models. Healthcare professionals must be made aware of the range of co-occurring physical health conditions that may be more common among autistic people. However, our findings also point towards potential avenues requiring further exploration, such as the association of autism with both Coeliac's disease and EDS.

sheet.es: Las personas autistas pueden tener más problemas de salud física, en muchos sistemas del cuerpo: digestivos, neurológicos, hormonales, de piel, vista u oído. Mañana puede ayudar anotar síntomas físicos (dolor de barriga, sueño, piel, mareos) y llevar esa lista a la consulta médica, pidiendo que no se atribuyan solo al autismo. Este estudio fue una encuesta en línea con 2305 adultos (49 % autistas, edad media 42 años) que informaron su propia salud. Sus límites: participaron sobre todo mujeres blancas, con estudios y del Reino Unido, y no incluyó a personas sin acceso a internet ni con discapacidad intelectual; no se aplica igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: Autistic people may have more physical health conditions across many body systems: digestive, neurological, hormonal, skin, vision and hearing. Tomorrow, it can help to note physical symptoms (stomach pain, sleep, skin, dizziness) and bring that list to medical appointments, asking that they are not put down to autism alone. This study was an online survey of 2,305 adults (49% autistic, average age 42) who self-reported their health. Its limits: participants were mostly white, highly educated women in the UK, and people without internet access or with intellectual disability were left out; it does not apply equally to every person.
sheet.sv: Autistiska personer kan ha fler fysiska hälsotillstånd i många av kroppens system: mage och tarm, nervsystem, hormoner, hud, syn och hörsel. I morgon kan det hjälpa att anteckna kroppsliga symtom (magont, sömn, hud, yrsel) och ta med listan till vården, och be att de inte bara förklaras med autism. Studien var en webbenkät med 2 305 vuxna (49 % autistiska, medelålder 42 år) som själva rapporterade sin hälsa. Begränsningar: deltagarna var mest vita, högutbildade kvinnor i Storbritannien, och personer utan internet eller med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning saknades; resultaten gäller inte lika för alla.

title: Applications of identity-based theories to understand the impact of stigma and camouflaging on mental health outcomes for autistic people.
authors: Rivera RA, Bennetto L
abstract: Autistic people have long been conceptualized from a deficit-based model of disability, but recent self-advocates and scholars have asserted the importance of recognizing autism as both a disability and an important part of a person's social identity. The autistic identity is subject to specific stigma and stressors beyond everyday discrimination and prejudice, which can have many downstream implications on mental health and well-being. Prior research on camouflaging has explained both quantitatively and qualitatively how autistic people conform to norms and mask their autistic traits to better fit in with non-autistic societal standards. Given this paradigm shift in understanding autistic peoples' lived experiences, researchers must also begin to reshape the theories guiding their work in order to improve diagnosis, intervention, and supports. This review examines the extant research on identity-related stigma and camouflaging and their subsequent impacts on mental health outcomes in autism. A model is proposed integrating identity-based theories-specifically the social model of disability, social identity theory, and minority stress model-to explain relationships across research areas and better explain the experiences of autistic people. We discuss how identity-based theories can be applied in autism research to better understand the impacts of stigma and camouflaging on autistic peoples' lived experiences and reduce disparities in their mental health outcomes.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista a la que acompañas parece agotada después del colegio, el trabajo o reuniones sociales, puede estar camuflando: ocultando rasgos autistas para encajar. Mañana puedes ofrecer espacios en casa donde no tenga que fingir, valorar su identidad autista y reducir exigencias de parecer «normal». Reconocer el estigma que vive puede proteger su bienestar. Esta revisión reúne investigaciones previas sobre estigma, camuflaje y salud mental en personas autistas, y propone un modelo basado en teorías de identidad y estrés minoritario. Su límite: es un marco teórico, no un estudio que pruebe intervenciones, y cada persona vive su identidad de forma distinta.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support seems drained after school, work or social events, they may be camouflaging: hiding autistic traits to fit in. Tomorrow you could offer spaces at home where they don't have to perform, value their autistic identity, and ease expectations to appear 'typical'. Acknowledging the stigma they face may help protect their wellbeing. This review gathers earlier research on stigma, camouflaging and mental health in autistic people, and proposes a model based on identity theories and minority stress. Its limit: it is a theoretical framework, not a study testing supports, and every person experiences their identity differently.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar verkar utmattad efter skola, jobb eller sociala sammanhang kan hen kamouflera: dölja autistiska drag för att passa in. I morgon kan du erbjuda platser hemma där hen inte behöver spela en roll, visa uppskattning för hens autistiska identitet och sänka kraven på att verka ”typisk”. Att erkänna stigmat hen möter kan skydda välmåendet. Denna översikt sammanställer tidigare forskning om stigma, kamouflering och psykisk hälsa hos autistiska personer och föreslår en modell byggd på identitetsteorier och minoritetsstress. Begränsning: det är en teoretisk ram, inte en studie som prövar stöd, och varje person upplever sin identitet olika.

title: Anti-ableism and scientific accuracy in autism research: a false dichotomy.
authors: Bottema-Beutel K, Kapp SK, Sasson N, Gernsbacher MA, Natri H, Botha M
abstract: It was recently argued that autism researchers committed to rejecting ableist frameworks in their research may sacrifice "scientifically accurate" conceptualizations of autism. In this perspective piece, we argue that: (a) anti-ableism vs. scientific accuracy is a false dichotomy, (b) there is no ideology-free science that has claim to scientific accuracy, and (c) autism science has a history of false leads in part because of unexamined ableist ideologies that undergird researcher framings and interpretations of evidence. To illustrate our claims, we discuss several avenues of autism research that were promoted as scientific advances, but were eventually debunked or shown to have much less explanatory value than initially proposed. These research programs have involved claims about autism etiology, the nature of autism and autistic characteristics, and autism intervention. Common to these false leads have been ableist assumptions about autism that inform researcher perspectives. Negative impacts of this work have been mitigated in some areas of autism research, but these perspectives continue to exert influence on the lives of autistic people, including the availability of services, discourses about autism, and sociocultural conceptualizations of autistic people. Examining these false leads may help current researchers better understand how ableism may negatively influence their areas of inquiry. We close with a positive argument that promoting anti-ableism can be done in tandem with increasing scientific accuracy.

sheet.es: Cuando lea sobre autismo, puede preguntarse con calma: ¿esta afirmación parte de la idea de que ser autista es un defecto? Varias teorías presentadas como avances sobre causas, naturaleza o intervenciones del autismo resultaron falsas o mucho menos útiles de lo prometido, en parte por supuestos capacitistas. Mañana puede elegir fuentes que escuchen a personas autistas y valorar lo que su hijo o hija comunica, sin aceptar etiquetas sin examinarlas. Evidencia: es un artículo de perspectiva que revisa la historia de la investigación sobre autismo; no recoge datos nuevos de participantes. Límite: es una argumentación de expertos, no un estudio empírico, y no ofrece pautas aplicables a cada persona.
sheet.en: When you read about autism, you can calmly ask: does this claim assume that being autistic is a defect? Several theories promoted as breakthroughs about autism's causes, nature or interventions were later debunked or proved far less useful than promised, partly because of ableist assumptions. Tomorrow, you might choose sources that listen to autistic people and value what your child communicates, rather than accepting labels unexamined. Evidence: this is a perspective article reviewing the history of autism research; it does not collect new data from participants. Limit: it is an expert argument, not an empirical study, and offers no rules that fit every person.
sheet.sv: När du läser om autism kan du lugnt fråga dig: utgår påståendet från att det är en brist att vara autistisk? Flera teorier som lanserades som genombrott om autismens orsaker, natur eller insatser visade sig senare vara fel eller mycket mindre användbara än utlovat, delvis på grund av funkofobiska antaganden. I morgon kan du välja källor som lyssnar på autistiska personer och ta vara på det ditt barn kommunicerar, i stället för att godta etiketter oprövade. Evidens: detta är en perspektivartikel som granskar autismforskningens historia; den samlar inga nya data från deltagare. Begränsning: det är en expertargumentation, inte en empirisk studie, och ger inga regler som passar alla.

title: 'Living in a world that's not about us': The impact of everyday life on the health and wellbeing of autistic women and gender diverse people.
authors: Grove R, Clapham H, Moodie T, Gurrin S, Hall G
abstract: Background Autistic women and gender diverse people have specific needs related to their physical and mental health. They also experience more barriers to accessing services. While there are autobiographical accounts of the 'invisible' challenges that autistic women and gender diverse people face day-to-day, there has been limited research that explores how these experiences impact health and wellbeing. Objectives This study aimed to understand the everyday experiences of autistic women and gender diverse people, and their impact on health and wellbeing. Design Qualitative methods were used to elicit rich information about the unique experiences of autistic women and gender diverse people. Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with 31 autistic adults. The data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results We identified 3 themes and 10 subthemes. Our first theme described 'all the stuff that you have to do to get through life', including managing domestic tasks, parenting, unique health needs and co-occurring physical conditions. The second theme outlined the impact of 'living in a world that's not about us', describing how navigating the neurotypical world, managing gender role expectations and trying to fit impacts on mental health. Our third theme outlined the positive impacts of 'shedding all the layers and being myself', including the importance of formal identification, exploring autistic identity and community, and including autistic people in research to support them to 'have a good life on their own terms'. Conclusion This study emphasized the importance of shifting the responsibility of health and wellbeing from the individual, and the importance of interpersonal, community, cultural, policy and societal factors in ensuring positive health outcomes for autistic women and gender diverse people. It also highlighted areas that enable autistic women and gender diverse people to flourish, including autistic community connectedness, positive relationships and autistic-affirming support from health professionals.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una mujer o persona de género diverso autista, reconoce el esfuerzo invisible de las tareas diarias: casa, crianza, salud y adaptarse a un mundo neurotípico. Ayuda reducir exigencias de «encajar», repartir tareas, apoyar el contacto con la comunidad autista y buscar profesionales que respeten su identidad. Ser ella misma, sin máscaras, se asoció con más bienestar. La evidencia procede de entrevistas cualitativas con 31 adultos autistas, analizadas temáticamente. Sus límites: es una muestra pequeña, sin grupo de comparación, y describe experiencias, no causas; no todas las personas vivirán lo mismo.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic woman or gender diverse person, recognise the invisible effort behind everyday life: household tasks, parenting, health needs and navigating a neurotypical world. It can help to ease pressure to 'fit in', share tasks, support connection with autistic community and look for affirming health professionals. Being able to drop the layers and be themselves was linked to better wellbeing. The evidence comes from qualitative interviews with 31 autistic adults, analysed thematically. Its limits: a small sample, no comparison group, and it describes experiences rather than causes; not everyone will share them.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk kvinna eller person med annan könsidentitet, erkänn den osynliga ansträngningen i vardagen: hushåll, föräldraskap, hälsobehov och att navigera i en neurotypisk värld. Det kan hjälpa att minska kraven på att passa in, dela på uppgifter, stödja kontakt med autistisk gemenskap och söka bekräftande vårdpersonal. Att få släppa fasaden och vara sig själv kopplades till bättre välmående. Underlaget är kvalitativa intervjuer med 31 autistiska vuxna, analyserade tematiskt. Begränsningar: litet urval, ingen jämförelsegrupp, och studien beskriver upplevelser, inte orsaker; alla delar inte dessa erfarenheter.

title: Linehan's biosocial model applied to emotion dysregulation in autism: a narrative review of the literature and an illustrative case conceptualization.
authors: Bemmouna D, Weiner L
abstract: Emotion dysregulation (ED) is a transdiagnostic difficulty prevalent in autism spectrum condition (ASC). Importantly, recent research has suggested that ED is involved in self-harm and suicidality. Pre-existing models on the etiology of ED in ASC focus mainly on biological factors to ASC features, such as sensory sensitivities, poor flexibility, and sensitivity to change. However, although psychosocial factors seem to play a role in the emergence of ED in ASC as well (e.g., childhood maltreatment and camouflaging), there is a lack of a comprehensive model conceptualizing biosocial factors involved in ED in autistic people. Linehan's biosocial model (1993) is one of the leading etiological models of ED in borderline personality disorder (BPD). It conceptualizes ED as emerging from transactions between a pre-existing emotional vulnerability in the child and an invalidating developmental environment. Beyond its clinical relevance, Linehan's model has gathered empirical evidence supporting its pertinence in BPD and in other psychiatric disorders. Although ASC and BPD are two distinct diagnoses, because they may share ED, Linehan's biosocial model might be useful for understanding the development of ED in ASC. Hence, this article aims to provide an application and extension of Linehan's model to conceptualize ED in ASC. To do so, we conducted a narrative review of the literature on ED and its underlying factors in ASC from a developmental perspective. To investigate the pertinence of the biosocial model applied to ED in autistic people, we were interested on data on (i) ED and its behavioral correlates in ASC, in relation to the biosocial model, (ii) the potential biological and psychosocial correlates of ED in ASC and (iii) the overlapping difficulties in ASC and BPD. Finally, to assess the pertinence of the model, we applied it to the case of an autistic woman presenting with ED and suicidal behaviors. Our review and application to the case of an autistic woman suggest that ED in ASC encompasses factors related to both biological and psychosocial risk factors as conceptualized in the BPD framework, although in both domains ASC-specific factors might be involved.

sheet.es: Las emociones intensas de una persona autista no dependen solo de su biología: también influye cómo responde su entorno. Validar lo que siente («entiendo que esto te desborda»), respetar sus necesidades sensoriales y reducir la presión de camuflarse puede ayudar a que se regule con más calma. Si aparecen autolesiones o ideas suicidas, busca apoyo profesional pronto. Esta es una revisión narrativa de la literatura que aplica el modelo biosocial de Linehan al autismo, ilustrada con el caso de una mujer autista. Sus límites: no es un estudio experimental, se basa en un solo caso y sus ideas aún deben comprobarse en más personas.
sheet.en: An autistic person's intense emotions are not only about biology: how the people around them respond matters too. Validating what they feel ("I can see this is overwhelming"), respecting sensory needs and easing the pressure to camouflage may help them regulate more calmly. If self-harm or suicidal thoughts appear, seek professional support early. This is a narrative literature review applying Linehan's biosocial model to autism, illustrated with the case of one autistic woman. Its limits: it is not an experimental study, it relies on a single case, and its ideas still need testing with more people.
sheet.sv: En autistisk persons starka känslor handlar inte bara om biologi: hur omgivningen bemöter dem spelar också roll. Att bekräfta det personen känner ("jag ser att det här blir för mycket"), respektera sensoriska behov och minska trycket att kamouflera kan hjälpa till med lugnare reglering. Om självskada eller självmordstankar dyker upp, sök professionellt stöd tidigt. Detta är en narrativ litteraturöversikt som tillämpar Linehans biosociala modell på autism, illustrerad med fallet med en autistisk kvinna. Begränsningar: det är ingen experimentell studie, den bygger på ett enda fall och idéerna behöver prövas på fler personer.

title: Psychiatric conditions in autistic adolescents: longitudinal stability from childhood and associated risk factors.
authors: Hollocks MJ, Leno VC, Chandler S, White P, Yorke I, Charman T, Pickles A, Baird G, Simonoff E
abstract: Autistic people experience high rates of co-occurring psychiatric diagnoses. Current prevalence estimates vary considerably due to an over-reliance on clinical cohorts and the longitudinal stability of diagnoses from childhood into adolescence is poorly understood. This study aims to provide prevalence rates of co-occurring DSM-5 psychiatric diagnosis for autistic adolescence and investigate, for the first time, the stability of diagnoses from childhood. Using a longitudinal stratified sample of autistic youth (N = 77; 13-17 years; 60% male), selected from a larger community-derived sample of those with pre-existing autism diagnoses (N = 277) weighted prevalence estimates of emotional (anxiety, depression), behavioural (oppositional and conduct disorders) and ADHD diagnoses were calculated based on semi-structured psychiatric interview. Prediction of adolescent psychiatric diagnosis based on childhood diagnostic status, sex, childhood IQ (both assessed at age 4-10 years) was tested. Emotional and behavioural disorders in adolescence were particularly prevalent, and significantly predicted by childhood disorder status. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity-disorder (ADHD) was prevalent but not predicted by childhood ADHD diagnosis. Neither sex nor childhood IQ predicted diagnostic outcomes.
