Autistic youth have high levels of co-occurring psychiatric conditions, which are broadly persistent across childhood and adolescence. Emotional disorders are particularly prevalent and remain persistent from childhood to adolescence. Greater diagnostic variability was found for ADHD with more adolescents moving across diagnostic thresholds.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tuvo ansiedad, tristeza persistente o dificultades de conducta en la infancia, conviene seguir atentos al llegar la adolescencia: en este estudio esas dificultades solían mantenerse, y el apoyo temprano y continuado puede marcar la diferencia. Habla con su equipo de salud si notas cambios, sin dar por hecho que pasarán solos. Los rasgos de TDAH, en cambio, variaron más con los años. La evidencia procede de un estudio longitudinal con 77 adolescentes autistas de 13 a 17 años, seleccionados de una muestra comunitaria y evaluados también entre los 4 y 10 años. Es una muestra pequeña y de un solo país, así que no predice lo que ocurrirá con cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child had anxiety, low mood or behavioural difficulties in childhood, it is worth staying attentive as they enter adolescence: in this study those difficulties often continued, and early, ongoing support can make a real difference. Talk with their care team if you notice changes, rather than assuming things will settle on their own. ADHD traits, by contrast, shifted more over the years. The evidence comes from a longitudinal study of 77 autistic adolescents aged 13 to 17, drawn from a community sample and also assessed at ages 4 to 10. The sample is small and from one country, so it cannot predict what will happen for any individual person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn hade ångest, nedstämdhet eller beteendesvårigheter i barndomen är det klokt att vara uppmärksam när tonåren börjar: i den här studien höll sådana svårigheter ofta i sig, och tidigt, fortlöpande stöd kan göra stor skillnad. Prata med vårdkontakten om du märker förändringar, i stället för att anta att det går över av sig självt. ADHD-drag varierade däremot mer över åren. Underlaget är en longitudinell studie med 77 autistiska ungdomar, 13–17 år, utvalda ur ett befolkningsbaserat urval och bedömda även vid 4–10 års ålder. Urvalet är litet och från ett land, så studien kan inte förutsäga vad som händer för varje enskild person.

title: Representation of autism in fictional media: A systematic review of media content and its impact on viewer knowledge and understanding of autism.
authors: Jones SC, Gordon CS, Mizzi S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract The way autism is represented in fictional media can impact people's views of autistic people. For example, representations may contribute to negative views of autistic people as being unusual or dangerous, or they may challenge stereotypes and instead highlight the strengths of autistic people. This work aimed to review previous research to understand how autistic people have been represented in fictional media (Part A). It also sought to understand whether viewing fictional portrayals of autism has an impact on people's knowledge of autism and attitudes towards autistic people (Part B). Of 14 studies that were included in Part A, several unhelpful and stereotypical portrayals of autism emerged. Positive portrayals were those that highlighted the strengths of autistic people and reflected nuance. There is a need for greater diversity in representation of autism in fictional media. For example, not all autistic people are white heterosexual males. Across the five studies included in Part B, there were no improvements in people's knowledge of autism after watching or reading a short segment from a fictional TV series or novel that depicts an autistic person. Although there was a significant improvement in people's attitudes towards autistic people, these findings do not provide a complete picture given the short length of the media exposure and small number of studies. Future studies should investigate how multiple exposures to the representation of autistic people in both fictional and non-fictional sources can affect people's understanding of autism. There is also a need to develop more accurate and respectful ways of measuring people's knowledge of, and attitudes towards, autism.

sheet.es: Las series y novelas pueden mejorar la actitud de la gente hacia las personas autistas, pero no bastan para que entiendan el autismo. Si su familia, el colegio o amistades conocen el autismo solo por la ficción, puede complementarlo con información de personas autistas reales y señalar con calma los estereotipos (genio, peligro, siempre varón blanco). Elija historias que muestren fortalezas y matices. Es una revisión sistemática de 14 estudios sobre contenidos y 5 sobre espectadores. Límites: pocos estudios, exposiciones muy breves a fragmentos y formas de medir conocimiento y actitudes que no siempre son precisas ni respetuosas.
sheet.en: TV series and novels may improve people's attitudes towards autistic people, but they are not enough to build real understanding of autism. If relatives, school staff or friends know autism mainly from fiction, you can add information from actual autistic people and calmly point out stereotypes (genius, danger, always a white man). Choose stories that show strengths and nuance. This is a systematic review of 14 studies on media content and 5 on viewers. Limits: few studies, very short exposure to clips or excerpts, and ways of measuring knowledge and attitudes that are not always accurate or respectful.
sheet.sv: Tv-serier och romaner kan förbättra människors attityder till autistiska personer, men de räcker inte för att skapa verklig förståelse för autism. Om släktingar, skolpersonal eller vänner mest känner till autism genom fiktion kan du komplettera med information från autistiska personer själva och lugnt peka ut stereotyper (geni, fara, alltid en vit man). Välj berättelser som visar styrkor och nyanser. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 14 studier om medieinnehåll och 5 om tittare. Begränsningar: få studier, mycket korta klipp eller utdrag, och mätmetoder för kunskap och attityder som inte alltid är träffsäkra eller respektfulla.

title: Autism through midlife: trajectories of symptoms, behavioral functioning, and health.
authors: Hong J, DaWalt LS, Taylor JL, Haider A, Mailick M
abstract: Background This study describes change in autism symptoms, behavioral functioning, and health measured prospectively over 22 years. Most studies tracking developmental trajectories have focused on autism during childhood, although adulthood is the longest stage of the life course. A robust understanding of how autistic people change through midlife and into older age has yet to be obtained. Methods Using an accelerated longitudinal design with 9 waves of data, developmental trajectories were estimated from adolescence through midlife and into early old age in a community-based cohort (n = 406). The overall aim was to determine whether there were age-related increases or decreases, whether the change was linear or curvilinear, and whether these trajectories differed between those who have ID and those who have average or above-average intellectual functioning. Subsequently, the slopes of the trajectories were evaluated to determine if they differed depending on age when the study began, with the goal of identifying possible cohort effects. Results There were significant trajectories of age-related change for all but one of the measures, although different measures manifested different patterns. Most autism symptoms improved through adulthood, while health worsened. An inverted U-shaped curve best described change for repetitive behavior symptoms, activities of daily living, maladaptive behaviors, and social interaction. For these measures, improved functioning was evident from adolescence until midlife. Then change leveled off, with worsening functioning from later midlife into early older age. Additionally, differences between autistic individuals with and without ID were evident. Although those who have ID had poorer levels of functioning, there were some indications that those without ID had accelerating challenges in their aging years that were not evident in those with ID - increases in medications for physical health problems and worsening repetitive behaviors. Conclusions Meeting the needs of the increasingly large population of autistic adults in midlife and old age requires a nuanced understanding of life course trajectories across the long stretch of adulthood and across multiple domains. Given the heterogeneity of autism, it will be important not to generalize across sub-groups, for example those who are minimally verbal and those who have above-average intellectual functioning.

sheet.es: Muchas personas autistas siguen ganando habilidades y viendo cambios positivos desde la adolescencia hasta la mediana edad; el crecimiento no termina en la infancia. A la vez, la salud física tiende a empeorar con los años, y en la madurez tardía pueden volver dificultades en la vida diaria o más conductas repetitivas. En la práctica: planifique revisiones de salud regulares y adapte los apoyos con la edad, también en adultos que antes parecían muy independientes. Evidencia: estudio longitudinal de 22 años con 406 personas autistas, con y sin discapacidad intelectual, de adolescentes a primera vejez. Límites: un solo grupo comunitario de Estados Unidos; los resultados son tendencias generales y no predicen la trayectoria de cada persona.
sheet.en: Many autistic people keep gaining skills and seeing positive changes from adolescence into midlife; growth does not stop in childhood. At the same time, physical health tends to decline with age, and in later midlife daily-living difficulties or repetitive behaviours may increase again. In practice: plan regular health check-ups and adjust support over time, including for adults who once seemed very independent. Evidence: a 22-year longitudinal study following 406 autistic people, with and without intellectual disability, from adolescence into early old age. Limits: one community cohort from the United States; the findings describe group trends and cannot predict any individual's path.
sheet.sv: Många autistiska personer fortsätter att utveckla färdigheter och se positiva förändringar från tonåren upp i medelåldern; utvecklingen slutar inte i barndomen. Samtidigt tenderar den fysiska hälsan att försämras med åren, och senare i medelåldern kan svårigheter i vardagen eller repetitiva beteenden öka igen. I praktiken: planera regelbundna hälsokontroller och anpassa stödet över tid, även för vuxna som tidigare verkat mycket självständiga. Evidens: en longitudinell studie över 22 år med 406 autistiska personer, med och utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, från tonåren till tidig ålderdom. Begränsningar: en enda grupp från USA; resultaten visar trender på gruppnivå och kan inte förutsäga en enskild persons utveckling.

title: Autism intervention meta-analysis of early childhood studies (Project AIM): updated systematic review and secondary analysis.
authors: Sandbank M, Bottema-Beutel K, Crowley LaPoint S, Feldman JI, Barrett DJ, Caldwell N, Dunham K, Crank J, Albarran S, Woynaroski T
abstract: Objective To summarize the breadth and quality of evidence supporting commonly recommended early childhood autism interventions and their estimated effects on developmental outcomes. Design Updated systematic review and meta-analysis (autism intervention meta-analysis; Project AIM). Data sources A search was conducted in November 2021 (updating a search done in November 2017) of the following databases and registers: Academic Search Complete, CINAHL Plus with full text, Education Source, Educational Administration Abstracts, ERIC, Medline, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses, PsycINFO, Psychology and Behavioral Sciences Collection, and SocINDEX with full text, Trials , and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligibility criteria for selecting studies Any controlled group study testing the effects of any non-pharmacological intervention on any outcome in young autistic children younger than 8 years. Review methods Newly identified studies were integrated into the previous dataset and were coded for participant, intervention, and outcome characteristics. Interventions were categorized by type of approach (such as behavioral, developmental, naturalistic developmental behavioral intervention, and technology based), and outcomes were categorized by domain (such as social communication, adaptive behavior, play, and language). Risks of bias were evaluated following guidance from Cochrane. Effects were estimated for all intervention and outcome types with sufficient contributing data, stratified by risk of bias, using robust variance estimation to account for intercorrelation of effects within studies and subgroups. Results The search yielded 289 reports of 252 studies, representing 13 304 participants and effects for 3291 outcomes. When contributing effects were restricted to those from randomized controlled trials, significant summary effects were estimated for behavioral interventions on social emotional or challenging behavior outcomes (Hedges' g=0.58, 95% confidence interval 0.11 to 1.06; P=0.02), developmental interventions on social communication (0.28, 0.12 to 0.44; P=0.003); naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions on adaptive behavior (0.23, 0.02 to 0.43; P=0.03), language (0.16, 0.01 to 0.31; P=0.04), play (0.19, 0.02 to 0.36; P=0.03), social communication (0.35, 0.23 to 0.47; P Conclusion The available evidence on interventions to support young autistic children has approximately doubled in four years. Some evidence from randomized controlled trials shows that behavioral interventions improve caregiver perception of challenging behavior and child social emotional functioning, and that technology based interventions support proximal improvements in specific social communication and social emotional skills. Evidence also shows that developmental interventions improve social communication in interactions with caregivers, and naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions improve core challenges associated with autism, particularly difficulties with social communication. However, potential benefits of these interventions cannot be weighed against the potential for adverse effects owing to inadequate monitoring and reporting.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para tu hijo o hija autista pequeño, los enfoques que se integran en el juego y la rutina diaria y siguen sus intereses (intervenciones del desarrollo y naturalistas) mostraron pequeñas mejoras en comunicación social, juego, lenguaje y habilidades de la vida diaria. Puedes preguntar a los profesionales cómo incluyen a la familia en momentos cotidianos y cómo vigilan el bienestar del niño. Es un metaanálisis de 252 estudios con más de 13.000 niños autistas menores de 8 años. Sus límites: los efectos fueron modestos, muchos estudios tenían riesgo de sesgo y casi ninguno registró posibles efectos negativos, así que observa siempre cómo vive tu hijo cada apoyo.
sheet.en: If you are looking for support for your young autistic child, approaches built into play and daily routines that follow the child's interests (developmental and naturalistic approaches) showed small gains in social communication, play, language and everyday skills. You can ask professionals how they involve the family in ordinary moments and how they check your child's wellbeing. This is a meta-analysis of 252 studies with over 13,000 autistic children under 8. Its limits: effects were modest, many studies had risk of bias, and almost none tracked possible harms, so keep noticing how your child experiences each kind of support.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd för ditt unga autistiska barn visade arbetssätt som byggs in i lek och vardagsrutiner och utgår från barnets intressen (utvecklingsinriktade och naturalistiska metoder) små förbättringar i social kommunikation, lek, språk och vardagsförmågor. Fråga gärna personalen hur de involverar familjen i vardagen och hur de följer barnets välbefinnande. Detta är en metaanalys av 252 studier med över 13 000 autistiska barn under 8 år. Begränsningar: effekterna var måttliga, många studier hade risk för snedvridning och nästan inga redovisade möjliga negativa effekter, så fortsätt lägga märke till hur ditt barn upplever varje stöd.

title: Resting-state EEG power differences in autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Neo WS, Foti D, Keehn B, Kelleher B
abstract: Narrative reviews have described various resting-state EEG power differences in autism across all five canonical frequency bands, with increased power for low and high frequencies and reduced power for middle frequencies. However, these differences have yet to be quantified using effect sizes and probed robustly for consistency, which are critical next steps for clinical translation. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic review of published and gray literature on resting-state EEG power in autism. We performed 10 meta-analyses to synthesize and quantify differences in absolute and relative resting-state delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma EEG power in autism. We also conducted moderator analyses to determine whether demographic characteristics, methodological details, and risk-of-bias indicators might account for heterogeneous study effect sizes. Our literature search and study selection processes yielded 41 studies involving 1,246 autistic and 1,455 neurotypical individuals. Meta-analytic models of 135 effect sizes demonstrated that autistic individuals exhibited reduced relative alpha (g = -0.35) and increased gamma (absolute: g = 0.37, relative: g = 1.06) power, but similar delta (absolute: g = 0.06, relative: g = 0.10), theta (absolute: g = -0.03, relative: g = -0.15), absolute alpha (g = -0.17), and beta (absolute: g = 0.01, relative: g = 0.08) power. Substantial heterogeneity in effect sizes was observed across all absolute (I 2 : 36.1-81.9%) and relative (I 2 : 64.6-84.4%) frequency bands. Moderator analyses revealed that age, biological sex, IQ, referencing scheme, epoch duration, and use of gold-standard autism diagnostic instruments did not moderate study effect sizes. In contrast, resting-state paradigm type (eyes-closed versus eyes-open) moderated absolute beta, relative delta, and relative alpha power effect sizes, and resting-state recording duration moderated relative alpha power effect sizes. These findings support further investigation of resting-state alpha and gamma power as potential biomarkers for autism.

sheet.es: Para mañana: este estudio no cambia nada en el día a día. Un EEG en reposo no sirve hoy para diagnosticar autismo ni para decidir apoyos; si alguien te ofrece un "diagnóstico por EEG", conviene pedir una segunda opinión. Lo útil sigue siendo observar qué necesita tu hijo o tú mismo y ajustar el entorno. Evidencia: un metaanálisis de 41 estudios con 1.246 personas autistas y 1.455 neurotípicas encontró, en promedio, menos actividad alfa relativa y más gamma en personas autistas. Límites: los resultados variaron mucho entre estudios y según cómo se hizo la medición, y son promedios de grupo que no describen a cada persona.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: this study changes nothing in daily life. A resting EEG cannot currently diagnose autism or guide support decisions; if someone offers an "EEG diagnosis", it is reasonable to seek a second opinion. What helps is still noticing what your child, or you, need and adapting the environment. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 41 studies with 1,246 autistic and 1,455 neurotypical people found, on average, lower relative alpha and higher gamma brain activity in autistic people. Limits: results varied widely between studies and depended on how recordings were made, and these are group averages that do not describe any single person.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon: studien förändrar inget i vardagen. Ett vilo-EEG kan i dag inte ställa autismdiagnos eller styra beslut om stöd; om någon erbjuder en "EEG-diagnos" är det rimligt att be om en second opinion. Det som hjälper är fortfarande att se vad ditt barn, eller du själv, behöver och anpassa miljön. Evidens: en metaanalys av 41 studier med 1 246 autistiska och 1 455 neurotypiska personer fann i genomsnitt lägre relativ alfa- och högre gammaaktivitet hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: resultaten varierade mycket mellan studier och berodde på hur mätningen gjordes, och det är gruppgenomsnitt som inte beskriver en enskild person.

title: "It felt like I had an old fashioned telephone ringing in my breasts": An online survey of UK Autistic birthing parents' experiences of infant feeding.
authors: Grant A, Griffiths C, Williams K, Brown A
abstract: Around 3% of people are Autistic. Autistic people communicate differently from non-Autistic people and experience the sensory world differently. There is limited evidence that Autistic people can face additional barriers to breastfeeding. We are an Autistic-led research team that developed an online survey following consultation with the Autistic community. Autistic people from the UK who had been pregnant were eligible to take part in the survey, which focused on the entire maternity journey. A total of 193 people participated, of whom 152 had experiences of infant feeding (137 breastfeeding, 82 formula feeding). Participants were highly motivated to breastfeed, and almost half of those who breastfed found it positive always or most of the time. However, breastfeeding-and in particular the milk let-down reflex-could result in pain and sensory difficulties, including 'feeling odd'. Expressing breastmilk always or most of the time was reported by 10% of breastfeeding participants. The intensity and unpredictability of both breast and formula feeding were challenging to manage. Parents reported that it was easy to understand how to prepare infant formula, but that it could also be a negative and anxiety-inducing experience. Support for breast and formula feeding was often considered inadequate. When parents did access breastfeeding support, this significantly improved a range of breastfeeding experiences. However, participants recommended more tailored support and continuity of carer. To meet the needs of Autistic birthing parents, those providing infant feeding support should receive training on Autism through a neurodiversity-affirming lens, which should be delivered by Autistic people.

sheet.es: Si eres madre o padre autista que alimenta a su bebé, es normal que el pecho, sobre todo la subida de la leche, cause dolor o sensaciones extrañas. Puede ayudar anotar qué sensaciones te molestan, pedir apoyo a la lactancia con antelación y solicitar ver a la misma profesional cada vez. La leche de fórmula también es una opción válida; si te genera ansiedad, planificar rutinas puede dar previsibilidad. Esta encuesta en línea, dirigida por un equipo autista, recogió las experiencias de 193 personas autistas del Reino Unido que habían estado embarazadas; recibir apoyo mejoró claramente la lactancia. Sus límites: participantes autoseleccionadas, solo del Reino Unido y respuestas basadas en recuerdos.
sheet.en: If you are an autistic parent feeding your baby, it is common for breastfeeding, especially the milk let-down, to bring pain or odd sensory feelings. It can help to note which sensations bother you, line up breastfeeding support early, and ask to see the same person each time. Formula feeding is also a valid choice; if preparing it feels stressful, planned routines can add predictability. This online survey, led by an autistic research team, gathered experiences from 193 autistic people in the UK who had been pregnant; getting support clearly improved breastfeeding experiences. Limits: participants chose to take part, all were UK-based, and answers relied on memory.
sheet.sv: Om du är en autistisk förälder som matar ditt barn är det vanligt att amning, särskilt utdrivningsreflexen, ger smärta eller konstiga sinnesupplevelser. Det kan hjälpa att notera vilka förnimmelser som stör dig, ordna amningsstöd tidigt och be om att träffa samma person varje gång. Modersmersättning är också ett giltigt val; om tillredningen känns stressig kan planerade rutiner ge förutsägbarhet. Denna webbenkät, ledd av ett autistiskt forskarteam, samlade erfarenheter från 193 autistiska personer i Storbritannien som varit gravida; stöd förbättrade tydligt amningsupplevelserna. Begränsningar: deltagarna valde själva att delta, alla bodde i Storbritannien och svaren byggde på minnet.

title: The association between social camouflage and mental health among autistic people in Japan and the UK: a cross-cultural study.
authors: Oshima F, Takahashi T, Tamura M, Guan S, Seto M, Hull L, Mandy W, Tsuchiya K, Shimizu E
abstract: Background To examine the relationship between social camouflage and mental health in Japanese autistic adults and make an international comparison with a sample from the UK. Methods This study analysed secondary data of participants with a self-reported diagnosis of autism from Japan (N = 210; 123 men and 87 women) and the UK (N = 305; 181 women, 104, men, and 18 nonbinary). The relationships between the quadratic term of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire and mental health scales, including depression and anxiety, were assessed. Results The UK sample showed linear relationships, whereas the Japanese sample showed significant nonlinear relationships. The quadratic terms of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire slightly explained generalised anxiety (β = .168, p = .007), depression (β = .121, p = .045), and well-being (β = - .127, p = .028). However, they did not explain the association between social anxiety and the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire. Limitations Participants had self-reported diagnoses, and while the autism-spectrum quotient provides a cut-off value for screening, it does not enable confirming diagnoses. Mean scores of the Japanese version of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire were lower as compared to the original CAT-Q, which implies that the social camouflage strategy types used by autistic people in Japan and the UK could differ. The cross-sectional design limits causal inferences. Conclusion In the UK, more social camouflage was associated with poorer mental health scores, whereas too little or too much social camouflage was associated with a low mental health score in Japan. The Japanese population is seemingly less aware of and educated on autistic characteristics and considers 'average' behaviour a good thing. This could influence Japanese autistic people's social camouflage use, differing from that of autistic people in the UK. The differences in the relationship between social camouflage and mental health between Japan and the UK could be associated with national-level divergence regarding the culture of autism.

sheet.es: Pregunta con calma a la persona autista que apoyas cuánto esfuerzo le cuesta «camuflarse» (ocultar rasgos autistas o imitar a otros) y en qué lugares siente que puede relajarse. Ofrecer espacios sin exigencias de aparentar puede cuidar su bienestar, pero el equilibrio adecuado depende de cada persona y de su entorno cultural. Este estudio con encuestas comparó a 210 adultos autistas en Japón y 305 en el Reino Unido: en el Reino Unido, más camuflaje se asoció con más ansiedad y depresión; en Japón, tanto muy poco como mucho camuflaje se asociaron con peor salud mental. Sus límites: diagnósticos autodeclarados, un único momento en el tiempo y no demuestra causa-efecto.
sheet.en: Gently ask the autistic person you support how much effort 'camouflaging' takes (hiding autistic traits or copying others) and where they feel they can relax. Offering spaces with no pressure to perform may protect their wellbeing, but the right balance depends on each person and their cultural setting. This survey study compared 210 autistic adults in Japan and 305 in the UK: in the UK, more camouflaging was linked to more anxiety and depression; in Japan, both very little and a lot of camouflaging were linked to poorer mental health. Its limits: self-reported diagnoses, a single point in time, and it cannot show cause and effect.
sheet.sv: Fråga lugnt den autistiska person du stöttar hur mycket kraft det kostar att ”kamouflera” (dölja autistiska drag eller härma andra) och var hen känner att hen kan slappna av. Att erbjuda miljöer utan krav på att verka som andra kan skydda välmåendet, men rätt balans beror på varje person och kulturell omgivning. Denna enkätstudie jämförde 210 autistiska vuxna i Japan och 305 i Storbritannien: i Storbritannien hängde mer kamouflering ihop med mer ångest och depression; i Japan hängde både väldigt lite och mycket kamouflering ihop med sämre psykisk hälsa. Begränsningar: självrapporterade diagnoser, en enda mättidpunkt och studien kan inte visa orsak och verkan.

title: Estimating life expectancy and years of life lost for autistic people in the UK: a matched cohort study.
authors: O'Nions E, Lewer D, Petersen I, Brown J, Buckman JEJ, Charlton R, Cooper C, El Baou C, Happé F, Manthorpe J, McKechnie DGJ, Richards M, Saunders R, Zanker C, Mandy W, Stott J
abstract: Background Previous research has shown that people who have been diagnosed autistic are more likely to die prematurely than the general population. However, statistics on premature mortality in autistic people have often been misinterpreted. In this study we aimed to estimate the life expectancy and years of life lost experienced by autistic people living in the UK. Methods We studied people in the IQVIA Medical Research Database with an autism diagnosis between January 1, 1989 and January 16, 2019. For each participant diagnosed autistic, we included ten comparison participants without an autism diagnosis, matched by age, sex, and primary care practice. We calculated age- and sex-standardised mortality ratios comparing people diagnosed autistic to the reference group. We used Poisson regression to estimate age-specific mortality rates, and life tables to estimate life expectancy at age 18 and years of life lost. We analysed the data separately by sex, and for people with and without a record of intellectual disability. We discuss the findings in the light of the prevalence of recorded diagnosis of autism in primary care compared to community estimates. Findings From a cohort of nearly 10 million people, we identified 17,130 participants diagnosed autistic without an intellectual disability (matched with 171,300 comparison participants), and 6450 participants diagnosed autistic with an intellectual disability (matched with 64,500 comparison participants). The apparent estimates indicated that people diagnosed with autism but not intellectual disability had 1.71 (95% CI: 1.39-2.11) times the mortality rate of people without these diagnoses. People diagnosed with autism and intellectual disability had 2.83 (95% CI: 2.33-3.43) times the mortality rate of people without these diagnoses. Likewise, the apparent reduction in life expectancy for people diagnosed with autism but not intellectual disability was 6.14 years (95% CI: 2.84-9.07) for men and 6.45 years (95% CI: 1.37-11.58 years) for women. The apparent reduction in life expectancy for people diagnosed with autism and intellectual disability was 7.28 years (95% CI: 3.78-10.27) for men and 14.59 years (95% CI: 9.45-19.02 years) for women. However, these findings are likely to be subject to exposure misclassification biases: very few autistic adults and older-adults have been diagnosed, meaning that we could only study a fraction of the total autistic population. Those who have been diagnosed may well be those with greater support needs and more co-occurring health conditions than autistic people on average. Interpretation The findings indicate that there is a group of autistic people who experience premature mortality, which is of significant concern. There is an urgent need for investigation into the reasons behind this. However, our estimates suggest that the widely reported statistic that autistic people live 16-years less on average is likely incorrect. Nine out of 10 autistic people may have been undiagnosed across the time-period studied. Hence, the results of our study do not generalise to all autistic people. Diagnosed autistic adults, and particularly older adults, are likely those with greater-than-average support needs. Therefore, we may have over-estimated the reduction in life expectancy experienced by autistic people on average. The larger reduction in life expectancy for women diagnosed with autism and intellectual disability vs. men may in part reflect disproportionate underdiagnosis of autism and/or intellectual disability in women. Funding Dunhill Medical Trust, Medical Research Council, National Institute for Health and Care Research, and the Royal College of Psychiatrists.

sheet.es: Si le ha preocupado la cifra de que las personas autistas viven 16 años menos, este estudio sugiere que probablemente es incorrecta. Aun así, algunas personas autistas, sobre todo con discapacidad intelectual, mueren antes de lo esperado. Un paso práctico: mantener revisiones de salud regulares, anotar síntomas físicos que la persona quizá no comunique fácilmente y pedir ajustes razonables en la atención médica. Es un estudio de cohortes emparejado en el Reino Unido con unas 23.600 personas diagnosticadas y 235.800 de comparación, a partir de historias de atención primaria. Su límite: unas nueve de cada diez personas autistas podían no estar diagnosticadas, así que los resultados no se aplican a todas y quizá exageren la reducción.
sheet.en: If the figure that autistic people live 16 years less has worried you, this study suggests it is probably wrong. Still, some autistic people, especially those with an intellectual disability, die earlier than expected. One practical step: keep up regular health checks, note physical symptoms the person may not easily communicate, and ask for reasonable adjustments in healthcare. This was a UK matched cohort study using primary care records, with about 23,600 diagnosed autistic people and 235,800 comparison participants. Its limit: around nine in ten autistic people may have been undiagnosed, so results do not apply to everyone and may overstate the reduction in life expectancy.
sheet.sv: Om siffran att autistiska personer lever 16 år kortare har oroat dig, tyder den här studien på att den troligen är fel. Ändå dör en del autistiska personer, särskilt med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, tidigare än väntat. Ett praktiskt steg: håll fast vid regelbundna hälsokontroller, anteckna kroppsliga symtom som personen kanske inte lätt kan förmedla och be om rimliga anpassningar i vården. Det är en matchad kohortstudie från Storbritannien baserad på journaler från primärvården, med cirka 23 600 diagnostiserade autistiska personer och 235 800 jämförelsepersoner. Begränsning: ungefär nio av tio autistiska personer kan ha saknat diagnos, så resultaten gäller inte alla och kan överskatta minskningen i livslängd.

title: Psychosocial therapeutic approaches for high-functioning autistic adults.
authors: Schweizer T, Endres D, Dziobek I, Tebartz van Elst L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by impaired social interaction and communication skills, repetitive behaviors, restricted interests, and specific sensory processing. Particularly, adults with high-functioning ASD often remain unrecognized, presumably due to their high compensatory skills, but at the cost of high stress, which is often linked to anxiety and depression. This may further explain the significantly high suicide rates and reduced life expectancy among individuals with ASD. Thus, providing support to high-functioning autistic adults in managing core symptoms, as well as co-occurring anxiety and depression, appears essential. To date, only a limited number of evidence-based psychosocial therapeutic options are available, and very few of them have undergone rigorous evaluation in a clinical context. To obtain a comprehensive understanding, a systematic literature search was conducted according to the PRISMA checklist, and only studies demonstrating robust methodological quality were included and discussed in this review article. Although promising initial key factors and methods have been identified, additional evidence-based studies are imperative to ascertain the optimal treatment and evaluate the long-term outcomes for adults with high-functioning ASD.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un adulto autista que parece «arreglárselas bien», presta atención al cansancio oculto: camuflar o compensar puede generar mucho estrés, ansiedad y tristeza. Pregunta con calma cómo está de verdad, valida su esfuerzo y, si lo desea, busquen juntos apoyo psicológico adaptado al autismo, sin intentar cambiar quién es. Esta revisión sistemática reunió estudios de buena calidad sobre terapias psicosociales para adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual y encontró enfoques prometedores. Sus límites: hay pocos estudios rigurosos, faltan datos a largo plazo y aún no se sabe qué apoyo funciona mejor para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult who seems to be 'coping fine', watch for hidden exhaustion: masking and compensating can bring high stress, anxiety and low mood. Gently ask how they are really doing, acknowledge the effort they put in, and, if they want, look together for autism-informed psychological support that respects who they are rather than trying to change them. This systematic review gathered good-quality studies on psychosocial therapies for autistic adults without intellectual disability and found promising approaches. Its limits: few rigorous studies exist, long-term data are missing, and it is not yet clear which support works best for whom.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen som verkar ”klara sig bra”, var uppmärksam på dold utmattning: att maskera och kompensera kan ge mycket stress, ångest och nedstämdhet. Fråga lugnt hur personen egentligen mår, bekräfta ansträngningen och sök gärna tillsammans, om hen vill, psykologiskt stöd anpassat för autism som respekterar vem hen är i stället för att försöka förändra hen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade studier av god kvalitet om psykosociala behandlingar för autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och fann lovande metoder. Begränsningar: få rigorösa studier, inga långtidsdata, och det är ännu oklart vilket stöd som passar vem bäst.

title: Social Validity of Pivotal Response Treatment for Young Autistic Children: Perspectives of Autistic Adults.
authors: Schuck RK, Dwyer P, Baiden KMP, Williams ZJ, Wang M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The social validity of autism behavioral intervention has been questioned. Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Interventions (NDBIs) attempt to address some concerns, but it is unclear whether autistic people consider NDBIs socially valid. Social validity of an NDBI, Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT), was investigated through autistic adults commenting on videos of autistic children receiving PRT. Qualitative coding of responses generated three themes: respect for individuals; assessment of intervention implementation; and socioemotional considerations. Although video brevity limits the scope of the present study's conclusions, participants highlighted PRT components that appeared socially valid (e.g., reinforcing attempts, following the child's lead) and aspects appearing invalid (e.g., overemphasis on spoken language). Therefore, adjustments appear necessary for PRT to be fully acceptable to the autistic community.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija participa en una terapia como PRT, puedes fijarte en lo que adultos autistas valoraron: que se siga el interés del niño, que se celebren los intentos y no solo los aciertos, y que se respete su forma de comunicarse. También señalaron un riesgo: dar demasiado peso al habla oral. Puedes pedir al equipo que acepte gestos, señas o comunicación aumentativa como comunicación válida. Es un estudio cualitativo en el que adultos autistas comentaron vídeos de niños autistas recibiendo PRT. Sus límites: los vídeos eran breves y las opiniones no representan a todas las personas autistas ni a cada niño.
sheet.en: If your child takes part in a therapy like PRT, you can look for what autistic adults valued: following the child's lead, rewarding attempts rather than only correct answers, and respecting how the child communicates. They also flagged a risk: putting too much weight on spoken language. You can ask the team to accept gestures, signs or AAC as real communication. This is a qualitative study in which autistic adults commented on videos of young autistic children receiving PRT. Its limits: the videos were short, and these views do not represent every autistic person or fit every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn deltar i en insats som PRT kan du titta efter det autistiska vuxna uppskattade: att man följer barnets intresse, belönar försök och inte bara rätt svar, och respekterar barnets sätt att kommunicera. De pekade också på en risk: att lägga för stor vikt vid talat språk. Du kan be teamet att räkna gester, tecken eller AKK som fullvärdig kommunikation. Det är en kvalitativ studie där autistiska vuxna kommenterade filmer av unga autistiska barn som fick PRT. Begränsningar: filmerna var korta, och åsikterna representerar inte alla autistiska personer eller passar varje barn.

title: Machine learning classification of autism spectrum disorder based on reciprocity in naturalistic social interactions.
authors: Koehler JC, Dong MS, Bierlich AM, Fischer S, Späth J, Plank IS, Koutsouleris N, Falter-Wagner CM
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder is characterized by impaired social communication and interaction. As a neurodevelopmental disorder typically diagnosed during childhood, diagnosis in adulthood is preceded by a resource-heavy clinical assessment period. The ongoing developments in digital phenotyping give rise to novel opportunities within the screening and diagnostic process. Our aim was to quantify multiple non-verbal social interaction characteristics in autism and build diagnostic classification models independent of clinical ratings. We analyzed videos of naturalistic social interactions in a sample including 28 autistic and 60 non-autistic adults paired in dyads and engaging in two conversational tasks. We used existing open-source computer vision algorithms for objective annotation to extract information based on the synchrony of movement and facial expression. These were subsequently used as features in a support vector machine learning model to predict whether an individual was part of an autistic or non-autistic interaction dyad. The two prediction models based on reciprocal adaptation in facial movements, as well as individual amounts of head and body motion and facial expressiveness showed the highest precision (balanced accuracies: 79.5% and 68.8%, respectively), followed by models based on reciprocal coordination of head (balanced accuracy: 62.1%) and body (balanced accuracy: 56.7%) motion, as well as intrapersonal coordination processes (balanced accuracy: 44.2%). Combinations of these models did not increase overall predictive performance. Our work highlights the distinctive nature of non-verbal behavior in autism and its utility for digital phenotyping-based classification. Future research needs to both explore the performance of different prediction algorithms to reveal underlying mechanisms and interactions, as well as investigate the prospective generalizability and robustness of these algorithms in routine clinical care.

sheet.es: Mañana no necesitas cambiar nada en casa: este estudio no es una herramienta que puedas usar ni un motivo para corregir cómo se mueve o gesticula una persona autista. Muestra que, en una conversación, la forma en que dos personas ajustan mutuamente sus expresiones faciales y movimientos puede ser distinta cuando participa alguien autista; es una diferencia de estilo, no un fallo. Se trata de un estudio que analizó con visión por ordenador vídeos de 28 adultos autistas y 60 no autistas conversando en parejas. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña, la precisión fue moderada y aún no se ha probado en la práctica clínica real.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change at home tomorrow: this study is not a tool you can use, nor a reason to correct how an autistic person moves or uses facial expressions. It suggests that in conversation, the way two people mirror each other's facial expressions and movements can differ when an autistic person takes part; this is a difference in style, not a flaw. The study used computer vision to analyse videos of 28 autistic and 60 non-autistic adults talking in pairs. Its limits: the sample was small, accuracy was moderate, and the method has not yet been tested in real clinical care.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras hemma i morgon: studien är inget verktyg du kan använda och inget skäl att rätta hur en autistisk person rör sig eller använder ansiktsuttryck. Den visar att sättet två personer anpassar sina ansiktsuttryck och rörelser efter varandra i ett samtal kan se annorlunda ut när en autistisk person deltar; det är en skillnad i stil, inte ett fel. Forskarna analyserade med datorseende videor där 28 autistiska och 60 icke-autistiska vuxna samtalade i par. Begränsningar: urvalet var litet, träffsäkerheten måttlig och metoden är ännu inte prövad i vanlig klinisk vård.

title: Parent, child, and family outcomes following Acceptance And Commitment Therapy for parents of autistic children: A randomized controlled trial.
authors: Maughan AL, Lunsky Y, Lake J, Mills JS, Fung K, Steel L, Weiss JA
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Parents of autistic children commonly experience difficulties with their own mental health. This study looked at the effects of a brief group-based Acceptance and Commitment Therapy program, developed for parents of autistic children, youth, and adults. ACT focuses on increasing psychological flexibility, which is the ability to be mindful and accepting of difficult thoughts and experiences, shown to be important for mental wellness. Participants included 54 parents of autistic people, ages 3-34. Parents were randomly divided into two groups: a Treatment group that received the intervention right away, and a Waitlist group that completed the program after the Treatment group completed the trial. All parents filled out questionnaires right before the program began, and at 3, 7, and 17 weeks after randomization. Compared to the group that was waiting to participate in the program, parents in the Treatment group reported greater improvements in depression and family distress, and these improvements were still present 4 months later. Parents in the Treatment group also reported short-term improvements in their positive feelings and personal goals, compared to those waiting. Results showed that ACT may help improve some aspects of mental health for parents of autistic children, but further research is recommended.

sheet.es: Cuidar también de tu propio bienestar cuenta. Un programa breve en grupo de Terapia de Aceptación y Compromiso (ACT), que enseña a notar pensamientos difíciles sin pelear con ellos y a actuar según lo que valoras, podría ayudarte. Mañana puedes probar algo pequeño: pararte un minuto, nombrar lo que sientes y elegir un paso alineado con lo que te importa. Se trata de un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 54 madres y padres de personas autistas de 3 a 34 años; quienes hicieron el programa refirieron menos depresión y menos tensión familiar, aún presentes cuatro meses después. Limitaciones: muestra pequeña, datos autoinformados y comparación solo con lista de espera, así que no funcionará igual para todas las familias.
sheet.en: Looking after your own wellbeing matters too. A brief group-based Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) program, which teaches noticing difficult thoughts without fighting them and acting on what you value, may help. Tomorrow you could try something small: pause for a minute, name what you feel, and choose one step that fits what matters to you. This was a randomized controlled trial with 54 parents of autistic people aged 3 to 34; parents who did the program reported less depression and family distress, still present four months later. Limits: a small sample, self-reported questionnaires, and comparison only with a waitlist, so it will not work the same way for every family.
sheet.sv: Att ta hand om ditt eget mående är också viktigt. Ett kort gruppbaserat program med Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), som lär ut att lägga märke till svåra tankar utan att kämpa emot dem och att handla utifrån det du värdesätter, kan hjälpa. I morgon kan du prova något litet: stanna upp en minut, sätt ord på vad du känner och välj ett steg som passar det som är viktigt för dig. Det här var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 54 föräldrar till autistiska personer i åldern 3 till 34 år; de som gick programmet rapporterade mindre depression och familjestress, även fyra månader senare. Begränsningar: litet urval, självskattning och jämförelse bara med väntelista, så det fungerar inte likadant för alla familjer.

title: Autism spectrum disorder: pathogenesis, biomarker, and intervention therapy.
authors: Zhuang H, Liang Z, Ma G, Qureshi A, Ran X, Feng C, Liu X, Yan X, Shen L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has become a common neurodevelopmental disorder. The heterogeneity of ASD poses great challenges for its research and clinical translation. On the basis of reviewing the heterogeneity of ASD, this review systematically summarized the current status and progress of pathogenesis, diagnostic markers, and interventions for ASD. We provided an overview of the ASD molecular mechanisms identified by multi-omics studies and convergent mechanism in different genetic backgrounds. The comorbidities, mechanisms associated with important physiological and metabolic abnormalities (i.e., inflammation, immunity, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction), and gut microbial disorder in ASD were reviewed. The non-targeted omics and targeting studies of diagnostic markers for ASD were also reviewed. Moreover, we summarized the progress and methods of behavioral and educational interventions, intervention methods related to technological devices, and research on medical interventions and potential drug targets. This review highlighted the application of high-throughput omics methods in ASD research and emphasized the importance of seeking homogeneity from heterogeneity and exploring the convergence of disease mechanisms, biomarkers, and intervention approaches, and proposes that taking into account individuality and commonality may be the key to achieve accurate diagnosis and treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Lo práctico para mañana: cada persona autista es distinta, así que lo que ayuda a una puede no servir a otra. Observa qué necesita tu hijo o hija (sueño, digestión, entorno sensorial, comunicación) y comparte esas observaciones con su equipo de salud. Si te ofrecen pruebas de «biomarcadores» o tratamientos basados en el intestino o el metabolismo, pregunta con calma qué evidencia tienen; todavía no hay pruebas biológicas de uso clínico rutinario. Esta es una revisión narrativa que resume estudios genéticos, biológicos y de apoyos educativos y conductuales, sin participantes propios. Su límite: no evalúa la calidad de cada estudio ni ofrece recomendaciones prácticas concretas.
sheet.en: The practical takeaway: every autistic person is different, so what helps one may not help another. Notice what your child needs (sleep, digestion, sensory environment, communication) and share those observations with their care team. If someone offers 'biomarker' tests or gut- or metabolism-based treatments, calmly ask what evidence supports them; no biological test is yet ready for routine clinical use. This is a narrative review summarising genetic, biological and educational or behavioural support research, with no participants of its own. Its limit: it does not systematically grade the quality of each study and gives no concrete everyday recommendations.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: varje autistisk person är olika, så det som hjälper en behöver inte hjälpa en annan. Lägg märke till vad ditt barn behöver (sömn, mage, sensorisk miljö, kommunikation) och dela dina iakttagelser med vårdteamet. Om någon erbjuder tester av ”biomarkörer” eller behandlingar riktade mot tarm eller ämnesomsättning, fråga lugnt vilket stöd det finns; inget biologiskt test är ännu redo för rutinmässig klinisk användning. Detta är en översiktsartikel som sammanfattar forskning om genetik, biologi och pedagogiskt eller beteendeinriktat stöd, utan egna deltagare. Begränsning: den bedömer inte systematiskt varje studies kvalitet och ger inga konkreta vardagsråd.

title: Participatory translational science of neurodivergence: model for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism research.
authors: Sonuga-Barke EJS, Chandler S, Lukito S, Kakoulidou M, Moore G, Cooper N, Matejko M, Jackson I, Balwani B, Boyens T, Poulton D, Harvey-Nguyen L, Baker S, Pavlopoulou G, RE-STAR team*
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
abstract: Background There are increasing calls for neurodivergent peoples' involvement in research into neurodevelopmental conditions. So far, however, this has tended to be achieved only through membership of external patient and public involvement (PPI) panels. The Regulating Emotions - Strengthening Adolescent Resilience (RE-STAR) programme is building a new participatory model of translational research that places young people with diagnoses of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism at the heart of the research team so that they can contribute to shaping and delivering its research plan. Aims To outline the principles on which the RE-STAR participatory model is based and describe its practical implementation and benefits, especially concerning the central role of members of the Youth Researcher Panel (Y-RPers). Method The model presented is a culmination of a 24-month process during which Y-RPers moved from advisors to co-researchers integrated within RE-STAR. It is shaped by the principles of co-intentionality. The account here was agreed following multiple iterative cycles of collaborative discussion between academic researchers, Y-RPers and other stakeholders. Results Based on our collective reflections we offer general guidance on how to effectively integrate young people with diagnoses of ADHD and/or autism into the core of the translational research process. We also describe the specific theoretical, methodological and analytical benefits of Y-RPer involvement in RE-STAR. Conclusions Although in its infancy, RE-STAR has demonstrated the model's potential to enrich translational science in a way that can change our understanding of the relationship between autism, ADHD and mental health. When appropriately adapted we believe the model can be applied to other types of neurodivergence and/or mental health conditions.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija adolescente es autista o tiene TDAH, su voz puede valer mucho más que una opinión puntual: puede ayudar a decidir qué se investiga y cómo. Mañana puedes preguntarle qué temas le importan y, si le interesa, buscar proyectos que integren a jóvenes como co-investigadores, no solo como asesores. Este artículo describe el modelo RE-STAR, construido durante 24 meses en el que jóvenes autistas y con TDAH pasaron de asesores a miembros del equipo investigador. Es una reflexión colectiva, no un ensayo que mida resultados, y el propio programa reconoce que está en sus inicios.
sheet.en: If your teenager is autistic or has ADHD, their voice can count for much more than a one-off opinion: they can help decide what gets researched and how. Tomorrow you might ask them which topics matter to them and, if they are interested, look for projects that include young people as co-researchers, not just advisors. This paper describes the RE-STAR model, built over 24 months as autistic and ADHD young people moved from advisors to full members of the research team. It is a collective reflection rather than a trial measuring outcomes, and the programme itself says it is still in its early stages.
sheet.sv: Om din tonåring är autistisk eller har adhd kan deras röst betyda mycket mer än en enstaka åsikt: de kan vara med och bestämma vad som forskas på och hur. I morgon kan du fråga vilka frågor som känns viktiga för dem och, om de vill, leta efter projekt där unga är medforskare och inte bara rådgivare. Artikeln beskriver modellen RE-STAR, som växte fram under 24 månader när autistiska unga och unga med adhd gick från rådgivare till fullvärdiga medlemmar i forskargruppen. Det är en gemensam reflektion, inte en studie som mäter effekter, och programmet beskriver sig självt som i ett tidigt skede.

title: Autism-related language preferences of English-speaking individuals across the globe: A mixed methods investigation.
authors: Keating CT, Hickman L, Leung J, Monk R, Montgomery A, Heath H, Sowden S
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Over the past two decades, there have been increasing discussions around which terms should be used to talk about autism. Whilst these discussions have largely revolved around the suitability of identity-first language and person-first language, more recently this debate has broadened to encompass other autism-related terminology (e.g., 'high-functioning'). To date, academic studies have not investigated the language preferences of autistic individuals outside of the United Kingdom or Australia, nor have they compared levels of endorsement across countries. Hence, the current study adopted a mixed-methods approach, employing both quantitative and qualitative techniques, to explore the linguistic preferences of 654 English-speaking autistic adults across the globe. Despite variation in levels of endorsement between countries, we found that the most popular terms were similar-the terms 'Autism', 'Autistic person', 'Is autistic', 'Neurological/Brain Difference', 'Differences', 'Challenges', 'Difficulties', 'Neurotypical people', and 'Neurotypicals' were consistently favored across countries. Despite relative consensus across groups, both our quantitative and qualitative data demonstrate that there is no universally accepted way to talk about autism. Our thematic analysis revealed the reasons underlying participants' preferences, generating six core themes, and illuminated an important guiding principle-to respect personal preferences. These findings have significant implications for informing practice, research and language policy worldwide.

sheet.es: Pregunte a la persona autista cómo prefiere que se hable de su autismo y respete su respuesta. Muchas personas prefieren «persona autista», «es autista», «diferencias» o «dificultades» en lugar de etiquetas como «alto funcionamiento», pero no existe una forma única aceptada por todos. Mañana puede preguntar con calma qué palabras le resultan cómodas y usarlas en casa, en la escuela o con profesionales. Evidencia: estudio de métodos mixtos (encuestas y respuestas abiertas) con 654 adultos autistas angloparlantes de varios países. Límites: solo participaron adultos que hablan inglés y respondieron en línea, por lo que puede no reflejar a niños, a personas que se comunican de otras formas ni a otros idiomas como el español.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person how they prefer autism to be talked about, and respect their answer. Many people prefer "autistic person", "is autistic", "differences" or "difficulties" over labels like "high-functioning", but there is no single way everyone accepts. Tomorrow you could calmly ask which words feel comfortable and use them at home, at school and with professionals. Evidence: a mixed-methods study (survey plus open answers) with 654 English-speaking autistic adults from several countries. Limits: only English-speaking adults who answered online took part, so the findings may not reflect children, people who communicate in other ways, or other languages.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen hur hen vill att man pratar om autism, och respektera svaret. Många föredrar ”autistisk person”, ”är autistisk”, ”skillnader” eller ”svårigheter” framför etiketter som ”högfungerande”, men det finns inget sätt som alla accepterar. I morgon kan du lugnt fråga vilka ord som känns bra och använda dem hemma, i skolan och med vårdpersonal. Evidens: en studie med blandade metoder (enkät och öppna svar) med 654 engelsktalande autistiska vuxna från flera länder. Begränsningar: bara engelsktalande vuxna som svarade digitalt deltog, så resultaten speglar kanske inte barn, personer som kommunicerar på andra sätt eller andra språk, som svenska.

title: The role of anxiety and depression in suicidal thoughts for autistic and non-autistic people: A theory-driven network analysis.
authors: Pelton MK, Crawford H, Bul K, Robertson AE, Adams J, de Beurs D, Rodgers J, Baron-Cohen S, Cassidy S
abstract: Background Autistic adults experience more frequent suicidal thoughts and mental health difficulties than non-autistic adults, but research has yet to explain how these experiences are connected. This study explored how anxiety and depression contribute to suicidal thoughts according to the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide for autistic and non-autistic adults. Methods Participants (autistic adults n = 463, 61% female; non-autistic n = 342, 64% female) completed online measures of anxiety, depression, thwarted belonging, and perceived burdensomeness. Network analysis explored whether: (i) being autistic is a risk marker for suicide; and (ii) pathways to suicidal thoughts are consistent for autistic and non-autistic adults. Results Being autistic connected closely with feeling like an outsider, anxiety, and movement, which connected to suicidal thoughts through somatic experiences, low mood, and burdensomeness. Networks were largely consistent for autistic and non-autistic people, but connections from mood symptoms to somatic and thwarted belonging experiences were absent for autistic adults. Conclusion Autistic people experience more life stressors than non-autistic people leading to reduced coping, low mood, and suicidal thoughts. Promoting belonging, reducing anxiety, and understanding the role of movement could inform suicide prevention for autistic people. Research should accurately capture autistic lived experience when modeling suicide to ensure suicide prevention meets autistic needs.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, cuidar su sensación de pertenencia puede importar mucho: invitarla sin presión, preguntarle cómo se siente en los grupos y reducir fuentes de ansiedad cotidiana. Toma en serio frases como «soy una carga» o «no encajo» y habla de ello con calma; si aparecen pensamientos suicidas, busca apoyo profesional o una línea de crisis. En este estudio, 463 adultos autistas y 342 no autistas respondieron cuestionarios en línea, analizados con redes que vinculan ansiedad, ánimo bajo, sentirse fuera y sentirse una carga. Es un estudio transversal: muestra conexiones, no causas, y quizá no refleje a quienes no participan en encuestas en línea.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, nurturing their sense of belonging may matter a lot: invite without pressure, ask how they feel in groups, and ease everyday sources of anxiety. Take phrases like "I'm a burden" or "I don't fit in" seriously and talk about them calmly; if suicidal thoughts come up, reach out to professional support or a crisis line. In this study, 463 autistic and 342 non-autistic adults completed online questionnaires, analysed as networks linking anxiety, low mood, feeling like an outsider and feeling like a burden. It is a cross-sectional study: it shows connections, not causes, and may not reflect people who don't take part in online surveys.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det betyda mycket att stärka känslan av tillhörighet: bjud in utan press, fråga hur personen trivs i grupper och minska vardagliga källor till oro. Ta uttryck som ”jag är en börda” eller ”jag passar inte in” på allvar och prata lugnt om dem; om självmordstankar dyker upp, sök professionellt stöd eller en stödlinje. I studien svarade 463 autistiska och 342 icke-autistiska vuxna på enkäter online, analyserade som nätverk som kopplar ihop ångest, nedstämdhet, utanförskap och känslan av att vara en börda. Det är en tvärsnittsstudie: den visar samband, inte orsaker, och speglar kanske inte dem som inte svarar på nätenkäter.

title: Functional contribution of the intestinal microbiome in autism spectrum disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and Rett syndrome: a systematic review of pediatric and adult studies.
authors: Caputi V, Hill L, Figueiredo M, Popov J, Hartung E, Margolis KG, Baskaran K, Joharapurkar P, Moshkovich M, Pai N
abstract: Introduction Critical phases of neurodevelopment and gut microbiota diversification occur in early life and both processes are impacted by genetic and environmental factors. Recent studies have shown the presence of gut microbiota alterations in neurodevelopmental disorders. Here we performed a systematic review of alterations of the intestinal microbiota composition and function in pediatric and adult patients affected by autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and Rett syndrome (RETT). Methods We searched selected keywords in the online databases of PubMed, Cochrane, and OVID (January 1980 to December 2021) with secondary review of references of eligible articles. Two reviewers independently performed critical appraisals on the included articles using the Critical Appraisal Skills Program for each study design. Results Our systematic review identified 18, 7, and 3 original articles describing intestinal microbiota profiles in ASD, ADHD, and RETT, respectively. Decreased Firmicutes and increased Bacteroidetes were observed in the gut microbiota of individuals affected by ASD and ADHD. Proinflammatory cytokines, short-chain fatty acids and neurotransmitter levels were altered in ASD and RETT. Constipation and visceral pain were related to changes in the gut microbiota in patients affected by ASD and RETT. Hyperactivity and impulsivity were negatively correlated with Faecalibacterium (phylum Firmicutes) and positively correlated with Bacteroides sp. (phylum Bacteroidetes) in ADHD subjects. Five studies explored microbiota-or diet-targeted interventions in ASD and ADHD. Probiotic treatments with Lactobacillus sp. and fecal microbiota transplantation from healthy donors reduced constipation and ameliorated ASD symptoms in affected children. Perinatal administration of Lactobacillus sp. prevented the onset of Asperger and ADHD symptoms in adolescence. Micronutrient supplementation improved disease symptomatology in ADHD without causing significant changes in microbiota communities' composition. Discussion Several discrepancies were found among the included studies, primarily due to sample size, variations in dietary practices, and a high prevalence of functional gastrointestinal symptoms. Further studies employing longitudinal study designs, larger sample sizes and multi-omics technologies are warranted to identify the functional contribution of the intestinal microbiota in developmental trajectories of the human brain and neurobehavior. Systematic review registration https://clinicaltrials.gov/, CRD42020158734.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene estreñimiento, dolor de barriga o molestias digestivas, merece atención por sí mismo: coméntalo con su equipo de salud y anota patrones de comida, deposiciones y sueño. Las molestias intestinales pueden afectar al bienestar y a la comunicación del malestar. No empieces probióticos, suplementos ni trasplantes por tu cuenta; la evidencia aún es temprana. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 28 estudios en niños y adultos autistas, con TDAH o síndrome de Rett, y encontró diferencias en la microbiota intestinal y su relación con el estreñimiento. Sus límites: estudios pequeños, dietas muy distintas y resultados contradictorios, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has constipation, tummy pain or other gut discomfort, it deserves attention in its own right: raise it with their health team and keep simple notes on food, bowel movements and sleep. Gut discomfort can affect wellbeing and how distress is shown. Don't start probiotics, supplements or transplants on your own; the evidence is still early. This systematic review gathered 28 studies of children and adults who are autistic, have ADHD or Rett syndrome, and found differences in gut bacteria linked with constipation. Its limits: small studies, very different diets and conflicting results, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har förstoppning, ont i magen eller andra magbesvär förtjänar det uppmärksamhet i sig: ta upp det med vårdteamet och för enkla anteckningar om mat, tarmtömning och sömn. Magbesvär kan påverka välmående och hur obehag uttrycks. Börja inte med probiotika, kosttillskott eller transplantationer på egen hand; forskningen är fortfarande tidig. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 28 studier av barn och vuxna som är autistiska, har ADHD eller Retts syndrom, och fann skillnader i tarmfloran kopplade till förstoppning. Begränsningar: små studier, mycket olika kost och motstridiga resultat, så det är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Systematic review and meta-analysis: multimodal functional and anatomical neural alterations in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Guo Z, Tang X, Xiao S, Yan H, Sun S, Yang Z, Huang L, Chen Z, Wang Y
abstract: Background This meta-analysis aimed to explore the most robust findings across numerous existing resting-state functional imaging and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) studies on the functional and structural brain alterations in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Methods A whole-brain voxel-wise meta-analysis was conducted to compare the differences in the intrinsic functional activity and gray matter volume (GMV) between individuals with ASD and typically developing individuals (TDs) using Seed-based d Mapping software. Results A total of 23 functional imaging studies (786 ASD, 710 TDs) and 52 VBM studies (1728 ASD, 1747 TDs) were included. Compared with TDs, individuals with ASD displayed resting-state functional decreases in the left insula (extending to left superior temporal gyrus [STG]), bilateral anterior cingulate cortex/medial prefrontal cortex (ACC/mPFC), left angular gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus, as well as increases in the right supplementary motor area and precuneus. For VBM meta-analysis, individuals with ASD displayed decreased GMV in the ACC/mPFC and left cerebellum, and increased GMV in the left middle temporal gyrus (extending to the left insula and STG), bilateral olfactory cortex, and right precentral gyrus. Further, individuals with ASD displayed decreased resting-state functional activity and increased GMV in the left insula after overlapping the functional and structural differences. Conclusions The present multimodal meta-analysis demonstrated that ASD exhibited similar alterations in both function and structure of the insula and ACC/mPFC, and functional or structural alterations in the default mode network (DMN), primary motor and sensory regions. These findings contribute to further understanding of the pathophysiology of ASD.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada práctico: este estudio describe diferencias cerebrales promedio, no cómo apoyar a tu hijo o a ti mismo. Puede ayudar a entender que vivir los sentidos, el cuerpo y las relaciones de otra manera tiene una base biológica real, no es capricho ni falta de esfuerzo. Sigue guiándote por lo que la persona autista te muestra que necesita. Se trata de un metaanálisis que reunió 75 estudios de imagen cerebral con unas 2.500 personas autistas y un número similar de personas no autistas. Sus límites: son promedios de grupo, los estudios usaron métodos distintos y una resonancia no sirve para diagnosticar ni para describir a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: Nothing practical changes tomorrow morning: this study describes average brain differences, not how to support your child or yourself. It may help to know that experiencing senses, the body and social life differently has a real biological basis; it is not stubbornness or lack of effort. Keep following what the autistic person shows you they need. This is a meta-analysis pooling 75 brain-imaging studies with about 2,500 autistic people and a similar number of non-autistic people. Its limits: the findings are group averages, the studies used varied methods, and a brain scan cannot diagnose or describe any individual person.
sheet.sv: Imorgon förändras inget i praktiken: studien beskriver genomsnittliga skillnader i hjärnan, inte hur du stöttar ditt barn eller dig själv. Den kan hjälpa till att förstå att det har en verklig biologisk grund att uppleva sinnen, kropp och socialt samspel annorlunda; det handlar inte om trots eller bristande vilja. Fortsätt utgå från vad den autistiska personen visar att hen behöver. Det är en metaanalys som samlade 75 hjärnavbildningsstudier med cirka 2 500 autistiska personer och ungefär lika många icke-autistiska. Begränsningar: resultaten är gruppgenomsnitt, studierna använde olika metoder och en hjärnröntgen kan varken ställa diagnos eller beskriva en enskild person.

title: Facilitators and barriers in psychotherapy from the perspective of autistic adults: an enhanced critical incident study.
authors: Jubenville-Wood T, Nicholas DB, Weiss J, Cairns S
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
abstract: Purpose A significant portion of autistic adults experience mental health challenges. Currently, the literature is incomplete when it comes to understanding the needs and preferences of autistic adults who receive therapy. This study elicited the perspectives of autistic adults, focusing on the facilitators, barriers and ways to enhance psychotherapy based on receiving this care for mental health problems. Methods Using the qualitative, exploratory approach of the Enhanced Critical Incident Technique, eight autistic adults took part in interviews. Results A total of 147 critical incidents were extracted from participant interviews and categories salient to therapeutic practice. The study identified key factors influencing therapy, such as trust and respect, practical approaches, client factors, structure of sessions, knowledge about autism, support for individualized needs, access to mental health services, and involvement of family/advocate. These factors were categorized into eight main areas relevant to therapeutic practice. Conclusions Findings from this research reveal that psychotherapy with autistic adults is analogous to performing this work with non-autistic adults, in the sense that this work too entails elements of individually tailored treatment and the reliance on common therapeutic factors. There are also differences in this work that necessitate providers having foundational knowledge about autism. Learning directly from autistic adults' insights may help to improve upon the delivery of mental health care for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta busca terapia psicológica, puede ayudar elegir a alguien que sepa sobre autismo y preguntar desde el principio cómo serán las sesiones. Según los participantes, lo que más ayuda es la confianza y el respeto, enfoques prácticos, una estructura clara, ajustes a las necesidades propias y, si la persona lo desea, la participación de un familiar o defensor. Puedes ofrecer apoyo para preparar preguntas o anotar qué funciona. Se trata de un estudio cualitativo basado en entrevistas a ocho adultos autistas, que describieron 147 situaciones concretas. Al ser pocas personas, sus experiencias no representan a todos los adultos autistas ni a todos los tipos de terapia.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is looking for psychotherapy, it can help to choose a therapist with real knowledge of autism and to ask early on how sessions will be run. Participants said what helps most is trust and respect, practical approaches, clear session structure, adjustments to individual needs and, if the person wants it, involving a family member or advocate. You might offer to help prepare questions or note what works. This is a qualitative study based on interviews with eight autistic adults, who described 147 specific incidents. With so few participants, their experiences cannot represent every autistic adult or every type of therapy.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen söker psykoterapi kan det hjälpa att välja en terapeut med verklig kunskap om autism och att tidigt fråga hur sessionerna kommer att gå till. Deltagarna beskrev att tillit och respekt, praktiska arbetssätt, tydlig struktur, anpassning efter egna behov och, om personen vill, att en anhörig eller företrädare får delta var det som hjälpte mest. Du kan erbjuda stöd med att förbereda frågor eller anteckna vad som fungerar. Det här är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av åtta autistiska vuxna, som beskrev 147 konkreta händelser. Med så få deltagare kan erfarenheterna inte representera alla autistiska vuxna eller alla terapiformer.

title: Perceived misdiagnosis of psychiatric conditions in autistic adults.
authors: Kentrou V, Livingston LA, Grove R, Hoekstra RA, Begeer S
abstract: Background Many autistic people, particularly women, do not receive an autism diagnosis until adulthood, delaying their access to timely support and clinical care. One possible explanation is that autistic traits may initially be misinterpreted as symptoms of other psychiatric conditions, leading some individuals to experience misdiagnosis of other psychiatric conditions prior to their autism diagnosis. However, little is currently known about the frequency and nature of psychiatric misdiagnoses in autistic adults. Methods Using data collected in the first half of 2019 from an ongoing longitudinal register of autistic adults in the Netherlands, this study explored the frequency of perceived psychiatric misdiagnoses before receiving an autism diagnosis. Gender differences were also explored. A sample of 1211 autistic adults (52.6% women, mean age 42.3 years), the majority of whom were Dutch and relatively highly educated, was evaluated. Findings Results showed that 24.6% ( n = 298) of participants reported at least one previous psychiatric diagnosis that was perceived as a misdiagnosis. Personality disorders were the most frequent perceived misdiagnoses, followed by anxiety disorders, mood disorders, chronic fatigue syndrome/burnout-related disorders, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Autistic women (31.7%) reported perceived misdiagnoses more frequently than men (16.7%). Women were specifically more likely than men to report perceived misdiagnoses of personality disorders, anxiety disorders, and mood disorders. Women also reported prior psychiatric diagnoses more often in general (65.8% versus 34.2% in men).
