Within the group of individuals with a prior diagnosis, perceived misdiagnoses were equally likely for men and women. Interpretation One in four autistic adults, and one in three autistic women, reported at least one psychiatric diagnosis, obtained prior to being diagnosed with autism, that was perceived as a misdiagnosis. Inaccurate diagnoses are linked to long diagnostic pathways and delayed recognition of autism. These findings highlight the need for improved training of mental health practitioners, in order to improve their awareness of the presentation of autism in adulthood and of the complex relationship between autism and co-occurring conditions. The current study constitutes a first step towards showing that autistic adults, and particularly women, may be at greater risk of experiencing misdiagnoses. Future studies based on larger, more representative samples are required, to replicate current findings and provide more reliable estimates of the overall frequency of misdiagnoses as well as the frequency of misdiagnoses for specific psychiatric conditions. Funding This study was made possible by funding from the Netherlands Organisation for Health Research and Development (ZonMW), project number 60-63600-98-834.

sheet.es: Si tú o la persona a la que cuidas recibisteis antes otros diagnósticos psiquiátricos que nunca encajaron del todo, puede valer la pena revisarlos con un profesional que conozca el autismo en adultos. Llevar por escrito el historial y las experiencias propias ayuda a esa conversación, sin descartar que algunas condiciones sí coexistan. Este estudio neerlandés preguntó a 1211 adultos autistas: una de cada cuatro personas, y una de cada tres mujeres, sentía que algún diagnóstico previo había sido erróneo, sobre todo trastornos de personalidad, ansiedad o ánimo. Sus límites: se basa en la percepción de los participantes, no en una revisión clínica, y la muestra era mayoritariamente neerlandesa y con estudios altos.
sheet.en: If you or the person you support received earlier psychiatric diagnoses that never quite fit, it may be worth reviewing them with a clinician who understands autism in adulthood. Bringing a written history and your own experiences can help that conversation, while keeping in mind that some conditions genuinely co-occur. This Dutch study surveyed 1,211 autistic adults: one in four, and one in three women, felt at least one earlier diagnosis had been wrong, most often personality, anxiety or mood disorders. Its limits: it relies on participants' own perceptions rather than clinical review, and the sample was mostly Dutch and highly educated.
sheet.sv: Om du eller personen du stöttar tidigare fått psykiatriska diagnoser som aldrig riktigt stämde kan det vara värt att gå igenom dem med en kliniker som känner till autism hos vuxna. En skriftlig sammanställning av historik och egna erfarenheter kan underlätta samtalet, samtidigt som vissa tillstånd faktiskt kan finnas samtidigt. Denna nederländska studie frågade 1 211 autistiska vuxna: var fjärde, och var tredje kvinna, upplevde att minst en tidigare diagnos varit fel, oftast personlighetssyndrom, ångest eller förstämning. Begränsningar: studien bygger på deltagarnas egna upplevelser snarare än klinisk granskning, och urvalet var mest nederländskt och högutbildat.

title: Effects of Physical Activity on Cognition, Behavior, and Motor Skills in Youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review of Intervention Studies.
authors: Suárez-Manzano S, Ruiz-Ariza A, de Loureiro NEM, Martínez-López EJ
abstract: The aim of this paper was to analyze the acute and chronic effects of physical activity (PA) on cognition, behavior, and motor skill in youth with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), taking into account potential confounders. In addition, it was intended to elaborate a guide of educational applications with strategies for PA use. Studies were identified in four databases from January 2010 to June 2023. A total of 19 interventional studies met the inclusion criteria. PA programs ranged from two weeks to one year in duration, with a frequency of one to five sessions per week. More than 58% of the studies showed positive effects of PA on cognition, and 45.5% on behavior and motor skill. Moderate-vigorous PA for 15-30 min has shown acute effects on cognition, general behavior, and stereotypic/repetitive behaviors in youth with ASD. A total of 9 out of 14 studies showed chronic effects on general behavior and stereotypic behaviors, and only 6 on motor skills.

sheet.es: Mañana podrías probar 15-30 minutos de movimiento que tu hijo o hija disfrute (correr, saltar, nadar, bailar) antes de una tarea que requiera concentración, observando con calma cómo le sienta. Elegir actividades que le gusten y respetar sus necesidades sensoriales importa más que la intensidad. Ojo: los movimientos repetitivos pueden ser una forma de autorregulación, no algo que haya que eliminar. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 19 estudios de intervención con niños y jóvenes autistas; más de la mitad encontró mejoras en atención y algunos en conducta y habilidades motoras. Los estudios eran variados y a menudo pequeños, y los resultados no fueron consistentes: no es una regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow you could try 15-30 minutes of movement your child enjoys (running, jumping, swimming, dancing) before a task that needs focus, and calmly notice how it feels for them. Choosing activities they like and respecting sensory needs matters more than intensity. Note that repetitive movements can be a way to self-regulate, not something to eliminate. This systematic review brought together 19 intervention studies with autistic children and young people; over half found benefits for attention, and some for behaviour and motor skills. The studies were varied and often small, and results were inconsistent, so this is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du prova 15–30 minuters rörelse som ditt barn tycker om (springa, hoppa, simma, dansa) före en uppgift som kräver fokus, och lugnt lägga märke till hur det känns för barnet. Att välja aktiviteter barnet gillar och respektera sensoriska behov är viktigare än intensiteten. Tänk på att upprepade rörelser kan vara ett sätt att reglera sig, inte något som måste tas bort. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 19 interventionsstudier med autistiska barn och unga; över hälften fann förbättringar i uppmärksamhet och vissa i beteende och motorik. Studierna var olika och ofta små, och resultaten spretade, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Correlations between sleep problems, core symptoms, and behavioral problems in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kim H, Kim JH, Yi JH, Kim JY, Solmi M, Cortese S, Smith L, Koyanagi A, Shin JI, Cheon KA, Fusar-Poli P
abstract: Children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience various sleep problems. Sleep problems co-occur in a bidirectional relationship with ASD core symptoms and behavioral problems. However, studies on how these three factors are intricately linked to each other are limited. This meta-analysis examined the differential relationship between specific sleep problems, core symptoms, and behavioral problems in this population. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42022339695). We systematically searched the PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus databases from inception to April 27, 2022. Observational studies that reported correlations between measures of sleep problems, ASD core symptoms, or ASD behavioral problems were included, and participants aged 18 years or below were enrolled. The correlation coefficient (r) was assessed as the primary effect metric. Total 22 cross-sectional studies were included, which comprised 2655 participants (mean age = 6.60 years old; mean percentage of boys = 80.64%). We found correlations between total sleep problems and total core symptoms (r 0.293 [95% confidence interval - 0.095 to 0.604]), total sleep problems and total behavioral problems (r 0.429 [0.299-0.544]), and total core symptoms and total behavioral problems (r - 0.050 [- 0.177 to 0.079]) and identified statistically significant correlations between specific components of sleep problems, ASD core symptoms, and ASD behavioral problems. Each specific sleep problem showed a unique association with core symptoms and behavioral problems. Sleep problems in ASD should be explored in detail, and the closely linked core symptoms and behavioral problems should be common therapeutic targets.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista duerme mal, vale la pena mirar el sueño con detalle: cuánto tarda en dormirse, si se despierta de noche, si descansa. Anotar unas semanas cómo duerme y cómo está al día siguiente (irritabilidad, cansancio, crisis) puede ayudarte a ver patrones y a hablar con el equipo de salud. Cuidar el sueño puede facilitar los días. Evidencia: un metaanálisis de 22 estudios con 2655 niños y adolescentes autistas (edad media 6,6 años) encontró que los problemas de sueño se asocian sobre todo con más dificultades de conducta y bienestar. Límites: todos los estudios eran transversales, así que no prueban causa, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If your autistic child sleeps poorly, it is worth looking at sleep in detail: how long it takes to fall asleep, night waking, whether they wake rested. Keeping simple notes for a few weeks on sleep and how the next day goes (irritability, tiredness, meltdowns) can reveal patterns and support conversations with your care team. Supporting sleep may make days easier. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 22 studies with 2,655 autistic children and adolescents (average age 6.6) found sleep problems were linked especially to more behavioural and emotional difficulties. Limits: all studies were cross-sectional, so they cannot show cause, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn sover dåligt kan det vara värt att titta närmare på sömnen: hur lång tid det tar att somna, nattliga uppvaknanden, om barnet vaknar utvilat. Att under några veckor anteckna sömnen och hur nästa dag blir (irritation, trötthet, sammanbrott) kan visa mönster och underlätta samtal med vården. Att stötta sömnen kan göra dagarna lättare. Evidens: en metaanalys av 22 studier med 2 655 autistiska barn och ungdomar (medelålder 6,6 år) fann att sömnproblem särskilt hängde ihop med fler beteendemässiga och känslomässiga svårigheter. Begränsningar: alla studier var tvärsnittsstudier, så de visar inte orsak, och varje person är olik.

title: A meta-ethnography of autistic people's experiences of social camouflaging and its relationship with mental health.
authors: Field SL, Williams MO, Jones CRG, Fox JRE
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Some autistic people describe trying to hide autistic behaviour and seem more neurotypical. Researchers called this 'social camouflaging' and have linked it with mental health difficulties. We used a step-by-step approach to identify research where autistic people talk about social camouflaging to explore the relationship between camouflaging and poor mental health. Thirteen studies were combined. The results describe how society negatively impacts autistic people's mental health, and camouflaging is a way to try and cope with this. Many autistic people find their camouflaging strategies have accidental negative consequences which also affect their mental health. Strategies which seemed 'successful' involved a lot of self-monitoring, were very mentally demanding or were very habitual and seemed to have more of an effect on mental health. This might be important for clinicians who support autistic people with mental health difficulties.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista a la que acompañas parece «estar bien» en público pero llega agotada a casa, puede estar camuflando: ocultando rasgos autistas para encajar. Mañana puedes ofrecer espacios sin exigencias sociales, aceptar sus formas de moverse y comunicarse, y preguntar con calma qué situaciones le cuestan más. Reducir la presión del entorno ayuda más que pedirle que se esfuerce más. Esta meta-etnografía combinó 13 estudios cualitativos donde personas autistas describen el camuflaje como respuesta a una sociedad poco acogedora, con costes para su salud mental. Límites: son experiencias de quienes participaron en esos estudios y no describen a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support seems 'fine' in public but comes home exhausted, they may be camouflaging: hiding autistic traits to fit in. Tomorrow you could offer time without social demands, welcome their ways of moving and communicating, and calmly ask which situations feel hardest. Easing pressure from the environment helps more than asking them to try harder. This meta-ethnography combined 13 qualitative studies in which autistic people describe camouflaging as a way to cope with an unaccommodating society, often at a cost to mental health. Limits: these are the experiences of people who took part in those studies and do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar verkar må bra ute bland folk men kommer hem helt slutkörd kan hen kamouflera: dölja autistiska drag för att passa in. I morgon kan du erbjuda tid utan sociala krav, välkomna hens sätt att röra sig och kommunicera, och lugnt fråga vilka situationer som är svårast. Att minska trycket från omgivningen hjälper mer än att be hen anstränga sig mer. Denna metaetnografi sammanförde 13 kvalitativa studier där autistiska personer beskriver kamouflering som ett sätt att hantera ett oförstående samhälle, ofta med kostnader för den psykiska hälsan. Begränsning: det gäller deltagarnas erfarenheter och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Camouflaging in Autism: Age Effects and Cross-Cultural Validation of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q).
authors: Lundin Remnélius K, Bölte S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Given that camouflaging has been suggested to contribute to delayed diagnosis and mental health problems among autistic people, validated measures of the construct are needed. This study describes the psychometric evaluation of the Swedish adaptation of the self-reported Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q) in autistic (n = 100) and general population (n = 539) samples aged 10 to 83 years. Analyses indicated good-to-excellent internal consistency and test-retest reliability. Construct validity was supported by autistic participants scoring higher than non-autistic, and autistic females scoring higher than autistic males on the measure. Also as expected, camouflaging was associated with theoretically linked traits, including autistic behaviors and depressive symptoms. On the other hand, the factor structure of the original CAT-Q did not provide a good fit in the Swedish data set, and validity issues were found, particularly in children younger than 15 years, warranting further investigation of the construct validity of the scale. Different age trajectories were observed, where camouflaging behaviors decreased during adulthood in non-autistic people but remained at an elevated level among autistic people.

sheet.es: Camuflar rasgos autistas (ocultarlos o imitar a otros para encajar) puede ser agotador y estar ligado a más síntomas depresivos. Mañana puede preguntar con calma dónde la persona siente que debe esforzarse por encajar y ofrecer espacios donde pueda ser ella misma sin explicarse. En la vida adulta, el camuflaje tendió a seguir alto en personas autistas, sobre todo en mujeres. Evidencia: estudio sueco con 100 personas autistas y 539 de la población general, de 10 a 83 años, que evaluó un cuestionario de camuflaje (CAT-Q). Límites: es un estudio transversal y el cuestionario funcionó peor en menores de 15 años, por lo que no sirve para juzgar a cada persona.
sheet.en: Camouflaging autistic traits (hiding them or copying others to fit in) can be exhausting and was linked to more depressive symptoms. Tomorrow you might calmly ask where the person feels they must work hard to fit in, and offer spaces where they can be themselves without explaining. Camouflaging tended to stay high through adulthood in autistic people, especially autistic women. Evidence: a Swedish study of 100 autistic people and 539 people from the general population, aged 10 to 83, testing a camouflaging questionnaire (CAT-Q). Limits: it is a cross-sectional snapshot, and the questionnaire worked less well for children under 15, so it cannot describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Att kamouflera autistiska drag (dölja dem eller härma andra för att passa in) kan vara utmattande och hängde ihop med fler depressiva symtom. I morgon kan du lugnt fråga var personen känner att hen måste anstränga sig för att passa in, och erbjuda platser där hen kan vara sig själv utan att förklara. Kamouflaget tenderade att ligga kvar högt i vuxen ålder hos autistiska personer, särskilt kvinnor. Evidens: en svensk studie med 100 autistiska personer och 539 från allmänbefolkningen, 10–83 år, som prövade ett kamouflageformulär (CAT-Q). Begränsningar: det är en ögonblicksbild, och formuläret fungerade sämre för barn under 15 år, så det beskriver inte varje individ.

title: New advances in the diagnosis and treatment of autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Qin L, Wang H, Ning W, Cui M, Wang Q
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a group of neurodevelopmental disorders that affect individuals' social interactions, communication skills, and behavioral patterns, with significant individual differences and complex etiology. This article reviews the definition and characteristics of ASD, epidemiological profile, early research and diagnostic history, etiological studies, advances in diagnostic methods, therapeutic approaches and intervention strategies, social and educational integration, and future research directions. The highly heritable nature of ASD, the role of environmental factors, genetic-environmental interactions, and the need for individualized, integrated, and technology-driven treatment strategies are emphasized. Also discussed is the interaction of social policy with ASD research and the outlook for future research and treatment, including the promise of precision medicine and emerging biotechnology applications. The paper points out that despite the remarkable progress that has been made, there are still many challenges to the comprehensive understanding and effective treatment of ASD, and interdisciplinary and cross-cultural research and global collaboration are needed to further deepen the understanding of ASD and improve the quality of life of patients.

sheet.es: Lo práctico para mañana: no existe un único camino que sirva a todas las personas autistas. Esta revisión subraya que los apoyos funcionan mejor cuando se adaptan a la persona concreta, combinando distintas áreas (comunicación, escuela, vida diaria) y, a veces, herramientas tecnológicas. Puede ser útil anotar qué ayuda de verdad a tu hijo o a ti, y compartirlo con el equipo profesional. Las novedades como la medicina de precisión todavía son prometedoras, no soluciones disponibles. Se trata de una revisión narrativa de la literatura existente, sin participantes propios. Su límite: resume tendencias generales, no compara apoyos de forma sistemática y usa un lenguaje médico que no recoge la perspectiva de las personas autistas.
sheet.en: The practical takeaway: there is no single path that suits every autistic person. This review stresses that support works best when it is tailored to the individual, bringing together different areas (communication, school, daily life) and sometimes technology-based tools. It can help to note what genuinely works for your child or for you, and share it with the professionals involved. Newer ideas such as precision medicine are still promising, not ready-made solutions. This is a narrative review of existing research, with no participants of its own. Its limit: it summarises broad trends, does not systematically compare supports, and uses medical framing that leaves out autistic people's own perspectives.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: det finns ingen enskild väg som passar alla autistiska personer. Översikten betonar att stöd fungerar bäst när det anpassas till individen och samlar olika områden (kommunikation, skola, vardag), ibland med hjälp av tekniska verktyg. Det kan vara bra att skriva ner vad som verkligen hjälper ditt barn eller dig själv och dela det med de professionella runt er. Nyheter som precisionsmedicin är fortfarande löften, inte färdiga lösningar. Detta är en berättande litteraturöversikt utan egna deltagare. Begränsningen: den sammanfattar breda trender, jämför inte stödinsatser systematiskt och använder ett medicinskt perspektiv där autistiska personers egna röster saknas.

title: Barriers to healthcare and a 'triple empathy problem' may lead to adverse outcomes for autistic adults: A qualitative study.
authors: Shaw SC, Carravallah L, Johnson M, O'Sullivan J, Chown N, Neilson S, Doherty M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people live with more mental and physical health conditions and, on average, die younger than non-autistic people. Despite widespread commitments to tackling these issues, autistic people still report various barriers to accessing healthcare. This article aims to explore the area in depth, from the perspective of autistic people. This research benefits from being led by autistic people, for autistic people - all of the researchers are autistic, and most of us are also medical doctors. Data, in the form of written comments and stories, were collected as part of a large survey. Here, we explored these for common themes and possible deeper meaning within the experiences. People who took part reported a variety of barriers. Here, our article gives voice to their stories, in their own words. Themes included: early barriers; communication mismatch; doubt - in oneself and from doctors; helplessness and fear; and healthcare avoidance and adverse health outcomes. Our findings allowed us to create a model that aimed to understand and explain the reported barriers in the context of the previously known consequences. We also built on wider autism theories to explain our findings in more depth.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un adulto autista al médico, prepara juntos lo esencial por escrito: síntomas, cómo prefiere comunicarse y qué ajustes necesita (luz, esperas, tiempo extra). Pide citas por correo o en línea si llamar es difícil, y tómate en serio sus síntomas aunque los exprese de forma distinta. Evitar la consulta por miedo o por haber sido desestimado es frecuente y puede tener consecuencias graves. Este estudio cualitativo, dirigido por investigadores autistas (la mayoría médicos), analizó comentarios escritos de adultos autistas recogidos en una gran encuesta. Sus límites: refleja experiencias de quienes respondieron, no mide con qué frecuencia ocurren estas barreras ni prueba soluciones concretas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult with healthcare, prepare the essentials together in writing: symptoms, preferred ways to communicate, and helpful adjustments (lighting, waiting, extra time). Book appointments by email or online if phoning is hard, and take their symptoms seriously even when expressed differently. Avoiding care after fear or being dismissed is common and can lead to serious health consequences. This qualitative study, led by autistic researchers (most also doctors), analysed written comments and stories from autistic adults collected in a large survey. Limits: it reflects the experiences of those who responded, does not measure how often these barriers occur, and does not test specific solutions.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen i vården, förbered det viktigaste skriftligt tillsammans: symtom, hur personen helst kommunicerar och vilka anpassningar som hjälper (ljus, väntetid, extra tid). Boka via e-post eller digitalt om telefonsamtal är svåra, och ta symtomen på allvar även när de uttrycks annorlunda. Att undvika vården efter rädsla eller att ha blivit avfärdad är vanligt och kan ge allvarliga följder för hälsan. Denna kvalitativa studie, ledd av autistiska forskare (de flesta även läkare), analyserade skriftliga kommentarer och berättelser från autistiska vuxna i en stor enkät. Begränsningar: den speglar svarandes erfarenheter, mäter inte hur vanliga hindren är och testar inga specifika lösningar.

title: Social motor synchrony in autism spectrum conditions: A systematic review.
authors: Glass D, Yuill N
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract When two people interact, they often fall into sync with one another by moving their bodies at the same time. Some say autistic people are not as good as non-autistic people at moving at the same time as a partner. This has led some researchers to ask whether measuring synchrony might help diagnose autism. We reviewed the research so far to look at differences in Social Motor Synchrony (SMS) (the way we move together) between autistic people and people they interact with. The research suggests that interactions involving an autistic partner (either two autistic partners, or an autistic and non-autistic partner) show lower synchrony than a non-autistic pair. However, we recognised elements in the research so far that may have affected SMS in interactions involving an autistic person. One way SMS may have been affected in research so far might be the way interactions have been set up in the research studies. Few papers studied interactions between two autistic people or looked at synchrony in comfortable environments with autistic-preferred tasks. The studies also do not explain why synchrony might be different, or weaker, in pairs involving autistic partners. We use these limitations to suggest improvements for future research.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o la persona autista con quien convives no se mueve "al compás" contigo (gestos, ritmo, postura), no es un fallo ni algo que corregir. Puedes buscar momentos cómodos y actividades que le gusten, donde la sincronía puede surgir de forma natural, y valorar otras formas de conexión. Esta revisión sistemática reunió estudios sobre la sincronía motora social en interacciones con personas autistas; las parejas con una persona autista mostraron menos sincronía que las parejas no autistas. Sus límites: pocos estudios observaron a dos personas autistas juntas o usaron entornos y tareas preferidos por personas autistas, y no explican por qué aparecen las diferencias.
sheet.en: If your child or the autistic person you live with doesn't move "in step" with you (gestures, rhythm, posture), it isn't a failure or something to fix. Try sharing comfortable moments and activities they enjoy, where moving together may happen naturally, and value other ways of connecting too. This systematic review gathered studies on social motor synchrony in interactions involving autistic people; pairs including an autistic partner showed less synchrony than non-autistic pairs. Its limits: few studies looked at two autistic people together or used comfortable settings and autistic-preferred tasks, and the research doesn't explain why the differences appear.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn eller den autistiska person du lever med inte rör sig "i takt" med dig (gester, rytm, hållning) är det inget misslyckande och inget som behöver rättas till. Försök dela lugna stunder och aktiviteter som personen tycker om, där samspelet kan uppstå naturligt, och värdesätt andra sätt att få kontakt. Denna systematiska översikt samlade studier om social motorisk synkronisering i samspel med autistiska personer; par med en autistisk person visade mindre synkronisering än icke-autistiska par. Begränsningar: få studier undersökte två autistiska personer tillsammans eller använde trygga miljöer och uppgifter som autistiska personer föredrar, och forskningen förklarar inte varför skillnaderna uppstår.

title: Aging Well and Autism: A Narrative Review and Recommendations for Future Research.
authors: Klein CB, Klinger LG
abstract: With autism first recognized in the 1940s, the early cohorts of autistic children are beginning to enter older adulthood. Little is known about the experiences and outcomes of autistic older adults. In the general population, "successful aging" is a dominant model among gerontologists and is used to evaluate outcomes in older adulthood. This narrative review aims to provide a framework for understanding and supporting successful aging in older autistic adults. Using Fernández-Ballesteros' four-domain model of "aging well" we review knowledge on aging and autism by examining outcomes in health and functioning, cognitive and physical functioning, positive affect and control, and social participation and engagement. Findings indicate that outcomes in autistic older adults are generally poor, marked by increased medical conditions, low adaptive skills, elevated risk of cognitive decline, limited physical activity, high rates of mental health conditions, low quality of life, and reduced social or community participation. Patterns of challenges are similar across cognitive abilities and profiles of autistic traits. Challenges and next steps in aging and autism research are identified, and future directions for the field are discussed.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que está envejeciendo, vale la pena planificar con antelación: revisiones médicas regulares, atención a la salud mental, oportunidades de movimiento que disfrute y contactos sociales a su ritmo. Pregúntale qué significa para ella «envejecer bien» y adapta los apoyos a sus preferencias sensoriales y de comunicación. Esta revisión narrativa reunió estudios sobre adultos autistas mayores en salud, cognición, bienestar y participación social, y encontró más problemas médicos, mayor riesgo de deterioro cognitivo y menos participación comunitaria. Sus límites: hay pocos estudios en este grupo, no es una revisión sistemática y los resultados generales no describen a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who is getting older, it helps to plan ahead: regular health check-ups, attention to mental health, ways of moving they actually enjoy, and social contact at their own pace. Ask them what 'aging well' means to them, and shape support around their sensory and communication preferences. This narrative review gathered research on older autistic adults across health, thinking skills, wellbeing and social participation, finding more medical conditions, higher risk of cognitive decline and less community participation. Its limits: research on this group is still scarce, it is not a systematic review, and group-level findings do not describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som blir äldre är det klokt att planera i förväg: regelbundna hälsokontroller, uppmärksamhet på psykisk hälsa, rörelse som personen tycker om och social kontakt i egen takt. Fråga vad ”att åldras väl” betyder för just hen, och anpassa stödet efter sensoriska behov och kommunikationssätt. Denna narrativa översikt samlade forskning om äldre autistiska vuxna kring hälsa, kognition, välmående och delaktighet, och fann fler medicinska tillstånd, högre risk för kognitiv nedgång och mindre delaktighet i samhället. Begränsningar: forskningen om gruppen är fortfarande begränsad, översikten är inte systematisk och resultat på gruppnivå beskriver inte varje person.

title: Affirming Neurodiversity within Applied Behavior Analysis.
authors: Mathur SK, Renz E, Tarbox J
abstract: Criticisms of applied behavior analysis (ABA) from the autistic community continue to intensify and have an appreciable impact on research, practice, and conversation in stakeholder groups. ABA providers aspire to increase quality of life for autistic people; thus, it is imperative for providers to listen with humility and openness to the population we serve. Autistic individuals have unparalleled expertise in their own lives and their own communities. The concerns raised by the autistic community cannot, morally or ethically, be swept aside. There may be a misguided and harmful tendency to devalue concerns due to the speaker's identification as autistic or due to their difference in professional credentials. The concept of neurodiversity can help the ABA field respond to these concerns and collaborate with the largest stakeholders of our services, the autistic clients we serve. This article summarizes some of the key criticisms that autistic advocates raise concerning ABA, discusses the social model of disability and the neurodiversity paradigm, and proposes practical guidance to help the field of ABA integrate neurodiversity and thereby evolve our research and practice. By openly acknowledging the criticisms against ABA and recognizing how we can do better as a field, we believe we can take practical steps towards a profession and a society that more fully embraces inclusion.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija recibe apoyo conductual (ABA), puede preguntar con tranquilidad: ¿los objetivos mejoran su calidad de vida o solo lo hacen parecer menos autista? Pida que se respeten el stimming, la comunicación propia y el derecho a decir no, y que se escuche la opinión de la persona autista. Las críticas de adultos autistas merecen tomarse en serio. Este artículo es una revisión que resume críticas de defensores autistas, el modelo social de la discapacidad y la neurodiversidad, y propone pautas para profesionales. Sus límites: no es un estudio con datos nuevos ni prueba que estas pautas funcionen en la práctica para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your child receives behavioural support (ABA), you can calmly ask: do the goals improve their quality of life, or just make them seem less autistic? Ask that stimming, their own ways of communicating and their right to say no are respected, and that the autistic person's views are heard. Criticism from autistic adults deserves to be taken seriously. This article is a review summarising concerns raised by autistic advocates, the social model of disability and the neurodiversity paradigm, and offering guidance for practitioners. Its limits: it presents no new data and does not show that this guidance works in practice for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn får beteendestöd (ABA) kan du lugnt fråga: förbättrar målen barnets livskvalitet, eller gör de bara att barnet verkar mindre autistiskt? Be om att stimming, barnets egna sätt att kommunicera och rätten att säga nej respekteras, och att den autistiska personens åsikter lyssnas på. Kritik från autistiska vuxna förtjänar att tas på allvar. Artikeln är en översikt som sammanfattar autistiska förespråkares kritik, den sociala modellen för funktionsnedsättning och neurodiversitetsperspektivet, och ger råd till yrkesverksamma. Begränsningar: den bygger inte på nya data och visar inte att råden fungerar i praktiken för varje person.

title: Cognitive and brain morphological deviations in middle-to-old aged autistic adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Wang J, Christensen D, Coombes SA, Wang Z
abstract: Cognitive challenges and brain structure variations are common in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) but are rarely explored in middle-to-old aged autistic adults. Cognitive deficits that overlap between young autistic individuals and elderlies with dementia raise an important question: does compromised cognitive ability and brain structure during early development drive autistic adults to be more vulnerable to pathological aging conditions, or does it protect them from further decline? To answer this question, we have synthesized current theoretical models of aging in ASD and conducted a systematic literature review (Jan 1, 1980 - Feb 29, 2024) and meta-analysis to summarize empirical studies on cognitive and brain deviations in middle-to-old aged autistic adults. We explored findings that support different aging theories in ASD and addressed study limitations and future directions. This review sheds light on the poorly understood consequences of aging question raised by the autism community to pave the way for future studies to identify sensitive and reliable measures that best predict the onset, progression, and prognosis of pathological aging in ASD.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista de mediana o avanzada edad, puede ayudar anotar con calma cambios en memoria, atención u organización a lo largo del tiempo, comparándola consigo misma y no con otras personas. Compartir esas notas con profesionales facilita distinguir rasgos de siempre de cambios nuevos. Este estudio es una revisión sistemática y metaanálisis de investigaciones publicadas entre 1980 y 2024 sobre cognición y estructura cerebral en adultos autistas de mediana y avanzada edad. Sus límites: hay pocos estudios en este grupo de edad y sus resultados apoyan teorías distintas, así que aún no se sabe si el envejecimiento autista conlleva más riesgo, menos o ninguna diferencia.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in mid or later life, it can help to calmly note changes in memory, attention or organisation over time, comparing them with themselves rather than with others. Sharing these notes with professionals makes it easier to tell lifelong traits apart from new changes. This study is a systematic review and meta-analysis of research published between 1980 and 2024 on thinking skills and brain structure in middle-to-older aged autistic adults. Its limits: few studies exist for this age group and the findings support different theories, so it is still unclear whether autistic ageing brings more risk, less, or no difference.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i medelåldern eller äldre kan det hjälpa att lugnt notera förändringar i minne, uppmärksamhet eller planering över tid, och jämföra personen med sig själv snarare än med andra. Att dela anteckningarna med vårdpersonal gör det lättare att skilja livslånga drag från nya förändringar. Studien är en systematisk översikt och metaanalys av forskning publicerad 1980–2024 om tänkande och hjärnans struktur hos autistiska vuxna i medel- och hög ålder. Begränsningar: det finns få studier i denna åldersgrupp och resultaten stöder olika teorier, så det är ännu oklart om åldrande som autistisk innebär högre risk, lägre risk eller ingen skillnad.

title: Mental Health Professionals' Experiences of Adapting Mental Health Interventions for Autistic Adults: A Systematic Review and Thematic Synthesis.
authors: Moore L, Larkin F, Foley S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic adults experience high rates of metal health difficulties and face significant barriers to accessing appropriate mental health care. Empirical research and recent professional guidelines emphasise the importance of modifying standard mental health interventions to best meet the needs of autistic adults. This systematic review explored mental health professionals' experiences of adapting mental health interventions for autistic adults. A systematic search was conducted on CINAHL, PsychINFO, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science in July 2022. The findings from 13 identified studies were synthesised using thematic synthesis. Three major analytical themes were generated, the unique experience of adapting interventions for autistic clients, factors which facilitate successful adaptations, and challenges to adapting interventions. Each theme contained a number of subsequent sub-themes. Professionals view the process of adapting interventions to be a highly individualised process. A range of personal traits, professional experiences, and systemic, service-based issues were identified in facilitating or challenging this individualised process. Further research regarding adaptations with different intervention models and increased supportive resources are required to enable professionals to successfully adapt interventions for autistic adult clients.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta va a empezar terapia psicológica, es razonable pedir al profesional que adapte la intervención: por ejemplo, lenguaje concreto, apoyos visuales, ritmo más pausado, ajustes sensoriales en la consulta o integrar sus intereses. Puede ayudar llevar una lista breve de lo que funciona y lo que no. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 13 estudios sobre experiencias de profesionales de salud mental que adaptan terapias para adultos autistas; describen la adaptación como algo muy individual, facilitado por la experiencia y la formación, y dificultado por limitaciones de los servicios. Su límite: refleja la visión de los profesionales, no la de las personas autistas, y no mide si las adaptaciones mejoran los resultados.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is starting mental health therapy, it is reasonable to ask the professional to adapt it: for example, concrete language, visual supports, a slower pace, sensory adjustments in the room, or building on the person's interests. Bringing a short list of what helps and what does not can make this easier. This systematic review combined 13 studies on mental health professionals' experiences of adapting therapy for autistic adults; they described adaptation as highly individual, helped by experience and training, and held back by service limitations. Its limit: it reflects professionals' views, not autistic people's own, and it does not measure whether adaptations improve outcomes.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen ska börja psykologisk behandling är det rimligt att be behandlaren anpassa den: till exempel konkret språk, visuellt stöd, lugnare tempo, sensoriska justeringar i rummet eller att utgå från personens intressen. Det kan hjälpa att ta med en kort lista över vad som fungerar och inte. Denna systematiska översikt sammanställde 13 studier om hur yrkesverksamma inom psykiatri upplever att anpassa behandling för autistiska vuxna; de beskrev anpassning som mycket individuell, underlättad av erfarenhet och utbildning och försvårad av begränsningar i verksamheten. Begränsning: den speglar behandlarnas perspektiv, inte autistiska personers egna, och mäter inte om anpassningarna ger bättre resultat.

title: Diagnosis of common health conditions among autistic adults in the UK: evidence from a matched cohort study.
authors: O'Nions E, Brown J, Buckman JEJ, Charlton R, Cooper C, El Baou C, Happé F, Hoare S, Lewer D, Manthorpe J, McKechnie DGJ, Richards M, Saunders R, Mandy W, Stott J
abstract: Background Autistic people are disproportionately likely to experience premature mortality and most mental and physical health conditions. We measured the incidence of diagnosed conditions accounting for the most disability-adjusted life years in the UK population according to the Global Burden of Disease study (anxiety, depression, self-harm, harmful alcohol use, substance use, migraine, neck or back pain, and gynaecological conditions). Methods Participants were aged 18 years or above and had an autism diagnosis recorded in the IQVIA Medical Research Database between 01/01/2000 and 16/01/2019. We included 15,675 autistic adults without intellectual disability, 6437 autistic adults with intellectual disability, and a comparison group matched (1:10) by age, sex, and primary care practice. We estimated crude incidences and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) adjusted for age and sex. Findings Autistic adults without intellectual disability experienced a higher incidence (IRR, 95% CI) of self-harm (2.07, 1.79-2.40), anxiety (1.91, 1.76-2.06), depressive disorders (1.79, 1.67-1.92), and substance use (1.24, 1.02-1.51) relative to comparison participants. Incidences of harmful alcohol use (1.01, 0.85-1.18), migraine (0.99, 0.84-1.17), and gynaecological conditions (1.19, 0.95-1.49) did not differ. Neck or back pain incidence was lower (0.88, 0.82-0.95). Autistic adults with intellectual disability experienced a higher incidence of self-harm (2.08, 1.69-2.56). Incidences of anxiety (1.14, 1.00-1.30), gynaecological conditions (1.22, 0.93-1.62), and substance use (1.08, 0.80-1.47) did not differ, and lower incidences were found for depressive disorders (0.73, 0.64-0.83), harmful alcohol use (0.65, 0.50-0.84), migraine (0.55, 0.42-0.74), and neck or back pain (0.49, 0.44-0.55). Interpretation Although our findings cannot be directly compared to previous prevalence studies, they contrast with the higher frequency of mental and physical health conditions in autistic adults reported in studies that directly assessed and/or surveyed autistic people about co-occurring conditions. The present findings may suggest under-diagnosis of common conditions in autistic people, particularly those with intellectual disability. Improved detection should be a clinical and policy priority to reduce health inequalities. Funding Dunhill Medical Trust, Economic and Social Research Council, National Institute of Health and Care Research.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, conviene estar atento a señales de ansiedad, tristeza, autolesiones, dolor o migraña que quizá no se expresan de forma típica, y anotarlas para comentarlas con su médico. Pide revisiones de salud regulares y adaptadas, sobre todo si la persona tiene discapacidad intelectual o se comunica de otras formas. Este estudio de cohortes emparejado revisó historias clínicas de atención primaria del Reino Unido de unos 22.000 adultos autistas y personas no autistas comparables. Su límite: solo mide diagnósticos registrados, no la salud real, por lo que menos diagnósticos podrían reflejar condiciones no detectadas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, keep an eye out for signs of anxiety, low mood, self-harm, pain or migraine that may not show up in typical ways, and jot them down to discuss with their doctor. Ask for regular, adapted health check-ups, especially if the person has an intellectual disability or communicates differently. This matched cohort study reviewed UK primary care records of about 22,000 autistic adults and comparable non-autistic people. Its limit: it only counts recorded diagnoses, not actual health, so fewer diagnoses may reflect conditions that were missed rather than conditions that are absent.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, var uppmärksam på tecken på ångest, nedstämdhet, självskada, smärta eller migrän som kanske inte visar sig på typiska sätt, och skriv ner dem inför läkarbesöket. Be om regelbundna, anpassade hälsokontroller, särskilt om personen har intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller kommunicerar på andra sätt. Denna matchade kohortstudie granskade brittiska journaler från primärvården för cirka 22 000 autistiska vuxna och jämförbara icke-autistiska personer. Begränsning: den mäter bara registrerade diagnoser, inte faktisk hälsa, så färre diagnoser kan betyda att tillstånd har missats snarare än att de saknas.

title: What are the autism research priorities of autistic adults in Scotland?
authors: Cage E, Crompton CJ, Dantas S, Strachan K, Birch R, Robinson M, Morgan-Appel S, MacKenzie-Nash C, Gallagher A, Botha M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Although research has the potential to improve autistic people's lives, lots of funding goes towards research looking at topics which autistic people say has little impact in their everyday lives. Autistic people's lives can be different depending on where they live, and Scotland is a unique country in many ways. We wanted to find out which topics autistic people in Scotland want to see research on. Our team of autistic and non-autistic researchers (including university-based and community researchers) created a survey where 225 autistic adults rated and ranked the importance of possible research topics and shared their thoughts on what topics mattered to them. The five most important topics were mental health and well-being, identifying and diagnosing autistic people, support services (including healthcare and social care), non-autistic people's knowledge and attitudes and issues impacting autistic women. The three least important topics were genetics or biological aspects of autism, autism treatments/interventions and causes of autism. Our findings indicate that autistic people in Scotland want research to focus on things that matter to their day-to-day lives. Also, the Scottish government says they will be listening to autistic people in their latest policy plans, and we believe that considering autistic people's research priorities is an important part of this. Our findings also add to growing calls for change to happen in how and what autism researchers do research on.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista, puedes preguntarle qué le importa en su día a día: salud mental y bienestar, acceso al diagnóstico, servicios de apoyo, actitudes de las personas no autistas y la experiencia de las mujeres autistas. Esas fueron sus prioridades; la genética, las causas y los «tratamientos» quedaron al final. Úsalo para orientar conversaciones con profesionales y servicios hacia lo cotidiano. La evidencia viene de una encuesta diseñada por investigadores autistas y no autistas, respondida por 225 adultos autistas en Escocia. Sus límites: refleja opiniones de quienes participaron en un país concreto y puede no representar a todas las personas autistas, incluidas quienes no usan encuestas escritas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, you can ask what matters in their daily life: mental health and well-being, access to diagnosis, support services, non-autistic people's attitudes and autistic women's experiences. These were the top priorities; genetics, causes and 'treatments' came last. Use this to steer conversations with professionals and services towards everyday needs. The evidence comes from a survey designed by autistic and non-autistic researchers and answered by 225 autistic adults in Scotland. Its limits: it reflects the views of people who took part in one country and may not represent all autistic people, including those who find written surveys inaccessible.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan du fråga vad som spelar roll i vardagen: psykisk hälsa och välmående, tillgång till diagnos, stödinsatser, icke-autistiska personers attityder och autistiska kvinnors erfarenheter. Det var de högsta prioriteringarna; genetik, orsaker och ”behandlingar” hamnade sist. Använd detta för att rikta samtal med vårdpersonal och stödverksamheter mot vardagens behov. Underlaget är en enkät utformad av autistiska och icke-autistiska forskare, besvarad av 225 autistiska vuxna i Skottland. Begränsningar: den speglar deltagarnas åsikter i ett enda land och representerar inte nödvändigtvis alla autistiska personer, till exempel de som har svårt med skriftliga enkäter.

title: The Gestalt of functioning in autism revisited: First revision of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health Core Sets.
authors: Bölte S, Alehagen L, Black MH, Hasslinger J, Wessman E, Lundin Remnélius K, Marschik PB, D'Arcy E, Crowson S, Freeth M, Seidel A, Girdler S, Zander E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people experience individual strengths and challenges as well as barriers and facilitators in their environment. All of these factors contribute to how well autistic people can cope in everyday life, fulfill the roles they choose, and meet their needs. The World Health Organization has developed a system aiming to capture the many factors within people (like how someone thinks and feels) and outside of people (things around a person) that influence their daily living, called the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health can be used for different purposes in research and practice to assess people's situations and plan support measures. Previously in 2019, the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health was adapted to autism by developing so-called Core Sets, which are shorter International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health versions for use in specific conditions. Here, we present the first revisions of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health Core Sets for autism, based on research, development results, and community feedback. Some factors influencing daily life for autistic people were added to the Core Sets, and other factors deemed less relevant were removed. Changes were also made in Core Sets designed for different age groups (0-5, 6-16, and ⩾17 years). Particularly, contents for sensory processing (like smell, touch, seeing, hearing) were added. We recommend these updated Core Sets for future use in autism research and practice. These changes to the Core Sets after 4 years indicate that there should be ongoing updates based on research and experience from practice and involvement of stakeholders.

sheet.es: Cuando hable con profesionales sobre apoyos, puede pedir que miren el día a día completo: fortalezas, dificultades y también el entorno (ruido, luz, actitudes, adaptaciones). La versión revisada de los Core Sets de la CIF para el autismo añade aspectos sensoriales como olfato, tacto, vista y oído, así que puede mencionarlos con confianza. Este trabajo revisó listas de la OMS para tres grupos de edad (0-5, 6-16 y 17 años o más), combinando investigación, resultados de desarrollo y opiniones de la comunidad autista y otras partes interesadas. Su límite: es una herramienta de evaluación y planificación, no prueba qué apoyos funcionan, y seguirá cambiando con el tiempo.
sheet.en: When you talk with professionals about support, you can ask them to look at the whole of daily life: strengths, difficulties, and the environment too (noise, light, attitudes, adjustments). The revised ICF Core Sets for autism now include sensory aspects such as smell, touch, sight and hearing, so you can raise these with confidence. This work updated World Health Organization checklists for three age groups (0-5, 6-16 and 17+), drawing on research, development results and feedback from the autistic community and other stakeholders. Its limit: it is a tool for assessment and planning, it does not show which supports work, and it will keep changing over time.
sheet.sv: När du pratar med professionella om stöd kan du be dem se hela vardagen: styrkor, svårigheter och även miljön (ljud, ljus, bemötande, anpassningar). De reviderade ICF Core Sets för autism innehåller nu sensoriska aspekter som lukt, beröring, syn och hörsel, så du kan med trygghet ta upp dem. Arbetet uppdaterade Världshälsoorganisationens checklistor för tre åldersgrupper (0–5, 6–16 och 17 år och äldre), baserat på forskning, utvecklingsresultat och synpunkter från den autistiska gemenskapen och andra berörda. Begränsning: det är ett verktyg för bedömning och planering, det visar inte vilka stöd som fungerar, och det kommer att fortsätta förändras.

title: How healthcare systems are experienced by autistic adults in the United Kingdom: A meta-ethnography.
authors: Radev S, Freeth M, Thompson AR
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults are more likely to experience mental and physical health difficulties, and yet can find it difficult to get the support that they need. A meta-ethnographic approach was used to review the existing research on autistic adults' experiences of accessing healthcare. Four databases were searched for qualitative and mixed-method studies which looked at the experiences of autistic adults who did not also have a learning disability when using healthcare services in the United Kingdom. Fifteen papers met the criteria to be included, and seven steps were used to analyse the information and develop new themes. Three main themes were identified: Professionals' lack of knowledge can be damaging , Need to reduce processing demands and Adaptation to improve engagement. This review highlights how damaging misdiagnosis, inappropriate treatment, overwhelming environments and systems that are difficult to access can have on the well-being of autistic adults. Limited knowledge and understanding about autism knowledge among healthcare professionals along with autistic adult's own communication and sensory differences indicate that there is a need for improved training developed with autistic adults and adaptations.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar preparar una nota breve con las necesidades sensoriales y de comunicación de la persona autista: pedir una sala tranquila, la primera cita del día, preguntas por escrito o más tiempo para responder. También es razonable explicar al profesional cómo se expresa el dolor o el malestar. Esta revisión meta-etnográfica reunió 15 estudios cualitativos sobre adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual en el Reino Unido, que describieron diagnósticos erróneos, entornos abrumadores y sistemas difíciles de usar. Sus límites: solo incluye el Reino Unido, deja fuera a personas con discapacidad intelectual y las experiencias varían de una persona a otra.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to prepare a short note on the autistic person's sensory and communication needs: asking for a quiet room, the first slot of the day, written questions or extra time to answer. It is also reasonable to explain to the clinician how pain or distress is expressed. This meta-ethnographic review brought together 15 qualitative studies of autistic adults without a learning disability in the UK, who described misdiagnosis, overwhelming environments and hard-to-navigate systems. Its limits: it covers only the UK, leaves out people with learning disabilities, and experiences vary from person to person.
sheet.sv: Inför ett vårdbesök kan det hjälpa att förbereda en kort lapp om den autistiska personens sensoriska behov och kommunikationsbehov: be om ett lugnt rum, dagens första tid, skriftliga frågor eller extra tid att svara. Det är också rimligt att förklara för vårdpersonalen hur smärta eller obehag visar sig. Denna metaetnografiska översikt samlade 15 kvalitativa studier om autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning i Storbritannien, som beskrev feldiagnoser, överväldigande miljöer och svårnavigerade system. Begränsningar: den gäller bara Storbritannien, utesluter personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, och erfarenheter skiljer sig mellan personer.

title: Effects of different exercise interventions on executive function in children with autism spectrum disorder: a network meta-analysis.
authors: Hou Y, Wang Y, Deng J, Song X
abstract: Background A large body of research has identified the positive effects of physical activity on children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). However, the specific benefits of different types of sports on executive functioning in children with ASD remain unclear. The aim of this study was to further analyze the effects of different sports on executive functioning in children with ASD using reticulated meta-analysis and to establish their effectiveness ranking. Methods This study conducted a comprehensive online search in Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, and CNKI databases. It included randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies, and synthesized the data using a Bayesian framework. Results Several relevant studies were included. The results showed that physical activity significantly improved all three dimensions of executive functioning (inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility, and working memory) in children with ASD. The improvement in cognitive flexibility and inhibitory control both reached a medium effect size. However, the improvement in inhibitory control was better than that in cognitive flexibility, while the improvement in working memory did not reach the level of a medium effect. Mini Basketball was effective in improving inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility, but not working memory. Ping Pong was more effective in cognitive flexibility and working memory, but weaker in inhibitory control. Fixed Bicycle was less effective in all three dimensions. Among other interventions, Learning Bicycles, Animal-assisted therapy, and Exergaming performed better in cognitive flexibility. SPARK, Neiyang Gong, and Martial Arts were also effective in improving inhibitory control. However, SPARK and Fixed Bicycle were not significant in improving working memory. Conclusion Physical activity as an intervention can significantly improve the executive function of children with ASD. The intervention effects of different sports on different dimensions of executive function vary. Mini Basketball was outstanding in improving inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility. Ping Pong was effective in improving cognitive flexibility and working memory. Fixed Bicycle was not effective in any dimension.

sheet.es: Moverse de forma activa y con juego puede apoyar habilidades como frenar un impulso, cambiar de plan o recordar instrucciones. Si a tu hijo o hija le atrae, prueba actividades interactivas como minibaloncesto, ping-pong, artes marciales o videojuegos de movimiento; lo más importante es que disfrute y se sienta seguro. Esta es una metaanálisis en red que combinó ensayos controlados y estudios cuasiexperimentales con niños autistas, comparando distintos deportes. Sus límites: los estudios eran pocos y pequeños, variados en calidad, y las clasificaciones entre deportes son estimaciones inciertas; no indica qué actividad sirve a cada niño en concreto.
sheet.en: Active, playful movement may support skills like pausing an impulse, switching plans, and holding instructions in mind. If your child is drawn to it, try interactive activities such as mini basketball, table tennis, martial arts or movement-based video games; what matters most is that they enjoy it and feel safe. This network meta-analysis pooled randomized and quasi-experimental studies of autistic children, comparing different sports. Its limits: the studies were few and small, of mixed quality, and the rankings between sports are uncertain estimates; it cannot tell you which activity will suit your particular child.
sheet.sv: Aktiv och lekfull rörelse kan stödja förmågor som att hejda en impuls, byta plan och komma ihåg instruktioner. Om ditt barn lockas av det, prova interaktiva aktiviteter som minibasket, pingis, kampsport eller rörelsebaserade tv-spel; det viktigaste är att barnet trivs och känner sig tryggt. Denna nätverksmetaanalys sammanställde randomiserade och kvasiexperimentella studier med autistiska barn och jämförde olika idrotter. Begränsningar: studierna var få och små, av varierande kvalitet, och rangordningen mellan idrotterna är osäkra uppskattningar; den säger inte vilken aktivitet som passar just ditt barn.

title: How are Autistic People Involved in the Design of Extended Reality Technologies? A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Newbutt N, Glaser N, Francois MS, Schmidt M, Cobb S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The primary aim of this systematic review is to investigate the inclusion of autistic individuals in the design process of immersive technologies. This study follows the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses standards for systematic literature reviews. To ensure the research questions and subsequent stages of the review incorporate pertinent parameters, the problem, interest, context framework has also been employed. Findings highlight that, while early proponents of immersive technology emphasized the importance of user involvement in design of new technology, immaturity of the technology often limited the implementation of direct user input to the design process. Nonetheless, analysis of the literature published between 2002-2022 identified 20 studies in which substantial influence of autistic individuals and stakeholders was found in the design process of immersive technologies. The roles of autistic individuals varied from active co-designers and co-creators to essential contributors in refining prototypes and providing critical feedback, ensuring the final products align with their needs and preferences. Results underscore the need to align research and design of immersive technologies more closely with the priorities and preferences of autistic individuals. Further is needed regarding actively involving autistic individuals in the design and implementation of immersive technology applications. On this basis, we maintain that more inclusive and effective deployment of immersive technologies is needed in order to ensure that resultant technologies are fit for purpose and address the actual needs of the autistic community.

sheet.es: Si te ofrecen una aplicación o programa de realidad virtual o aumentada para tu hijo o hija autista, puedes preguntar: ¿participaron personas autistas en su diseño? Mañana, pruébalo juntos con calma, observa su comodidad (sonidos, luces, casco) y deja que su opinión guíe si seguir o no. Su experiencia es información valiosa. Esta revisión sistemática analizó estudios publicados entre 2002 y 2022 y encontró solo 20 en los que personas autistas influyeron de verdad en el diseño, como co-diseñadoras o probando prototipos. Limitación: describe cómo se diseñan estas tecnologías, no demuestra que funcionen ni que sirvan para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are offered a virtual or augmented reality app or program for your autistic child, it is fair to ask: were autistic people involved in designing it? Tomorrow, try it together calmly, notice their comfort (sounds, lights, headset) and let their feedback guide whether to continue. Their experience is valuable information. This systematic review looked at studies published between 2002 and 2022 and found only 20 where autistic people had real influence on design, as co-designers or by testing prototypes. Limitation: it describes how these technologies are designed, not whether they work or suit every person.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds en app eller ett program med virtuell eller förstärkt verklighet för ditt autistiska barn kan du fråga: var autistiska personer med och utformade det? I morgon kan ni prova tillsammans i lugn takt, lägga märke till hur bekvämt det känns (ljud, ljus, headset) och låta barnets åsikt avgöra om ni fortsätter. Deras upplevelse är värdefull information. Denna systematiska översikt granskade studier publicerade 2002–2022 och fann bara 20 där autistiska personer verkligen påverkade designen, som meddesigners eller genom att testa prototyper. Begränsning: den beskriver hur tekniken utformas, inte om den fungerar eller passar alla.

title: Association of self-harm and suicidality with psychiatric co-occurring conditions in autistic individuals: a systematic review and pooled analysis.
authors: Kim JH, Lee J, Shim S, Cheon KA
abstract: Background Autistic individuals frequently experience psychiatric co-occurring conditions, but the association with self-harm/suicidality according to these conditions was not yet elucidated. We aimed to summarize the association between self-harm/suicidality and psychiatric co-occurring conditions in autistic people. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews until June 4, 2024 (PROSPERO registration number: CRD42023412860). Observational studies were included that provided information to calculate the odds ratio (OR) regarding the association between self-harm/suicidality and psychiatric co-occurring conditions in autistic individuals. We summarized the identified associations by presenting OR range or meta-analyzing when 7 or more estimates are available. Findings The systematic search found 20 eligible studies with 301,841 participants. Our findings suggested that autistic individuals with any psychiatric disorder ( k = 1; OR 3.55; 95% CI 1.27-9.98), ADHD ( k = 3; OR range: 1.07-1.65), or mood disorder ( k = 1; OR 1.26; 95% CI 1.05-1.51) may be associated with higher odds of self-harm than those without these conditions. We identified potential positive associations between suicidality and the following co-occurring conditions: any psychiatric disorder ( k = 1; OR 11.65; 95% CI 10.68-12.71), psychotic disorder ( k = 4; OR range: 1.95-10.97), mood disorder ( k = 3; OR range: 1.75-9.82), bipolar disorder ( k = 2; OR range: 2.55-4.95), depressive disorder ( k = 10; pooled OR 2.29; 95% CI 1.39-3.77), trauma- and stress-related disorder ( k = 2; OR range: 1.28-10.47), and adjustment disorder ( k = 1; OR 3.52; 95% CI 2.89-4.28). Interpretation We found psychiatric co-occurring conditions that may be associated with higher odds of self-harm/suicidality in autistic individuals. However, our findings should be interpreted with caution considering the limited number of included studies. We suggested that clinicians should remain vigilant for autistic individuals with psychiatric co-occurring conditions for their potentially higher likelihood of self-harm and suicidality. Funding This research was supported by a grant of the R&D project, funded by the National Center for Mental Health (grant number: MHER22A01).

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas también tiene depresión, TDAH, trauma u otra condición de salud mental, conviene prestar más atención a señales de autolesión o pensamientos suicidas. Pregunta con calma y directamente cómo está, en el formato de comunicación que le resulte más cómodo, y pide a su equipo de salud un plan de seguridad. Si hay riesgo inmediato, contacta con emergencias. Es una revisión sistemática de 20 estudios observacionales con más de 300.000 personas autistas. Sus límites: pocos estudios por condición, muestran asociación y no causa, y no predicen lo que le pasará a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support also has depression, ADHD, trauma or another mental health condition, it is worth paying closer attention to signs of self-harm or suicidal thoughts. Ask calmly and directly how they are doing, in whatever communication format suits them best, and ask their care team for a safety plan. If there is immediate risk, contact emergency services. This is a systematic review of 20 observational studies including over 300,000 autistic people. Its limits: few studies per condition, they show association rather than cause, and they cannot predict what will happen to any one person.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar också har depression, ADHD, trauma eller ett annat psykiskt tillstånd är det värt att vara extra uppmärksam på tecken på självskada eller självmordstankar. Fråga lugnt och rakt hur personen mår, på det kommunikationssätt som passar hen bäst, och be vårdteamet om en säkerhetsplan. Vid akut risk, ring 112. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 20 observationsstudier med över 300 000 autistiska personer. Begränsningar: få studier per tillstånd, de visar samband snarare än orsak och kan inte förutsäga vad som händer en enskild person.

title: Camouflaging, not sensory processing or autistic identity, predicts eating disorder symptoms in autistic adults.
authors: Bradley S, Moore F, Duffy F, Clark L, Suratwala T, Knightsmith P, Gillespie-Smith K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract This study aimed to explore the impact of Autistic identity (i.e. feeling like you belong to the Autistic community), sensory profiles (e.g. being over or under responsive to sensations) and camouflaging behaviours (i.e. masking) on eating disorder symptoms in Autistic adults. 180 Autistic people were recruited from the community and NHS. The Autistic people completed online questionnaires measuring Autistic identity, sensory profiles, camouflaging behaviours, autistic traits and eating disorder symptoms. The analysis showed that higher levels of camouflaging behaviour predicted higher levels of eating disorder symptoms. Sensory profiles were related to but did not predict eating disorder symptoms and there was no relationship between level of Autistic identity and eating disorder symptoms. This shows that camouflaging is the most important predictor of eating disorder symptoms in Autistic people, and warrants further exploration.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas se esfuerza mucho por camuflar o «enmascarar» su forma de ser, vale la pena prestar atención también a su relación con la comida. Puedes crear espacios donde no necesite fingir y preguntar con calma cómo se siente al comer, sin juicios. Si notas preocupación por la comida o el cuerpo, busca apoyo profesional que conozca el autismo. Evidencia: estudio con cuestionarios en línea respondidos por 180 adultos autistas del Reino Unido; más camuflaje se asoció con más síntomas de trastornos alimentarios. Límites: es una foto en un momento, basada en autoinforme, y no demuestra que el camuflaje cause estos síntomas ni aplica igual a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support works hard to camouflage or mask who they are, it is worth gently paying attention to their relationship with food as well. You can create spaces where they don't need to pretend and calmly ask how eating feels, without judgement. If you notice worries about food or body, look for professional support that understands autism. Evidence: an online questionnaire study with 180 autistic adults in the UK; more camouflaging was linked to more eating disorder symptoms. Limits: it is a snapshot based on self-report, it does not prove camouflaging causes these symptoms, and it will not apply the same way to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar anstränger sig mycket för att kamouflera eller maskera sig kan det vara klokt att också varsamt uppmärksamma hens förhållande till mat. Skapa gärna miljöer där hen inte behöver låtsas, och fråga lugnt och utan att döma hur det känns att äta. Om du märker oro kring mat eller kropp, sök professionellt stöd med kunskap om autism. Evidens: en enkätstudie online med 180 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien; mer kamouflering hängde ihop med fler symtom på ätstörning. Begränsningar: studien är en ögonblicksbild byggd på självskattning, visar inte att kamouflering orsakar symtomen och gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

title: Neurodivergence, intersectionality, and eating disorders: a lived experience-led narrative review.
authors: Cobbaert L, Millichamp AR, Elwyn R, Silverstein S, Schweizer K, Thomas E, Miskovic-Wheatley J
abstract: Autistic people and those with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder are at a high risk of developing an eating disorder. While there is limited evidence on the relationship between other forms of neurodivergence and eating disorders, research suggests associations between giftedness, intellectual disability, obsessive-compulsive disorder, psychosis, Tourette's syndrome, and disordered eating. Factors underlying disordered eating and/or eating disorder risk for neurodivergent people are multifaceted and complex, encompassing a wide range of intertwined psychosocial, environmental, and biological processes. Moreover, research shows that neurodivergent individuals experience poorer treatment outcomes compared to neurotypical individuals. However, there is a paucity of research in this area overall. More specifically, lived experience-led research remains rare, despite its critical role for improving individualised eating disorder care, as well as mental healthcare more broadly. Indeed, the importance of eating disorder care individuation is increasingly being recognised, particularly within the context of neurodivergence, given the heterogeneous experiences and support needs of neurodivergent people affected by disordered eating and/or eating disorders. Furthermore, despite documented overlaps between various forms of neurodivergence (e.g., co-occurring autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder), research looking at eating disorders in the context of neurodivergence through a transdiagnostic perspective is scarce. This lived experience-led narrative review aims to shed light on the intersectional factors underlying elevated disordered eating and/or eating disorder risk for neurodivergent individuals. First, an overview of prevalence data is provided, followed by a thematic framework identifying factors underlying disordered eating and/or eating disorder risk in relation to neurodivergence. A critical appraisal of current eating disorder research and care is then offered before suggestions for neurodiversity-affirming eating disorder care are made. In this view, this paper offers a foundation for future empirical work in this nascent field of inquiry by providing a lived experience-led, transdiagnostic, and intersectional account of eating disorders in the context of neurodivergence.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista o con TDAH de tu entorno cambia su forma de comer, conviene observarlo con calma y curiosidad, sin juzgar. Las razones pueden ser sensoriales, emocionales, sociales o de rutina, y suelen mezclarse. Pregunta qué le resulta difícil, respeta sus necesidades y busca profesionales que adapten el apoyo a la persona en lugar de aplicar un modelo único. Esta es una revisión narrativa dirigida por personas con experiencia vivida, que reúne estudios previos sobre neurodivergencia y trastornos alimentarios. Sus límites: no aporta datos nuevos, la investigación disponible es escasa y sus propuestas aún deben comprobarse en estudios futuros.
sheet.en: If an autistic person or someone with ADHD in your life changes how they eat, notice it calmly and with curiosity, without judgement. Reasons can be sensory, emotional, social or routine-related, and often overlap. Ask what feels hard, respect their needs, and look for professionals who adapt support to the person rather than using one fixed model. This is a narrative review led by people with lived experience, bringing together earlier research on neurodivergence and eating disorders. Its limits: it offers no new data, the existing research is scarce, and its suggestions still need testing in future studies.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person eller någon med ADHD i din närhet ändrar sitt sätt att äta, lägg märke till det lugnt och nyfiket, utan att döma. Orsakerna kan vara sensoriska, känslomässiga, sociala eller kopplade till rutiner, och de hänger ofta ihop. Fråga vad som känns svårt, respektera personens behov och sök professionella som anpassar stödet efter individen i stället för att följa en enda modell. Detta är en narrativ översikt ledd av personer med egen erfarenhet, som sammanställer tidigare forskning om neurodivergens och ätstörningar. Begränsningar: den ger inga nya data, forskningen är fortfarande begränsad och förslagen behöver prövas i framtida studier.

title: Differential diagnosis of autism, attachment disorders, complex post-traumatic stress disorder and emotionally unstable personality disorder: A Delphi study.
authors: Sarr R, Spain D, Quinton AMG, Happé F, Brewin CR, Radcliffe J, Jowett S, Miles S, González RA, Albert I, Scholwin A, Stirling M, Markham S, Strange S, Rumball F
abstract: Individuals diagnosed with autism, attachment disorders, emotionally unstable personality disorder (EUPD) or complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) can present with similar features. This renders differential and accurate diagnosis of these conditions difficult, leading to diagnostic overshadowing and misdiagnosis.
