The purpose of this study was to explore professionals' perspectives on the differential diagnosis of autism, attachment disorders and CPTSD in young people; and of autism, CPTSD and EUPD in adults. A co-produced three-round Delphi study gathered information through a series of questionnaires from 106 international professionals with expertise in assessing and/or diagnosing at least one of these conditions. To provide specialist guidance and data triangulation, working groups of experts by experience, clinicians and researchers were consulted. Delphi statements were considered to have reached consensus if at least 80% of participants were in agreement. Two hundred and seventy-five Delphi statements reached consensus. Overlapping and differentiating features, methods of assessment, difficulties encountered during differential diagnosis and suggestions for improvements were identified. The findings highlight current practices for differential diagnosis of autism, attachment disorders, CPTSD and EUPD in young people and adults. Areas for future research, clinical and service provision implications, were also identified.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a su cargo ha recibido diagnósticos que no parecen encajar, o está en evaluación, puede pedir con calma que se consideren varias explicaciones: el autismo, el trauma complejo, el apego y el trastorno de personalidad emocionalmente inestable pueden parecerse. Anote ejemplos concretos de la vida diaria, desde la infancia, y compártalos con el equipo; ayudan a distinguir. Este estudio Delphi recogió el acuerdo de 106 profesionales de varios países, con apoyo de personas con experiencia vivida, y logró consenso en 275 afirmaciones sobre rasgos comunes, diferencias y métodos de evaluación. Su límite: refleja opiniones de expertos, no pruebas de que un método funcione mejor, y no sustituye una evaluación individual.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support has diagnoses that don't seem to fit, or is being assessed, you can calmly ask the team to consider several explanations: autism, complex trauma, attachment difficulties and emotionally unstable personality disorder can look alike. Write down concrete everyday examples, including from early childhood, and share them; they help clinicians tell conditions apart. This Delphi study gathered agreement from 106 international professionals, supported by people with lived experience, reaching consensus on 275 statements about shared features, differences and assessment methods. Its limit: it reflects expert opinion, not proof that any method works better, and it cannot replace an individual assessment.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar har diagnoser som inte verkar stämma, eller håller på att utredas, kan du lugnt be teamet att överväga flera förklaringar: autism, komplext trauma, anknytningssvårigheter och emotionellt instabil personlighetsstörning kan likna varandra. Skriv ner konkreta exempel från vardagen, även från tidig barndom, och dela dem; de hjälper att skilja tillstånden åt. Denna Delphi-studie samlade enighet från 106 internationella yrkesverksamma, med stöd av personer med egen erfarenhet, och nådde konsensus om 275 påståenden om gemensamma drag, skillnader och bedömningsmetoder. Begränsning: den speglar expertåsikter, inte bevis för att någon metod fungerar bättre, och ersätter inte en individuell utredning.

title: The global epidemiology and health burden of the autism spectrum: findings from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021.
authors: Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 Autism Spectrum Collaborators
abstract: Background High-quality estimates of the epidemiology of the autism spectrum and the health needs of autistic people are necessary for service planners and resource allocators. Here we present the global prevalence and health burden of autism spectrum disorder from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2021 following improvements to the epidemiological data and burden estimation methods. Methods For GBD 2021, a systematic literature review involving searches in PubMed, Embase, PsycINFO, the Global Health Data Exchange, and consultation with experts identified data on the epidemiology of autism spectrum disorder. Eligible data were used to estimate prevalence via a Bayesian meta-regression tool (DisMod-MR 2.1). Modelled prevalence and disability weights were used to estimate health burden in years lived with disability (YLDs) as the measure of non-fatal health burden and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) as the measure of overall health burden. Data by ethnicity were not available. People with lived experience of autism were involved in the design, preparation, interpretation, and writing of this Article. Findings An estimated 61·8 million (95% uncertainty interval 52·1-72·7) individuals (one in every 127 people) were on the autism spectrum globally in 2021. The global age-standardised prevalence was 788·3 (663·8-927·2) per 100 000 people, equivalent to 1064·7 (898·5-1245·7) autistic males per 100 000 males and 508·1 (424·6-604·3) autistic females per 100 000 females. Autism spectrum disorder accounted for 11·5 million (7·8-16·3) DALYs, equivalent to 147·6 (100·2-208·2) DALYs per 100 000 people (age-standardised) globally. At the super-region level, age-standardised DALY rates ranged from 126·5 (86·0-178·0) per 100 000 people in southeast Asia, east Asia, and Oceania to 204·1 (140·7-284·7) per 100 000 people in the high-income super-region. DALYs were evident across the lifespan, emerging for children younger than age 5 years (169·2 [115·0-237·4] DALYs per 100 000 people) and decreasing with age (163·4 [110·6-229·8] DALYs per 100 000 people younger than 20 years and 137·7 [93·9-194·5] DALYs per 100 000 people aged 20 years and older). Autism spectrum disorder was ranked within the top-ten causes of non-fatal health burden for people younger than 20 years. Interpretation The high prevalence and high rank for non-fatal health burden of autism spectrum disorder in people younger than 20 years underscore the importance of early detection and support to autistic young people and their caregivers globally. Work to improve the precision and global representation of our findings is required, starting with better global coverage of epidemiological data so that geographical variations can be better ascertained. The work presented here can guide future research efforts, and importantly, decisions concerning allocation of health services that better address the needs of all autistic individuals. Funding Queensland Health and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

sheet.es: Su familia no está sola: alrededor de 1 de cada 127 personas en el mundo es autista, y las necesidades de apoyo existen a lo largo de toda la vida, especialmente en la infancia y la juventud. Esto respalda pedir evaluación temprana y apoyos concretos en la escuela y los servicios de salud, también para usted como cuidador. Puede usar estas cifras al solicitar recursos. Se trata de una revisión sistemática mundial (GBD 2021) que combinó estudios de muchos países mediante modelos estadísticos, con participación de personas autistas en su diseño y redacción. Sus límites: faltan datos de muchas regiones y por etnia, y las cifras promedio no describen a ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: Your family is not alone: about 1 in 127 people worldwide is autistic, and support needs exist across the lifespan, especially in childhood and youth. This backs up asking for early assessment and concrete support at school and in health services, including support for you as a caregiver. You can cite these figures when requesting resources. This is a global systematic review (GBD 2021) that combined studies from many countries using statistical modelling, with autistic people involved in its design and writing. Its limits: data are missing for many regions and by ethnicity, and average figures do not describe any individual person.
sheet.sv: Er familj är inte ensam: ungefär 1 av 127 människor i världen är autistisk, och behov av stöd finns genom hela livet, särskilt i barndomen och ungdomen. Det stärker er rätt att be om tidig utredning och konkret stöd i skolan och vården, även stöd till dig som anhörig. Du kan hänvisa till siffrorna när du ansöker om resurser. Det här är en global systematisk översikt (GBD 2021) som sammanställde studier från många länder med statistiska modeller, och autistiska personer deltog i design och skrivande. Begränsningar: data saknas för många regioner och om etnicitet, och genomsnitt beskriver inte en enskild person.

title: A Mixed Method Systematic Review Into the Impact of ED Treatment in Autistic People and Those With High Autistic Traits.
authors: Nimbley E, Sharpe H, Maloney E, Gillespie-Smith K, Tchanturia K, Duffy F
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
abstract: Objective Our understanding of the impact of eating disorders (ED) treatment in Autistic people remains elusive. Research has begun to explore ED treatment outcomes and experiences in this population, however current understandings are poorly integrated. The current review therefore sought to explore the impact of ED treatment on Autistic people and those with higher Autistic traits. Method A convergent, segregated approach was used, independently evaluating quantitative then qualitative studies before integrating findings into a coherent narrative synthesis. Results Autistic people and people with higher Autistic traits report poorer experiences of treatment and may be at increased risk of inpatient admission and prolonged inpatient treatment, possibly explained by difficulties with treatment timeframes and a lack of autism-informed support. Both groups reported similar improvements in ED symptoms and BMI. Higher rates of psychosocial difficulties pre-and post-treatment were reported in those with higher Autistic traits, and emotion-focused interventions were felt to be particularly relevant to Autistic presentations of EDs. Concerns were reported as to how well aligned group-based programs and cognitive-based interventions are for Autistic individuals and those reporting higher Autistic traits. Discussion Future research in diagnosed autism samples is urgently needed to develop a more robust understanding of Autistic outcomes and experiences. Review findings demonstrate the need for increased understanding of ED presentations and the possible need for treatment adaptations, for Autistic people or those with higher Autistic traits.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo recibe tratamiento para un trastorno de la conducta alimentaria, puede ayudar pedir al equipo adaptaciones: plazos más flexibles, apoyo informado sobre el autismo y atención a las emociones, no solo a pensamientos o a sesiones grupales. Los síntomas y el peso pueden mejorar igual que en otras personas, pero la experiencia del tratamiento suele ser peor y puede haber más ingresos o ingresos más largos. Esta revisión sistemática combinó estudios cuantitativos y cualitativos con personas autistas y con rasgos autistas elevados. Su límite: muchos estudios no incluían diagnósticos confirmados de autismo, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support is in eating disorder treatment, it may help to ask the team for adaptations: more flexible timeframes, autism-informed support, and attention to emotions rather than only thought-focused or group-based work. Symptoms and weight can improve just as for others, but the treatment experience is often worse, and there may be more or longer inpatient stays. This systematic review combined quantitative and qualitative studies of autistic people and people with higher autistic traits. Its limit: many studies did not include confirmed autism diagnoses, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar får behandling för en ätstörning kan det hjälpa att be teamet om anpassningar: mer flexibla tidsramar, autismkunnigt stöd och fokus på känslor, inte bara på tankearbete eller gruppbehandling. Symtom och vikt kan förbättras lika mycket som för andra, men upplevelsen av behandlingen är ofta sämre och det kan bli fler eller längre slutenvårdsperioder. Denna systematiska översikt kombinerade kvantitativa och kvalitativa studier med autistiska personer och personer med fler autistiska drag. Begränsning: många studier saknade bekräftade autismdiagnoser, och varje person är unik.

title: The experiences of autistic adults who were previously diagnosed with borderline or emotionally unstable personality disorder: A phenomenological study.
authors: Tamilson B, Eccles JA, Shaw SCK
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people face many barriers to receiving an autism diagnosis. Often, they may be misdiagnosed with borderline personality disorder instead. For our study, we interviewed 10 autistic adults who had previously been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. This helped us to better understand their experiences. They explained how borderline personality disorder is quite stigmatised and may suggest that people are to blame for their differences in behaviour. They found the treatments they had to try for borderline personality disorder to be harmful. For example, these treatments promoted 'masking'. Previous research showed that masking can be harmful for autistic people, linking it to risk of suicide. This diagnosis also led to healthcare professionals neglecting them and discounting their beliefs. Once they were diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, it was hard to access an autism assessment. When they did receive their autism diagnoses, this was much more positive. This diagnosis was validating. It also improved their mental health, as they were no longer expected to mask - their differences were now accepted. They still felt that autism was stigmatised in society. However, this was very different to the stigma around borderline personality disorder. They felt autism stigma was more about their competence as people, whereas borderline personality disorder stigma was about how they were broken and might be harmful to others. This study is important because it allows their stories to be heard by researchers and healthcare professionals alike. Adding their voices helps to humanise them, promoting positive change in mental health services. More research is now needed.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista que conoces recibió antes un diagnóstico de trastorno límite de la personalidad, escucha su historia sin juzgar: muchas personas describen ese diagnóstico como estigmatizante y los tratamientos como presiones para enmascarar. Puedes apoyarla en pedir una evaluación de autismo si lo desea, y validar su forma de ser en casa, sin exigirle que oculte sus diferencias. Este estudio fenomenológico entrevistó a 10 personas adultas autistas que habían sido diagnosticadas con trastorno límite; el diagnóstico de autismo fue para ellas validante y mejoró su bienestar. Es un grupo pequeño y sus experiencias no representan a todas las personas ni sirven para revisar diagnósticos individuales.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support was previously diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, listen to their story without judgement: many describe that label as stigmatising and the treatments as pressure to mask. You can support them in seeking an autism assessment if they want one, and make home a place where their differences don't need hiding. This phenomenological study interviewed 10 autistic adults previously diagnosed with borderline personality disorder; receiving an autism diagnosis felt validating and improved their mental health. It is a small group, so their experiences don't speak for everyone and can't be used to judge any individual diagnosis.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar tidigare fått diagnosen emotionellt instabil personlighetsstörning, lyssna på hens berättelse utan att döma: många beskriver den diagnosen som stigmatiserande och behandlingarna som press att maskera. Du kan stötta hen i att söka en autismutredning om hen vill, och göra hemmet till en plats där olikheter inte behöver döljas. Denna fenomenologiska studie intervjuade 10 autistiska vuxna med en tidigare sådan diagnos; autismdiagnosen kändes bekräftande och förbättrade deras psykiska mående. Gruppen är liten, så erfarenheterna gäller inte alla och kan inte användas för att bedöma en enskild persons diagnos.

title: Effectiveness of Virtual Reality Technology Interventions in Improving the Social Skills of Children and Adolescents With Autism: Systematic Review.
authors: Yang X, Wu J, Ma Y, Yu J, Cao H, Zeng A, Fu R, Tang Y, Ren Z
abstract: Background Virtual reality (VR) technology has shown significant potential in improving the social skills of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Objective This study aimed to systematically review the evidence supporting the effectiveness of VR technology in improving the social skills of children and adolescents with ASD. Methods The search for eligible studies encompassed 4 databases: PubMed, Web of Science, IEEE, and Scopus. Two (XY and JW) researchers independently assessed the extracted studies according to predefined criteria for inclusion and exclusion. These researchers also independently extracted information regarding gathered data on the sources, samples, measurement methods, primary results, and data related to the main results of the studies that met the inclusion criteria. The quality of the studies was further evaluated using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database scale. Results This review analyzed 14 studies on using VR technology interventions to improve social skills in children and adolescents with ASD. Our findings indicate that VR interventions have a positive effect on improving social skills in children and adolescents with ASD. Compared with individuals with low-functioning autism (LFA), those with high-functioning autism (HFA) benefited more from the intervention. The duration and frequency of the intervention may also influence its effectiveness. In addition, immersive VR is more suitable for training complex skills in individuals with HFA. At the same time, nonimmersive VR stands out in terms of lower cost and flexibility, making it more appropriate for basic skill interventions for people with LFA. Finally, while VR technology positively enhances social skills, some studies have reported potential adverse side effects. According to the quality assessment using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database scale, of the 14 studies, 6 (43%) were classified as high quality, 4 (29%) as moderate quality, and 4 (29%) as low quality. Conclusions This systematic review found that VR technology interventions positively impact social skills in children and adolescents with ASD, with particularly significant effects on the enhancement of complex social skills in individuals with HFA. For children and adolescents with LFA, progress was mainly observed in basic skills. Immersive VR interventions are more suitable for the development of complex skills. At the same time, nonimmersive VR, due to its lower cost and greater flexibility, also holds potential for application in specific contexts. However, the use of VR technology may lead to side effects such as dizziness, eye fatigue, and sensory overload, particularly in immersive settings. These potential issues should be carefully addressed in intervention designs to ensure user comfort and safety. Future research should focus on optimizing individualized interventions and further exploring the long-term effects of VR interventions. Trial registration International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols INPLASY202420079U1; https://inplasy.com/inplasy-2024-2-0079/.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija prueba la realidad virtual (RV) para practicar situaciones sociales, empiece con sesiones cortas, observe señales de mareo, cansancio visual o sobrecarga sensorial, y permita parar en cualquier momento. Las pantallas no inmersivas (ordenador o tableta) son más baratas y flexibles y pueden servir para habilidades básicas; los cascos inmersivos parecen más útiles para practicar situaciones complejas. Elija según los intereses, la comodidad y el ritmo de cada persona. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 14 estudios con niños, niñas y adolescentes autistas. Sus límites: estudios pequeños y de calidad desigual (cuatro de baja calidad), poco seguimiento a largo plazo y resultados que no aplican a todo el mundo.
sheet.en: If your child tries virtual reality (VR) to practise social situations, start with short sessions, watch for dizziness, eye strain or sensory overload, and make it easy to stop at any time. Non-immersive VR (computer or tablet) is cheaper and more flexible and may suit basic skills; immersive headsets seemed more helpful for practising complex situations. Choose based on your child's interests, comfort and pace, and treat social practice as a choice, not a requirement. This systematic review pooled 14 studies with autistic children and adolescents. Limits: small studies of mixed quality (four rated low), little long-term follow-up, and results that will not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn provar virtuell verklighet (VR) för att öva sociala situationer, börja med korta pass, var uppmärksam på yrsel, trötta ögon eller sensorisk överbelastning, och gör det lätt att avbryta när som helst. Icke-immersiv VR (dator eller surfplatta) är billigare och mer flexibel och kan passa för grundläggande färdigheter; VR-glasögon verkade mer hjälpsamma för att öva komplexa situationer. Utgå från barnets intressen, bekvämlighet och tempo, och se social träning som ett val, inte ett krav. Denna systematiska översikt sammanställde 14 studier med autistiska barn och ungdomar. Begränsningar: små studier av varierande kvalitet (fyra bedömdes som låg), lite långtidsuppföljning, och resultaten passar inte alla.

title: Autism, ADHD, and Their Traits in Adults with Obesity: A Scoping Review.
authors: Makin L, Meyer A, Zesch E, Mondelli V, Tchanturia K
abstract: Introduction: Autism and ADHD shape behaviours related to food, exercise, and body image, potentially influencing obesity treatment outcomes, as seen in eating disorder research. Resultantly, autistic and ADHD patients with obesity may have distinct experiences and differences compared to non-autistic and non-ADHD patients. This review maps existing literature on autism and ADHD in adults with obesity. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, six databases (Embase, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Scopus) were searched for studies on autism and/or ADHD (diagnosed, probable, or traits) in adults with obesity. Screening and data extraction were conducted twice independently for each record. Results: Thirty-one studies were included, with 1,027,773 participants. Two case reports described successful use of weight loss drugs in autistic people with obesity. Eight prevalence studies suggested ADHD is overrepresented in obesity, regardless of binge eating status. Nineteen studies examined clinical profiles: ADHD patients had lower socioeconomic status, poorer health-related quality of life, increased impulsivity, cognitive inflexibility, and neuroticism, alongside lower agreeableness, conscientiousness, self-directedness, and cooperativeness. ADHD patients also exhibited higher psychopathology, problematic alcohol use, and disordered eating. Eight studies assessed treatment responses, noting poorer outcomes from behavioural programs and obesity pharmacotherapy, but similar post-surgical weight outcomes, despite increased complications. Two studies considered ADHD-specific treatment adaptions, one reporting a successful trial of ADHD medication for weight loss and the other reporting on switching to transdermal ADHD medications after bariatric surgery. Conclusions: This review underscores the need for more research on autism and obesity. For ADHD, findings suggest frequent co-occurrence with obesity, but lived experiences and tailored interventions remain underexplored.

sheet.es: Si una persona adulta autista o con TDAH busca apoyo para el peso, conviene pedir al equipo de salud que adapte el plan: rutinas claras, recordatorios, opciones sensoriales aceptables y menos dependencia de la fuerza de voluntad. Un programa estándar que no funcione no es un fracaso personal. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de 31 estudios con adultos con obesidad; el TDAH aparecía con más frecuencia y los programas conductuales daban peores resultados. Sus límites: casi no hay investigación sobre adultos autistas (solo dos casos) y faltan las experiencias vividas, así que no es una regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic or ADHD adult is seeking support around weight, it is reasonable to ask the health team to adapt the plan: clear routines, reminders, sensory-acceptable food options and less reliance on willpower. If a standard programme does not work, that is not a personal failure. The evidence comes from a scoping review of 31 studies of adults with obesity; ADHD appeared more often, and behavioural programmes gave poorer results. Its limits: there is almost no research on autistic adults (only two case reports), and lived experience is missing, so this is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen eller en vuxen med adhd söker stöd kring vikt är det rimligt att be vårdteamet anpassa upplägget: tydliga rutiner, påminnelser, mat som fungerar sensoriskt och mindre fokus på viljestyrka. Om ett standardprogram inte fungerar är det inget personligt misslyckande. Underlaget är en översikt av 31 studier om vuxna med fetma; adhd var vanligare och beteendeprogram gav sämre resultat. Begränsningar: det finns nästan ingen forskning om autistiska vuxna (bara två fallrapporter) och levda erfarenheter saknas, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: The global prevalence of autism spectrum disorder in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Issac A, Halemani K, Shetty A, Thimmappa L, Vijay VR, Koni K, Mishra P, Kapoor V
journal: Osong public health and research perspectives
abstract: Background The objective of this review was to analyze quantitative data on autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and to increase the accuracy of estimates of the prevalence of ASD. Methods This review, which was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement, included studies conducted from January 2008 to June 2024 on children aged 3 to 18 years that used standardized measurement tools and reported cut-off scores for ASD. The prevalence of ASD was the primary outcome analyzed in this review. The PubMed, Clinical Key, Scopus, Embase, CINAHL, and Web of Science databases were reviewed for relevant studies. The review protocol was registered with PROSPERO and followed the Cochrane collaboration guidelines. Results A total of 66 studies reported on the prevalence of ASD, screening 21,313,061 children worldwide. Among these, 25 studies were conducted in Europe, 22 in Asia, and 13 in America. Additionally, 3 studies each were reported from Africa and Australia. According to a meta-analysis, 0.77% of children globally are diagnosed with ASD, with boys comprising 1.14% of this group. Notably, Australia showed the highest prevalence rate, with an effect size of 2.18, highlighting it as a critical area for public health focus. Conclusion ASD represents a significant global health burden. Early detection, increased awareness among parents, and prompt intervention are crucial for mitigating developmental problems in children later in life. It is essential for health policymakers to acknowledge the prevalence and growing trends of ASD in order to implement effective interventions.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija es autista, no estáis solos: este estudio estima que alrededor de 0,77 % de los niños y niñas del mundo tienen un diagnóstico de autismo, con cifras más altas en chicos (1,14 %). Puede ayudarte a pedir apoyos en la escuela o en servicios locales recordando que el autismo es común y merece recursos. Es un metaanálisis de 66 estudios (2008-2024) con más de 21 millones de niños de 3 a 18 años en varios continentes. Sus límites: pocos estudios de África y Australia, métodos distintos entre países, y las niñas autistas pueden estar infradiagnosticadas; las cifras no describen a ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic, you are not alone: this study estimates that about 0.77% of children worldwide have an autism diagnosis, with higher figures among boys (1.14%). You can use this when asking schools or local services for support, as a reminder that autism is common and deserves resources. It is a meta-analysis of 66 studies (2008–2024) covering over 21 million children aged 3 to 18 across several continents. Its limits: few studies from Africa and Australia, different methods between countries, and autistic girls may be underdiagnosed; the numbers describe populations, not any individual person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt är ni inte ensamma: studien uppskattar att omkring 0,77 % av barn i världen har en autismdiagnos, med högre siffror bland pojkar (1,14 %). Du kan använda detta när du ber skolan eller kommunen om stöd, som en påminnelse om att autism är vanligt och förtjänar resurser. Det är en metaanalys av 66 studier (2008–2024) med över 21 miljoner barn i åldern 3–18 år på flera kontinenter. Begränsningar: få studier från Afrika och Australien, olika metoder mellan länder, och autistiska flickor kan vara underdiagnostiserade; siffrorna beskriver grupper, inte en enskild person.

title: The Social Validity of Behavioral Interventions: Seeking Input from Autistic Adults.
authors: Baiden KMP, Williams ZJ, Schuck RK, Dwyer P, Wang M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Many in the autistic community have expressed concerns regarding the use of behavioral interventions with autistic children, suggesting that these interventions may not be socially valid. Though behavioral interventions have evolved to be more naturalistic and child-centered, little structured research has been done to explicitly seek autistic perspectives on the acceptability of specific components of behavioral interventions. Autistic adults (N = 235) were recruited online to take the Autism Intervention Attitudes Scale (AIAS), a questionnaire designed to gather feedback on common intervention goals and practices. Results indicate that participants find goals and practices that highlight quality of life, safety, and autistic interactions acceptable, while those that focus on normalization based on neurotypical standards are not. An exploratory graph analysis revealed three communities of goals ("uncontroversial goals", "controversial goals", and "social goals"). Comparison between naturalistic and structured intervention components additionally showed that autistic participants favored naturalistic strategies. These findings are in line with known criticisms of behavioral intervention from autistic adults, but also provide more information on the specific ways in which behavioral interventions can be reformed. This information can guide professionals in the development of appropriate goals and decisions around intervention planning.

sheet.es: Al revisar los objetivos de apoyo de tu hijo o hija, pregúntate si buscan calidad de vida, seguridad y bienestar, o si solo buscan que parezca no autista. Puedes pedir al equipo que priorice objetivos como comunicarse, estar a salvo y disfrutar, y que use estrategias naturales, dentro del juego y la rutina diaria, en lugar de ejercicios rígidos. Este estudio preguntó con un cuestionario en línea a 235 adultos autistas qué objetivos y prácticas de intervención conductual consideraban aceptables. Sus límites: participaron solo personas reclutadas por internet que pueden responder un cuestionario, así que no representa todas las voces autistas, y mide opiniones, no resultados de las intervenciones.
sheet.en: When you review your child's support goals, ask whether each one serves quality of life, safety and wellbeing, or mainly aims to make them look less autistic. You can ask the team to prioritise goals like communicating, staying safe and enjoying life, and to use naturalistic strategies woven into play and daily routines rather than rigid drills. This study used an online questionnaire with 235 autistic adults, asking which behavioural intervention goals and practices they found acceptable. Its limits: participants were recruited online and able to complete a questionnaire, so not every autistic voice is represented, and it measures opinions, not intervention outcomes.
sheet.sv: När du går igenom ditt barns stödmål, fråga dig om varje mål handlar om livskvalitet, trygghet och välmående, eller mest om att barnet ska verka mindre autistiskt. Du kan be teamet prioritera mål som att kommunicera, vara säker och trivas, och att använda naturliga strategier i lek och vardagsrutiner i stället för stela övningar. Studien använde ett webbformulär där 235 autistiska vuxna fick bedöma vilka mål och metoder inom beteendeinterventioner de tyckte var acceptabla. Begränsningar: deltagarna rekryterades på nätet och kunde fylla i en enkät, så alla autistiska röster finns inte med, och studien mäter åsikter, inte effekter av insatser.

title: Is There a Bias Towards Males in the Diagnosis of Autism? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Cruz S, Zubizarreta SC, Costa AD, Araújo R, Martinho J, Tubío-Fungueiriño M, Sampaio A, Cruz R, Carracedo A, Fernández-Prieto M
abstract: Autism is more frequently diagnosed in males, with evidence suggesting that females are more likely to be misdiagnosed or underdiagnosed. Possibly, the male/female ratio imbalance relates to phenotypic and camouflaging differences between genders. Here, we performed a comprehensive approach to phenotypic and camouflaging research in autism addressed in two studies. First (Study 1 - Phenotypic Differences in Autism), we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of gender differences in autism phenotype. The electronic datasets Pubmed, Scopus, Web of Science, and PsychInfo were searched. We included 67 articles that compared females and males in autism core symptoms, and in cognitive, socioemotional, and behavioural phenotypes. Autistic males exhibited more severe symptoms and social interaction difficulties on standard clinical measures than females, who, in turn, exhibited more cognitive and behavioural difficulties. Considering the hypothesis of camouflaging possibly underlying these differences, we then conducted a meta-analysis of gender differences in camouflaging (Study 2 - Camouflaging Differences in Autism). The same datasets as the first study were searched. Ten studies were included. Females used more compensation and masking camouflage strategies than males. The results support the argument of a bias in clinical procedures towards males and the importance of considering a 'female autism phenotype'-potentially involving camouflaging-in the diagnostic process.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña o mujer que parece «arreglárselas bien» pero llega agotada a casa, eso merece atención: puede estar camuflando, es decir, ocultando o compensando rasgos autistas con mucho esfuerzo. Anota lo que observas en casa y compártelo con profesionales, pidiendo que consideren cómo el autismo puede presentarse distinto en chicas. Ofrece espacios seguros donde no tenga que fingir. Este metaanálisis reunió 67 estudios sobre diferencias entre géneros y 10 sobre camuflaje, y halló que las mujeres autistas camuflan más y que las herramientas clínicas pueden favorecer el diagnóstico en varones. Límites: los estudios usan categorías binarias de género y métodos variados; no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support a girl or woman who seems to be "coping fine" but comes home exhausted, that deserves attention: she may be camouflaging, hiding or compensating for autistic traits with great effort. Note what you see at home and share it with professionals, asking them to consider how autism can look different in girls. Offer safe spaces where she doesn't have to perform. This meta-analysis pooled 67 studies on gender differences and 10 on camouflaging, finding that autistic females camouflage more and that clinical tools may favour diagnosing males. Limits: studies used binary gender categories and varied methods; the findings don't describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en flicka eller kvinna som verkar "klara sig bra" men kommer hem helt slutkörd är det värt att uppmärksamma: hon kan kamouflera, alltså dölja eller kompensera autistiska drag med stor ansträngning. Anteckna vad du ser hemma och dela det med professionella, och be dem tänka på att autism kan se annorlunda ut hos flickor. Erbjud trygga platser där hon inte behöver spela en roll. Denna metaanalys sammanställde 67 studier om könsskillnader och 10 om kamouflering, och fann att autistiska kvinnor kamouflerar mer och att kliniska verktyg kan gynna diagnos hos pojkar. Begränsningar: studierna använde binära könskategorier och olika metoder; resultaten beskriver inte varje person.

title: Exercise Interventions for Autistic People: An Integrative Review of Evidence from Clinical Trials.
authors: Rivera RA, Robertson MC, McCleery JP
abstract: Purpose of review This review integrates recent findings from randomized controlled clinical trial (RCT) research examining the impacts of physical exercise activities on various aspects and areas of functioning for autistic individuals. Recent findings Recent meta-analytic and clinical trials research indicates physical exercise intervention programs improve social and communication skills for autistic children and adolescents, improve executive functioning skills for autistic children, improve sleep-related behavior for autistic children and adolescents, and may be helpful for improving physical health for autistic children. There is very limited RCT research evidence on exercise intervention approaches or impacts for autistic adults, for autistic girls or women, for autistic people with co-occurring intellectual disability, and for reducing negative emotional symptoms (e.g., anxiety, depression) for any autistic population. The extant clinical trials research provides convincing, consistent evidence for positive impacts of physical exercise programs on multiple areas of functioning for autistic children and adolescents. Additional research is needed to determine and ensure potential impacts of physical exercise activity programs for important autistic sub-populations, including adults.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija le gusta moverse, puede valer la pena incluir actividad física regular que disfrute: nadar, bailar, montar en bici o juegos en el parque. Elige algo que respete su ritmo y sus preferencias sensoriales, sin forzar. Esta revisión integradora reunió ensayos clínicos aleatorizados con niños, niñas y adolescentes autistas, y encontró mejoras en comunicación social, funciones ejecutivas y sueño. Sus límites: casi no hay estudios con personas adultas, chicas y mujeres, personas con discapacidad intelectual, ni sobre ansiedad o depresión, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If your child enjoys moving, it may be worth building in regular physical activity they actually like: swimming, dancing, cycling or playground games. Choose something that respects their pace and sensory preferences, without pressure. This integrative review brought together randomized controlled trials with autistic children and adolescents and found improvements in social communication, executive functioning and sleep. Its limits: there is very little research with autistic adults, girls and women, people with intellectual disability, or on anxiety and depression, so it is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn tycker om att röra sig kan det vara värt att lägga in regelbunden fysisk aktivitet som barnet faktiskt gillar: simning, dans, cykling eller lek på lekplatsen. Välj något som respekterar barnets tempo och sinnesmässiga preferenser, utan press. Denna integrativa översikt samlade randomiserade kontrollerade studier med autistiska barn och ungdomar och fann förbättringar i social kommunikation, exekutiva funktioner och sömn. Begränsningar: det finns mycket lite forskning om autistiska vuxna, flickor och kvinnor, personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller om ångest och depression, så resultaten är ingen regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: A systematic review of ecological momentary assessment in autism research.
authors: Chen Y, Xi Z, Greene T, Mandy W
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Ecological momentary assessment has been increasingly used in autism studies over the last decade to capture and understand autistic people's behaviours, thoughts, feelings and daily experiences. This systematic review synthesised previous autism ecological momentary assessment studies to learn about the feasibility of ecological momentary assessment with autistic people and derive ideas to optimise the applicability of ecological momentary assessment in autism studies. Five databases (MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, EMBASE and CINAHL) were searched, covering the time between January 1990 and October 2024, for studies using ecological momentary assessment with autistic participants. We identified 32 studies with 930 autistic participants. These studies supported the acceptability and feasibility of ecological momentary assessment with young and middle-aged autistic adults with average or above-average intelligence and language skills. Previous researchers and autistic participants in the reviewed literature suggested considering adaptations in the design of sampling schedules, ecological momentary assessment questionnaires and the implementation of incentive strategies, to improve the applicability of ecological momentary assessment with the autistic population. Future ecological momentary assessment studies could address the limitations in the extant literature, for example, lack of evidence from youth and older autistic people and a wider range of study topics.Lay abstractEcological momentary assessments assess people's in-the-moment thoughts and behaviours in their daily lives in natural environments. The number of ecological momentary assessment studies with autistic people has increased over the last decade. For the first time, this review (1) summarises how well ecological momentary assessment works for allowing autistic people to describe and express their thoughts, emotions and experiences, and (2) provides suggestions for the design of ecological momentary assessment to make this research method more accessible to future autistic participants. In total, we synthesised participation experiences from 930 autistic people. Overall, ecological momentary assessment is generally acceptable for autistic adults aged from 18 to 60 and with average or above-average intelligence and language. We also identified several issues in the ecological momentary assessment procedure and suggested researchers consider these when designing future ecological momentary assessment studies with autistic people. The findings of this review provide evidence that ecological momentary assessment can be used to investigate many different questions with autistic people and suggest a wider application of ecological momentary assessment in future studies with autistic people.

sheet.es: Si quieres entender cómo vive el día una persona autista, preguntas breves en el momento (por ejemplo, un mensaje corto en el móvil varias veces al día sobre cómo se siente) pueden funcionar bien, sobre todo si se adaptan: horarios previsibles, preguntas claras y pocas, y libertad para no responder. Pregunta a la persona qué formato le resulta cómodo. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 32 estudios con 930 participantes autistas que usaron este método de registro diario. Su límite: casi todos eran adultos de 18 a 60 años con buen lenguaje verbal, así que no sabemos si sirve igual para niños, jóvenes, personas mayores o quienes se comunican de otras formas.
sheet.en: If you want to understand how an autistic person's day really feels, short in-the-moment check-ins (for example, a brief phone prompt a few times a day asking how they feel) can work well, especially when adapted: predictable timing, few and clear questions, and freedom to skip. Ask the person which format feels comfortable to them. This systematic review brought together 32 studies with 930 autistic participants who used this kind of daily-life tracking. Its limit: most participants were adults aged 18 to 60 with strong spoken language, so we don't know if it works the same for children, teens, older people or those who communicate in other ways.
sheet.sv: Om du vill förstå hur en autistisk persons vardag verkligen känns kan korta avstämningar i stunden (till exempel en kort fråga i mobilen några gånger per dag om hur hen mår) fungera bra, särskilt när de anpassas: förutsägbara tider, få och tydliga frågor och frihet att hoppa över. Fråga personen vilket format som känns bekvämt. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 32 studier med 930 autistiska deltagare som använde den här typen av vardagsregistrering. Begränsningen: de flesta var vuxna mellan 18 och 60 år med starkt talat språk, så vi vet inte om det fungerar likadant för barn, unga, äldre eller personer som kommunicerar på andra sätt.

title: 'Nothing About Us, Without Us': Research Priorities for Autistic Girls, Women and Gender Diverse People in Australia.
authors: Grove R, Clapham H, Moodie T, Gurrin S, Hall G
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic girls, women and gender diverse people have specific needs that are underrepresented in research. Research priorities are often established by funding bodies, researchers, parents, carers and health professionals and may not meet the needs of the diverse Autistic community. This co-produced project aimed to identify what research would benefit the lives of Autistic girls, women and gender diverse people in Australia. We interviewed 47 Autistic girls, women and gender diverse people aged seven and above and obtained feedback from an additional 411 Autistic people through an online survey. Autistic young people identified six key research priorities including (1) better understanding and support at school, (2) understanding our experiences, strengths and challenges, (3) autism specific mental health support, (4) Autistic friendships and relationships, (5) experiences of gender diversity and (6) accommodations to make life easier for us. Eight key research priority areas were identified by Autistic adults including (1) understanding and supporting specific needs in adulthood, (2) experiences of trauma, abuse and sexual violence, (3) supporting mental health and wellbeing, (4) addressing barriers in healthcare, (5) understanding and supporting physical health needs, (6) addressing barriers in education and the workplace, (7) understanding the role of society, embracing neurodiversity and the importance of Autistic identity and (8) co-designing research and supports with Autistic people. We provide a discussion around the importance of focusing on these research priority areas in future autism research in Australia.

sheet.es: Pregunte directamente a su hija, o a la persona autista que acompaña, qué le ayudaría más: en la escuela, con amistades, salud mental o ajustes en casa. Las propias personas autistas señalaron como prioridades el apoyo escolar, la salud mental adaptada, las relaciones, la diversidad de género, la atención sanitaria accesible y la seguridad frente a abusos. Este estudio coproducido entrevistó a 47 niñas, mujeres y personas de género diverso autistas (desde los siete años) y recogió la opinión de 411 personas autistas más en una encuesta en Australia. Sus límites: describe prioridades de investigación, no prueba qué apoyos funcionan, y refleja sobre todo a quienes pudieron participar.
sheet.en: Ask your daughter, or the autistic person you support, directly what would help most: at school, with friendships, mental health or everyday adjustments at home. Autistic people themselves named priorities such as school support, autism-informed mental health care, relationships, gender diversity, accessible healthcare and safety from abuse. This co-produced study interviewed 47 autistic girls, women and gender diverse people (aged seven and up) and gathered feedback from 411 more autistic people through an online survey in Australia. Its limits: it describes research priorities rather than testing which supports work, and mainly reflects those able to take part.
sheet.sv: Fråga din dotter, eller den autistiska person du stöttar, direkt vad som skulle hjälpa mest: i skolan, med vänskap, psykisk hälsa eller vardagliga anpassningar hemma. Autistiska personer själva lyfte prioriteringar som stöd i skolan, autismanpassad psykiatrisk vård, relationer, könsmångfald, tillgänglig sjukvård och skydd mot övergrepp. Denna samskapade studie intervjuade 47 autistiska flickor, kvinnor och icke-binära eller könsdiversa personer (från sju år) och samlade synpunkter från ytterligare 411 autistiska personer via en webbenkät i Australien. Begränsningar: den beskriver forskningsprioriteringar, testar inte vilket stöd som fungerar, och speglar främst dem som kunde delta.

title: Understanding the Autistic Experience of Restrictive Eating Disorders-A Systematic Review and Qualitative-Synthesis.
authors: Loomes R, Chivers K, Georgeaux-Healy C, Mandy W, Jewell T
journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
abstract: Objective To synthesise qualitative findings on the autistic experience of restrictive eating disorders in order to identify common themes and use this to inform future research on the development of more effective care. Method This systematic review was pre-registered on PROSPERO (CRD42023434116) and followed PRISMA guidelines. CINAHL, PsycINFO, Medline, Embase, Web of Science and Global Health databases were searched. Studies were included if they contained qualitative data detailing the autistic experience of restrictive eating disorders from autistic people, carers or healthcare professionals. The Critical Appraisal Skills Programme was used to assess quality of studies. Recurring themes were identified via thematic synthesis. Results Nine studies met the inclusion criteria, all focused on anorexia nervosa. Four themes arose from the analysis: (1) the relationship between autism and restrictive eating; (2) the journey to self-understanding; (3) experience of eating disorder services; (4) suggested treatment adaptations. Conclusion Findings suggest a broad range of mechanisms underlying the development and perpetuation of anorexia nervosa that are related to autism and are not consistently acknowledged and addressed in current care provision. This emphasises the need for more research into developing adapted or novel interventions for autistic people with eating disorders, as well as training programmes for clinicians.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista de tu entorno restringe la comida, puede ayudar ver ese comer a través de su experiencia autista: sensibilidad sensorial, necesidad de rutina y previsibilidad, o una forma de manejar la ansiedad. Al buscar apoyo profesional, puedes pedir que el equipo conozca el autismo y adapte el tratamiento, por ejemplo con comunicación clara, entornos tranquilos y respeto a las necesidades sensoriales. Esta revisión sistemática reunió nueve estudios cualitativos con personas autistas, familiares y profesionales, todos sobre anorexia nerviosa. Sus límites: pocos estudios, ninguno sobre otros trastornos restrictivos, y las experiencias descritas no se aplican a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person close to you is restricting food, it can help to understand their eating through their autistic experience: sensory sensitivities, a need for routine and predictability, or a way of coping with anxiety. When seeking professional support, you can ask that the team understands autism and adapts care, for example with clear communication, calm settings and respect for sensory needs. This systematic review brought together nine qualitative studies with autistic people, carers and clinicians, all about anorexia nervosa. Its limits: few studies, none on other restrictive eating disorders, and the experiences described will not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person nära dig begränsar sitt ätande kan det hjälpa att förstå ätandet utifrån hens autistiska upplevelse: sensorisk känslighet, behov av rutiner och förutsägbarhet, eller ett sätt att hantera ångest. När ni söker professionellt stöd kan du be att teamet har kunskap om autism och anpassar vården, till exempel med tydlig kommunikation, lugna miljöer och respekt för sensoriska behov. Denna systematiska översikt sammanställde nio kvalitativa studier med autistiska personer, anhöriga och vårdpersonal, alla om anorexi. Begränsningar: få studier, inga om andra restriktiva ätstörningar, och erfarenheterna passar inte alla.

title: Understanding the child and adolescent eating disorder treatment experiences of autistic people and parents.
authors: Alford C, Wallis A, Hay P, Mitchison D
abstract: BACKGROUND: Autistic people are overrepresented in eating disorders services and often require more intensive and extended treatment. Little is known about the eating disorder treatment experiences of autistic young people. The aim of this research was to understand the child and adolescent eating disorder treatment experiences of autistic people and parents of autistic young people. METHODS: Constructivist grounded theory was employed. Nine autistic people with lived experience of an eating disorder as an adolescent as well as nine parents of autistic young people engaged in paediatric eating disorders treatment were recruited through purposive sampling and then interviewed using a semi-structured design. Each interview was transcribed and analysed to identify themes and develop emergent theory directly from the data. RESULTS: Two major themes emerged (1) Misunderstood and (2) Safe and supportive eating disorder treatment for autistic young people and their families. Being ‘Misunderstood’ was found to occur across eight different domains including problems related to diagnosis, misattribution, neuro-normative definitions of eating and recovery, a one size fits all approach, siloed expertise, limited expertise and treatment options for eating disorders outside of anorexia nervosa, family neurodivergence and autism not being accommodated. The effects of being misunderstood included an increased burden of case management and advocacy, distress and trauma, mistrust of health professionals, identity disruption, and setbacks in recovery. ‘Safe and supportive eating disorders treatment for autistic young people and their families’ is informed by lived experience and built on a foundation of general care principles and autism-specific elements. CONCLUSIONS: Being misunderstood is a recursive process that occurs across multiple aspects of eating disorder care. Autistic young people and their families desire and need safety and understanding. This is achieved through care characteristics that promote connection and nuance, and autism specific adaptations and accommodations that provide optimal support conditions and strengthen therapeutic alliance. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This research was approved for prospective registration on Open Science Framework (OSF) on the 8th December 2023.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista está en tratamiento por un trastorno alimentario, puedes pedir al equipo que tenga en cuenta su forma de ser autista: necesidades sensoriales, preferencias de alimentos, comunicación y rutinas. Compartir lo que sabes de tu hijo y pedir ajustes concretos puede ayudar a que se sienta seguro y comprendido, y a reforzar la confianza con los profesionales. Este estudio cualitativo entrevistó a nueve personas autistas que vivieron un trastorno alimentario en la adolescencia y a nueve madres o padres; describieron sentirse incomprendidos y valoraron una atención flexible y adaptada al autismo. Al ser un grupo pequeño, sus experiencias no representan a todas las familias ni prueban qué tratamiento funciona mejor.
sheet.en: If your autistic child is in eating disorder treatment, you can ask the team to take their autistic way of being into account: sensory needs, food preferences, communication and routines. Sharing what you know about your child and asking for specific adjustments may help them feel safe and understood, and strengthen trust with professionals. This qualitative study interviewed nine autistic people who had an eating disorder as teenagers and nine parents; they described feeling misunderstood and valued flexible, autism-adapted care. Because the group was small, these experiences do not represent every family and do not prove which treatment works best.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn får behandling för en ätstörning kan du be teamet ta hänsyn till barnets autistiska sätt att fungera: sensoriska behov, matpreferenser, kommunikation och rutiner. Att dela det du vet om ditt barn och be om konkreta anpassningar kan hjälpa barnet att känna sig tryggt och förstått, och stärka förtroendet för vårdpersonalen. Denna kvalitativa studie intervjuade nio autistiska personer som haft en ätstörning i tonåren och nio föräldrar; de beskrev att de känt sig missförstådda och värdesatte flexibel, autismanpassad vård. Eftersom gruppen var liten speglar erfarenheterna inte alla familjer och visar inte vilken behandling som fungerar bäst.

title: Communication in Autistic Adults: An Action-Focused Review.
authors: de Marchena A, Cuneo N, Gurbuz E, Brown M, Trujillo J, Bergstrom J
abstract: Purpose of review This review focuses on recent research (primarily published between 2020-2024) describing unique aspects of communication in autistic adults. We review research on communication-related outcomes, as well as four communication topics frequently cited as important to autistic people (literal and non-literal language, augmentative and alternative communication, nonverbal communication, and double empathy). Recent findings A substantial proportion of autistic adults do not develop fluent language by adulthood. Autistic adults frequently experience communication barriers impacting relationships, employment, and health. These barriers arise from multiple sources (e.g., language, nonverbal communication, and unaccommodating environments and communication partners). Thus, it is essential to take a multifaceted approach to supporting autistic adults to ensure their communication success. We conclude that it is vital for clinicians and researchers to understand how autistic traits commonly manifest in adults and to accept and accommodate communication differences as they arise. To that end, we offer specific recommendations to help clinicians and researchers strengthen their interactions with the autistic people in their lives.

sheet.es: Mañana, prueba a ajustar tu forma de comunicarte en lugar de esperar que la persona autista adulta se adapte: habla de forma clara y literal, acepta otras formas de comunicarse (escritura, tableros, apps de CAA, gestos) y no interpretes la falta de contacto visual o expresión facial como desinterés. La comunicación es responsabilidad compartida: muchas barreras vienen del entorno y de los interlocutores, no solo de la persona. Esta es una revisión narrativa de investigaciones de 2020 a 2024 sobre adultos autistas, incluidos temas que las propias personas autistas consideran importantes. Sus límites: no es un estudio nuevo ni sistemático, y cada persona necesita apoyos distintos.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, try adjusting how you communicate rather than expecting the autistic adult to adapt: speak clearly and literally, welcome other ways of communicating (writing, letter boards, AAC apps, gestures), and don't read limited eye contact or facial expression as lack of interest. Communication is a shared responsibility: many barriers come from environments and communication partners, not just the person. This is a narrative review of research from 2020 to 2024 on autistic adults, covering topics autistic people themselves rate as important. Its limits: it is not a new or systematic study, and each person needs different supports.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du prova att anpassa ditt eget sätt att kommunicera i stället för att förvänta dig att den autistiska vuxna ska anpassa sig: tala tydligt och bokstavligt, välkomna andra kommunikationssätt (skrift, bokstavstavlor, AKK-appar, gester) och tolka inte lite ögonkontakt eller ansiktsuttryck som ointresse. Kommunikation är ett delat ansvar: många hinder kommer från miljön och samtalspartnerna, inte bara från personen. Detta är en narrativ översikt av forskning från 2020–2024 om autistiska vuxna, med ämnen som autistiska personer själva lyfter som viktiga. Begränsningar: det är ingen ny eller systematisk studie, och varje person behöver olika stöd.

title: Physical Activity for Anxiety for Autistic People: A Systematic Review.
authors: Riis K, Samulski B, Neely KA, Laverdure P
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Clinical anxiety is a common comorbidity in autistic people. Due to the prevalence of anxiety in the autism population and the adverse effects it causes, there is a critical need to develop effective interventions which address anxiety symptoms for autistic people. Therefore, the purpose of this systematic review was to examine the effectiveness of the use of physical activity as an intervention to reduce anxiety in autistic people. Three databases PubMed, PsychInfo, and Cochrane RCTs, were searched utilizing key terms. PRISMA systematic search procedures identified 44 studies meeting predetermined inclusion criteria. Participant characteristics, the type of physical activity performed, the nature of the physical activity program/delivery, anxiety-related outcomes, and research methodology was evaluated for each study. Each paper included was appraised and scored for risk of bias using Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions risk of bias tool. Titles and abstracts of 44 articles were reviewed and 8 articles met inclusion criteria which evaluated interventions. Evidence from 8 studies suggests that yoga, a community-based football program, an app-assisted walking program, group exercise programs, and horseback riding interventions reduced anxiety for autistic people. The studies included in this systematic review provide strong-to-moderate evidence that physical activity can reduce anxiety for autistic children and adults. However, additional research is needed to identify which mode of physical activity is most beneficial for anxiety reduction. Further, future research should evaluate frequency, duration, and intensity and their effects on anxiety for autistic people.

sheet.es: Moverse puede ayudar con la ansiedad. Mañana podéis probar una actividad física que a la persona le resulte agradable y predecible: un paseo corto, yoga suave, montar a caballo o un grupo de deporte tranquilo. Elegid juntos, empezad poco a poco y respetad sus preferencias sensoriales y su ritmo; si algo genera más estrés, se puede cambiar. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 8 estudios con niños y adultos autistas, y encontró que yoga, fútbol comunitario, caminatas con app, ejercicio en grupo y equitación redujeron la ansiedad. Sus límites: son pocos estudios y todavía no se sabe qué tipo, frecuencia, duración o intensidad funciona mejor, ni sirve igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Movement may help with anxiety. Tomorrow you could try a physical activity the person finds enjoyable and predictable: a short walk, gentle yoga, horseback riding or a calm group sport. Choose together, start small, and respect their sensory preferences and pace; if something adds stress, it can be changed. This systematic review brought together 8 studies with autistic children and adults, finding that yoga, community football, app-assisted walking, group exercise and horseback riding reduced anxiety. Its limits: only a few studies were included, and it is still unclear which type, frequency, duration or intensity works best, and it will not suit everyone equally.
sheet.sv: Rörelse kan hjälpa mot ångest. I morgon kan ni prova en fysisk aktivitet som personen tycker om och som känns förutsägbar: en kort promenad, lugn yoga, ridning eller en lugn gruppsport. Välj tillsammans, börja i liten skala och respektera personens sensoriska behov och tempo; om något ökar stressen går det att byta. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 8 studier med autistiska barn och vuxna och fann att yoga, fotboll i föreningsregi, promenader med app, gruppträning och ridning minskade ångest. Begränsningar: studierna är få, och det är ännu oklart vilken typ, frekvens, längd eller intensitet som fungerar bäst, och det passar inte alla lika bra.

title: Eating Disorder and Autism Collaborative project outline: promoting eating disorder research embedded in a neurodiversity-affirming culture.
authors: Duffy F, Gillespie-Smith K, Sharpe H, Buchan K, Nimbley E, Maloney E, Sader M, Kettley S, Kerr-Gaffney J, Waiter G, Tchanturia K
abstract: EDAC (Eating Disorders and Autism Collaborative) is an innovative project aiming to increase research capacity by supporting collaboration in the fields of eating disorders and autism. EDAC comprises four integrated workstreams to co-produce interdisciplinary research, directed by Autistic individuals with lived experience of eating disorders. Workstream 1 will outline best collaborative practices, informing the research network. Workstream 2 will use arts-based methodologies to set research priorities, with emphasis on the perspectives of underrepresented groups. Workstream 3 will support interdisciplinary collaborations to develop innovative research. Finally, workstream 4 will maximise knowledge mobilisation with the aim of reducing barriers to rapid incorporation of research into policy and clinical practice. A core aim of EDAC is to embed a neurodiversity-affirming culture within eating disorder research and to support the development of a new generation of researchers conducting innovative and meaningful research with the potential to improve clinical outcomes.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista con dificultades con la comida, puedes saber que la investigación empieza a escuchar directamente a personas autistas con experiencia de trastornos alimentarios. Mañana, puedes preguntar a tu familiar qué le ayuda y qué no al comer, y anotar sensaciones, texturas o rutinas importantes para compartir con profesionales. Este artículo describe un proyecto en el Reino Unido (EDAC), dirigido por personas autistas con experiencia vivida, para fijar prioridades de investigación y llevar resultados a la práctica clínica. Su límite: es un plan de proyecto, no aporta todavía datos ni pruebas sobre qué apoyos funcionan.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who finds eating difficult, it helps to know that research is starting to listen directly to autistic people with lived experience of eating disorders. Tomorrow, you could ask your family member what helps and what doesn't around food, and note important sensations, textures or routines to share with professionals. This article outlines a UK project (EDAC), led by autistic people with lived experience, to set research priorities and move findings into clinical practice. Its limit: it is a project plan, so it does not yet offer data or evidence on which supports work.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som har svårt med mat kan det vara bra att veta att forskningen börjar lyssna direkt på autistiska personer med egen erfarenhet av ätstörningar. I morgon kan du fråga din närstående vad som hjälper och inte hjälper kring mat, och anteckna viktiga sinnesintryck, konsistenser eller rutiner att dela med vården. Artikeln beskriver ett brittiskt projekt (EDAC), lett av autistiska personer med egen erfarenhet, för att sätta forskningsprioriteringar och föra ut resultat i vården. Begränsning: det är en projektplan, så den ger ännu inga data eller belägg för vilket stöd som fungerar.

title: 'A certain magic' - autistic adults' experiences of interacting with other autistic people and its relation to Quality of Life: A systematic review and thematic meta-synthesis.
authors: Watts G, Crompton C, Grainger C, Long J, Botha M, Somerville M, Cage E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: There is an increasing focus on research exploring autistic communication and community. In this review, we systematically collate and analyse how autistic adults describe their experiences of other autistic people and the relationship this has with their Quality of Life (QoL). Fifty two qualitative papers were analysed using thematic meta-synthesis. Results found many experiences of other autistic people were positive and were associated with improved QoL across a range of domains. The heterogeneity of the autistic experiences described indicates a need for further research to explore which factors predict a positive impact on QoL. Analysis also highlighted a paucity of data on autistic people with co-occurring intellectual disability in relation to this phenomenon. Implications for research and practice are discussed.Lay abstractResearch has suggested that autistic people enjoy spending time with other autistic people and find them easier to talk to. We wanted to find out what autistic people say about spending time with other autistic people and whether this makes their life better. We found 52 papers which described this and reviewed what they found. We found that many autistic people had positive experiences of spending time with other autistic people and these experiences had positive impact on their lives in a range of different ways. The papers did not tell us whether this also happens for autistic people with a learning disability. More research is needed to find out more about why spending time with other autistic people helps some autistic people.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, puede valer la pena ayudarle a encontrar espacios con otras personas autistas: grupos, asociaciones, foros o actividades por intereses compartidos. Muchas personas autistas describen estos encuentros como más fáciles y cómodos, y los relacionan con una mejor calidad de vida. Respeta su ritmo y sus preferencias; no a todo el mundo le sirve lo mismo. La evidencia viene de una revisión sistemática que reunió 52 estudios cualitativos con adultos autistas que contaban sus propias experiencias. Sus límites: las experiencias fueron muy variadas, no sabemos qué factores marcan la diferencia y casi no hay datos sobre personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it may be worth helping them find spaces with other autistic people: peer groups, autistic-led organisations, online forums or activities built around shared interests. Many autistic adults describe these connections as easier and more comfortable, and link them to a better quality of life. Follow their pace and preferences; what helps one person may not suit another. The evidence comes from a systematic review that brought together 52 qualitative studies in which autistic adults described their own experiences. Its limits: experiences varied widely, we don't yet know which factors make the difference, and there is very little data on autistic people with an intellectual disability.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det vara värt att hjälpa hen hitta sammanhang med andra autistiska personer: kamratgrupper, autistledda föreningar, nätforum eller aktiviteter kring gemensamma intressen. Många autistiska vuxna beskriver sådana möten som enklare och tryggare, och kopplar dem till bättre livskvalitet. Följ personens takt och önskemål; det som hjälper en passar inte alltid en annan. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt som samlade 52 kvalitativa studier där autistiska vuxna berättade om sina egna erfarenheter. Begränsningar: erfarenheterna varierade mycket, vi vet ännu inte vilka faktorer som gör skillnad, och det finns nästan inga data om autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning.

title: Complementary and Alternative Medicine for Autism - A Systematic Review.
authors: Doherty M, Foley KR, Schloss J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) is a therapeutic option currently used by autistic people with continued interest and uptake. There remains limited evidence regarding the efficacy of CAM use in autism. The aim of this systematic review is to comprehensively review published clinical trials to explore the efficacy of CAM in autism. A systematic literature review of available research published from June 2013 to March 2023 was conducted. Our literature search identified 1826 eligible citations, and duplications removed (n = 694) with 102 articles eligible for title/abstract screening. After full text review, 39 studies were included. The results of this systematic review identified that for autistic people, vitamin and mineral supplements may only be of benefit if there is a deficiency. The results also found that the main interventions used were dietary interventions and nutraceuticals, including targeted supplements, vitamins and minerals, omega 3 s and prebiotics, probiotics and digestive enzymes. The evidence does not support some of the most frequently utilised dietary interventions, such as a Gluten Free Casein Free (GFCF) diet, and the use of targeted nutraceutical supplements may be of benefit, but more conclusive research is still required to direct safe and effective treatment.

sheet.es: Si estás pensando en suplementos, vitaminas o dietas especiales, una opción tranquila es hablar primero con el equipo de salud y pedir que revisen si existe alguna carencia real; según esta revisión, las vitaminas y minerales parecen ayudar sobre todo cuando falta algo. La dieta sin gluten ni caseína, muy usada, no mostró respaldo claro. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de 39 ensayos clínicos con personas autistas, publicados entre 2013 y 2023. Sus límites: los estudios eran variados y a menudo pequeños, así que los resultados no sirven como regla para cada persona y hace falta más investigación sobre seguridad y eficacia.
sheet.en: If you are considering supplements, vitamins or special diets, a calm first step is to talk with your health team and ask them to check for any actual deficiency; this review suggests vitamins and minerals mainly help when something is lacking. The widely used gluten-free, casein-free diet did not show clear support. This is a systematic review of 39 clinical trials with autistic people, published between 2013 and 2023. Its limits: the studies varied and were often small, so the findings are not a rule for every person, and more research on safety and effectiveness is still needed.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på kosttillskott, vitaminer eller särskilda dieter kan ett lugnt första steg vara att prata med vården och be dem undersöka om det finns någon faktisk brist; enligt denna översikt verkar vitaminer och mineraler främst hjälpa när något saknas. Den vanliga gluten- och kaseinfria kosten fick inget tydligt stöd. Det är en systematisk översikt av 39 kliniska studier med autistiska personer, publicerade 2013–2023. Begränsningar: studierna var olika och ofta små, så resultaten är ingen regel för varje person, och mer forskning om säkerhet och effekt behövs.

title: Polygenic and developmental profiles of autism differ by age at diagnosis.
authors: Zhang X, Grove J, Gu Y, Buus CK, Nielsen LK, Neufeld SAS, Koko M, Malawsky DS, Wade EM, Verhoef E, Gui A, Hegemann L, APEX Consortium, iPSYCH Autism Consortium, PGC-PTSD Consortium, Geschwind DH, Wray
abstract: Although autism has historically been conceptualized as a condition that emerges in early childhood 1,2 , many autistic people are diagnosed later in life 3-5 . It is unknown whether earlier- and later-diagnosed autism have different developmental trajectories and genetic profiles. Using longitudinal data from four independent birth cohorts, we demonstrate that two different socioemotional and behavioural trajectories are associated with age at diagnosis. In independent cohorts of autistic individuals, common genetic variants account for approximately 11% of the variance in age at autism diagnosis, similar to the contribution of individual sociodemographic and clinical factors, which typically explain less than 15% of this variance. We further demonstrate that the polygenic architecture of autism can be broken down into two modestly genetically correlated (r g = 0.38, s.e. = 0.07) autism polygenic factors. One of these factors is associated with earlier autism diagnosis and lower social and communication abilities in early childhood, but is only moderately genetically correlated with attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and mental-health conditions. Conversely, the second factor is associated with later autism diagnosis and increased socioemotional and behavioural difficulties in adolescence, and has moderate to high positive genetic correlations with ADHD and mental-health conditions. These findings indicate that earlier- and later-diagnosed autism have different developmental trajectories and genetic profiles. Our findings have important implications for how we conceptualize autism and provide a model to explain some of the diversity found in autism.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o tú recibisteis el diagnóstico de autismo en la adolescencia o la adultez, no significa que «se pasó por alto algo obvio»: el autismo puede mostrarse de formas distintas en distintas etapas. En personas diagnosticadas más tarde, conviene prestar atención también al bienestar emocional, la ansiedad o rasgos de TDAH, y buscar apoyos adaptados a esa etapa. Este estudio analizó datos de cuatro grandes cohortes de nacimiento seguidas durante años y muestras genéticas de personas autistas, y encontró dos perfiles de desarrollo y genéticos asociados a la edad de diagnóstico. Sus límites: describe tendencias de grupo, la genética explica solo una parte pequeña y no predice nada sobre una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you or your child were diagnosed autistic in adolescence or adulthood, it doesn't mean something obvious was simply missed: autism can show up differently at different ages. For people diagnosed later, it can help to also pay attention to emotional wellbeing, anxiety or ADHD traits, and to look for support that fits that life stage. This study used long-term data from four large birth cohorts and genetic samples from autistic people, finding two developmental and genetic profiles linked to age at diagnosis. Its limits: it describes group trends, genetics explains only a small part, and it cannot predict anything about one individual.
sheet.sv: Om du eller ditt barn fick en autismdiagnos i tonåren eller som vuxen betyder det inte att något uppenbart bara missades: autism kan visa sig olika i olika åldrar.
