För den som får diagnos senare kan det hjälpa att även uppmärksamma psykiskt välmående, oro eller ADHD-drag, och söka stöd som passar den livsfasen. Studien använde långtidsdata från fyra stora födelsekohorter och genetiska prover från autistiska personer, och fann två utvecklings- och genetiska profiler kopplade till diagnosålder. Begränsningar: den beskriver gruppmönster, genetiken förklarar bara en liten del och den kan inte förutsäga något om en enskild person.

title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Mismatch Negativity in Autism: Insights Into Predictive Mechanisms.
authors: Sapey-Triomphe LA, Bouet R, Mattout J, Sonié S, Schmitz C, Lecaignard F
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Mismatch negativity (MMN) has been frequently used to assess auditory processing and change detection in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but findings have been fairly inconsistent. To address this issue, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of MMN amplitude (76 effect sizes) and latency (62 effect sizes) in ASD to identify factors contributing to this heterogeneity and to interpret findings within the predictive coding framework. While residual heterogeneity remained, significant effects of the interaction between age group and design type (unifeature vs. multifeature, i.e., one or several types of deviants) and deviant type were found for MMN amplitude. In multifeature designs, autistic children and adolescents exhibited reduced MMN amplitudes compared to neurotypical peers (g = 0.25, p = 0.01), whereas autistic adults showed increased MMN amplitudes (g = -0.26, p = 0.02). In addition, autistic individuals had significantly smaller MMN amplitudes than neurotypical individuals in paradigms using phoneme deviants (g = 0.41, p < 0.001). Across designs, no significant MMN latency differences were observed between neurotypical and autistic individuals. These results are discussed within the predictive coding framework, as MMN responses are thought to reflect prediction errors, aligning with theories suggesting heightened prediction errors in autistic adults. Future studies with larger samples and improved data reporting are needed to further clarify the developmental trajectory and variability of MMN responses in ASD. Additionally, computational modeling approaches can help characterize learning dynamics and disentangle predictive coding accounts among autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Esta investigación sugiere que el cerebro autista puede reaccionar de forma diferente a cambios inesperados en los sonidos, y que esto cambia con la edad. En la práctica: si alguien reacciona con fuerza a ruidos nuevos o le cuesta seguir cambios rápidos en el habla, puede ayudar avisar antes de los cambios, hablar con calma y dar tiempo para procesar. Pregunte a la persona qué sonidos le resultan difíciles. Es un metaanálisis que reunió estudios de electroencefalografía con niños, adolescentes y adultos autistas y no autistas. Sus límites: los resultados variaban mucho entre estudios, las muestras eran pequeñas y medir ondas cerebrales no describe la experiencia de cada persona.
sheet.en: This research suggests autistic brains may respond differently to unexpected changes in sounds, and that this shifts with age. In practice: if someone reacts strongly to new noises or finds fast changes in speech hard to follow, it may help to give warnings before changes, speak calmly and allow processing time. Ask the person which sounds feel difficult. This is a meta-analysis combining EEG studies of autistic and non-autistic children, adolescents and adults. Its limits: results varied a lot between studies, samples were small, and brainwave measures do not describe any individual's lived experience.
sheet.sv: Den här forskningen tyder på att autistiska hjärnor kan reagera annorlunda på oväntade förändringar i ljud, och att detta förändras med åldern. I praktiken: om någon reagerar starkt på nya ljud eller har svårt att följa snabba växlingar i tal kan det hjälpa att förvarna inför förändringar, tala lugnt och ge tid att bearbeta. Fråga personen vilka ljud som känns svåra. Det är en metaanalys av EEG-studier med autistiska och icke-autistiska barn, ungdomar och vuxna. Begränsningar: resultaten skilde sig mycket mellan studierna, grupperna var små och hjärnvågsmätningar beskriver inte den enskilda personens upplevelse.

title: Workplace Accommodations and Employment Outcomes Among Employees With Autism: A Systematic Review.
authors: Heinze C
abstract: Individuals with autism often face challenges in achieving and maintaining meaningful employment, but workplace accommodations can bridge these gaps by enabling inclusion, satisfaction, and productivity. The goal of this review was to systematically evaluate and synthesize the existing evidence base on workplace accommodations for adults with autism. After conducting a systematic search of numerous databases, ten empirical studies published between 2010 and 2025, including randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, surveys, and qualitative studies, were included. The quality of studies was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP), the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI), and Risk-of-Bias (RoB) instruments, with the majority of studies being assessed as moderate-to-high quality but having small sample sizes and relying on self-report. Accommodation reports fall into four groups: assistive technology; organizational, sensory, and environmental adaptations; supervisory and relational support; and skills and psychosocial support. In general, the evidence indicated that accommodations were linked to better job acquisition, stability, satisfaction, and productivity, albeit with variability in effectiveness based on relational quality, disclosure practice, and organizational culture. Consistent results highlighted the value of individually tailored support and respectful supervisory relationships, while variations indicated lingering barriers to stigma, ignorance, and uneven policy implementation. However, the heterogeneity of methods and the exclusion of broader autism groups limit the generalizability of findings in these studies. Longitudinal and intervention studies, participatory approaches to design, and representation of underrepresented groups are essential priorities for future research to further develop evidence-based practice and guide employer training and policy.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a un adulto autista que trabaja o busca empleo, puede ayudar hablar juntos sobre qué ajustes le servirían: tecnología de apoyo, cambios sensoriales o del entorno (luz, ruido, espacio tranquilo), instrucciones claras de la supervisión y apoyo en habilidades o bienestar. Lo que más parece importar es que el apoyo se adapte a la persona y que la relación con quien supervisa sea respetuosa. La decisión de revelar el diagnóstico es suya. Esta revisión sistemática reunió diez estudios (2010-2025) con adultos autistas y encontró vínculos entre ajustes y mejor acceso, estabilidad, satisfacción y productividad. Sus límites: estudios pequeños, basados en autoinforme y poco representativos de todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult who works or is job-seeking, it may help to talk together about which accommodations would suit them: assistive technology, sensory or environmental changes (lighting, noise, a quiet space), clear communication from supervisors, and support with skills or wellbeing. What seems to matter most is support tailored to the person and a respectful relationship with their manager. Whether to disclose is their choice. This systematic review pooled ten studies (2010-2025) with autistic adults and found accommodations linked to better hiring, job stability, satisfaction and productivity. Limits: the studies were small, relied on self-report and did not represent all autistic people.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen som arbetar eller söker jobb kan det hjälpa att tillsammans prata om vilka anpassningar som skulle passa: hjälpmedel och teknik, sensoriska eller miljömässiga ändringar (ljus, ljud, en lugn plats), tydlig kommunikation från chefen och stöd med färdigheter eller välmående. Det som verkar betyda mest är att stödet är individuellt och att relationen till chefen är respektfull. Om man berättar om sin diagnos är personens eget val. Denna systematiska översikt samlade tio studier (2010-2025) med autistiska vuxna och fann samband mellan anpassningar och bättre anställning, stabilitet, trivsel och produktivitet. Begränsningar: små studier, självrapportering och bristande representation av alla autistiska personer.

title: The Assessment and Treatment of Post-traumatic Stress Disorder in Autistic People: A Systematic Review.
authors: Quinton AMG, Ali D, Danese A, Happé F, Rumball F
journal: Review journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Adverse life events and mental health conditions are unfortunately common amongst autistic adults and children; this may present a vulnerability to developing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). This systematic review provides an update of Rumball's ( Review Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders , 6 , 294-324, 2019) systematic review of PTSD in autistic individuals and identifies 18 new studies published from 2017 to 2022, reflecting increased research interest in PTSD in autistic populations. Included literature suggests that autistic adults and children experience more severe PTSD symptoms compared to their non-autistic peers, with at least comparable rates of occurrence. We provide a comprehensive overview of this emerging field and identify the need for future research to validate PTSD symptom assessment tools and treatment strategies and investigate unique manifestations of trauma-related symptoms in autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a su cargo ha vivido experiencias difíciles, conviene tomarse en serio posibles señales de trauma: cambios en el sueño, más ansiedad, evitación de lugares o personas, o pérdida de habilidades. Estas señales pueden verse distintas en personas autistas, así que anote lo que observa y compártalo con profesionales que conozcan tanto el autismo como el trauma. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 18 estudios nuevos (2017-2022) con niños y adultos autistas, y sugiere que el TEPT es al menos igual de frecuente y a menudo más intenso que en personas no autistas. Sus límites: las herramientas de evaluación y los tratamientos aún no están validados para personas autistas, y cada persona es diferente.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support has been through hard experiences, it is worth taking possible signs of trauma seriously: changes in sleep, more anxiety, avoiding places or people, or losing skills. These signs can look different in autistic people, so note what you notice and share it with professionals who understand both autism and trauma. This systematic review gathered 18 new studies (2017-2022) with autistic children and adults, and suggests PTSD is at least as common and often more severe than in non-autistic peers. Its limits: assessment tools and treatments are not yet validated for autistic people, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar har varit med om svåra händelser är det klokt att ta möjliga tecken på trauma på allvar: förändrad sömn, mer oro, att undvika platser eller personer, eller att tappa förmågor. Tecknen kan se annorlunda ut hos autistiska personer, så anteckna vad du ser och dela det med yrkespersoner som förstår både autism och trauma. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 18 nya studier (2017-2022) med autistiska barn och vuxna och tyder på att PTSD är minst lika vanligt och ofta mer intensivt än hos icke-autistiska. Begränsningar: bedömningsverktyg och behandlingar är ännu inte validerade för autistiska personer, och varje person är unik.

title: Camouflaging and autism: Conceptualisation and methodological issues.
authors: Arnold WM, Bitsika V, Sharpley CF
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: It has been suggested that there is poor clarity of the 'camouflaging' concept in autism research, and potential confounding of its measurement tools, such as the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q). A critical review of 389 studies was conducted to investigate these potential conceptual and methodological issues. The findings question whether the same construct has been investigated across studies, as there is inconsistency in: (a) which terms are used; (b) reference made to established conceptual literature; (c) how terms are used (e.g. interchangeably or distinctly); and (d) how terms are defined. Although the CAT-Q has excellent reliability, there is mixed support for its validity, which is evidenced by its confounding by other constructs (e.g. social anxiety) and its limited autism-specificity. The validity of informant discrepancy measures of camouflaging is also questioned due to insufficient reference to established methodology. Finally, the generalisability of camouflaging to the overall autistic population is unclear due to: (a) overrepresentation of autistic females diagnosed during adulthood; and (b) underrepresentation of autistic people with co-occurring intellectual or language difficulties, and those with greater support needs. These issues are considered both in terms of their clinical relevance and how future research might resolve them.Lay AbstractMany autistic people have reported using 'camouflaging' strategies to adapt or cope within the non-autistic social world and avoid being negatively judged by other people. However, many terms have been used synonymously with camouflaging, such as masking, compensation and impression management. Due to this confusion about which terms to use, there is some suggestion that there is poor clarity and understanding of the camouflaging concept, and that this may contribute to inaccuracy of the tools used to measure this behaviour. We review 389 previous studies to examine these concerns. Our findings confirm this lack of clarity by showing that studies are inconsistent in: (a) which terms they used to refer to behavioural strategies that resemble camouflaging; (b) whether they referred to existing literature; (c) whether they used different terms to refer to the same concept or to separate types of behaviour; and (d) how they defined the terms that they used. Our findings also question the accuracy of camouflaging measurement tools, as these tools may also be measuring other behaviours (e.g. social anxiety) that are not only experienced by autistic people. We also find that camouflaging studies have mostly focused on autistic females with no accompanying cognitive or language difficulties, and who have received their diagnosis in adulthood. Although camouflaging may contribute to the underdiagnosis of some autistic females, most autistic people are male and are diagnosed during early childhood, and a large number of autistic people do experience those other difficulties. Because of this, it is not clear whether the findings of previous camouflaging studies can apply to all autistic people. We provide some suggestions for how researchers might resolve some of these issues in their future studies, and we consider what the findings mean for clinicians who work with autistic people.

sheet.es: Si su familiar autista dice que «enmascara» o se adapta para encajar, tome en serio su propia descripción: qué hace, cuándo y cuánto le cuesta. Un cuestionario puntuado no capta toda su experiencia; hablar con calma sobre momentos concretos y ofrecer espacios donde no necesite fingir puede ayudar más. Esta revisión crítica analizó 389 estudios y encontró que se usan términos distintos (camuflaje, enmascaramiento, compensación) sin definiciones comunes, y que herramientas como el CAT-Q pueden medir también ansiedad social. Su límite: revisa investigaciones centradas sobre todo en mujeres diagnosticadas en la adultez, así que no sabemos cuánto se aplica a niños, a personas con discapacidad intelectual o del lenguaje, ni a quienes necesitan más apoyos.
sheet.en: If your autistic family member says they 'mask' or adapt to fit in, take their own description seriously: what they do, when, and what it costs them. A scored questionnaire won't capture their whole experience; calm conversations about specific moments, and offering spaces where they don't need to pretend, may help more. This critical review examined 389 studies and found that terms like camouflaging, masking and compensation are used without shared definitions, and that tools such as the CAT-Q may also measure social anxiety. Its limit: the research reviewed focused mostly on women diagnosed in adulthood, so it is unclear how well findings apply to children, people with intellectual or language disabilities, or those with higher support needs.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska närstående säger att hen ”maskerar” eller anpassar sig för att passa in, ta hens egen beskrivning på allvar: vad hen gör, när och vad det kostar. Ett poängsatt frågeformulär fångar inte hela upplevelsen; lugna samtal om konkreta situationer och platser där hen inte behöver låtsas kan hjälpa mer. Denna kritiska översikt granskade 389 studier och fann att begrepp som kamouflering, maskering och kompensation används utan gemensamma definitioner, och att verktyg som CAT-Q även kan mäta social ångest. Begränsning: forskningen gällde främst kvinnor diagnostiserade i vuxen ålder, så det är oklart hur väl resultaten gäller barn, personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller språksvårigheter, eller de med större stödbehov.

title: Autism and Dementia: A Summative Report from the 2nd International Summit on Intellectual Disabilities and Dementia.
authors: Janicki MP, McCallion P, Jokinen N, Larsen FK, Mughal D, Palanisamy V, Santos F, Service K, Shih A, Shooshtari S, Thakur A, Tiziano G, Watchman K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This article synthesizes findings, from the Autism/Dementia Work Group of the 2nd International Summit on Intellectual Disabilities and Dementia, on the nature of autism/autism spectrum disorder and later-age neuropathologies, particularly dementia. The convened group of experts explored genetic, neurobiological, and environmental risk factors that may affect the lifespan and lived experiences of older adults with autism. A review of current literature indicates a lack of comprehensive information on the demographics and factors associated with aging in autistic adults. However, our understanding of autism is evolving, challenging traditional views of it as a static, inherited neurodevelopmental disorder. The relationship between autism and other neurodevelopmental conditions-such as Down syndrome, fragile X syndrome, and tuberous sclerosis complex-reflects the complex genetic landscape of neurodevelopmental disorders. These genetic and familial factors may contribute to progressive health challenges and cognitive decline in later life. Key findings reveal a complex link between autism and dementia, despite limited research on this relationship, particularly among older adults. The overall prevalence of dementia in this population appears to be influenced by co-occurring intellectual disabilities, particularly Down syndrome. While the association between autism and specific types of dementia is still not well understood, the reviewed evidence suggests a notable connection with frontotemporal dementia, although causality has not been established. Exploration of biomarkers may offer further insights. Currently, the relationship between autism, cognitive health, and cognitive decline in older adults remains a complex and underexplored area of research.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que envejece, merece la pena anotar su forma habitual de comunicarse, sus rutinas y habilidades, para notar a tiempo cambios nuevos y comentarlos con su equipo de salud. Un cambio no significa demencia: el estrés, el dolor o el agotamiento también influyen. La evidencia procede de un informe de expertos de una cumbre internacional que revisó la investigación sobre autismo y demencia; sugiere un posible vínculo, sobre todo con la demencia frontotemporal y cuando hay síndrome de Down. Sus límites: hay muy pocos estudios con personas autistas mayores, no se ha demostrado causalidad y no predice lo que vivirá cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who is getting older, it can help to note their usual ways of communicating, routines and skills, so new changes are noticed early and shared with their health team. A change does not mean dementia: stress, pain or burnout matter too. The evidence comes from an expert summit report reviewing research on autism and dementia; it suggests a possible link, especially with frontotemporal dementia and when Down syndrome is present. Its limits: very few studies include older autistic adults, causation has not been shown, and it cannot predict any individual's future.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som blir äldre kan det hjälpa att anteckna hur hen brukar kommunicera, sina rutiner och förmågor, så att nya förändringar upptäcks tidigt och kan tas upp med vården. En förändring betyder inte demens: stress, smärta eller utmattning spelar också roll. Underlaget är en rapport från en internationell expertkonferens som granskat forskning om autism och demens; den antyder ett möjligt samband, särskilt med frontotemporal demens och vid Downs syndrom. Begränsningar: mycket få studier omfattar äldre autistiska vuxna, orsakssamband är inte visat och rapporten kan inte förutsäga enskilda personers framtid.

title: Shared heritability of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Rommelse NN, Franke B, Geurts HM, Hartman CA, Buitelaar JK
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are both highly heritable neurodevelopmental disorders. Evidence indicates both disorders co-occur with a high frequency, in 20-50% of children with ADHD meeting criteria for ASD and in 30-80% of ASD children meeting criteria for ADHD. This review will provide an overview on all available studies [family based, twin, candidate gene, linkage, and genome wide association (GWA) studies] shedding light on the role of shared genetic underpinnings of ADHD and ASD. It is concluded that family and twin studies do provide support for the hypothesis that ADHD and ASD originate from partly similar familial/genetic factors. Only a few candidate gene studies, linkage studies and GWA studies have specifically addressed this co-occurrence, pinpointing to some promising pleiotropic genes, loci and single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), but the research field is in urgent need for better designed and powered studies to tackle this complex issue. We propose that future studies examining shared familial etiological factors for ADHD and ASD use a family-based design in which the same phenotypic (ADHD and ASD), candidate endophenotypic, and environmental measurements are obtained from all family members. Multivariate multi-level models are probably best suited for the statistical analysis.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista también muestra rasgos de ADHD (atención, impulsividad, inquietud), no es raro: ambos suelen aparecer juntos y pueden compartir raíces familiares. Puede ser útil comentar estos rasgos con el equipo profesional y observar si otros familiares viven experiencias parecidas, sin culpas: la genética no es responsabilidad de nadie. Mañana, prueba apoyos que sirvan para ambos perfiles, como pausas de movimiento y tareas cortas. Es una revisión de estudios familiares, de gemelos y genéticos que encontró que el autismo y el ADHD comparten en parte factores genéticos. Límites: es de 2010, los estudios genéticos eran pocos y pequeños, y no permite predecir nada para una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If your autistic child also shows ADHD traits (attention differences, impulsivity, restlessness), that is common: the two often occur together and may share family roots. It can help to mention these traits to your care team and notice whether relatives have similar experiences, without blame: genetics is nobody's fault. Tomorrow, try supports that suit both profiles, such as movement breaks and shorter tasks. This is a review of family, twin and genetic studies, concluding that autism and ADHD partly share genetic factors. Limits: it dates from 2010, the genetic studies were few and small, and it cannot predict anything for an individual person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn också visar ADHD-drag (uppmärksamhetsskillnader, impulsivitet, rastlöshet) är det vanligt: de förekommer ofta tillsammans och kan ha delvis gemensamma rötter i familjen. Det kan hjälpa att ta upp dragen med vårdteamet och lägga märke till om släktingar har liknande erfarenheter, utan skuld: genetik är ingens fel. I morgon kan du prova stöd som passar båda profilerna, som rörelsepauser och kortare uppgifter. Detta är en översikt av familje-, tvilling- och genstudier som drar slutsatsen att autism och ADHD delvis delar genetiska faktorer. Begränsningar: den är från 2010, genstudierna var få och små, och den kan inte förutsäga något för en enskild person.

title: Anxiety disorders and sensory over-responsivity in children with autism spectrum disorders: is there a causal relationship?
authors: Green SA, Ben-Sasson A
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Anxiety disorders and sensory over-responsivity (SOR) are common in children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD), and there is evidence for an association between these two conditions. Currently, it is unclear what causal mechanisms may exist between SOR and anxiety. We propose three possible theories to explain the association between anxiety and SOR: (a) SOR is caused by anxiety; (b) Anxiety is caused by SOR; or (c) SOR and anxiety are causally unrelated but are associated through a common risk factor or diagnostic overlap. In this paper, we examine support for each theory in the existing anxiety, autism, and neuroscience literature, and discuss how each theory informs choice of interventions and implications for future studies.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista reacciona con fuerza a ruidos, texturas o luces, y además muestra ansiedad, puede ayudar observar ambas cosas juntas: anota qué estímulos aparecen antes de los momentos de angustia y ofrece opciones como cascos, pausas o un rincón tranquilo. Reducir la carga sensorial y anticipar situaciones nuevas puede aliviar a la vez el malestar sensorial y la preocupación. Se trata de una revisión teórica de estudios previos sobre ansiedad, autismo y neurociencia; no incluyó participantes nuevos. Su límite principal es que no demuestra qué causa qué: solo plantea hipótesis, y cada niño o niña es diferente.
sheet.en: If your autistic child reacts strongly to sounds, textures or lights and also shows anxiety, it may help to watch both together: note which sensations come before moments of distress, and offer options like ear defenders, breaks or a quiet corner. Lowering sensory load and previewing new situations may ease both sensory discomfort and worry at once. This is a theoretical review of earlier research on anxiety, autism and neuroscience; it did not involve new participants. Its main limit is that it does not prove which causes which: it only proposes possible explanations, and every child is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn reagerar starkt på ljud, texturer eller ljus och samtidigt visar oro kan det hjälpa att se på båda sakerna tillsammans: notera vilka sinnesintryck som kommer före stunder av stress, och erbjud till exempel hörselkåpor, pauser eller en lugn vrå. Att minska sinnesbelastningen och förbereda nya situationer kan lindra både obehaget och oron. Detta är en teoretisk översikt av tidigare forskning om ångest, autism och neurovetenskap; inga nya deltagare ingick. Den största begränsningen är att den inte visar vad som orsakar vad, utan bara föreslår möjliga förklaringar, och varje barn är olika.

title: Employment and post-secondary educational activities for young adults with autism spectrum disorders during the transition to adulthood.
authors: Taylor JL, Seltzer MM
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Tras la escuela, una gran parte de jóvenes autistas queda sin empleo ni formación, sobre todo quienes necesitan más apoyo: la transición a la vida adulta exige planificación.
claim.en: After school, a large share of autistic young adults have no job or training, especially those needing more support: the transition to adulthood needs planning.
claim.sv: Efter skolan saknar en stor andel autistiska unga vuxna arbete eller utbildning, särskilt de med större stödbehov: övergången till vuxenlivet kräver planering.

supports.es: Empezar a planificar la transición años antes de que acabe la escuela.
supports.en: Starting transition planning years before school ends.
supports.sv: Att börja planera övergången flera år innan skolan tar slut.

doesNotSupport.es: Que los resultados estén fijados; los apoyos los cambian.
doesNotSupport.en: That outcomes are fixed; supports change them.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att utfallen är givna; stöd förändrar dem.

title: Why are autism spectrum conditions more prevalent in males?
authors: Baron-Cohen S, Lombardo MV, Auyeung B, Ashwin E, Chakrabarti B, Knickmeyer R
abstract: Autism Spectrum Conditions (ASC) are much more common in males, a bias that may offer clues to the etiology of this condition. Although the cause of this bias remains a mystery, we argue that it occurs because ASC is an extreme manifestation of the male brain. The extreme male brain (EMB) theory, first proposed in 1997, is an extension of the Empathizing-Systemizing (E-S) theory of typical sex differences that proposes that females on average have a stronger drive to empathize while males on average have a stronger drive to systemize. In this first major update since 2005, we describe some of the evidence relating to the EMB theory of ASC and consider how typical sex differences in brain structure may be relevant to ASC. One possible biological mechanism to account for the male bias is the effect of fetal testosterone (fT). We also consider alternative biological theories, the X and Y chromosome theories, and the reduced autosomal penetrance theory. None of these theories has yet been fully confirmed or refuted, though the weight of evidence in favor of the fT theory is growing from converging sources (longitudinal amniocentesis studies from pregnancy to age 10 years old, current hormone studies, and genetic association studies of SNPs in the sex steroid pathways). Ultimately, as these theories are not mutually exclusive and ASC is multi-factorial, they may help explain the male prevalence of ASC.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: que el autismo se diagnostique más en chicos no significa que las chicas o mujeres no sean autistas. Si una hija, hermana o pareja te resulta familiar en lo que lees, vale la pena observar con calma y pedir una valoración profesional, sin descartarlo por ser mujer. Y no hace falta encajar en estereotipos de «cerebro masculino»: cada persona autista tiene su propio perfil de intereses y formas de conectar. Evidencia: es una revisión de 2011 que resume teorías como la del «cerebro masculino extremo» y la testosterona fetal. Límites: son hipótesis no confirmadas, y estudios posteriores sugieren que en chicas el autismo a menudo pasa desapercibido.
sheet.en: The practical point: autism being diagnosed more often in boys does not mean girls and women aren't autistic. If a daughter, sister or partner seems familiar in what you read, it's reasonable to observe calmly and seek a professional assessment, rather than ruling it out because she's female. Nobody needs to fit an 'extreme male brain' stereotype: each autistic person has their own mix of interests and ways of connecting. Evidence: this is a 2011 review summarising theories such as the 'extreme male brain' and fetal testosterone. Limits: these are unconfirmed hypotheses, and later research suggests autism in girls is often missed.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: att autism oftare diagnostiseras hos pojkar betyder inte att flickor och kvinnor inte är autistiska. Om en dotter, syster eller partner känns igen i det du läser är det rimligt att lugnt iaktta och söka en professionell utredning, i stället för att avfärda det för att hon är kvinna. Ingen behöver passa in i stereotypen om en ”extremt manlig hjärna”: varje autistisk person har sin egen blandning av intressen och sätt att knyta an. Evidens: en översikt från 2011 som sammanfattar teorier som ”extremt manlig hjärna” och fostrets testosteron. Begränsningar: hypoteserna är obekräftade, och senare forskning tyder på att autism hos flickor ofta missas.

title: Alterations of GABAergic signaling in autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Pizzarelli R, Cherubini E
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of pathological conditions, mainly of genetic origin, characterized by stereotyped behavior, marked impairment in verbal and nonverbal communication, social skills, and cognition. Interestingly, in a small number of cases, ASDs are associated with single mutations in genes encoding for neuroligin-neurexin families. These are adhesion molecules which, by regulating transsynaptic signaling, contribute to maintain a proper excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance at the network level. Furthermore, GABA, the main inhibitory neurotransmitter in adult life, at late embryonic/early postnatal stages has been shown to depolarize and excite targeted cell through an outwardly directed flux of chloride. The depolarizing action of GABA and associated calcium influx regulate a variety of developmental processes from cell migration and differentiation to synapse formation. Here, we summarize recent data concerning the functional role of GABA in building up and refining neuronal circuits early in development and the molecular mechanisms regulating the E/I balance. A dysfunction of the GABAergic signaling early in development leads to a severe E/I unbalance in neuronal circuits, a condition that may account for some of the behavioral deficits observed in ASD patients.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en la práctica: esta revisión explica teorías sobre cómo se desarrolla el cerebro, no ofrece pautas de apoyo ni tratamientos. Puede ayudar a entender que algunas diferencias sensoriales o de procesamiento en personas autistas podrían tener raíces biológicas tempranas, no en la crianza ni en la voluntad. Sigue observando qué ambientes, ritmos y estímulos le resultan cómodos o abrumadores a tu familiar, y ajústalos con él o ella. Se trata de una revisión narrativa de 2011 que resume estudios de laboratorio, sobre todo en animales y células, sobre el equilibrio entre excitación e inhibición (GABA). Sus límites: no incluye a personas autistas como participantes directos y sus hipótesis no se aplican igual a todos.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change tomorrow: this review explains theories about brain development, not support strategies or treatments. It may help to know that some sensory or processing differences in autistic people could have early biological roots, not causes in parenting or willpower. Keep noticing which environments, rhythms and stimuli feel comfortable or overwhelming for your family member, and adjust them together. This is a 2011 narrative review summarising laboratory research, mostly in animals and cells, on the balance between excitation and inhibition (GABA signalling). Its limits: autistic people did not take part directly, the ideas are hypotheses, and they will not apply in the same way to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I morgon behöver inget ändras: den här översikten förklarar teorier om hjärnans utveckling, inte stödstrategier eller behandlingar. Det kan vara bra att veta att vissa sensoriska skillnader eller skillnader i bearbetning hos autistiska personer kan ha tidiga biologiska rötter, och inte bero på uppfostran eller vilja. Fortsätt att lägga märke till vilka miljöer, rytmer och intryck som känns bekväma eller överväldigande för din närstående, och anpassa dem tillsammans. Det är en narrativ översikt från 2011 som sammanfattar laboratorieforskning, främst på djur och celler, om balansen mellan excitation och hämning (GABA). Begränsningar: autistiska personer deltog inte direkt, idéerna är hypoteser och gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

title: Autism: a "critical period" disorder?
authors: LeBlanc JJ, Fagiolini M
abstract: Cortical circuits in the brain are refined by experience during critical periods early in postnatal life. Critical periods are regulated by the balance of excitatory and inhibitory (E/I) neurotransmission in the brain during development. There is now increasing evidence of E/I imbalance in autism, a complex genetic neurodevelopmental disorder diagnosed by abnormal socialization, impaired communication, and repetitive behaviors or restricted interests. The underlying cause is still largely unknown and there is no fully effective treatment or cure. We propose that alteration of the expression and/or timing of critical period circuit refinement in primary sensory brain areas may significantly contribute to autistic phenotypes, including cognitive and behavioral impairments. Dissection of the cellular and molecular mechanisms governing well-established critical periods represents a powerful tool to identify new potential therapeutic targets to restore normal plasticity and function in affected neuronal circuits.

sheet.es: Para mañana: esta revisión no cambia nada concreto en la rutina diaria. Propone una idea teórica: que en el cerebro autista el momento y la forma en que los circuitos sensoriales se ajustan con la experiencia temprana podrían ser diferentes. Puede ayudar a entender por qué muchas personas autistas viven sonidos, luces o texturas de otra manera; observar y respetar esas diferencias sensoriales sigue siendo útil. Se trata de una revisión teórica de 2011 basada sobre todo en estudios con animales y de laboratorio, sin participantes autistas propios. Su límite: es una hipótesis, no ofrece pruebas directas ni orientaciones prácticas, y usa un enfoque de déficit que hoy se cuestiona.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: this review doesn't change anything concrete in daily routines. It puts forward a theoretical idea: that in autistic brains, the timing and way sensory circuits are shaped by early experience may differ. This can help explain why many autistic people experience sounds, lights or textures differently; noticing and respecting those sensory differences remains worthwhile. It is a 2011 theoretical review drawing mainly on animal and laboratory research, with no autistic participants of its own. Its limit: it is a hypothesis, offers no direct evidence or practical guidance, and uses a deficit framing that is now widely questioned.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon: den här översikten ändrar inget konkret i vardagen. Den lägger fram en teoretisk idé: att tidpunkten och sättet som sinnesbearbetande nätverk i hjärnan formas av tidiga erfarenheter kan skilja sig hos autistiska personer. Det kan hjälpa till att förklara varför många autistiska personer upplever ljud, ljus eller material annorlunda; att lägga märke till och respektera sådana sensoriska skillnader är fortfarande värdefullt. Det är en teoretisk översikt från 2011 som främst bygger på djur- och laboratorieforskning, utan egna autistiska deltagare. Begränsning: det är en hypotes utan direkta belägg eller praktiska råd, och den använder ett bristperspektiv som i dag ifrågasätts.

title: Anxiety disorders in children and adolescents with autistic spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis.
authors: van Steensel FJ, Bögels SM, Perrin S
journal: Clinical child and family psychology review
abstract: There is considerable evidence that children and adolescents with autistic spectrum disorders (ASD) are at increased risk of anxiety and anxiety disorders. However, it is less clear which of the specific DSM-IV anxiety disorders occur most in this population. The present study used meta-analytic techniques to help clarify this issue. A systematic review of the literature identified 31 studies involving 2,121 young people (aged <18 years) with ASD, and where the presence of anxiety disorder was assessed using standardized questionnaires or diagnostic interviews. Across studies, 39.6% of young people with ASD had at least one comorbid DSM-IV anxiety disorder, the most frequent being specific phobia (29.8%) followed by OCD (17.4%) and social anxiety disorder (16.6%). Associations were found between the specific anxiety disorders and ASD subtype, age, IQ, and assessment method (questionnaire versus interview). Implications for the identification and treatment of anxiety in young people with ASD are discussed.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista parece muy preocupado, evita ciertas situaciones o repite rituales que le cuestan, puede valer la pena preguntarse si hay ansiedad detrás, y no atribuirlo todo al autismo. Anotar qué situaciones le generan malestar puede ayudar a hablar con un profesional. Este metaanálisis reunió 31 estudios con 2.121 jóvenes autistas menores de 18 años: cerca del 40 % tenía al menos un trastorno de ansiedad, sobre todo fobias específicas, TOC y ansiedad social. Sus límites: los estudios usaron métodos distintos (cuestionarios o entrevistas), los resultados variaron según la edad y el CI, y las cifras no predicen qué le pasa a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child seems very worried, avoids certain situations or repeats rituals that distress them, it may be worth asking whether anxiety is involved, rather than putting everything down to autism. Noting which situations cause distress can help when talking with a professional. This meta-analysis combined 31 studies with 2,121 autistic young people under 18: about 40% had at least one anxiety disorder, most often specific phobias, OCD and social anxiety. Its limits: studies used different methods (questionnaires or interviews), results varied with age and IQ, and the figures cannot predict what any individual child experiences.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn verkar mycket oroligt, undviker vissa situationer eller upprepar ritualer som känns jobbiga, kan det vara värt att fundera på om ångest finns med, i stället för att tillskriva allt autismen. Att anteckna vilka situationer som väcker obehag kan underlätta samtal med en professionell. Denna metaanalys samlade 31 studier med 2 121 autistiska unga under 18 år: omkring 40 % hade minst en ångeststörning, oftast specifika fobier, tvångssyndrom och social ångest. Begränsningar: studierna använde olika metoder (enkäter eller intervjuer), resultaten varierade med ålder och IK, och siffrorna kan inte förutsäga hur det är för varje enskilt barn.

claim.es: Cerca del 40 % de niños y adolescentes autistas tienen al menos un trastorno de ansiedad; la ansiedad es común, no rara.
claim.en: About 40% of autistic children and adolescents have at least one anxiety disorder; anxiety is common, not rare.
claim.sv: Omkring 40 % av autistiska barn och ungdomar har minst ett ångestsyndrom; ångest är vanligt, inte ovanligt.

supports.es: Leer la agitación o el rechazo como posible ansiedad y reducir la incertidumbre.
supports.en: Reading agitation or refusal as possible anxiety and reducing uncertainty.
supports.sv: Att tolka oro eller vägran som möjlig ångest och minska osäkerheten.

doesNotSupport.es: Diagnosticar ansiedad en casa; eso es cosa de profesionales clínicos.
doesNotSupport.en: Diagnosing anxiety at home; that is for clinicians.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att diagnostisera ångest hemma; det är klinikers sak.

title: Autism spectrum disorders and schizophrenia: meta-analysis of the neural correlates of social cognition.
authors: Sugranyes G, Kyriakopoulos M, Corrigall R, Taylor E, Frangou S
abstract: Context Impaired social cognition is a cardinal feature of Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) and Schizophrenia (SZ). However, the functional neuroanatomy of social cognition in either disorder remains unclear due to variability in primary literature. Additionally, it is not known whether deficits in ASD and SZ arise from similar or disease-specific disruption of the social cognition network. Objective To identify regions most robustly implicated in social cognition processing in SZ and ASD. Data sources Systematic review of English language articles using MEDLINE (1995-2010) and reference lists. Study selection Studies were required to use fMRI to compare ASD or SZ subjects to a matched healthy control group, provide coordinates in standard stereotactic space, and employ standardized facial emotion recognition (FER) or theory of mind (TOM) paradigms. Data extraction Activation foci from studies meeting inclusion criteria (n = 33) were subjected to a quantitative voxel-based meta-analysis using activation likelihood estimation, and encompassed 146 subjects with ASD, 336 SZ patients and 492 healthy controls. Results Both SZ and ASD showed medial prefrontal hypoactivation, which was more pronounced in ASD, while ventrolateral prefrontal dysfunction was associated mostly with SZ. Amygdala hypoactivation was observed in SZ patients during FER and in ASD during more complex ToM tasks. Both disorders were associated with hypoactivation within the Superior Temporal Sulcus (STS) during ToM tasks, but activation in these regions was increased in ASD during affect processing. Disease-specific differences were noted in somatosensory engagement, which was increased in SZ and decreased in ASD. Reduced thalamic activation was uniquely seen in SZ. Conclusions Reduced frontolimbic and STS engagement emerged as a shared feature of social cognition deficits in SZ and ASD. However, there were disease- and stimulus-specific differences. These findings may aid future studies on SZ and ASD and facilitate the formulation of new hypotheses regarding their pathophysiology.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: este estudio no cambia lo que haces mañana. Muestra que, en tareas de laboratorio sobre reconocer emociones en rostros o inferir lo que otros piensan, el cerebro de personas autistas se activa de forma diferente en ciertas regiones, y que esas diferencias no son iguales a las de la esquizofrenia. Sirve para recordar que autismo y esquizofrenia son experiencias distintas. Evidencia: metaanálisis de 33 estudios de resonancia magnética funcional, con 146 personas autistas, 336 con esquizofrenia y 492 controles. Límites: muestras pequeñas, tareas artificiales, datos hasta 2010 y un enfoque centrado en déficits; activación cerebral distinta no indica cómo vive o conecta cada persona.
sheet.en: The practical point: this study does not change what you do tomorrow. It shows that during lab tasks on reading facial emotions or inferring what others think, autistic people's brains activate some regions differently, and these patterns are not the same as in schizophrenia. It is a useful reminder that autism and schizophrenia are distinct experiences. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 33 functional MRI studies including 146 autistic people, 336 people with schizophrenia and 492 controls. Limits: small samples, artificial tasks, data only up to 2010, and a deficit-focused framing; different brain activation says nothing about how any individual person feels, communicates or connects.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: studien ändrar inte vad du gör i morgon. Den visar att autistiska personers hjärnor aktiverar vissa områden annorlunda under laboratorieuppgifter om att läsa känslor i ansikten eller förstå vad andra tänker, och att mönstren skiljer sig från dem vid schizofreni. Den påminner om att autism och schizofreni är olika erfarenheter. Evidens: en metaanalys av 33 studier med funktionell magnetkamera, med 146 autistiska personer, 336 personer med schizofreni och 492 kontrollpersoner. Begränsningar: små grupper, konstgjorda uppgifter, data bara till 2010 och ett bristfokuserat perspektiv; annorlunda hjärnaktivitet säger inget om hur en enskild person känner, kommunicerar eller knyter an.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Rossignol DA, Frye RE
abstract: A comprehensive literature search was performed to collate evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) with two primary objectives. First, features of mitochondrial dysfunction in the general population of children with ASD were identified. Second, characteristics of mitochondrial dysfunction in children with ASD and concomitant mitochondrial disease (MD) were compared with published literature of two general populations: ASD children without MD, and non-ASD children with MD. The prevalence of MD in the general population of ASD was 5.0% (95% confidence interval 3.2, 6.9%), much higher than found in the general population (≈ 0.01%). The prevalence of abnormal biomarker values of mitochondrial dysfunction was high in ASD, much higher than the prevalence of MD. Variances and mean values of many mitochondrial biomarkers (lactate, pyruvate, carnitine and ubiquinone) were significantly different between ASD and controls. Some markers correlated with ASD severity. Neuroimaging, in vitro and post-mortem brain studies were consistent with an elevated prevalence of mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD. Taken together, these findings suggest children with ASD have a spectrum of mitochondrial dysfunction of differing severity. Eighteen publications representing a total of 112 children with ASD and MD (ASD/MD) were identified. The prevalence of developmental regression (52%), seizures (41%), motor delay (51%), gastrointestinal abnormalities (74%), female gender (39%), and elevated lactate (78%) and pyruvate (45%) was significantly higher in ASD/MD compared with the general ASD population. The prevalence of many of these abnormalities was similar to the general population of children with MD, suggesting that ASD/MD represents a distinct subgroup of children with MD. Most ASD/MD cases (79%) were not associated with genetic abnormalities, raising the possibility of secondary mitochondrial dysfunction. Treatment studies for ASD/MD were limited, although improvements were noted in some studies with carnitine, co-enzyme Q10 and B-vitamins. Many studies suffered from limitations, including small sample sizes, referral or publication biases, and variability in protocols for selecting children for MD workup, collecting mitochondrial biomarkers and defining MD. Overall, this evidence supports the notion that mitochondrial dysfunction is associated with ASD. Additional studies are needed to further define the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista ha perdido habilidades que ya tenía, tiene convulsiones, retraso motor o problemas digestivos persistentes, puedes anotar cuándo ocurren y comentarlo con su equipo médico; a veces vale la pena revisar cómo funciona la energía de las células (mitocondrias). No es motivo de alarma ni afecta a la mayoría de personas autistas. Este metaanálisis reunió estudios publicados, incluidos 112 niños autistas con enfermedad mitocondrial, y estimó que alrededor del 5 % de los niños autistas podría tenerla. Sus límites: muestras pequeñas, sesgos de derivación y publicación, y criterios muy distintos entre estudios; los datos sobre suplementos son escasos y no sirven como recomendación.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has lost skills they once had, has seizures, motor delays or ongoing digestive problems, you can note when these happen and bring them to their medical team; sometimes it is worth looking at how their cells produce energy (mitochondria). This is not cause for alarm and does not apply to most autistic people. This meta-analysis pooled published studies, including 112 autistic children with mitochondrial disease, and estimated that about 5% of autistic children may have it. Its limits: small samples, referral and publication bias, and very different criteria across studies; evidence on supplements is scarce and is not a recommendation.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har tappat färdigheter det tidigare hade, har epileptiska anfall, motorisk försening eller långvariga magproblem kan du anteckna när det händer och ta upp det med barnets vårdteam; ibland kan det vara värt att undersöka hur cellernas energiproduktion (mitokondrierna) fungerar. Det är ingen anledning till oro och gäller inte de flesta autistiska personer. Denna metaanalys sammanställde publicerade studier, bland annat 112 autistiska barn med mitokondriell sjukdom, och uppskattade att omkring 5 % av autistiska barn kan ha det. Begränsningar: små urval, remiss- och publiceringsbias samt olika kriterier mellan studierna; underlaget om kosttillskott är litet och utgör ingen rekommendation.

title: Age-dependent brain gene expression and copy number anomalies in autism suggest distinct pathological processes at young versus mature ages.
authors: Chow ML, Pramparo T, Winn ME, Barnes CC, Li HR, Weiss L, Fan JB, Murray S, April C, Belinson H, Fu XD, Wynshaw-Boris A, Schork NJ, Courchesne E
abstract: Autism is a highly heritable neurodevelopmental disorder, yet the genetic underpinnings of the disorder are largely unknown. Aberrant brain overgrowth is a well-replicated observation in the autism literature; but association, linkage, and expression studies have not identified genetic factors that explain this trajectory. Few studies have had sufficient statistical power to investigate whole-genome gene expression and genotypic variation in the autistic brain, especially in regions that display the greatest growth abnormality. Previous functional genomic studies have identified possible alterations in transcript levels of genes related to neurodevelopment and immune function. Thus, there is a need for genetic studies involving key brain regions to replicate these findings and solidify the role of particular functional pathways in autism pathogenesis. We therefore sought to identify abnormal brain gene expression patterns via whole-genome analysis of mRNA levels and copy number variations (CNVs) in autistic and control postmortem brain samples. We focused on prefrontal cortex tissue where excess neuron numbers and cortical overgrowth are pronounced in the majority of autism cases. We found evidence for dysregulation in pathways governing cell number, cortical patterning, and differentiation in young autistic prefrontal cortex. In contrast, adult autistic prefrontal cortex showed dysregulation of signaling and repair pathways. Genes regulating cell cycle also exhibited autism-specific CNVs in DNA derived from prefrontal cortex, and these genes were significantly associated with autism in genome-wide association study datasets. Our results suggest that CNVs and age-dependent gene expression changes in autism may reflect distinct pathological processes in the developing versus the mature autistic prefrontal cortex. Our results raise the hypothesis that genetic dysregulation in the developing brain leads to abnormal regional patterning, excess prefrontal neurons, cortical overgrowth, and neural dysfunction in autism.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en el día a día: este estudio describe biología del cerebro, no estrategias de apoyo. Puede ayudar saber que el autismo tiene raíces del desarrollo y genéticas, y que no es culpa de la crianza. Las necesidades de una persona autista también pueden cambiar con la edad, así que conviene revisar los apoyos a lo largo de la vida. En cuanto a la evidencia, se analizó la expresión génica y las variaciones genéticas en tejido cerebral post mortem de la corteza prefrontal de personas autistas y no autistas, de edades jóvenes y adultas, junto con datos genéticos de otros estudios. Entre sus límites, hubo pocas muestras cerebrales, los resultados son hipótesis y no permiten predecir nada sobre una persona concreta.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change in daily routines tomorrow: this study describes brain biology, not support strategies. It may help to know that autism has developmental and genetic roots and is not caused by parenting. An autistic person's needs may also shift with age, so it is worth revisiting supports across the lifespan. As evidence, researchers analysed gene expression and genetic variations in post-mortem prefrontal brain tissue from autistic and non-autistic people of younger and adult ages, alongside genetic data from other studies. Its limits are that there were few brain samples, the findings remain hypotheses, and they cannot predict anything about an individual.
sheet.sv: I morgon behöver inget ändras i vardagen: studien beskriver hjärnans biologi, inte stödstrategier. Det kan ändå vara bra att veta att autism har utvecklingsmässiga och genetiska rötter och inte orsakas av föräldraskap. En autistisk persons behov kan också förändras med åldern, så det är värt att se över stödet genom hela livet. Som underlag analyserade forskarna genuttryck och genetiska variationer i hjärnvävnad från pannloben, tagen efter döden från autistiska och icke-autistiska personer i yngre och vuxen ålder, tillsammans med genetiska data från andra studier. Begränsningarna är att det fanns få hjärnprover, att resultaten är hypoteser och att de inte kan förutsäga något om en enskild person.

title: A review of research trends in physiological abnormalities in autism spectrum disorders: immune dysregulation, inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and environmental toxicant exposures.
authors: Rossignol DA, Frye RE
abstract: Recent studies have implicated physiological and metabolic abnormalities in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and other psychiatric disorders, particularly immune dysregulation or inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and environmental toxicant exposures ('four major areas'). The aim of this study was to determine trends in the literature on these topics with respect to ASD. A comprehensive literature search from 1971 to 2010 was performed in these four major areas in ASD with three objectives. First, publications were divided by several criteria, including whether or not they implicated an association between the physiological abnormality and ASD. A large percentage of publications implicated an association between ASD and immune dysregulation/inflammation (416 out of 437 publications, 95%), oxidative stress (all 115), mitochondrial dysfunction (145 of 153, 95%) and toxicant exposures (170 of 190, 89%). Second, the strength of evidence for publications in each area was computed using a validated scale. The strongest evidence was for immune dysregulation/inflammation and oxidative stress, followed by toxicant exposures and mitochondrial dysfunction. In all areas, at least 45% of the publications were rated as providing strong evidence for an association between the physiological abnormalities and ASD. Third, the time trends in the four major areas were compared with trends in neuroimaging, neuropathology, theory of mind and genetics ('four comparison areas'). The number of publications per 5-year block in all eight areas was calculated in order to identify significant changes in trends. Prior to 1986, only 12 publications were identified in the four major areas and 51 in the four comparison areas (42 for genetics). For each 5-year period, the total number of publications in the eight combined areas increased progressively. Most publications (552 of 895, 62%) in the four major areas were published in the last 5 years (2006-2010). Evaluation of trends between the four major areas and the four comparison areas demonstrated that the largest relative growth was in immune dysregulation/inflammation, oxidative stress, toxicant exposures, genetics and neuroimaging. Research on mitochondrial dysfunction started growing in the last 5 years. Theory of mind and neuropathology research has declined in recent years. Although most publications implicated an association between the four major areas and ASD, publication bias may have led to an overestimation of this association. Further research into these physiological areas may provide insight into general or subset-specific processes that could contribute to the development of ASD and other psychiatric disorders.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no cambia nada de lo que hagas mañana por la mañana. Muestra que la investigación sobre inflamación, estrés oxidativo, mitocondrias y tóxicos ambientales en el autismo creció mucho entre 2006 y 2010. No ofrece pruebas, dietas ni tratamientos. Si te preocupa la salud física de tu hijo o hija autista, por ejemplo infecciones frecuentes, cansancio o problemas digestivos, coméntalo con su médico como harías con cualquier niño. Ten cautela con productos que prometen «desintoxicar». Se trata de una revisión de unas 900 publicaciones de 1971 a 2010, no de un estudio con participantes. Sus límites: los propios autores señalan que el sesgo de publicación puede exagerar estas asociaciones, y asociación no significa causa.
sheet.en: This review changes nothing about what you do tomorrow morning. It shows that research on inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondria and environmental toxicants in autism grew sharply between 2006 and 2010. It offers no tests, diets or treatments. If you are concerned about your autistic child's physical health, such as frequent infections, fatigue or digestive problems, raise it with their doctor as you would for any child. Be cautious with products promising to "detox". The evidence comes from a review of about 900 publications from 1971 to 2010, not a study with participants. Its limits: the authors themselves note that publication bias may overstate these associations, and association does not mean cause.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ändrar ingenting i det du gör i morgon bitti. Den visar att forskningen om inflammation, oxidativ stress, mitokondrier och miljögifter vid autism ökade kraftigt mellan 2006 och 2010. Den erbjuder inga tester, dieter eller behandlingar. Om du är orolig för ditt autistiska barns fysiska hälsa, till exempel täta infektioner, trötthet eller magbesvär, ta upp det med läkaren precis som för vilket barn som helst. Var försiktig med produkter som lovar att "avgifta". Underlaget är en genomgång av cirka 900 publikationer från 1971–2010, inte en studie med deltagare. Begränsningar: författarna påpekar själva att publiceringsbias kan överdriva sambanden, och ett samband betyder inte orsak.

title: An exploration of sensory and movement differences from the perspective of individuals with autism.
authors: Robledo J, Donnellan AM, Strandt-Conroy K
abstract: Parents, teachers, and people who themselves experience sensory and movement differences have consistently reported disturbances of sensation and movement associated with autism. Our review of the literature has revealed both historical and recent references to and research about sensory and movement difference characteristics and symptoms for individuals with autism. What is notably infrequent in this literature, however, is research that highlights the perspective of the individual with autism. If we wish to truly understand the experience of sensory and movement differences for individuals with autism, we must explore their experiences and perspectives. This study presents a qualitative analysis of more than 40 h in-depth inquiry into the lives of five individuals with the autism label. Data were sorted into six categories: perception, action, posture, emotion, communication, and cognition. The insights into sensory and movement differences and autism offered by these individuals was illuminating. We found that the data strongly supported the presence of disruption of organization and regulation of sensory and movement differences in the lived experience of these participants with autism. The present data suggests that in autism this disruption of organization and regulation is amplified in terms of quantity, quality, intensity, and may affect everyday life. These data contribute to a more expansive view of autism that incorporates the possibility that autism is a disorder that affects motor planning, behavior, communication, the sensory motor system, and the dynamic interaction of all of these.

sheet.es: Si a tu familiar le cuesta empezar, detener o cambiar un movimiento, o responder cuando hay mucho ruido o luz, puede no ser falta de ganas ni de comprensión. Mañana prueba a darle más tiempo, reducir estímulos y preguntarle (con palabras, imágenes o gestos) qué le ayuda a organizar su cuerpo. Sus explicaciones valen tanto como lo que tú observas. Este estudio cualitativo analizó más de 40 horas de conversaciones con cinco personas autistas sobre percepción, movimiento, postura, emociones, comunicación y pensamiento. Al ser solo cinco personas, sus experiencias iluminan, pero no describen a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If your family member struggles to start, stop or switch a movement, or to respond when there is a lot of noise or light, it may not be a lack of willingness or understanding. Tomorrow, try giving extra time, lowering sensory input, and asking (with words, pictures or gestures) what helps them organise their body. Their own explanations matter as much as what you observe. This qualitative study analysed over 40 hours of in-depth conversations with five autistic people about perception, movement, posture, emotion, communication and thinking. With only five participants, their experiences are illuminating but do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om din anhöriga har svårt att starta, stoppa eller byta en rörelse, eller att svara när det är mycket ljud eller ljus, behöver det inte handla om ovilja eller bristande förståelse. Prova i morgon att ge mer tid, minska intrycken och fråga (med ord, bilder eller gester) vad som hjälper hen att organisera kroppen. Hens egna förklaringar är lika viktiga som det du ser. Den här kvalitativa studien analyserade över 40 timmars djupsamtal med fem autistiska personer om perception, rörelse, hållning, känslor, kommunikation och tänkande. Med bara fem deltagare ger erfarenheterna viktiga insikter, men de beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Autism risk factors: genes, environment, and gene-environment interactions.
authors: Chaste P, Leboyer M
abstract: The aim of this review is to summarize the key findings from genetic and epidemiological research, which show that autism is a complex disorder resulting from the combination of genetic and environmental factors. Remarkable advances in the knowledge of genetic causes of autism have resulted from the great efforts made in the field of genetics. The identification of specific alleles contributing to the autism spectrum has supplied important pieces for the autism puzzle. However, many questions remain unanswered, and new questions are raised by recent results. Moreover, given the amount of evidence supporting a significant contribution of environmental factors to autism risk, it is now clear that the search for environmental factors should be reinforced. One aspect of this search that has been neglected so far is the study of interactions between genes and environmental factors.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas «¿qué hice mal?», esta revisión ofrece una respuesta tranquilizadora: el autismo surge de una combinación compleja de muchos factores genéticos y ambientales, no de una única causa ni de decisiones de crianza. Mañana puedes dejar a un lado la culpa y centrar tu energía en conocer cómo percibe el mundo tu hijo o hija y qué apoyos le sirven. Se trata de una revisión narrativa de 2012 que resume estudios genéticos y epidemiológicos, no de un estudio con participantes propios. Sus límites: es anterior a mucha investigación reciente, usa un lenguaje de «riesgo» y «trastorno», y no ofrece pautas prácticas para ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you've been asking yourself "what did I do wrong?", this review offers a calming answer: autism arises from a complex mix of many genetic and environmental factors, not from a single cause or from parenting choices. Tomorrow you can set guilt aside and put your energy into learning how your child experiences the world and which supports actually help. This is a 2012 narrative review summarising genetic and epidemiological research, not a study with its own participants. Its limits: it predates much recent research, frames autism in terms of "risk" and "disorder", and gives no practical guidance for any individual person.
sheet.sv: Om du har frågat dig själv ”vad gjorde jag fel?” ger den här översikten ett lugnande svar: autism uppstår ur en komplex blandning av många genetiska faktorer och miljöfaktorer, inte ur en enda orsak eller ur föräldrarnas val. I morgon kan du lägga skulden åt sidan och i stället lägga din energi på att förstå hur ditt barn upplever världen och vilket stöd som faktiskt hjälper. Det här är en narrativ översikt från 2012 som sammanfattar genetisk och epidemiologisk forskning, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Begränsningar: den är äldre än mycket ny forskning, beskriver autism i termer av ”risk” och ”störning” och ger inga praktiska råd för en enskild person.

title: Rethinking autism: implications of sensory and movement differences for understanding and support.
authors: Donnellan AM, Hill DA, Leary MR
abstract: For decades autism has been defined as a triad of deficits in social interaction, communication, and imaginative play. Though there is now broad acknowledgment of the neurological basis of autism, there is little attention paid to the contribution of such neurological differences to a person's development and functioning. Communication, relationship, and participation require neurological systems to coordinate and synchronize the organization and regulation of sensory information and movement. Developmental differences in these abilities are likely to result in differences in the way a person behaves and expresses intention and meaning. The present paper shares our emerging awareness that people may struggle with difficulties that are not immediately evident to an outsider. This paper explores the symptoms of sensory and movement differences and the possible implications for autistic people. It provides a review of the history and literature that describes the neurological basis for many of the socalled behavioral differences that people experience. The paper emphasizes the importance of our acknowledgment that a social interpretation of differences in behavior, relationship, and communication can lead us far away from the lived experience of individuals with the autism label and those who support them. We suggest alternative ways to address the challenges faced by people with autism.

sheet.es: Cuando tu hijo o hija autista no responde, se queda inmóvil o repite un movimiento, puede no ser falta de interés ni desobediencia: quizá su cuerpo tarda en organizar lo que percibe y en iniciar o detener una acción. Mañana prueba a dar más tiempo, ofrecer apoyo físico o visual si lo acepta, reducir ruido o luz, y preguntar qué le ayuda. Interpreta la conducta con curiosidad, no como un mensaje social. Este artículo revisa la historia y la literatura sobre diferencias sensoriales y de movimiento, e incluye experiencias de personas autistas. Es una revisión narrativa de 2012, no un ensayo que compare apoyos, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: When your autistic child doesn't respond, freezes, or repeats a movement, it may not mean disinterest or defiance: their body may need time to organise what they sense and to start or stop an action. Tomorrow, try giving extra time, offering physical or visual support if welcome, lowering noise or light, and asking what helps. Read behaviour with curiosity rather than as a social message. This paper reviews the history and literature on sensory and movement differences, drawing on autistic people's experiences. It is a 2012 narrative review, not a trial comparing supports, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: När ditt autistiska barn inte svarar, fastnar eller upprepar en rörelse behöver det inte betyda ointresse eller trots: kroppen kan behöva tid att organisera sinnesintryck och att starta eller stoppa en handling. I morgon kan du ge mer tid, erbjuda fysiskt eller visuellt stöd om det är välkommet, sänka ljud eller ljus och fråga vad som hjälper. Tolka beteendet med nyfikenhet snarare än som ett socialt budskap. Artikeln går igenom historik och forskning om sensoriska och motoriska skillnader och bygger på autistiska personers erfarenheter. Det är en berättande översikt från 2012, ingen studie som jämför stödformer, och varje person är olik.

title: Embodiment and sense-making in autism.
authors: De Jaegher H
abstract: In this article, I sketch an enactive account of autism. For the enactive approach to cognition, embodiment, experience, and social interaction are fundamental to understanding mind and subjectivity. Enaction defines cognition as sense-making: the way cognitive agents meaningfully connect with their world, based on their needs and goals as self-organizing, self-maintaining, embodied agents. In the social realm, the interactive coordination of embodied sense-making activities with others lets us participate in each other's sense-making (social understanding = participatory sense-making). The enactive approach provides new concepts to overcome the problems of traditional functionalist accounts of autism, which can only give a piecemeal and disintegrated view because they consider cognition, communication, and perception separately, do not take embodied into account, and are methodologically individualistic. Applying the concepts of enaction to autism, I show: How embodiment and sense-making connect, i.e., how autistic particularities of moving, perceiving, and emoting relate to how people with autism make sense of their world. For instance, restricted interests or preference for detail will have certain sensorimotor correlates, as well as specific meaning for autistic people.That reduced flexibility in interactional coordination correlates with difficulties in participatory sense-making. At the same time, seemingly irrelevant "autistic behaviors" can be quite attuned to the interactive context. I illustrate this complexity in the case of echolalia. An enactive account of autism starts from the embodiment, experience, and social interactions of autistic people. Enaction brings together the sensorimotor, cognitive, social, experiential, and affective aspects of autism in a coherent framework based on a complex non-linear multi-causality. This foundation allows to build new bridges between autistic people and their often non-autistic context, and to improve quality of life prospects.

sheet.es: Mañana, cuando tu hijo o hija repita frases (ecolalia), se mueva de forma particular o se centre en detalles, prueba a preguntarte qué sentido tiene eso para él o ella en ese momento, en lugar de verlo como algo sin importancia. Muchas veces estas conductas encajan con lo que está pasando en la interacción. Ajustar tu ritmo, tus movimientos y tu forma de hablar al suyo puede facilitar que construyáis significado juntos. La evidencia: es un artículo teórico (2013) que propone el enfoque «enactivo», uniendo cuerpo, percepción, emoción e interacción social en el autismo. Límites: no recoge datos nuevos de participantes; son ideas para comprender, no una regla válida para cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, when your child repeats phrases (echolalia), moves in their own way, or focuses on details, try asking what that means for them right now, rather than treating it as irrelevant. These behaviours are often tuned to what is happening in the interaction. Matching your pace, movement and way of speaking to theirs can help you build meaning together. The evidence: this is a 2013 theoretical article proposing an 'enactive' approach that connects body, perception, emotion and social interaction in autism. Limits: it does not report new data from participants; it offers a way of understanding, not a rule that fits every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I morgon, när ditt barn upprepar fraser (ekolali), rör sig på sitt eget sätt eller fokuserar på detaljer, försök fråga dig vad det betyder för barnet just nu, i stället för att se det som oviktigt. Sådana beteenden är ofta anpassade till det som händer i samspelet. Att matcha ditt tempo, dina rörelser och ditt sätt att prata med barnets kan hjälpa er att skapa mening tillsammans. Evidensen: en teoretisk artikel från 2013 som föreslår ett ”enaktivt” synsätt där kropp, perception, känslor och socialt samspel hänger ihop vid autism. Begränsningar: den redovisar inga nya data från deltagare; den ger ett sätt att förstå, inte en regel för varje autistisk person.

title: Comparison of healthcare experiences in autistic and non-autistic adults: a cross-sectional online survey facilitated by an academic-community partnership.
authors: Nicolaidis C, Raymaker D, McDonald K, Dern S, Boisclair WC, Ashkenazy E, Baggs A

claim.es: Adultos autistas informan peor comunicación con profesionales sanitarios y más necesidades no atendidas que adultos no autistas.
claim.en: Autistic adults report worse communication with healthcare providers and more unmet needs than non-autistic adults.
claim.sv: Autistiska vuxna rapporterar sämre kommunikation med vårdpersonal och fler ouppfyllda behov än icke-autistiska vuxna.

supports.es: Llevar a las citas un resumen escrito y las preferencias de comunicación de la persona.
supports.en: Bringing a written summary and the person's communication preferences to appointments.
supports.sv: Att ta med en skriftlig sammanfattning och personens kommunikationspreferenser till besök.

doesNotSupport.es: Que haya que evitar la sanidad; significa que debe hacerse accesible.
doesNotSupport.en: That healthcare should be avoided; it means it must be made accessible.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att vården ska undvikas; det betyder att den måste göras tillgänglig.

title: Sniffing around oxytocin: review and meta-analyses of trials in healthy and clinical groups with implications for pharmacotherapy.
authors: Bakermans-Kranenburg MJ, van I Jzendoorn MH
abstract: The popularity of oxytocin (OT) has grown exponentially during the past decade, and so has the number of OT trials in healthy and clinical groups. We take stock of the evidence from these studies to explore potentials and limitations of pharmacotherapeutic applications. In healthy participants, intranasally administered OT leads to better emotion recognition and more trust in conspecifics, but the effects appear to be moderated by context (perceived threat of the 'out-group'), personality and childhood experiences. In individuals with untoward childhood experiences, positive behavioral or neurobiological effects seem lowered or absent. In 19 clinical trials, covering autism, social anxiety, postnatal depression, obsessive-compulsive problems, schizophrenia, borderline personality disorder and post-traumatic stress, the effects of OT administration were tested, with doses ranging from 15 IU to more than 7000 IU. The combined effect size was d=0.32 (N=304; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.18-0.47; P<0.01). However, of all disorders, only studies on autism spectrum disorder showed a significant combined effect size (d=0.57; N=68; 95% CI: 0.15-0.99; P<0.01).
