We hypothesize that for some of the other disorders, etiological factors rooted in negative childhood experiences may also have a role in the diminished effectiveness of treatment with OT.

sheet.es: Si oye hablar de la oxitocina nasal como ayuda para la vida social de una persona autista, conviene tomarlo con calma: es un tema de investigación, no una solución lista para usar en casa. Cualquier pregunta sobre ella corresponde al equipo médico, y mientras tanto lo que más ayuda sigue siendo un entorno predecible, comunicación respetuosa y apoyos que la propia persona valora. Este metaanálisis de 2013 reunió 19 ensayos clínicos en varias condiciones; en autismo encontró un efecto moderado, pero basado solo en 68 participantes. Los estudios eran pequeños y diversos, y la oxitocina mostró efectos que dependían mucho del contexto y de las experiencias vividas, así que no se puede generalizar a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you hear about nasal oxytocin as a way to help an autistic person socially, it is worth staying calm and cautious: this is a research topic, not a ready-made solution to try at home. Any questions about it belong with the medical team, and meanwhile what helps most is still a predictable environment, respectful communication and supports the person themselves values. This 2013 meta-analysis pooled 19 clinical trials across several conditions; for autism it found a moderate effect, but based on only 68 participants. The trials were small and varied, and oxytocin's effects depended strongly on context and life experiences, so results cannot be applied to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du hör talas om nässpray med oxytocin som ett sätt att stödja en autistisk person socialt, är det klokt att vara lugn och försiktig: det är ett forskningsområde, inte en färdig lösning att prova hemma. Frågor om det hör hemma hos vårdteamet, och under tiden hjälper fortfarande en förutsägbar miljö, respektfull kommunikation och stöd som personen själv uppskattar mest. Denna metaanalys från 2013 sammanställde 19 kliniska studier inom flera tillstånd; för autism fanns en måttlig effekt, men bara utifrån 68 deltagare. Studierna var små och olika, och effekterna berodde mycket på sammanhang och livserfarenheter, så resultaten gäller inte varje person.

title: Autism as a developmental disorder in intentional movement and affective engagement.
authors: Trevarthen C, Delafield-Butt JT
abstract: We review evidence that autistic spectrum disorders have their origin in early prenatal failure of development in systems that program timing, serial coordination and prospective control of movements, and that regulate affective evaluations of experiences. There are effects in early infancy, before medical diagnosis, especially in motor sequencing, selective or exploratory attention, affective expression and intersubjective engagement with parents. These are followed by retardation of cognitive development and language learning in the second or third year, which lead to a diagnosis of ASD. The early signs relate to abnormalities that have been found in brain stem systems and cerebellum in the embryo or early fetal stage, before the cerebral neocortex is functional, and they have clear consequences in infancy when neocortical systems are intensively elaborated. We propose, with evidence of the disturbances of posture, locomotion and prospective motor control in children with autism, as well as of their facial expression of interest and affect, and attention to other persons' expressions, that examination of the psychobiology of motor affective disorders, rather than later developing cognitive or linguistic ones, may facilitate early diagnosis. Research in this area may also explain how intense interaction, imitation or "expressive art" therapies, which respond intimately with motor activities, are effective at later stages. Exceptional talents of some autistic people may be acquired compensations for basic problems with expectant self-regulations of movement, attention and emotion.

sheet.es: Mañana puede prestar atención a cómo se mueve su hijo o hija autista: el ritmo, la coordinación y cómo anticipa los movimientos. Ir más despacio, sincronizarse con su ritmo, imitar sus gestos o compartir música, movimiento o arte puede facilitar la conexión sin exigir palabras. Respetar sus intereses intensos también tiene sentido: pueden ser fortalezas propias. La evidencia proviene de una revisión teórica que reúne estudios sobre movimiento, atención y expresión emocional en bebés y niños autistas. Sus límites: es una propuesta interpretativa, no un ensayo nuevo, usa un lenguaje de déficit y no demuestra que una terapia concreta funcione para cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, you might notice how your autistic child moves: their timing, coordination and how they anticipate actions. Slowing down, matching their rhythm, imitating their gestures, or sharing music, movement or art can open connection without demanding words. Honouring intense interests also makes sense; they may be genuine strengths. The evidence comes from a theoretical review that brings together studies on movement, attention and emotional expression in autistic infants and children. Its limits: it is an interpretive proposal rather than new trial data, it uses deficit-based language, and it does not show that any specific therapy works for every person.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du lägga märke till hur ditt autistiska barn rör sig: tajming, koordination och hur hen förbereder rörelser. Att sakta ner, följa barnets rytm, härma gester eller dela musik, rörelse eller skapande kan ge kontakt utan krav på ord. Att respektera starka intressen är också klokt; de kan vara verkliga styrkor. Underlaget är en teoretisk översikt som samlar studier om rörelse, uppmärksamhet och känslouttryck hos autistiska spädbarn och barn. Begränsningar: det är ett tolkningsförslag, inte nya försöksdata, språket utgår från brister, och den visar inte att någon särskild terapi fungerar för alla.

title: Comparison of white matter integrity between autism spectrum disorder subjects and typically developing individuals: a meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging tractography studies.
authors: Aoki Y, Abe O, Nippashi Y, Yamasue H
abstract: Background Aberrant brain connectivity, especially with long-distance underconnectivity, has been recognized as a candidate pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorders. However, a number of diffusion tensor imaging studies investigating people with autism spectrum disorders have yielded inconsistent results. Methods To test the long-distance underconnectivity hypothesis, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging studies in subjects with autism spectrum disorder. Diffusion tensor imaging studies comparing individuals with autism spectrum disorders with typically developing individuals were searched using MEDLINE, Web of Science and EMBASE from 1980 through 1 August 2012. Standardized mean differences were calculated as an effect size of the tracts. Results A comprehensive literature search identified 25 relevant diffusion tensor imaging studies comparing autism spectrum disorders and typical development with regions-of-interest methods. Among these, 14 studies examining regions of interest with suprathreshold sample sizes were included in the meta-analysis. A random-effects model demonstrated significant fractional anisotropy reductions in the corpus callosum (P = 0.023, n = 387 (autism spectrum disorders/typically developing individuals: 208/179)), left uncinate fasciculus (P = 0.011, n = 242 (117/125)), and left superior longitudinal fasciculus (P = 0.016, n = 182 (96/86)), and significant increases of mean diffusivity in the corpus callosum (P = 0.006, n = 254 (129/125)) and superior longitudinal fasciculus bilaterally (P = 0.031 and 0.011, left and right, respectively, n = 109 (51/58)), in subjects with autism spectrum disorders compared with typically developing individuals with no significant publication bias. Conclusion The current meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging studies in subjects with autism spectrum disorders emphasizes important roles of the superior longitudinal fasciculus, uncinate fasciculus, and corpus callosum in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorders and supports the long-distance underconnectivity hypothesis.

sheet.es: Para mañana: este estudio no cambia lo que haces en casa ni sirve para diagnosticar a nadie. Sugiere que, en promedio, algunas conexiones cerebrales de larga distancia funcionan de forma diferente en personas autistas, lo que puede ayudar a entender por qué integrar mucha información a la vez cuesta más energía. Ofrecer tiempo extra, una cosa cada vez y apoyos visuales sigue siendo una forma respetuosa de acompañar. Es un metaanálisis de 14 estudios de imagen cerebral (DTI) que comparan a personas autistas y no autistas, con grupos de 109 a 387 participantes. Límites: muestras pequeñas, métodos distintos entre estudios y promedios de grupo que no describen a cada persona.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: this study does not change what you do at home and cannot diagnose anyone. It suggests that, on average, some long-distance brain connections work differently in autistic people, which may help explain why combining lots of information at once can take more energy. Offering extra time, one thing at a time and visual supports remains a respectful way to help. This is a meta-analysis of 14 brain imaging (DTI) studies comparing autistic and non-autistic people, with groups of 109 to 387 participants. Limits: small samples, differing methods across studies, and group averages that do not describe any individual person.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon: studien ändrar inte vad du gör hemma och kan inte användas för att ställa diagnos. Den tyder på att vissa långa förbindelser i hjärnan i genomsnitt fungerar annorlunda hos autistiska personer, vilket kan bidra till att förklara varför det kan kräva mer energi att hantera mycket information samtidigt. Att ge extra tid, en sak i taget och visuellt stöd är fortfarande ett respektfullt sätt att stötta. Det är en metaanalys av 14 hjärnavbildningsstudier (DTI) som jämför autistiska och icke-autistiska personer, med grupper på 109 till 387 deltagare. Begränsningar: små urval, olika metoder mellan studierna och gruppgenomsnitt som inte beskriver enskilda personer.

title: Global prevalence of autism and other pervasive developmental disorders.
authors: Elsabbagh M, Divan G, Koh YJ, Kim YS, Kauchali S, Marcín C, Montiel-Nava C, Patel V, Paula CS, Wang C, Yasamy MT, Fombonne E
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: We provide a systematic review of epidemiological surveys of autistic disorder and pervasive developmental disorders (PDDs) worldwide. A secondary aim was to consider the possible impact of geographic, cultural/ethnic, and socioeconomic factors on prevalence estimates and on clinical presentation of PDD. Based on the evidence reviewed, the median of prevalence estimates of autism spectrum disorders was 62/10 000. While existing estimates are variable, the evidence reviewed does not support differences in PDD prevalence by geographic region nor of a strong impact of ethnic/cultural or socioeconomic factors. However, power to detect such effects is seriously limited in existing data sets, particularly in low-income countries. While it is clear that prevalence estimates have increased over time and these vary in different neighboring and distant regions, these findings most likely represent broadening of the diagnostic concets, diagnostic switching from other developmental disabilities to PDD, service availability, and awareness of autistic spectrum disorders in both the lay and professional public. The lack of evidence from the majority of the world's population suggests a critical need for further research and capacity building in low- and middle-income countries.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija es autista, no está solo: en 2012, alrededor de 6 de cada 1000 personas recibían este diagnóstico en el mundo, sin grandes diferencias claras entre regiones, culturas o niveles económicos. El aumento de diagnósticos con los años se explica sobre todo por criterios más amplios, más servicios y más conocimiento, no por una «epidemia». Puede ser útil buscar comunidades de familias y personas autistas cerca de usted. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de encuestas epidemiológicas de muchos países. Su límite: casi no hay datos de países de ingresos bajos y medios, donde vive la mayoría de la población mundial.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic, you are not alone: in 2012, about 6 in every 1,000 people worldwide had an autism diagnosis, with no clear large differences between regions, cultures or income levels. The rise in diagnoses over time is mostly explained by broader criteria, more services and greater awareness, not an "epidemic". It may help to look for local communities of families and autistic people. This is a systematic review of epidemiological surveys from many countries. Its limit: there is very little data from low- and middle-income countries, where most of the world's population lives.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt är ni inte ensamma: 2012 hade ungefär 6 av 1 000 människor i världen en autismdiagnos, utan tydliga stora skillnader mellan regioner, kulturer eller inkomstnivåer. Att diagnoserna ökat över tid förklaras främst av bredare kriterier, fler stödinsatser och större kunskap, inte av en "epidemi". Det kan hjälpa att söka gemenskap med andra familjer och autistiska personer i närheten. Detta är en systematisk översikt av epidemiologiska undersökningar från många länder. Begränsning: det finns mycket lite data från låg- och medelinkomstländer, där största delen av världens befolkning bor.

title: Non-specialist psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents with intellectual disability or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Reichow B, Servili C, Yasamy MT, Barbui C, Saxena S
abstract: Background The development of effective treatments for use by non-specialists is listed among the top research priorities for improving the lives of people with mental illness worldwide. The purpose of this review is to appraise which interventions for children with intellectual disabilities or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders delivered by non-specialist care providers in community settings produce benefits when compared to either a no-treatment control group or treatment-as-usual comparator. Methods and findings We systematically searched electronic databases through 24 June 2013 to locate prospective controlled studies of psychosocial interventions delivered by non-specialist providers to children with intellectual disabilities or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders. We screened 234 full papers, of which 34 articles describing 29 studies involving 1,305 participants were included. A majority of the studies included children exclusively with a diagnosis of lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders (15 of 29, 52%). Fifteen of twenty-nine studies (52%) were randomized controlled trials and just under half of all effect sizes (29 of 59, 49%) were greater than 0.50, of which 18 (62%) were statistically significant. For behavior analytic interventions, the best outcomes were shown for development and daily skills; cognitive rehabilitation, training, and support interventions were found to be most effective for improving developmental outcomes, and parent training interventions to be most effective for improving developmental, behavioral, and family outcomes. We also conducted additional subgroup analyses using harvest plots. Limitations include the studies' potential for performance bias and that few were conducted in lower- and middle-income countries. Conclusions The findings of this review support the delivery of psychosocial interventions by non-specialist providers to children who have intellectual disabilities or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders. Given the scarcity of specialists in many low-resource settings, including many lower- and middle-income countries, these findings may provide guidance for scale-up efforts for improving outcomes for children with developmental disorders or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders. Protocol registration PROSPERO CRD42012002641

sheet.es: Si no tienes acceso a especialistas, no estás sin opciones: los apoyos aplicados por familias, docentes o personal comunitario formado pueden ayudar. Pide a tu servicio local formación para madres y padres, o apoyo práctico para habilidades cotidianas, y adáptalo al ritmo y los intereses de tu hijo o hija. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 29 estudios con 1.305 niños y adolescentes autistas con altas necesidades de apoyo o con discapacidad intelectual; la formación a familias mostró beneficios en desarrollo, conducta y bienestar familiar. Límites: muchos estudios podían tener sesgos, pocos se hicieron en países de ingresos bajos y medios, y los resultados no se aplican igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If specialists are hard to reach, you still have options: support delivered by trained parents, teachers or community workers can help. Ask your local service about parent training or practical support for everyday skills, and shape it around your child's pace and interests. This systematic review pooled 29 studies with 1,305 autistic children and teens with high support needs or with intellectual disability; parent training showed benefits for development, behaviour and family wellbeing. Limits: many studies risked bias, few were done in low- and middle-income countries, and results won't apply the same way to every person.
sheet.sv: Om specialister är svåra att nå finns ändå möjligheter: stöd som ges av utbildade föräldrar, lärare eller personal i närmiljön kan hjälpa. Fråga din lokala verksamhet om föräldrautbildning eller praktiskt stöd för vardagsfärdigheter, och anpassa det efter ditt barns tempo och intressen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 29 studier med 1 305 autistiska barn och unga med stora stödbehov eller med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning; föräldrautbildning gav fördelar för utveckling, beteende och familjens välmående. Begränsningar: många studier riskerade snedvridning, få gjordes i låg- och medelinkomstländer, och resultaten gäller inte likadant för alla.

title: Systematic review of the properties of tools used to measure outcomes in anxiety intervention studies for children with autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Wigham S, McConachie H
abstract: Background Evidence about relevant outcomes is required in the evaluation of clinical interventions for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). However, to date, the variety of outcome measurement tools being used, and lack of knowledge about the measurement properties of some, compromise conclusions regarding the most effective interventions. Objectives This two-stage systematic review aimed to identify the tools used in studies evaluating interventions for anxiety for high-functioning children with ASD in middle childhood, and then to evaluate the tools for their appropriateness and measurement properties. Methods Electronic databases including Medline, PsychInfo, Embase, and the Cochrane database and registers were searched for anxiety intervention studies for children with ASD in middle childhood. Articles examining the measurement properties of the tools used were then searched for using a methodological filter in PubMed, and the quality of the papers evaluated using the COSMIN checklist. Results Ten intervention studies were identified in which six tools measuring anxiety and one of overall symptom change were used as primary outcomes. One further tool was included as it is recommended for standard use in UK children's mental health services. Sixty three articles on the properties of the tools were evaluated for the quality of evidence, and the quality of the measurement properties of each tool was summarised. Conclusions Overall three questionnaires were found robust in their measurement properties, the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, its revised version - the Revised Children's Anxiety and Depression Scale, and also the Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders. Crucially the articles on measurement properties provided almost no evidence on responsiveness to change, nor on the validity of use of the tools for evaluation of interventions for children with ASD. Prospero registration number CRD42012002684.

sheet.es: Si un servicio usa un cuestionario para medir la ansiedad de tu hijo autista antes y después de una terapia, puedes preguntar cuál es y cómo se interpretarán los resultados. Tres cuestionarios mostraron propiedades sólidas: la Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, su versión revisada (RCADS) y el SCARED. Aun así, tus observaciones diarias y lo que cuenta el propio niño siguen siendo valiosas. Esta revisión sistemática analizó diez estudios de intervención sobre ansiedad en niños autistas de 7 a 12 años con lenguaje verbal, y 63 artículos sobre las herramientas. Limitación: casi no hay pruebas de que estos cuestionarios detecten bien los cambios ni de que sean válidos específicamente para niños autistas.
sheet.en: If a service uses a questionnaire to measure your autistic child's anxiety before and after therapy, it's reasonable to ask which one and how results will be interpreted. Three questionnaires showed solid properties: the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, its revised version (RCADS) and the SCARED. Your everyday observations and your child's own account still matter alongside any score. This systematic review examined ten anxiety intervention studies with speaking autistic children in middle childhood, plus 63 articles about the tools. Limitation: there was almost no evidence that these questionnaires reliably capture change, or that they are valid specifically for autistic children.
sheet.sv: Om en verksamhet använder ett frågeformulär för att mäta ångest hos ditt autistiska barn före och efter en behandling kan du fråga vilket det är och hur resultaten ska tolkas. Tre formulär visade goda egenskaper: Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, dess reviderade version (RCADS) och SCARED. Dina vardagliga iakttagelser och barnets egen berättelse är fortfarande viktiga vid sidan av poängen. Denna systematiska översikt granskade tio interventionsstudier om ångest hos talande autistiska barn i mellanåren, samt 63 artiklar om verktygen. Begränsning: det fanns nästan inga belägg för att formulären fångar förändring väl eller att de är validerade specifikt för autistiska barn.

title: Environmental toxicants and autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Rossignol DA, Genuis SJ, Frye RE
abstract: Although the involvement of genetic abnormalities in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is well-accepted, recent studies point to an equal contribution by environmental factors, particularly environmental toxicants. However, these toxicant-related studies in ASD have not been systematically reviewed to date. Therefore, we compiled publications investigating potential associations between environmental toxicants and ASD and arranged these publications into the following three categories: (a) studies examining estimated toxicant exposures in the environment during the preconceptional, gestational and early childhood periods; (b) studies investigating biomarkers of toxicants; and (c) studies examining potential genetic susceptibilities to toxicants. A literature search of nine electronic scientific databases through November 2013 was performed. In the first category examining ASD risk and estimated toxicant exposures in the environment, the majority of studies (34/37; 92%) reported an association. Most of these studies were retrospective case-control, ecological or prospective cohort studies, although a few had weaker study designs (for example, case reports or series). Toxicants implicated in ASD included pesticides, phthalates, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), solvents, toxic waste sites, air pollutants and heavy metals, with the strongest evidence found for air pollutants and pesticides. Gestational exposure to methylmercury (through fish exposure, one study) and childhood exposure to pollutants in water supplies (two studies) were not found to be associated with ASD risk. In the second category of studies investigating biomarkers of toxicants and ASD, a large number was dedicated to examining heavy metals. Such studies demonstrated mixed findings, with only 19 of 40 (47%) case-control studies reporting higher concentrations of heavy metals in blood, urine, hair, brain or teeth of children with ASD compared with controls. Other biomarker studies reported that solvent, phthalate and pesticide levels were associated with ASD, whereas PCB studies were mixed. Seven studies reported a relationship between autism severity and heavy metal biomarkers, suggesting evidence of a dose-effect relationship. Overall, the evidence linking biomarkers of toxicants with ASD (the second category) was weaker compared with the evidence associating estimated exposures to toxicants in the environment and ASD risk (the first category) because many of the biomarker studies contained small sample sizes and the relationships between biomarkers and ASD were inconsistent across studies. Regarding the third category of studies investigating potential genetic susceptibilities to toxicants, 10 unique studies examined polymorphisms in genes associated with increased susceptibilities to toxicants, with 8 studies reporting that such polymorphisms were more common in ASD individuals (or their mothers, 1 study) compared with controls (one study examined multiple polymorphisms). Genes implicated in these studies included paraoxonase (PON1, three of five studies), glutathione S-transferase (GSTM1 and GSTP1, three of four studies), δ-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase (one study), SLC11A3 (one study) and the metal regulatory transcription factor 1 (one of two studies). Notably, many of the reviewed studies had significant limitations, including lack of replication, limited sample sizes, retrospective design, recall and publication biases, inadequate matching of cases and controls, and the use of nonstandard tools to diagnose ASD. The findings of this review suggest that the etiology of ASD may involve, at least in a subset of children, complex interactions between genetic factors and certain environmental toxicants that may act synergistically or in parallel during critical periods of neurodevelopment, in a manner that increases the likelihood of developing ASD. Because of the limitations of many of the reviewed studies, additional high-quality epidemiological studies concerning environmental toxicants and ASD are warranted to confirm and clarify many of these findings.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si algo que hiciste durante el embarazo o la infancia «causó» el autismo de tu hijo o hija, esta revisión no permite culpar a nadie. Sugiere que, en algunos casos, la contaminación del aire y ciertos pesticidas podrían interactuar con la genética, pero no ofrece pruebas para tratamientos de «desintoxicación» ni análisis de metales en pelo u orina. Mañana puedes centrarte en lo que ayuda ahora: apoyo, comprensión y entornos adaptados. Es una revisión sistemática de estudios publicados hasta 2013 sobre exposiciones ambientales y autismo. Muchos estudios eran pequeños, retrospectivos y con posibles sesgos de memoria y publicación, así que sus resultados no se aplican a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether something during pregnancy or early childhood "caused" your child's autism, this review gives no basis for blame. It suggests that in some cases air pollution and certain pesticides may interact with genetics, but it offers no evidence for "detox" treatments or hair or urine metal tests. Tomorrow you can focus on what helps now: support, understanding and adapted environments. This is a systematic review of studies published up to 2013 on environmental exposures and autism. Many studies were small and retrospective, with possible recall and publication bias, so the findings do not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om något under graviditeten eller tidig barndom "orsakade" ditt barns autism ger den här översikten ingen grund för skuld. Den antyder att luftföroreningar och vissa bekämpningsmedel i en del fall kan samverka med genetik, men den ger inget stöd för "detox"-behandlingar eller metalltester i hår eller urin. I morgon kan du fokusera på det som hjälper nu: stöd, förståelse och anpassade miljöer. Det är en systematisk översikt av studier publicerade fram till 2013 om miljöexponering och autism. Många studier var små och retrospektiva, med risk för minnes- och publiceringsbias, så resultaten gäller inte varje person.

title: Developmental pathways to autism: a review of prospective studies of infants at risk.
authors: Jones EJ, Gliga T, Bedford R, Charman T, Johnson MH
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) are neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by impairments in social interaction and communication, and the presence of restrictive and repetitive behaviors. Symptoms of ASD likely emerge from a complex interaction between pre-existing neurodevelopmental vulnerabilities and the child's environment, modified by compensatory skills and protective factors. Prospective studies of infants at high familial risk for ASD (who have an older sibling with a diagnosis) are beginning to characterize these developmental pathways to the emergence of clinical symptoms. Here, we review the range of behavioral and neurocognitive markers for later ASD that have been identified in high-risk infants in the first years of life. We discuss theoretical implications of emerging patterns, and identify key directions for future work, including potential resolutions to several methodological challenges for the field. Mapping how ASD unfolds from birth is critical to our understanding of the developmental mechanisms underlying this disorder. A more nuanced understanding of developmental pathways to ASD will help us not only to identify children who need early intervention, but also to improve the range of interventions available to them.

sheet.es: Si tienes un hijo autista y un bebé más pequeño, puedes observar con calma cómo se desarrolla el bebé: cómo mira, juega, se comunica y responde a las personas. Las diferencias suelen aparecer poco a poco durante los primeros años, no de golpe. Si algo te inquieta, comentarlo pronto con el equipo de salud infantil puede abrir apoyos útiles, sin necesidad de esperar ni alarmarse. Esta revisión de 2014 reúne estudios que siguieron desde el nacimiento a bebés con un hermano mayor autista. Sus límites: resume investigaciones anteriores, se centra en familias con hermanos autistas y describe tendencias de grupo, no lo que ocurrirá en cada niño.
sheet.en: If you have an autistic child and a younger baby, you can calmly notice how the baby develops: how they look, play, communicate and respond to people. Differences usually appear gradually over the first years rather than all at once. If something concerns you, mentioning it early to your child health team can open useful support, without waiting and without alarm. This 2014 review brings together studies that followed babies with an autistic older sibling from early infancy. Its limits: it summarises earlier research, focuses on families with autistic siblings, and describes group trends, not what will happen for any individual child.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett autistiskt barn och en yngre bebis kan du lugnt lägga märke till hur bebisen utvecklas: hur hen tittar, leker, kommunicerar och svarar på människor. Skillnader brukar visa sig gradvis under de första åren, inte plötsligt. Om något oroar dig kan det öppna för användbart stöd att tidigt ta upp det med barnavårdscentralen, utan att vänta och utan panik. Denna översikt från 2014 samlar studier som följt bebisar med ett autistiskt äldre syskon från tidig ålder. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar tidigare forskning, gäller familjer med autistiska syskon och beskriver mönster i grupper, inte vad som händer för varje enskilt barn.

title: Evidence linking oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and inflammation in the brain of individuals with autism.
authors: Rossignol DA, Frye RE
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders that are defined solely on the basis of behavioral observations. Therefore, ASD has traditionally been framed as a behavioral disorder. However, evidence is accumulating that ASD is characterized by certain physiological abnormalities, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and immune dysregulation/inflammation. While these abnormalities have been reported in studies that have examined peripheral biomarkers such as blood and urine, more recent studies have also reported these abnormalities in brain tissue derived from individuals diagnosed with ASD as compared to brain tissue derived from control individuals. A majority of these brain tissue studies have been published since 2010. The brain regions found to contain these physiological abnormalities in individuals with ASD are involved in speech and auditory processing, social behavior, memory, and sensory and motor coordination. This manuscript examines the evidence linking oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and immune dysregulation/inflammation in the brain of ASD individuals, suggesting that ASD has a clear biological basis with features of known medical disorders. This understanding may lead to new testing and treatment strategies in individuals with ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no cambia nada que debas hacer mañana. Su mensaje útil: el autismo tiene bases biológicas, no es fruto de la crianza. Si tu hijo o hija tiene problemas de salud física (digestivos, sueño, cansancio inusual), merece que su equipo médico los tome en serio, no que se atribuyan sin más al autismo. Evita suplementos o tratamientos que prometan corregir el estrés oxidativo sin consultar. Es una revisión de estudios con tejido cerebral donado tras el fallecimiento y marcadores en sangre y orina, comparando personas autistas y no autistas. Sus límites: muestras pequeñas, hallazgos de asociación (no de causa) y no ofrece pruebas ni tratamientos validados para nadie en concreto.
sheet.en: This study changes nothing you need to do tomorrow. Its useful message: autism has biological roots and is not caused by parenting. If your child has physical health concerns (digestion, sleep, unusual tiredness), they deserve to be taken seriously by their medical team rather than simply put down to autism. Be cautious of supplements or treatments promising to fix oxidative stress without professional advice. This is a review of studies using donated post-mortem brain tissue, plus blood and urine markers, comparing autistic and non-autistic people. Its limits: small samples, findings show associations rather than causes, and it offers no validated tests or treatments for any individual.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ändrar inget du behöver göra i morgon. Det användbara budskapet: autism har biologiska rötter och orsakas inte av föräldraskap. Om ditt barn har fysiska besvär (mage, sömn, ovanlig trötthet) förtjänar det att vården tar dem på allvar i stället för att bara skylla på autismen. Var försiktig med kosttillskott eller behandlingar som lovar att rätta till oxidativ stress utan råd från vården. Det är en översikt av studier på donerad hjärnvävnad efter döden samt markörer i blod och urin, där autistiska och icke-autistiska personer jämförts. Begränsningar: små urval, samband snarare än orsaker, och inga validerade tester eller behandlingar för enskilda personer.

title: The co-occurrence of autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in children - what do we know?
authors: Leitner Y
abstract: Symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autistic spectrum disorder (ASD) often co-occur. The DSM-IV had specified that an ASD diagnosis is an exclusion criterion for ADHD, thereby limiting research of this common clinical co-occurrence. As neurodevelopmental disorders, both ASD and ADHD share some phenotypic similarities, but are characterized by distinct diagnostic criteria. The present review will examine the frequency and implications of this clinical co-occurrence in children, with an emphasis on the available data regarding pre-school age. The review will highlight possible etiologies explaining it, and suggest future research directions necessary to enhance our understanding of both etiology and therapeutic interventions, in light of the new DSM-V criteria, allowing for a dual diagnosis.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista también muestra mucha inquietud, impulsividad o dificultad para sostener la atención, vale la pena comentarlo con su equipo profesional: autismo y TDAH aparecen juntos con frecuencia y, desde el DSM-5, pueden diagnosticarse ambos. Mañana puedes anotar situaciones concretas (cuándo, dónde, qué ayudó) para compartirlas; eso facilita apoyos ajustados a la persona, no a una etiqueta. La evidencia viene de una revisión narrativa de estudios sobre niños y niñas, con atención especial a la edad preescolar. Su límite: resume investigación previa, en parte hecha cuando el doble diagnóstico no estaba permitido, y no ofrece datos nuevos ni pautas de intervención probadas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child also seems very restless, impulsive or finds it hard to sustain attention, it is worth raising with their care team: autism and ADHD often occur together, and since DSM-5 both can be diagnosed. Tomorrow you could start noting concrete moments (when, where, what helped) to share; this supports help fitted to the person, not to a label. The evidence comes from a narrative review of studies on children, with a focus on preschool age. Its limit: it summarises earlier research, partly done when a dual diagnosis was not allowed, and offers no new data or tested intervention guidance.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn också verkar mycket rastlöst, impulsivt eller har svårt att hålla kvar uppmärksamheten kan det vara värt att ta upp med vårdteamet: autism och ADHD förekommer ofta tillsammans, och sedan DSM-5 kan båda diagnostiseras. I morgon kan du börja anteckna konkreta situationer (när, var, vad som hjälpte) att dela; det gör stödet mer anpassat till personen, inte till en etikett. Underlaget är en narrativ översikt av studier om barn, med fokus på förskoleåldern. Begränsning: den sammanfattar tidigare forskning, delvis gjord när dubbeldiagnos inte var tillåten, och ger inga nya data eller prövade insatsråd.

title: GABAergic signaling as therapeutic target for autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Cellot G, Cherubini E
abstract: γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA), the main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the adult brain, early in postnatal life exerts a depolarizing and excitatory action. This depends on accumulation of chloride inside the cell via the cation-chloride importer NKCC1, being the expression of the chloride exporter KCC2 very low at birth. The developmentally regulated expression of KCC2 results in extrusion of chloride with age and a shift of GABA from the depolarizing to the hyperpolarizing direction. The depolarizing action of GABA leads to intracellular calcium rise through voltage-dependent calcium channels and/or N-methyl-d-aspartate receptors. GABA-mediated calcium signals regulate a variety of developmental processes from cell proliferation migration, differentiation, synapse maturation, and neuronal wiring. Therefore, it is not surprising that some forms of neuro-developmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are associated with alterations of GABAergic signaling and impairment of the excitatory/inhibitory balance in selective neuronal circuits. In this review, we will discuss how changes of GABAA-mediated neurotransmission affect several forms of ASDs including the Fragile X, the Angelman, and Rett syndromes. Then, we will describe various animal models of ASDs with GABAergic dysfunctions, highlighting their behavioral deficits and the possibility to rescue them by targeting selective components of the GABAergic synapse. In particular, we will discuss how in some cases, reverting the polarity of GABA responses from the depolarizing to the hyperpolarizing direction with the diuretic bumetanide, a selective blocker of NKCC1, may have beneficial effects on ASDs, thus opening new therapeutic perspectives for the treatment of these devastating disorders.

sheet.es: Para mañana: no hace falta cambiar nada en casa por este estudio. Explica una hipótesis sobre cómo el cerebro equilibra excitación e inhibición (señal GABA) y por qué algunas personas autistas pueden procesar los estímulos con más intensidad. Si tu familiar se satura con ruido o luz, seguir ofreciendo pausas, espacios tranquilos y previsibilidad sigue siendo útil. Si lees sobre fármacos como la bumetanida, habla con el equipo médico antes de decidir nada. Evidencia: es una revisión de 2014 que resume estudios de laboratorio, sobre todo en modelos animales y síndromes como X frágil, Angelman y Rett. Límite: no prueba tratamientos en personas ni se aplica a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: nothing needs to change at home because of this paper. It explains a hypothesis about how the brain balances excitation and inhibition (GABA signalling) and why some autistic people may experience input more intensely. If your family member gets overwhelmed by noise or light, offering breaks, quiet spaces and predictability remains helpful. If you read about drugs such as bumetanide, talk with the medical team before deciding anything. Evidence: this is a 2014 review summarising laboratory research, mostly animal models and conditions like Fragile X, Angelman and Rett syndromes. Limit: it does not test treatments in people and does not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon: ingenting behöver ändras hemma på grund av den här artikeln. Den beskriver en hypotes om hur hjärnan balanserar aktivering och hämning (GABA-signalering) och varför vissa autistiska personer kan uppleva intryck starkare. Om din närstående blir överväldigad av ljud eller ljus är pauser, lugna platser och förutsägbarhet fortfarande till hjälp. Läser du om läkemedel som bumetanid, prata med vårdteamet innan du bestämmer något. Evidens: en översiktsartikel från 2014 som sammanfattar laboratorieforskning, mest djurmodeller och tillstånd som fragilt X, Angelman och Rett. Begränsning: den prövar inga behandlingar på människor och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Gene × Environment interactions in autism spectrum disorders: role of epigenetic mechanisms.
authors: Tordjman S, Somogyi E, Coulon N, Kermarrec S, Cohen D, Bronsard G, Bonnot O, Weismann-Arcache C, Botbol M, Lauth B, Ginchat V, Roubertoux P, Barburoth M, Kovess V, Geoffray MM, Xavier J
abstract: Several studies support currently the hypothesis that autism etiology is based on a polygenic and epistatic model. However, despite advances in epidemiological, molecular and clinical genetics, the genetic risk factors remain difficult to identify, with the exception of a few chromosomal disorders and several single gene disorders associated with an increased risk for autism. Furthermore, several studies suggest a role of environmental factors in autism spectrum disorders (ASD). First, arguments for a genetic contribution to autism, based on updated family and twin studies, are examined. Second, a review of possible prenatal, perinatal, and postnatal environmental risk factors for ASD are presented. Then, the hypotheses are discussed concerning the underlying mechanisms related to a role of environmental factors in the development of ASD in association with genetic factors. In particular, epigenetics as a candidate biological mechanism for gene × environment interactions is considered and the possible role of epigenetic mechanisms reported in genetic disorders associated with ASD is discussed. Furthermore, the example of in utero exposure to valproate provides a good illustration of epigenetic mechanisms involved in ASD and innovative therapeutic strategies. Epigenetic remodeling by environmental factors opens new perspectives for a better understanding, prevention, and early therapeutic intervention of ASD.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: el autismo surge de una mezcla compleja de muchos genes y factores del entorno; no hay una sola causa ni nada que usted hiciera «mal». Si le preocupan antecedentes familiares o medicamentos tomados en el embarazo (como el valproato), puede comentarlo con calma con su equipo médico o de genética, sin culpas. Lo más útil hoy sigue siendo apoyar a su hijo o hija tal como es. Evidencia: es una revisión narrativa de 2014 que resume estudios de familias, gemelos y factores prenatales y posnatales, y propone la epigenética como mecanismo. Límites: no aporta datos nuevos, muchas hipótesis no están confirmadas y no ofrece pautas aplicables a cada persona.
sheet.en: The practical point: autism arises from a complex mix of many genes and environmental factors; there is no single cause and nothing you did "wrong". If you have questions about family history or medicines taken during pregnancy (such as valproate), you can raise them calmly with your medical or genetics team, without blame. The most useful thing today is still supporting your child as they are. Evidence: this is a 2014 narrative review summarising family, twin and prenatal and postnatal studies, proposing epigenetics as a mechanism. Limits: it adds no new data, many hypotheses remain unconfirmed, and it offers no guidance that applies to every person.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: autism uppstår ur en komplex blandning av många gener och miljöfaktorer; det finns ingen enskild orsak och inget du gjort "fel". Har du frågor om ärftlighet eller läkemedel under graviditeten (som valproat) kan du lugnt ta upp dem med vården eller en genetisk mottagning, utan skuld. Det mest värdefulla idag är fortfarande att stötta ditt barn som det är. Evidens: en narrativ översikt från 2014 som sammanfattar familje- och tvillingstudier samt pre- och postnatala faktorer, och föreslår epigenetik som mekanism. Begränsningar: inga nya data, många hypoteser är obekräftade och den ger inga råd som gäller varje person.

title: Meta-analysis of SHANK Mutations in Autism Spectrum Disorders: a gradient of severity in cognitive impairments.
authors: Leblond CS, Nava C, Polge A, Gauthier J, Huguet G, Lumbroso S, Giuliano F, Stordeur C, Depienne C, Mouzat K, Pinto D, Howe J, Lemière N, Durand CM, Guibert J, Ey E, Toro R, Peyre H, Mathieu A, Amselle
abstract: SHANK genes code for scaffold proteins located at the post-synaptic density of glutamatergic synapses. In neurons, SHANK2 and SHANK3 have a positive effect on the induction and maturation of dendritic spines, whereas SHANK1 induces the enlargement of spine heads. Mutations in SHANK genes have been associated with autism spectrum disorders (ASD), but their prevalence and clinical relevance remain to be determined. Here, we performed a new screen and a meta-analysis of SHANK copy-number and coding-sequence variants in ASD. Copy-number variants were analyzed in 5,657 patients and 19,163 controls, coding-sequence variants were ascertained in 760 to 2,147 patients and 492 to 1,090 controls (depending on the gene), and, individuals carrying de novo or truncating SHANK mutations underwent an extensive clinical investigation. Copy-number variants and truncating mutations in SHANK genes were present in ∼1% of patients with ASD: mutations in SHANK1 were rare (0.04%) and present in males with normal IQ and autism; mutations in SHANK2 were present in 0.17% of patients with ASD and mild intellectual disability; mutations in SHANK3 were present in 0.69% of patients with ASD and up to 2.12% of the cases with moderate to profound intellectual disability. In summary, mutations of the SHANK genes were detected in the whole spectrum of autism with a gradient of severity in cognitive impairment. Given the rare frequency of SHANK1 and SHANK2 deleterious mutations, the clinical relevance of these genes remains to be ascertained. In contrast, the frequency and the penetrance of SHANK3 mutations in individuals with ASD and intellectual disability-more than 1 in 50-warrant its consideration for mutation screening in clinical practice.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene además una discapacidad intelectual moderada o profunda, puede valer la pena preguntar al equipo médico si un estudio genético (incluido el gen SHANK3) tiene sentido en su caso. Un resultado puede orientar el seguimiento y conectar con otras familias, pero no cambia quién es tu hijo ni lo que necesita hoy. Este metaanálisis reunió datos genéticos de miles de personas autistas y controles; los cambios en genes SHANK aparecieron en cerca del 1 %, y en SHANK3 en más de 1 de cada 50 personas con discapacidad intelectual. Límites: los cambios en SHANK1 y SHANK2 son muy raros y su relevancia clínica aún no está clara.
sheet.en: If your autistic child also has a moderate to profound intellectual disability, it may be worth asking your medical team whether genetic testing (including the SHANK3 gene) makes sense for them. A result can guide follow-up and connect you with other families, but it does not change who your child is or what they need today. This meta-analysis pooled genetic data from thousands of autistic people and controls; SHANK gene changes appeared in about 1%, and SHANK3 changes in more than 1 in 50 people with intellectual disability. Limits: SHANK1 and SHANK2 changes are very rare, and their clinical relevance is still unclear.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn också har en måttlig till svår intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kan det vara värt att fråga vårdteamet om en genetisk utredning (inklusive genen SHANK3) är meningsfull. Ett resultat kan vägleda uppföljningen och ge kontakt med andra familjer, men det ändrar inte vem ditt barn är eller vad hen behöver i dag. Denna metaanalys samlade genetiska data från tusentals autistiska personer och kontrollpersoner; förändringar i SHANK-gener fanns hos ungefär 1 %, och i SHANK3 hos mer än 1 av 50 personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Begränsningar: förändringar i SHANK1 och SHANK2 är mycket ovanliga och deras kliniska betydelse är fortfarande oklar.

title: What should autism research focus upon? Community views and priorities from the United Kingdom.
authors: Pellicano E, Dinsmore A, Charman T
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: The rise in the measured prevalence of autism has been accompanied by much new research and research investment internationally. This study sought to establish whether the pattern of current UK autism research funding maps on to the concerns of the autism community. Interviews and focus groups were conducted with autistic adults, family members, practitioners and researchers to identify their priorities for research. We also captured the views of a large number of stakeholders via an online survey. There was a clear disparity between the United Kingdom's pattern of funding for autism research and the priorities articulated by the majority of participants. There was general consensus that future priorities for autism research should lie in those areas that make a difference to people's day-to-day lives. There needs to be greater involvement of the autism community both in priority setting and in research more broadly to ensure that resources reach where they are most needed and can make the most impact.

sheet.es: Su experiencia diaria cuenta como conocimiento. Si le ofrecen participar en investigación, puede preguntar cómo ayudará en la vida cotidiana y si personas autistas y familias participaron en su diseño. También puede compartir sus prioridades, como apoyos prácticos, servicios o bienestar, con profesionales y organizaciones. Este estudio del Reino Unido combinó entrevistas y grupos focales con adultos autistas, familiares, profesionales e investigadores, más una encuesta en línea amplia; la mayoría quería investigación que mejore el día a día, algo distinto de lo que se financiaba. Sus límites: refleja opiniones de un país en 2014 y quienes respondieron quizá no representen a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Your everyday experience counts as knowledge. If you are invited to take part in research, you can ask how it will help daily life and whether autistic people and families helped shape it. You can also share your own priorities, such as practical support, services or wellbeing, with professionals and organisations. This UK study combined interviews and focus groups with autistic adults, family members, practitioners and researchers, plus a large online survey; most wanted research that improves day-to-day life, which differed from what was being funded. Its limits: it reflects views from one country in 2014, and those who responded may not represent all autistic people.
sheet.sv: Din vardagserfarenhet räknas som kunskap. Om du blir tillfrågad att delta i forskning kan du fråga hur den ska hjälpa i vardagen och om autistiska personer och familjer varit med och utformat den. Du kan också berätta om dina egna prioriteringar, som praktiskt stöd, tjänster eller välmående, för yrkesverksamma och organisationer. Denna brittiska studie kombinerade intervjuer och fokusgrupper med autistiska vuxna, anhöriga, yrkesverksamma och forskare, samt en stor webbenkät; de flesta ville ha forskning som förbättrar vardagen, vilket skilde sig från vad som finansierades. Begränsningar: den speglar åsikter från ett land 2014, och de som svarade representerar kanske inte alla autistiska personer.

title: The relationship between sleep and behavior in autism spectrum disorder (ASD): a review.
authors: Cohen S, Conduit R, Lockley SW, Rajaratnam SM, Cornish KM
abstract: Although there is evidence that significant sleep problems are common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and that poor sleep exacerbates problematic daytime behavior, such relationships have received very little attention in both research and clinical practice. Treatment guidelines to help manage challenging behaviors in ASD fail to mention sleep at all, or they present a very limited account. Moreover, limited attention is given to children with low-functioning autism, those individuals who often experience the most severe sleep disruption and behavioral problems. This paper describes the nature of sleep difficulties in ASD and highlights the complexities of sleep disruption in individuals with low-functioning autism. It is proposed that profiling ASD children based on the nature of their sleep disruption might help to understand symptom and behavioral profiles (or vice versa) and therefore lead to better-targeted interventions. This paper concludes with a discussion of the limitations of current knowledge and proposes areas that are important for future research. Treating disordered sleep in ASD has great potential to improve daytime behavior and family functioning in this vulnerable population.

sheet.es: Si un día resulta especialmente difícil para tu hijo o hija, vale la pena mirar también cómo durmió. Anotar durante unas semanas horas de sueño, despertares y cómo fue el día puede ayudar a ver patrones y a hablar con el equipo de salud sobre el descanso, no solo sobre la conducta. Esta revisión de 2014 reunió estudios sobre sueño y conducta en niños y niñas autistas, incluidos quienes necesitan más apoyo, y señala que el sueño suele quedar fuera de las guías. Su límite: no aporta datos nuevos y la investigación disponible era escasa, sobre todo en autistas con más necesidades de apoyo.
sheet.en: If your child is having an especially hard day, it can help to also look at how they slept. Keeping simple notes for a few weeks on sleep times, night waking and how the day went may reveal patterns and help you raise sleep, not just behaviour, with your healthcare team. This 2014 review brought together studies on sleep and daytime behaviour in autistic children, including those with higher support needs, and notes that sleep is often missing from guidelines. Its limit: it adds no new data, and the research it drew on was sparse, especially for autistic children with higher support needs.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har en särskilt tung dag kan det hjälpa att också titta på hur hen har sovit. Att under några veckor anteckna sovtider, nattliga uppvaknanden och hur dagen blev kan visa mönster och göra det lättare att ta upp sömnen, inte bara beteendet, med vården. Den här översikten från 2014 samlade studier om sömn och beteende under dagen hos autistiska barn, även barn med stora stödbehov, och påpekar att sömn ofta saknas i riktlinjer. Begränsning: den tillför inga nya data, och forskningen den byggde på var tunn, särskilt för autistiska barn med stora stödbehov.

title: Sex/gender differences and autism: setting the scene for future research.
authors: Lai MC, Lombardo MV, Auyeung B, Chakrabarti B, Baron-Cohen S
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
abstract: Objective The relationship between sex/gender differences and autism has attracted a variety of research ranging from clinical and neurobiological to etiological, stimulated by the male bias in autism prevalence. Findings are complex and do not always relate to each other in a straightforward manner. Distinct but interlinked questions on the relationship between sex/gender differences and autism remain underaddressed. To better understand the implications from existing research and to help design future studies, we propose a 4-level conceptual framework to clarify the embedded themes. Method We searched PubMed for publications before September 2014 using search terms "'sex OR gender OR females' AND autism." A total of 1,906 articles were screened for relevance, along with publications identified via additional literature reviews, resulting in 329 articles that were reviewed. Results Level 1, "Nosological and diagnostic challenges," concerns the question, "How should autism be defined and diagnosed in males and females?" Level 2, "Sex/gender-independent and sex/gender-dependent characteristics," addresses the question, "What are the similarities and differences between males and females with autism?" Level 3, "General models of etiology: liability and threshold," asks the question, "How is the liability for developing autism linked to sex/gender?" Level 4, "Specific etiological-developmental mechanisms," focuses on the question, "What etiological-developmental mechanisms of autism are implicated by sex/gender and/or sexual/gender differentiation?" Conclusions Using this conceptual framework, findings can be more clearly summarized, and the implications of the links between findings from different levels can become clearer. Based on this 4-level framework, we suggest future research directions, methodology, and specific topics in sex/gender differences and autism.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña, mujer o persona de género diverso autista, recuerda que el autismo puede verse distinto a los estereotipos basados en chicos: intereses menos llamativos, más camuflaje social, agotamiento tras el colegio. Anota lo que observas en casa y compártelo con profesionales; tu descripción puede ayudar a que no se pase por alto. Es una revisión de 329 artículos publicados hasta 2014, que propone un marco de cuatro niveles para ordenar qué sabemos sobre sexo, género y autismo. Su límite: no aporta datos nuevos ni pautas prácticas, y muchos estudios incluidos tenían pocas mujeres y no distinguían bien sexo de género.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic girl, woman or gender-diverse person, remember that autism can look different from boy-based stereotypes: quieter interests, more social camouflaging, exhaustion after school. Write down what you notice at home and share it with professionals; your description can help keep their needs from being overlooked. This is a review of 329 articles published up to 2014, proposing a four-level framework to organise what is known about sex, gender and autism. Its limit: it offers no new data or practical guidelines, and many included studies had few women and did not clearly separate sex from gender.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk flicka, kvinna eller person med annan könsidentitet, kom ihåg att autism kan se annorlunda ut än pojkbaserade stereotyper: mindre iögonfallande intressen, mer socialt kamouflage, utmattning efter skolan. Skriv ner vad du märker hemma och dela det med professionella; din beskrivning kan hjälpa till så att behoven inte förbises. Detta är en översikt av 329 artiklar publicerade fram till 2014, som föreslår en ram i fyra nivåer för att ordna kunskapen om kön, genus och autism. Begränsning: den ger inga nya data eller praktiska riktlinjer, och många ingående studier hade få kvinnor och skilde inte tydligt på kön och genus.

title: Measuring autistic traits in the general population: a systematic review of the Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ) in a nonclinical population sample of 6,900 typical adult males and females.
authors: Ruzich E, Allison C, Smith P, Watson P, Auyeung B, Ring H, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: The Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ) is a self-report measure of autistic traits. It is frequently cited in diverse fields and has been administered to adults of at least average intelligence with autism and to nonclinical controls, as well as to clinical control groups such as those with schizophrenia, prosopagnosia, anorexia, and depression. However, there has been no empirical systematic review of the AQ since its inception in 2001. The present study reports a comprehensive systematic review of the literature to estimate a reliable mean AQ score in individuals without a diagnosis of an autism spectrum condition (ASC), in order to establish a reference norm for future studies. A systematic search of computerized databases was performed to identify studies that administered the AQ to nonclinical participant samples representing the adult male and female general population. Inclusion was based on a set of formalized criteria that evaluated the quality of the study, the usage of the AQ, and the population being assessed. After selection, 73 articles, detailing 6,934 nonclinical participants, as well as 1,963 matched clinical cases of ASC (from available cohorts within each individual study), were analyzed. Mean AQ score for the nonclinical population was 16.94 (95% CI 11.6, 20.0), while mean AQ score for the clinical population with ASC was found to be 35.19 (95% CI 27.6, 41.1). In addition, in the nonclinical population, a sex difference in autistic traits was found, although no sex difference in AQ score was seen in the clinical ASC population. These findings have implications for the study of autistic traits in the general population. Here, we confirm previous norms with more rigorous data and for the first time establish average AQ scores based on a systematic review, for populations of adult males and females with and without ASC. Finally, we advise future researchers to avoid risk of bias by carefully considering the recruitment strategy for both clinical and nonclinical groups and to demonstrate transparency by reporting recruitment methods for all participants.

sheet.es: Si usted o alguien cercano ha completado el cuestionario AQ, recuerde que es una herramienta de autoinforme que describe rasgos, no un diagnóstico. En esta revisión, las personas sin diagnóstico puntuaron de media unos 17 y las personas autistas unos 35, con amplios rangos que se solapan. Los rasgos autistas aparecen en toda la población, y una puntuación sirve para iniciar una conversación con profesionales, no para definir a nadie. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de 73 estudios con unos 6.900 adultos sin diagnóstico y 1.963 adultos autistas. Sus límites: incluyó sobre todo adultos sin discapacidad intelectual, y la forma de reclutar participantes pudo sesgar los resultados.
sheet.en: If you or someone close to you has filled in the AQ questionnaire, remember it is a self-report tool that describes traits, not a diagnosis. In this review, people without a diagnosis scored about 17 on average and autistic people about 35, with wide, overlapping ranges. Autistic traits exist across the whole population, and a score can open a conversation with professionals, not define anyone. This is a systematic review of 73 studies covering about 6,900 adults without a diagnosis and 1,963 autistic adults. Its limits: it mostly included adults without intellectual disability, and how participants were recruited may have biased the results.
sheet.sv: Om du eller någon nära dig har fyllt i AQ-formuläret, kom ihåg att det är ett självskattningsverktyg som beskriver drag, inte en diagnos. I denna översikt fick personer utan diagnos i genomsnitt cirka 17 poäng och autistiska personer cirka 35, med breda intervall som överlappar. Autistiska drag finns i hela befolkningen, och en poäng kan öppna ett samtal med professionella, inte definiera någon. Det är en systematisk översikt av 73 studier med cirka 6 900 vuxna utan diagnos och 1 963 autistiska vuxna. Begränsningar: främst vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning ingick, och hur deltagarna rekryterades kan ha snedvridit resultaten.

title: Sex differences in brain plasticity: a new hypothesis for sex ratio bias in autism.
authors: Mottron L, Duret P, Mueller S, Moore RD, Forgeot d'Arc B, Jacquemont S, Xiong L
abstract: Several observations support the hypothesis that differences in synaptic and regional cerebral plasticity between the sexes account for the high ratio of males to females in autism. First, males are more susceptible than females to perturbations in genes involved in synaptic plasticity. Second, sex-related differences in non-autistic brain structure and function are observed in highly variable regions, namely, the heteromodal associative cortices, and overlap with structural particularities and enhanced activity of perceptual associative regions in autistic individuals. Finally, functional cortical reallocations following brain lesions in non-autistic adults (for example, traumatic brain injury, multiple sclerosis) are sex-dependent. Interactions between genetic sex and hormones may therefore result in higher synaptic and consecutively regional plasticity in perceptual brain areas in males than in females. The onset of autism may largely involve mutations altering synaptic plasticity that create a plastic reaction affecting the most variable and sexually dimorphic brain regions. The sex ratio bias in autism may arise because males have a lower threshold than females for the development of this plastic reaction following a genetic or environmental event.

sheet.es: Para el día a día, este trabajo no cambia lo que haces mañana: es una idea teórica sobre por qué se diagnostica autismo con más frecuencia en chicos que en chicas. Un recordatorio útil: si cuidas a una niña o mujer, sus rasgos autistas pueden ser igual de reales aunque se noten menos o se expresen de otra forma; confía en lo que observas y en lo que ella cuenta. En cuanto a la evidencia, es una hipótesis que reúne estudios previos de genética, imagen cerebral y lesiones cerebrales en adultos no autistas; no recogió datos nuevos con participantes. Su límite: es una propuesta por comprobar, no una explicación demostrada ni válida para cada persona.
sheet.en: For daily life, this paper does not change what you do tomorrow: it is a theoretical idea about why autism is diagnosed more often in boys than in girls. One useful reminder: if you support a girl or woman, her autistic traits can be just as real even when they are less visible or show up differently; trust what you notice and what she tells you. On the evidence, this is a hypothesis paper that brings together earlier studies on genetics, brain imaging and brain injury in non-autistic adults; it did not collect new data from participants. Its limit: it is a proposal still to be tested, not a proven explanation or one that fits every person.
sheet.sv: I vardagen ändrar den här artikeln inte vad du gör i morgon: den är en teoretisk idé om varför autism oftare diagnostiseras hos pojkar än hos flickor. En användbar påminnelse: om du stöttar en flicka eller kvinna kan hennes autistiska drag vara lika verkliga även när de syns mindre eller visar sig på andra sätt; lita på det du ser och det hon berättar. När det gäller underlaget är detta en hypotesartikel som sammanför tidigare studier om genetik, hjärnavbildning och hjärnskador hos icke-autistiska vuxna; inga nya data samlades in från deltagare. Begränsningen: det är ett förslag som behöver prövas, inte en bevisad förklaring eller något som gäller varje person.

title: Sensory Adapted Dental Environments to Enhance Oral Care for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
authors: Cermak SA, Stein Duker LI, Williams ME, Dawson ME, Lane CJ, Polido JC
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Un entorno dental adaptado (luz baja, menos ruido, presión profunda) redujo el estrés y el malestar de niños autistas durante la limpieza.
claim.en: A sensory-adapted dental environment (dim light, less noise, deep pressure) reduced stress and discomfort for autistic children during cleaning.
claim.sv: En sensoriskt anpassad tandvårdsmiljö (dämpat ljus, mindre ljud, djupt tryck) minskade stress och obehag hos autistiska barn vid rengöring.

supports.es: Pedir a la clínica menos luz y sonido y una secuencia predecible.
supports.en: Asking a clinic for lower light and sound and a predictable sequence.
supports.sv: Att be kliniken om mindre ljus och ljud och en förutsägbar ordning.

doesNotSupport.es: Que la adaptación elimine la necesidad de consentimiento y pausas.
doesNotSupport.en: That adaptation removes the need for consent and pauses.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att anpassning tar bort behovet av samtycke och pauser.

title: Cerebro-cerebellar circuits in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: D'Mello AM, Stoodley CJ
abstract: The cerebellum is one of the most consistent sites of abnormality in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and cerebellar damage is associated with an increased risk of ASD symptoms, suggesting that cerebellar dysfunction may play a crucial role in the etiology of ASD. The cerebellum forms multiple closed-loop circuits with cerebral cortical regions that underpin movement, language, and social processing. Through these circuits, cerebellar dysfunction could impact the core ASD symptoms of social and communication deficits and repetitive and stereotyped behaviors. The emerging topography of sensorimotor, cognitive, and affective subregions in the cerebellum provides a new framework for interpreting the significance of regional cerebellar findings in ASD and their relationship to broader cerebro-cerebellar circuits. Further, recent research supports the idea that the integrity of cerebro-cerebellar loops might be important for early cortical development; disruptions in specific cerebro-cerebellar loops in ASD might impede the specialization of cortical regions involved in motor control, language, and social interaction, leading to impairments in these domains. Consistent with this concept, structural, and functional differences in sensorimotor regions of the cerebellum and sensorimotor cerebro-cerebellar circuits are associated with deficits in motor control and increased repetitive and stereotyped behaviors in ASD. Further, communication and social impairments are associated with atypical activation and structure in cerebro-cerebellar loops underpinning language and social cognition. Finally, there is converging evidence from structural, functional, and connectivity neuroimaging studies that cerebellar right Crus I/II abnormalities are related to more severe ASD impairments in all domains. We propose that cerebellar abnormalities may disrupt optimization of both structure and function in specific cerebro-cerebellar circuits in ASD.

sheet.es: Lo práctico para mañana: las diferencias en movimiento, coordinación, lenguaje y en lo social pueden tener una base cerebral real, no son falta de esfuerzo ni mala voluntad. Ofrece tiempo extra para tareas motoras, divide los pasos, acepta los movimientos repetitivos que regulan y apoya la comunicación de la forma que funcione para la persona. Esta es una revisión de 2015 que reúne estudios de neuroimagen sobre los circuitos entre el cerebelo y la corteza en personas autistas. Límites: propone una hipótesis, no ofrece pruebas directas ni orientaciones prácticas, y los hallazgos de grupo no describen a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway for tomorrow: differences in movement, coordination, language and social connection may have a real brain basis; they are not a lack of effort or willingness. Allow extra time for motor tasks, break steps down, accept repetitive movements that help with regulation, and support communication in whatever way works for the person. This is a 2015 review bringing together brain-imaging studies on circuits linking the cerebellum and the cerebral cortex in autistic people. Limits: it proposes a hypothesis rather than testing it directly, gives no practical guidance, and group findings do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Praktiskt för i morgon: skillnader i rörelse, koordination, språk och socialt samspel kan ha en verklig grund i hjärnan; de handlar inte om brist på ansträngning eller vilja. Ge extra tid för motoriska uppgifter, dela upp moment i små steg, acceptera upprepade rörelser som hjälper till att reglera och stötta kommunikationen på det sätt som fungerar för personen. Detta är en översikt från 2015 som sammanställer hjärnavbildningsstudier om kretsar mellan lillhjärnan och hjärnbarken hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den föreslår en hypotes snarare än att pröva den direkt, ger inga praktiska råd, och gruppfynd beskriver inte varje autistisk person.

title: Autism spectrum disorders and neuropathology of the cerebellum.
authors: Hampson DR, Blatt GJ
abstract: The cerebellum contains the largest number of neurons and synapses of any structure in the central nervous system. The concept that the cerebellum is solely involved in fine motor function has become outdated; substantial evidence has accumulated linking the cerebellum with higher cognitive functions including language. Cerebellar deficits have been implicated in autism for more than two decades. The computational power of the cerebellum is essential for many, if not most of the processes that are perturbed in autism including language and communication, social interactions, stereotyped behavior, motor activity and motor coordination, and higher cognitive functions. The link between autism and cerebellar dysfunction should not be surprising to those who study its cellular, physiological, and functional properties. Postmortem studies have revealed neuropathological abnormalities in cerebellar cellular architecture while studies on mouse lines with cell loss or mutations in single genes restricted to cerebellar Purkinje cells have also strongly implicated this brain structure in contributing to the autistic phenotype. This connection has been further substantiated by studies investigating brain damage in humans restricted to the cerebellum. In this review, we summarize advances in research on idiopathic autism and three genetic forms of autism that highlight the key roles that the cerebellum plays in this spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders.

sheet.es: No hay nada que cambiar mañana por este estudio, pero ayuda a entender algo: el cerebelo no solo coordina el movimiento, también participa en el lenguaje, la comunicación y la interacción. Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene una coordinación motora distinta o necesita más tiempo para procesar, puede tener una base cerebral real, no es falta de esfuerzo. Ofrecer paciencia, tiempo y apoyos prácticos sigue siendo lo útil. Es una revisión de 2015 que reúne estudios post mortem, modelos en ratones, lesiones cerebrales en humanos y formas genéticas de autismo. Sus límites: gran parte de la evidencia viene de animales y de pocos cerebros, y no ofrece pruebas diagnósticas ni intervenciones concretas.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change tomorrow because of this study, but it offers useful context: the cerebellum does more than coordinate movement; it also supports language, communication and social interaction. If your autistic child moves differently or needs extra processing time, there may be a real brain basis for it, not a lack of effort. Patience, time and practical supports remain the helpful response. This is a 2015 review bringing together postmortem studies, mouse models, human cerebellar injury and three genetic forms of autism. Its limits: much of the evidence comes from animals and small numbers of brains, and it provides no diagnostic tests or specific interventions.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras i morgon på grund av den här studien, men den ger nyttig förståelse: lillhjärnan styr inte bara rörelser utan bidrar också till språk, kommunikation och socialt samspel. Om ditt autistiska barn rör sig annorlunda eller behöver mer tid att bearbeta kan det ha en verklig grund i hjärnan, inte handla om bristande ansträngning. Tålamod, tid och praktiskt stöd är fortfarande det som hjälper. Detta är en översikt från 2015 som samlar obduktionsstudier, musmodeller, skador på lillhjärnan hos människor och tre genetiska former av autism. Begränsningar: mycket av underlaget kommer från djur och få hjärnor, och den ger varken diagnostiska tester eller konkreta insatser.

title: At the cross-roads of participatory research and biomarker discovery in autism: the need for empirical data.
authors: Yusuf A, Elsabbagh M
abstract: Background Identifying biomarkers for autism can improve outcomes for those affected by autism. Engaging the diverse stakeholders in the research process using community-based participatory research (CBPR) can accelerate biomarker discovery into clinical applications. However, there are limited examples of stakeholder involvement in autism research, possibly due to conceptual and practical concerns. We evaluate the applicability of CBPR principles to biomarker discovery in autism and critically review empirical studies adopting these principles. Methods Using a scoping review methodology, we identified and evaluated seven studies using CBPR principles in biomarker discovery. Results and conclusions The limited number of studies in biomarker discovery adopting CBPR principles coupled with their methodological limitations suggests that such applications are feasible but challenging. These studies illustrate three CBPR themes: community assessment, setting global priorities, and collaboration in research design. We propose that further research using participatory principles would be useful in accelerating the pace of discovery and the development of clinically meaningful biomarkers. For this goal to be successful we advocate for increased attention to previously identified conceptual and methodological challenges to participatory approaches in health research, including improving scientific rigor and developing long-term partnerships among stakeholders.
