sheet.es: Si te invitan a participar en un estudio de biomarcadores (pruebas biológicas como análisis de sangre o genéticos), puedes preguntar si personas autistas y familias ayudaron a diseñarlo, qué preguntas investiga y cómo te informarán de los resultados. Tienes derecho a opinar y a decir no. Esta revisión de alcance analizó solo siete estudios que aplicaron investigación participativa en la búsqueda de biomarcadores del autismo; concluye que es posible, pero difícil, y que conviene crear alianzas duraderas con la comunidad. Sus límites: hay pocos estudios, con debilidades de método, y no ofrece resultados clínicos que cambien la vida diaria.
sheet.en: If you are invited to join a biomarker study (biological tests such as blood or genetic samples), you can ask whether autistic people and families helped design it, what questions it explores, and how results will be shared with you. You have the right to give your view and to say no. This scoping review examined only seven studies that used participatory research in autism biomarker discovery; it concludes this is feasible but challenging, and that lasting partnerships with the community are needed. Its limits: very few studies, with methodological weaknesses, and it offers no clinical findings that change daily life.
sheet.sv: Om ni blir inbjudna till en studie om biomarkörer (biologiska tester som blodprov eller genetiska prover) kan ni fråga om autistiska personer och familjer var med och utformade den, vilka frågor den undersöker och hur resultaten kommer att delas med er. Ni har rätt att tycka till och att tacka nej. Denna kartläggande översikt granskade bara sju studier som använde deltagande forskning för att hitta biomarkörer för autism; slutsatsen är att det är möjligt men svårt, och att långsiktiga samarbeten med autistiska personer och familjer behövs. Begränsningar: mycket få studier, med metodsvagheter, och inga kliniska fynd som påverkar vardagen.

title: Characteristics of Brains in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Structure, Function and Connectivity across the Lifespan.
authors: Ha S, Sohn IJ, Kim N, Sim HJ, Cheon KA
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social communication and restricted and repetitive behaviors (RRBs). Over the past decade, neuroimaging studies have provided considerable insights underlying neurobiological mechanisms of ASD. In this review, we introduce recent findings from brain imaging studies to characterize the brains of ASD across the human lifespan. Results of structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies dealing with total brain volume, regional brain structure and cortical area are summarized. Using task-based functional MRI (fMRI), many studies have shown dysfunctional activation in critical areas of social communication and RRBs. We also describe several data to show abnormal connectivity in the ASD brains. Finally, we suggest the possible strategies to study ASD brains in the future.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: los escáneres cerebrales no sirven hoy para diagnosticar ni para decidir apoyos para tu hijo o hija. Lo útil es observar a la persona concreta: cómo se comunica, qué le regula, qué le abruma. Esta investigación sugiere que el cerebro autista se desarrolla y conecta de forma diferente a lo largo de la vida, lo que ayuda a entender que sus maneras de procesar el mundo son reales, no caprichos. Es una revisión de 2015 que resume estudios de resonancia magnética en personas autistas de distintas edades. Sus límites: los estudios revisados son pequeños y variados, usan un lenguaje de déficit y los promedios de grupo no describen a ninguna persona individual.
sheet.en: The practical point: brain scans cannot currently diagnose your child or decide what support they need. What helps is watching the actual person: how they communicate, what calms them, what overwhelms them. This research suggests autistic brains develop and connect differently across the lifespan, which supports the idea that their ways of processing the world are real, not wilfulness. It is a 2015 review summarising MRI studies of autistic people of various ages. Its limits: the studies it covers are often small and inconsistent, they use deficit-based language, and group averages do not describe any single individual.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: hjärnröntgen kan i dag inte ställa diagnos eller avgöra vilket stöd ditt barn behöver. Det som hjälper är att se den faktiska personen: hur hen kommunicerar, vad som lugnar och vad som blir för mycket. Forskningen tyder på att autistiska hjärnor utvecklas och kopplas samman annorlunda genom livet, vilket stöder att deras sätt att uppfatta världen är verkligt, inte trots. Det är en översikt från 2015 som sammanfattar MR-studier av autistiska personer i olika åldrar. Begränsningar: studierna är ofta små och spretiga, använder bristfokuserat språk, och gruppgenomsnitt beskriver ingen enskild individ.

title: Exploring the Validity of Valproic Acid Animal Model of Autism.
authors: Mabunga DF, Gonzales EL, Kim JW, Kim KC, Shin CY
abstract: The valproic acid (VPA) animal model of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is one of the most widely used animal model in the field. Like any other disease models, it can't model the totality of the features seen in autism. Then, is it valid to model autism? This model demonstrates many of the structural and behavioral features that can be observed in individuals with autism. These similarities enable the model to define relevant pathways of developmental dysregulation resulting from environmental manipulation. The uncovering of these complex pathways resulted to the growing pool of potential therapeutic candidates addressing the core symptoms of ASD. Here, we summarize the validity points of VPA that may or may not qualify it as a valid animal model of ASD.

sheet.es: Para el día a día, este estudio no cambia nada: trata sobre cómo los investigadores usan ratones y ratas para estudiar el autismo, no sobre apoyos para personas. Si lees titulares sobre «tratamientos» descubiertos en animales, conviene tomarlos con calma: lo que funciona en un modelo animal a menudo no se traslada a personas, y nunca reemplaza lo que tú observas y lo que la persona autista expresa. Se trata de una revisión de estudios con animales expuestos a ácido valproico antes de nacer; no participaron personas. Su límite principal: los propios autores reconocen que ningún modelo animal refleja la experiencia autista completa.
sheet.en: For daily life, this study changes nothing: it is about how researchers use mice and rats to study autism, not about support for people. If you see headlines about "treatments" found in animals, it helps to read them calmly: what works in an animal model often does not carry over to humans, and it never replaces what you notice and what the autistic person tells you. This is a review of studies in animals exposed to valproic acid before birth; no people took part. Its main limit: the authors themselves acknowledge that no animal model captures the full autistic experience.
sheet.sv: I vardagen förändrar den här studien ingenting: den handlar om hur forskare använder möss och råttor för att studera autism, inte om stöd till människor. Om du ser rubriker om "behandlingar" som upptäckts hos djur kan du läsa dem lugnt: det som fungerar i en djurmodell går ofta inte att överföra till människor, och det ersätter aldrig det du själv märker och det den autistiska personen berättar. Det är en översikt av studier på djur som utsatts för valproinsyra före födseln; inga människor deltog. Den största begränsningen: författarna medger själva att ingen djurmodell fångar hela den autistiska upplevelsen.

title: Autism, oxytocin and interoception.
authors: Quattrocki E, Friston K
abstract: Autism is a pervasive developmental disorder characterized by profound social and verbal communication deficits, stereotypical motor behaviors, restricted interests, and cognitive abnormalities. Autism affects approximately 1% of children in developing countries. Given this prevalence, identifying risk factors and therapeutic interventions are pressing objectives—objectives that rest on neurobiologically grounded and psychologically informed theories about the underlying pathophysiology. In this article, we review the evidence that autism could result from a dysfunctional oxytocin system early in life. As a mediator of successful procreation, not only in the reproductive system, but also in the brain, oxytocin plays a crucial role in sculpting socio-sexual behavior. Formulated within a (Bayesian) predictive coding framework, we propose that oxytocin encodes the saliency or precision of interoceptive signals and enables the neuronal plasticity necessary for acquiring a generative model of the emotional and social 'self.' An aberrant oxytocin system in infancy could therefore help explain the marked deficits in language and social communication—as well as the sensory, autonomic, motor, behavioral, and cognitive abnormalities—seen in autism.

sheet.es: Lo práctico para mañana: muchas personas autistas perciben de forma distinta las señales internas del cuerpo, como hambre, sed, cansancio, dolor o ganas de ir al baño. Puede ayudar ofrecer recordatorios tranquilos, horarios previsibles para comer y beber, y preguntar con opciones concretas («¿tienes frío o calor?») en lugar de suponer. Respeta cómo la persona describe sus sensaciones. Sobre la evidencia: es una revisión teórica que propone que la oxitocina influye en cómo el cerebro interpreta las señales corporales, sin participantes propios. Límites: es una hipótesis, no una prueba, usa lenguaje deficitario y no justifica ningún tratamiento con oxitocina.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway for tomorrow: many autistic people sense internal body signals differently, such as hunger, thirst, tiredness, pain or needing the toilet. Calm reminders, predictable times for eating and drinking, and concrete choice questions ("are you cold or warm?") can help more than guessing. Respect how the person describes their own sensations. On the evidence: this is a theoretical review proposing that oxytocin shapes how the brain weighs bodily signals; it did not include its own participants. Limits: it is a hypothesis, not proof, it uses deficit-based language, and it does not support any oxytocin treatment.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska inför i morgon: många autistiska personer uppfattar kroppens inre signaler annorlunda, till exempel hunger, törst, trötthet, smärta eller behov av toalett. Lugna påminnelser, förutsägbara tider för mat och dryck och konkreta valfrågor ("fryser du eller är du varm?") kan hjälpa mer än att gissa. Respektera hur personen själv beskriver sina förnimmelser. Om evidensen: detta är en teoretisk översikt som föreslår att oxytocin påverkar hur hjärnan väger kroppssignaler; den hade inga egna deltagare. Begränsningar: det är en hypotes, inte ett bevis, den använder bristfokuserat språk och stöder ingen behandling med oxytocin.

title: Using the Autism-Spectrum Quotient to Measure Autistic Traits in Anorexia Nervosa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Westwood H, Eisler I, Mandy W, Leppanen J, Treasure J, Tchanturia K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Interest in the link between Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Anorexia Nervosa (AN) has led to estimates of the prevalence of autistic traits in AN. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the use of the Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ) or abbreviated version (AQ-10) to examine whether patients with AN have elevated levels of autistic traits. Seven studies were identified and subsequent meta-analysis indicated that those with AN appear to have significant difficulties of a manner characteristic of ASD, relative to controls. Whilst this analysis supports previous indications of higher prevalence of ASD in AN, the aetiology of these traits remains unclear. Studies using more robust clinical measures of ASD within AN are needed to confirm what self-report measures appear to show.

sheet.es: Si una persona que cuidas vive con anorexia, puede ser útil considerar también rasgos autistas: preferencias sensoriales, necesidad de rutina o diferencias sociales pueden influir en la alimentación y en qué apoyo le resulta cómodo. Pregunta con calma por esas experiencias y compártelas con el equipo de salud, sin sacar conclusiones por tu cuenta. Este metaanálisis reunió siete estudios que usaron el cuestionario AQ o AQ-10; las personas con anorexia puntuaron más alto en rasgos autistas que los grupos de comparación. Como límite, el AQ es un autoinforme, no un diagnóstico, y no se sabe si los rasgos son previos o efecto de la propia anorexia.
sheet.en: If someone you support lives with anorexia, it may help to also consider autistic traits: sensory preferences, a need for routine or social differences can shape eating and which kinds of support feel manageable. Gently ask about these experiences and share them with the care team, rather than drawing conclusions yourself. This meta-analysis pooled seven studies using the AQ or AQ-10 questionnaire; people with anorexia scored higher on autistic traits than comparison groups. A key limit: the AQ is self-report, not a diagnosis, and it remains unclear whether these traits came first or partly reflect the effects of anorexia itself.
sheet.sv: Om någon du stöttar lever med anorexi kan det hjälpa att också tänka på autistiska drag: sensoriska preferenser, behov av rutiner eller sociala skillnader kan påverka ätandet och vilket stöd som känns hanterbart. Fråga lugnt om sådana erfarenheter och dela dem med vårdteamet, istället för att dra egna slutsatser. Denna metaanalys sammanställde sju studier som använde enkäten AQ eller AQ-10; personer med anorexi skattade högre på autistiska drag än jämförelsegrupper. En viktig begränsning: AQ är självskattning, inte en diagnos, och det är oklart om dragen fanns före anorexin eller delvis speglar dess effekter.

title: Striatal Circuits as a Common Node for Autism Pathophysiology.
authors: Fuccillo MV
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are characterized by two seemingly unrelated symptom domains-deficits in social interactions and restrictive, repetitive patterns of behavioral output. Whether the diverse nature of ASD symptomatology represents distributed dysfunction of brain networks or abnormalities within specific neural circuits is unclear. Striatal dysfunction is postulated to underlie the repetitive motor behaviors seen in ASD, and neurological and brain-imaging studies have supported this assumption. However, as our appreciation of striatal function expands to include regulation of behavioral flexibility, motivational state, goal-directed learning, and attention, we consider whether alterations in striatal physiology are a central node mediating a range of autism-associated behaviors, including social and cognitive deficits that are hallmarks of the disease. This review investigates multiple genetic mouse models of ASD to explore whether abnormalities in striatal circuits constitute a common pathophysiological mechanism in the development of autism-related behaviors. Despite the heterogeneity of genetic insult investigated, numerous genetic ASD models display alterations in the structure and function of striatal circuits, as well as abnormal behaviors including repetitive grooming, stereotypic motor routines, deficits in social interaction and decision-making. Comparative analysis in rodents provides a unique opportunity to leverage growing genetic association data to reveal canonical neural circuits whose dysfunction directly contributes to discrete aspects of ASD symptomatology. The description of such circuits could provide both organizing principles for understanding the complex genetic etiology of ASD as well as novel treatment routes. Furthermore, this focus on striatal mechanisms of behavioral regulation may also prove useful for exploring the pathogenesis of other neuropsychiatric diseases, which display overlapping behavioral deficits with ASD.

sheet.es: Mañana no hace falta cambiar nada en casa por este estudio. Sugiere que una zona del cerebro, el estriado, podría estar relacionada con la repetición, la flexibilidad, la motivación y la atención en el autismo. Para quien cuida, puede ayudar a ver los movimientos repetitivos y la necesidad de rutinas como parte de cómo funciona ese cerebro, no como algo que haya que corregir: anticipar cambios y respetar formas de autorregularse sigue siendo útil. Es una revisión de estudios con ratones modificados genéticamente; no participaron personas autistas. Sus límites son claros: los ratones no reflejan la experiencia humana y no ofrece tratamientos ni conclusiones válidas para cada persona.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change at home tomorrow because of this study. It suggests that one brain area, the striatum, may be linked to repetition, flexibility, motivation and attention in autism. For caregivers, it can help frame repetitive movements and the need for routine as part of how that brain works, not something to fix: preparing for changes and respecting ways of self-regulating remain helpful. This is a review of studies in genetically modified mice; no autistic people took part. Its limits are clear: mice cannot reflect human experience, and it offers no treatments or conclusions that apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Ingenting behöver ändras hemma i morgon på grund av den här studien. Den antyder att ett hjärnområde, striatum, kan ha samband med upprepning, flexibilitet, motivation och uppmärksamhet vid autism. För dig som stöttar kan den hjälpa till att se upprepade rörelser och behovet av rutiner som en del av hur hjärnan fungerar, inte något som ska rättas till: att förbereda förändringar och respektera sätt att självreglera är fortfarande värdefullt. Det är en översikt av studier på genmodifierade möss; inga autistiska personer deltog. Begränsningarna är tydliga: möss speglar inte mänsklig erfarenhet, och översikten ger inga behandlingar eller slutsatser som gäller alla.

title: A review of executive function deficits in autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
authors: Craig F, Margari F, Legrottaglie AR, Palumbi R, de Giambattista C, Margari L
abstract: Executive dysfunction has been shown to be a promising endophenotype in neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This article reviewed 26 studies that examined executive function comparing ASD and/or ADHD children. In light of findings from this review, the ASD + ADHD group appears to share impairment in both flexibility and planning with the ASD group, while it shares the response inhibition deficit with the ADHD group. Conversely, deficit in attention, working memory, preparatory processes, fluency, and concept formation does not appear to be distinctive in discriminating from ASD, ADHD, or ASD + ADHD group. On the basis of neurocognitive endophenotype, the common co-occurrence of executive function deficits seems to reflect an additive comorbidity, rather than a separate condition with distinct impairments.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija es autista, y quizá también tiene TDAH, puede ayudar observar qué le cuesta concretamente: cambiar de plan, organizar pasos o frenar un impulso. Avisar de los cambios con antelación, dividir tareas en pasos visibles y dar pausas antes de responder son apoyos sencillos que puedes probar mañana, ajustándolos a la persona. Esta revisión reunió 26 estudios con niños y niñas autistas, con TDAH o con ambos; quienes tenían ambos mostraban a la vez las dificultades típicas de cada uno, sumadas. Limitación: compara promedios de grupos con pruebas de laboratorio, así que no describe a cada niño ni su vida diaria.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic, and perhaps also has ADHD, it can help to notice what specifically is hard: switching plans, organising steps, or pausing before acting. Announcing changes ahead of time, breaking tasks into visible steps, and allowing a pause before responding are simple supports you can try tomorrow, adjusted to the person. This review gathered 26 studies of autistic children, children with ADHD, and children with both; those with both showed the typical differences of each, added together. Limitation: it compares group averages from lab tests, so it does not describe every child or their daily life.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt, och kanske också har ADHD, kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till vad som konkret är svårt: att byta plan, organisera steg eller hejda en impuls. Att förvarna om förändringar, dela upp uppgifter i synliga steg och ge en paus innan svar är enkla stöd du kan prova i morgon, anpassade efter personen. Översikten samlade 26 studier med autistiska barn, barn med ADHD och barn med båda; de med båda visade de typiska skillnaderna från vardera, sammanlagda. Begränsning: den jämför gruppgenomsnitt från labbtester och beskriver därför inte varje barn eller dess vardag.

title: Alteration of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder: effect of age and anatomical distance.
authors: Long Z, Duan X, Mantini D, Chen H
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with disruption of local- and long-range functional connectivity (FC). The direction of those changes in FC (increase or decrease), however, is inconsistent across studies. Further, age-dependent changes of distance-specific FC in ASD remain unclear. In this study, we used resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from sixty-four typical controls (TC) and sixty-four patients with ASD, whom we further classified into child ( 18 years). Functional connectivity (FC) analysis was conducted at voxel level. We employed a three-way analysis of covariance on FC to conduct statistical analyses. Results revealed that patients with ASD had lower FC than TC in cerebellum, fusiform gyrus, inferior occipital gyrus and posterior inferior temporal gyrus. Significant diagnosis-by-distance interaction was observed in ASD patients with reduced short-range and long-range FC in posterior cingulate cortex and medial prefrontal cortex. Importantly, we found significant diagnosis-by-age-by-distance interaction in orbitofrontal cortex with short-range FC being lower in autistic children, but -to a less extent- higher in autistic adults. Our findings suggest a major role of connection length in development changes of FC in ASD. We hope our study will facilitate deeper understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying ASD.

sheet.es: Para mañana: este estudio no cambia nada de lo que haces en casa. Muestra que el cerebro autista se conecta de forma diferente y que esas diferencias cambian con la edad, lo que respalda la idea de que las necesidades de tu hijo o familiar pueden evolucionar con los años. Sigue observando qué le ayuda hoy, sin compararlo con otros. Evidencia: estudio de resonancia magnética en reposo con 64 personas autistas (niños, adolescentes y adultos) y 64 no autistas. Límites: muestra pequeña por grupo de edad, datos de un solo momento y sin relación directa con la vida diaria ni con apoyos concretos.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: this study doesn't change anything you do at home. It shows that autistic brains connect differently and that these differences shift with age, which supports the idea that your child's or loved one's needs may change over the years. Keep noticing what helps them today, without comparing them to others. Evidence: a resting-state brain scan (MRI) study with 64 autistic people (children, teens and adults) and 64 non-autistic people. Limits: small numbers in each age group, a single snapshot in time, and no direct link to daily life or specific supports.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon: studien ändrar inget i det du gör hemma. Den visar att autistiska hjärnor kopplar samman på andra sätt och att skillnaderna förändras med åldern, vilket stöder tanken att ditt barns eller din närståendes behov kan förändras över åren. Fortsätt lägga märke till vad som hjälper i dag, utan att jämföra med andra. Evidens: en studie med hjärnavbildning i vila (MR) med 64 autistiska personer (barn, tonåringar och vuxna) och 64 icke-autistiska. Begränsningar: få deltagare per åldersgrupp, en enda mätning och ingen direkt koppling till vardagen eller konkreta stöd.

title: Aggression in autism spectrum disorder: presentation and treatment options.
authors: Fitzpatrick SE, Srivorakiat L, Wink LK, Pedapati EV, Erickson CA
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent difficulties in social communication and social interaction, coupled with restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior or interest. Research indicates that aggression rates may be higher in individuals with ASD compared to those with other developmental disabilities. Aggression is associated with negative outcomes for children with ASD and their caregivers, including decreased quality of life, increased stress levels, and reduced availability of educational and social support. Therapeutic strategies including functional behavioral assessment, reinforcement strategies, and functional communication training may have a significant impact in reducing the frequency and intensity of aggressive behavior in individuals with ASD. Pharmacologic treatments, particularly the use of second-generation antipsychotics, may also be of some benefit in reducing aggression in individuals with ASD. With the ever-increasing rate of ASD diagnosis, development of effective therapeutic and pharmacologic methods for preventing and treating aggression are essential to improving outcomes in this disorder.

sheet.es: Cuando tu hijo o hija pega o empuja, suele estar comunicando algo: dolor, sobrecarga, miedo o una necesidad que no puede expresar de otra forma. Mañana puedes anotar qué pasó justo antes y después de cada episodio, buscar patrones (ruido, cambios, hambre, demandas) y ofrecer una forma sencilla de pedir pausa o ayuda, como una tarjeta, un gesto o una palabra, reforzándola cada vez que la use. Pide apoyo profesional para entender la función de la conducta. Se trata de una revisión de 2016 que resume estudios previos con niños y niñas autistas. Sus límites: no aporta datos nuevos, se centra en la infancia y no todas las estrategias sirven igual para cada persona.
sheet.en: When your child hits or pushes, they are often communicating something: pain, overload, fear, or a need they cannot express another way. Tomorrow you can note what happened just before and after each episode, look for patterns (noise, changes, hunger, demands), and offer a simple way to ask for a break or help, like a card, a gesture or a word, praising it every time it is used. Ask a professional to help understand what the behaviour is for. This is a 2016 review summarising earlier studies with autistic children. Its limits: it adds no new data, focuses on childhood, and no strategy works the same for every person.
sheet.sv: När ditt barn slår eller knuffar kommunicerar hen ofta något: smärta, överbelastning, rädsla eller ett behov som inte går att uttrycka på annat sätt. I morgon kan du anteckna vad som hände precis före och efter varje tillfälle, leta efter mönster (ljud, förändringar, hunger, krav) och erbjuda ett enkelt sätt att be om paus eller hjälp, som ett kort, en gest eller ett ord, och uppmuntra det varje gång det används. Be en yrkesperson om hjälp att förstå vad beteendet fyller för funktion. Detta är en översikt från 2016 som sammanfattar tidigare studier med autistiska barn. Begränsningar: den ger inga nya data, fokuserar på barndomen och ingen strategi fungerar likadant för alla.

title: Atopic diseases and inflammation of the brain in the pathogenesis of autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Theoharides TC, Tsilioni I, Patel AB, Doyle R
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) affect as many as 1 in 45 children and are characterized by deficits in sociability and communication, as well as stereotypic movements. Many children also show severe anxiety. The lack of distinct pathogenesis and reliable biomarkers hampers the development of effective treatments. As a result, most children with ASD are prescribed psychopharmacologic agents that do not address the core symptoms of ASD. Autoantibodies against brain epitopes in mothers of children with ASD and many such children strongly correlate with allergic symptoms and indicate an aberrant immune response, as well as disruption of the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Recent epidemiological studies have shown a strong statistical correlation between risk for ASD and either maternal or infantile atopic diseases, such as asthma, eczema, food allergies and food intolerance, all of which involve activation of mast cells (MCs). These unique tissue immune cells are located perivascularly in all tissues, including the thalamus and hypothalamus, which regulate emotions. MC-derived inflammatory and vasoactive mediators increase BBB permeability. Expression of the inflammatory molecules interleukin (IL-1β), IL-6, 1 L-17 and tumor necrosis factor (TNF) is increased in the brain, cerebrospinal fluid and serum of some patients with ASD, while NF-kB is activated in brain samples and stimulated peripheral blood immune cells of other patients; however, these molecules are not specific. Instead the peptide neurotensin is uniquely elevated in the serum of children with ASD, as is corticotropin-releasing hormone, secreted from the hypothalamus under stress. Both peptides trigger MC to release IL-6 and TNF, which in turn, stimulate microglia proliferation and activation, leading to disruption of neuronal connectivity. MC-derived IL-6 and TGFβ induce maturation of Th17 cells and MCs also secrete IL-17, which is increased in ASD. Serum IL-6 and TNF may define an ASD subgroup that benefits most from treatment with the natural flavonoid luteolin. Atopic diseases may create a phenotype susceptible to ASD and formulations targeting focal inflammation of the brain could have great promise in the treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene asma, eccema o alergias alimentarias, merece la pena tratarlas bien con su equipo de salud: el malestar físico, el picor o la dificultad para respirar pueden afectar al sueño, la ansiedad y el día a día. Anote síntomas y momentos difíciles para compartirlos en la consulta. Esta revisión narrativa reúne estudios previos que relacionan las alergias y la inflamación con el autismo; no incluyó participantes propios. Sus límites: plantea hipótesis sobre causas biológicas aún no confirmadas, y no demuestra que ningún suplemento o tratamiento antiinflamatorio sea adecuado para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has asthma, eczema or food allergies, it is worth managing them well with your health team: physical discomfort, itching or breathing difficulties can affect sleep, anxiety and everyday life. Keep brief notes on symptoms and hard moments to share at appointments. This narrative review brings together earlier studies linking allergies and inflammation with autism; it did not recruit its own participants. Its limits: it proposes biological explanations that are not yet confirmed, and it does not show that any supplement or anti-inflammatory treatment suits every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har astma, eksem eller matallergi är det värt att behandla dem ordentligt tillsammans med vården: kroppsligt obehag, klåda eller andningsbesvär kan påverka sömn, oro och vardagen. Skriv korta anteckningar om symtom och svåra stunder att ta med till besöken. Denna narrativa översikt sammanställer tidigare studier som kopplar allergier och inflammation till autism; den hade inga egna deltagare. Begränsningar: den föreslår biologiska förklaringar som ännu inte är bekräftade, och den visar inte att något kosttillskott eller antiinflammatorisk behandling passar alla.

title: Heritability of autism spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis of twin studies.
authors: Tick B, Bolton P, Happé F, Rutter M, Rijsdijk F
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background The etiology of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) has been recently debated due to emerging findings on the importance of shared environmental influences. However, two recent twin studies do not support this and instead re-affirm strong genetic effects on the liability to ASD, a finding consistent with previous reports. This study conducts a systematic review and meta-analysis of all twin studies of ASD published to date and explores the etiology along the continuum of a quantitative measure of ASD. Methods A PubMed Central, Science Direct, Google Scholar, Web of Knowledge structured search conducted online, to identify all twin studies on ASD published to date. Thirteen primary twin studies were identified, seven were included in the meta-analysis by meeting Systematic Recruitment criterion; correction for selection and ascertainment strategies, and applied prevalences were assessed for these studies. In addition, a quantile DF extremes analysis was carried out on Childhood Autism Spectrum Test scores measured in a population sample of 6,413 twin pairs including affected twins. Results The meta-analysis correlations for monozygotic twins (MZ) were almost perfect at .98 (95% Confidence Interval, .96-.99). The dizygotic (DZ) correlation, however, was .53 (95% CI .44-.60) when ASD prevalence rate was set at 5% (in line with the Broad Phenotype of ASD) and increased to .67 (95% CI .61-.72) when applying a prevalence rate of 1%. The meta-analytic heritability estimates were substantial: 64-91%. Shared environmental effects became significant as the prevalence rate decreased from 5-1%: 07-35%. The DF analyses show that for the most part, there is no departure from linearity in heritability. Conclusions We demonstrate that: (a) ASD is due to strong genetic effects; (b) shared environmental effects become significant as a function of lower prevalence rate; (c) previously reported significant shared environmental influences are likely a statistical artefact of overinclusion of concordant DZ twins.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si algo que hiciste causó el autismo de tu hijo o hija, este estudio ofrece calma: el autismo tiene una base genética fuerte, no es fruto de la crianza. Mañana puedes dejar la culpa a un lado y centrar tu energía en conocer cómo percibe el mundo tu hijo y qué apoyos le ayudan. También puede ser útil saber que hermanos y familiares pueden compartir rasgos. Es un metaanálisis de siete estudios de gemelos, más un análisis de 6.413 parejas de gemelos. Sus límites: las estimaciones de heredabilidad (64-91%) varían según cómo se calcule la prevalencia, y describen poblaciones, no explican la historia de cada persona.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether something you did caused your child's autism, this study offers reassurance: autism has a strong genetic basis and is not the result of parenting. Tomorrow you can set guilt aside and put your energy into understanding how your child experiences the world and which supports help. It may also help to know that siblings and relatives can share some traits. This is a meta-analysis of seven twin studies, plus an analysis of 6,413 twin pairs. Its limits: heritability estimates (64-91%) shift depending on assumed prevalence, and they describe populations, not any single person's story.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om något du gjort orsakade ditt barns autism ger den här studien lugn: autism har en stark genetisk grund och beror inte på uppfostran. I morgon kan du lägga skulden åt sidan och lägga din energi på att förstå hur ditt barn upplever världen och vilket stöd som hjälper. Det kan också vara bra att veta att syskon och släktingar kan dela vissa drag. Detta är en metaanalys av sju tvillingstudier, plus en analys av 6 413 tvillingpar. Begränsningar: ärftlighetsskattningarna (64–91 %) varierar med antagen förekomst, och de beskriver grupper, inte en enskild persons historia.

title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Multiple Airborne Pollutants and Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Lam J, Sutton P, Kalkbrenner A, Windham G, Halladay A, Koustas E, Lawler C, Davidson L, Daniels N, Newschaffer C, Woodruff T
abstract: Background Exposure to ambient air pollution is widespread and may be detrimental to human brain development and a potential risk factor for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). We conducted a systematic review of the human evidence on the relationship between ASD and exposure to all airborne pollutants, including particulate matter air pollutants and others (e.g. pesticides and metals). Objective To answer the question: "is developmental exposure to air pollution associated with ASD?" Methods We conducted a comprehensive search of the literature, identified relevant studies using inclusion/exclusion criteria pre-specified in our protocol (registered in PROSPERO, CRD # 42015017890), evaluated the potential risk of bias for each included study and identified an appropriate subset of studies to combine in a meta-analysis. We then rated the overall quality and strength of the evidence collectively across all air pollutants. Results Of 1,158 total references identified, 23 human studies met our inclusion criteria (17 case-control, 4 ecological, 2 cohort). Risk of bias was generally low across studies for most domains; study limitations were related to potential confounding and accuracy of exposure assessment methods. We rated the quality of the body of evidence across all air pollutants as "moderate." From our meta-analysis, we found statistically significant summary odds ratios (ORs) of 1.07 (95% CI: 1.06, 1.08) per 10-μg/m3 increase in PM10 exposure (n = 6 studies) and 2.32 (95% CI: 2.15, 2.51) per 10-μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 exposure (n = 3 studies). For pollutants not included in a meta-analysis, we collectively evaluated evidence from each study in rating the strength and quality of overall evidence considering factors such as inconsistency, imprecision, and evidence of dose-response. All included studies generally showed increased risk of ASD with increasing exposure to air pollution, although not consistently across all chemical components. Conclusion After considering strengths and limitations of the body of research, we concluded that there is "limited evidence of toxicity" for the association between early life exposure to air pollution as a whole and diagnosis of ASD. The strongest evidence was between prenatal exposure to particulate matter and ASD. However, the small number of studies in the meta-analysis and unexplained statistical heterogeneity across the individual study estimates means that the effect could be larger or smaller (including not significant) than these studies estimate. Our research supports the need for health protective public policy to reduce exposures to harmful airborne contaminants among pregnant women and children and suggests opportunities for optimizing future research.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija ya es autista, este estudio no significa que hicieras algo mal: el aire que respiramos depende sobre todo de decisiones colectivas, no de una familia. Lo útil es apoyar políticas de aire limpio y, si estás embarazada o planeas estarlo, hablar con tu equipo de salud sobre formas sencillas de reducir la exposición a contaminación. Es una revisión sistemática con metaanálisis de 23 estudios en humanos que encontró una asociación entre partículas finas en el embarazo y diagnósticos de autismo. Sus límites: pocos estudios combinados, resultados variables y posibles factores de confusión; muestra asociación, no causa, y la evidencia se calificó como limitada.
sheet.en: If your child is already autistic, this study does not mean you did something wrong: the air we breathe depends mostly on collective decisions, not on one family. A useful step is supporting clean-air policies and, if you are pregnant or planning to be, talking with your health team about simple ways to reduce pollution exposure. This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 human studies that found an association between fine particulate matter during pregnancy and autism diagnoses. Its limits: few studies were combined, results varied, and confounding is possible; it shows association, not cause, and the evidence was rated as limited.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn redan är autistiskt betyder studien inte att du gjort något fel: luften vi andas beror främst på gemensamma beslut, inte på en enskild familj. Ett användbart steg är att stödja politik för ren luft och, om du är gravid eller planerar att bli det, prata med vårdpersonal om enkla sätt att minska exponeringen för luftföroreningar. Detta är en systematisk översikt och metaanalys av 23 studier på människor som fann ett samband mellan fina partiklar under graviditeten och autismdiagnoser. Begränsningar: få studier kunde slås samman, resultaten varierade och störfaktorer är möjliga; studien visar samband, inte orsak, och evidensen bedömdes som begränsad.

title: Synaptopathies: synaptic dysfunction in neurological disorders - A review from students to students.
authors: Lepeta K, Lourenco MV, Schweitzer BC, Martino Adami PV, Banerjee P, Catuara-Solarz S, de La Fuente Revenga M, Guillem AM, Haidar M, Ijomone OM, Nadorp B, Qi L, Perera ND, Refsgaard LK, Reid KM, Sabbar
abstract: Synapses are essential components of neurons and allow information to travel coordinately throughout the nervous system to adjust behavior to environmental stimuli and to control body functions, memories, and emotions. Thus, optimal synaptic communication is required for proper brain physiology, and slight perturbations of synapse function can lead to brain disorders. In fact, increasing evidence has demonstrated the relevance of synapse dysfunction as a major determinant of many neurological diseases. This notion has led to the concept of synaptopathies as brain diseases with synapse defects as shared pathogenic features. In this review, which was initiated at the 13th International Society for Neurochemistry Advanced School, we discuss basic concepts of synapse structure and function, and provide a critical view of how aberrant synapse physiology may contribute to neurodevelopmental disorders (autism, Down syndrome, startle disease, and epilepsy) as well as neurodegenerative disorders (Alzheimer and Parkinson disease). We finally discuss the appropriateness and potential implications of gathering synapse diseases under a single term. Understanding common causes and intrinsic differences in disease-associated synaptic dysfunction could offer novel clues toward synapse-based therapeutic intervention for neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders. In this Review, which was initiated at the 13th International Society for Neurochemistry (ISN) Advanced School, we discuss basic concepts of synapse structure and function, and provide a critical view of how aberrant synapse physiology may contribute to neurodevelopmental (autism, Down syndrome, startle disease, and epilepsy) as well as neurodegenerative disorders (Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases), gathered together under the term of synaptopathies. Read the Editorial Highlight for this article on page 783.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en el día a día: esta revisión no ofrece estrategias ni tratamientos para la vida cotidiana. Explica que la comunicación entre neuronas (sinapsis) puede funcionar de forma distinta en el autismo y en otras condiciones, lo que ayuda a entender que las diferencias en procesamiento sensorial o en el ritmo de aprendizaje tienen una base biológica real, no son falta de esfuerzo. Se trata de una revisión narrativa escrita por estudiantes de neuroquímica que resume estudios de laboratorio, sin participantes autistas propios. Su límite: agrupa condiciones muy diferentes bajo una sola etiqueta y no permite sacar conclusiones sobre ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change tomorrow morning: this review offers no strategies or treatments for daily life. It explains that communication between brain cells (synapses) may work differently in autism and other conditions, which can help you see that differences in sensory processing or learning pace have a real biological basis, not a lack of effort. It is a narrative review written by neurochemistry students, summarising mostly laboratory research, with no autistic participants of its own. Its limit: it groups very different conditions under one label and cannot tell you anything about a specific person.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras i morgon bitti: översikten ger inga strategier eller behandlingar för vardagen. Den förklarar att kommunikationen mellan nervceller (synapser) kan fungera annorlunda vid autism och andra tillstånd, vilket kan hjälpa dig att se att skillnader i sinnesintryck eller inlärningstakt har en verklig biologisk grund och inte handlar om bristande ansträngning. Det är en berättande översikt skriven av neurokemistudenter som sammanfattar främst laboratorieforskning, utan egna autistiska deltagare. Begränsningen: den samlar mycket olika tillstånd under en etikett och säger ingenting om en enskild person.

title: A Systematic Review of Research on Autism Spectrum Disorders in Sub-Saharan Africa.
authors: Abubakar A, Ssewanyana D, Newton CR
abstract: The burden of autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is not well known. We carried out a systematic review of the literature to identify published work from SSA. We have systematically searched four databases, namely, Medline, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Child Development & Adolescent Studies, through EBSCO and identified studies from across SSA. Based on predefined inclusion criteria, 47 studies were included in this review. Most of the identified studies (74%) were conducted in only 2 African countries, that is, South Africa and Nigeria. Additionally, most of these studies (83%) were carried out in the last decade. These studies had four major themes: development of measurement tools of ASD in Africa, examining the prevalence of ASD, identifying risk factors and risk markers, and examining psychosocial issues. We identified only a single population level study aimed at documenting the prevalence of ASD and could not identify a single case-control study aimed at examining a comprehensive set of potential risk factors. All intervention studies were based on very small sample sizes. Put together, our findings suggest that current evidence base is too scanty to provide the required information to plan adequately for effective intervention strategies for children with ASD in Africa.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista en África subsahariana, o vienes de allí, es normal sentir que la información disponible no refleja tu realidad. Puedes confiar en lo que observas a diario, anotar qué ayuda a tu familiar y buscar redes locales de familias y personas autistas. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 47 estudios publicados sobre autismo en la región; la mayoría se hicieron en Sudáfrica y Nigeria, y se centraron en herramientas de evaluación, prevalencia, factores de riesgo y aspectos sociales. Su límite principal es que la evidencia es escasa: solo hubo un estudio poblacional y los estudios de apoyo tenían muy pocos participantes, así que no ofrece pautas válidas para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in sub-Saharan Africa, or your family comes from there, it is understandable to feel that available information does not reflect your reality. You can trust what you observe day to day, note what helps your family member, and look for local networks of families and autistic people. This systematic review examined 47 published studies on autism in the region; most came from South Africa and Nigeria and focused on assessment tools, prevalence, risk factors and social issues. Its main limit is how thin the evidence is: there was only one population study and support studies had very few participants, so it offers no rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i Afrika söder om Sahara, eller om din familj kommer därifrån, är det begripligt att känna att tillgänglig information inte speglar er verklighet. Du kan lita på det du ser i vardagen, anteckna vad som hjälper din närstående och söka lokala nätverk av familjer och autistiska personer. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 47 publicerade studier om autism i regionen; de flesta kom från Sydafrika och Nigeria och handlade om bedömningsverktyg, förekomst, riskfaktorer och sociala frågor. Den största begränsningen är att underlaget är tunt: bara en befolkningsstudie fanns och stödstudierna hade mycket få deltagare, så den ger ingen regel för alla.

title: The role of sex-differential biology in risk for autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Werling DM
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a developmental condition that affects approximately four times as many males as females, a strong sex bias that has not yet been fully explained. Understanding the causes of this biased prevalence may highlight novel avenues for treatment development that could benefit patients with diverse genetic backgrounds, and the expertise of sex differences researchers will be invaluable in this endeavor. In this review, I aim to assess current evidence pertaining to the sex difference in ASD prevalence and to identify outstanding questions and remaining gaps in our understanding of how males come to be more frequently affected and/or diagnosed with ASD. Though males consistently outnumber females in ASD prevalence studies, prevalence estimates generated using different approaches report male/female ratios of variable magnitude that suggest that ascertainment or diagnostic biases may contribute to the male skew in ASD. Here, I present the different methods applied and implications of their findings. Additionally, even as prevalence estimations challenge the degree of male bias in ASD, support is growing for the long-proposed female protective effect model of ASD risk, and I review the relevant results from recurrence rate, quantitative trait, and genetic analyses. Lastly, I describe work investigating several sex-differential biological factors and pathways that may be responsible for females' protection and/or males' increased risk predicted by the female protective effect model, including sex steroid hormone exposure and regulation and sex-differential activity of certain neural cell types. However, much future work from both the ASD and sex differences research communities will be required to flesh out our understanding of how these factors act to influence the developing brain and modulate ASD risk.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña o mujer y notas rasgos autistas, vale la pena pedir una evaluación aunque no encaje en la imagen típica: el autismo en chicas puede pasar desapercibido. Anota ejemplos concretos de su día a día (sensorialidad, cansancio social, intereses intensos) y llévalos a la consulta. Esta es una revisión narrativa de estudios sobre por qué se diagnostica autismo más en varones; sugiere que influyen tanto sesgos diagnósticos como factores biológicos, como hormonas y genética. Sus límites: no aporta datos nuevos, muchas hipótesis biológicas siguen sin confirmar y no sirve para predecir nada sobre una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you support a girl or woman and notice autistic traits, it is worth asking for an assessment even if she does not fit the typical picture: autism in girls can be overlooked. Write down concrete everyday examples (sensory experiences, social exhaustion, intense interests) and bring them to appointments. This is a narrative review of research on why autism is diagnosed more often in males; it suggests both diagnostic bias and biological factors, such as hormones and genetics, play a part. Its limits: it adds no new data, many biological ideas remain unconfirmed, and it cannot predict anything about one individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en flicka eller kvinna och ser autistiska drag kan det vara värt att be om en utredning även om hon inte passar den typiska bilden: autism hos flickor kan förbises. Skriv ner konkreta vardagsexempel (sinnesintryck, social utmattning, starka intressen) och ta med dem till besöket. Detta är en narrativ översikt av forskning om varför autism oftare diagnostiseras hos pojkar och män; den pekar på både diagnostiska skevheter och biologiska faktorer, som hormoner och genetik. Begränsningar: den tillför inga nya data, många biologiska hypoteser är obekräftade och den kan inte förutsäga något om en enskild person.

title: The neuroanatomy of autism - a developmental perspective.
authors: Donovan AP, Basson MA
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) are a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders that are diagnosed solely on the basis of behaviour. A large body of work has reported neuroanatomical differences between individuals with ASD and neurotypical controls. Despite the huge clinical and genetic heterogeneity that typifies autism, some of these anatomical features appear to be either present in most cases or so dramatically altered in some that their presence is now reasonably well replicated in a number of studies. One such finding is the tendency towards overgrowth of the frontal cortex during the early postnatal period. Although these reports have been focused primarily on the presumed pathological anatomy, they are providing us with important insights into normal brain anatomy and are stimulating new ideas and hypotheses about the normal trajectory of brain development and the function of specific anatomical brain structures. The use of model systems that include genetic model organisms such as the mouse and, more recently, human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoids to model normal and pathological human cortical development, is proving particularly informative. Here we review some of the neuroanatomical alterations reported in autism, with a particular focus on well-validated findings and recent advances in the field, and ask what these observations can tell us about normal and abnormal brain development.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: no necesitas pruebas cerebrales para apoyar a tu hijo o familiar autista mañana. Esta investigación describe diferencias en cómo se desarrolla el cerebro autista, por ejemplo un crecimiento temprano mayor de la corteza frontal en algunos niños, lo que recuerda que muchas formas de percibir y reaccionar tienen una base biológica real, no son mala voluntad. Observa qué le ayuda y ajusta el entorno. Se trata de una revisión de estudios con personas, ratones y organoides cerebrales de laboratorio. Límite: los hallazgos son promedios de grupo, no describen a cada persona ni sirven para diagnosticar o decidir apoyos individuales.
sheet.en: The practical point: you don't need brain scans to support your autistic child or family member tomorrow. This research describes differences in how the autistic brain develops, such as faster early growth of the frontal cortex in some children, a reminder that many ways of perceiving and reacting have a real biological basis rather than being wilful. Notice what helps and adjust the environment. This is a review of studies involving people, mice and lab-grown brain organoids. Limit: the findings are group averages; they don't describe every person and can't be used to diagnose or choose individual support.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: du behöver inga hjärnundersökningar för att stötta ditt autistiska barn eller din autistiska anhörige i morgon. Forskningen beskriver skillnader i hur den autistiska hjärnan utvecklas, till exempel snabbare tidig tillväxt av pannloben hos en del barn, en påminnelse om att många sätt att uppfatta och reagera har en verklig biologisk grund och inte handlar om ovilja. Lägg märke till vad som hjälper och anpassa miljön. Det här är en översikt av studier på människor, möss och odlade hjärnorganoider. Begränsning: fynden är gruppgenomsnitt, beskriver inte varje person och kan inte användas för att ställa diagnos eller välja individuellt stöd.

title: Resting-State Functional Connectivity in Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Review.
authors: Hull JV, Dokovna LB, Jacokes ZJ, Torgerson CM, Irimia A, Van Horn JD
abstract: Ongoing debate exists within the resting-state functional MRI (fMRI) literature over how intrinsic connectivity is altered in the autistic brain, with reports of general over-connectivity, under-connectivity, and/or a combination of both. Classifying autism using brain connectivity is complicated by the heterogeneous nature of the condition, allowing for the possibility of widely variable connectivity patterns among individuals with the disorder. Further differences in reported results may be attributable to the age and sex of participants included, designs of the resting-state scan, and to the analysis technique used to evaluate the data. This review systematically examines the resting-state fMRI autism literature to date and compares studies in an attempt to draw overall conclusions that are presently challenging. We also propose future direction for rs-fMRI use to categorize individuals with autism spectrum disorder, serve as a possible diagnostic tool, and best utilize data-sharing initiatives.

sheet.es: Si alguien le ofrece un escáner cerebral para «confirmar» o «clasificar» el autismo de su hijo o el suyo propio, puede tomarlo con calma: hoy no existe un patrón cerebral único del autismo. Cada cerebro autista conecta de forma distinta, y conocer a la persona, sus fortalezas y sus necesidades sigue siendo lo más útil en el día a día. Esta revisión de 2016 reunió estudios de resonancia magnética funcional en reposo con personas autistas de distintas edades. Sus límites: los estudios usaron métodos, edades y grupos muy diferentes, y los resultados se contradicen, así que no sirve como herramienta de diagnóstico.
sheet.en: If someone offers a brain scan to “confirm” or “classify” your child’s autism or your own, you can stay calm: today there is no single autistic brain pattern. Each autistic brain connects differently, and getting to know the person, their strengths and their needs remains the most useful thing day to day. This 2016 review gathered resting-state functional MRI studies of autistic people of different ages. Its limits: the studies used very different methods, ages and groups, and their results contradict each other, so this is not a diagnostic tool.
sheet.sv: Om någon erbjuder en hjärnskanning för att ”bekräfta” eller ”klassificera” ditt barns autism eller din egen kan du ta det lugnt: i dag finns inget enskilt autistiskt hjärnmönster. Varje autistisk hjärna kopplar på sitt eget sätt, och att lära känna personen, dess styrkor och behov är fortfarande det mest användbara i vardagen. Denna översikt från 2016 samlade studier med funktionell MR i vila hos autistiska personer i olika åldrar. Begränsningar: studierna använde mycket olika metoder, åldrar och grupper, och resultaten motsäger varandra, så det fungerar inte som diagnosverktyg.

title: Sensory, Emotional and Cognitive Contributions to Anxiety in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: South M, Rodgers J
abstract: Severe symptoms of anxiety add substantial additional burden to many individuals diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Improved understanding of specific factors that contribute to anxiety in ASD can aid research regarding the causes of autism and also provide targets for more effective intervention. This mini-review article focuses on emerging evidence for three concepts that appear to be related to each other and which also strongly predict anxiety in ASD samples. Atypical sensory function is included in the diagnostic criteria for ASD and is likely an important contributor to anxiety. Difficulties in understanding and labeling emotions ( alexithymia ), although a co-morbidity, may arise in part from atypical sensory function and can lead to confusion and uncertainty about how to respond to social and emotional situations. Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) describes people who have a particularly hard time with ambiguity and is known to be a key mechanism underlying some anxiety disorders. While evidence for linking these ideas is to date incomplete, we put forward a model including each concept as a framework for future studies. Specifically, we propose that IU is a critical mediator for anxiety in ASD, and explore the relationships between sensory function, alexithymia and IU. We further explore the role of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) in regulating emotional response, in connection with limbic and insula-based networks, and suggest that disrupted integration in these networks underlies difficulties with habituation to strong emotional stimuli, which results in an enhanced perception of threat in many people with ASD. Behavioral and biologically-based treatments for anxiety in ASD will benefit from attending to these specific mechanisms as adjunct to traditional interventions.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo se muestra ansiosa, puede ayudar fijarse en tres cosas: cómo vive los sonidos, luces o texturas; si le cuesta reconocer o nombrar lo que siente; y cuánto le pesa no saber qué va a pasar. Mañana podrías anticipar los cambios del día con claridad, reducir estímulos molestos y ofrecer palabras o imágenes para expresar emociones, sin presionar. Se trata de una mini-revisión que reúne estudios previos y propone un modelo que conecta sensorialidad, dificultad para identificar emociones (alexitimia) e intolerancia a la incertidumbre con la ansiedad. Es una propuesta teórica: la evidencia aún es incompleta y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support seems anxious, it may help to look at three things: how they experience sounds, lights or textures; whether naming their feelings is hard; and how much not knowing what comes next weighs on them. Tomorrow you could preview the day's changes clearly, reduce bothersome sensory input, and offer words or pictures for emotions, without pressure. This is a mini-review that gathers earlier research and proposes a model linking sensory experience, difficulty identifying emotions (alexithymia) and intolerance of uncertainty to anxiety. It is a theoretical proposal: the evidence is still incomplete, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar verkar orolig kan det hjälpa att titta på tre saker: hur hen upplever ljud, ljus eller texturer; om det är svårt att sätta ord på känslor; och hur tungt det är att inte veta vad som händer härnäst. I morgon kan du tydligt förbereda dagens förändringar, minska störande sinnesintryck och erbjuda ord eller bilder för känslor, utan press. Detta är en kort översikt som samlar tidigare forskning och föreslår en modell som kopplar sinnesupplevelser, svårighet att identifiera känslor (alexitymi) och intolerans mot osäkerhet till ångest. Det är ett teoretiskt förslag: evidensen är ännu ofullständig och varje person är olik.

title: Specificity, contexts, and reference groups matter when assessing autistic traits.
authors: Gernsbacher MA, Stevenson JL, Dern S
abstract: Many of the personality and behavioral traits (e.g., social imperviousness, directness in conversation, lack of imagination, affinity for solitude, difficulty displaying emotions) that are known to be sensitive to context (with whom?) and reference group (according to whom?) also appear in questionnaire-based assessments of autistic traits. Therefore, two experiments investigated the effects of specifying contexts and reference groups when assessing autistic traits in autistic and non-autistic participants. Experiment 1 (124 autistic and 124 non-autistic participants) demonstrated that context matters when assessing autistic traits (F(1,244) = 267.5, p < .001, η2p = .523). When the context of the Broad Autism Phenotype Questionnaire was specified as the participants' out-group (e.g., "I like being around non-autistic people" or "I like being around autistic people"), both autistic and non-autistic participants self-reported having more autistic traits; when the context was specified as the participants' in-group, participants reported having fewer autistic traits. Experiment 2 (82 autistic and 82 non-autistic participants) demonstrated that reference group matters when assessing autistic traits (F(2,160) = 94.38, p < .001, η2p = .541). When the reference group on the Social Responsiveness Scale was specified as the participants' out-group (e.g., "According to non-autistic people, I have unusual eye contact"), autistic participants reported having more autistic traits; when the reference group was their in-group, autistic participants reported having fewer autistic traits. Non-autistic participants appeared insensitive to reference group on the Social Responsiveness Scale. Exploratory analyses suggested that when neither the context nor the reference group is specified (for assessing autistic traits on the Autism-Spectrum Quotient), both autistic and non-autistic participants use the majority ("non-autistic people") as the implied context and reference group.

sheet.es: Lo que parece un «rasgo autista» depende mucho de con quién está la persona y de quién la juzga. Mañana, al observar o describir a tu familiar, pregúntate: ¿con quién estaba?, ¿según quién es «raro» su contacto visual o su forma de hablar? Puede sentirse cómoda y conversadora entre personas autistas y retraída entre no autistas. Anota los contextos donde está a gusto y busca más de ellos. Evidencia: dos experimentos con cuestionarios en los que participaron adultos autistas y no autistas (124+124 y 82+82). Límites: se basa en autoinformes en línea de adultos, y quizá no refleje a niños ni a personas que no usan el habla.
sheet.en: What looks like an "autistic trait" depends a lot on who the person is with and who is judging. Tomorrow, when you observe or describe your family member, ask: who were they with? According to whom is their eye contact or way of talking "unusual"? They may feel at ease and chatty among autistic people and withdrawn among non-autistic people. Note the settings where they feel comfortable and look for more of them. Evidence: two questionnaire experiments with autistic and non-autistic adults (124+124 and 82+82). Limits: it relies on online self-reports from adults, and may not reflect children or people who do not use speech.
sheet.sv: Det som ser ut som ett "autistiskt drag" beror mycket på vem personen är med och vem som bedömer. I morgon, när du iakttar eller beskriver din närstående, fråga dig: vem var hen med? Enligt vem är ögonkontakten eller sättet att prata "ovanligt"? Hen kan känna sig trygg och pratsam bland autistiska personer och dra sig undan bland icke-autistiska. Notera i vilka sammanhang hen trivs och sök fler sådana. Evidens: två enkätexperiment med autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna (124+124 och 82+82). Begränsningar: studien bygger på vuxnas självskattningar online och speglar kanske inte barn eller personer som inte använder tal.

title: Physical activity, sedentary behavior and their correlates in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A systematic review.
authors: Jones RA, Downing K, Rinehart NJ, Barnett LM, May T, McGillivray JA, Papadopoulos NV, Skouteris H, Timperio A, Hinkley T
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder affects up to 2.5% of children and is associated with harmful health outcomes (e.g. obesity). Low levels of physical activity and high levels of sedentary behaviors may contribute to harmful health outcomes. To systematically review the prevalence and correlates of physical activity and sedentary behaviors in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder, electronic databases (PsycINFO, SPORTDiscus, EMBASE, Medline) were searched from inception to November 2015. The review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42014013849). Peer-reviewed, English language studies were included. Two reviewers screened potentially relevant articles. Outcomes of interest were physical activity and sedentary behaviour levels and their potential correlates. Data were collected and analysed in 2015. Of 35 included studies, 15 reported physical activity prevalence, 10 reported physical activity correlates, 18 reported sedentary behavior prevalence, and 10 reported sedentary behavior correlates. Estimates of children's physical activity (34-166 mins/day, average 86 mins/day) and sedentary behavior (126-558 mins/day in screen time, average 271 mins/day; 428-750 mins/day in total sedentary behavior, average 479 mins/day) varied across studies. Age was consistently inversely associated, and sex inconsistently associated with physical activity. Age and sex were inconsistently associated with sedentary behavior. Sample sizes were small. All but one of the studies were classified as having high risk of bias. Few correlates have been reported in sufficient studies to provide overall estimates of associations. Potential correlates in the physical environment remain largely unexamined. This review highlights varying levels of physical activity and sedentary behavior in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Research is needed to consistently identify the correlates of these behaviors. There is a critical need for interventions to support healthy levels of these behaviors.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista se mueve menos a medida que crece, no es algo raro: en esta revisión, la actividad física solía bajar con la edad. Mañana puedes buscar una forma de movimiento que le resulte agradable y predecible, como un paseo con ruta conocida, saltar en una cama elástica o nadar, y reservar momentos sin pantallas que no se vivan como castigo. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de 35 estudios con niños y niñas autistas, con cifras muy variables entre estudios. Sus límites: muestras pequeñas, casi todos los estudios con alto riesgo de sesgo y poca información sobre el entorno; no sirve como norma para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your autistic child moves less as they get older, you are not alone: in this review, physical activity tended to drop with age. Tomorrow you could look for one kind of movement your child enjoys and finds predictable, such as a familiar walking route, a trampoline or swimming, and plan some screen-free moments that don't feel like punishment. This is a systematic review of 35 studies of autistic children, and activity and screen-time levels varied widely between them. Its limits: samples were small, nearly all studies had high risk of bias, and the physical environment was barely studied, so it is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn rör sig mindre ju äldre det blir är ni inte ensamma: i den här översikten minskade fysisk aktivitet ofta med åldern. I morgon kan du leta efter en rörelseform som barnet tycker om och som känns förutsägbar, till exempel en välbekant promenadrunda, studsmatta eller simning, och planera skärmfria stunder som inte upplevs som straff. Det är en systematisk översikt av 35 studier med autistiska barn, där nivåerna av aktivitet och skärmtid varierade mycket. Begränsningar: små urval, nästan alla studier hade hög risk för bias och den fysiska miljön var knappt undersökt, så resultaten är ingen regel för varje barn.

title: Relationship between Long Chain n-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Autism Spectrum Disorder: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Case-Control and Randomised Controlled Trials.
authors: Mazahery H, Stonehouse W, Delshad M, Kruger MC, Conlon CA, Beck KL, von Hurst PR
abstract: Omega-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation ( n -3 LCPUFA) for treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is popular. The results of previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses of n -3 LCPUFA supplementation on ASD outcomes were inconclusive. Two meta-analyses were conducted; meta-analysis 1 compared blood levels of LCPUFA and their ratios arachidonic acid (ARA) to docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), ARA to eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), or total n -6 to total n -3 LCPUFA in ASD to those of typically developing individuals (with no neurodevelopmental disorders), and meta-analysis 2 compared the effects of n -3 LCPUFA supplementation to placebo on symptoms of ASD. Case-control studies and randomised controlled trials (RCTs) were identified searching electronic databases up to May, 2016. Mean differences were pooled and analysed using inverse variance models. Heterogeneity was assessed using I ² statistic. Fifteen case-control studies ( n = 1193) were reviewed. Compared with typically developed, ASD populations had lower DHA (-2.14 [95% CI -3.22 to -1.07]; p I ² = 97%), EPA (-0.72 [95% CI -1.25 to -0.18]; p = 0.008; I ² = 88%), and ARA (-0.83 [95% CI, -1.48 to -0.17]; p = 0.01; I ² = 96%) and higher total n -6 LCPUFA to n -3 LCPUFA ratio (0.42 [95% CI 0.06 to 0.78]; p = 0.02; I ² = 74%). Four RCTs were included in meta-analysis 2 ( n = 107). Compared with placebo, n -3 LCPUFA improved social interaction (-1.96 [95% CI -3.5 to -0.34]; p = 0.02; I ² = 0) and repetitive and restricted interests and behaviours (-1.08 [95% CI -2.17 to -0.01]; p = 0.05; I ² = 0). Populations with ASD have lower n -3 LCPUFA status and n -3 LCPUFA supplementation can potentially improve some ASD symptoms. Further research with large sample size and adequate study duration is warranted to confirm the efficacy of n -3 LCPUFA.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas por los suplementos de omega-3, esta revisión no ofrece una respuesta firme. Antes de probar algo, conviene hablarlo con el equipo de salud. Mientras tanto, una alimentación variada que incluya pescado u otras fuentes de omega-3, adaptada a las preferencias sensoriales de tu familiar, es un paso tranquilo. Evidencia: metaanálisis de 15 estudios de casos y controles (1193 personas), que encontraron niveles más bajos de omega-3 en personas autistas, y de 4 ensayos con placebo (107 participantes), con pequeñas mejoras en interacción social e intereses repetitivos. Límites: muy pocos participantes, ensayos cortos y resultados muy variables entre estudios; no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are wondering about omega-3 supplements, this review gives no firm answer. Before trying anything, talk it through with your health team. Meanwhile, a varied diet that includes fish or other omega-3 sources, adapted to your family member's sensory preferences, is a calm step. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 15 case-control studies (1,193 people), which found lower omega-3 levels in autistic people, and of 4 placebo-controlled trials (107 participants), showing small improvements in social interaction and repetitive interests. Limits: very few participants, short trials and highly varied results between studies; it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på omega-3-tillskott ger den här översikten inget säkert svar. Prata med vårdteamet innan du provar något. Under tiden är en varierad kost med fisk eller andra omega-3-källor, anpassad efter din närståendes sensoriska preferenser, ett lugnt steg. Evidens: en metaanalys av 15 fall-kontrollstudier (1 193 personer), som visade lägre omega-3-nivåer hos autistiska personer, och av 4 placebokontrollerade studier (107 deltagare) med små förbättringar i socialt samspel och repetitiva intressen. Begränsningar: mycket få deltagare, korta studier och stor variation mellan studierna; resultaten är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Environmental risk factors for autism: an evidence-based review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
authors: Modabbernia A, Velthorst E, Reichenberg A
abstract: Background According to recent evidence, up to 40-50% of variance in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) liability might be determined by environmental factors. In the present paper, we conducted a review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of environmental risk factors for ASD. We assessed each review for quality of evidence and provided a brief overview of putative mechanisms of environmental risk factors for ASD. Findings Current evidence suggests that several environmental factors including vaccination, maternal smoking, thimerosal exposure, and most likely assisted reproductive technologies are unrelated to risk of ASD. On the contrary, advanced parental age is associated with higher risk of ASD. Birth complications that are associated with trauma or ischemia and hypoxia have also shown strong links to ASD, whereas other pregnancy-related factors such as maternal obesity, maternal diabetes, and caesarian section have shown a less strong (but significant) association with risk of ASD. The reviews on nutritional elements have been inconclusive about the detrimental effects of deficiency in folic acid and omega 3, but vitamin D seems to be deficient in patients with ASD. The studies on toxic elements have been largely limited by their design, but there is enough evidence for the association between some heavy metals (most important inorganic mercury and lead) and ASD that warrants further investigation. Mechanisms of the association between environmental factors and ASD are debated but might include non-causative association (including confounding), gene-related effect, oxidative stress, inflammation, hypoxia/ischemia, endocrine disruption, neurotransmitter alterations, and interference with signaling pathways. Conclusions Compared to genetic studies of ASD, studies of environmental risk factors are in their infancy and have significant methodological limitations. Future studies of ASD risk factors would benefit from a developmental psychopathology approach, prospective design, precise exposure measurement, reliable timing of exposure in relation to critical developmental periods and should take into account the dynamic interplay between gene and environment by using genetically informed designs.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si algo que hiciste causó el autismo de tu hijo o hija, esta revisión ofrece calma: las vacunas, el timerosal y fumar en el embarazo no se asocian con el autismo. Algunos factores, como la edad avanzada de los padres o complicaciones en el parto, muestran asociaciones, pero asociación no significa culpa ni causa directa. Puedes soltar la culpa y centrar tu energía en apoyar a tu hijo tal como es hoy. Es una revisión de revisiones sistemáticas y metaanálisis que evaluó la calidad de la evidencia sobre factores ambientales. Sus límites: muchos estudios incluidos tienen diseños débiles y no pueden demostrar causa ni aplicarse a cada familia.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether something you did caused your child's autism, this review offers calm: vaccines, thimerosal and smoking during pregnancy are not linked to autism. Some factors, such as older parental age or birth complications, show associations, but association does not mean blame or direct cause. You can let go of guilt and put your energy into supporting your child as they are today. This is a review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses that rated the quality of evidence on environmental factors. Its limits: many included studies had weak designs, cannot prove cause, and do not apply to every family.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om något du gjorde orsakade ditt barns autism ger denna översikt lugn: vaccin, timerosal och rökning under graviditeten har inget samband med autism. Vissa faktorer, som högre ålder hos föräldrar eller förlossningskomplikationer, visar samband, men samband betyder inte skuld eller direkt orsak. Du kan släppa skulden och lägga din energi på att stötta ditt barn som det är i dag. Detta är en översikt av systematiska översikter och metaanalyser som bedömde evidensens kvalitet om miljöfaktorer.
