This framework postulates that an increase in the proliferation of neural progenitor cells and hyper-expansion of cortical surface area in the first year, occurring during a pre-symptomatic period characterized by disrupted sensorimotor and attentional experience, leads to altered experience-dependent neuronal development and decreased elimination of neuronal processes. This process is linked to brain volume overgrowth and disruption of the refinement of neural circuit connections and is associated with the emergence of autistic social deficits in the second year of life. A better understanding of the timing of developmental brain and behavior mechanisms in autism during infancy, a period which precedes the emergence of the defining features of this disorder, will likely have important implications for designing rational approaches to early intervention.

sheet.es: Si tienes un bebé con un hermano o hermana autista, puedes observar con calma cómo explora, se mueve y presta atención durante el primer y segundo año, y compartir lo que notes con el equipo de salud infantil. Los rasgos autistas suelen hacerse visibles entre el final del primer año y el segundo, no antes, así que no hace falta buscar señales en cada gesto. Esta es una revisión que reúne estudios de imagen cerebral en bebés hermanos de niños autistas, datos genéticos y modelos animales. Sus límites: propone un marco teórico, no una prueba diagnóstica, y no describe a cada niño ni indica qué apoyo concreto funciona.
sheet.en: If you have a baby whose older sibling is autistic, you can calmly notice how they explore, move and pay attention across the first two years, and share what you see with your child health team. Autistic traits usually become visible from late in the first year into the second, not earlier, so there is no need to search every gesture for signs. This is a review bringing together brain-imaging studies of infant siblings of autistic children, genetic findings and animal research. Its limits: it proposes a theoretical framework, not a diagnostic test, and it does not describe every child or say which specific support works.
sheet.sv: Om du har en bebis vars äldre syskon är autistiskt kan du i lugn och ro lägga märke till hur barnet utforskar, rör sig och riktar uppmärksamhet under de första två åren, och berätta vad du ser för barnhälsovården. Autistiska drag blir oftast synliga från slutet av första året och under andra året, inte tidigare, så du behöver inte leta tecken i varje gest. Detta är en översikt som samlar hjärnavbildningsstudier av småsyskon till autistiska barn, genetiska fynd och djurforskning. Begränsningar: den föreslår en teoretisk modell, inte ett diagnostiskt test, och beskriver inte varje barn eller vilket konkret stöd som fungerar.

title: Supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids may improve hyperactivity, lethargy, and stereotypy in children with autism spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authors: Cheng YS, Tseng PT, Chen YW, Stubbs B, Yang WC, Yang WC, Chen TY, Wu CK, Lin PY
abstract: Aim Deficiency of omega 3 fatty acids may be linked to autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Evidence about the potential therapeutic effects of supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids is lacking in ASD patients. Methods We searched major electronic databases from inception to June 21, 2017, for randomized clinical trials, which compared treatment outcomes between supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids and placebo in patients with ASD. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of the included studies was undertaken. Results and conclusion Six trials were included (n=194). Meta-analysis showed that supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids improved hyperactivity (difference in means =-2.692, 95% confidence interval [CI] =-5.364 to -0.020, P =0.048, studies =4, n=109), lethargy (difference in means =-1.969, 95% CI =-3.566 to -0.372, P =0.016, studies =4, n=109), and stereotypy (difference in means =-1.071, 95% CI =-2.114 to -0.029, P =0.044, studies =4, n=109). No significant differences emerged between supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids and placebo in global assessment of functioning (n=169) or social responsiveness (n=97). Our preliminary meta-analysis suggests that supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids may improve hyperactivity, lethargy, and stereotypy in ASD patients. However, the number of studies was limited and the overall effects were small, precluding definitive conclusions. Future large-scale randomized clinical trials are needed to confirm or refute our findings.

sheet.es: Si piensas en dar omega 3 a tu hijo o hija autista, consúltalo primero con su pediatra: puede ser seguro para algunas familias, pero no esperes grandes cambios. Observa y anota cómo está tu hijo antes y después, sin dejar los apoyos que ya funcionan. El 'stimming' (movimientos repetitivos) suele cumplir una función y no hace falta eliminarlo. Este metaanálisis reunió seis ensayos aleatorizados con 194 niños autistas y encontró pequeñas mejoras en hiperactividad, letargo y movimientos repetitivos, pero no en el funcionamiento general ni en la respuesta social. Sus límites: pocos estudios, muestras pequeñas y efectos débiles; no sirve como regla para todos.
sheet.en: If you are considering omega-3 for your autistic child, talk with their doctor first: it may be safe for some families, but don't expect big changes. Note how your child is doing before and after, and keep the supports that already help. Stimming often serves a purpose and doesn't need to be removed. This meta-analysis pooled six randomized controlled trials with 194 autistic children and found small improvements in hyperactivity, lethargy and repetitive movements, but none in overall functioning or social responsiveness. Its limits: few studies, small samples and weak effects, so it is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på omega-3 till ditt autistiska barn, prata först med barnets läkare: det kan vara säkert för vissa familjer, men förvänta dig inga stora förändringar. Anteckna hur barnet mår före och efter, och behåll det stöd som redan fungerar. Stimming fyller ofta en funktion och behöver inte tas bort. Denna metaanalys samlade sex randomiserade kontrollerade studier med 194 autistiska barn och fann små förbättringar i hyperaktivitet, slöhet och repetitiva rörelser, men inga i övergripande funktion eller social lyhördhet. Begränsningar: få studier, små grupper och svaga effekter, så resultatet gäller inte alla barn.

title: Comparative safety of antiepileptic drugs for neurological development in children exposed during pregnancy and breast feeding: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
authors: Veroniki AA, Rios P, Cogo E, Straus SE, Finkelstein Y, Kealey R, Reynen E, Soobiah C, Thavorn K, Hutton B, Hemmelgarn BR, Yazdi F, D'Souza J, MacDonald H, Tricco AC
abstract: Objectives Compare the safety of antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) on neurodevelopment of infants/children exposed in utero or during breast feeding. Design and setting Systematic review and Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA). MEDLINE, EMBASE and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched until 27 April 2017. Screening, data abstraction and quality appraisal were completed in duplicate by independent reviewers. Participants 29 cohort studies including 5100 infants/children. Interventions Monotherapy and polytherapy AEDs including first-generation (carbamazepine, clobazam, clonazepam, ethosuximide, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, valproate) and newer-generation (gabapentin, lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, vigabatrin) AEDs. Epileptic women who did not receive AEDs during pregnancy or breast feeding served as the control group. Primary and secondary outcome measures Cognitive developmental delay and autism/dyspraxia were primary outcomes. Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, language delay, neonatal seizures, psychomotor developmental delay and social impairment were secondary outcomes. Results The NMA on cognitive developmental delay (11 cohort studies, 933 children, 18 treatments) suggested that among all AEDs only valproate was statistically significantly associated with more children experiencing cognitive developmental delay compared with control (OR=7.40, 95% credible interval (CrI) 3.00 to 18.46). The NMA on autism (5 cohort studies, 2551 children, 12 treatments) suggested that oxcarbazepine (OR 13.51, CrI 1.28 to 221.40), valproate (OR 17.29, 95% CrI 2.40 to 217.60), lamotrigine (OR 8.88, CrI 1.28 to 112.00) and lamotrigine+valproate (OR 132.70, CrI 7.41 to 3851.00) were associated with significantly greater odds of developing autism compared with control. The NMA on psychomotor developmental delay (11 cohort studies, 1145 children, 18 treatments) found that valproate (OR 4.16, CrI 2.04 to 8.75) and carbamazepine+phenobarbital+valproate (OR 19.12, CrI 1.49 to 337.50) were associated with significantly greater odds of psychomotor delay compared with control. Conclusions Valproate alone or combined with another AED is associated with the greatest odds of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes compared with control. Oxcarbazepine and lamotrigine were associated with increased occurrence of autism. Counselling is advised for women considering pregnancy to tailor the safest regimen. Trial registration number PROSPERO database (CRD42014008925).

sheet.es: Si tomas medicación para la epilepsia y estás pensando en un embarazo o en amamantar, lo práctico es pedir una consulta con tu neuróloga o neurólogo antes de cambiar nada: nunca suspendas ni ajustes la medicación por tu cuenta, porque las crisis también tienen riesgos. Lleva preguntas sobre qué tratamiento es más seguro para ti. Este metaanálisis reunió 29 estudios de cohortes con unos 5100 niños y niñas expuestos durante el embarazo o la lactancia; el valproato se asoció con más diferencias en el desarrollo, y algunos otros fármacos con más diagnósticos de autismo. Sus límites: estudios observacionales, a veces pequeños, con intervalos muy amplios; muestra asociaciones, no causas, ni predice lo que ocurrirá en cada familia.
sheet.en: If you take epilepsy medication and are considering pregnancy or breastfeeding, the practical step is to book a conversation with your neurologist before changing anything: never stop or adjust medication on your own, because seizures carry risks too. Bring questions about which treatment is safest for you. This meta-analysis pooled 29 cohort studies with about 5,100 children exposed during pregnancy or breastfeeding; valproate was linked to more developmental differences, and some other drugs to more autism diagnoses. Its limits: observational studies, some small, with very wide uncertainty ranges; it shows associations, not causes, and cannot predict what will happen in any one family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar epilepsimedicin och funderar på graviditet eller amning är det praktiska steget att boka ett samtal med din neurolog innan du ändrar något: sluta eller justera aldrig medicinen på egen hand, eftersom anfall också innebär risker. Ta med frågor om vilken behandling som är säkrast för dig. Denna metaanalys samlade 29 kohortstudier med cirka 5 100 barn som exponerats under graviditet eller amning; valproat var kopplat till fler utvecklingsskillnader och vissa andra läkemedel till fler autismdiagnoser. Begränsningar: observationsstudier, ibland små, med mycket breda osäkerhetsintervall; den visar samband, inte orsaker, och kan inte förutsäga vad som händer i en enskild familj.

title: Fundamental Elements in Autism: From Neurogenesis and Neurite Growth to Synaptic Plasticity.
authors: Gilbert J, Man HY
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a set of neurodevelopmental disorders with a high prevalence and impact on society. ASDs are characterized by deficits in both social behavior and cognitive function. There is a strong genetic basis underlying ASDs that is highly heterogeneous; however, multiple studies have highlighted the involvement of key processes, including neurogenesis, neurite growth, synaptogenesis and synaptic plasticity in the pathophysiology of neurodevelopmental disorders. In this review article, we focus on the major genes and signaling pathways implicated in ASD and discuss the cellular, molecular and functional studies that have shed light on common dysregulated pathways using in vitro , in vivo and human evidence. Highlights Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has a prevalence of 1 in 68 children in the United States.ASDs are highly heterogeneous in their genetic basis.ASDs share common features at the cellular and molecular levels in the brain.Most ASD genes are implicated in neurogenesis, structural maturation, synaptogenesis and function.

sheet.es: Para mañana: este estudio no cambia nada de lo que hagas en casa. Explica que el autismo tiene una base biológica y genética en cómo se forman y conectan las neuronas, no es fruto de la crianza ni de algo que hiciste mal. Puedes seguir apoyando a tu hijo o hija según sus necesidades, ritmos y fortalezas concretas. Se trata de una revisión de 2017 que resume estudios en células, animales y personas sobre genes y vías cerebrales relacionadas con el autismo. Su límite: es investigación básica, describe la biología con lenguaje de déficit y no ofrece pruebas, tratamientos ni pautas prácticas para ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: this study doesn't change anything you do at home. It explains that autism has a biological and genetic basis in how brain cells grow and connect, so it is not caused by parenting or something you did wrong. You can keep supporting your child according to their own needs, pace and strengths. This is a 2017 review summarising cell, animal and human studies on genes and brain pathways linked to autism. Its limit: it is basic research, describes biology in deficit language, and offers no tests, treatments or practical guidance for any individual person.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon: den här studien ändrar inget i det du gör hemma. Den förklarar att autism har en biologisk och genetisk grund i hur hjärnceller växer och kopplas samman, så den beror inte på uppfostran eller något du gjort fel. Du kan fortsätta stötta ditt barn utifrån hens egna behov, tempo och styrkor. Det är en översikt från 2017 som sammanfattar studier på celler, djur och människor om gener och signalvägar kopplade till autism. Begränsning: det är grundforskning, den beskriver biologin med bristspråk och ger inga tester, behandlingar eller praktiska råd för en enskild person.

title: Epilepsy in patients with autism: links, risks and treatment challenges.
authors: Besag FM
abstract: Autism is more common in people with epilepsy, approximately 20%, and epilepsy is more common in people with autism with reported rates of approximately 20%. However, these figures are likely to be affected by the current broader criteria for autism spectrum disorder (ASD), which have contributed to an increased prevalence of autism, with the result that the rate for ASD in epilepsy is likely to be higher and the figure for epilepsy in ASD is likely to be lower. Some evidence suggests that there are two peaks of epilepsy onset in autism, in infancy and adolescence. The rate of autism in epilepsy is much higher in those with intellectual disability. In conditions such as the Landau-Kleffner syndrome and nonconvulsive status epilepticus, the epilepsy itself may present with autistic features. There is no plausible mechanism for autism causing epilepsy, however. The co-occurrence of autism and epilepsy is almost certainly the result of underlying factors predisposing to both conditions, including both genetic and environmental factors. Conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, anxiety and sleep disorders are common in both epilepsy and autism. Epilepsy is generally not a contraindication to treating these conditions with suitable medication, but it is important to take account of relevant drug interactions. One of the greatest challenges in autism is to determine why early childhood regression occurs in perhaps 25%. Further research should focus on finding the cause for such regression. Whether epilepsy plays a role in the regression of a subgroup of children with autism who lose skills remains to be determined.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, conviene conocer los signos de epilepsia: ausencias, miradas fijas, sacudidas o pérdida repentina de habilidades. Anota cuándo ocurren y coméntalo con su equipo médico, sobre todo en la primera infancia y la adolescencia, cuando la epilepsia parece aparecer con más frecuencia. Si toma medicación para el sueño, la ansiedad o el TDAH, pregunta por posibles interacciones. Esta revisión resume estudios previos: cerca de un 20 % de personas autistas tienen epilepsia, más a menudo si hay discapacidad intelectual. Sus límites: las cifras varían según los criterios diagnósticos y no aporta datos nuevos ni aclara si la epilepsia influye en la regresión.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it helps to know possible signs of epilepsy: absence moments, staring spells, jerking movements or a sudden loss of skills. Note when they happen and share this with their healthcare team, especially in early childhood and adolescence, when epilepsy seems to start more often. If they take medication for sleep, anxiety or ADHD, ask about possible interactions. This review summarises earlier research: around 20% of autistic people have epilepsy, more often when intellectual disability is present. Its limits: figures shift with changing diagnostic criteria, it adds no new data, and it cannot say whether epilepsy plays a role in skill regression.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är det bra att känna till möjliga tecken på epilepsi: frånvaroattacker, stirrande, ryckningar eller att förmågor plötsligt försvinner. Anteckna när det händer och berätta för vårdteamet, särskilt under tidig barndom och tonår, då epilepsi verkar debutera oftare. Om personen tar läkemedel för sömn, ångest eller ADHD, fråga om möjliga interaktioner. Denna översikt sammanfattar tidigare forskning: ungefär 20 % av autistiska personer har epilepsi, oftare vid intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Begränsningar: siffrorna påverkas av ändrade diagnoskriterier, översikten ger inga nya data och kan inte avgöra om epilepsi bidrar till förlust av förmågor.

title: Antidepressant use during pregnancy and risk of autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: systematic review of observational studies and methodological considerations.
authors: Morales DR, Slattery J, Evans S, Kurz X
abstract: Background Antidepressant exposure during pregnancy has been associated with an increased risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in several observational studies. We performed a systematic review of these studies to highlight the effect that important methodological limitations have on such analyses and to consider approaches to the conduct, reporting and interpretation of future studies. Methods A review of MEDLINE and EMBASE identified case-control, cohort and sibling studies assessing the risk of ASD and ADHD with antidepressant use during pregnancy. Approaches to confounding adjustment were described. Crude and adjusted effect estimates for comparisons between antidepressant exposure during pregnancy vs. all unexposed women were first meta-analysed using a generic inverse variance method of analysis, followed by effect estimates for alternative pre-selected comparison groups. Results A total of 15 studies measuring ASD as an outcome (involving 3,585,686 children and 40,585 cases) and seven studies measuring ADHD as an outcome (involving 2,765,723 patients and 52,313 cases) were identified. Variation in confounding adjustment existed between studies. Updated effect estimates for the association between maternal antidepressant exposure during pregnancy vs. all unexposed women remained statistically significant for ASD (adjusted random-effects risk ratio [RaRR] 1.53, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.31-1.78). Similar significant associations were observed using pre-pregnancy maternal antidepressant exposure (RaRR 1.48, 95% CI 1.29-1.71) and paternal antidepressant exposure during pregnancy (1.29, 95% CI 1.08-1.53), but analyses restricted to using women with a history of affective disorder (1.18, 95% CI 0.91-1.52) and sibling studies (0.96, 95% CI 0.65-1.42) were not statistically significant. Corresponding associations for risk of ADHD with exposure were: RaRR 1.38, 95% CI 1.13-1.69 (during pregnancy), RaRR 1.38, 95% CI 1.14-1.69 (during pre-pregnancy), RaRR 1.71, 95% CI 1.31-2.23 (paternal exposure), RaRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.77-1.24 (women with a history of affective disorder) and RaRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.70-1.11 (sibling studies). Conclusions Existing observational studies measuring the risk of ASD and ADHD with antidepressant exposure are heterogeneous in their design. Classical comparisons between exposed and unexposed women during pregnancy are at high risk of residual confounding. Alternative comparisons and sibling designs may aid the interpretation of causality and their utility requires further evaluation, including understanding potential limitations of undertaking meta-analyses with such data.

sheet.es: Si tomaste antidepresivos durante el embarazo y tu hijo o hija es autista, esta revisión ofrece un mensaje tranquilizador: el vínculo observado parece explicarse sobre todo por otros factores, como la genética familiar o la propia depresión, y no por el medicamento. Cuando se comparó entre hermanos o con madres que también tenían depresión, la asociación desapareció; incluso aparecía cuando quien tomaba antidepresivos era el padre. Es un metaanálisis de 15 estudios observacionales con más de 3,5 millones de niños y niñas. Sus límites: los estudios eran muy diferentes entre sí y no pueden probar causa. Cualquier decisión sobre tratamiento se habla con tu equipo de salud.
sheet.en: If you took antidepressants during pregnancy and your child is autistic, this review offers a reassuring message: the link seen in earlier studies seems to be explained mostly by other factors, such as family genetics or depression itself, rather than the medication. When siblings were compared, or mothers who also had depression, the association disappeared; it even appeared when the father took antidepressants. This is a meta-analysis of 15 observational studies including over 3.5 million children. Its limits: the studies differed a lot in design and cannot prove cause. Any treatment decision belongs in a conversation with your healthcare team.
sheet.sv: Om du tog antidepressiva under graviditeten och ditt barn är autistiskt ger den här översikten ett lugnande budskap: sambandet i tidigare studier verkar främst förklaras av andra faktorer, som ärftlighet i familjen eller depressionen i sig, snarare än läkemedlet. När syskon jämfördes, eller mammor som också hade depression, försvann sambandet; det syntes till och med när pappan tog antidepressiva. Det är en metaanalys av 15 observationsstudier med över 3,5 miljoner barn. Begränsningar: studierna var mycket olika i upplägg och kan inte bevisa orsak. Beslut om behandling tas tillsammans med din vårdkontakt.

title: Experiences of Autism Acceptance and Mental Health in Autistic Adults.
authors: Cage E, Di Monaco J, Newell V
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Mental health difficulties are highly prevalent in individuals on the autism spectrum. The current study examined how experiences and perceptions of autism acceptance could impact on the mental health of autistic adults. 111 adults on the autism spectrum completed an online survey examining their experiences of autism acceptance, along with symptoms of depression, anxiety and stress. Regression analyses showed that autism acceptance from external sources and personal acceptance significantly predicted depression. Acceptance from others also significantly predicted stress but acceptance did not predict anxiety. Further analyses suggested that experiences of "camouflaging" could relate to higher rates of depression. The current study highlights the importance of considering how autism acceptance could contribute to mental health in autism.

sheet.es: Mostrar aceptación real del autismo de una persona puede proteger su bienestar. Mañana podrías nombrar el autismo con naturalidad, valorar sus formas de comunicarse y reducir la presión para «parecer» no autista: menos camuflaje puede significar menos agotamiento. Pregúntale qué le ayuda a sentirse aceptado o aceptada. En este estudio, 111 adultos autistas respondieron una encuesta en línea; quienes sentían más aceptación de otras personas y de sí mismos tenían menos depresión, y la aceptación externa se relacionó con menos estrés, no con la ansiedad. Límites: es una encuesta en un solo momento, muestra pequeña y autoinformada; muestra asociaciones, no causas, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: Showing genuine acceptance of a person's autism may support their wellbeing. Tomorrow you could talk about autism openly and positively, respect how they communicate, and ease pressure to 'pass' as non-autistic: less camouflaging may mean less exhaustion. Ask them what helps them feel accepted. In this study, 111 autistic adults completed an online survey; those who felt more accepted by others and by themselves reported less depression, and acceptance from others was linked to less stress, though not to anxiety. Limits: it was a one-time, self-reported survey with a small sample, so it shows associations rather than causes, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Att visa verklig acceptans för en persons autism kan stödja hens välmående. I morgon kan du prata öppet och positivt om autism, respektera hur personen kommunicerar och minska trycket att verka icke-autistisk: mindre kamouflering kan betyda mindre utmattning. Fråga vad som får hen att känna sig accepterad. I studien svarade 111 autistiska vuxna på en webbenkät; de som kände mer acceptans från andra och från sig själva rapporterade mindre depression, och acceptans från andra hängde ihop med mindre stress, men inte med ångest. Begränsningar: en enda självrapporterad enkät med litet urval visar samband, inte orsaker, och varje person är olik.

title: Understanding, Recognising and Treating Co-occurring Anxiety in Autism.
authors: Rodgers J, Ofield A
abstract: Purpose of review Autistic people are at increased risk of anxiety, with around 50% of autistic adults and children experiencing this debilitating mental health condition. The purpose of this review is to consider some contemporary ideas about underlying mechanisms for anxiety in autism, explore issues in the identification and assessment of anxiety and discuss emerging trends in anxiety interventions for autistic people, before identifying some important next steps in the field. Recent findings Emerging evidence suggests that anxiety may present differently in autism compared to the general population and that whilst CBT holds promise, there may be important differences in neurobiological, affective and cognitive responses to stressors for autistic people, which warrant tailored anxiety models, assessments and interventions. Summary We conclude that research is needed to develop and evaluate theoretical frameworks, assessment methods and interventions for anxiety in autism, particularly for autistic adults and those with co-occurring intellectual disability.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas parece más tensa, irritable, se aferra más a rutinas o se retira, considera que podría ser ansiedad: en el autismo puede verse distinta a lo habitual. Observa qué situaciones la desencadenan, pregúntale de forma adaptada a su comunicación y busca profesionales que ajusten la evaluación y el apoyo, por ejemplo una terapia cognitivo-conductual adaptada. Se trata de una revisión de investigaciones con niños y adultos autistas, que indica que cerca de la mitad vive con ansiedad. Su límite: resume ideas emergentes, no prueba un método concreto, y hay poca evidencia sobre adultos y personas con discapacidad intelectual.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support seems more tense, irritable, more attached to routines or withdrawn, consider that it might be anxiety: in autism it can look different from what people usually expect. Notice which situations trigger it, ask in a way that fits their communication, and look for professionals who adapt assessment and support, such as tailored cognitive behavioural therapy. This is a review of research with autistic children and adults, suggesting about half experience anxiety. Its limit: it summarises emerging ideas rather than testing a specific method, and evidence on autistic adults and people with intellectual disability is still scarce.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar verkar mer spänd, irriterad, håller hårdare fast vid rutiner eller drar sig undan, kan det vara ångest: vid autism kan den se annorlunda ut än man brukar förvänta sig. Lägg märke till vilka situationer som utlöser den, fråga på ett sätt som passar personens kommunikation och sök professionella som anpassar bedömning och stöd, till exempel anpassad kognitiv beteendeterapi. Detta är en översikt av forskning med autistiska barn och vuxna, som tyder på att ungefär hälften har ångest. Begränsning: den sammanfattar nya idéer snarare än att pröva en metod, och kunskapen om vuxna och personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning är fortfarande liten.

title: Mental Health Interventions for Parent Carers of Children with Autistic Spectrum Disorder: Practice Guidelines from a Critical Interpretive Synthesis (CIS) Systematic Review.
authors: Catalano D, Holloway L, Mpofu E
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Parent carers of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often report increased levels of stress, depression, and anxiety. Unmet parent carer mental health needs pose a significant risk to the psychological, physical, and social well-being of the parents of the child affected by ASD and jeopardize the adaptive functioning of the family as well as the potential of the child affected by ASD. This systematic review identifies key qualities of interventions supporting the mental health of parent carers and proposes practitioner-parent carer support guidelines. A search of four databases (Medline, PubMed, PsycINFO, and Social Science Data) was conducted to identify studies that met the following criteria: (1) an intervention was delivered to parent carers of a child with ASD under the age of 18 years; (2) the research design allowed for a comparison on outcomes across groups; and (3) outcome measures of the parent carers' mental health were used. A total of 23 studies met the inclusion criteria. A critical interpretive synthesis approach was used to produce an integrated conceptualization of the evidence. Findings suggest practitioner guidelines to support the mental health and wellbeing of parent carers should include addressing the parent's self-perspective taking and skill for real time problem-solving.

sheet.es: Cuidar tu propia salud mental no es un lujo: también sostiene a tu familia. Si buscas apoyo, puede ayudarte elegir programas que te enseñen a mirar tus propios pensamientos y emociones con más amabilidad y a resolver problemas en el momento, en situaciones reales del día a día. Pedir ayuda para ti es legítimo. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 23 estudios con grupos de comparación sobre intervenciones para madres y padres de niños y niñas autistas menores de 18 años, y propone pautas para profesionales. Sus límites: los estudios eran variados, el método es interpretativo y no indica qué programa concreto funciona mejor para cada familia.
sheet.en: Looking after your own mental health is not a luxury: it also supports your whole family. If you look for support, it may help to choose programmes that teach you to notice your own thoughts and feelings with more kindness and to solve problems in the moment, in real everyday situations. Asking for help for yourself is legitimate. This systematic review looked at 23 studies with comparison groups on interventions for parents of autistic children under 18, and proposes guidelines for practitioners. Its limits: the studies varied widely, the method is interpretive, and it does not show which specific programme works best for each family.
sheet.sv: Att ta hand om din egen psykiska hälsa är ingen lyx: det stöttar också hela familjen. Om du söker stöd kan det hjälpa att välja program som lär dig att se dina egna tankar och känslor med mer vänlighet och att lösa problem i stunden, i verkliga vardagssituationer. Att be om hjälp för din egen skull är helt rimligt. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 23 studier med jämförelsegrupper om insatser för föräldrar till autistiska barn under 18 år och föreslår riktlinjer för yrkesverksamma. Begränsningar: studierna var mycket olika, metoden är tolkande och den visar inte vilket program som fungerar bäst för varje familj.

title: Parents Suggest Which Indicators of Progress and Outcomes Should be Measured in Young Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: McConachie H, Livingstone N, Morris C, Beresford B, Le Couteur A, Gringras P, Garland D, Jones G, Macdonald G, Williams K, Parr JR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Evaluation of interventions for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is hampered by the multitude of outcomes measured and tools used. Measurement in research with young children tends to focus on core impairments in ASD. We conducted a systematic review of qualitative studies of what matters to parents. Parent advisory groups completed structured activities to explore their perceptions of the relative importance of a wide range of outcome constructs. Their highest ranked outcomes impacted directly on everyday life and functioning (anxiety, distress, hypersensitivity, sleep problems, happiness, relationships with brothers and sisters, and parent stress). Collaboration between professionals, researchers and parents/carers is required to determine an agreed core set of outcomes to use across evaluation research.

sheet.es: Cuando valores si un apoyo funciona para tu hijo o hija, puedes fijarte en lo que cambia el día a día: si duerme mejor, si siente menos ansiedad o malestar, cómo vive las sensibilidades sensoriales, si se le ve feliz, cómo se relaciona con sus hermanos y cuánto estrés hay en casa. Es legítimo pedir a los profesionales que midan también estas cosas. La evidencia procede de una revisión sistemática de estudios cualitativos sobre lo que importa a las familias, junto con grupos asesores de padres y madres de niños pequeños autistas. Sus límites: refleja la visión de los padres, no la de los propios niños autistas, y las prioridades de cada familia pueden ser distintas.
sheet.en: When you judge whether a support is working for your child, you can look at what changes everyday life: better sleep, less anxiety or distress, how sensory sensitivities are going, whether your child seems happy, how they get on with siblings, and how much stress there is at home. It is reasonable to ask professionals to track these things too. The evidence comes from a systematic review of qualitative studies on what matters to families, plus advisory groups of parents of young autistic children. Its limits: it reflects parents' views rather than those of autistic children themselves, and each family's priorities may differ.
sheet.sv: När du bedömer om ett stöd fungerar för ditt barn kan du titta på det som förändrar vardagen: bättre sömn, mindre oro eller stress, hur sensoriska känsligheter fungerar, om barnet verkar glatt, hur relationen till syskonen är och hur mycket stress det finns i familjen. Det är rimligt att be yrkespersoner att följa upp även detta. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av kvalitativa studier om vad som är viktigt för familjer, kompletterad med rådgivande grupper av föräldrar till unga autistiska barn. Begränsningar: den speglar föräldrarnas syn snarare än de autistiska barnens egen, och varje familjs prioriteringar kan skilja sig.

title: Enhancing the Validity of a Quality of Life Measure for Autistic People.
authors: McConachie H, Mason D, Parr JR, Garland D, Wilson C, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Accurate measurement of quality of life (QoL) is important for evaluation of autism services and trials of interventions. We undertook psychometric validation of the World Health Organisation measure-WHOQoL-BREF, examined construct validity of the WHO Disabilities module and developed nine additional autism-specific items (ASQoL) from extensive consultation with the autism community. The sample of 309 autistic people was recruited from the Adult Autism Spectrum Cohort-UK. The WHOQoL-BREF had good psychometric properties, including criterion, convergent, divergent and discriminant validity. The WHO Disabilities module showed adequate construct validity and reliability. The ASQoL items form a unitary factor of QoL, with one global item. Future studies can use the WHO measures alongside the ASQoL items to measure QoL of autistic people.

sheet.es: Si quiere saber cómo le va a una persona autista, pregunte por su calidad de vida desde su propia perspectiva, no solo por sus síntomas o conductas. Este estudio muestra que un cuestionario de la OMS (WHOQoL-BREF) funciona bien con adultos autistas, y añade nueve preguntas creadas junto con la comunidad autista, por ejemplo sobre aspectos sensoriales o de aceptación. Puede usar estas ideas para conversar con calma sobre lo que importa. La evidencia procede de 309 adultos autistas del Reino Unido que respondieron cuestionarios. Sus límites: participaron adultos capaces de responder por escrito, así que puede no reflejar a niños ni a personas que se comunican de otras formas.
sheet.en: If you want to know how an autistic person is doing, ask about their quality of life from their own perspective, not only about traits or behaviour. This study shows that a World Health Organization questionnaire (WHOQoL-BREF) works well with autistic adults, and it adds nine questions developed with the autistic community, covering things like sensory experiences and acceptance. You can use these ideas to start calm conversations about what matters to them. The evidence comes from 309 autistic adults in the UK who completed questionnaires. Its limits: participants were adults able to answer written surveys, so results may not reflect children or people who communicate in other ways.
sheet.sv: Om du vill veta hur en autistisk person mår, fråga om livskvalitet utifrån personens eget perspektiv, inte bara om drag eller beteenden. Studien visar att ett frågeformulär från Världshälsoorganisationen (WHOQoL-BREF) fungerar väl för autistiska vuxna, och lägger till nio frågor som tagits fram tillsammans med den autistiska gemenskapen, till exempel om sinnesintryck och acceptans. Du kan använda idéerna för lugna samtal om det som är viktigt. Underlaget kommer från 309 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien som besvarade enkäter. Begränsningar: deltagarna var vuxna som kunde svara skriftligt, så resultaten speglar kanske inte barn eller personer som kommunicerar på andra sätt.

title: Parenting Stress and Resilience in Parents of Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in Southeast Asia: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ilias K, Cornish K, Kummar AS, Park MS, Golden KJ
abstract: Background: This paper aimed to review the literature on the factors associated with parenting stress and resilience among parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in the South East Asia (SEA) region. Methods: An extensive search of articles in multiple online databases (PsycNET, ProQuest, PudMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Google Scholar) resulted in 28 papers that met the inclusion criteria (i.e., conducted in the SEA region, specific to ASD only, published in a peer-reviewed journal, full text in English). Studies found were conducted in the following countries: Brunei, n = 1; Indonesia, n = 2; Malaysia, n = 12; Philippines, n = 5; Singapore, n = 5, Thailand, n = 2; and Vietnam, n = 1, but none from Cambodia, East Timor, Laos, and Myanmar were identified. Results: Across the studies, six main factors were found to be associated with parenting stress: social support, severity of autism symptoms, financial difficulty, parents' perception and understanding toward ASD, parents' anxiety and worries about their child's future, and religious beliefs. These six factors could also be categorized as either a source of parenting stress or a coping strategy/resilience mechanism that may attenuate parenting stress. Conclusion: The findings suggest that greater support services in Western countries may underlie the cultural differences observed in the SEA region. Limitations in the current review were identified. The limited number of studies yielded from the search suggests a need for expanded research on ASD and parenting stress, coping, and resilience in the SEA region especially in Cambodia, East Timor, Laos, and Myanmar. The identified stress and resilience factors may serve as sociocultural markers for clinicians, psychologists, and other professionals to consider when supporting parents of children with ASD.

sheet.es: Su propio bienestar importa. Mañana puede dar un paso pequeño: pedir ayuda concreta a alguien de confianza, buscar información fiable sobre el autismo o anotar qué le preocupa del futuro para hablarlo con un profesional. En esta revisión, el apoyo social, comprender mejor el autismo y, para algunas familias, la fe se asociaron con menos estrés; las dificultades económicas y la preocupación por el futuro, con más. Es una revisión sistemática de 28 estudios con madres y padres de niños autistas en siete países del Sudeste Asiático. Sus límites: los estudios eran pocos y desiguales (casi la mitad de Malasia), solo en inglés, y muestran asociaciones, no causas; lo que ayuda varía en cada familia.
sheet.en: Your own wellbeing matters. Tomorrow you could take one small step: ask someone you trust for a specific kind of help, look for reliable information about autism, or jot down your worries about the future to discuss with a professional. In this review, social support, understanding autism better and, for some families, faith were linked with lower stress; money difficulties and worry about the future were linked with higher stress. It is a systematic review of 28 studies of parents of autistic children in seven Southeast Asian countries. Limits: studies were few and uneven (nearly half from Malaysia), English-only, and show associations rather than causes; what helps differs between families.
sheet.sv: Ditt eget mående spelar roll. I morgon kan du ta ett litet steg: be någon du litar på om en konkret sorts hjälp, söka pålitlig information om autism eller skriva ner dina oror inför framtiden för att ta upp med en professionell. I denna översikt hängde socialt stöd, bättre förståelse för autism och, för vissa familjer, tro ihop med mindre stress; ekonomiska svårigheter och oro för framtiden hängde ihop med mer stress. Det är en systematisk översikt av 28 studier med föräldrar till autistiska barn i sju länder i Sydostasien. Begränsningar: studierna var få och ojämnt fördelade (nästan hälften från Malaysia), bara på engelska, och visar samband, inte orsaker; vad som hjälper skiljer sig mellan familjer.

title: Self-reported sex differences in high-functioning adults with autism: a meta-analysis.
authors: Moseley RL, Hitchiner R, Kirkby JA
abstract: Background Sex differences in autistic symptomatology are believed to contribute to the mis- and missed diagnosis of many girls and women with an autism spectrum condition (ASC). Whilst recent years have seen the emergence of clinical and empirical reports delineating the profile of young autistic girls, recognition of sex differences in symptomatology in adulthood is far more limited. Methods We chose here to focus on symptomatology as reported using a screening instrument, the Ritvo Autism Asperger Diagnostic Scale-Revised (RAADS-R). In a meta-analysis, we pooled and analysed RAADS-R data from a number of experimental groups. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) searched for the presence of main effects of Sex and Diagnosis and for interactions between these factors in our sample of autistic and non-autistic adults. Results In social relatedness and circumscribed interests, main effects of Diagnosis revealed that as expected, autistic adults reported significantly greater lifetime prevalence of symptoms in these domains; an effect of Sex, in circumscribed interests, also suggested that males generally reported more prevalent symptoms than females. An interaction of Sex and Diagnosis in language symptomatology revealed that a normative sex difference in language difficulties was attenuated in autism. An interaction of Sex and Diagnosis in the sensorimotor domain revealed the opposite picture: a lack of sex differences between typically developing men and women and a greater prevalence of sensorimotor symptoms in autistic women than autistic men. Conclusions We discuss the literature on childhood sex differences in relation to those which emerged in our adult sample. Where childhood sex differences fail to persist in adulthood, several interpretations exist, and we discuss, for example, an inherent sampling bias that may mean that only autistic women most similar to the male presentation are diagnosed. The finding that sensorimotor symptomatology is more highly reported by autistic women is a finding requiring objective confirmation, given its potential importance in diagnosis.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una mujer autista, pregúntale con calma por su experiencia sensorial y motora: sonidos, texturas, luces, equilibrio o coordinación. En este estudio, las mujeres autistas describieron más diferencias sensoriomotoras que los hombres autistas, algo que puede pasar desapercibido y que merece espacio en la vida diaria, por ejemplo con pausas, auriculares o ropa cómoda. Es un metaanálisis que reunió respuestas de adultos autistas y no autistas al cuestionario RAADS-R. Sus límites: los datos son autoinformados, las personas participantes ya tenían diagnóstico (quizá mujeres con perfiles más parecidos a los masculinos) y los resultados necesitan confirmación con medidas objetivas. No describe a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic woman, gently ask about her sensory and motor experiences: sounds, textures, light, balance or coordination. In this study, autistic women reported more sensorimotor differences than autistic men, something that is easy to overlook and worth making room for in daily life, such as breaks, headphones or comfortable clothing. This is a meta-analysis pooling autistic and non-autistic adults' answers to the RAADS-R screening questionnaire. Its limits: the data are self-reported, participants already had diagnoses (possibly favouring women whose profiles resemble men's), and the findings still need objective confirmation. It does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk kvinna, fråga lugnt om hennes sensoriska och motoriska upplevelser: ljud, texturer, ljus, balans eller koordination. I den här studien beskrev autistiska kvinnor fler sensomotoriska skillnader än autistiska män, något som lätt förbises och som förtjänar utrymme i vardagen, till exempel pauser, hörlurar eller bekväma kläder. Det är en metaanalys som slog samman autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxnas svar på screeningformuläret RAADS-R. Begränsningar: svaren är självrapporterade, deltagarna hade redan diagnos (kanske kvinnor med profiler som liknar mäns) och resultaten behöver bekräftas med objektiva mått. Studien beskriver inte alla.

title: Current Enlightenment About Etiology and Pharmacological Treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Eissa N, Al-Houqani M, Sadeq A, Ojha SK, Sasse A, Sadek B
abstract: Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental brain disorder characterized by two core behavioral symptoms, namely impairments in social communication and restricted/repetitive behavior. The molecular mechanisms underlying ASD are not well understood. Recent genetic as well as non-genetic animal models contributed significantly in understanding the pathophysiology of ASD, as they establish autism-like behavior in mice and rats. Among the genetic causes, several chromosomal mutations including duplications or deletions could be possible causative factors of ASD. In addition, the biochemical basis suggests that several brain neurotransmitters, e.g., dopamine (DA), serotonin (5-HT), gamma-amino butyric acid (GABA), acetylcholine (ACh), glutamate (Glu) and histamine (HA) participate in the onset and progression of ASD. Despite of convincible understanding, risperidone and aripiprazole are the only two drugs available clinically for improving behavioral symptoms of ASD following approval by Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Till date, up to our knowledge there is no other drug approved for clinical usage specifically for ASD symptoms. However, many novel drug candidates and classes of compounds are underway for ASD at different phases of preclinical and clinical drug development. In this review, the diversity of numerous aetiological factors and the alterations in variety of neurotransmitter generation, release and function linked to ASD are discussed with focus on drugs currently used to manage neuropsychiatric symptoms related to ASD. The review also highlights the clinical development of drugs with emphasis on their pharmacological targets aiming at improving core symptoms in ASD.

sheet.es: Lo práctico para mañana: ningún medicamento cambia lo que significa ser autista; los fármacos aprobados se usan solo para algunas dificultades concretas, como la irritabilidad intensa. Si te preocupa el malestar de tu hijo o familiar, anota cuándo aparece, qué lo desencadena y qué lo calma, y comparte esas notas con su equipo de salud para decidir juntos. Esta es una revisión narrativa de 2018 que resume investigaciones genéticas, estudios en ratones y ratas, y fármacos en desarrollo; no incluyó participantes propios. Su límite: gran parte se basa en modelos animales y usa un lenguaje centrado en el déficit, por lo que no describe la experiencia real de cada persona autista.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway for tomorrow: no medication changes what it means to be autistic; the approved drugs are used only for some specific difficulties, such as intense irritability. If you are worried about your child's or family member's distress, note when it appears, what triggers it and what soothes it, and share those notes with their health team so you can decide together. This is a 2018 narrative review summarising genetic research, studies in mice and rats, and drugs in development; it had no participants of its own. Its limit: much of it relies on animal models and deficit-focused language, so it does not describe the real experience of each autistic person.
sheet.sv: Praktiskt för i morgon: inget läkemedel förändrar vad det innebär att vara autistisk; de godkända läkemedlen används bara för vissa specifika svårigheter, som intensiv irritabilitet. Om du oroar dig för ditt barns eller din anhörigs mående, anteckna när det uppstår, vad som utlöser det och vad som lugnar, och dela anteckningarna med vårdteamet så att ni kan besluta tillsammans. Detta är en narrativ översikt från 2018 som sammanfattar genetisk forskning, studier på möss och råttor samt läkemedel under utveckling; den hade inga egna deltagare. Begränsning: mycket bygger på djurmodeller och ett bristfokuserat språk, så den beskriver inte varje autistisk persons verkliga upplevelse.

title: The role of oxytocin receptor gene (OXTR) DNA methylation (DNAm) in human social and emotional functioning: a systematic narrative review.
authors: Maud C, Ryan J, McIntosh JE, Olsson CA
abstract: Background The neuropeptide Oxytocin (OXT) plays a central role in birthing, mother-infant bonding and a broad range of related social behaviours in mammals. More recently, interest has extended to epigenetic programming of genes involved in oxytocinergic neurotransmission. This review brings together early findings in a rapidly developing field of research, examining relationships between DNA methylation (DNAm) of the Oxytocin Receptor Gene (OXTR) and social and emotional behaviour in human populations. Method A systematic search across Web of Knowledge/Science, Scopus, Medline and EMBASE captured all published studies prior to June 2017 examining the association between OXTR DNAm and human social and emotional outcomes. Search terms included 'oxytocin gene' or 'oxytocin receptor gene' and 'epigenetics' or 'DNA methylation'. Any article with a focus on social and emotional functioning was then identified from this set by manual review. Results Nineteen studies met eligibility criteria. There was considerable heterogeneity of study populations, tissue samples, instrumentation, measurement, and OXTR site foci. Only three studies examined functional consequences of OXTR DNAm on gene expression and protein synthesis. Increases in OXTR DNAm were associated with callous-unemotional traits in youth, social cognitive deficits in Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD), rigid thinking in anorexia nervosa, affect regulation problems, and problems with facial and emotional recognition. In contrast, reductions in DNAm were associated with perinatal stress, postnatal depression, social anxiety and autism in children. Conclusions Consistent with an emerging field of inquiry, there is not yet sufficient evidence to draw conclusions about the role of OXTR DNAm in human social and emotional behaviour. However, taken together, findings point to increased OXTR DNAm in general impairments in social, cognitive and emotional functioning, and decreased OXTR DNAm in specific patterns of impairment related to mood and anxiety disorders (but not in all). Future progress in this field would be enhanced by adequately powered designs, greater phenotypic precision, and methodological improvements including longitudinal studies with multiple time-points to facilitate causal inference.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en casa: esta investigación no ofrece pruebas ni tratamientos útiles para su familia. Si alguien le ofrece análisis de «metilación del gen de la oxitocina» para explicar la vida social de su hijo o hija, puede responder con calma que la ciencia aún no lo respalda. Lo que sí ayuda es observar cómo se comunica y conecta la persona a su manera, y apoyarla desde ahí. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de 19 estudios con poblaciones muy distintas, solo algunos sobre personas autistas. Sus límites: métodos y muestras muy variados, resultados contradictorios y ningún estudio permite saber qué causa qué.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change at home tomorrow: this research offers no tests or treatments that are useful for your family yet. If someone offers "oxytocin gene methylation" testing to explain your child's social life, you can calmly say the science does not support it. What does help is noticing how your child communicates and connects in their own way, and supporting them from there. This is a systematic review of 19 studies with very different populations, only some involving autistic people. Its limits: methods and samples varied widely, findings pointed in opposite directions, and no study can show what causes what.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras hemma i morgon: den här forskningen erbjuder ännu inga tester eller behandlingar som är till nytta för er familj. Om någon erbjuder analys av ”metylering av oxytocingenen” för att förklara ditt barns sociala liv kan du lugnt säga att forskningen inte stödjer det. Det som hjälper är att se hur barnet kommunicerar och knyter an på sitt eget sätt, och stötta utifrån det. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 19 studier med mycket olika grupper, där bara några gällde autistiska personer. Begränsningar: metoder och urval skilde sig mycket, resultaten pekade åt olika håll och ingen studie kan visa orsak och verkan.

title: Role of mTOR Complexes in Neurogenesis.
authors: LiCausi F, Hartman NW
abstract: Dysregulation of neural stem cells (NSCs) is associated with several neurodevelopmental disorders, including epilepsy and autism spectrum disorder. The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) integrates the intracellular signals to control cell growth, nutrient metabolism, and protein translation. mTOR regulates many functions in the development of the brain, such as proliferation, differentiation, migration, and dendrite formation. In addition, mTOR is important in synaptic formation and plasticity. Abnormalities in mTOR activity is linked with severe deficits in nervous system development, including tumors, autism, and seizures. Dissecting the wide-ranging roles of mTOR activity during critical periods in development will greatly expand our understanding of neurogenesis.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en la rutina diaria: esta revisión trata de biología básica del cerebro, no de apoyos ni tratamientos. Explica que mTOR, una vía de señales dentro de las células, ayuda a guiar cómo crecen y se conectan las neuronas, y que sus alteraciones se han relacionado con el autismo, la epilepsia y algunos tumores. Si tu familia convive con autismo y epilepsia, puede ser útil comentar con el equipo médico si hay preguntas genéticas. Es una revisión narrativa de estudios de laboratorio y con animales, sin participantes humanos. Su límite: no ofrece pruebas sobre qué ayuda a una persona autista concreta ni justifica ningún tratamiento.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change in tomorrow's routine: this review is about basic brain biology, not supports or treatments. It explains that mTOR, a signalling pathway inside cells, helps guide how neurons grow and connect, and that changes in it have been linked to autism, epilepsy and some tumours. If your family lives with both autism and epilepsy, it may be worth raising genetic questions with your medical team. The evidence is a narrative review of laboratory and animal research, with no human participants. Its limit: it says nothing about what helps any particular autistic person and does not justify any treatment.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras i morgondagens rutiner: den här översikten handlar om grundläggande hjärnbiologi, inte om stöd eller behandling. Den förklarar att mTOR, en signalväg inne i cellerna, hjälper till att styra hur nervceller växer och kopplas samman, och att förändringar i den har kopplats till autism, epilepsi och vissa tumörer. Om er familj har erfarenhet av både autism och epilepsi kan det vara värt att ta upp genetiska frågor med vårdteamet. Underlaget är en narrativ översikt av laboratorie- och djurforskning, utan mänskliga deltagare. Begränsningen: den säger inget om vad som hjälper en enskild autistisk person och motiverar ingen behandling.

title: Autism spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis of executive function.
authors: Demetriou EA, Lampit A, Quintana DS, Naismith SL, Song YJC, Pye JE, Hickie I, Guastella AJ
abstract: Evidence of executive dysfunction in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) across development remains mixed and establishing its role is critical for guiding diagnosis and intervention. The primary objectives of this meta-analysis is to analyse executive function (EF) performance in ASD, the fractionation across EF subdomains, the clinical utility of EF measures and the influence of multiple moderators (for example, age, gender, diagnosis, measure characteristics). The Embase, Medline and PsychINFO databases were searched to identify peer-reviewed studies published since the inclusion of Autism in DSM-III (1980) up to end of June 2016 that compared EF in ASD with neurotypical controls. A random-effects model was used and moderators were tested using subgroup analysis. The primary outcome measure was Hedges' g effect size for EF and moderator factors. Clinical sensitivity was determined by the overlap percentage statistic (OL%). Results were reported according to the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. A total of 235 studies comprising 14 081 participants were included (N, ASD=6816, Control=7265). A moderate overall effect size for reduced EF (Hedges' g=0.48, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43-0.53) was found with similar effect sizes across each domain. The majority of moderator comparisons were not significant although the overall effect of executive dysfunction has gradually reduced since the introduction of ASD. Only a small number of EF measures achieved clinical sensitivity. This study confirms a broad executive dysfunction in ASD that is relatively stable across development. The fractionation of executive dysfunction into individual subdomains was not supported, nor was diagnostic sensitivity. Development of feasible EF measures focussing on clinical sensitivity for diagnosis and treatment studies should be a priority.

sheet.es: Muchas personas autistas encuentran más difícil planificar, cambiar de tarea, recordar pasos o frenar un impulso, y esto suele mantenerse a lo largo de la vida. Mañana puede ayudar dar apoyos visuales, dividir tareas en pasos cortos y avisar antes de los cambios, sin interpretarlo como falta de esfuerzo. Este metaanálisis reunió 235 estudios con más de 14 000 participantes (6816 autistas) y encontró una diferencia moderada y amplia en funciones ejecutivas, similar en todas las áreas. Límites: son promedios de grupo con mucha superposición; muchas personas autistas no tienen estas dificultades, y las pruebas no sirven para diagnosticar.
sheet.en: Many autistic people find planning, switching tasks, holding steps in mind or pausing an impulse harder, and this tends to stay fairly steady across life. Tomorrow, visual supports, breaking tasks into short steps and giving warning before changes may help, without reading difficulties as lack of effort. This meta-analysis pooled 235 studies with over 14,000 participants (6,816 autistic) and found a moderate, broad difference in executive functions, similar across all areas. Limits: these are group averages with large overlap; many autistic people do not have these difficulties, and the tests are not useful for diagnosis.
sheet.sv: Många autistiska personer tycker att det är svårare att planera, växla mellan uppgifter, hålla steg i minnet eller hejda en impuls, och det håller ofta i sig genom livet. I morgon kan bildstöd, uppgifter uppdelade i korta steg och förvarning inför förändringar hjälpa, utan att svårigheter tolkas som brist på ansträngning. Denna metaanalys samlade 235 studier med över 14 000 deltagare (6 816 autistiska) och fann en måttlig, bred skillnad i exekutiva funktioner, likartad inom alla områden. Begränsningar: det är gruppgenomsnitt med stor överlappning; många autistiska personer har inte dessa svårigheter, och testerna duger inte för diagnos.

title: Measurement properties of tools used to assess depression in adults with and without autism spectrum conditions: A systematic review.
authors: Cassidy SA, Bradley L, Bowen E, Wigham S, Rodgers J
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Depression is the most commonly experienced mental health condition in adults with autism spectrum conditions (ASC). However, it is unclear what tools are currently being used to assess depression in ASC, or whether tools need to be adapted for this group. This systematic review therefore aimed to identify tools used to assess depression in adults with and without ASC, and then evaluate these tools for their appropriateness and measurement properties. Medline, PsychINFO and Web of Knowledge were searched for studies of depression in: (a) adults with ASC, without co-morbid intellectual disability; and (b) adults from the general population without co-morbid conditions. Articles examining the measurement properties of these tools were then searched for using a methodological filter in PubMed, and the quality of the evidence was evaluated using the COSMIN checklist. Twelve articles were identified which utilized three tools to assess depression in adults with ASC, but only one article which assessed the measurement properties of one of these tools was identified and thus evaluated. Sixty-four articles were identified which utilized five tools to assess depression in general population adults, and fourteen articles had assessed the measurement properties of these tools. Overall, two tools were found to be robust in their measurement properties in the general population-the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II), and the patient health questionnaire (PHQ-9). Crucially only one study was identified from the COSMIN search, which showed weak evidence in support of the measurement properties of the BDI-II in an ASC sample. Implications for effective measurement of depression in ASC are discussed. Autism Res 2018, 11: 738-754. © 2018 The Authors Autism Research published by International Society for Autism Research and Wiley Periodicals, Inc. Lay summary Depression is the most common mental health problem experienced by adults with autism. However, the current study found very limited evidence regarding how useful tools developed for the general population are for adults with autism. We therefore suggest how these tools could be adapted to more effectively assess depression in adults with autism, and improve these individuals access to mental health assessment and support.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta completa un cuestionario de depresión (como el BDI-II o el PHQ-9), tómalo como un punto de partida, no como la última palabra. Algunas preguntas pueden medir rasgos autistas, como el cansancio social o los cambios de rutina, y no tristeza. Puedes ayudar anotando cambios respecto a su forma habitual de ser: sueño, intereses, energía, retirada. Comparte esas observaciones con el profesional y pide que te expliquen los resultados. Evidencia: revisión sistemática de estudios con adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual y adultos de la población general. Límite: solo un estudio evaluó una herramienta en personas autistas, con evidencia débil, así que aún no se sabe qué cuestionario funciona mejor.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult fills in a depression questionnaire (such as the BDI-II or PHQ-9), treat the score as a starting point, not the final word. Some questions may pick up autistic traits, like social tiredness or routine changes, rather than low mood. You can help by noting changes from the person's own usual baseline: sleep, interests, energy, withdrawal. Share these observations with the clinician and ask them to explain the results. Evidence: a systematic review of studies with autistic adults without intellectual disability and general-population adults. Limit: only one study tested a tool in autistic people, with weak evidence, so we do not yet know which questionnaire works best.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen fyller i ett formulär om depression (till exempel BDI-II eller PHQ-9), se resultatet som en utgångspunkt, inte som sista ordet. Vissa frågor kan fånga autistiska drag, som social trötthet eller förändrade rutiner, snarare än nedstämdhet. Du kan hjälpa till genom att notera förändringar jämfört med personens vanliga sätt att vara: sömn, intressen, energi, tillbakadragande. Dela dina iakttagelser med vårdpersonalen och be dem förklara resultaten. Evidens: en systematisk översikt av studier med autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och vuxna i allmänbefolkningen. Begränsning: bara en studie prövade ett verktyg hos autistiska personer, med svagt stöd, så vi vet ännu inte vilket formulär som fungerar bäst.

title: Case-control meta-analysis of blood DNA methylation and autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Andrews SV, Sheppard B, Windham GC, Schieve LA, Schendel DE, Croen LA, Chopra P, Alisch RS, Newschaffer CJ, Warren ST, Feinberg AP, Fallin MD, Ladd-Acosta C
abstract: Background Several reports have suggested a role for epigenetic mechanisms in ASD etiology. Epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may shed light on particular biological mechanisms. However, studies of ASD cases versus controls have been limited by post-mortem timing and severely small sample sizes. Reports from in-life sampling of blood or saliva have also been very limited in sample size and/or genomic coverage. We present the largest case-control EWAS for ASD to date, combining data from population-based case-control and case-sibling pair studies. Methods DNA from 968 blood samples from children in the Study to Explore Early Development (SEED 1) was used to generate epigenome-wide array DNA methylation (DNAm) data at 485,512 CpG sites for 453 cases and 515 controls, using the Illumina 450K Beadchip. The Simons Simplex Collection (SSC) provided 450K array DNAm data on an additional 343 cases and their unaffected siblings. We performed EWAS meta-analysis across results from the two data sets, with adjustment for sex and surrogate variables that reflect major sources of biological variation and technical confounding such as cell type, batch, and ancestry. We compared top EWAS results to those from a previous brain-based analysis. We also tested for enrichment of ASD EWAS CpGs for being targets of meQTL associations using available SNP genotype data in the SEED sample. Findings In this meta-analysis of blood-based DNA from 796 cases and 858 controls, no single CpG met a Bonferroni discovery threshold of p - 7 . Seven CpGs showed differences at p - 5 and 48 at 1 × 10 - 4 . Of the top 7, 5 showed brain-based ASD associations as well, often with larger effect sizes, and the top 48 overall showed modest concordance ( r = 0.31) in direction of effect with cerebellum samples. Finally, we observed suggestive evidence for enrichment of CpG sites controlled by SNPs (meQTL targets) among the EWAS CpG hits, which was consistent across EWAS and meQTL discovery p value thresholds. Conclusions No single CpG site showed a large enough DNAm difference between cases and controls to achieve epigenome-wide significance in this sample size. However, our results suggest the potential to observe disease associations from blood-based samples. Among the seven sites achieving suggestive statistical significance, we observed consistent, and stronger, effects at the same sites among brain samples. Discovery-oriented EWAS for ASD using blood samples will likely need even larger samples and unified genetic data to further understand DNAm differences in ASD.

sheet.es: Para el día a día no cambia nada: hoy no existe un análisis de sangre que muestre el autismo ni que guíe el apoyo a tu hijo o hija, y este estudio lo confirma. Puedes seguir apoyándote en lo que observas: sus necesidades sensoriales, su forma de comunicarse y lo que le da calma. Se trata de un metaanálisis que combinó dos estudios con muestras de sangre de 796 niños autistas y 858 niños no autistas, y buscó marcas químicas en el ADN (metilación). Ningún sitio mostró una diferencia clara; solo hubo señales débiles, algunas parecidas a las halladas en tejido cerebral. Sus límites: los propios autores dicen que harían falta muestras mucho mayores, y los resultados no sirven para diagnosticar ni para predecir nada en una persona concreta.
sheet.en: Nothing changes day to day: there is currently no blood test that shows autism or guides how to support your child, and this study confirms that. You can keep relying on what you observe: their sensory needs, how they communicate, and what helps them feel calm. This was a meta-analysis that combined two studies, using blood samples from 796 autistic and 858 non-autistic children, and it looked for chemical marks on DNA (methylation). No single site showed a clear difference; there were only weak signals, some resembling findings in brain tissue. Its limits: the authors themselves say much larger samples are needed, and the results cannot diagnose or predict anything for an individual person.
sheet.sv: I vardagen förändras ingenting: i dag finns inget blodprov som visar autism eller vägleder stödet till ditt barn, och den här studien bekräftar det. Du kan fortsätta att utgå från det du själv ser: barnets sensoriska behov, hur hen kommunicerar och vad som ger lugn. Det här var en metaanalys som slog samman två studier med blodprover från 796 autistiska och 858 icke-autistiska barn och letade efter kemiska markeringar på DNA (metylering). Ingen enskild plats visade en tydlig skillnad; det fanns bara svaga signaler, varav några liknade fynd i hjärnvävnad. Begränsningar: forskarna skriver själva att det behövs betydligt större urval, och resultaten kan inte användas för att diagnostisera eller förutsäga något hos en enskild person.

title: Inflammation and Neuro-Immune Dysregulations in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Siniscalco D, Schultz S, Brigida AL, Antonucci N
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and interaction and restricted-repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities. Strong inflammation states are associated with ASD. This inflammatory condition is often linked to immune system dysfunction. Several cell types are enrolled to trigger and sustain these processes. Neuro-inflammation and neuro-immune abnormalities have now been established in ASD as key factors in its development and maintenance. In this review, we will explore inflammatory conditions, dysfunctions in neuro-immune cross-talk, and immune system treatments in ASD management.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: si tu hijo o hija autista parece tener molestias físicas frecuentes (dolor, problemas digestivos, alergias, infecciones repetidas), vale la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su médico; el bienestar físico puede influir en el sueño, la energía y el ánimo. No hace falta cambiar nada solo por este artículo. Se trata de una revisión de 2018 que resume estudios previos sobre inflamación y sistema inmunitario en personas autistas. Sus límites: no es un estudio nuevo con participantes, mezcla investigaciones muy distintas, no demuestra causa y efecto ni que estos hallazgos se apliquen a cada persona, y los tratamientos inmunológicos que menciona siguen siendo experimentales.
sheet.en: The practical takeaway: if your autistic child seems to have frequent physical discomfort (pain, gut problems, allergies, repeated infections), it is worth keeping simple notes and sharing them with their doctor; physical wellbeing can affect sleep, energy and mood. Nothing needs to change based on this paper alone. This is a 2018 review summarising earlier studies on inflammation and the immune system in autistic people. Its limits: it is not a new study with participants, it pools very different research, it does not prove cause and effect or that the findings apply to every person, and the immune-based treatments it discusses remain experimental.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: om ditt autistiska barn verkar ha ofta återkommande kroppsliga besvär (smärta, magproblem, allergier, upprepade infektioner) kan det vara värt att föra enkla anteckningar och ta upp dem med läkaren; kroppsligt välmående kan påverka sömn, ork och humör. Inget behöver ändras enbart utifrån den här artikeln. Det är en översikt från 2018 som sammanfattar tidigare studier om inflammation och immunsystemet hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: det är ingen ny studie med deltagare, den väger samman mycket olika forskning, visar inte orsakssamband eller att fynden gäller varje person, och de immunbaserade behandlingar som nämns är fortfarande experimentella.

title: Towards a Treatment for Intolerance of Uncertainty for Autistic Adults: A Single Case Experimental Design Study.
authors: Rodgers J, Herrema R, Honey E, Freeston M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) is indicated as an important transdiagnostic process variable in a range of anxiety disorders. Anxiety is very common in autistic adults. This study evaluates a manualised treatment programme for autistic adults, which focused on IU. An eight session programme (CUES-A©) was developed and delivered to four autistic adults on an individual basis. A single case experimental design was used to provide a preliminary evaluation of the feasibility, acceptability and preliminary effectiveness of the programme. Data regarding retention, acceptability and feasibility indicate that the participants valued the programme. Analyses of outcome measures indicate that the programme has promise as a treatment option for autistic adults experiencing IU.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta se angustia mucho ante lo incierto o lo imprevisto, puede valer la pena preguntar a su equipo de salud por programas centrados en la «intolerancia a la incertidumbre», adaptados a personas autistas. Mientras tanto, se puede hablar con calma de qué situaciones inciertas pesan más y qué ayuda a afrontarlas paso a paso, respetando su ritmo. Este estudio de diseño de caso único probó un programa individual de ocho sesiones (CUES-A) con cuatro adultos autistas, que lo valoraron positivamente y mostraron señales prometedoras. Al ser solo cuatro personas y sin grupo de comparación, los resultados son preliminares y no aplican a todos.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult feels very anxious when things are uncertain or unexpected, it may be worth asking their health team about programmes that focus on 'intolerance of uncertainty' and are adapted for autistic people. Meanwhile, you can calmly talk together about which uncertain situations feel hardest and what helps to face them step by step, at their own pace. This single case experimental design study tested an eight-session individual programme (CUES-A) with four autistic adults, who valued it and showed promising changes. With only four people and no comparison group, the findings are early and will not fit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen blir mycket orolig när saker är osäkra eller oväntade kan det vara värt att fråga vården om program som fokuserar på 'intolerans för osäkerhet' och är anpassade för autistiska personer. Under tiden kan ni lugnt prata om vilka osäkra situationer som känns svårast och vad som hjälper att möta dem steg för steg, i personens egen takt. Studien, en experimentell single case-design, prövade ett individuellt program med åtta sessioner (CUES-A) med fyra autistiska vuxna, som uppskattade det och visade lovande förändringar. Med bara fyra deltagare och ingen jämförelsegrupp är resultaten preliminära och passar inte alla.

title: Risk markers for suicidality in autistic adults.
authors: Cassidy S, Bradley L, Shaw R, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Research has shown high rates of suicidality in autism spectrum conditions (ASC), but there is lack of research into why this is the case. Many common experiences of autistic adults, such as depression or unemployment, overlap with known risk markers for suicide in the general population. However, it is unknown whether there are risk markers unique to ASC that require new tailored suicide prevention strategies. Methods Through consultation with a steering group of autistic adults, a survey was developed aiming to identify unique risk markers for suicidality in this group.
