The survey measured suicidality (SBQ-R), non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI-AT), mental health problems, unmet support needs, employment, satisfaction with living arrangements, self-reported autistic traits (AQ), delay in ASC diagnosis, and 'camouflaging' ASC. One hundred sixty-four autistic adults (65 male, 99 female) and 169 general population adults (54 males, 115 females) completed the survey online. Results A majority of autistic adults (72%) scored above the recommended psychiatric cut-off for suicide risk on the SBQ-R; significantly higher than general population (GP) adults (33%). After statistically controlling for a range of demographics and diagnoses, ASC diagnosis and self-reported autistic traits in the general population significantly predicted suicidality. In autistic adults, non-suicidal self-injury, camouflaging, and number of unmet support needs significantly predicted suicidality. Conclusions Results confirm previously reported high rates of suicidality in ASC, and demonstrate that ASC diagnosis, and self-reported autistic traits in the general population are independent risk markers for suicidality. This suggests there are unique factors associated with autism and autistic traits that increase risk of suicidality. Camouflaging and unmet support needs appear to be risk markers for suicidality unique to ASC. Non-suicidal self-injury, employment, and mental health problems appear to be risk markers shared with the general population that are significantly more prevalent in the autistic community. Implications for understanding and prevention of suicide in ASC are discussed.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, pregúntale con calma qué apoyos le faltan y ayúdale a conseguir al menos uno. Crea espacios donde no tenga que esforzarse por 'parecer no autista' (camuflaje), y toma en serio las autolesiones: pide ayuda profesional. Si hay riesgo inmediato, llama a emergencias. Este estudio con encuestas en línea comparó a 164 adultos autistas con 169 adultos de la población general, diseñadas con un grupo asesor autista; el camuflaje, las necesidades de apoyo no cubiertas y las autolesiones se asociaron con más riesgo de suicidio. Límites: es una encuesta en un solo momento, autoinformada y online, así que muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, calmly ask which supports are missing and help secure at least one. Make spaces where they don't have to work at 'passing' as non-autistic (camouflaging), and take self-injury seriously by seeking professional help. If there is immediate danger, call emergency services. This online survey, designed with an autistic steering group, compared 164 autistic adults with 169 general-population adults; camouflaging, unmet support needs and self-injury were linked to higher suicide risk. Limits: it is a one-time, self-reported online survey, so it shows associations, not causes, and does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, fråga lugnt vilket stöd som saknas och hjälp till att ordna åtminstone ett. Skapa sammanhang där personen inte behöver anstränga sig för att verka icke-autistisk (kamouflering), och ta självskada på allvar genom att söka professionell hjälp. Vid akut fara, ring 112. Denna webbenkät, utformad med en autistisk referensgrupp, jämförde 164 autistiska vuxna med 169 vuxna i allmänbefolkningen; kamouflering, ouppfyllda stödbehov och självskada var kopplade till högre suicidrisk. Begränsningar: en självrapporterad enkät vid ett enda tillfälle visar samband, inte orsaker, och beskriver inte varje person.

title: Interoceptive impairments do not lie at the heart of autism or alexithymia.
authors: Nicholson TM, Williams DM, Grainger C, Christensen JF, Calvo-Merino B, Gaigg SB
abstract: Quattrocki and Friston (2014) argued that abnormalities in interoception-the process of representing one's internal physiological states-could lie at the heart of autism, because of the critical role interoception plays in the ontogeny of social-affective processes. This proposal drew criticism from proponents of the alexithymia hypothesis, who argue that social-affective and underlying interoceptive impairments are not a feature of autism per se, but of alexithymia (a condition characterized by difficulties describing and identifying one's own emotions), which commonly co-occurs with autism. Despite the importance of this debate for our understanding of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and of the role of interoceptive impairments in psychopathology, more generally, direct empirical evidence is scarce and inconsistent. Experiment 1 examined in a sample of 137 neurotypical (NT) individuals the association among autistic traits, alexithymia, and interoceptive accuracy (IA) on a standard heartbeat-tracking measure of IA. In Experiment 2, IA was assessed in 46 adults with ASD (27 of whom had clinically significant alexithymia) and 48 NT adults. Experiment 1 confirmed strong associations between autistic traits and alexithymia, but yielded no evidence to suggest that either was associated with interoceptive difficulties. Similarly, Experiment 2 provided no evidence for interoceptive impairments in autistic adults, irrespective of any co-occurring alexithymia. Bayesian analyses consistently supported the null hypothesis. The observations pose a significant challenge to notions that interoceptive impairments constitute a core feature of either ASD or alexithymia, at least as far as the direct perception of interoceptive signals is concerned. (PsycINFO Database Record

sheet.es: No dé por hecho que una persona autista no siente las señales de su cuerpo, como el latido, el hambre o el cansancio. Puede percibirlas bien y, aun así, necesitar tiempo o apoyo para ponerles nombre a sus emociones. Pregunte con calma, ofrezca palabras o imágenes y respete su forma de describir lo que siente. Evidencia: dos experimentos, uno con 137 adultos no autistas y otro con 46 adultos autistas y 48 no autistas, midieron la precisión al contar latidos y no hallaron diferencias, tuvieran o no alexitimia. Límites: solo adultos, una única tarea de latidos bastante discutida, y no se estudiaron niños ni personas con mayores necesidades de apoyo.
sheet.en: Don't assume an autistic person cannot sense their body's signals, such as heartbeat, hunger or tiredness. They may perceive them well and still need time or support to name their emotions. Ask calmly, offer words or pictures, and respect the way they describe what they feel. Evidence: two experiments, one with 137 non-autistic adults and another with 46 autistic and 48 non-autistic adults, measured accuracy at counting heartbeats and found no differences, with or without alexithymia. Limits: adults only, a single, much-debated heartbeat task, and children or people with higher support needs were not studied.
sheet.sv: Utgå inte från att en autistisk person inte känner kroppens signaler, som hjärtslag, hunger eller trötthet. Hen kan uppfatta dem väl och ändå behöva tid eller stöd för att sätta ord på sina känslor. Fråga lugnt, erbjud ord eller bilder och respektera hur hen beskriver det hen känner. Evidens: två experiment, ett med 137 icke-autistiska vuxna och ett med 46 autistiska och 48 icke-autistiska vuxna, mätte hur exakt deltagarna räknade sina hjärtslag och fann inga skillnader, oavsett alexitymi. Begränsningar: endast vuxna, en enda omdiskuterad hjärtslagsuppgift, och barn eller personer med större stödbehov ingick inte.

title: Social Skills Deficits in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Potential Biological Origins and Progress in Developing Therapeutic Agents.
authors: Frye RE
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder is defined by two core symptoms: a deficit in social communication and the presence of repetitive behaviors and/or restricted interests. Currently, there is no US Food and Drug Administration-approved drug for these core symptoms. This article reviews the biological origins of the social function deficit associated with autism spectrum disorder and the drug therapies with the potential to treat this deficit. A review of the history of autism demonstrates that a deficit in social interaction has been the defining feature of the concept of autism from its conception. Abnormalities identified in early social skill development and an overview of the pathophysiology abnormalities associated with autism spectrum disorder are discussed as are the abnormalities in brain circuits associated with the social function deficit. Previous and ongoing clinical trials examining agents that have the potential to improve social deficits associated with autism spectrum disorder are discussed in detail. This discussion reveals that agents such as oxytocin and propranolol are particularly promising and undergoing active investigation, while other agents such as vasopressin agonists and antagonists are being activity investigated but have limited published evidence at this time. In addition, agents such as bumetanide and manipulation of the enteric microbiome using microbiota transfer therapy appear to have promising effects on core autism spectrum disorder symptoms including social function. Other pertinent issues associated with developing treatments in autism spectrum disorder, such as disease heterogeneity, high placebo response rates, trial design, and the most appropriate way of assessing effects on social skills (outcome measures), are also discussed.

sheet.es: Mañana no hace falta cambiar nada en casa por este estudio. Esta revisión explica que, en 2018, no existía ningún fármaco aprobado para la comunicación social autista. Algunas sustancias se estaban investigando, pero seguían en fase experimental. Si alguien le ofrece un 'tratamiento' para la socialidad, pida pruebas y háblelo con un profesional de confianza. Mientras tanto, lo útil es adaptar el entorno, respetar la forma de comunicarse de la persona y preguntarle qué necesita. Se trata de una revisión narrativa de investigaciones previas, sin participantes propios. Como límite, ve el autismo desde el déficit, los ensayos que analiza tenían altas respuestas placebo y resultados preliminares, y no sirve como guía para cada persona.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change at home tomorrow because of this paper. This review explains that, as of 2018, no drug was approved for autistic social communication. Some substances were being studied, but they were still experimental. If someone offers a 'treatment' for sociability, ask for evidence and discuss it with a trusted professional. Meanwhile, what helps is adapting the environment, respecting how the person communicates and asking what they need. This is a narrative review of earlier research, with no participants of its own. On the limits, it frames autism as a deficit, the trials it covers showed high placebo responses and early results, and it is not a guide for every individual.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras hemma i morgon på grund av den här artikeln. Översikten förklarar att det 2018 inte fanns något godkänt läkemedel för autistisk social kommunikation. Vissa substanser studerades, men de var fortfarande experimentella. Om någon erbjuder en 'behandling' för socialt samspel, be om belägg och prata med en professionell du litar på. Under tiden hjälper det att anpassa miljön, respektera personens sätt att kommunicera och fråga vad hen behöver. Det är en narrativ översikt av tidigare forskning, utan egna deltagare. Den har också begränsningar: den beskriver autism som brist, de granskade studierna visade hög placeboeffekt och preliminära resultat, och den är ingen vägledning för varje individ.

title: Effectiveness of Virtual Reality for Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: An Evidence-Based Systematic Review.
authors: Mesa-Gresa P, Gil-Gómez H, Lozano-Quilis JA, Gil-Gómez JA
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disease that is specially characterized by impairments in social communication and social skills. ASD has a high prevalence in children, affecting 1 in 160 subjects. Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as an effective tool for intervention in the health field. Different recent papers have reviewed the VR-based treatments in ASD, but they have an important limitation because they only use clinical databases and do not include important technical indexes such as the Web of Science index or the Scimago Journal & Country Rank. To our knowledge, this is the first contribution that has carried out an evidence-based systematic review including both clinical and technical databases about the effectiveness of VR-based intervention in ASD. The initial search identified a total of 450 records. After the exclusion of the papers that are not studies, duplicated articles, and the screening of the abstract and full text, 31 articles met the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparison and Outcomes) criteria and were selected for analysis. The studies examined suggest moderate evidence about the effectiveness of VR-based treatments in ASD. VR can add many advantages to the treatment of ASD symptomatology, but it is necessary to develop consistent validations in future studies to state that VR can effectively complement the traditional treatments.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija le atraen la tecnología o los videojuegos, la realidad virtual puede ser una forma más de practicar situaciones sociales o cotidianas en un entorno predecible y seguro, siempre a su ritmo y con su consentimiento. No sustituye el apoyo habitual ni las relaciones reales; puede complementarlo si le resulta cómodo. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 31 estudios con niños, niñas y adolescentes autistas y encontró evidencia moderada de beneficios. Sus límites: los estudios eran pequeños y variados, y los autores piden validaciones más sólidas antes de afirmar que funciona de forma fiable. Además, enfoca el autismo como déficit, no como una forma distinta de ser.
sheet.en: If your child enjoys technology or games, virtual reality could be one more way to practise social or everyday situations in a predictable, safe setting, always at their own pace and with their agreement. It doesn't replace usual support or real relationships; it may complement them if it feels comfortable. This systematic review looked at 31 studies with autistic children and teenagers and found moderate evidence of benefits. Its limits: the studies were small and varied, and the authors call for stronger validation before saying it reliably works. It also frames autism as a deficit rather than a different way of being.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn gillar teknik eller spel kan virtuell verklighet vara ytterligare ett sätt att öva sociala eller vardagliga situationer i en förutsägbar och trygg miljö, alltid i barnets egen takt och med dess samtycke. Det ersätter inte ordinarie stöd eller verkliga relationer, men kan komplettera dem om det känns bekvämt. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 31 studier med autistiska barn och tonåringar och fann måttligt stöd för nytta. Begränsningar: studierna var små och olikartade, och författarna efterlyser bättre validering innan man kan säga att metoden fungerar tillförlitligt. Den beskriver också autism som brist snarare än ett annat sätt att vara.

title: Study protocol for the Australian autism biobank: an international resource to advance autism discovery research.
authors: Alvares GA, Dawson PA, Dissanayake C, Eapen V, Gratten J, Grove R, Henders A, Heussler H, Lawson L, Masi A, Raymond E, Rose F, Wallace L, Wray NR, Whitehouse AJO, Australian Autism Biobank team
abstract: Background The phenotypic and genetic heterogeneity of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) presents considerable challenges in understanding etiological pathways, selecting effective therapies, providing genetic counselling, and predicting clinical outcomes. With advances in genetic and biological research alongside rapid-pace technological innovations, there is an increasing imperative to access large, representative, and diverse cohorts to advance knowledge of ASD. To date, there has not been any single collective effort towards a similar resource in Australia, which has its own unique ethnic and cultural diversity. The Australian Autism Biobank was initiated by the Cooperative Research Centre for Living with Autism (Autism CRC) to establish a large-scale repository of biological samples and detailed clinical information about children diagnosed with ASD to facilitate future discovery research. Methods The primary group of participants were children with a confirmed diagnosis of ASD, aged between 2 and 17 years, recruited through four sites in Australia. No exclusion criteria regarding language level, cognitive ability, or comorbid conditions were applied to ensure a representative cohort was recruited. Both biological parents and siblings were invited to participate, along with children without a diagnosis of ASD, and children who had been queried for an ASD diagnosis but did not meet diagnostic criteria. All children completed cognitive assessments, with probands and parents completing additional assessments measuring ASD symptomatology. Parents completed questionnaires about their child's medical history and early development. Physical measurements and biological samples (blood, stool, urine, and hair) were collected from children, and physical measurements and blood samples were collected from parents. Samples were sent to a central processing site and placed into long-term storage. Discussion The establishment of this biobank is a valuable international resource incorporating detailed clinical and biological information that will help accelerate the pace of ASD discovery research. Recruitment into this study has also supported the feasibility of large-scale biological sample collection in children diagnosed with ASD with comprehensive phenotyping across a wide range of ages, intellectual abilities, and levels of adaptive functioning. This biological and clinical resource will be open to data access requests from national and international researchers to support future discovery research that will benefit the autistic community.

sheet.es: Este estudio no cambia nada en el día a día de su familia: describe cómo se creó un gran banco de datos y muestras para investigar el autismo en el futuro. Si alguna vez le invitan a participar en un biobanco, puede preguntar qué se recogerá, cómo se protegerán los datos y quién podrá usarlos; participar es siempre voluntario. Es un protocolo australiano que reunió a niños y niñas autistas de 2 a 17 años, sin excluir a nadie por lenguaje o capacidad cognitiva, junto con padres, hermanos y otros niños. Su límite: no ofrece resultados ni conclusiones, solo explica el método.
sheet.en: This study changes nothing in your family's daily life: it describes how a large bank of data and samples was set up for future autism research. If you are ever invited to join a biobank, you can ask what will be collected, how the data will be protected and who can use it; taking part is always voluntary. It is an Australian protocol that included autistic children aged 2 to 17, without excluding anyone based on language or cognitive ability, along with parents, siblings and other children. Its limit: it offers no findings or conclusions, it only explains the method.
sheet.sv: Den här studien förändrar ingenting i er familjs vardag: den beskriver hur en stor bank med data och prover byggdes upp för framtida autismforskning. Om ni någon gång blir inbjudna till en biobank kan ni fråga vad som samlas in, hur uppgifterna skyddas och vem som får använda dem; att delta är alltid frivilligt. Det är ett australiskt protokoll med autistiska barn mellan 2 och 17 år, där ingen uteslöts på grund av språk eller kognitiv förmåga, samt föräldrar, syskon och andra barn. Begränsningen: den ger inga resultat eller slutsatser, utan förklarar bara metoden.

title: Supporting and hindering environments for participation of adolescents diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder: A scoping review.
authors: Krieger B, Piškur B, Schulze C, Jakobs U, Beurskens A, Moser A
abstract: The influence of a person's environment and its modifying potential on participation is well recognized for most childhood disabilities, but scarcely studied for adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). A scoping review was conducted, the aim of which was to map the existing literature about supporting and hindering environments for the participation of adolescents with ASD. Sources of scientific evidence were searched for in four databases. Inclusion criteria were the perspectives of adolescents between 12 and 21, families, peers, or significant others; ecologic validity; and a clear connection between environment and participation. The publication dates ranged from 2001 to 2014 and partly up to 2018. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) served as the guiding framework for inclusion/exclusion during the selection process. Thematic analysis was performed by five independent reviewers. Results were additionally validated by stakeholders. This scoping review identified 5528 articles, and finally included 31 studies. Two main themes were found: "providing security" indicates how the environment, and specifically the parental, physical, and informational environments, have a securing or intimidating effect. The second theme, "helping to connect", indicates which environments support or hinder social relationships or social activities, and hence participation. An additional third main theme, "tension in participation", relates to ambiguities that seem essential to understand participation or isolation of adolescents with ASD. Results show that participation is a value-laden concept. This research widens the field of dealing with adolescents with ASD, as it directs attention towards the responsibility of the environment regarding participation.

sheet.es: Mañana puede preguntarse qué hace que su adolescente autista se sienta seguro para participar: un espacio predecible, información clara de antemano sobre qué va a pasar, y adultos que acompañan sin presionar. También vale la pena buscar entornos que faciliten conectar con otros a su manera, por ejemplo alrededor de intereses compartidos. Recuerde que participar no significa lo mismo para todos; a veces estar a solas también tiene valor. Es una revisión exploratoria de 31 estudios con perspectivas de adolescentes de 12 a 21 años, familias y pares, validada por personas implicadas. Sus límites: los estudios son diversos y en su mayoría anteriores a 2015, y no prueban qué cambios funcionan mejor para cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, you might ask what helps your autistic teenager feel safe enough to take part: a predictable space, clear information in advance about what will happen, and adults who stay close without pushing. It is also worth looking for settings that make connecting with others easier on their own terms, such as around shared interests. Remember that participation does not mean the same thing for everyone; time alone can have value too. This is a scoping review of 31 studies including the views of adolescents aged 12–21, families and peers, checked with stakeholders. Its limits: the studies vary widely, are mostly older than 2015, and do not test which changes work best for each person.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du fundera på vad som gör att din autistiska tonåring känner sig trygg nog att delta: en förutsägbar miljö, tydlig information i förväg om vad som ska hända och vuxna som finns nära utan att pressa. Det kan också löna sig att leta efter sammanhang där det blir lättare att knyta an till andra på eget sätt, till exempel kring gemensamma intressen. Kom ihåg att delaktighet inte betyder samma sak för alla; egen tid kan också ha värde. Detta är en kartläggande översikt av 31 studier med perspektiv från ungdomar 12–21 år, familjer och jämnåriga, granskad av berörda personer. Begränsningar: studierna skiljer sig mycket åt, är mest från före 2015 och testar inte vilka förändringar som fungerar bäst för varje person.

title: Sex: A Significant Risk Factor for Neurodevelopmental and Neurodegenerative Disorders.
authors: Pinares-Garcia P, Stratikopoulos M, Zagato A, Loke H, Lee J
abstract: Males and females sometimes significantly differ in their propensity to develop neurological disorders. Females suffer more from mood disorders such as depression and anxiety, whereas males are more susceptible to deficits in the dopamine system including Parkinson's disease (PD), attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism. Despite this, biological sex is rarely considered when making treatment decisions in neurological disorders. A better understanding of the molecular mechanism(s) underlying sex differences in the healthy and diseased brain will help to devise diagnostic and therapeutic strategies optimal for each sex. Thus, the aim of this review is to discuss the available evidence on sex differences in neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders regarding prevalence, progression, symptoms and response to therapy. We also discuss the sex-related factors such as gonadal sex hormones and sex chromosome genes and how these might help to explain some of the clinically observed sex differences in these disorders. In particular, we highlight the emerging role of the Y-chromosome gene, SRY, in the male brain and its potential role as a male-specific risk factor for disorders such as PD, autism, and ADHD in many individuals.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: el autismo se diagnostica más en chicos, pero eso no significa que las chicas y mujeres no sean autistas; a menudo se las reconoce más tarde. Si cuidas a una niña o mujer con señales, vale la pena pedir una evaluación sin esperar a que encaje en el perfil típico masculino. También es razonable preguntar a profesionales si consideran el sexo al planificar apoyos. Evidencia: es una revisión narrativa de estudios sobre diferencias de sexo en varias condiciones neurológicas, incluida una hipótesis sobre el gen SRY del cromosoma Y. Límites: no recoge datos nuevos, gran parte se basa en investigación biológica y animal, y no ofrece pautas aplicables a cada persona.
sheet.en: The practical point: autism is diagnosed more often in boys, but that does not mean girls and women are not autistic; they are often recognised later. If you support a girl or woman showing signs, it is worth asking for an assessment without waiting for her to fit a typical male profile. It is also reasonable to ask professionals whether they consider sex when planning support. Evidence: this is a narrative review of studies on sex differences across several neurological conditions, including a hypothesis about the Y-chromosome gene SRY. Limits: it collects no new data, much of it rests on biological and animal research, and it offers no guidance that applies to every individual.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: autism diagnostiseras oftare hos pojkar, men det betyder inte att flickor och kvinnor inte är autistiska; de upptäcks ofta senare. Om du stöttar en flicka eller kvinna med tecken kan det vara värt att be om en utredning utan att vänta på att hon ska passa en typisk manlig bild. Det är också rimligt att fråga vården om de tar hänsyn till kön när stöd planeras. Evidens: detta är en narrativ översikt av studier om könsskillnader i flera neurologiska tillstånd, inklusive en hypotes om genen SRY på Y-kromosomen. Begränsningar: den samlar inga nya data, bygger till stor del på biologisk forskning och djurstudier och ger inga råd som gäller varje person.

title: Clinical and Molecular Characteristics of Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Rose S, Niyazov DM, Rossignol DA, Goldenthal M, Kahler SG, Frye RE
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects ~ 2% of children in the United States. The etiology of ASD likely involves environmental factors triggering physiological abnormalities in genetically sensitive individuals. One of these major physiological abnormalities is mitochondrial dysfunction, which may affect a significant subset of children with ASD. Here we systematically review the literature on human studies of mitochondrial dysfunction related to ASD. Clinical aspects of mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD include unusual neurodevelopmental regression, especially if triggered by an inflammatory event, gastrointestinal symptoms, seizures, motor delays, fatigue and lethargy. Traditional biomarkers of mitochondrial disease are widely reported to be abnormal in ASD, but appear non-specific. Newer biomarkers include buccal cell enzymology, biomarkers of fatty acid metabolism, non-mitochondrial enzyme function, apoptosis markers and mitochondrial antibodies. Many genetic abnormalities are associated with mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD, including chromosomal abnormalities, mitochondrial DNA mutations and large-scale deletions, and mutations in both mitochondrial and non-mitochondrial nuclear genes. Mitochondrial dysfunction has been described in immune and buccal cells, fibroblasts, muscle and gastrointestinal tissue and the brains of individuals with ASD. Several environmental factors, including toxicants, microbiome metabolites and an oxidized microenvironment are shown to modulate mitochondrial function in ASD tissues. Investigations of treatments for mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD are promising but preliminary. The etiology of mitochondrial dysfunction and how to define it in ASD is currently unclear. However, preliminary evidence suggests that the mitochondria may be a fruitful target for treatment and prevention of ASD. Further research is needed to better understand the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathophysiology of ASD.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista pierde habilidades que ya tenía (sobre todo tras una fiebre o infección), o tiene cansancio inusual, problemas digestivos, convulsiones o retrasos motores, anótalo con fechas y coméntalo con su equipo médico; puede valer la pena una evaluación del metabolismo energético. Esta revisión sistemática reúne estudios en humanos sobre el funcionamiento de las mitocondrias en personas autistas. Sus límites: los marcadores son poco específicos, no hay una definición clara del problema, los tratamientos estudiados son preliminares, y no describe a todas las personas autistas ni busca cambiar quién es tu hijo.
sheet.en: If your autistic child loses skills they already had (especially after a fever or infection), or has unusual tiredness, gut problems, seizures or motor delays, write it down with dates and raise it with their medical team; an assessment of energy metabolism may be worth discussing. This systematic review gathers human studies on how mitochondria work in autistic people. Its limits: the markers are not very specific, there is no clear definition of the problem, the treatments studied are preliminary, and it does not describe every autistic person or aim to change who your child is.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn tappar förmågor det redan hade (särskilt efter feber eller infektion), eller har ovanlig trötthet, magbesvär, krampanfall eller motoriska förseningar, skriv ner det med datum och ta upp det med barnets vårdteam; en utredning av energiomsättningen kan vara värd att diskutera. Denna systematiska översikt samlar studier på människor om hur mitokondrierna fungerar hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: markörerna är ospecifika, problemet saknar tydlig definition, studerade behandlingar är preliminära, och den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer eller syftar till att ändra vem ditt barn är.

title: Developmental disabilities among children younger than 5 years in 195 countries and territories, 1990-2016: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2016.
authors: Global Research on Developmental Disabilities Collaborators
abstract: Background The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) mandate systematic monitoring of the health and wellbeing of all children to achieve optimal early childhood development. However, global epidemiological data on children with developmental disabilities are scarce. The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2016 provides a comprehensive assessment of prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) for development disabilities among children younger than 5 years in 195 countries and territories from 1990 to 2016. Methods We estimated prevalence and YLDs for epilepsy, intellectual disability, hearing loss, vision loss, autism spectrum disorder, and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. YLDs were estimated as the product of the prevalence estimate and the disability weight for each mutually exclusive disorder, corrected for comorbidity. We used DisMod-MR 2.1, a Bayesian meta-regression tool, on a pool of primary data derived from systematic reviews of the literature, health surveys, hospital and claims databases, cohort studies, and disease-specific registries. Findings Globally, 52·9 million (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 48·7-57·3; or 8·4% [7·7-9·1]) children younger than 5 years (54% males) had developmental disabilities in 2016 compared with 53·0 million (49·0-57·1; or 8·9% [8·2-9·5]) in 1990. About 95% of these children lived in low-income and middle-income countries. YLDs among these children increased from 3·8 million (95% UI 2·8-4·9) in 1990 to 3·9 million (2·9-5·2) in 2016. These disabilities accounted for 13·3% of the 29·3 million YLDs for all health conditions among children younger than 5 years in 2016. Vision loss was the most prevalent disability, followed by hearing loss, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder. However, intellectual disability was the largest contributor to YLDs in both 1990 and 2016. Although the prevalence of developmental disabilities among children younger than 5 years decreased in all countries (except for North America) between 1990 and 2016, the number of children with developmental disabilities increased significantly in sub-Saharan Africa (71·3%) and in North Africa and the Middle East (7·6%). South Asia had the highest prevalence of children with developmental disabilities in 2016 and North America had the lowest. Interpretation The global burden of developmental disabilities has not significantly improved since 1990, suggesting inadequate global attention on the developmental potential of children who survived childhood as a result of child survival programmes, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and south Asia. The SDGs provide a framework for policy and action to address the needs of children with or at risk of developmental disabilities, particularly in resource-poor countries. Funding The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo pequeño es autista o tiene otra discapacidad del desarrollo, no estás solo: este estudio estima que unos 53 millones de niños menores de 5 años en el mundo viven con alguna, sobre todo pérdida de visión o audición, discapacidad intelectual o autismo. En la práctica, vale la pena pedir revisiones tempranas de vista y oído, porque son frecuentes y pueden coexistir con el autismo. Es un análisis sistemático del Global Burden of Disease con datos de 195 países entre 1990 y 2016. Sus límites: son estimaciones estadísticas con datos escasos en muchos países, y no dicen nada sobre apoyos concretos ni sobre la experiencia de cada niño.
sheet.en: If your young child is autistic or has another developmental disability, you are far from alone: this study estimates that about 53 million children under 5 worldwide have one, most often vision loss, hearing loss, intellectual disability or autism. Practically, it is worth asking for early vision and hearing checks, since these are common and can occur alongside autism. This is a systematic analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study, pooling data from 195 countries between 1990 and 2016. Its limits: these are statistical estimates, with thin data in many countries, and they say nothing about specific supports or each child's own experience.
sheet.sv: Om ditt lilla barn är autistiskt eller har en annan utvecklingsrelaterad funktionsnedsättning är ni långt ifrån ensamma: studien uppskattar att omkring 53 miljoner barn under 5 år i världen har någon, oftast synnedsättning, hörselnedsättning, intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller autism. I praktiken kan det vara klokt att be om tidig syn- och hörselkontroll, eftersom dessa är vanliga och kan finnas samtidigt som autism. Det är en systematisk analys inom Global Burden of Disease, med data från 195 länder 1990–2016. Begränsningar: det rör sig om statistiska uppskattningar med bristfälliga data i många länder, och studien säger inget om konkret stöd eller varje barns egen upplevelse.

title: The Association Between Emotional and Behavioral Problems in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and Psychological Distress in Their Parents: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Yorke I, White P, Weston A, Rafla M, Charman T, Simonoff E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This review (Prospero Registration Number: CRD42017057915) aimed to systematically identify and summarize existing research on the relationship between additional emotional and behavioral problems (EBP) in children with autism, and parenting stress (PS) and mental health problems (MHP) in their parents. Sixty-seven studies met criteria for inclusion in the review, 61 of which were included in the meta-analysis. Pooled correlation coefficients were in the low to moderate range ([Formula: see text]). Some evidence for moderation by measurement characteristics was found. Narrative review of concurrent adjusted associations showed some evidence for shared relationships with other factors, most notably ASD severity and parent perception of own parenting. Longitudinal studies showed mixed evidence for bidirectional predictive relationships between child EBP and parent psychological distress variables.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo autista vive momentos de mucha angustia emocional y tú te sientes agotado o estresado, no es un fallo tuyo: ambas cosas suelen ir juntas y pueden influirse mutuamente. Cuidar tu propio bienestar (pedir apoyo, descansar, hablar con alguien) también forma parte de cuidar a tu hijo, y cómo valoras tu propia crianza importa. Esta evidencia viene de un metaanálisis que reunió 67 estudios sobre niños autistas y sus padres, con asociaciones de baja a moderada intensidad. Sus límites: la mayoría de los estudios miden un solo momento, así que no prueban qué causa qué, y cada familia es distinta.
sheet.en: If your autistic child is going through a lot of emotional distress and you feel worn out or stressed, that is not a personal failure: the two often go together and may influence each other. Looking after your own wellbeing (asking for support, resting, talking to someone) is part of caring for your child, and how you see your own parenting matters too. This comes from a meta-analysis pooling 67 studies of autistic children and their parents, finding low to moderate associations. Its limits: most studies looked at one point in time, so they cannot show what causes what, and every family is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har det emotionellt tufft och du själv känner dig sliten eller stressad är det inte ditt misslyckande: de två hänger ofta ihop och kan påverka varandra. Att ta hand om ditt eget mående (be om stöd, vila, prata med någon) är också en del av att ta hand om ditt barn, och hur du ser på ditt eget föräldraskap spelar roll. Detta bygger på en metaanalys av 67 studier om autistiska barn och deras föräldrar, med svaga till måttliga samband. Begränsningar: de flesta studier mätte vid ett enda tillfälle, så de visar inte vad som orsakar vad, och varje familj är unik.

title: Autism Diagnosis in the United Kingdom: Perspectives of Autistic Adults, Parents and Professionals.
authors: Crane L, Batty R, Adeyinka H, Goddard L, Henry LA, Hill EL
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Accessing an autism diagnosis is a key milestone, both for an individual and their family. Using a qualitative methodology, the current study examined the views and experiences of ten autistic adults, ten parents of children on the autism spectrum, and ten professionals involved in autism diagnosis, all based in the United Kingdom (UK). Interviewing these 30 respondents about the diagnostic process and subsequent support options, the goal was to identify aspects of the diagnostic process that are working well, and areas in which improvements are needed. Using thematic analysis, three key themes were identified: the process of understanding and accepting autism; multiple barriers to satisfaction with the diagnostic process; and inadequate post-diagnostic support provision.

sheet.es: Si usted o su familia están buscando un diagnóstico de autismo, puede ayudar saber que comprender y aceptar el autismo lleva tiempo, y que muchas personas encuentran obstáculos en el proceso. Prepare sus preguntas, anote ejemplos de la vida diaria y pregunte desde el principio qué apoyo habrá después del diagnóstico; a menudo es escaso, así que buscar grupos de personas autistas o de familias puede llenar ese vacío. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 10 adultos autistas, 10 madres o padres y 10 profesionales del Reino Unido. Son pocas personas en un solo país y sistema sanitario, por lo que las experiencias pueden ser distintas en otros lugares.
sheet.en: If you or your family are seeking an autism diagnosis, it may help to know that understanding and accepting autism takes time, and many people meet obstacles along the way. Prepare your questions, note everyday examples, and ask early what support will follow the diagnosis; it is often limited, so connecting with autistic-led or family groups can help fill that gap. This qualitative study interviewed 10 autistic adults, 10 parents and 10 diagnostic professionals in the United Kingdom. It involved a small number of people in one country and health system, so experiences elsewhere may differ.
sheet.sv: Om du eller din familj söker en autismutredning kan det hjälpa att veta att förståelse och acceptans av autism tar tid, och att många möter hinder på vägen. Förbered dina frågor, skriv ner exempel från vardagen och fråga tidigt vilket stöd som finns efter diagnosen; det är ofta begränsat, så kontakt med grupper för autistiska personer eller familjer kan fylla tomrummet. Studien är kvalitativ och bygger på intervjuer med 10 autistiska vuxna, 10 föräldrar och 10 yrkespersoner i Storbritannien. Den omfattar få personer i ett land och ett vårdsystem, så erfarenheterna kan se annorlunda ut på andra håll.

title: Savant syndrome has a distinct psychological profile in autism.
authors: Hughes JEA, Ward J, Gruffydd E, Baron-Cohen S, Smith P, Allison C, Simner J
abstract: Background Savant syndrome is a condition where prodigious talent can co-occur with developmental conditions such as autism spectrum conditions (autism). It is not yet clear why some autistic people develop savant skills while others do not. Methods We tested three groups of adults: autistic individuals who have savant skills, autistic individuals without savant skills, and typical controls without autism or savant syndrome. In experiment 1, we investigated the cognitive and behavioural profiles of these three groups by asking participants to complete a battery of self-report measures of sensory sensitivity, obsessional behaviours, cognitive styles, and broader autism-related traits including social communication and systemising. In experiment 2, we investigated how our three groups learned a novel savant skill-calendar calculation. Results Heightened sensory sensitivity, obsessional behaviours, technical/spatial abilities, and systemising were all key aspects in defining the savant profile distinct from autism alone, along with a different approach to task learning. Conclusions These results reveal a unique cognitive and behavioural profile in autistic adults with savant syndrome that is distinct from autistic adults without a savant skill.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene un talento excepcional (por ejemplo, cálculo de calendarios, música o dibujo), puede ser útil observar también su sensibilidad sensorial y sus intereses intensos: suelen ir juntos. Ofrecer espacios tranquilos, respetar sus rutinas de práctica y apoyar su forma propia de aprender puede ayudar a que ese talento crezca sin sobrecarga. Evidencia: estudio con adultos autistas con y sin habilidades savant y adultos no autistas, mediante cuestionarios y una tarea de aprendizaje de cálculo de calendarios. Límites: grupos pequeños, sobre todo autoinformes y solo adultos; no indica que todo talento siga este patrón ni cómo fomentarlo en niños.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has an exceptional talent (for example calendar calculation, music or drawing), it may help to also notice their sensory sensitivity and intense interests, as these often go together. Offering quiet spaces, respecting their practice routines and supporting their own way of learning can help the talent grow without overload. Evidence: a study of autistic adults with and without savant skills and non-autistic adults, using questionnaires and a calendar-calculation learning task. Limits: small groups, mostly self-report and adults only; it does not show that every talent follows this pattern or how to nurture it in children.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har en exceptionell talang (till exempel kalenderräkning, musik eller teckning) kan det hjälpa att också uppmärksamma hens sensoriska känslighet och intensiva intressen, eftersom de ofta hör ihop. Att erbjuda lugna miljöer, respektera hens övningsrutiner och stötta hens eget sätt att lära kan låta talangen växa utan överbelastning. Evidens: en studie med autistiska vuxna med och utan savantförmågor samt icke-autistiska vuxna, med frågeformulär och en inlärningsuppgift i kalenderräkning. Begränsningar: små grupper, mest självskattning och bara vuxna; studien visar inte att varje talang följer mönstret eller hur den kan stödjas hos barn.

title: Language delay aggregates in toddler siblings of children with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Marrus N, Hall LP, Paterson SJ, Elison JT, Wolff JJ, Swanson MR, Parish-Morris J, Eggebrecht AT, Pruett JR, Hazlett HC, Zwaigenbaum L, Dager S, Estes AM, Schultz RT, Botteron KN, Piven J, Constantino
abstract: Background Language delay is extremely common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet it is unclear whether measurable variation in early language is associated with genetic liability for ASD. Assessment of language development in unaffected siblings of children with ASD can inform whether decreased early language ability aggregates with inherited risk for ASD and serves as an ASD endophenotype. Methods We implemented two approaches: (1) a meta-analysis of studies comparing language delay, a categorical indicator of language function, and language scores, a continuous metric, in unaffected toddlers at high and low familial risk for ASD, and (2) a parallel analysis of 350 unaffected 24-month-olds in the Infant Brain Imaging Study (IBIS), a prospective study of infants at high and low familial risk for ASD. An advantage of the former was its detection of group differences from pooled data across unique samples; an advantage of the latter was its sensitivity in quantifying early manifestations of language delay while accounting for covariates within a single large sample. Results Meta-analysis showed that high-risk siblings without ASD (HR-noASD) were three to four times more likely to exhibit language delay versus low-risk siblings without ASD (LR-noASD) and had lower mean receptive and expressive language scores. Analyses of IBIS data corroborated that language delay, specifically receptive language delay, was more frequent in the HR-noASD (n = 235) versus LR-noASD group (n = 115). IBIS language scores were continuously and unimodally distributed, with a pathological shift towards decreased language function in HR-noASD siblings. The elevated inherited risk for ASD was associated with lower receptive and expressive language scores when controlling for sociodemographic factors. For receptive but not expressive language, the effect of risk group remained significant even when controlling for nonverbal cognition. Conclusions Greater frequency of language delay and a lower distribution of language scores in high-risk, unaffected toddler-aged siblings support decreased early language ability as an endophenotype for ASD, with a more pronounced effect for receptive versus expressive language. Further characterization of language development is warranted to refine genetic investigations of ASD and to elucidate factors influencing the progression of core autistic traits and related symptoms.

sheet.es: Si tienes un hijo autista y un hermano o hermana más pequeño, vale la pena observar con calma cómo el menor entiende el lenguaje (seguir instrucciones, reconocer palabras), no solo cuánto habla. Si notas dudas, pide una valoración del lenguaje temprana: el apoyo temprano ayuda, haya o no autismo. Evidencia: un metaanálisis más un estudio de 350 niños de 24 meses mostró que los hermanos no autistas de niños autistas tenían 3-4 veces más retraso del lenguaje, sobre todo en comprensión. Límites: son diferencias de grupo a los dos años; muchos hermanos se desarrollan sin retraso y el estudio no predice el futuro de cada niño.
sheet.en: If you have an autistic child and a younger sibling, it is worth calmly noticing how the younger child understands language (following simple instructions, recognising words), not only how much they speak. If you have concerns, ask for an early language assessment: early support helps whether or not the child is autistic. Evidence: a meta-analysis plus a study of 350 two-year-olds found that non-autistic siblings of autistic children were three to four times more likely to show language delay, especially in understanding. Limits: these are group differences at age two; many siblings develop without delay, and the findings cannot predict any individual child's path.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett autistiskt barn och ett yngre syskon kan det vara bra att lugnt lägga märke till hur det yngre barnet förstår språk (följer enkla uppmaningar, känner igen ord), inte bara hur mycket det pratar. Om du är orolig, be om en tidig språkbedömning: tidigt stöd hjälper oavsett om barnet är autistiskt eller inte. Evidens: en metaanalys och en studie av 350 tvååringar visade att icke-autistiska syskon till autistiska barn hade tre till fyra gånger oftare språkförsening, särskilt i språkförståelse. Begränsningar: det gäller skillnader mellan grupper vid två års ålder; många syskon utvecklas utan försening och resultaten kan inte förutsäga enskilda barns utveckling.

title: Reduction in social anxiety after MDMA-assisted psychotherapy with autistic adults: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study.
authors: Danforth AL, Grob CS, Struble C, Feduccia AA, Walker N, Jerome L, Yazar-Klosinski B, Emerson A
abstract: Rationale Standard therapeutic approaches to reduce social anxiety in autistic adults have limited effectiveness. Since 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA)-assisted psychotherapy shows promise as a treatment for other anxiety disorders, a blinded, placebo-controlled pilot study was conducted. Objectives To explore feasibility and safety of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for reduction of social fear and avoidance that are common in the autistic population. Methods Autistic adults with marked to very severe social anxiety were randomized to receive MDMA (75 to 125 mg, n = 8) or inactive placebo (0 mg, n = 4) during two 8-h psychotherapy sessions (experimental sessions) in a controlled clinical setting. Double-blinded experimental sessions were spaced approximately 1 month apart with 3 non-drug psychotherapy sessions following each. The primary outcome was change in Leibowitz Social Anxiety Scale (LSAS) Total scores from Baseline to one month after the second experimental session. Outcomes were measured again six months after the last experimental session. Results Improvement in LSAS scores from baseline to the primary endpoint was significantly greater for MDMA group compared to the placebo group (P = 0.037), and placebo-subtracted Cohen's d effect size was very large (d = 1.4, CI - 0.074, 2.874). Change in LSAS scores from baseline to 6-month follow-up showed similar positive results (P = 0.036), with a Cohen's d effect size of 1.1 (CI - 0.307, 2.527). Social anxiety remained the same or continued to improve slightly for most participants in the MDMA group after completing the active treatment phase. Conclusions This pilot trial demonstrated rapid and durable improvement in social anxiety symptoms in autistic adults following MDMA-assisted psychotherapy. Initial safety and efficacy outcomes support expansion of research into larger samples to further investigate this novel treatment for social anxiety. Trial registration clinicaltrials.gov identifier, NCT02008396.

sheet.es: Lo práctico para mañana: si un adulto autista vive con mucha ansiedad social, esto no es algo para probar en casa ni por cuenta propia; es investigación temprana en un entorno clínico controlado. Lo útil hoy es hablar con su equipo de salud sobre apoyos para la ansiedad que respeten su forma de ser, como reducir exigencias sociales innecesarias o acordar señales de pausa. Evidencia: ensayo piloto aleatorizado y doble ciego con 12 adultos autistas, en el que la terapia asistida con MDMA redujo la ansiedad social más que el placebo. Límites: muestra muy pequeña, sustancia no aprobada para uso clínico general y resultados que necesitan estudios mayores.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway for tomorrow: if an autistic adult lives with intense social anxiety, this is not something to try at home or on your own; it is early research done in a controlled clinical setting. What helps today is talking with their care team about anxiety support that respects who they are, such as reducing unnecessary social demands or agreeing on break signals. Evidence: a randomized, double-blind pilot trial with 12 autistic adults found MDMA-assisted therapy reduced social anxiety more than placebo. Limits: the sample was very small, the substance is not approved for general clinical use, and larger studies are needed.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska inför i morgon: om en autistisk vuxen lever med stark social ångest är detta inget att prova hemma eller på egen hand; det är tidig forskning i en kontrollerad klinisk miljö. Det som hjälper i dag är att prata med vårdteamet om stöd mot ångest som respekterar personen, till exempel att minska onödiga sociala krav eller komma överens om signaler för paus. Evidens: en randomiserad, dubbelblind pilotstudie med 12 autistiska vuxna där MDMA-assisterad terapi minskade social ångest mer än placebo. Begränsningar: mycket litet urval, substansen är inte godkänd för allmän klinisk användning och större studier behövs.

title: Predictors of quality of life for autistic adults.
authors: Mason D, McConachie H, Garland D, Petrou A, Rodgers J, Parr JR
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Research with adults on the autism spectrum is as yet limited in scope and quality. The present study describes quality of life (QoL) of a large sample of autistic adults in the UK and investigates characteristics that may be predictive of QoL. A total of 370 autistic adults from the Adult Autism Spectrum Cohort-UK (ASC-UK) completed the WHOQoL-BREF, and the Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS, autism symptom severity), along with the ASC-UK registration questionnaire giving information on mental health and their life situation. QoL for autistic adults was lower than for the general population for each WHOQoL domain. Younger participants reported higher QoL than older participants in psychological and environment domains. Males reported higher physical QoL than females, and females reported higher social QoL than males. Significant positive predictors of QoL were: being employed (physical QoL), receiving support (social and environment QoL), and being in a relationship (social QoL). Having a mental health condition and higher SRS total score were negative predictors of QoL across all four domains. Autistic adults require access to effective mental health interventions, and informal and formal support for their social difficulties, to improve their quality of life. Autism Res 2018, 11: 1138-1147. © 2018 The Authors Autism Research published by International Society for Autism Research and Wiley Periodicals, Inc. LAY SUMMARY: There has been limited research into the lived experience of autistic adults. Using the World Health Organization quality of life measure, we found that autistic people (370) in the UK reported their quality of life to be lower than that of the general population. Better quality of life was associated with being in a relationship; those with a mental health condition had poorer quality of life. This research suggests some ways in which autistic people can be helped to improve their quality of life.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona adulta autista, vale la pena prestar atención a su salud mental y a si tiene apoyos reales: ayuda práctica, alguien de confianza, conexiones que ella misma elija. En este estudio, recibir apoyo, tener trabajo o pareja se asociaron con mejor calidad de vida, y tener una condición de salud mental con peor calidad de vida en todas las áreas. Pregunta qué apoyo desea, sin imponer metas. Evidencia: encuesta del Reino Unido con 370 adultos autistas que valoraron su propia calidad de vida. Límites: muestra transversal y voluntaria; muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no todas las personas autistas se ven reflejadas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it is worth paying attention to their mental health and to whether they have real support: practical help, someone they trust, connections they choose themselves. In this study, receiving support, having a job or being in a relationship were linked to better quality of life, while having a mental health condition was linked to lower quality of life in every area. Ask what support they want, without imposing goals. Evidence: a UK survey of 370 autistic adults who rated their own quality of life. Limits: a one-time, volunteer sample; it shows associations, not causes, and does not reflect every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen är det värt att uppmärksamma den psykiska hälsan och om personen har verkligt stöd: praktisk hjälp, någon att lita på, relationer hen själv väljer. I studien hängde stöd, arbete och parrelation ihop med bättre livskvalitet, medan psykisk ohälsa hängde ihop med lägre livskvalitet inom alla områden. Fråga vilket stöd personen själv vill ha, utan att påtvinga mål. Underlag: en brittisk enkät där 370 autistiska vuxna skattade sin egen livskvalitet. Begränsningar: ett frivilligt urval vid ett enda tillfälle; studien visar samband, inte orsaker, och speglar inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Gender Identity in Autism: Sex Differences in Social Affiliation with Gender Groups.
authors: Cooper K, Smith LGE, Russell AJ
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: High rates of gender variance have been reported in autistic people, with higher variance in autistic females than males. The social component of gender identity may be affected, with autistic females experiencing lower identification with and feeling less positively about their gender groups than controls. We measured gender identification, gender self-esteem, and aspects of gender expression (masculinity and femininity) in autistic natal males and females, and controls (N = 486). We found that autistic people had lower gender identification and gender self-esteem than controls, and autistic natal females had lower gender identification than autistic natal males and natal female controls. In conclusion, autistic people, particularly natal females, had lower social identification with and more negative feelings about a gender group.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo dice sentirse poco unida a «las chicas» o «los chicos», o no le gusta encajar en un grupo de género, es algo frecuente y merece escucha sin presión. Puedes ofrecer espacios para hablar, aceptar su forma de vestir o expresarse y evitar frases como «compórtate como una chica». Este estudio con 486 personas adultas, autistas y no autistas, encontró que las personas autistas, sobre todo las asignadas mujer al nacer, se identificaban menos con su grupo de género y tenían sentimientos menos positivos hacia él. Se basó en cuestionarios en un solo momento, así que no explica causas ni describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support says they feel little connection to "girls" or "boys", or dislikes fitting a gender group, this is common and worth listening to without pressure. You can offer space to talk, accept how they dress or express themselves, and avoid phrases like "act like a proper girl". This study of 486 adults, autistic and non-autistic, found that autistic people, especially those assigned female at birth, identified less with their gender group and felt less positive about it. It used questionnaires at a single point in time, so it does not explain causes or describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar säger att hen känner liten samhörighet med "tjejer" eller "killar", eller ogillar att passa in i en könsgrupp, är det vanligt och värt att lyssna på utan press. Du kan erbjuda utrymme att prata, acceptera hur hen klär sig eller uttrycker sig och undvika fraser som "bete dig som en riktig tjej". Studien med 486 vuxna, autistiska och icke-autistiska, visade att autistiska personer, särskilt de som tilldelats kvinnligt kön vid födseln, identifierade sig mindre med sin könsgrupp och kände sig mindre positiva till den. Den byggde på enkäter vid ett enda tillfälle, så den förklarar inte orsaker eller beskriver varje individ.

title: Social Cognition in Schizophrenia and Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Direct Comparisons.
authors: Fernandes JM, Cajão R, Lopes R, Jerónimo R, Barahona-Corrêa JB
abstract: Background: Deficits in social cognition are well-recognized in both schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders (ASD). However, it is less clear how social cognition deficits differ between both disorders and what distinct mechanisms may underlie such differences. We aimed at reviewing available evidence from studies directly comparing social cognitive performance between individuals with schizophrenia and ASD. Methods: We performed a systematic review of literature up to May 22, 2018 on Pubmed, Web of Science, and Scopus. Search terms included combinations of the keywords "social cognition," "theory of mind," "autism," "Asperger," "psychosis," and "schizophrenia." Two researchers independently selected and extracted data according to PRISMA guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted for performance on social cognitive tasks evaluating: (1) emotion perception; (2) theory of mind (ToM); (3) emotional intelligence (managing emotions score of the Mayer-Salovey-Caruso Emotional Intelligence Test); and (4) social skills. Results: We identified 19 eligible studies for meta-analysis including a total of 1,040 patients (558 with schizophrenia and 482 with ASD). Eight studies provided data on facial emotion perception that evidenced a better performance by participants with schizophrenia compared to those with ASD (Hedges' g = 0.43; p = 0.031). No significant differences were found between groups in the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (8 studies; Hedges' g = 0.22; p = 0.351), other ToM tasks (9 studies; Hedges' g = -0.03; p = 0.903), emotional intelligence (3 studies; Hedges' g = -0.17; p = 0.490), and social skills (3 studies; Hedges' g = 0.86; p = 0.056). Participants' age was a significant moderator of effect size in emotion perception and RMET analyzes, with larger differences favoring patients with schizophrenia being observed in studies with younger participants. Conclusions: The instruments that are currently available to evaluate social cognition poorly differentiate between individuals with schizophrenia and ASD. Combining behavioral tasks with neurophysiologic assessments may better characterize the differences in social cognition between both disorders.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista ha recibido evaluaciones de «cognición social», recuerde que estas pruebas no distinguen bien entre autismo y esquizofrenia, y no captan cómo la persona realmente entiende a otras ni cómo se comunica a su manera. Pregunte qué medía cada prueba y complemente con lo que usted observa en la vida diaria. Este metaanálisis reunió 19 estudios con 1.040 adultos y jóvenes (482 autistas y 558 con esquizofrenia); solo en el reconocimiento de emociones faciales hubo diferencias, mayores en participantes más jóvenes. Sus límites: pocos estudios, pruebas de laboratorio y un enfoque centrado en déficits que no refleja la diversidad de cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has had “social cognition” assessments, keep in mind that these tests do not separate autism and schizophrenia well, and they miss how the person actually understands others and communicates in their own way. Ask what each test measured and add what you notice in everyday life. This meta-analysis pooled 19 studies with 1,040 young people and adults (482 autistic, 558 with schizophrenia); the only clear difference was in recognising facial emotions, larger in younger participants. Its limits: few studies, laboratory tasks, and a deficit-focused framing that does not reflect each person’s diversity.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har gjort tester av ”social kognition”, kom ihåg att testerna inte skiljer autism från schizofreni särskilt väl, och att de missar hur personen faktiskt förstår andra och kommunicerar på sitt eget sätt. Fråga vad varje test mätte och lägg till det du ser i vardagen. Denna metaanalys samlade 19 studier med 1 040 unga och vuxna (482 autistiska, 558 med schizofreni); den enda tydliga skillnaden gällde att känna igen ansiktsuttryck, större bland yngre deltagare. Begränsningar: få studier, laboratorieuppgifter och ett bristfokuserat synsätt som inte speglar varje persons mångfald.

title: Immune Dysfunction and Autoimmunity as Pathological Mechanisms in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Hughes HK, Mills Ko E, Rose D, Ashwood P
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a group of heterogeneous neurological disorders that are highly variable and are clinically characterized by deficits in social interactions, communication, and stereotypical behaviors. Prevalence has risen from 1 in 10,000 in 1972 to 1 in 59 children in the United States in 2014. This rise in prevalence could be due in part to better diagnoses and awareness, however, these together cannot solely account for such a significant rise. While causative connections have not been proven in the majority of cases, many current studies focus on the combined effects of genetics and environment. Strikingly, a distinct picture of immune dysfunction has emerged and been supported by many independent studies over the past decade. Many players in the immune-ASD puzzle may be mechanistically contributing to pathogenesis of these disorders, including skewed cytokine responses, differences in total numbers and frequencies of immune cells and their subsets, neuroinflammation, and adaptive and innate immune dysfunction, as well as altered levels of immunoglobulin and the presence of autoantibodies which have been found in a substantial number of individuals with ASD. This review summarizes the latest research linking ASD, autoimmunity and immune dysfunction, and discusses evidence of a potential autoimmune component of ASD.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: si la persona autista que acompañas tiene infecciones frecuentes, alergias, problemas de piel o digestivos, o cambios bruscos cuando está enferma, vale la pena anotarlo y comentarlo con su médico, igual que con cualquier otra persona. Esta investigación no ofrece tratamientos ni pruebas para hacer en casa, y no conviene probar dietas o terapias 'inmunes' sin orientación profesional. La evidencia: es una revisión narrativa de 2018 que resume estudios que encontraron diferencias en el sistema inmunitario de algunas personas autistas. Límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas; los hallazgos varían mucho entre estudios y no describen a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: The practical point: if the autistic person you support has frequent infections, allergies, skin or digestive issues, or big changes when unwell, it is worth noting these and raising them with their doctor, as you would for anyone. This research does not offer treatments or home tests, and it is wise not to try 'immune' diets or therapies without professional guidance. The evidence: a 2018 narrative review summarising studies that found immune system differences in some autistic people. Limits: it shows associations, not causes; findings vary widely between studies and do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: om den autistiska person du stöttar ofta har infektioner, allergier, hud- eller magbesvär, eller förändras mycket vid sjukdom, kan det vara bra att anteckna detta och ta upp det med läkaren, precis som för vem som helst. Forskningen erbjuder inga behandlingar eller tester att göra hemma, och det är klokt att inte prova 'immun'-dieter eller terapier utan professionell vägledning. Evidensen: en översiktsartikel från 2018 som sammanfattar studier som funnit skillnader i immunsystemet hos vissa autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker; resultaten skiljer sig mycket mellan studier och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Fragile X-Associated Neuropsychiatric Disorders (FXAND).
authors: Hagerman RJ, Protic D, Rajaratnam A, Salcedo-Arellano MJ, Aydin EY, Schneider A
abstract: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is caused by the full mutation (>200 CGG repeats) in the Fragile X Mental Retardation 1 ( FMR1 ) gene. It is the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability (ID) and autism. This review focuses on neuropsychiatric disorders frequently experienced by premutation carriers with 55 to 200 CGG repeats and the pathophysiology involves elevated FMR1 mRNA levels, which is different from the absence or deficiency of fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP) seen in FXS. Neuropsychiatric disorders are the most common problems associated with the premutation, and they affect approximately 50% of individuals with 55 to 200 CGG repeats in the FMR1 gene. Neuropsychiatric disorders in children with the premutation include anxiety, ADHD, social deficits, or autism spectrum disorders (ASD). In adults with the premutation, anxiety and depression are the most common problems, although obsessive compulsive disorder, ADHD, and substance abuse are also common. These problems are often exacerbated by chronic fatigue, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, autoimmune disorders and sleep problems, which are also associated with the premutation. Here we review the clinical studies, neuropathology and molecular underpinnings of RNA toxicity associated with the premutation. We also propose the name Fragile X-associated Neuropsychiatric Disorders (FXAND) in an effort to promote research and the use of fragile X DNA testing to enhance recognition and treatment for these disorders.

sheet.es: Si en tu familia hay síndrome X frágil, las personas portadoras de la premutación (incluidos padres y madres) pueden vivir con más ansiedad, depresión, TDAH, cansancio crónico, dolor o problemas de sueño. Cuidar también tu propia salud no es egoísmo: comentar estos síntomas con tu médico y preguntar si una prueba genética de X frágil tiene sentido puede ayudar a obtener apoyo adecuado. En niños portadores, conviene estar atentos a la ansiedad y a necesidades sociales o de atención. Es una revisión narrativa de estudios clínicos y biológicos, no un ensayo nuevo. Sus cifras (alrededor del 50 % afectado) proceden de muestras a menudo clínicas, por lo que no describen a cada portador.
sheet.en: If fragile X runs in your family, people who carry the premutation (including parents) may experience more anxiety, depression, ADHD, chronic fatigue, pain or sleep problems. Looking after your own health is not selfish: mentioning these symptoms to your doctor and asking whether fragile X DNA testing makes sense can open doors to fitting support. For children who are carriers, it helps to watch gently for anxiety and for social or attention needs. This is a narrative review of clinical and biological studies, not a new trial. Its figures (about 50% affected) often come from clinic-based samples, so they do not describe every carrier.
sheet.sv: Om fragilt X finns i din familj kan personer som bär premutationen (även föräldrar) oftare uppleva ångest, depression, ADHD, kronisk trötthet, smärta eller sömnproblem. Att ta hand om din egen hälsa är inte själviskt: att nämna dessa symtom för din läkare och fråga om ett DNA-test för fragilt X är meningsfullt kan ge tillgång till passande stöd. Hos barn som är bärare kan det vara bra att vara lyhörd för oro och för sociala behov eller uppmärksamhetsbehov. Detta är en narrativ översikt av kliniska och biologiska studier, inte en ny studie. Siffrorna (cirka 50 % påverkade) kommer ofta från kliniska urval och beskriver därför inte varje bärare.

title: Assessing subtypes of restricted and repetitive behaviour using the Adult Repetitive Behaviour Questionnaire-2 in autistic adults.
authors: Barrett SL, Uljarević M, Jones CRG, Leekam SR
abstract: Background The majority of previous research into restricted and repetitive behaviours (RRBs) has focussed on children, partly due to a lack of suitable measures for RRBs in adults. This study aimed to explore the psychometric properties of the Adult Repetitive Behaviour Questionnaire-2 (RBQ-2A) in a large sample of autistic adults using a self-report questionnaire method. Methods The RBQ-2A and Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ) were administered online. Data from 275 autistic adults aged 18-66 ( M = 36.56, SD = 12.24; 100 men and 171 women) were analysed using polychoric principal components analysis (PCA). Reliability and validity were assessed using Cronbach's alpha and correlation analyses. Results PCA resulted in two components of the RBQ-2A, interpretable as repetitive sensory and motor behaviours (RSMB) and insistence on sameness (IS). Both components showed acceptable internal consistency ( α = .70 and .81 respectively) and were significantly moderately correlated with scores on the AQ ( r s = .25 and .42). Participants' scores on IS were higher than their scores on RSMB. RSMB, but not IS, was negatively associated with age, particularly in older adults (≥ 50 years). There were no gender differences. Conclusions The RBQ-2A is a reliable and valid self-report measure of RRBs in the present sample of autistic adults. As one of the few measures of RRBs aimed at adults, it is suitable for adults with the ability to read and complete a self-report questionnaire. Results build on previous work with children using the Repetitive Behaviour Questionnaire-2 (RBQ-2).

sheet.es: Las conductas repetitivas en personas autistas adultas suelen agruparse en dos tipos: movimientos y búsquedas sensoriales (balancearse, tocar texturas) y la preferencia por la rutina y lo previsible. Si acompañas a un adulto autista, puede ayudar preguntarle cuál de las dos le importa más hoy: muchas personas valoran especialmente la previsibilidad, así que avisar de cambios con tiempo puede ser un buen punto de partida. Evidencia: un estudio con cuestionario en línea respondido por 275 adultos autistas de 18 a 66 años mostró que este cuestionario (RBQ-2A) es fiable. Límites: solo participaron personas que podían leer y responder solas, y las respuestas eran autoinformadas.
sheet.en: Repetitive behaviours in autistic adults often fall into two kinds: sensory and motor actions (rocking, touching textures) and a preference for sameness and predictability. If you support an autistic adult, it can help to ask which matters more to them right now; many people value predictability especially, so giving early notice of changes may be a good starting point. Evidence: an online questionnaire study with 275 autistic adults aged 18 to 66 found this questionnaire (RBQ-2A) reliable. Limits: only people able to read and answer on their own took part, and all answers were self-reported.
sheet.sv: Repetitiva beteenden hos autistiska vuxna delar ofta upp sig i två slag: sensoriska och motoriska handlingar (gunga, känna på texturer) och en önskan om förutsägbarhet och att saker förblir lika. Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att fråga vad som är viktigast för personen just nu; många värdesätter särskilt förutsägbarhet, så att förvarna om förändringar i god tid kan vara en bra början. Evidens: en webbenkätstudie med 275 autistiska vuxna mellan 18 och 66 år visade att formuläret (RBQ-2A) är tillförlitligt. Begränsningar: bara personer som kunde läsa och svara själva deltog, och alla svar var självrapporterade.

title: Testing the Empathizing-Systemizing theory of sex differences and the Extreme Male Brain theory of autism in half a million people.
authors: Greenberg DM, Warrier V, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstract: The Empathizing-Systemizing (E-S) theory of typical sex differences suggests that individuals may be classified based on empathy and systemizing. An extension of the E-S theory, the Extreme Male Brain (EMB) theory suggests that autistic people on average have a shift towards a more masculinized brain along the E-S dimensions. Both theories have been investigated in small sample sizes, limiting their generalizability. Here we leverage two large datasets (discovery n = 671,606, including 36,648 autistic individuals primarily; and validation n = 14,354, including 226 autistic individuals) to investigate 10 predictions of the E-S and the EMB theories. In the discovery dataset, typical females on average showed higher scores on short forms of the Empathy Quotient (EQ) and Sensory Perception Quotient (SPQ), and typical males on average showed higher scores on short forms of the Autism Spectrum Quotient (AQ) and Systemizing Quotient (SQ). Typical sex differences in these measures were attenuated in autistic individuals. Analysis of "brain types" revealed that typical females on average were more likely to be Type E (EQ > SQ) or Extreme Type E and that typical males on average were more likely to be Type S (SQ > EQ) or Extreme Type S. In both datasets, autistic individuals, regardless of their reported sex, on average were "masculinized." Finally, we demonstrate that D-scores (difference between EQ and SQ) account for 19 times more of the variance in autistic traits (43%) than do other demographic variables including sex. Our results provide robust evidence in support of both the E-S and EMB theories.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: las puntuaciones medias de grandes grupos no describen a tu hijo, hija o familiar. Muchas personas autistas, de cualquier sexo, disfrutan de patrones, sistemas y reglas; apoyarse en esos intereses puede facilitar el aprendizaje y la calma.
