Esto no significa falta de afecto ni de cuidado por los demás: pregunta y observa cómo cada persona muestra su empatía. Evidencia: estudio con cuestionarios en línea de más de medio millón de personas, incluidas unas 37.000 autistas. Límites: son autoinformes voluntarios, sin diagnóstico verificado, y las etiquetas «cerebro masculino» o «empatía» son teorías discutidas que simplifican diferencias individuales muy amplias.
sheet.en: The practical point: averages from huge groups don't describe your child or family member. Many autistic people, of any sex, enjoy patterns, systems and rules; building on those interests can support learning and calm. This does not mean a lack of warmth or care for others: ask and notice how each person shows empathy in their own way. Evidence: an online questionnaire study of over half a million people, including about 37,000 autistic people. Limits: answers were voluntary self-reports without verified diagnoses, and labels like 'male brain' or 'empathy type' are debated theories that oversimplify wide individual differences.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: medelvärden från stora grupper beskriver inte ditt barn eller din närstående. Många autistiska personer, oavsett kön, uppskattar mönster, system och regler; att bygga vidare på de intressena kan underlätta lärande och lugn. Det betyder inte brist på värme eller omtanke om andra: fråga och lägg märke till hur varje person visar empati på sitt eget sätt. Evidens: en enkätstudie på nätet med över en halv miljon deltagare, varav cirka 37 000 autistiska. Begränsningar: svaren var frivilliga självskattningar utan bekräftade diagnoser, och etiketter som ”manlig hjärna” eller ”empatityp” är omdiskuterade teorier som förenklar stora individuella skillnader.

title: Synaptopathology Involved in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Guang S, Pang N, Deng X, Yang L, He F, Wu L, Chen C, Yin F, Peng J
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) encompasses a group of multifactorial neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by impaired social communication, social interaction and repetitive behaviors. ASD affects 1 in 59 children, and is about 4 times more common among boys than among girls. Strong genetic components, together with environmental factors in the early stage of development, contribute to the pathogenesis of ASD. Multiple studies have revealed that mutations in genes like NRXN, NLGN , SHANK , TSC1/2 , FMR1 , and MECP2 converge on common cellular pathways that intersect at synapses. These genes encode cell adhesion molecules, scaffolding proteins and proteins involved in synaptic transcription, protein synthesis and degradation, affecting various aspects of synapses including synapse formation and elimination, synaptic transmission and plasticity. This suggests that the pathogenesis of ASD may, at least in part, be attributed to synaptic dysfunction. In this article, we will review major genes and signaling pathways implicated in synaptic abnormalities underlying ASD, and discuss molecular, cellular and functional studies of ASD experimental models.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada concreto en el día a día: esta revisión trata de biología básica, no de apoyos ni tratamientos. Puede ayudar saber que el autismo tiene raíces genéticas y del desarrollo temprano, y que no es causado por la crianza. Si su familia tiene preguntas sobre genética, puede hablarlo con un profesional de genética clínica. Evidencia: es una revisión narrativa que resume estudios sobre genes como SHANK, NLGN o FMR1 y su papel en las sinapsis, sobre todo en modelos de laboratorio y animales. Límites: no incluye participantes humanos propios, usa un lenguaje centrado en el déficit y sus hallazgos no describen a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change in your routine tomorrow: this review is about basic biology, not about supports or treatments. It may help to know that autism has genetic and early-developmental roots and is not caused by parenting. If your family has questions about genetics, a clinical genetics professional can talk them through with you. Evidence: this is a narrative review summarising research on genes such as SHANK, NLGN and FMR1 and how they affect synapses, mostly from laboratory and animal models. Limits: it includes no new human participants, uses deficit-focused language, and its findings do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I morgon behöver inget i vardagen ändras: denna översikt handlar om grundläggande biologi, inte om stöd eller behandling. Det kan vara bra att veta att autism har genetiska rötter och rötter i tidig utveckling, och att det inte orsakas av föräldraskap. Om familjen har frågor om genetik kan en klinisk genetiker hjälpa er att reda ut dem. Evidens: en berättande översikt som sammanfattar forskning om gener som SHANK, NLGN och FMR1 och hur de påverkar synapser, främst från laboratorie- och djurmodeller. Begränsningar: inga egna mänskliga deltagare, ett bristfokuserat språk, och resultaten beskriver inte varje autistisk person.

title: Investigating alexithymia in autism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kinnaird E, Stewart C, Tchanturia K
journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
abstract: Background New research suggests that, rather than representing a core feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), emotional processing difficulties reflect co-occurring alexithymia. Autistic individuals with alexithymia could therefore represent a specific subgroup of autism who may benefit from tailored interventions. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to explore the nature and prevalence of alexithymia in autism using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS). Methods Online scientific databases were searched systematically for studies on ASD popu lations using the TAS. Meta-analyses were performed to evaluate differences in scores between the ASD and neurotypical groups, and to determine the prevalence of alexithymia in these populations. Results 15 articles comparing autistic and neurotypical (NT) groups were identified. Autistic people scored significantly higher on all scores compared to the NT group. There was also a higher prevalence of alexithymia in the ASD group (49.93% compared to 4.89%), with a significantly increased risk of alexithymia in autistic participants. Conclusions This review highlights that alexithymia is common, rather than universal, in ASD, supporting a growing body of evidence that co-occurring autism and alexithymia represents a specific subgroup in the ASD population that may have specific clinical needs. More research is needed to understand the nature and implications of co-occurring ASD and alexithymia.

sheet.es: Si a tu familiar autista le cuesta nombrar lo que siente, no lo des por hecho en todas las personas autistas: puede ser alexitimia, una dificultad para identificar y describir emociones que aparece en aproximadamente la mitad, no en todas. Mañana puedes probar apoyos sencillos: preguntar por sensaciones del cuerpo («¿tienes calor, tensión, hambre?»), usar escalas visuales o dar tiempo sin presionar por una palabra exacta. Este metaanálisis reunió 15 estudios que compararon a personas autistas y no autistas con un cuestionario (TAS); la alexitimia fue mucho más frecuente en el grupo autista (50 % frente a 5 %). Límites: se basa en autoinformes, que pueden ser difíciles justamente para quien tiene alexitimia, y no prueba qué apoyos funcionan.
sheet.en: If your autistic family member finds it hard to name what they feel, don't assume this is true of every autistic person: it may be alexithymia, difficulty identifying and describing emotions, which affects about half of autistic people, not all. Tomorrow you could try simple supports: ask about body signals ("are you hot, tense, hungry?"), use visual scales, or allow time without pushing for the exact word. This meta-analysis combined 15 studies comparing autistic and non-autistic adults using a questionnaire (TAS); alexithymia was far more common in the autistic group (50% vs 5%). Limits: it relies on self-report, which can be hard precisely for people with alexithymia, and it doesn't test which supports help.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska närstående har svårt att sätta ord på känslor, utgå inte från att det gäller alla autistiska personer: det kan vara alexitymi, svårigheter att identifiera och beskriva känslor, som finns hos ungefär hälften, inte alla. I morgon kan du pröva enkelt stöd: fråga om kroppssignaler (”är du varm, spänd, hungrig?”), använd visuella skalor eller ge tid utan krav på exakt rätt ord. Denna metaanalys sammanställde 15 studier som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska personer med ett frågeformulär (TAS); alexitymi var mycket vanligare i den autistiska gruppen (50 % mot 5 %). Begränsningar: den bygger på självskattning, som kan vara svår just vid alexitymi, och visar inte vilket stöd som fungerar.

title: Overlaps and distinctions between attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder in young adulthood: Systematic review and guiding framework for EEG-imaging research.
authors: Lau-Zhu A, Fritz A, McLoughlin G
abstract: Attention deficit/hyperactivity disorders (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorders (ASD) frequently co-occur. However, we know little about the neural basis of the overlaps and distinctions between these disorders, particularly in young adulthood - a critical time window for brain plasticity across executive and socioemotional domains. Here, we systematically review 75 articles investigating ADHD and ASD in young adult samples (mean ages 16-26) using cognitive tasks, with neural activity concurrently measured via electroencephalography (EEG) - the most accessible neuroimaging technology. The majority of studies focused on event-related potentials (ERPs), with some beginning to capitalise on oscillatory approaches. Overlapping and specific profiles for ASD and ADHD were found mainly for four neurocognitive domains: attention processing, performance monitoring, face processing and sensory processing. No studies in this age group directly compared both disorders or considered dual diagnosis with both disorders. Moving forward, understanding of ADHD, ASD and their overlap in young adulthood would benefit from an increased focus on cross-disorder comparisons, using similar paradigms and in well-powered samples and longitudinal cohorts.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija adulto joven es autista y también tiene TDAH, o se pregunta por ambos, es razonable observar juntos cuatro áreas: atención, cómo detecta y corrige errores, cómo procesa caras y cómo vive los estímulos sensoriales. Anotar qué le ayuda en cada una puede orientar apoyos concretos, como pausas, menos ruido o instrucciones claras. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 75 estudios con EEG en personas de 16 a 26 años y encontró rasgos compartidos y distintos en esas áreas. Su límite: ningún estudio comparó directamente autismo y TDAH ni incluyó a personas con ambos, así que no sirve para diagnosticar ni aplica igual a todos.
sheet.en: If your young adult is autistic and also has ADHD, or wonders about both, it can help to look together at four areas: attention, noticing and correcting mistakes, processing faces, and sensory experiences. Noting what helps in each can guide concrete supports, such as breaks, less noise or clear instructions. This systematic review gathered 75 EEG studies of people aged 16 to 26 and found both shared and distinct patterns in these areas. Its limit: no study directly compared autism and ADHD or included people with both, so it cannot be used for diagnosis and does not apply the same way to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om din unga vuxna är autistisk och också har ADHD, eller undrar över båda, kan det hjälpa att tillsammans titta på fyra områden: uppmärksamhet, att märka och rätta misstag, att uppfatta ansikten och sinnesintryck. Att anteckna vad som hjälper inom varje område kan leda till konkret stöd, som pauser, mindre ljud eller tydliga instruktioner. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 75 EEG-studier med personer mellan 16 och 26 år och fann både gemensamma och olika mönster inom dessa områden. Begränsning: ingen studie jämförde autism och ADHD direkt eller inkluderade personer med båda, så den kan inte användas för diagnos och gäller inte lika för alla.

title: EEG Frequency Bands in Psychiatric Disorders: A Review of Resting State Studies.
authors: Newson JJ, Thiagarajan TC
abstract: A significant proportion of the electroencephalography (EEG) literature focuses on differences in historically pre-defined frequency bands in the power spectrum that are typically referred to as alpha, beta, gamma, theta and delta waves. Here, we review 184 EEG studies that report differences in frequency bands in the resting state condition (eyes open and closed) across a spectrum of psychiatric disorders including depression, attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism, addiction, bipolar disorder, anxiety, panic disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) and schizophrenia to determine patterns across disorders. Aggregating across all reported results we demonstrate that characteristic patterns of power change within specific frequency bands are not necessarily unique to any one disorder but show substantial overlap across disorders as well as variability within disorders. In particular, we show that the most dominant pattern of change, across several disorder types including ADHD, schizophrenia and OCD, is power increases across lower frequencies (delta and theta) and decreases across higher frequencies (alpha, beta and gamma). However, a considerable number of disorders, such as PTSD, addiction and autism show no dominant trend for spectral change in any direction. We report consistency and validation scores across the disorders and conditions showing that the dominant result across all disorders is typically only 2.2 times as likely to occur in the literature as alternate results, and typically with less than 250 study participants when summed across all studies reporting this result. Furthermore, the magnitudes of the results were infrequently reported and were typically small at between 20% and 30% and correlated weakly with symptom severity scores. Finally, we discuss the many methodological challenges and limitations relating to such frequency band analysis across the literature. These results caution any interpretation of results from studies that consider only one disorder in isolation, and for the overall potential of this approach for delivering valuable insights in the field of mental health.

sheet.es: Si alguien le ofrece un EEG en reposo (las «ondas cerebrales») como forma de confirmar el autismo o de elegir un tratamiento, puede tomarlo con cautela y preguntar qué evidencia lo respalda. Esta revisión no encontró un patrón de ondas típico del autismo: los resultados iban en direcciones distintas y se solapaban con otras condiciones. Lo que mejor orienta sigue siendo observar a la persona, escucharla y conocer sus necesidades. Se trata de una revisión de 184 estudios de EEG en reposo sobre autismo, TDAH, depresión y otras condiciones. Como límite, los estudios usaban métodos muy diferentes, tenían pocos participantes y rara vez informaban del tamaño de las diferencias.
sheet.en: If someone offers a resting EEG ("brain waves") as a way to confirm autism or to choose a treatment, you can be cautious and ask what evidence supports it. This review found no typical brain-wave pattern for autism: results pointed in different directions and overlapped with other conditions. Observing the person, listening to them and understanding their needs remain the best guides. The evidence is a review of 184 resting-state EEG studies covering autism, ADHD, depression and other conditions. As for limits, the studies used very different methods, had few participants and rarely reported how large the differences were.
sheet.sv: Om någon erbjuder ett vilo-EEG (”hjärnvågor”) för att bekräfta autism eller välja ett stöd, kan du vara försiktig och fråga vilken evidens som finns. Den här översikten hittade inget typiskt hjärnvågsmönster för autism: resultaten pekade åt olika håll och överlappade med andra tillstånd. Att iaktta personen, lyssna på hen och förstå hens behov är fortfarande den bästa vägledningen. Underlaget är en översikt av 184 vilo-EEG-studier om autism, ADHD, depression och andra tillstånd. En begränsning är att studierna använde mycket olika metoder, hade få deltagare och sällan redovisade hur stora skillnaderna var.

title: Altered composition and function of intestinal microbiota in autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Liu F, Li J, Wu F, Zheng H, Peng Q, Zhou H
abstract: At present, the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remains unclear. Increasing evidence suggested that gut microbiota plays a critical role in gastrointestinal symptoms and behavioral impairment in ASD patients. The primary aim of this systematic review is to investigate potential evidence for the characteristic dysbiosis of gut microbiota in ASD patients compared with healthy controls (HCs). The MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science and Scopus were systematically searched before March 2018. Human studies that compared the composition of gut microbiota in ASD patients and HCs using culture-independent techniques were included. Independent data extraction and quality assessment of studies were conducted according to PRISMA statement and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States (PICRUSt) was used to infer biological functional changes of the shifted microbiota with the available data in four studies. Sixteen studies with a total sample size of 381 ASD patients and 283 HCs were included in this systematic review. The quality of the studies was evaluated as medium to high. The overall changing of gut bacterial community in terms of β-diversity was consistently observed in ASD patients compared with HCs. Furthermore, Bifidobacterium, Blautia, Dialister, Prevotella, Veillonella, and Turicibacter were consistently decreased, while Lactobacillus, Bacteroides, Desulfovibrio, and Clostridium were increased in patients with ASD relative to HCs in certain studies. This systematic review demonstrated significant alterations of gut microbiota in ASD patients compared with HCs, strengthen the evidence that dysbiosis of gut microbiota may correlate with behavioral abnormality in ASD patients. However, results of inconsistent changing also existed and further big-sampled well-designed studies are needed. Generally, as a potential mediator of risk factors, the gut microbiota could be a novel target for ASD patients in the future.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene molestias digestivas como dolor, estreñimiento o diarrea, merece la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su pediatra o médico de cabecera: son reales y tratables. Esta revisión sugiere que la flora intestinal de muchas personas autistas es distinta, pero no indica ninguna dieta, suplemento ni tratamiento concreto. Desconfía de productos que prometan «curar» el autismo por el intestino. Evidencia: revisión sistemática de 16 estudios con 381 personas autistas y 283 no autistas. Límites: muestras pequeñas, resultados a veces contradictorios y diseños que muestran asociación, no causa; cada persona es diferente.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has digestive discomfort such as pain, constipation or diarrhoea, it is worth noting it down and raising it with their doctor: these problems are real and treatable. This review suggests gut bacteria often differ in autistic people, but it does not point to any specific diet, supplement or treatment. Be wary of products promising to "fix" autism through the gut. Evidence: a systematic review of 16 studies including 381 autistic and 283 non-autistic people. Limits: small samples, some inconsistent findings, and designs that show association, not cause; every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har magbesvär som smärta, förstoppning eller diarré är det värt att anteckna dem och ta upp dem med barnets läkare: besvären är verkliga och går att behandla. Översikten tyder på att tarmbakterierna ofta skiljer sig hos autistiska personer, men den pekar inte ut någon särskild kost, något kosttillskott eller någon behandling. Var försiktig med produkter som lovar att ”bota” autism via magen. Evidens: en systematisk översikt av 16 studier med 381 autistiska och 283 icke-autistiska personer. Begränsningar: små urval, delvis motstridiga resultat och studier som visar samband, inte orsak; varje person är olik.

title: Genetics and epigenetics of autism spectrum disorder-current evidence in the field.
authors: Wiśniowiecka-Kowalnik B, Nowakowska BA
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is a heterogenous group of neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by problems in social interaction and communication as well as the presence of repetitive and stereotyped behavior. It is estimated that the prevalence of ASD is 1-2% in the general population with the average male to female ratio 4-5:1. Although the causes of ASD remain largely unknown, the studies have shown that both genetic and environmental factors play an important role in the etiology of these disorders. Array comparative genomic hybridization and whole exome/genome sequencing studies identified common and rare copy number or single nucleotide variants in genes encoding proteins involved in brain development, which play an important role in neuron and synapse formation and function. The genetic etiology is recognized in ~ 25-35% of patients with ASD. In this article, we review the current state of knowledge about the genetic etiology of ASD and also propose a diagnostic algorithm for patients.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija es autista, saber que la genética influye mucho puede aliviar la culpa: el autismo no lo causa la crianza. Si la familia lo desea, se puede preguntar al equipo médico si una consulta genética tiene sentido en vuestro caso, por ejemplo cuando hay otras condiciones de salud o planes familiares. El resultado no cambia quién es la persona ni sus apoyos diarios. Esta es una revisión de 2019 que resume estudios genéticos previos y propone un algoritmo diagnóstico, sin participantes propios. Su límite: solo en un 25-35% se identifica una causa genética, y usa un lenguaje centrado en el déficit.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic, knowing that genetics plays a large role can ease guilt: autism is not caused by parenting. If your family wishes, you can ask your care team whether a genetic consultation makes sense for you, for example when there are other health conditions or family planning questions. A result does not change who the person is or the everyday support they need. This is a 2019 review summarising earlier genetic studies and proposing a diagnostic algorithm, with no participants of its own. Its limit: a genetic cause is found in only about 25-35% of people, and it uses deficit-focused language.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt kan det lätta på skulden att veta att genetik spelar stor roll: autism orsakas inte av föräldraskap. Om familjen vill kan ni fråga vården om en genetisk utredning är meningsfull för er, till exempel vid andra hälsotillstånd eller frågor om familjeplanering. Ett resultat ändrar inte vem personen är eller vilket vardagsstöd hen behöver. Detta är en översikt från 2019 som sammanfattar tidigare genetiska studier och föreslår en diagnostisk algoritm, utan egna deltagare. Begränsning: en genetisk orsak hittas bara hos cirka 25-35 %, och texten använder ett bristfokuserat språk.

title: Telehealth as a Model for Providing Behaviour Analytic Interventions to Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ferguson J, Ferguson J, Craig EA, Dounavi K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Interventions based on applied behaviour analysis are considered evidence based practice for autism spectrum disorders. Due to the shortage of highly qualified professionals required for their delivery, innovative models should be explored, such as telehealth. Telehealth utilises technology for remote training and supervision. The purpose of our study was to systematically review the literature researching telehealth and ABA. We analysed intervention characteristics, outcomes and research quality in 28 studies and identified gaps. Intervention characteristics were: (1) research design (2) participants (3) technology (4) dependent variables (5) aims. Outcomes were favourable with all studies reporting improvements in at least one variable. Quality ratings were significantly low. Implications for future research and practice are discussed in light of identified methodological downfalls.

sheet.es: Si vives lejos de especialistas, el apoyo por videollamada puede ser una opción real: un profesional puede formarte y acompañarte a distancia mientras tú practicas estrategias en casa con tu hijo o hija autista. Conviene preguntar qué objetivos se trabajarán, cómo se respetará el bienestar y los intereses de tu hijo, y cómo se revisará si algo no encaja. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 28 estudios sobre intervenciones basadas en análisis de conducta ofrecidas por telesalud; todos informaron mejoras en al menos un aspecto, a menudo en las habilidades de familiares o docentes. Sin embargo, la calidad de los estudios fue baja, con muestras pequeñas, así que los resultados no garantizan lo mismo para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you live far from specialists, video-based support can be a real option: a professional can coach and guide you remotely while you practise strategies at home with your autistic child. It helps to ask which goals will be worked on, how your child's wellbeing and interests will be respected, and how you will review things if something doesn't fit. This systematic review looked at 28 studies of behaviour analytic interventions delivered through telehealth; every study reported improvement in at least one area, often in the skills of parents or teachers. However, study quality was rated low, with small samples, so the results cannot promise the same outcome for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du bor långt från specialister kan stöd via videosamtal vara ett verkligt alternativ: en yrkesperson kan handleda dig på distans medan du övar strategier hemma med ditt autistiska barn. Det är bra att fråga vilka mål som ska arbetas med, hur barnets välmående och intressen respekteras och hur ni utvärderar om något inte passar. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 28 studier om beteendeanalytiska insatser via distansvård; alla rapporterade förbättring inom minst ett område, ofta i föräldrars eller lärares färdigheter. Studiernas kvalitet bedömdes dock som låg, med små urval, så resultaten kan inte lova samma effekt för varje person.

title: Development and Validation of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q).
authors: Hull L, Mandy W, Lai MC, Baron-Cohen S, Allison C, Smith P, Petrides KV
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: There currently exist no self-report measures of social camouflaging behaviours (strategies used to compensate for or mask autistic characteristics during social interactions). The Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q) was developed from autistic adults' experiences of camouflaging, and was administered online to 354 autistic and 478 non-autistic adults. Exploratory factor analysis suggested three factors, comprising of 25 items in total. Good model fit was demonstrated through confirmatory factor analysis, with measurement invariance analyses demonstrating equivalent factor structures across gender and diagnostic group. Internal consistency (α = 0.94) and preliminary test-retest reliability (r = 0.77) were acceptable. Convergent validity was demonstrated through comparison with measures of autistic traits, wellbeing, anxiety, and depression. The present study provides robust psychometric support for the CAT-Q.

sheet.es: Si tu familiar autista parece «estar bien» en público pero llega agotado a casa, puede estar camuflando: ocultando o compensando rasgos autistas para encajar. Vale la pena hablarlo con calma, ofrecer tiempo de recuperación sin exigencias y espacios donde no tenga que fingir. El CAT-Q es un cuestionario de 25 preguntas que puede ayudar a poner palabras a esa experiencia. Evidencia: estudio en línea con 354 adultos autistas y 478 no autistas; el cuestionario mostró buena fiabilidad y se relacionó con ansiedad, depresión y bienestar. Límites: solo adultos que respondieron en internet sobre sí mismos; no sirve para diagnosticar ni describe a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic family member seems fine in public but comes home exhausted, they may be camouflaging: hiding or compensating for autistic traits to fit in. It can help to talk about it gently, offer recovery time without demands, and create spaces where they don't have to perform. The CAT-Q, a 25-item questionnaire, can help put words to this experience. Evidence: an online study with 354 autistic and 478 non-autistic adults; the questionnaire showed good reliability and was linked to anxiety, depression and wellbeing. Limits: only adults self-reporting online; it is not a diagnostic tool and does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska närstående verkar må bra bland andra men kommer hem helt slut kan hen kamouflera: dölja eller kompensera autistiska drag för att passa in. Det kan hjälpa att prata lugnt om det, erbjuda återhämtning utan krav och skapa platser där hen inte behöver spela en roll. CAT-Q, ett frågeformulär med 25 frågor, kan hjälpa till att sätta ord på upplevelsen. Evidens: en webbstudie med 354 autistiska och 478 icke-autistiska vuxna; formuläret visade god tillförlitlighet och hängde ihop med ångest, depression och välmående. Begränsningar: bara vuxna som själva svarade på nätet; det är inget diagnosverktyg och beskriver inte alla.

title: Selection bias on intellectual ability in autism research: a cross-sectional review and meta-analysis.
authors: Russell G, Mandy W, Elliott D, White R, Pittwood T, Ford T
abstract: Background Current global estimates suggest the proportion of the population with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who have intellectual disability (ID) is approximately 50%. Our objective was to ascertain the existence of selection bias due to under-inclusion of populations with ID across all fields of autism research. A sub-goal was to evaluate inconsistencies in reporting of findings. Methods This review covers all original research published in 2016 in autism-specific journals with an impact factor greater than 3. Across 301 included studies, 100,245 participants had ASD. A random effects meta-analysis was used to estimate the proportion of participants without ID. Selection bias was defined as where more than 75% of participants did not have ID. Results Meta-analysis estimated 94% of all participants identified as being on the autism spectrum in the studies reviewed did not have ID (95% CI 0.91-0.97). Eight out of ten studies demonstrated selection bias against participants with ID. The reporting of participant characteristics was generally poor: information about participants' intellectual ability was absent in 38% of studies ( n = 114). Where there was selection bias on ID, only 31% of studies mentioned lack of generalisability as a limitation. Conclusions We found selection bias against ID throughout all fields of autism research. We recommend transparent reporting about ID and strategies for inclusion for this much marginalised group.

sheet.es: Cuando lea un estudio sobre autismo, compruebe si incluyó a personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual. Si su hijo o la persona que acompaña tiene discapacidad intelectual, los resultados pueden no aplicarse a ella; pregunte a los profesionales en qué evidencia se basan sus consejos y confíe también en lo que usted observa a diario. Este metaanálisis revisó 301 estudios publicados en 2016 con más de 100.000 participantes autistas: el 94% no tenía discapacidad intelectual, aunque se estima que alrededor de la mitad de las personas autistas sí la tiene. Su límite: solo analizó un año y revistas especializadas de alto impacto, y muchos estudios no informaban sobre la capacidad intelectual.
sheet.en: When you read autism research, check whether autistic people with intellectual disability were included. If your child or the person you support has intellectual disability, the findings may not apply to them; ask professionals what evidence their advice rests on, and trust what you observe every day too. This meta-analysis reviewed 301 studies published in 2016, with over 100,000 autistic participants: 94% did not have intellectual disability, although about half of autistic people are estimated to have it. Its limit: it covered only one year and high-impact autism journals, and many studies did not report intellectual ability at all.
sheet.sv: När du läser autismforskning, kontrollera om autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning var med. Om ditt barn eller personen du stöttar har intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kanske resultaten inte gäller henne eller honom; fråga yrkespersoner vilken evidens deras råd bygger på, och lita också på det du ser i vardagen. Denna metaanalys granskade 301 studier publicerade 2016 med över 100 000 autistiska deltagare: 94 % hade ingen intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, trots att ungefär hälften av autistiska personer uppskattas ha det. Begränsning: den omfattade bara ett år och tidskrifter med hög genomslagskraft, och många studier rapporterade inte intellektuell förmåga alls.

title: Resting-state abnormalities in Autism Spectrum Disorders: A meta-analysis.
authors: Lau WKW, Leung MK, Lau BWM
abstract: The gold standard for clinical assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) relies on assessing behavior via semi-structured play-based interviews and parent interviews. Although these methods show good sensitivity and specificity in diagnosing ASD cases, behavioral assessments alone may hinder the identification of asymptomatic at-risk group. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) could be an appropriate approach to produce objective neural markers to supplement behavioral assessments due to its non-invasive and task-free nature. Previous neuroimaging studies reported inconsistent resting-state abnormalities in ASD, which may be explained by small sample sizes and phenotypic heterogeneity in ASD subjects, and/or the use of different analytical methods across studies. The current study aims to investigate the local resting-state abnormalities of ASD regardless of subject age, IQ, gender, disease severity and methodological differences, using activation likelihood estimation (ALE). MEDLINE/PubMed databases were searched for whole-brain rs-fMRI studies on ASD published until Feb 2018. Eight experiments involving 424 subjects were included in the ALE meta-analysis. We demonstrate two ASD-related resting-state findings: local underconnectivity in the dorsal posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) and in the right medial paracentral lobule. This study contributes to uncovering a consistent pattern of resting-state local abnormalities that may serve as potential neurobiological markers for ASD.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en la práctica: el diagnóstico y el apoyo siguen basándose en conocer a la persona, sus necesidades y sus fortalezas, no en escáneres cerebrales. Este estudio busca diferencias en la actividad cerebral en reposo que algún día podrían complementar la evaluación, pero hoy no es una prueba disponible ni dice nada sobre cómo apoyar a tu familiar. Es un metaanálisis de ocho estudios de resonancia magnética con 424 participantes, que encontró menor conectividad local en dos zonas del cerebro. Sus límites: pocos estudios, muestras pequeñas y variadas, y diferencias de grupo que no describen a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: Nothing changes in practice tomorrow: diagnosis and support still rest on knowing the person, their needs and strengths, not on brain scans. This study looks for differences in resting brain activity that might one day add to assessment, but it is not an available test today and says nothing about how to support your family member. It is a meta-analysis of eight brain-imaging (MRI) studies with 424 participants, finding lower local connectivity in two brain areas. Its limits: few studies, small and varied samples, and group-level differences that do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I praktiken ändras ingenting i morgon: utredning och stöd bygger fortfarande på att känna personen, hennes behov och styrkor, inte på hjärnröntgen. Studien letar efter skillnader i hjärnans viloaktivitet som kanske en dag kan komplettera bedömningar, men det är inget test som finns i dag och säger inget om hur du stöttar din närstående. Det är en metaanalys av åtta hjärnavbildningsstudier (MR) med 424 deltagare, som fann lägre lokal konnektivitet i två hjärnområden. Begränsningar: få studier, små och varierade urval, och skillnader på gruppnivå som inte beskriver varje autistisk person.

title: Risk and Protective Environmental Factors Associated with Autism Spectrum Disorder: Evidence-Based Principles and Recommendations.
authors: Emberti Gialloreti L, Mazzone L, Benvenuto A, Fasano A, Alcon AG, Kraneveld A, Moavero R, Raz R, Riccio MP, Siracusano M, Zachor DA, Marini M, Curatolo P
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex condition with early childhood onset, characterized by a set of common behavioral features. The etiology of ASD is not yet fully understood; however, it reflects the interaction between genetics and environment. While genetics is now a well-established risk factor, several data support a contribution of the environment as well. This paper summarizes the conclusions of a consensus conference focused on the potential pathogenetic role of environmental factors and on their interactions with genetics. Several environmental factors have been discussed in terms of ASD risk, namely advanced parental age, assisted reproductive technologies, nutritional factors, maternal infections and diseases, environmental chemicals and toxicants, and medications, as well as some other conditions. The analysis focused on their specific impact on three biologically relevant time windows for brain development: the periconception, prenatal, and early postnatal periods. Possible protective factors that might prevent or modify an ASD trajectory have been explored as well. Recommendations for clinicians to reduce ASD risk or its severity have been proposed. Developments in molecular biology and big data approaches, which are able to assess a large number of coexisting factors, are offering new opportunities to disentangle the gene⁻environment interplay that can lead to the development of ASD.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si algo que hiciste causó el autismo de tu hijo o hija, esta revisión te ofrece calma: el autismo surge de una interacción compleja entre genética y entorno, y ningún factor aislado lo explica. No hace falta buscar culpables; lo útil mañana es centrarse en apoyar a tu hijo tal como es. Se trata de una revisión que resume las conclusiones de una conferencia de consenso de expertos sobre factores como la edad parental, infecciones, nutrición o sustancias químicas durante el embarazo y la primera infancia. Su límite: se basa en estudios de asociación, no demuestra causas y sus recomendaciones se dirigen a profesionales clínicos, no a familias individuales.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether something you did caused your child's autism, this review offers reassurance: autism arises from a complex interplay of genetics and environment, and no single factor explains it. There is no need to search for blame; what helps tomorrow is focusing on supporting your child as they are. This is a review summarising a expert consensus conference on factors such as parental age, infections, nutrition and chemicals around pregnancy and early childhood. Its limit: it relies on association studies, does not prove causes, and its recommendations are aimed at clinicians, not at individual families.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om något du gjorde orsakade ditt barns autism ger den här översikten lugn: autism uppstår ur ett komplext samspel mellan gener och miljö, och ingen enskild faktor förklarar den. Du behöver inte leta efter skuld; det som hjälper i morgon är att stötta ditt barn som det är. Detta är en översikt som sammanfattar en konsensuskonferens med experter om faktorer som föräldrars ålder, infektioner, näring och kemikalier kring graviditet och tidig barndom. Begränsning: den bygger på sambandsstudier, bevisar inte orsaker, och rekommendationerna riktar sig till vårdpersonal, inte till enskilda familjer.

title: The contribution of environmental exposure to the etiology of autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Bölte S, Girdler S, Marschik PB
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition of heterogeneous etiology. While it is widely recognized that genetic and environmental factors and their interactions contribute to autism phenotypes, their precise causal mechanisms remain poorly understood. This article reviews our current understanding of environmental risk factors of ASD and their presumed adverse physiological mechanisms. It comprehensively maps the significance of parental age, teratogenic compounds, perinatal risks, medication, smoking and alcohol use, nutrition, vaccination, toxic exposures, as well as the role of extreme psychosocial factors. Further, we consider the role of potential protective factors such as folate and fatty acid intake. Evidence indicates an increased offspring vulnerability to ASD through advanced maternal and paternal age, valproate intake, toxic chemical exposure, maternal diabetes, enhanced steroidogenic activity, immune activation, and possibly altered zinc-copper cycles and treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Epidemiological studies demonstrate no evidence for vaccination posing an autism risk. It is concluded that future research needs to consider categorical autism, broader autism phenotypes, as well as autistic traits, and examine more homogenous autism variants by subgroup stratification. Our understanding of autism etiology could be advanced by research aimed at disentangling the causal and non-causal environmental effects, both founding and moderating, and gene-environment interplay using twin studies, longitudinal and experimental designs. The specificity of many environmental risks for ASD remains unknown and control of multiple confounders has been limited. Further understanding of the critical windows of neurodevelopmental vulnerability and investigating the fit of multiple hit and cumulative risk models are likely promising approaches in enhancing the understanding of role of environmental factors in the etiology of ASD.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si algo que hiciste causó el autismo de tu hijo o hija, esta revisión ofrece calma: el autismo surge de una combinación compleja de genética y entorno, y ningún factor aislado lo explica. Las vacunas no aumentan la probabilidad de autismo; los estudios epidemiológicos lo muestran con claridad. Algunos factores, como la edad de los padres, la diabetes materna o ciertos fármacos en el embarazo, se asocian con mayor probabilidad, pero asociación no significa culpa ni causa. Se trata de una revisión narrativa que resume investigaciones previas, sin participantes propios. Sus límites: muchos estudios no controlaron bien otras variables y aún no se sabe qué factores son realmente causales.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether something you did caused your child's autism, this review offers reassurance: autism arises from a complex mix of genetics and environment, and no single factor explains it. Vaccines do not raise the likelihood of autism; epidemiological studies show this clearly. Some factors, such as parental age, maternal diabetes or certain medicines during pregnancy, are linked to a higher likelihood, but a link does not mean blame or cause. This is a narrative review summarising earlier research, with no participants of its own. Its limits: many studies did not control well for other variables, and it is still unclear which factors are truly causal.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om något du gjorde orsakade ditt barns autism ger den här översikten lugn: autism uppstår ur en komplex blandning av gener och miljö, och ingen enskild faktor förklarar den. Vaccin ökar inte sannolikheten för autism; epidemiologiska studier visar det tydligt. Vissa faktorer, som föräldrarnas ålder, diabetes hos mamman eller vissa läkemedel under graviditeten, hänger ihop med högre sannolikhet, men ett samband betyder varken skuld eller orsak. Detta är en narrativ översikt som sammanfattar tidigare forskning, utan egna deltagare. Begränsningar: många studier kontrollerade inte andra faktorer väl, och det är fortfarande oklart vilka faktorer som verkligen är orsaker.

title: The Role of Eye Gaze During Natural Social Interactions in Typical and Autistic People.
authors: Cañigueral R, Hamilton AFC
abstract: Social interactions involve complex exchanges of a variety of social signals, such as gaze, facial expressions, speech and gestures. Focusing on the dual function of eye gaze, this review explores how the presence of an audience, communicative purpose and temporal dynamics of gaze allow interacting partners to achieve successful communication. First, we focus on how being watched modulates social cognition and behavior. We then show that the study of interpersonal gaze processing, particularly gaze temporal dynamics, can provide valuable understanding of social behavior in real interactions. We propose that the Interpersonal Gaze Processing model, which combines both sensing and signaling functions of eye gaze, provides a framework to make sense of gaze patterns in live interactions. Finally, we discuss how autistic individuals process the belief in being watched and interpersonal dynamics of gaze, and suggest that systematic manipulation of factors modulating gaze signaling can reveal which aspects of social eye gaze are challenging in autism.

sheet.es: Mirar a los ojos cumple dos funciones a la vez: recibir información y enviar señales. Para muchas personas autistas, sentirse observadas puede cambiar cómo se sienten y comunican. En la práctica: no exija contacto visual como prueba de atención; ofrezca conversaciones lado a lado, durante un paseo o una actividad compartida, y fíjese en otras señales de escucha. Pregunte qué le resulta cómodo a esa persona. La evidencia es una revisión teórica que reúne estudios sobre la mirada en interacciones reales con personas autistas y no autistas. Su límite: propone un modelo, no prueba intervenciones, y cada persona vive la mirada de forma distinta.
sheet.en: Eye gaze does two jobs at once: taking in information and sending signals. For many autistic people, the feeling of being watched can change how they feel and communicate. In practice: don't require eye contact as proof of attention; offer side-by-side conversations, during a walk or a shared activity, and notice other signs of listening. Ask the person what feels comfortable. The evidence is a theoretical review bringing together studies on gaze in real interactions with autistic and non-autistic people. Its limit: it proposes a model rather than testing any support, and every person experiences gaze differently.
sheet.sv: Blicken gör två saker samtidigt: tar in information och skickar signaler. För många autistiska personer kan känslan av att bli iakttagen påverka hur de mår och kommunicerar. I praktiken: kräv inte ögonkontakt som bevis på uppmärksamhet; erbjud samtal sida vid sida, under en promenad eller en gemensam aktivitet, och lägg märke till andra tecken på att personen lyssnar. Fråga vad som känns bekvämt för just den personen. Underlaget är en teoretisk översikt som sammanfattar studier om blick i verkliga samspel med autistiska och icke-autistiska personer. Begränsning: den föreslår en modell men prövar inga stödinsatser, och alla upplever blickkontakt olika.

title: Systematic Review of the Relationship Between Autism Stigma and Informal Caregiver Mental Health.
authors: Papadopoulos C, Lodder A, Constantinou G, Randhawa G
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Families play a crucial role in determining the mental health of the autistic individual(s) they are caring for. However, the stigma associated with autism can impair caregiver health. To investigate this, empirical evidence pertaining to stigma's impact on informal caregivers' mental health was systematically reviewed. All twelve included studies (n = 1442 informal caregivers) consistently reported the impact of autism related stigma upon caregiver mental health to be significant, meaningful and complex. A new theoretical framework describing the relationship between stigma and caregiver mental health is constructed. Moderating variables include those both changeable through intervention (e.g. hopelessness, self-esteem, self-compassion) and not changeable (gender, culture, financial burden and time since diagnosis). Implications and recommendations for professionals, interventions and future research are proposed.

sheet.es: Si sientes miradas o comentarios por el autismo de tu hijo o hija, ese peso es real y puede afectar tu salud mental. Mañana puedes darte un gesto de autocompasión: hablarte como hablarías a una amiga, buscar a alguien que entienda o anotar qué situaciones te pesan más. Cuidar tu ánimo también cuida a tu familia. La evidencia procede de una revisión sistemática de doce estudios con 1442 cuidadores familiares, que encontraron de forma constante que el estigma afecta su bienestar. Sus límites: son estudios variados, mayormente observacionales, y el modelo propuesto aún debe comprobarse; no todas las personas lo viven igual.
sheet.en: If you feel judged or stared at because of your child's autism, that weight is real and can affect your mental health. Tomorrow, try one act of self-compassion: speak to yourself as you would to a friend, reach out to someone who understands, or note which situations weigh on you most. Caring for your own wellbeing also supports your family. The evidence comes from a systematic review of twelve studies with 1,442 family caregivers, which consistently found that stigma affects caregiver mental health. Its limits: the studies varied, were mostly observational, and the proposed model still needs testing; experiences differ between people.
sheet.sv: Om du känner dig dömd eller iakttagen på grund av ditt barns autism är den tyngden verklig och kan påverka din psykiska hälsa. I morgon kan du pröva en handling av självmedkänsla: prata med dig själv som med en vän, kontakta någon som förstår eller anteckna vilka situationer som tynger mest. Att ta hand om ditt eget mående stöttar också din familj. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av tolv studier med 1 442 anhörigvårdare, som genomgående visade att stigma påverkar deras psykiska hälsa. Begränsningar: studierna var olika och mest observationella, och den föreslagna modellen behöver prövas; alla upplever det inte likadant.

title: A 'choice', an 'addiction', a way 'out of the lost': exploring self-injury in autistic people without intellectual disability.
authors: Moseley RL, Gregory NJ, Smith P, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) describes a phenomenon where individuals inflict deliberate pain and tissue damage to their bodies. Self-injurious behaviour is especially prevalent across the autism spectrum, but little is understood about the features and functions of self-injury for autistic individuals without intellectual disability, or about the risk factors that might be valuable for clinical usage in this group. Methods One hundred and three autistic adults who responded to an online advertisement were classified as current, historic or non-self-harmers in accordance with responses to the Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Assessment Tool (NSSI-AT). Multinomial regression aimed to predict categorisation of participants in accordance with scores on tests of autistic traits, alexithymia, depression, anxiety, mentalising and sensory sensitivity. Linear regression examined relationships between these predictors and the range, frequency, lifetime occurrence and functional purposes of NSSI. Qualitative analysis explored the therapeutic interventions that participants had found helpful, and what they wished people understood about self-injury. Results Current, historic and non-self-harming participants did not differ in age, age at diagnosis, male-to-female ratio, level of employment or education (the majority qualified to at least degree level). The most common function of NSSI was the regulation of low-energy affective states (depression, dissociation), followed by the regulation of high-energy states such as anger and anxiety. Alexithymia significantly predicted the categorisation of participants as current, historic or non-self-harmers, and predicted use of NSSI for regulating high-energy states and communicating distress to others. Depression, anxiety and sensory-sensitivity also differentiated participant groups, and sensory differences also predicted the range of bodily areas targeted, lifetime incidence and frequency of NSSI. Sensory differences, difficulty expressing and identifying emotions also emerged as problematic in the qualitative analysis, where participants expressed the need for compassion, patience, non-judgement and the need to recognise diversity between self-harmers, with some participants perceiving NSSI as a practical, non-problematic coping strategy. Conclusions Alexithymia, depression, anxiety and sensory differences may place some autistic individuals at especial risk of self-injury. Investigating the involvement of these variables and their utility for identification and treatment is of high importance, and the voices of participants offer guidance to practitioners confronted with NSSI in their autistic clients.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista que conoces se autolesiona, responde con calma, paciencia y sin juzgar. Puede ayudar explorar juntos cómo identificar y nombrar emociones, y revisar el entorno sensorial, porque las dificultades para reconocer emociones y las diferencias sensoriales aparecieron muy ligadas a la autolesión. Para muchas personas servía para salir del bajón o la desconexión, o para calmar enfado y ansiedad. Escucha qué significa para esa persona. Evidencia: estudio con cuestionarios online y respuestas abiertas de 103 adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual, la mayoría con estudios universitarios. Límites: muestra voluntaria y no representativa; muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no se aplica igual a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you know self-injures, respond with calm, patience and no judgement. It may help to explore together ways to notice and name emotions, and to look at the sensory environment, since difficulty identifying feelings and sensory differences were closely linked to self-injury. For many, it helped lift low or numb states, or calm anger and anxiety. Ask what it means for that person. Evidence: an online survey with open answers from 103 autistic adults without intellectual disability, most with university degrees. Limits: a self-selected, non-representative sample; it shows associations, not causes, and does not apply equally to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du känner skadar sig själv, möt det med lugn, tålamod och utan att döma. Det kan hjälpa att tillsammans utforska sätt att känna igen och sätta ord på känslor, och att se över den sensoriska miljön, eftersom svårigheter att identifiera känslor och sensoriska skillnader var starkt kopplade till självskada. För många hjälpte det mot nedstämdhet eller avstängdhet, eller för att dämpa ilska och ångest. Fråga vad det betyder för just den personen. Evidens: en webbenkät med öppna svar från 103 autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, de flesta med högskoleutbildning. Begränsningar: frivilligt, icke-representativt urval; visar samband, inte orsaker, och gäller inte alla lika.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorders and the Gut Microbiota.
authors: Fattorusso A, Di Genova L, Dell'Isola GB, Mencaroni E, Esposito S
abstract: In recent years, there has been an emerging interest in the possible role of the gut microbiota as a co-factor in the development of autism spectrum disorders (ASDs), as many studies have highlighted the bidirectional communication between the gut and brain (the so-called "gut-brain axis"). Accumulating evidence has shown a link between alterations in the composition of the gut microbiota and both gastrointestinal and neurobehavioural symptoms in children with ASD. The aim of this narrative review was to analyse the current knowledge about dysbiosis and gastrointestinal (GI) disorders in ASD and assess the current evidence for the role of probiotics and other non-pharmacological approaches in the treatment of children with ASD. Analysis of the literature showed that gut dysbiosis in ASD has been widely demonstrated; however, there is no single distinctive profile of the composition of the microbiota in people with ASD. Gut dysbiosis could contribute to the low-grade systemic inflammatory state reported in patients with GI comorbidities. The administration of probiotics (mostly a mixture of Bifidobacteria , Streptococci and Lactobacilli ) is the most promising treatment for neurobehavioural symptoms and bowel dysfunction, but clinical trials are still limited and heterogeneous. Well-designed, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trials are required to validate the effectiveness of probiotics in the treatment of ASD and to identify the appropriate strains, dose, and timing of treatment.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene molestias digestivas como estreñimiento, diarrea o dolor de barriga, vale la pena tomarlas en serio y comentarlas con su equipo de salud, porque pueden afectar al sueño, al ánimo y al bienestar diario. Antes de probar probióticos u otros cambios, consulta con un profesional; no hay una pauta única que sirva para todos. Esta revisión narrativa de 2019 resume estudios sobre la microbiota intestinal en niños y niñas autistas y encuentra diferencias frecuentes, pero ningún perfil común. Sus límites: no es un estudio nuevo, y los ensayos con probióticos son pocos, pequeños y muy distintos entre sí, así que la evidencia aún es preliminar.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has digestive discomfort such as constipation, diarrhoea or tummy pain, it is worth taking seriously and raising with their healthcare team, as it can affect sleep, mood and everyday wellbeing. Before trying probiotics or other changes, talk with a professional; there is no single approach that fits everyone. This 2019 narrative review summarises research on gut bacteria in autistic children and finds differences are common, but no shared pattern. Its limits: it is not a new study, and probiotic trials so far are few, small and very varied, so the evidence is still early.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har magbesvär som förstoppning, diarré eller ont i magen är det värt att ta det på allvar och ta upp det med vården, eftersom det kan påverka sömn, humör och vardagens välmående. Prata med en professionell innan ni provar probiotika eller andra förändringar; det finns inget upplägg som passar alla. Den här narrativa översikten från 2019 sammanfattar forskning om tarmbakterier hos autistiska barn och visar att skillnader är vanliga, men att det inte finns något gemensamt mönster. Begränsningar: det är ingen ny studie, och studierna om probiotika är få, små och mycket olika, så kunskapsläget är fortfarande tidigt.

title: Music Therapy and Other Music-Based Interventions in Pediatric Health Care: An Overview.
authors: Stegemann T, Geretsegger M, Phan Quoc E, Riedl H, Smetana M
abstract: Background: In pediatric health care, non-pharmacological interventions such as music therapy have promising potential to complement traditional medical treatment options in order to facilitate recovery and well-being. Music therapy and other music-based interventions are increasingly applied in the clinical treatment of children and adolescents in many countries world-wide. The purpose of this overview is to examine the evidence regarding the effectiveness of music therapy and other music-based interventions as applied in pediatric health care. Methods: Surveying recent literature and summarizing findings from systematic reviews, this overview covers selected fields of application in pediatric health care (autism spectrum disorder; disability; epilepsy; mental health; neonatal care; neurorehabilitation; pain, anxiety and stress in medical procedures; pediatric oncology and palliative care) and discusses the effectiveness of music interventions in these areas. Results: Findings show that there is a growing body of evidence regarding the beneficial effects of music therapy, music medicine, and other music-based interventions for children and adolescents, although more rigorous research is still needed. The highest quality of evidence for the positive effects of music therapy is available in the fields of autism spectrum disorder and neonatal care. Conclusions: Music therapy can be considered a safe and generally well-accepted intervention in pediatric health care to alleviate symptoms and improve quality of life. As an individualized intervention that is typically provided in a person-centered way, music therapy is usually easy to implement into clinical practices. However, it is important to note that to exploit the potential of music therapy in an optimal way, specialized academic and clinical training and careful selection of intervention techniques to fit the needs of the client are essential.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija le atrae la música, puede valer la pena explorar la musicoterapia con un profesional formado: suele ser segura, bien aceptada y adaptable a cada persona. En casa, la música compartida puede ser un espacio tranquilo de conexión, siguiendo sus preferencias y su ritmo, sin forzar. Esta es una revisión general de 2019 que resume revisiones sistemáticas sobre niños y adolescentes en distintos ámbitos de salud; la evidencia más sólida se encontró en autismo y en cuidados neonatales. Sus límites: es un resumen amplio, no un estudio nuevo, los autores piden investigación más rigurosa y los resultados no aplican igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your child is drawn to music, it may be worth exploring music therapy with a trained professional: it is generally safe, well accepted and tailored to each person. At home, shared music can be a calm space for connection, following their preferences and pace, never forced. This is a 2019 overview summarising systematic reviews on children and adolescents across several areas of health care; the strongest evidence was found for autism and neonatal care. Its limits: it is a broad summary rather than a new study, the authors call for more rigorous research, and results will not apply the same way to every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn dras till musik kan det vara värt att utforska musikterapi med en utbildad terapeut: den är i regel säker, väl accepterad och anpassas till varje person. Hemma kan gemensam musik bli en lugn stund av kontakt, på barnets villkor och i dess takt, utan tvång. Detta är en översikt från 2019 som sammanfattar systematiska översikter om barn och ungdomar inom flera vårdområden; starkast evidens fanns för autism och neonatalvård. Begränsningar: det är en bred sammanfattning, inte en ny studie, författarna efterlyser mer rigorös forskning och resultaten gäller inte alla personer på samma sätt.

title: Understanding the Reasons, Contexts and Costs of Camouflaging for Autistic Adults.
authors: Cage E, Troxell-Whitman Z
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Camouflaging entails 'masking' in or 'passing' social situations. Research suggests camouflaging behaviours are common in autistic people, and may negatively impact mental health. To enhance understanding of camouflaging, this study examined reasons, contexts and costs of camouflaging. 262 autistic people completed measures of camouflaging behaviours, camouflaging contexts (e.g. work vs. family), camouflaging reasons (e.g. to make friends) and mental health symptoms. Findings indicated a gender difference in reasons for camouflaging, with autistic women more likely to endorse "conventional" reasons (e.g. getting by in formal settings such as work). Both camouflaging highly across contexts and 'switching' between camouflaging in some contexts but not in others, related to poorer mental health. These findings have implications for understanding camouflaging in autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta de su entorno parece agotada después del trabajo o de reuniones, puede estar camuflándose: ocultando rasgos autistas para encajar. Ayuda ofrecer espacios donde no tenga que fingir, preguntar con calma qué situaciones le cuestan más y respetar sus tiempos de descanso. Este estudio encuestó a 262 adultos autistas: camuflarse mucho en muchos contextos, o alternar entre camuflarse en unos sí y en otros no, se asoció con peor salud mental; las mujeres autistas citaron más motivos 'convencionales', como desenvolverse en el trabajo. Limitaciones: fueron cuestionarios en un solo momento, así que no prueban causa y efecto, y cada persona vive el camuflaje de forma distinta.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult you support seems drained after work or social gatherings, they may be camouflaging: hiding autistic traits to fit in. It can help to offer spaces where they don't have to perform, gently ask which settings feel most demanding, and protect their recovery time. This survey study of 262 autistic adults found that camouflaging heavily across many settings, or switching between camouflaging in some places and not others, was linked to poorer mental health; autistic women more often gave 'conventional' reasons, such as getting by at work. Limits: questionnaires at one point in time cannot show cause and effect, and camouflaging feels different for each person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen du stöttar verkar helt slut efter jobbet eller sociala sammanhang kan hen kamouflera, alltså dölja autistiska drag för att passa in. Det kan hjälpa att erbjuda platser där hen inte behöver spela en roll, lugnt fråga vilka miljöer som kräver mest och skydda tid för återhämtning. I denna enkätstudie med 262 autistiska vuxna hängde mycket kamouflering i många sammanhang, eller växlande mellan att kamouflera på vissa ställen men inte andra, ihop med sämre psykisk hälsa; autistiska kvinnor angav oftare 'konventionella' skäl, som att klara sig på jobbet. Begränsningar: enkäter vid ett tillfälle visar inte orsak och verkan, och kamouflering upplevs olika för varje person.

title: A meta-analysis of working memory in individuals with autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Habib A, Harris L, Pollick F, Melville C
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are lifelong neurodevelopmental disorders. It is not clear whether working memory (WM) deficits are commonly experienced by individuals with ASD. Aim To determine whether individuals with ASD experience significant impairments in WM and whether there are specific domains of working memory that are impaired. Methods We conducted a meta-analysis using four electronic databases EMBASE (OVID), MEDLINE (OVID), PsychINFO (EBSCOHOST), and Web of Science, to examine the literature to investigate whether people with ASD experience impairments related to WM. Meta-analyses were conducted separately for phonological and visuospatial domains of WM. Subgroup analyses investigated age and intelligence quotient as potential moderators. Results A total of 29 papers containing 34 studies measuring phonological and visuospatial domains of WM met the inclusion criteria. WM scores were significantly lower for individuals with ASD compared to typically developed (TD) controls, in both the visuospatial domain when investigating accuracy (d: -0.73, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.42, p 0.05) and error rate (d: 1.45, 95% CI -0.07 to 2.96, p = 0.06). Age and IQ did not explain the differences in WM in ASD. Conclusions The findings of this meta-analysis indicate that across the lifespan, individuals with ASD demonstrate large impairments in WM across both phonological and visuospatial WM domains when compared to healthy individuals.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o a la persona autista que acompañas le cuesta retener varias instrucciones a la vez, puede ayudar dar un paso cada vez, usar apoyos visuales (listas, imágenes, horarios) y dejar tiempo para procesar. No es falta de interés ni de esfuerzo. Este metaanálisis reunió 34 estudios con personas autistas de distintas edades y encontró, en promedio, puntuaciones más bajas en memoria de trabajo verbal y visoespacial que en personas no autistas, sin que la edad ni el CI explicaran la diferencia. Límites: los estudios eran pequeños y variados, miden tareas de laboratorio y los promedios no describen a cada persona; muchas personas autistas tienen una memoria de trabajo fuerte.
sheet.en: If your child or the autistic person you support finds it hard to hold several instructions in mind at once, it can help to give one step at a time, use visual supports (lists, pictures, schedules) and allow extra processing time. This is not a lack of interest or effort. This meta-analysis pooled 34 studies of autistic people across ages and found, on average, lower scores on verbal and visuospatial working memory tasks than non-autistic peers; age and IQ did not explain the difference. Limits: the studies were small and varied, used lab tasks, and averages do not describe every individual; many autistic people have strong working memory.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn eller den autistiska person du stöttar har svårt att hålla flera instruktioner i huvudet samtidigt kan det hjälpa att ge ett steg i taget, använda visuellt stöd (listor, bilder, scheman) och ge extra tid att bearbeta. Det handlar inte om ointresse eller bristande vilja. Denna metaanalys samlade 34 studier med autistiska personer i olika åldrar och fann i genomsnitt lägre resultat på verbala och visuospatiala arbetsminnesuppgifter än hos icke-autistiska jämförelsepersoner; ålder och IQ förklarade inte skillnaden. Begränsningar: studierna var små och olika, byggde på laboratorieuppgifter, och genomsnitt beskriver inte varje individ; många autistiska personer har ett starkt arbetsminne.

title: Mapping the Autistic Advantage from the Accounts of Adults Diagnosed with Autism: A Qualitative Study.
authors: Russell G, Kapp SK, Elliott D, Elphick C, Gwernan-Jones R, Owens C
abstract: Background: Autism has been associated with specific cognitive strengths. Strengths and weaknesses have traditionally been conceptualized as dichotomous. Methods: We conducted 28 semi-structured interviews with autistic adults. Maximum variation sampling was used to ensure diversity in relation to support needs. We asked which personal traits adults attributed to their autism, and how these have helped in the workplace, in relationships, and beyond. Data were collected in two stages. Responses were analyzed using content and thematic techniques. Results: The ability to hyperfocus, attention to detail, good memory, and creativity were the most frequently described traits. Participants also described specific qualities relating to social interaction, such as honesty, loyalty, and empathy for animals or for other autistic people. In thematic analysis we found that traits associated with autism could be experienced either as advantageous or disadvantageous dependent on moderating influences. Moderating influences included the social context in which behaviors occurred, the ability to control behaviors, and the extent to which traits were expressed. Conclusions: Separating autistic strengths from weaknesses may be a false dichotomy if traits cannot be isolated as separate constructs of strengths or deficits. If attempts to isolate problematic traits from advantageous traits are ill conceived, there may be implications for interventions that have reduction in autistic traits as a primary outcome measure. Lay summary Why was this study done?: The study was done to find out what autistic adults could tell us about their own abilities. They told us about their abilities and how these abilities had helped them in their everyday lives: at work, in their relationships with other people, and at home. What was the purpose of this study?: To tell a story about what aspects of their autism adults thought were of benefit, when going about their daily lives. What did the researchers do?: The researchers interviewed 24 adults who had an autism diagnosis. Some lived in residential care and others lived alone in rented apartments. Some people were interviewed twice. Most people said they enjoyed the experience of being interviewed.Once the interviews were done, they were typed up and the researchers tried to figure out what were the common themes over all the stories they had heard. They thought about the themes, then did some more interviews with autistic adults to check they were on the right lines. After discussing them, they wrote the story. What were the results of the study?: Hyper focus, attention to detail, and the ability to remember were the abilities that autistic people said benefitted them most often. But autistic adults who were interviewed said although their autistic traits were sometimes helpful, at other times they hindered their progress. So the same trait might be useful in some circumstances and unhelpful in other situations. For example, hypersensitivity led one person to enjoy nature, but was difficult to cope with in crowded streets. The study highlights this interchangeability. What do these findings add to what was already known?: Before, autistic people were known to have both strengths and challenges, but studies tended to separate autistic strengths and weaknesses as different things. We theorize that some traits are expressed as behaviors that may serve to improve or hinder autistic people's progress, but this depends on their situation (context). What are potential weaknesses in the study?: Because the researchers used interviews, they did not include any nonverbal autistic people in the study. How will these findings help autistic adults now or in the future?: It could be useful to think about autism in a way that does not focus on deficits and this study will help us to do that. Plus, if an autistic trait can give people an advantage or a disadvantage, interventions aimed at reducing autistic behaviors might risk dampening advantageous traits as they seek to help with difficulties. That means, autistic adults and children might lose useful abilities when and if they are treated for traits that can also be problematic. The researchers hope their study will lead to more discussion about these types of ideas.

sheet.es: Antes de intentar «reducir» un rasgo autista, pregúntate en qué contextos ayuda y en cuáles dificulta. El hiperfoco, la atención al detalle, la memoria o la sensibilidad sensorial pueden ser una ventaja o una carga según el entorno, el control que la persona tenga sobre ellos y su intensidad. Cambiar el contexto (menos ruido, tiempo para un interés, pausas) puede funcionar mejor que eliminar el rasgo. Habla con la persona sobre qué rasgos valora. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 28 adultos autistas con distintas necesidades de apoyo. Límites: no participaron personas autistas no hablantes, la muestra es pequeña y los resultados no se aplican a todas las personas.
sheet.en: Before trying to "reduce" an autistic trait, ask where it helps and where it gets in the way. Hyperfocus, attention to detail, memory or sensory sensitivity can be an advantage or a burden depending on the setting, how much control the person has, and how intense the trait is. Adjusting the context (less noise, time for an interest, breaks) may work better than removing the trait. Talk with the person about which traits they value. Evidence: a qualitative study interviewing 28 autistic adults with varied support needs. Limits: nonspeaking autistic people were not included, the sample is small, and findings will not fit everyone.
sheet.sv: Innan du försöker "minska" ett autistiskt drag, fråga dig var det hjälper och var det står i vägen. Hyperfokus, detaljseende, gott minne eller sensorisk känslighet kan vara en fördel eller en börda beroende på miljön, hur mycket kontroll personen har och hur starkt draget uttrycks. Att anpassa sammanhanget (mindre ljud, tid för ett intresse, pauser) kan fungera bättre än att ta bort draget. Prata med personen om vilka drag hen själv värdesätter. Evidens: en kvalitativ intervjustudie med 28 autistiska vuxna med olika stödbehov. Begränsningar: icke-talande autistiska personer deltog inte, urvalet är litet och resultaten passar inte alla.

title: Neurodivergent intersubjectivity: Distinctive features of how autistic people create shared understanding.
authors: Heasman B, Gillespie A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autistic people are neurologically divergent, yet approaches to studying autism are framed by neurotypical definitions of being social. Using the concept of intersubjectivity, which conceptualises a variety of ways of socially relating, we investigate distinctive features of how autistic people build social understanding. A total of 30 members of a charity supporting adults with autism were video-recorded during a social activity they enjoyed, namely collaborative video gaming. Mapping the coherence, affect and symmetry of each conversational turn revealed shifting patterns of intersubjectivity within each interaction. Focussing on clusters of consistent and fragmented turns led us to identify two features of neurodivergent intersubjectivity: a generous assumption of common ground that, when understood, led to rapid rapport, and, when not understood, resulted in potentially disruptive utterances; and a low demand for coordination that ameliorated many challenges associated with disruptive turns. Our findings suggest that neurodivergent intersubjectivity reveals potential for unconventional forms of social relating and that a within-interaction analysis is a viable methodology for exploring neurodivergent communication. Future research should examine the varieties of neurodivergent intersubjectivity, with associated problems and potentials, and how those forms of intersubjectivity can be enabled to flourish, particularly in autistic-to-neurotypical encounters.

sheet.es: Las formas autistas de conectar pueden ser distintas y funcionar bien. Si su familiar autista habla como si usted ya supiera de qué trata algo, pregunte con calma en lugar de corregir; y no exija turnos perfectos ni contacto visual: en actividades compartidas que disfruta, como los videojuegos, la conexión puede surgir rápido con pocas exigencias de coordinación. Evidencia: estudio con 30 adultos autistas de una organización benéfica, grabados en vídeo mientras jugaban juntos; se analizó cada turno de conversación.
