Límites: grupo pequeño, una sola actividad y solo interacciones entre personas autistas; no describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Autistic ways of connecting can be different and still work well. If your autistic family member talks as if you already share the background, ask gently rather than correct; and don't insist on perfect turn-taking or eye contact. In shared activities they enjoy, like video gaming, rapport can build quickly when demands for coordination are low. Evidence: a study of 30 autistic adults from a support charity, video-recorded while gaming together, analysing each conversational turn. Limits: a small group, one activity, and only autistic-to-autistic interactions; it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Autistiska sätt att skapa kontakt kan vara annorlunda och ändå fungera bra. Om din autistiska närstående pratar som om du redan vet sammanhanget, fråga lugnt i stället för att rätta; och kräv inte perfekt turtagning eller ögonkontakt. I gemensamma aktiviteter personen tycker om, som datorspel, kan samhörighet växa snabbt när kraven på samordning är låga. Evidens: en studie med 30 autistiska vuxna från en stödorganisation, filmade när de spelade tillsammans, där varje samtalstur analyserades. Begränsningar: liten grupp, en enda aktivitet och bara samtal mellan autistiska personer; den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Making the future together: Shaping autism research through meaningful participation.
authors: Fletcher-Watson S, Adams J, Brook K, Charman T, Crane L, Cusack J, Leekam S, Milton D, Parr JR, Pellicano E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Participatory research methods connect researchers with relevant communities to achieve shared goals. These methods can deliver results that are relevant to people's lives and thus likely to have a positive impact. In the context of a large and growing body of autism research, with continued poor implementation, and some evidence of community dissatisfaction, there is a powerful case for participatory autism research. In order to develop a framework for such collaborative working, a UK seminar series was organised and co-produced by autistic and non-autistic people with academic, practitioner and lived expertise. This article reports on the outcomes from the series, identifying five topics relevant to building a community of practice in participatory research: Respect, Authenticity, Assumptions, Infrastructure and Empathy. Each topic is connected to a specific example from within and beyond research, to inspire new practices in the field. We call for the development of participatory research skills among the autism research community and the facilitation of greater autistic leadership of, and partnership in, research. Such work, if delivered to a high standard, is likely to lead to better translation into practice and improved outcomes for autistic people and those who support them.

sheet.es: Mañana puedes aplicar una idea sencilla: cuando algo afecte a la persona autista que acompañas, decide con ella, no por ella. Pregunta qué le importa, escucha cómo lo explica y revisa tus suposiciones. Los cinco temas del artículo (respeto, autenticidad, suposiciones, infraestructura y empatía) sirven también en casa o al elegir servicios: ¿quién participa en las decisiones? Este trabajo resume una serie de seminarios en el Reino Unido, coorganizada por personas autistas y no autistas con experiencia académica, profesional y vivida. Su límite: es un marco de reflexión y propuestas, no un estudio que mida resultados, así que sus ideas son orientativas y cada persona y familia es distinta.
sheet.en: Tomorrow you can try one simple idea: when something affects the autistic person you support, decide with them, not for them. Ask what matters to them, listen to how they put it, and check your own assumptions. The article's five themes (respect, authenticity, assumptions, infrastructure and empathy) also work at home or when choosing services: who gets a say? This paper summarises a UK seminar series co-produced by autistic and non-autistic people with academic, practitioner and lived expertise. Its limit: it is a framework of reflections and proposals, not a study measuring outcomes, so treat it as guidance, and remember every person and family is different.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du pröva en enkel idé: när något påverkar den autistiska person du stöttar, bestäm tillsammans med hen, inte åt hen. Fråga vad som är viktigt, lyssna på hur hen uttrycker det och granska dina egna antaganden. Artikelns fem teman (respekt, autenticitet, antaganden, infrastruktur och empati) fungerar också hemma eller när ni väljer stöd: vem får vara med och bestämma? Artikeln sammanfattar en seminarieserie i Storbritannien, skapad av autistiska och icke-autistiska personer med akademisk, professionell och egen erfarenhet. Begränsning: det är ett ramverk med reflektioner och förslag, ingen studie som mäter effekter, så se det som vägledning – varje person och familj är olika.

claim.es: La investigación en autismo es más útil y respetuosa cuando las personas autistas participan en diseñarla.
claim.en: Autism research is more useful and respectful when autistic people take part in designing it.
claim.sv: Autismforskning blir mer användbar och respektfull när autistiska personer deltar i utformningen.

supports.es: Construir herramientas con personas autistas, no solo para ellas.
supports.en: Building tools with autistic people, not only for them.
supports.sv: Att bygga verktyg tillsammans med autistiska personer, inte bara för dem.

doesNotSupport.es: Ninguna intervención concreta; trata de cómo se construye el conocimiento.
doesNotSupport.en: Any specific intervention; this is about how knowledge is made.
doesNotSupport.sv: Ingen specifik insats; det handlar om hur kunskap skapas.

title: The distribution of autistic traits across the autism spectrum: evidence for discontinuous dimensional subpopulations underlying the autism continuum.
authors: Abu-Akel A, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S, Heinke D
abstract: Background A considerable amount of research has discussed whether autism and psychiatric/neurodevelopmental conditions in general are best described categorically or dimensionally. In recent years, finite mixture models have been increasingly applied to mixed populations of autistic and non-autistic individuals to answer this question. However, the use of such methods with mixed populations may not be appropriate for two reasons: First, subgroups within mixed populations are often skewed and thus violate mixture models assumptions, which are based on weighted sum of Gaussian distributions. Second, these analyses have, to our knowledge, been solely applied to enriched samples, where the prevalence of the clinical condition within the study sample far exceeds epidemiological estimates. Method We employed a dual Weibull mixture model to examine the distribution of the Autism Spectrum Quotient scores of a mixed sample of autistic and non-autistic adults ( N = 4717; autism = 811), as well as of a derived sample (from the enriched sample; N = 3973; autism = 67) that reflects the current prevalence of autism within the general population. Results In a mixed autistic and non-autistic population, our model provided a better description of the underlying structure of autistic traits than traditional finite Gaussian mixture models and performed well when applied to a sample that reflected the prevalence of autism in the general population. The model yielded results, which are consistent with predictions of current theories advocating for the co-existence of a mixed categorical and dimensional architecture within the autism spectrum. Conclusion The results provide insight into the continuum nature of the distribution of autistic traits, support the complementary role of both categorical and dimensional approaches to autism spectrum condition, and underscore the importance of analyzing samples that reflect the epidemiological prevalence of the condition. Owing to its flexibility to represent a wide variety of distributions, the Weibull distribution might be better suited for latent structure studies, within enriched and prevalence-true samples.

sheet.es: Puede ser útil pensar en el autismo de dos maneras a la vez: como una identidad diferenciada y como rasgos que varían en intensidad de una persona a otra. Mañana, en lugar de preguntarse «¿cuánto autismo tiene?», puede observar qué rasgos concretos influyen en el día de su familiar y qué apoyos le sirven. Este estudio analizó cuestionarios de rasgos autistas (AQ) de 4.717 adultos, 811 de ellos autistas, con un modelo estadístico nuevo. Sus límites: se basa en un cuestionario autoinformado en adultos, no observa la vida diaria y no dice nada sobre cómo apoyar a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: It can help to think about autism in two ways at once: as a distinct identity, and as traits that vary in strength from person to person. Tomorrow, instead of asking "how autistic is my family member?", you might notice which specific traits shape their day and which supports actually help. This study analysed autistic-trait questionnaires (AQ) from 4,717 adults, 811 of them autistic, using a new statistical model. Its limits: it relies on a self-report questionnaire completed by adults, does not observe daily life, and says nothing about how to support any individual person.
sheet.sv: Det kan hjälpa att tänka på autism på två sätt samtidigt: som en egen identitet och som drag som varierar i styrka från person till person. I morgon kan du, i stället för att fråga "hur autistisk är min närstående?", lägga märke till vilka konkreta drag som påverkar dagen och vilket stöd som faktiskt hjälper. Studien analyserade enkätsvar om autistiska drag (AQ) från 4 717 vuxna, varav 811 autistiska, med en ny statistisk modell. Begränsningar: den bygger på självskattning hos vuxna, observerar inte vardagen och säger inget om hur en enskild person bäst stöttas.

title: The Possible Role of the Microbiota-Gut-Brain-Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Srikantha P, Mohajeri MH
abstract: New research points to a possible link between autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and the gut microbiota as many autistic children have co-occurring gastrointestinal problems. This review focuses on specific alterations of gut microbiota mostly observed in autistic patients. Particularly, the mechanisms through which such alterations may trigger the production of the bacterial metabolites, or leaky gut in autistic people are described. Various altered metabolite levels were observed in the blood and urine of autistic children, many of which were of bacterial origin such as short chain fatty acids (SCFAs), indoles and lipopolysaccharides (LPS). A less integrative gut-blood-barrier is abundant in autistic individuals. This explains the leakage of bacterial metabolites into the patients, triggering new body responses or an altered metabolism. Some other co-occurring symptoms such as mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress in cells, altered tight junctions in the blood-brain barrier and structural changes in the cortex, hippocampus, amygdala and cerebellum were also detected. Moreover, this paper suggests that ASD is associated with an unbalanced gut microbiota (dysbiosis). Although the cause-effect relationship between ASD and gut microbiota is not yet well established, the consumption of specific probiotics may represent a side-effect free tool to re-establish gut homeostasis and promote gut health. The diagnostic and therapeutic value of bacterial-derived compounds as new possible biomarkers, associated with perturbation in the phenylalanine metabolism, as well as potential therapeutic strategies will be discussed.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene molestias digestivas frecuentes (estreñimiento, diarrea, dolor de barriga), tómalas en serio: pueden afectar al sueño, al ánimo y a la comodidad diaria. Anota síntomas y comidas durante unas semanas y llévalo a su médico. Antes de probar probióticos o cambios de dieta, consúltalo con un profesional sanitario. Esta es una revisión narrativa de estudios previos, sobre todo con niños autistas, que describe diferencias en la flora intestinal y en sustancias de origen bacteriano. Límite: no demuestra causa y efecto, y la afirmación de que los probióticos no tienen efectos secundarios no está bien respaldada; no aplica igual a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child often has tummy troubles (constipation, diarrhoea, stomach pain), take them seriously: gut discomfort can affect sleep, mood and everyday comfort. Keep a simple diary of symptoms and meals for a few weeks and bring it to their doctor. Talk with a health professional before trying probiotics or diet changes. This is a narrative review of earlier studies, mostly involving autistic children, describing differences in gut bacteria and bacterial substances in blood and urine. Limits: it cannot show cause and effect, its claim that probiotics are side-effect free is not well supported, and findings will not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn ofta har magbesvär (förstoppning, diarré, magont), ta det på allvar: obehag i magen kan påverka sömn, humör och vardagens välbefinnande. För en enkel dagbok över symtom och måltider i några veckor och ta med den till läkaren. Prata med vårdpersonal innan ni provar probiotika eller kostförändringar. Detta är en översikt av tidigare studier, främst med autistiska barn, som beskriver skillnader i tarmbakterier och bakteriella ämnen i blod och urin. Begränsningar: den kan inte visa orsak och verkan, påståendet att probiotika saknar biverkningar är dåligt underbyggt, och resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: Autistic traits in adults who have attempted suicide.
authors: Richards G, Kenny R, Griffiths S, Allison C, Mosse D, Holt R, O'Connor RC, Cassidy S, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background An emerging literature suggests that autistic adults are at increased risk of experiencing suicidal thoughts, making suicidal plans and attempts, and dying by suicide. However, few studies have investigated whether autistic traits are related to suicidal behaviour. The current study examined autistic traits in a sample of adults who reported at least one suicide attempt. Methods An online questionnaire was advertised between June and September 2017 on suicide prevention websites, research databases, and social media. Participants reported whether they had ever attempted suicide (yes/no), and if so, how many times they had attempted (once/more than once). They also reported diagnosed and suspected mental health or neurodevelopmental conditions, and completed the Autism Spectrum Quotient (AQ). Two hundred forty-five adults accessed the survey; 132 reported having attempted suicide and also completed the AQ. It was hypothesised that AQ total scores and subscale scores would be higher in adults who had attempted suicide more than once compared to adults who had attempted once. These hypotheses were tested using an independent samples t test, Mann-Whitney U tests, and binary logistic regression. Results Most participants were female (83.3%, male = 12.9%, other = 3.8%), and ages ranged from 18 to 65 (median = 36.00; IQR = 19.00). Total AQ scores, as well as communication and imagination subscale scores were significantly higher in adults who had attempted suicide more than once compared to adults who had attempted suicide once. Even after removing participants with diagnosed or suspected autism ( n = 34), 40.6% had an AQ score indicative of clinical concern (≥ 26). Conclusions The findings suggest that high levels of autistic traits may frequently be present in adults who have attempted suicide, and that AQ scores are higher in those with a history of more than one suicide attempt. It may be possible to better identify suicide risk by screening autistic adults with mental health conditions for suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and by screening people with suicidal thoughts and/or behaviours for autism.

sheet.es: Si cuidas o acompañas a un adulto autista, o a alguien con rasgos autistas no diagnosticados, vale la pena preguntar con calma y directamente por pensamientos de suicidio, y pedir a los servicios de salud mental que tengan en cuenta el autismo. Preguntar no aumenta el riesgo; abre una puerta. Si hay peligro inmediato, contacta con emergencias. Evidencia: encuesta en línea con 132 adultos (mayoría mujeres) que habían intentado suicidarse; quienes lo intentaron más de una vez mostraban más rasgos autistas, y muchos sin diagnóstico puntuaban alto. Límites: muestra pequeña y autoseleccionada, datos autoinformados y un cuestionario que no diagnostica; no muestra causa ni aplica a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, or someone with possibly undiagnosed autistic traits, it is worth asking calmly and directly about suicidal thoughts, and asking mental health services to consider autism. Asking does not raise risk; it opens a door. If there is immediate danger, contact emergency services. Evidence: an online survey of 132 adults (mostly women) who had attempted suicide; those with more than one attempt reported more autistic traits, and many without a diagnosis scored high. Limits: a small, self-selected sample, self-reported data and a questionnaire that cannot diagnose; it does not show cause and does not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, eller någon med kanske odiagnostiserade autistiska drag, kan det vara värt att lugnt och rakt fråga om självmordstankar, och be psykiatrin att ta hänsyn till autism. Att fråga ökar inte risken; det öppnar en dörr. Vid akut fara, kontakta 112. Evidens: en webbenkät med 132 vuxna (mest kvinnor) som hade gjort självmordsförsök; de med fler än ett försök rapporterade fler autistiska drag, och många utan diagnos fick höga poäng. Begränsningar: litet, självvalt urval, självrapporterade uppgifter och ett formulär som inte kan ställa diagnos; studien visar inte orsak och gäller inte alla.

title: "Older Adults with ASD: The Consequences of Aging." Insights from a series of special interest group meetings held at the International Society for Autism Research 2016-2017.
authors: Roestorf A, Bowler DM, Deserno MK, Howlin P, Klinger L, McConachie H, Parr JR, Powell P, Van Heijst BFC, Geurts HM
abstract: A special interest group (SIG) entitled "Older Adults with ASD: The Consequences of Aging" was held at the International Society for Autism Research (INSAR) annual meetings in 2016 and 2017. The SIG and subsequent meetings brought together, for the first time, international delegates who were members of the autistic community, researchers, practitioners and service providers. Based on aging autism research that is already underway in UK, Europe, Australia and North America, discussions focussed on conceptualising the parameters of aging when referring to autism, and the measures that are appropriate to use with older adults when considering diagnostic assessment, cognitive factors and quality of life in older age. Thus, the aim of this SIG was to progress the research agenda on current and future directions for autism research in the context of aging. A global issue on how to define 'aging' when referring to ASD was at the forefront of discussions. The 'aging' concept can in principle refer to all developmental transitions. However, in this paper we focus on the cognitive and physical changes that take place from mid-life onwards. Accordingly, it was agreed that aging and ASD research should focus on adults over the age of 50 years, given the high rates of co-occurring physical and mental health concerns and increased risk of premature death in some individuals. Moreover, very little is known about the cognitive change, care needs and outcomes of autistic adults beyond this age. Discussions on the topics of diagnostic and cognitive assessments, and of quality of life and well-being were explored through shared knowledge about which measures are currently being used and which background questions should be asked to obtain comprehensive and informative developmental and medical histories. Accordingly, a survey was completed by SIG delegates who were representatives of international research groups across four continents, and who are currently conducting studies with older autistic adults. Considerable overlap was identified across different research groups in measures of both autism and quality of life, which pointed to combining data and shared learnings as the logical next step. Regarding the background questions that were asked, the different research groups covered similar topics but the groups differed in the way these questions were formulated when working with autistic adults across a range of cognitive abilities. It became clear that continued input from individuals on the autism spectrum is important to ensure that questionnaires used in ongoing and future are accessible and understandable for people across the whole autistic spectrum, including those with limited verbal abilities.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista mayor de 50 años, conviene prestar atención regular a su salud física y mental, y registrar su historia de desarrollo y médica: ayudará en cualquier evaluación futura. Pide que los cuestionarios y entrevistas se adapten a su forma de comunicarse, incluida la comunicación no verbal. Este artículo resume reuniones de un grupo de interés de INSAR (2016-2017) con personas autistas, investigadores y profesionales de cuatro continentes, más una encuesta a grupos de investigación. Sus límites: es un documento de consenso y agenda, no prueba ninguna intervención, y aún se sabe muy poco sobre el envejecimiento autista.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person over 50, it is worth keeping regular attention on both physical and mental health, and keeping notes on their developmental and medical history: this helps with any future assessment. Ask that questionnaires and interviews be adapted to how they communicate, including people who speak little or not at all. This paper summarises INSAR special interest group meetings (2016-2017) with autistic people, researchers and practitioners from four continents, plus a survey of research groups. Its limits: it is a consensus and agenda-setting paper, it tests no support or intervention, and very little is yet known about autistic aging.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person över 50 år är det klokt att regelbundet uppmärksamma både fysisk och psykisk hälsa, och att spara anteckningar om personens utvecklings- och sjukdomshistoria: det underlättar framtida bedömningar. Be om att frågeformulär och intervjuer anpassas efter hur personen kommunicerar, även om hen talar lite eller inte alls. Artikeln sammanfattar möten i en intressegrupp vid INSAR (2016–2017) med autistiska personer, forskare och yrkesverksamma från fyra kontinenter, samt en enkät till forskargrupper. Begränsningar: det är ett konsensus- och agendadokument som inte prövar något stöd, och kunskapen om autistiskt åldrande är fortfarande mycket begränsad.

title: Systematic Review of Sleep Disturbances and Circadian Sleep Desynchronization in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Toward an Integrative Model of a Self-Reinforcing Loop.
authors: Carmassi C, Palagini L, Caruso D, Masci I, Nobili L, Vita A, Dell'Osso L
abstract: Background: A compelling number of studies, conducted in both children and adults, have reported an association between sleep disturbances/circadian sleep alterations and autism spectrum disorder (ASD); however, the data are sparse and the nature of this link is still unclear. The present review aimed to systematically collect the literature data relevant on sleep disturbances and circadian sleep dysrhythmicity related to ASD across all ages and to provide an integrative theoretical framework of their association. Methods: A systematic review of the MEDLINE, PubMed, and Cochrane databases was conducted from November 2018 to February 2019. The search strategies used were MeSH headings and keywords for "sleep-wake circadian rhythms" OR "circadian sleep disorders" OR "sleep-wake pattern" OR "sleep disorders" OR "melatonin" AND "autism spectrum disorder" OR "autism". Results: One hundred and three studies were identified, 15 regarded circadian sleep dysrhythmicity, 74 regarded sleep disturbances, and 17 regarded melatonin alterations in children and adults with ASD. Our findings suggested that autistic subjects frequently present sleep disturbances in particular short sleep duration, low sleep quality/efficiency, and circadian sleep desynchronization such as delayed phases and/or eveningness. Sleep disturbances and circadian sleep alterations have been related to the severity of autistic symptoms. Genetic studies have shown polymorphisms in circadian CLOCK genes and in genes involved in melatonin pathways in subjects with ASD. Conclusions: Sleep disturbances and circadian sleep alterations are frequent in subjects with autistic symptoms. These subjects have shown polymorphisms in clock genes expression and in genes involved in melatonin production. The impairment of circadian sleep regulation may increase the individual's vulnerability to develop symptoms of ASD by altering the sleep regulation in toto , which plays a key role in normal brain development. Even though controversies and "research gaps" are present in literature at this point, we may hypothesize a bidirectional relation between circadian sleep dysfunction and ASD. In particular, circadian sleep dysrhythmicity may predispose to develop ASD symptoms and vice versa within a self-reinforcing feedback loop. By targeting sleep disturbances and circadian sleep dysrhythmicity, we may improve treatment strategies for both children and adults with ASD.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista con la que convives duerme poco, se despierta a menudo o tiende a dormirse y despertarse tarde, no es culpa de nadie: es frecuente y puede tener una base biológica. Mañana puedes anotar durante una o dos semanas horas de sueño, luz y rutinas, y llevar ese registro al equipo de salud. Una luz matinal, horarios estables y noches tranquilas pueden ayudar a algunas personas. La evidencia: una revisión sistemática de 103 estudios con niños y adultos autistas, que encontró sueño corto, menor calidad y ritmos desplazados, además de variantes en genes del reloj y de la melatonina. Límites: los estudios eran diversos y la idea de un círculo que se refuerza es una hipótesis, no algo demostrado.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you live with sleeps little, wakes often or tends to fall asleep and wake late, it is nobody's fault: this is common and may have a biological basis. Tomorrow you could start a one- or two-week log of sleep times, light and routines, and bring it to your health team. Morning light, steady schedules and calm evenings may help some people. The evidence: a systematic review of 103 studies with autistic children and adults, finding short sleep, lower sleep quality and delayed body clocks, plus variants in clock and melatonin genes. Limits: the studies varied widely, and the idea of a self-reinforcing loop is a hypothesis, not proven.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du lever med sover lite, vaknar ofta eller somnar och vaknar sent är det ingens fel: det är vanligt och kan ha en biologisk grund. I morgon kan du börja föra en sömndagbok i en eller två veckor med sovtider, ljus och rutiner, och ta med den till vården. Morgonljus, jämna tider och lugna kvällar kan hjälpa en del. Evidensen: en systematisk översikt av 103 studier med autistiska barn och vuxna som visade kort sömn, sämre sömnkvalitet och förskjuten dygnsrytm, samt varianter i klock- och melatoningener. Begränsningar: studierna var mycket olika, och tanken om en självförstärkande loop är en hypotes, inte bevisad.

title: A systematic review of ayres sensory integration intervention for children with autism.
authors: Schoen SA, Lane SJ, Mailloux Z, May-Benson T, Parham LD, Smith Roley S, Schaaf RC
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Sensory integration is one of the most highly utilized interventions in autism, however, a lack of consensus exists regarding its evidence base. An increasing number of studies are investigating the effectiveness of this approach. This study used the Council for Exceptional Children (CEC) Standards for Evidence-based Practices in Special Education to evaluate the effectiveness research from 2006 to 2017 on Ayres Sensory Integration (ASI) intervention for children with autism. A systematic review was conducted in three stages. Stage 1 involved an extensive database search for relevant studies using search terms related to sensory integration and autism, interventions suggesting a sensory integration approach, and high-quality study designs. Searches yielded 19 studies that were evaluated in Stage 2. Six of these met inclusion criteria of being peer-reviewed, written in English, description of intervention this is consistent with ASI intervention, and comparison group design or single subject method employed. Prior to analysis using CEC standards, three articles were excluded because intervention details were not consistent with the core principles of ASI, or because of major methodological flaws. In Stage 3, the remaining three studies were rated using the CEC quality indicators and standards for an evidence-based practice. Two randomized controlled trials respectively met 100% and 85% of the CEC criteria items. One additional study met more than 50% of the criteria. Based on CEC criteria, ASI can be considered an evidence-based practice for children with autism ages 4-12 years old. Autism Research 2019, 12: 6-19. © 2018 The Authors. Autism Research published by International Society for Autism Research and Wiley Periodicals, Inc. LAY SUMMARY: Ayres Sensory Integration intervention is one of the most frequently requested and highly utilized interventions in autism. This intervention has specific requirements for therapist qualifications and the process of therapy. This systematic review of studies providing Ayres Sensory Integration therapy to children with autism indicates that it is an evidence-based practice according to the criteria of the Council for Exceptional Children.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista de 4 a 12 años vive las sensaciones de forma intensa, puede valer la pena preguntar por la Integración Sensorial de Ayres, impartida por terapeutas ocupacionales con formación específica. Pregunta por su certificación y por objetivos claros elegidos junto con tu familia y, cuando sea posible, con tu hijo. No es lo mismo que usar chalecos con peso o cepillados sueltos. La evidencia: una revisión sistemática analizó estudios de 2006 a 2017 y solo tres cumplieron los criterios; dos ensayos aleatorizados fueron de alta calidad. Límites: muy pocos estudios, muestras pequeñas y solo infancia; puede no ser adecuada para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child aged 4 to 12 experiences sensations intensely, it may be worth asking about Ayres Sensory Integration, delivered by occupational therapists with specific training. Ask about their certification and about clear goals chosen together with your family and, where possible, your child. It is not the same as weighted vests or isolated brushing routines. The evidence: a systematic review examined studies from 2006 to 2017, and only three met its criteria; two randomised trials were of high quality. Limits: very few studies, small samples and children only, so it may not suit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn i åldern 4–12 år upplever sinnesintryck intensivt kan det vara värt att fråga om Ayres sensorisk integration, som ges av arbetsterapeuter med särskild utbildning. Fråga om deras certifiering och om tydliga mål som valts tillsammans med er familj och, när det går, med barnet. Det är inte samma sak som tyngdvästar eller enstaka borstningsrutiner. Evidensen: en systematisk översikt granskade studier från 2006–2017, och bara tre uppfyllde kriterierna; två randomiserade studier höll hög kvalitet. Begränsningar: mycket få studier, små grupper och bara barn, så metoden passar inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: Sleep determines quality of life in autistic adults: A longitudinal study.
authors: Deserno MK, Borsboom D, Begeer S, Agelink van Rentergem JA, Mataw K, Geurts HM
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Many individuals with autism report generally low quality of life (QoL). Identifying predictors for pathways underlying this outcome is an urgent priority. We aim to examine multivariate patterns that predict later subjective and objective QoL in autistic individuals. Autistic characteristics, comorbid complaints, aspects of daily functioning, and demographics were assessed online in a 2-year longitudinal study with 598 autistic adults. Regression trees were fitted to baseline data to identify factors that could predict QoL at follow-up. We found that sleep problems are an important predictor of later subjective QoL, while the subjective experience of a person's societal contribution is important when it comes to predicting the level of daily activities. Sleep problems are the most important predictor of QoL in autistic adults and may offer an important treatment target for improving QoL. Our results additionally suggest that social satisfaction can buffer this association. Autism Research 2019, 12: 794-801. © 2019 International Society for Autism Research, Wiley Periodicals, Inc. LAY SUMMARY: Many individuals with autism report generally low quality of life (QoL). In this study, we looked at factors that predict long-term QoL and found that sleep problems are highly influential. Our results additionally suggest that social satisfaction can buffer this influence. These findings suggest that sleep and social satisfaction could be monitored to increase QoL in autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, vale la pena prestar atención a su sueño: preguntar con calma cómo duerme, qué le ayuda a descansar y si quiere apoyo para hablarlo con su equipo de salud. También importa cuidar las relaciones que a ella le resultan satisfactorias y su sensación de aportar algo valioso. En este estudio longitudinal de dos años, 598 adultos autistas respondieron cuestionarios en línea; los problemas de sueño fueron el factor que mejor predijo la calidad de vida posterior, y la satisfacción social pareció amortiguar ese efecto. Sus límites: los datos son autoinformados en línea, muestran asociaciones y no causas, y no valen igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it is worth paying attention to their sleep: ask calmly how they are sleeping, what helps them rest, and whether they would like support raising it with their healthcare team. It also matters to nurture the relationships they find satisfying and their sense of contributing something of value. In this two-year longitudinal study, 598 autistic adults completed online questionnaires; sleep problems were the strongest predictor of later quality of life, and social satisfaction seemed to buffer that link. Limits: the data were self-reported online, show associations rather than causes, and will not apply equally to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det vara värt att uppmärksamma sömnen: fråga lugnt hur hen sover, vad som hjälper hen att vila och om hen vill ha stöd att ta upp det med sin vård. Det är också viktigt att värna de relationer hen själv upplever som givande och känslan av att bidra med något värdefullt. I denna tvååriga longitudinella studie besvarade 598 autistiska vuxna enkäter på nätet; sömnproblem var den starkaste förutsägaren av senare livskvalitet, och social tillfredsställelse tycktes dämpa sambandet. Begränsningar: uppgifterna är självrapporterade via nätet, visar samband snarare än orsaker och gäller inte alla personer på samma sätt.

title: 'People like me don't get support': Autistic adults' experiences of support and treatment for mental health difficulties, self-injury and suicidality.
authors: Camm-Crosbie L, Bradley L, Shaw R, Baron-Cohen S, Cassidy S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autistic people are at high risk of mental health problems, self-injury and suicidality. However, no studies have explored autistic peoples' experiences of treatment and support for these difficulties. In partnership with a steering group of autistic adults, an online survey was developed to explore these individuals' experiences of treatment and support for mental health problems, self-injury and suicidality for the first time. A total of 200 autistic adults (122 females, 77 males and 1 unreported) aged 18-67 (mean = 38.9 years, standard deviation = 11.5), without co-occurring intellectual disability, completed the online survey. Thematic analysis of open-ended questions resulted in an overarching theme that individually tailored treatment and support was both beneficial and desirable, which consisted of three underlying themes: (1) difficulties in accessing treatment and support; (2) lack of understanding and knowledge of autistic people with co-occurring mental health difficulties and (3) appropriate treatment and support, or lack of, impacted autistic people's well-being and likelihood of seeing suicide as their future. Findings demonstrate an urgent need for autism treatment pathways in mental health services.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a la que acompañas atraviesa un momento difícil de salud mental, autolesiones o pensamientos suicidas, pide ayuda que se adapte a ella: comunicación clara, ajustes sensoriales y profesionales que conozcan el autismo. Vale la pena insistir si el primer servicio no encaja, y tomar en serio lo que ella dice que le funciona. En este estudio, 200 adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual respondieron una encuesta en línea diseñada junto con personas autistas; contaron barreras de acceso y falta de comprensión, y que el apoyo adecuado mejoraba su bienestar. Sus límites: fue una encuesta voluntaria, sin personas con discapacidad intelectual, y no evaluó tratamientos concretos.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support is struggling with mental health, self-injury or suicidal thoughts, look for help that fits them: clear communication, sensory adjustments and professionals who understand autism. It is worth persisting if the first service does not fit, and taking seriously what they say works for them. In this study, 200 autistic adults without intellectual disability answered an online survey co-designed with autistic people; they described barriers to access and lack of understanding, and said appropriate support improved their well-being and hope. Limits: it was a voluntary online survey, excluded people with intellectual disability, and did not test specific treatments.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar mår psykiskt dåligt, skadar sig själv eller har självmordstankar, sök hjälp som passar just hen: tydlig kommunikation, sensoriska anpassningar och personal som förstår autism. Det är värt att fortsätta söka om den första mottagningen inte passar, och att ta på allvar vad personen själv säger hjälper. I studien svarade 200 autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning på en webbenkät som utformats tillsammans med autistiska personer; de beskrev svårigheter att få hjälp och bristande förståelse, och att rätt stöd stärkte välbefinnande och hopp. Begränsningar: frivillig webbenkät, personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning ingick inte, och specifika behandlingar prövades inte.

title: A Systematic Review of What Barriers and Facilitators Prevent and Enable Physical Healthcare Services Access for Autistic Adults.
authors: Mason D, Ingham B, Urbanowicz A, Michael C, Birtles H, Woodbury-Smith M, Brown T, James I, Scarlett C, Nicolaidis C, Parr JR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic people are more likely to: be diagnosed with a range of physical health conditions (i.e. cardio-vascular disease); experience premature mortality (for most disease categories); and experience barriers to effectively accessing healthcare. This systematic review sought to identify studies that report on barriers and facilitators to physical healthcare access for autistic people. A total of 3111 records were screened and six studies were included: two quantitative, two qualitative, and two mixed-methodology studies. Patient-provider communication, sensory sensitivities, and executive functioning/planning issues emerged as important barriers to healthcare. Recommendations for clinicians and those planning services are discussed.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar preparar juntos una nota breve con los síntomas y preguntas, pedir la cita a una hora tranquila, avisar de sensibilidades sensoriales (luces, ruido, tacto) y solicitar que el profesional explique los pasos con claridad o por escrito. Organizar la cita, el transporte y el seguimiento también puede repartirse con apoyo. Esta revisión sistemática reunió seis estudios con adultos autistas y encontró que la comunicación con el profesional, la sensorialidad y la planificación eran barreras importantes para acceder a la atención física. Sus límites: pocos estudios, métodos distintos, y cada persona puede necesitar apoyos diferentes.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to prepare a short note together with symptoms and questions, ask for a quiet appointment time, mention sensory sensitivities (lights, noise, touch) and request that the clinician explain each step clearly or in writing. Booking, travel and follow-up can also be shared with support. This systematic review brought together six studies with autistic adults and found that patient-clinician communication, sensory experiences and planning were key barriers to physical healthcare. Its limits: very few studies, mixed methods, and each person may need different supports.
sheet.sv: Inför ett läkarbesök kan det hjälpa att tillsammans skriva en kort lapp med symtom och frågor, be om en lugn tid, berätta om sensoriska känsligheter (ljus, ljud, beröring) och be vårdpersonalen förklara varje steg tydligt eller skriftligt. Bokning, resa och uppföljning kan också delas upp med stöd. Denna systematiska översikt samlade sex studier med autistiska vuxna och fann att kommunikation med vårdpersonal, sensoriska upplevelser och planering var viktiga hinder för fysisk vård. Begränsningar: mycket få studier, blandade metoder, och varje person kan behöva olika stöd.

title: Risk Factors for Unhealthy Weight Gain and Obesity among Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Dhaliwal KK, Orsso CE, Richard C, Haqq AM, Zwaigenbaum L
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a developmental disorder characterized by social and communication deficits and repetitive behaviors. Children with ASD are also at a higher risk for developing overweight or obesity than children with typical development (TD). Childhood obesity has been associated with adverse health outcomes, including insulin resistance, diabetes, heart disease, and certain cancers. Importantly some key factors that play a mediating role in these higher rates of obesity include lifestyle factors and biological influences, as well as secondary comorbidities and medications. This review summarizes current knowledge about behavioral and lifestyle factors that could contribute to unhealthy weight gain in children with ASD, as well as the current state of knowledge of emerging risk factors such as the possible influence of sleep problems, the gut microbiome, endocrine influences and maternal metabolic disorders. We also discuss some of the clinical implications of these risk factors and areas for future research.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa el peso de tu hijo autista, puede ayudar mirar el conjunto con calma: sueño, actividad física que disfrute, alimentación selectiva y posibles efectos de medicamentos. Llevar unas notas sencillas sobre sueño, comidas y movimiento puede facilitar una conversación tranquila con el equipo de salud, sin culpas ni dietas estrictas. Esta revisión resume investigaciones previas sobre factores que podrían contribuir al aumento de peso en niños autistas, incluidos el sueño, la microbiota intestinal, las hormonas y la salud metabólica materna. Su límite: no aporta datos nuevos y muchos de estos factores emergentes aún están poco estudiados, así que no se aplican igual a cada niño.
sheet.en: If you are concerned about your autistic child's weight, it can help to look calmly at the whole picture: sleep, physical activity they actually enjoy, selective eating and possible medication side effects. Keeping simple notes on sleep, meals and movement can support a relaxed conversation with your health team, without blame or strict diets. This review summarises earlier research on factors that may contribute to weight gain in autistic children, including sleep, gut microbiome, hormones and maternal metabolic health. Its limit: it adds no new data, and many of these emerging factors are still poorly understood, so they will not apply the same way to every child.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för ditt autistiska barns vikt kan det hjälpa att lugnt se helheten: sömn, rörelse som barnet faktiskt tycker om, selektivt ätande och möjliga biverkningar av läkemedel. Enkla anteckningar om sömn, måltider och rörelse kan underlätta ett lugnt samtal med vården, utan skuld eller strikta dieter. Den här översikten sammanfattar tidigare forskning om faktorer som kan bidra till viktuppgång hos autistiska barn, bland annat sömn, tarmflora, hormoner och mammans metabola hälsa. Begränsning: den tillför inga nya data och många av de nya faktorerna är fortfarande dåligt utforskade, så de gäller inte på samma sätt för alla barn.

title: Linking knowledge and attitudes: Determining neurotypical knowledge about and attitudes towards autism.
authors: Kuzminski R, Netto J, Wilson J, Falkmer T, Chamberlain A, Falkmer M
abstract: "Why are neurotypicals so pig-ignorant about autism?" an autistic person wrote on the Curtin Autism Research Group's on-line portal as a response to a call for research questions. Co-produced with an autistic researcher, knowledge about and attitudes towards autism were analysed from 1,054 completed surveys, representing the Australian neurotypical adult population. The majority, 81.5% of participants had a high level of knowledge and 81.3% of participants had a strong positive attitude towards autism. Neither age, nor education level had an impact on attitudes. However, attitudes were influenced by knowledge about 'Societal Views and Ideas'; 'What it Could be Like to Have Autism'; and the demographic variables 'Knowing and having spent time around someone with autism'; and gender (women having more positive attitudes than men). Thus, targeted interventions, geared more towards men than women, to increase knowledge about autism could further improve attitudes and increase acceptance of the autistic community.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: las actitudes hacia el autismo mejoran cuando la gente entiende cómo puede ser la vida de una persona autista y pasa tiempo con ella. Mañana puede compartir con familiares, docentes o vecinos algo concreto sobre su hijo o hija (qué le ayuda, qué le cuesta), y crear ocasiones tranquilas de convivencia; los hombres del entorno quizá se beneficien especialmente. Evidencia: encuesta coproducida con un investigador autista, con 1.054 adultos neurotípicos australianos; la mayoría mostró buen conocimiento y actitudes positivas. Límites: es una encuesta en un solo país, mide lo que la gente declara y no demuestra que informar cambie la conducta real.
sheet.en: The practical point: attitudes towards autism improve when people understand what life can be like for an autistic person and spend time with them. Tomorrow you might share something concrete with relatives, teachers or neighbours about your child (what helps, what is hard) and create calm chances to spend time together; men around you may benefit especially. Evidence: a survey co-produced with an autistic researcher, involving 1,054 neurotypical Australian adults; most showed good knowledge and positive attitudes. Limits: it is a single-country survey, measures what people report, and does not show that sharing information changes real behaviour.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: attityder till autism blir bättre när människor förstår hur livet kan vara för en autistisk person och tillbringar tid tillsammans. I morgon kan du berätta något konkret för släkt, lärare eller grannar om ditt barn (vad som hjälper, vad som är svårt) och skapa lugna tillfällen att umgås; män i omgivningen kan ha särskild nytta av det. Evidens: en enkät som utformats tillsammans med en autistisk forskare, med 1 054 neurotypiska vuxna i Australien; de flesta hade god kunskap och positiva attityder. Begränsningar: enkäten gäller ett land, mäter självrapporterade svar och visar inte att information förändrar verkligt beteende.

title: Depression and anxiety in parents of children with intellectual and developmental disabilities: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Scherer N, Verhey I, Kuper H
abstract: Introduction Although caring for a child with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) can have positive outcomes, parents may be at a greater risk of depression and anxiety, due to a number of associated stressors, such as increased caregiver demands and financial strain. This systematic review updates previous data, exploring the relationship between parenting a child with IDD and parental depression and anxiety. Methods Five electronic databases were searched for eligible English-language articles, published between January 2004 and July 2018. All epidemiological study designs were eligible, provided the level of depression and/or anxiety was compared between parents of children (aged Results Of the 5,839 unique records screened, 19 studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria. The majority of studies were conducted in high-income (n = 8, 42%) or upper-middle income countries (n = 10, 53%). Of the 19 studies, 69% focused on parents of children with cerebral palsy (n = 7, 37%) or autism (n = 6, 32%). Nearly all studies found a positive association between parenting a child with IDD and depression (n = 18, 95%) and anxiety (n = 9, 90%) symptoms. Factors associated with higher levels of depression symptoms amongst parents of children with IDD included disability severity (n = 8, 78%) and lower household income (n = 4, 80%). Approximately one third (31%) of parents of children with IDD reach the clinical cut-off score for moderate depression, compared with 7% of parents of children without IDD. 31% of parents of children with IDD reach the cut-off score for moderate anxiety, compared with 14% of parents of children without IDD. The meta-analyses demonstrated moderate effect sizes for elevated depression amongst parents of children with autism and cerebral palsy. Conclusions Results indicate elevated levels of depressive symptoms amongst parents of children with IDD. Quality concerns amongst the existing literature support the need for further research, especially in low- and middle-income countries.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño con discapacidad intelectual o del desarrollo, tu propio bienestar también importa. Sentirte agotado, triste o ansioso es frecuente y no es un fallo personal: conviene hablarlo con tu médico, buscar apoyo práctico (respiro, grupos de familias, ayudas económicas) y reservar pequeños momentos para ti. Esta revisión sistemática con metaanálisis reunió 19 estudios; cerca de un tercio de los padres de niños con discapacidad, incluidos niños autistas, superaba el umbral de depresión moderada, frente al 7% de otros padres, y los ingresos bajos se asociaban a más síntomas. Límites: estudios de calidad desigual, solo en inglés y pocos de países de ingresos bajos; no describe a cada familia.
sheet.en: If you care for a child with an intellectual or developmental disability, your own wellbeing matters too. Feeling worn out, low or anxious is common and not a personal failing: it is worth talking to your doctor, seeking practical support (respite, family groups, financial help) and protecting small moments for yourself. This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled 19 studies; about one third of parents of disabled children, including autistic children, reached the cut-off for moderate depression, compared with 7% of other parents, and lower income was linked to more symptoms. Limits: study quality varied, only English-language papers were included, and few came from low-income countries; it does not describe every family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett barn med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller utvecklingsrelaterad funktionsnedsättning spelar ditt eget mående också roll. Att känna sig utmattad, nedstämd eller orolig är vanligt och inget personligt misslyckande: prata gärna med din läkare, sök praktiskt stöd (avlösning, föräldragrupper, ekonomiskt stöd) och skydda små stunder för dig själv. Denna systematiska översikt med metaanalys samlade 19 studier; ungefär en tredjedel av föräldrarna till barn med funktionsnedsättning, även autistiska barn, nådde gränsen för måttlig depression, jämfört med 7 % av andra föräldrar, och lägre inkomst hängde ihop med fler symtom. Begränsningar: studiernas kvalitet varierade, bara engelskspråkiga artiklar ingick och få kom från låginkomstländer; resultaten beskriver inte varje familj.

title: Association Between Gut Microbiota and Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Xu M, Xu X, Li J, Li F
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by stereotyped behavior and deficits in communication and social interactions. Gastrointestinal (GI) dysfunction is an ASD-associated comorbidity, implying a potential role of the gut microbiota in ASD GI pathophysiology. Several recent studies found that autistic individuals harbor an altered bacterial gut microbiota. In some cases, remodeling the gut microbiota by antibiotic administration and microbiota transfer therapy reportedly alleviated the symptoms of ASD. However, there is little consensus on specific bacterial species that are similarly altered across individual studies. The aim of this study is to summarize previously published data and analyze the alteration of the relative abundance of bacterial genera in the gut microbiota in controls and individuals with ASD using meta-analysis. We analyzed nine studies, including 254 patients with ASD, and found that children with ASD had lower percentages of Akkermansia , Bacteroides , Bifidobacterium , and Parabacteroides and a higher percentage of Faecalibacterium in the total detected microflora compared to controls. In contrast, children with ASD had lower abundance of Enterococcus , Escherichia coli , Bacteroides , and Bifidobacterium and higher abundance of Lactobacillus . This meta-analysis suggests an association between ASD and alteration of microbiota composition and warrants additional prospective cohort studies to evaluate the association of bacterial changes with ASD symptoms, which would provide further evidence for the precise microbiological treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene molestias digestivas (estreñimiento, diarrea, dolor de barriga), vale la pena tomarlas en serio y comentarlas con su pediatra: pueden afectar al sueño, al ánimo y a la comodidad diaria. No hace falta cambiar la dieta ni comprar probióticos por tu cuenta; anotar síntomas y comidas puede ayudar en la consulta. Este metaanálisis reunió nueve estudios con 254 niños autistas y encontró diferencias en algunas bacterias intestinales respecto a otros niños. Sus límites: los estudios eran pequeños y variados, solo muestran asociación, no causa, y no prueban que ningún tratamiento funcione para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has digestive discomfort (constipation, diarrhoea, tummy pain), it is worth taking seriously and raising with their doctor: gut problems can affect sleep, mood and everyday comfort. There is no need to change their diet or buy probiotics on your own; keeping a simple note of symptoms and meals can help at the appointment. This meta-analysis pooled nine studies including 254 autistic children and found differences in some gut bacteria compared with other children. Its limits: the studies were small and varied, they show an association rather than a cause, and they do not prove any treatment works for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har besvär med magen (förstoppning, diarré, magont) är det värt att ta det på allvar och ta upp det med barnets läkare: magbesvär kan påverka sömn, humör och vardagligt välmående. Du behöver inte ändra kosten eller köpa probiotika på egen hand; att anteckna symtom och måltider kan underlätta vid besöket. Denna metaanalys sammanställde nio studier med 254 autistiska barn och fann skillnader i vissa tarmbakterier jämfört med andra barn. Begränsningar: studierna var små och olika, de visar ett samband snarare än en orsak, och de bevisar inte att någon behandling fungerar för alla.

title: State of the Field: Differentiating Intellectual Disability From Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Thurm A, Farmer C, Salzman E, Lord C, Bishop S
abstract: The topic of this special issue on secondary versus idiopathic autism allows for discussion of how different groups may come to manifest autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ASD-like symptoms despite important etiological differences. A related issue is that, because many of the social communication deficits that define ASD represent a failure to acquire developmentally expected skills, these same deficits would be expected to occur to some extent in all individuals with intellectual disability (ID). Thus, regardless of etiology, ASD symptoms may appear across groups of individuals with vastly different profiles of underlying deficits and strengths. In this focused review, we consider the impact of ID on the diagnosis of ASD. We discuss behavioral distinctions between ID and ASD, in light of the diagnostic criterion mandating that ASD should not be diagnosed if symptoms are accounted for by ID or general developmental delay. We review the evolution of the autism diagnosis and ASD diagnostic tools to understand how this distinction has been conceptualized previously. We then consider ways that operationalized criteria may be beneficial for making the clinical distinction between ID with and without ASD. Finally, we consider the impact of the blurred diagnostic boundaries between ID and ASD on the study of secondary versus idiopathic ASD. Especially pertinent to this discussion are findings that a diagnosis of ID in the context of an ASD diagnosis may be one of the strongest indicators that an associated condition or specific etiological factor is present (i.e., secondary autism).

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija tiene discapacidad intelectual, algunas diferencias en comunicación social pueden deberse a su ritmo general de desarrollo y no necesariamente al autismo. Puede ayudar pedir a los profesionales que expliquen cómo distinguen ambas cosas y que comparen sus habilidades sociales con su nivel de desarrollo, no solo con su edad. Cuando hay autismo y discapacidad intelectual juntos, vale la pena preguntar si conviene explorar causas asociadas, como factores genéticos. Esto es una revisión narrativa de investigaciones y herramientas diagnósticas, sin participantes nuevos. Su límite: ofrece reflexiones y propuestas, no criterios definitivos, y cada persona tiene un perfil propio.
sheet.en: If your child has an intellectual disability, some differences in social communication may reflect their overall developmental pace rather than autism specifically. It can help to ask professionals how they tell the two apart, and to compare social skills with your child's developmental level, not just their age. When autism and intellectual disability occur together, it may be worth asking whether exploring associated causes, such as genetic factors, makes sense. This is a narrative review of earlier research and diagnostic tools, with no new participants. Its limit: it offers reflections and proposals, not settled criteria, and every person has their own profile.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har en intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kan vissa skillnader i social kommunikation hänga ihop med barnets övergripande utvecklingstakt snarare än specifikt med autism. Det kan hjälpa att fråga professionella hur de skiljer på de två och att jämföra sociala färdigheter med barnets utvecklingsnivå, inte bara ålder. När autism och intellektuell funktionsnedsättning finns samtidigt kan det vara värt att fråga om det är meningsfullt att utreda bakomliggande orsaker, till exempel genetiska. Detta är en översikt över tidigare forskning och diagnosverktyg, utan nya deltagare. Begränsning: den ger resonemang och förslag, inte fastställda kriterier, och varje person har sin egen profil.

title: Changing Developmental Trajectories of Toddlers With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Strategies for Bridging Research to Community Practice.
authors: Wetherby AM, Woods J, Guthrie W, Delehanty A, Brown JA, Morgan L, Holland RD, Schatschneider C, Lord C
journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
abstract: Purpose The need for community-viable, evidence-based intervention strategies for toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a national priority. The purpose of this research forum article is to identify gaps in intervention research and needs in community practice for toddlers with ASD, incorporate published findings from a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of the Early Social Interaction (ESI) model (Wetherby et al., 2014) to illustrate community-based intervention, report new findings on child active engagement from the ESI RCT, and offer solutions to bridge the research-to-community practice gap. Method Research findings were reviewed to identify gaps in the evidence base for toddlers with ASD. Published and new findings from the multisite ESI RCT compared the effects of two different ESI conditions for 82 toddlers with ASD to teach parents how to support active engagement in natural environments. Results The RCT of the ESI model was the only parent-implemented intervention that reported differential treatment effects on standardized measures of child outcomes, including social communication, developmental level, and adaptive behavior. A new measure of active engagement in the natural environment was found to be sensitive to change in 3 months for young toddlers with ASD and to predict outcomes on the standardized measures of child outcomes. Strategies for utilizing the Autism Navigator collection of web-based courses and tools using extensive video footage for families and professional development are offered for scaling up in community settings to change developmental trajectories of toddlers with ASD. Conclusions Current health care and education systems are challenged to provide intervention of adequate intensity for toddlers with ASD. The use of innovative technology can increase acceleration of access to evidence-based early intervention for toddlers with ASD that addresses health disparities, enables immediate response as soon as ASD is suspected, and rapidly bridges the research-to-practice gap.

sheet.es: Durante las rutinas diarias (comer, bañarse, jugar, vestirse), puedes buscar momentos para compartir atención con tu hijo o hija pequeño autista: seguir su interés, esperar su respuesta y disfrutar juntos. Pequeños momentos de participación activa en casa pueden sumar. Herramientas en línea con vídeos, como Autism Navigator, pueden ayudarte a aprender estas estrategias sin esperar meses. Evidencia: es una revisión que incluye un ensayo controlado con 82 niños autistas pequeños y sus familias, en el que los padres aprendían a apoyar la participación en entornos naturales. Límites: los autores desarrollaron el modelo que evalúan, el grupo era reducido y no todo funciona igual para cada niño o familia.
sheet.en: During everyday routines (meals, bath, play, getting dressed), you can look for moments to share attention with your autistic toddler: follow their interest, wait for their response, and enjoy the activity together. Small moments of active engagement at home can add up. Video-based online tools such as Autism Navigator may help you learn these strategies without waiting months for services. Evidence: this is a review that includes a randomised controlled trial with 82 autistic toddlers and their families, where parents learned to support engagement in natural settings. Limits: the authors developed the model they evaluate, the group was fairly small, and no approach works the same for every child or family.
sheet.sv: Under vardagens rutiner (måltider, bad, lek, påklädning) kan du leta efter stunder att dela uppmärksamhet med ditt autistiska småbarn: följ barnets intresse, vänta in svaret och njut av aktiviteten tillsammans. Små stunder av aktivt engagemang hemma kan göra skillnad över tid. Videobaserade webbverktyg som Autism Navigator kan hjälpa dig att lära dig strategierna utan att vänta i månader. Evidens: detta är en översikt som inkluderar en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 82 autistiska småbarn och deras familjer, där föräldrar lärde sig stödja engagemang i naturliga miljöer. Begränsningar: författarna har själva utvecklat modellen de utvärderar, gruppen var ganska liten och inget arbetssätt passar alla barn eller familjer.

title: Temporal Changes in Effect Sizes of Studies Comparing Individuals With and Without Autism: A Meta-analysis.
authors: Rødgaard EM, Jensen K, Vergnes JN, Soulières I, Mottron L
abstract: Importance The definition and nature of autism have been highly debated, as exemplified by several revisions of the DSM (DSM-III, DSM-IIIR, DSM-IV, and DSM-5) criteria. There has recently been a move from a categorical view toward a spectrum-based view. These changes have been accompanied by a steady increase in the prevalence of the condition. Changes in the definition of autism that may increase heterogeneity could affect the results of autism research; specifically, a broadening of the population with autism could result in decreasing effect sizes of group comparison studies. Objective To examine the correlation between publication year and effect size of autism-control group comparisons across several domains of published autism neurocognitive research. Data sources This meta-analysis investigated 11 meta-analyses obtained through a systematic search of PubMed for meta-analyses published from January 1, 1966, through January 27, 2019, using the search string autism AND (meta-analysis OR meta-analytic). The last search was conducted on January 27, 2019. Study selection Meta-analyses were included if they tested the significance of group differences between individuals with autism and control individuals on a neurocognitive construct. Meta-analyses were only included if the tested group difference was significant and included data with a span of at least 15 years. Data extraction and synthesis Data were extracted and analyzed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) reporting guideline using fixed-effects models. Main outcomes and measures Estimated slope of the correlation between publication year and effect size, controlling for differences in methods, sample size, and study quality. Results The 11 meta-analyses included data from a total of 27 723 individuals. Demographic data such as sex and age were not available for the entire data set. Seven different psychological and neurologic constructs were analyzed based on data from these meta-analyses. Downward temporal trends for effect size were found for all constructs (slopes: -0.067 to -0.003), with the trend being significant in 5 of 7 cases: emotion recognition (slope: -0.028 [95% CI, -0.048 to -0.007]), theory of mind (-0.045 [95% CI, -0.066 to -0.024]), planning (-0.067 [95% CI, -0.125 to -0.009]), P3b amplitude (-0.048 [95% CI, -0.093 to -0.004]), and brain size (-0.047 [95% CI, -0.077 to -0.016]). In contrast, 3 analogous constructs in schizophrenia, a condition that is also heterogeneous but with no reported increase in prevalence, did not show a similar trend. Conclusions and relevance The findings suggest that differences between individuals with autism and those without the diagnosis have decreased over time and that possible changes in the definition of autism from a narrowly defined and homogenous population toward an inclusive and heterogeneous population may reduce our capacity to build mechanistic models of the condition.

sheet.es: Si lee que las personas autistas «tienen menos teoría de la mente» o «reconocen peor las emociones», tómelo con cautela: esas diferencias medias se han ido reduciendo con los años, a medida que la definición de autismo se amplió. Lo que dice un estudio sobre «el grupo» puede no describir a su hijo o a usted; observe a la persona concreta, sus fortalezas y lo que necesita. Esta es un metaanálisis de 11 metaanálisis con datos de 27 723 personas, que comparó grupos autistas y no autistas a lo largo de décadas. Límites: faltaban datos de edad y sexo, y analiza tendencias en publicaciones, no cambios en personas reales.
sheet.en: If you read that autistic people "lack theory of mind" or "struggle to recognise emotions", hold it lightly: these average group differences have shrunk over the years as the definition of autism broadened. What research says about "the group" may not describe your child or you; look at the actual person, their strengths and what they need. This is a meta-analysis of 11 earlier meta-analyses, covering 27,723 people, comparing autistic and non-autistic groups across decades. Limits: age and sex data were missing, and it tracks trends in published studies, not changes in real individuals.
sheet.sv: Om du läser att autistiska personer "saknar mentaliseringsförmåga" eller "har svårt att känna igen känslor", ta det med en nypa salt: sådana genomsnittliga gruppskillnader har minskat över åren i takt med att autismdefinitionen breddats. Det forskningen säger om "gruppen" behöver inte stämma för ditt barn eller dig; utgå från personen, dennes styrkor och behov. Detta är en metaanalys av 11 tidigare metaanalyser med data från 27 723 personer, som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska grupper över flera decennier. Begränsningar: uppgifter om ålder och kön saknades, och studien följer trender i publicerad forskning, inte förändringar hos enskilda människor.

title: Genetic Causes and Modifiers of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Rylaarsdam L, Guemez-Gamboa A
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is one of the most prevalent neurodevelopmental disorders, affecting an estimated 1 in 59 children. ASD is highly genetically heterogeneous and may be caused by both inheritable and de novo gene variations. In the past decade, hundreds of genes have been identified that contribute to the serious deficits in communication, social cognition, and behavior that patients often experience. However, these only account for 10-20% of ASD cases, and patients with similar pathogenic variants may be diagnosed on very different levels of the spectrum. In this review, we will describe the genetic landscape of ASD and discuss how genetic modifiers such as copy number variation, single nucleotide polymorphisms, and epigenetic alterations likely play a key role in modulating the phenotypic spectrum of ASD patients. We also consider how genetic modifiers can alter convergent signaling pathways and lead to impaired neural circuitry formation. Lastly, we review sex-linked modifiers and clinical implications. Further understanding of these mechanisms is crucial for both comprehending ASD and for developing novel therapies.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas «por qué» tu hijo o hija es autista, esta revisión sugiere que no existe una sola causa: cientos de genes, heredados o nuevos, influyen, y nada apunta a algo que la familia hiciera mal. Incluso personas con la misma variante genética pueden vivir el autismo de formas muy distintas, así que conviene centrarse en las necesidades y fortalezas concretas de tu familiar, no en una etiqueta genética. Si os ofrecen pruebas genéticas, puedes preguntar con calma qué información aportarían. Se trata de una revisión de estudios previos, no de un estudio con participantes nuevos. Sus límites: los genes conocidos explican solo un 10-20 % de los casos y usa un lenguaje centrado en déficits.
sheet.en: If you wonder "why" your child is autistic, this review suggests there is no single cause: hundreds of genes, inherited or new, play a part, and nothing points to something the family did wrong. Even people with the same genetic variant can experience autism very differently, so it helps to focus on your family member's actual needs and strengths rather than a genetic label. If genetic testing is offered, you can calmly ask what it would actually tell you. This is a review of earlier research, not a study with new participants. Its limits: known genes explain only about 10-20% of cases, and it uses deficit-focused language.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar ”varför” ditt barn är autistiskt pekar denna översikt på att det inte finns en enda orsak: hundratals gener, ärvda eller nya, spelar in, och inget tyder på att familjen gjort något fel. Även personer med samma genetiska variant kan uppleva autism mycket olika, så det hjälper att utgå från din närståendes faktiska behov och styrkor snarare än en genetisk etikett. Om ni erbjuds genetisk utredning kan du lugnt fråga vad den faktiskt skulle ge. Detta är en översikt av tidigare forskning, inte en studie med nya deltagare. Begränsningar: kända gener förklarar bara cirka 10–20 % av fallen, och texten använder ett bristfokuserat språk.

title: Eating as an autistic adult: An exploratory qualitative study.
authors: Kinnaird E, Norton C, Pimblett C, Stewart C, Tchanturia K
abstract: Background Although eating difficulties are known to be common in children on the autism spectrum, there is a lack of research on whether these behaviours persist or change into adulthood. Emerging evidence suggests that autistic adults may experience higher levels of disordered eating than the general population, indicating the impact of autism on eating in this adult population warrants further exploration. Method This study interviewed 12 autistic adults about their eating habits, with a focus on the continuing or changing presence of behaviours often seen in autistic children such as sensory sensitivity or a preference for routines. Interviews were transcribed and analysed using thematic analysis. Results Overall, participants suggested that autism did continue to impact their eating into adulthood, particularly in the areas of sensory sensitivity, medical difficulties, executive functioning difficulties, and rigidity, but that they had learned to adapt so that these issues no longer represented a problem. However, a minority of participants did feel that their autism had a negative effect on their eating, particularly those diagnosed with eating disorders. Additionally, eating behaviours associated with autism were identified as potentially contributing to having an unhealthy body weight. Conclusions Certain traits associated with autism, such as cognitive rigidity and sensory sensitivity, could potentially continue to influence the eating behaviours of autistic adults. These traits are typically experienced as differences which can be adapted around and managed, rather than specific problems. However, these traits can potentially contribute to difficulties such as disordered eating and weight gain, and the implications of these should be explored by future research.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas es adulta, sus diferencias al comer (sensibilidad a texturas u olores, preferencia por rutinas, dificultad para planificar comidas) pueden seguir presentes, y muchas personas aprenden estrategias propias que funcionan. Pregunta qué le ayuda: comidas seguras, menús repetidos, preparación sencilla. Respeta esas adaptaciones y presta atención, sin alarmarte, si comer le causa malestar o cambios de peso; ahí puede valer la pena buscar apoyo profesional. La evidencia viene de entrevistas cualitativas con 12 adultos autistas que describieron su experiencia. Es un grupo pequeño y exploratorio, así que no representa a todas las personas autistas ni mide causas.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support is an adult, their eating differences (sensitivity to textures or smells, preference for routines, difficulty planning meals) may still be present, and many people develop their own strategies that work. Ask what helps: safe foods, repeated menus, simple preparation. Respect those adaptations, and calmly notice if eating causes distress or weight changes; that may be a moment to seek professional support. The evidence comes from qualitative interviews with 12 autistic adults describing their own experiences. It is a small, exploratory group, so it does not represent all autistic people or measure causes.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar är vuxen kan skillnader kring mat (känslighet för konsistens eller lukt, behov av rutiner, svårt att planera måltider) finnas kvar, och många hittar egna strategier som fungerar. Fråga vad som hjälper: trygga livsmedel, återkommande menyer, enkel matlagning. Respektera anpassningarna och var lugnt uppmärksam om ätandet orsakar obehag eller viktförändringar; då kan professionellt stöd vara värt att söka. Underlaget kommer från kvalitativa intervjuer med 12 autistiska vuxna om deras egna erfarenheter. Gruppen är liten och studien utforskande, så den representerar inte alla autistiska personer och mäter inte orsaker.

title: Association of Cesarean Delivery With Risk of Neurodevelopmental and Psychiatric Disorders in the Offspring: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Zhang T, Sidorchuk A, Sevilla-Cermeño L, Vilaplana-Pérez A, Chang Z, Larsson H, Mataix-Cols D, Fernández de la Cruz L
abstract: Importance Birth by cesarean delivery is increasing globally, particularly cesarean deliveries without medical indication. Children born via cesarean delivery may have an increased risk of negative health outcomes, but the evidence for psychiatric disorders is incomplete. Objective To evaluate the association between cesarean delivery and risk of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders in the offspring. Data sources Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to December 19, 2018. Search terms included all main mental disorders in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (Fifth Edition). Study selection Two researchers independently selected observational studies that examined the association between cesarean delivery and neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders in the offspring. Data extraction and synthesis Two researchers independently extracted data according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) and Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) reporting guidelines and assessed study quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.
