Den är liten och utforskande, med begränsad mångfald och få personer med större stödbehov, så den beskriver inte alla.

claim.es: El 'burnout autista' —agotamiento profundo, pérdida de habilidades, menos tolerancia a estímulos— lo describen adultos autistas como resultado de exigencias sostenidas sin apoyo.
claim.en: 'Autistic burnout' — deep exhaustion, loss of skills, less tolerance to stimuli — is described by autistic adults as the result of sustained demands without support.
claim.sv: 'Autistisk utmattning' — djup trötthet, förlust av färdigheter, mindre tolerans för stimuli — beskrivs av autistiska vuxna som följden av ihållande krav utan stöd.

supports.es: Reducir exigencias y carga sensorial cuando baja la capacidad, en vez de forzar.
supports.en: Reducing demands and sensory load when capacity drops, instead of pushing through.
supports.sv: Att minska krav och sensorisk belastning när kapaciteten sjunker, i stället för att pressa på.

doesNotSupport.es: Un diagnóstico clínico; es una definición desde la experiencia vivida.
doesNotSupport.en: A clinical diagnosis; this is a lived-experience definition.
doesNotSupport.sv: En klinisk diagnos; det här är en definition utifrån levd erfarenhet.

title: A Review of Default Mode Network Connectivity and Its Association With Social Cognition in Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder and Early-Onset Psychosis.
authors: Nair A, Jolliffe M, Lograsso YSS, Bearden CE
abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated substantial phenotypic overlap, notably social impairment, between autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia. However, the neural mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of social impairments across these distinct neuropsychiatric disorders has not yet been fully examined. Most neuroimaging studies to date have focused on adults with these disorders, with little known about the neural underpinnings of social impairments in younger populations. Here, we present a narrative review of the literature available through April 2020 on imaging studies of adolescents with either ASD or early-onset psychosis (EOP), to better understand the shared and unique neural mechanisms of social difficulties across diagnosis from a developmental framework. We specifically focus on functional connectivity studies of the default mode network (DMN), as the most extensively studied brain network relevant to social cognition across both groups. Our review included 29 studies of DMN connectivity in adolescents with ASD (Mean age range = 11.2-21.6 years), and 14 studies in adolescents with EOP (Mean age range = 14.2-24.3 years). Of these, 15 of 29 studies in ASD adolescents found predominant underconnectivity when examining DMN connectivity. In contrast, findings were mixed in adolescents with EOP, with five of 14 studies reporting DMN underconnectivity, and an additional six of 14 studies reporting both under- and over-connectivity of the DMN. Specifically, intra-DMN networks were more frequently underconnected in ASD, but overconnected in EOP. On the other hand, inter-DMN connectivity patterns were mixed (both under- and over-connected) for each group, especially DMN connectivity with frontal, sensorimotor, and temporoparietal regions in ASD, and with frontal, temporal, subcortical, and cerebellar regions in EOP. Finally, disrupted DMN connectivity appeared to be associated with social impairments in both groups, less so with other features distinct to each condition, such as repetitive behaviors/restricted interests in ASD and hallucinations/delusions in EOP. Further studies on demographically well-matched groups of adolescents with each of these conditions are needed to systematically explore additional contributing factors in DMN connectivity patterns such as clinical heterogeneity, pubertal development, and medication effects that would better inform treatment targets and facilitate prediction of outcomes in the context of these developmental neuropsychiatric conditions.

sheet.es: Para mañana: este trabajo no cambia nada de lo que hace en casa. Si su adolescente autista tiene un estilo social distinto, no es lo mismo que la psicosis; las dos condiciones pueden parecerse por fuera pero los escáneres sugieren patrones cerebrales diferentes. Si nota cambios nuevos, como percepciones inusuales o retraimiento repentino, coméntelo con su equipo profesional en lugar de suponer que es parte del autismo. Evidencia: revisión narrativa de 29 estudios de neuroimagen con adolescentes autistas y 14 con psicosis de inicio temprano. Límites: los estudios fueron pequeños y variados, los grupos no estaban bien emparejados y los hallazgos de imagen no sirven para diagnosticar ni describir a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: this paper changes nothing about daily routines at home. If your autistic teenager has a different social style, that is not the same as psychosis; the two can look alike from the outside, yet brain scans suggest different patterns. If you notice new changes, such as unusual perceptions or sudden withdrawal, raise them with your care team rather than assuming they are part of being autistic. Evidence: a narrative review of 29 brain-imaging studies with autistic adolescents and 14 with early-onset psychosis. Limits: studies were small and varied, groups were not well matched, and imaging findings cannot diagnose or describe any individual person.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon: den här studien ändrar inget i vardagen hemma. Om din autistiska tonåring har ett annorlunda socialt sätt är det inte samma sak som psykos; de två kan likna varandra utifrån, men hjärnavbildning tyder på olika mönster. Märker du nya förändringar, som ovanliga upplevelser eller plötslig tillbakadragenhet, ta upp det med vårdteamet i stället för att anta att det hör till autismen. Evidens: en narrativ översikt av 29 hjärnavbildningsstudier med autistiska ungdomar och 14 med tidigt debuterande psykos. Begränsningar: studierna var små och olika, grupperna var inte väl matchade och fynden kan inte ställa diagnos eller beskriva en enskild person.

title: Genetics of structural and functional brain changes in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Hashem S, Nisar S, Bhat AA, Yadav SK, Azeem MW, Bagga P, Fakhro K, Reddy R, Frenneaux MP, Haris M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurological and developmental disorder characterized by social impairment and restricted interactive and communicative behaviors. It may occur as an isolated disorder or in the context of other neurological, psychiatric, developmental, and genetic disorders. Due to rapid developments in genomics and imaging technologies, imaging genetics studies of ASD have evolved in the last few years. Increased risk for ASD diagnosis is found to be related to many specific single-nucleotide polymorphisms, and the study of genetic mechanisms and noninvasive imaging has opened various approaches that can help diagnose ASD at the nascent level. Identifying risk genes related to structural and functional changes in the brain of ASD patients provide a better understanding of the disease's neuropsychiatry and can help identify targets for therapeutic intervention that could be useful for the clinical management of ASD patients.

sheet.es: Lo práctico para mañana: esta investigación no cambia lo que hacéis en casa. Las diferencias genéticas y cerebrales asociadas al autismo forman parte de cómo es la persona, no son culpa de nadie ni de la crianza. Si os ofrecen pruebas genéticas o de imagen cerebral, podéis preguntar con calma qué aportarían en concreto a vuestra vida diaria. Se trata de una revisión que resume estudios previos que combinan genética e imágenes del cerebro en personas autistas. Su límite: no presenta datos nuevos, usa un lenguaje centrado en el déficit y sus posibles aplicaciones para diagnóstico o apoyo siguen siendo, por ahora, más una promesa que una herramienta disponible.
sheet.en: The practical takeaway for tomorrow: this research doesn't change what you do at home. The genetic and brain differences linked to autism are part of who the person is, and they are nobody's fault, including not the result of parenting. If you're offered genetic testing or brain imaging, it's fine to calmly ask what it would actually change in daily life. This is a review summarising earlier studies that combine genetics and brain imaging in autistic people. Its limits: it presents no new data, uses deficit-focused language, and its possible uses for diagnosis or support remain more a promise than a tool available today.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska inför i morgon: den här forskningen ändrar inte det ni gör hemma. De genetiska skillnader och skillnader i hjärnan som kopplas till autism är en del av vem personen är och inte någons fel, inte heller ett resultat av föräldraskapet. Om ni erbjuds genetiska tester eller hjärnavbildning går det bra att lugnt fråga vad det faktiskt skulle tillföra i vardagen. Detta är en översikt som sammanfattar tidigare studier där genetik och hjärnavbildning kombineras hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den bygger inte på nya data, använder ett bristfokuserat språk, och de möjliga användningarna för diagnos eller stöd är än så länge mer ett löfte än ett tillgängligt verktyg.

title: Clinical Assessment, Genetics, and Treatment Approaches in Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).
authors: Genovese A, Butler MG
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) consists of a genetically heterogenous group of neurobehavioral disorders characterized by impairment in three behavioral domains including communication, social interaction, and stereotypic repetitive behaviors. ASD affects more than 1% of children in Western societies, with diagnoses on the rise due to improved recognition, screening, clinical assessment, and diagnostic testing. We reviewed the role of genetic and metabolic factors which contribute to the causation of ASD with the use of new genetic technology. Up to 40 percent of individuals with ASD are now diagnosed with genetic syndromes or have chromosomal abnormalities including small DNA deletions or duplications, single gene conditions, or gene variants and metabolic disturbances with mitochondrial dysfunction. Although the heritability estimate for ASD is between 70 and 90%, there is a lower molecular diagnostic yield than anticipated. A likely explanation may relate to multifactorial causation with etiological heterogeneity and hundreds of genes involved with a complex interplay between inheritance and environmental factors influenced by epigenetics and capabilities to identify causative genes and their variants for ASD. Behavioral and psychiatric correlates, diagnosis and genetic evaluation with testing are discussed along with psychiatric treatment approaches and pharmacogenetics for selection of medication to treat challenging behaviors or comorbidities commonly seen in ASD. We emphasize prioritizing treatment based on targeted symptoms for individuals with ASD, as treatment will vary from patient to patient based on diagnosis, comorbidities, causation, and symptom severity.

sheet.es: Si tu familia se pregunta por la causa del autismo de tu hijo o hija, puedes hablar con el equipo de salud sobre una evaluación genética: en algunas personas encuentra una explicación útil para cuidar la salud general y planificar apoyos. Cualquier apoyo debería centrarse en las necesidades concretas de cada persona, no en un plan único para todos. Es una revisión narrativa de estudios previos sobre genética, metabolismo, diagnóstico y tratamiento; no incluyó participantes propios. Sus límites: no evalúa sistemáticamente la calidad de las pruebas, usa un enfoque médico centrado en déficits y muchas personas no obtendrán un resultado genético claro.
sheet.en: If your family wonders about the cause of your child's autism, you can ask your healthcare team about genetic evaluation: for some people it finds an explanation that helps with overall health care and planning support. Any support should focus on the specific needs of each person, not on one plan for everyone. This is a narrative review of earlier research on genetics, metabolism, diagnosis and treatment; it did not include its own participants. Its limits: it does not systematically grade the evidence, it uses a deficit-focused medical framing, and many people will not get a clear genetic result.
sheet.sv: Om din familj undrar över orsaken till ditt barns autism kan ni fråga vården om en genetisk utredning: för vissa personer ger den en förklaring som hjälper vid den allmänna hälsovården och vid planering av stöd. Allt stöd bör utgå från varje persons konkreta behov, inte från en plan för alla. Detta är en narrativ översikt av tidigare forskning om genetik, ämnesomsättning, diagnos och behandling; den hade inga egna deltagare. Begränsningar: evidensen granskas inte systematiskt, perspektivet är medicinskt och bristfokuserat, och många får inget tydligt genetiskt svar.

title: Healthcare access for autistic adults: A systematic review.
authors: Calleja S, Islam FMA, Kingsley J, McDonald R
abstract: Background People with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have an increased susceptibility for many chronic health conditions compared with their peers. An increasing number of adolescents are transitioning from pediatric to adult healthcare services. Thus, being able to access appropriate healthcare services that can not only address specific needs of the person but enable them to better manage healthcare conditions and decrease the development of preventable disease is necessary. A systematic review was conducted to identify barriers and enablers of healthcare access for autistic adults. Methods The studies included in the review were quantitative and qualitative and were published between 2003 and 2019. The participants for the review are considered to be adults (over 18 years of age) with a primary diagnosis of ASD. Results In total, 1290 studies were initially identified and 13 studies were included based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria outlined in a previous protocol paper. The analysis of these studies identified areas of concern to access appropriate healthcare, such as clinician knowledge, the environment, and life events. Conclusion Identifying the barriers to healthcare, highlights ways healthcare services can regulate scope of practice, the physical environment, and the process of managing health conditions, thus, autistic adults can strive for optimal health. This review contributes to peer-reviewed evidence for future research and up-to-date information when developing and piloting health interventions for autistic adults. Ethics and dissemination There are no human participants, data, or tissue being directly studied for the purposes of the review; therefore, ethics approval and consent to participate is not applicable. Registration and status PROSPERO 2018 CRD42018116093.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar preparar juntos una nota breve sobre cómo se comunica la persona, qué le resulta difícil del entorno (luz, ruido, esperas) y qué apoyos necesita. Pedir la primera o última cita del día, o esperar fuera, puede reducir la carga sensorial. Si el profesional sabe poco sobre autismo, compartir esa información con calma es útil. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 13 estudios (2003-2019) con adultos autistas y encontró barreras en el conocimiento clínico, el entorno y los cambios vitales, como pasar a servicios para adultos. Sus límites: pocos estudios, diseños distintos y resultados que quizá no reflejen la experiencia de cada persona ni de cada país.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to prepare a short note together about how the person communicates, what is hard about the setting (lights, noise, waiting) and what support they need. Asking for the first or last slot of the day, or waiting outside, may ease sensory load. If the clinician knows little about autism, calmly sharing that note is useful. This systematic review pooled 13 studies (2003-2019) with autistic adults and found barriers in clinician knowledge, the environment and life events such as moving to adult services. Its limits: few studies, mixed designs, and findings that may not match every person's or country's experience.
sheet.sv: Inför ett vårdbesök kan det hjälpa att tillsammans skriva en kort lapp om hur personen kommunicerar, vad som är svårt i miljön (ljus, ljud, väntan) och vilket stöd som behövs. Att be om dagens första eller sista tid, eller att vänta utomhus, kan minska den sensoriska belastningen. Om vårdpersonalen kan lite om autism är det bra att lugnt dela lappen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 13 studier (2003-2019) med autistiska vuxna och fann hinder i vårdpersonalens kunskap, miljön och livshändelser som övergången till vuxenvården. Begränsningar: få studier, olika upplägg och resultat som kanske inte stämmer för varje person eller varje land.

title: Conceptualising compensation in neurodevelopmental disorders: Reflections from autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Livingston LA, Happé F
abstract: Within research into neurodevelopmental disorders, little is known about the mechanisms underpinning changes in symptom severity across development. When the behavioural presentation of a condition improves/symptoms lessen, this may be because core underlying atypicalities in cognition/neural function have ameliorated. An alternative possibility is 'compensation'; that the behavioural presentation appears improved, despite persisting deficits at cognitive and/or neurobiological levels. There is, however, currently no agreed technical definition of compensation or its behavioural, cognitive and neural characteristics. Furthermore, its workings in neurodevelopmental disorders have not been studied directly. Here, we review current evidence for compensation in neurodevelopmental disorders, using Autism Spectrum Disorder as an example, in order to move towards a better conceptualisation of the construct. We propose a transdiagnostic framework, where compensation represents the processes responsible for an observed mismatch between behaviour and underlying cognition in a neurodevelopmental disorder, at any point in development. Further, we explore potential cognitive and neural mechanisms driving compensation and discuss the broader relevance of the concept within research and clinical settings.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista parece «estar mejor» con los años, no significa necesariamente que sus diferencias hayan desaparecido. Puede estar compensando: usando estrategias aprendidas para encajar, a menudo con gran esfuerzo. Mañana puedes preguntar con calma qué le cuesta, aunque por fuera parezca fácil, y dejar espacio para descansar después de situaciones sociales. Esta es una revisión teórica de investigaciones previas en autismo; no estudió personas directamente, sino que propone un marco para entender la compensación. Su límite: no existe aún una definición acordada y los mecanismos no se han medido de forma directa, así que no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person seems to be “doing better” over the years, it does not necessarily mean their differences have gone away. They may be compensating: using learned strategies to fit in, often with considerable effort. Tomorrow you could calmly ask what feels hard, even when it looks easy from the outside, and leave room to rest after social situations. This is a theoretical review of earlier autism research; it did not study people directly but proposes a framework for understanding compensation. Its limit: there is no agreed definition yet and the mechanisms have not been measured directly, so it does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person verkar ”må bättre” med åren betyder det inte nödvändigtvis att skillnaderna har försvunnit. Personen kan kompensera: använda inlärda strategier för att passa in, ofta med stor ansträngning. I morgon kan du lugnt fråga vad som känns svårt, även när det ser lätt ut utifrån, och ge utrymme för vila efter sociala situationer. Detta är en teoretisk översikt av tidigare autismforskning; den studerade inte personer direkt utan föreslår en modell för att förstå kompensation. Begränsning: det finns ännu ingen gemensam definition och mekanismerna har inte mätts direkt, så den beskriver inte varje person.

title: Towards a brain-based predictome of mental illness.
authors: Rashid B, Calhoun V
abstract: Neuroimaging-based approaches have been extensively applied to study mental illness in recent years and have deepened our understanding of both cognitively healthy and disordered brain structure and function. Recent advancements in machine learning techniques have shown promising outcomes for individualized prediction and characterization of patients with psychiatric disorders. Studies have utilized features from a variety of neuroimaging modalities, including structural, functional, and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging data, as well as jointly estimated features from multiple modalities, to assess patients with heterogeneous mental disorders, such as schizophrenia and autism. We use the term "predictome" to describe the use of multivariate brain network features from one or more neuroimaging modalities to predict mental illness. In the predictome, multiple brain network-based features (either from the same modality or multiple modalities) are incorporated into a predictive model to jointly estimate features that are unique to a disorder and predict subjects accordingly. To date, more than 650 studies have been published on subject-level prediction focusing on psychiatric disorders. We have surveyed about 250 studies including schizophrenia, major depression, bipolar disorder, autism spectrum disorder, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, social anxiety disorder, posttraumatic stress disorder, and substance dependence. In this review, we present a comprehensive review of recent neuroimaging-based predictomic approaches, current trends, and common shortcomings and share our vision for future directions.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: hoy no existe ningún escáner cerebral ni programa de inteligencia artificial que pueda diagnosticar el autismo de forma fiable a una persona concreta. Si alguien le ofrece una «prueba cerebral» para confirmar o descartar el autismo, conviene pedir con calma qué evidencia la respalda y seguir confiando en la evaluación clínica y en lo que conoce de su familiar. Esta es una revisión sistemática de unos 250 estudios que usaron resonancia magnética y aprendizaje automático en autismo, TDAH, depresión y otras condiciones. Su límite: los propios autores señalan muestras pequeñas, resultados poco replicados y métodos aún en fase de investigación.
sheet.en: The practical point: right now, no brain scan or artificial intelligence tool can reliably diagnose autism in an individual person. If someone offers you a "brain test" to confirm or rule out autism, it is reasonable to calmly ask what evidence supports it, and to keep trusting clinical assessment and what you know about your family member. This is a systematic review of about 250 studies that used MRI and machine learning in autism, ADHD, depression and other conditions. Its limit: the authors themselves point to small samples, results that are rarely replicated, and methods still at the research stage.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: i dag finns ingen hjärnröntgen eller AI-metod som säkert kan ställa en autismdiagnos hos en enskild person. Om någon erbjuder ett ”hjärntest” för att bekräfta eller utesluta autism är det rimligt att lugnt fråga vilket stöd det har, och att fortsätta lita på den kliniska utredningen och på det du vet om din närstående. Detta är en systematisk översikt av cirka 250 studier som använde magnetkamera och maskininlärning vid autism, adhd, depression och andra tillstånd. Begränsning: författarna pekar själva på små urval, resultat som sällan upprepats och metoder som fortfarande befinner sig på forskningsstadiet.

title: 'I never realised everybody felt as happy as I do when I am around autistic people': A thematic analysis of autistic adults' relationships with autistic and neurotypical friends and family.
authors: Crompton CJ, Hallett S, Ropar D, Flynn E, Fletcher-Watson S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Although autistic people may struggle to interact with others, many autistic people have said they find interacting with other autistic people more comfortable. To find out whether this was a common experience, we did hour-long interviews with 12 autistic adults. We asked them questions about how it feels when spending time with their friends and family, and whether it felt different depending on whether the friends and family were autistic or neurotypical. We analysed the interviews and found three common themes in what our participants said. First, they found spending with other autistic people easier and more comfortable than spending time with neurotypical people, and felt they were better understood by other autistic people. Second, autistic people often felt they were in a social minority, and in order to spend time with neurotypical friends and family, they had to conform with what the neurotypical people wanted and were used to. Third, autistic people felt like they belonged with other autistic people and that they could be themselves around them. These findings show that having time with autistic friends and family can be very beneficial for autistic people and played an important role in a happy social life.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista, vale la pena facilitar tiempo con otras personas autistas: grupos, clubes de intereses, comunidades en línea o familiares autistas. Muchas personas autistas cuentan que con sus pares se sienten comprendidas, pueden ser ellas mismas y no tienen que adaptarse constantemente a normas neurotípicas. También ayuda reducir la presión de "encajar" en reuniones familiares y respetar sus formas de comunicarse. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con entrevistas de una hora a 12 adultos autistas sobre sus relaciones con amigos y familiares autistas y neurotípicos. Límites: muestra pequeña, solo adultos que pueden participar en entrevistas; no representa a cada persona ni mide efectos a largo plazo.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it is worth making room for time with other autistic people: groups, interest clubs, online communities or autistic relatives. Many autistic people say that with autistic peers they feel understood, can be themselves and do not have to keep adapting to neurotypical expectations. It also helps to ease the pressure to "fit in" at family gatherings and to respect their ways of communicating. Evidence: a qualitative study using hour-long interviews with 12 autistic adults about relationships with autistic and neurotypical friends and family. Limits: a small sample of adults able to take part in interviews; it does not speak for every person or measure long-term effects.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det vara värt att skapa tillfällen att umgås med andra autistiska personer: grupper, intresseklubbar, nätgemenskaper eller autistiska släktingar. Många autistiska personer berättar att de med autistiska jämlikar känner sig förstådda, kan vara sig själva och slipper anpassa sig hela tiden till neurotypiska förväntningar. Det hjälper också att minska trycket att "passa in" på familjeträffar och att respektera personens sätt att kommunicera. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie med timslånga intervjuer med 12 autistiska vuxna om relationer med autistiska och neurotypiska vänner och familj. Begränsningar: litet urval av vuxna som kunde delta i intervjuer; resultaten gäller inte alla och mäter inte långsiktiga effekter.

title: 'When my autism broke': A qualitative study spotlighting autistic voices on menopause.
authors: Moseley RL, Druce T, Turner-Cobb JM
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic girls are known to struggle with the onset of menstruation, reporting that during their period, sensory sensitivities are heightened, it becomes more difficult to think clearly and control their emotions and they struggle more with everyday life and self-care. Yet surprisingly, nothing is known about how autistic women handle the menopausal transition in midlife. In non-autistic women, the menopause brings many physical changes and challenging symptoms from hot flushes to feeling more anxious and depressed. Because autistic women are already vulnerable to suicide, poor physical and mental health, and because they may already struggle with planning, controlling their emotions and coping with change, the menopause may be an especially challenging time. Yet, not one single study exists on the menopause in autism, so we conducted an online discussion (focus group) with seven autistic women. They confirmed that very little is known about menopause in autistic people, very little support is available and that menopause might be especially difficult for autistic people. Autism-related difficulties (including sensory sensitivity, socializing with others and communicating needs) were reported to worsen during the menopause, often so dramatically that some participants suggested they found it impossible to continue to mask their struggles. Participants also reported having extreme meltdowns, experiencing anxiety and depression, and feeling suicidal. This study highlights how important it is that professionals pay attention to menopause in autism, and discusses future research directions.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista cercana está en la mediana edad, la menopausia puede intensificar la sensibilidad sensorial, el cansancio social y la dificultad para comunicar necesidades. Ayuda preguntar con calma qué ha cambiado, reducir estímulos en casa, aceptar que quizá ya no pueda «enmascarar» como antes y buscar profesionales que conozcan el autismo. Si aparecen pensamientos suicidas, pedid ayuda urgente. La evidencia viene de un grupo de discusión en línea con siete mujeres autistas que compartieron sus experiencias. Es un grupo muy pequeño y autoseleccionado, así que no describe a todas las personas autistas; muestra temas importantes, no reglas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person close to you is in midlife, menopause may intensify sensory sensitivity, social exhaustion and difficulty communicating needs. It can help to calmly ask what has changed, lower sensory load at home, accept that masking may no longer be possible as before, and look for professionals who understand autism. If suicidal thoughts appear, seek urgent help. The evidence comes from an online focus group with seven autistic women sharing their experiences. It is a very small, self-selected group, so it does not describe every autistic person; it highlights important themes, not rules.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person nära dig är i medelåldern kan klimakteriet förstärka sensorisk känslighet, social utmattning och svårigheter att uttrycka behov. Det kan hjälpa att lugnt fråga vad som har förändrats, minska sinnesintryck hemma, acceptera att maskering kanske inte längre går som förut och söka vårdpersonal med kunskap om autism. Om självmordstankar dyker upp, sök hjälp akut. Underlaget är en fokusgrupp online med sju autistiska kvinnor som delade sina erfarenheter. Gruppen är mycket liten och självvald, så den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer; den lyfter viktiga teman, inte regler.

title: Alexithymia may explain the relationship between autistic traits and eating disorder psychopathology.
authors: Vuillier L, Carter Z, Teixeira AR, Moseley RL
abstract: Background Autistic people are disproportionately vulnerable to anorexia nervosa and other eating disorders (ED), and within the general population, autistic traits correlate with ED psychopathology. A putative mechanism which may underpin this heightened risk is alexithymia, a difficulty identifying and describing emotional states which is observed in both autism and ED. In two experiments with independent non-clinical samples, we explored whether alexithymia might mediate the heightened risk of eating psychopathology in individuals high in autistic traits. Methods Our first experiment used the PROCESS macro for SPSS to examine relationships between alexithymia (measured by the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20)), autistic traits (autism quotient (AQ)), and eating psychopathology (Eating Attitudes Test (EAT-26)) in 121 participants. Our second experiment (n = 300) replicated and furthered this analysis by examining moderating effects of sex and controlling for anxiety and depression as covariates. We also included an additional performance-based measure of alexithymia, the Levels of Emotional Awareness Scale (LEAS). Results Study 1 suggested that TAS-20 scores mediated the relationship between heightened autistic traits and eating psychopathology. Replication and further scrutiny of this finding, in study 2, revealed that this mediation effect was partial and specific to the female participants in this sample. The mediation effect appeared to be carried by the difficulty identifying feelings subscale of the TAS-20, even when depression and anxiety were controlled for. LEAS scores, however, were not significantly related to autistic traits or eating psychopathology. Limitations Cross-sectional data prevents any conclusions around the direction and causality of relationships between alexithymia, autistic traits, and eating psychopathology (alongside depression and anxiety), necessitating longitudinal research. Our non-clinical sample was predominantly Caucasian undergraduate students, so it remains to be seen if these results would extrapolate to clinical and/or autistic samples. Divergence between the TAS-20 and LEAS raises crucial questions regarding the construct validity of these measures. Conclusions Our findings with respect to autistic traits suggest that alexithymia could partially explain the prevalence of ED in autistic people and may as such be an important consideration in the pathogenesis and treatment of ED in autistic and non-autistic people alike. Further research with clinical samples is critical to explore these ideas. Differences between men and women, furthermore, emphasize the importance of looking for sex-specific as well as generic risk factors in autistic and non-autistic men and women.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista a la que acompañas tiene dificultad para identificar lo que siente, puede ayudar ofrecer formas sencillas de nombrar emociones y sensaciones del cuerpo (tarjetas, escalas, dibujos) y prestar atención tranquila a cambios en la relación con la comida. Esto no significa que vaya a desarrollar un trastorno alimentario. Evidencia: dos estudios transversales con 121 y 300 estudiantes universitarios no clínicos encontraron que la dificultad para identificar sentimientos explicaba en parte la relación entre rasgos autistas y actitudes alimentarias problemáticas, sobre todo en mujeres. Límites: no participaron personas autistas diagnosticadas, la muestra era poco diversa y el diseño no permite saber qué causa qué.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support finds it hard to identify their feelings, it may help to offer simple ways to name emotions and body sensations (cards, scales, drawings) and to notice, calmly, any changes in their relationship with food. This does not mean they will develop an eating disorder. Evidence: two cross-sectional studies with 121 and 300 non-clinical university students found that difficulty identifying feelings partly explained the link between autistic traits and disordered eating attitudes, mainly in women. Limits: no diagnosed autistic people took part, the sample was not diverse, and the design cannot show what causes what.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar har svårt att identifiera sina känslor kan det hjälpa att erbjuda enkla sätt att sätta ord på känslor och kroppsförnimmelser (bildkort, skalor, teckningar) och lugnt lägga märke till förändringar i relationen till mat. Det betyder inte att personen kommer att utveckla en ätstörning. Evidens: två tvärsnittsstudier med 121 och 300 icke-kliniska universitetsstudenter fann att svårigheter att identifiera känslor delvis förklarade sambandet mellan autistiska drag och problematiska ätattityder, främst hos kvinnor. Begränsningar: inga diagnostiserade autistiska personer deltog, urvalet var inte mångfaldigt och designen kan inte visa vad som orsakar vad.

title: Self-guided mindfulness and cognitive behavioural practices reduce anxiety in autistic adults: A pilot 8-month waitlist-controlled trial of widely available online tools.
authors: Gaigg SB, Flaxman PE, McLaven G, Shah R, Bowler DM, Meyer B, Roestorf A, Haenschel C, Rodgers J, South M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Anxiety in autism is an important target for psychological therapies because it is very common and because it significantly impacts upon quality of life and well-being. Growing evidence suggests that cognitive behaviour therapies and mindfulness-based therapies can help autistic individuals learn to manage feelings of anxiety but access to such therapies remains problematic. In the current pilot study, we examined whether existing online cognitive behaviour therapy and mindfulness-based therapy self-help tools can help reduce anxiety in autistic adults. Specifically, 35 autistic adults were asked to try either an existing online cognitive behaviour therapy (n = 16) or mindfulness-based therapy (n = 19) programme while a further 19 autistic adults served as a waitlist comparison group. A first important finding was that 23 of the 35 (66%) participants who tried the online tools completed them, suggesting that such tools are, in principle, acceptable to many autistic adults. In addition, adults in the cognitive behaviour therapy and mindfulness-based therapy conditions reported significant decreases in anxiety over 3 and to some extent also 6 months that were less apparent in the waitlist group of participants. On broader measures of mental health and well-being, the benefits of the online tools were less apparent. Overall, the results suggest that online self-help cognitive behaviour therapy and mindfulness-based therapy tools should be explored further as a means of providing cost-effective mental health support to at least those autistic individuals who can engage effectively with such online tools.

sheet.es: Si un adulto autista con quien convives quiere trabajar su ansiedad y le resultan cómodas las herramientas digitales, podéis explorar juntos programas online de autoayuda basados en terapia cognitivo-conductual o mindfulness, a su ritmo y respetando sus preferencias. Puede ser un apoyo útil mientras se espera otra ayuda, no un sustituto. En este estudio piloto, 54 adultos autistas se repartieron entre programas online y un grupo en lista de espera; quienes usaron los programas (dos de cada tres los terminaron) refirieron menos ansiedad a los 3 y, en parte, a los 6 meses. Es un estudio pequeño, sin cambios claros en el bienestar general, y no sirve para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult in your life wants to work on anxiety and feels comfortable with digital tools, you could explore online self-help programmes based on cognitive behavioural therapy or mindfulness together, at their own pace and respecting their preferences. This can be a useful support while waiting for other help, not a replacement for it. In this pilot trial, 54 autistic adults were split between online programmes and a waitlist group; those using the programmes (two in three completed them) reported less anxiety at 3 and, partly, 6 months. It was a small study, showed no clear change in broader well-being, and will not suit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen i din närhet vill arbeta med sin ångest och trivs med digitala verktyg kan ni tillsammans utforska självhjälpsprogram på nätet som bygger på kognitiv beteendeterapi eller mindfulness, i personens egen takt och utifrån dennes önskemål. Det kan vara ett bra stöd i väntan på annan hjälp, inte en ersättning. I denna pilotstudie delades 54 autistiska vuxna in i nätprogram eller en väntelistegrupp; de som använde programmen (två av tre slutförde dem) rapporterade mindre ångest efter 3 och delvis 6 månader. Studien var liten, visade ingen tydlig förändring i övergripande välmående och passar inte alla.

title: Autism and Epilepsy in Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
authors: Specchio N, Pietrafusa N, Trivisano M, Moavero R, De Palma L, Ferretti A, Vigevano F, Curatolo P
abstract: Introduction: Individuals with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) are at increased risk of developing both epilepsy and autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but the relationship between these conditions is little understood. We reviewed published reports to elucidate the relationship between ASD, epilepsy, and TSC, and to define the genetic and neurological risk factors. Methods: Articles (January 2004-May 2019) were identified via PubMed, EMBASE, and CENTRAL databases. Article inclusion required report on individuals with TSC-associated ASD and epilepsy with prevalence, odds ratio, or rate report on the comorbidity of ASD in epileptic patients due to TSC. Results: A total of 841 abstracts were identified in the original search. Thirty-six articles were included, which identified study populations, ASD measures used, and study confounders as bias factors. This review included 2,666 TSC patients, with a mean age of 15.9 years (range 1.94-30.3 years). The percentage of TSC patients with epilepsy and autism was 33.7%. Patients with TSC and autism showed more frequent seizures and earlier epilepsy onset than TSC patients without autism. ASD and intractable epilepsy were both predicted by a higher number of areas with dysplastic features revealed in brain MR scans. ASD, the onset of seizures in children 3 tubers have all been associated with an increased risk of refractory epilepsy in TSC patients. However, the direction of the relationship is not clear because a history of epilepsy, or infantile spasms in patients with TSC is also associated with an increased likelihood of ASD. Overall, 73.2% of patients carried TSC2 genetic variant and, among patients with TSC and autism, the percentage of TSC2 individuals was 85.6%. Conclusions: The complex interrelationship between TSC, autism, and epilepsy, coupled with limited knowledge on the neurobiological basis for the interrelationship, limits overall understanding and opportunities for management. The results of this review highlight the need for early identification and management to optimize favorable outcomes in the most vulnerable individuals with TSC. Regardless of whether studies are considered individually or collectively, interpretation is made difficult due to the differences between the studies, most notably between methods and diagnostic criteria used to assess intellectual ability.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a alguien con complejo de esclerosis tuberosa (CET), conviene observar de cerca las crisis epilépticas y el desarrollo social y comunicativo desde los primeros años, y comentar cualquier cambio con su equipo médico. Detectar pronto ambas cosas permite apoyos más tempranos. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 36 estudios con 2.666 personas con CET, de 1 a 30 años: alrededor de un tercio tenía epilepsia y era autista, y quienes eran autistas solían tener crisis más tempranas y frecuentes. Sus límites: los estudios usaron métodos y criterios distintos, y no aclara qué causa qué ni predice lo que vivirá cada persona.
sheet.en: If you care for someone with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), it helps to watch closely for seizures and for social and communication development from the early years, and to share any changes with their medical team. Noticing both early opens the door to earlier support. This systematic review pooled 36 studies covering 2,666 people with TSC aged about 1 to 30: roughly a third had epilepsy and were autistic, and autistic participants tended to have earlier, more frequent seizures. Its limits: the studies used different methods and criteria, and it cannot show what causes what or predict any one person's path.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar någon med tuberös skleros (TSC) kan det vara bra att tidigt och noga hålla koll på epileptiska anfall och på social och kommunikativ utveckling, och berätta om förändringar för vårdteamet. Att upptäcka båda tidigt ger möjlighet till tidigare stöd. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 36 studier med 2 666 personer med TSC i åldern cirka 1–30 år: ungefär en tredjedel hade epilepsi och var autistiska, och autistiska deltagare fick ofta anfall tidigare och oftare. Begränsningar: studierna använde olika metoder och kriterier, och översikten kan inte visa orsak och verkan eller förutsäga en enskild persons väg.

title: Prevalence of physical and mental health conditions in Medicare-enrolled, autistic older adults.
authors: Hand BN, Angell AM, Harris L, Carpenter LA
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: While there is emerging evidence on the prevalence of physical and mental health conditions among autistic adults, less is known about this population's needs during older adulthood (aged 65+). We conducted a cross-sectional retrospective cohort study of 2016-2017 Medicare data to compare the prevalence of physical and mental health conditions in a national sample of autistic older adults (N = 4685) to a matched population comparison (N = 46,850) cohort. Autistic older adults had significantly greater odds of nearly all physical health conditions including epilepsy (odds ratio = 18.9; 95% confidence interval = 17.2-20.7), Parkinson's disease (odds ratio = 6.1; 95% confidence interval = 5.3-7.0), and gastrointestinal conditions (odds ratio = 5.2; 95% confidence interval = 4.9-5.5). Most mental health conditions were more common among autistic older adults, including schizophrenia and psychotic disorders (odds ratio = 25.3; 95% confidence interval = 22.4-28.7), attention deficit disorders (odds ratio = 24.4; 95% confidence interval = 16.2-31.0), personality disorders (odds ratio = 24.1; 95% confidence interval = 17.8-32.5), and suicidality or self-inflicted injury (odds ratio = 11.1; 95% confidence interval = 8.9-13.8). Health conditions commonly associated with advanced age in the general population (e.g. osteoporosis, cognitive disorders, heart disease, cancer, cerebrovascular disease, osteoarthritis) were also significantly more common among autistic older adults. By highlighting the significant physical and mental health needs for which autistic older adults require care, our findings can inform healthcare systems, healthcare providers, and public health initiatives seeking to promote well-being in this growing population.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista mayor de 65 años, conviene pedir revisiones de salud regulares que incluyan cuerpo y mente: epilepsia, digestión, movilidad, huesos, corazón, memoria y estado de ánimo. Anota cambios en el día a día y llévalos a la consulta; pregunta también, con calma, por pensamientos de hacerse daño. Este estudio analizó datos de Medicare (EE. UU.) de 4.685 personas autistas mayores comparadas con 46.850 personas no autistas, y encontró más diagnósticos físicos y de salud mental en el grupo autista. Sus límites: usa registros administrativos, no muestra causas, puede reflejar errores de diagnóstico y no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person over 65, it helps to ask for regular health check-ups covering both body and mind: epilepsy, digestion, mobility, bones, heart, memory and mood. Note everyday changes and bring them to appointments; also gently ask about thoughts of self-harm. This study used US Medicare records from 4,685 autistic older adults compared with 46,850 non-autistic peers, and found more physical and mental health diagnoses in the autistic group. Its limits: it relies on billing records, cannot show causes, may reflect misdiagnosis, and does not describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person över 65 år kan det vara bra att be om regelbundna hälsokontroller som gäller både kropp och psyke: epilepsi, mage, rörlighet, skelett, hjärta, minne och stämningsläge. Anteckna förändringar i vardagen och ta med dem till vården; fråga också lugnt om tankar på att skada sig själv. Studien använde amerikanska Medicare-register för 4 685 äldre autistiska personer jämfört med 46 850 icke-autistiska, och fann fler fysiska och psykiska diagnoser hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den bygger på administrativa register, visar inte orsaker, kan påverkas av feldiagnoser och beskriver inte varje individ.

title: Autism spectrum disorder at the crossroad between genes and environment: contributions, convergences, and interactions in ASD developmental pathophysiology.
authors: Cheroni C, Caporale N, Testa G
abstract: The complex pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder encompasses interactions between genetic and environmental factors. On the one hand, hundreds of genes, converging at the functional level on selective biological domains such as epigenetic regulation and synaptic function, have been identified to be either causative or risk factors of autism. On the other hand, exposure to chemicals that are widespread in the environment, such as endocrine disruptors, has been associated with adverse effects on human health, including neurodevelopmental disorders. Interestingly, experimental results suggest an overlap in the regulatory pathways perturbed by genetic mutations and environmental factors, depicting convergences and complex interplays between genetic susceptibility and toxic insults. The pervasive nature of chemical exposure poses pivotal challenges for neurotoxicological studies, regulatory agencies, and policy makers. This highlights an emerging need of developing new integrative models, including biomonitoring, epidemiology, experimental, and computational tools, able to capture real-life scenarios encompassing the interaction between chronic exposure to mixture of substances and individuals' genetic backgrounds. In this review, we address the intertwined roles of genetic lesions and environmental insults. Specifically, we outline the transformative potential of stem cell models, coupled with omics analytical approaches at increasingly single cell resolution, as converging tools to experimentally dissect the pathogenic mechanisms underlying neurodevelopmental disorders, as well as to improve developmental neurotoxicology risk assessment.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas qué «causó» el autismo de tu hijo o hija, esta revisión recuerda que no hay una única causa ni nada que tú hicieras mal: muchos genes y factores ambientales interactúan de formas que aún se investigan. Mañana puedes dejar de buscar culpables y centrarte en lo que ayuda hoy: rutinas previsibles, comunicación respetuosa y apoyos a su medida. Es una revisión narrativa de estudios genéticos, toxicológicos y de laboratorio con células madre; no participaron familias directamente. Su límite: describe hipótesis y herramientas de investigación, no ofrece pruebas, tratamientos ni consejos prácticos que valgan para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you wonder what "caused" your child's autism, this review is a reminder that there is no single cause and nothing you did wrong: many genes and environmental factors interact in ways researchers are still exploring. Tomorrow you can let go of searching for blame and focus on what helps now: predictable routines, respectful communication and supports that fit your child. This is a narrative review of genetic, toxicology and stem cell laboratory research; no families took part directly. Its limit: it describes hypotheses and research tools, not tests, treatments or practical advice that applies to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar vad som ”orsakade” ditt barns autism påminner den här översikten om att det inte finns en enda orsak och att du inte gjort något fel: många gener och miljöfaktorer samverkar på sätt som forskare fortfarande utforskar. I morgon kan du släppa jakten på skuld och fokusera på det som hjälper nu: förutsägbara rutiner, respektfull kommunikation och stöd som passar ditt barn. Det är en narrativ översikt av genetisk, toxikologisk och stamcellsbaserad laboratorieforskning; inga familjer deltog direkt. Begränsning: den beskriver hypoteser och forskningsverktyg, inte tester, behandlingar eller råd som gäller alla.

title: Is Camouflaging Autistic Traits Associated with Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviours? Expanding the Interpersonal Psychological Theory of Suicide in an Undergraduate Student Sample.
authors: Cassidy SA, Gould K, Townsend E, Pelton M, Robertson AE, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The current study explored whether people who camouflage autistic traits are more likely to experience thwarted belongingness and suicidality, as predicted by the Interpersonal Psychological Theory of Suicide (IPTS). 160 undergraduate students (86.9% female, 18-23 years) completed a cross-sectional online survey from 8th February to 30th May 2019 including self-report measures of thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness, autistic traits, depression, anxiety, camouflaging autistic traits, and lifetime suicidality. Results suggest that camouflaging autistic traits is associated with increased risk of experiencing thwarted belongingness and lifetime suicidality. It is important for suicide theories such as the IPTS to include variables relevant to the broader autism phenotype, to increase applicability of models to both autistic and non-autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona joven oculta o disimula sus rasgos autistas para encajar, vale la pena preguntarle con calma cómo se siente y si siente que pertenece a algún grupo. Ofrecer espacios donde pueda ser ella misma, sin tener que fingir, puede ayudar. Si aparecen pensamientos de suicidio, buscar apoyo profesional sin demora es lo adecuado. Este estudio fue una encuesta en línea a 160 estudiantes universitarios de 18 a 23 años (casi todas mujeres) y encontró que camuflar rasgos autistas se asociaba con sentirse menos parte de los demás y con más pensamientos y conductas suicidas. Es un estudio transversal y de autoinforme: muestra una asociación, no una causa, y no todos los participantes eran autistas.
sheet.en: If a young person hides or masks their autistic traits to fit in, it is worth gently asking how they feel and whether they feel they belong somewhere. Offering spaces where they can be themselves, without performing, may help. If thoughts of suicide come up, seeking professional support promptly is the right step. This study was an online survey of 160 university students aged 18 to 23 (mostly women) and found that camouflaging autistic traits was linked with feeling less connected to others and with more lifetime suicidal thoughts and behaviours. It was cross-sectional and self-reported: it shows a link, not a cause, and not all participants were autistic.
sheet.sv: Om en ung person döljer eller maskerar sina autistiska drag för att passa in kan det vara värt att lugnt fråga hur hen mår och om hen känner tillhörighet någonstans. Att erbjuda sammanhang där hen kan vara sig själv, utan att spela en roll, kan hjälpa. Om tankar på självmord dyker upp är det rätt att snabbt söka professionellt stöd. Studien var en webbenkät med 160 universitetsstudenter i åldern 18–23 år (mest kvinnor) och fann att kamouflering av autistiska drag hängde ihop med mindre känsla av tillhörighet och fler självmordstankar och självmordshandlingar under livet. Den var en tvärsnittsstudie med självskattning: den visar ett samband, inte orsak, och alla deltagare var inte autistiska.

title: Measurement Properties of the Suicidal Behaviour Questionnaire-Revised in Autistic Adults.
authors: Cassidy SA, Bradley L, Cogger-Ward H, Shaw R, Bowen E, Glod M, Baron-Cohen S, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: We explored the appropriateness and measurement properties of a suicidality assessment tool (SBQ-R) developed for the general population, in autistic adults-a high risk group for suicide. 188 autistic adults and 183 general population adults completed the tool online, and a sub-sample (n = 15) were interviewed while completing the tool. Multi-group factorial invariance analysis of the online survey data found evidence for metric non-invariance of the SBQ-R, particularly for items three (communication of suicidal intent) and four (likelihood of suicide attempt in the future). Cognitive interviews revealed that autistic adults did not interpret these items as intended by the tool designers. Results suggest autistic adults interpret key questions regarding suicide risk differently to the general population. Future research must adapt tools to better capture suicidality in autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si un profesional usa un cuestionario general sobre pensamientos suicidas con una persona autista adulta, conviene no fiarse solo de la puntuación. Pregunte directamente y con palabras concretas, dé tiempo para responder y compruebe que ambos entienden lo mismo, sobre todo en preguntas sobre si ha contado a alguien sus intenciones o qué probabilidad ve de intentarlo en el futuro. Este estudio comparó respuestas en línea de 188 adultos autistas y 183 adultos de la población general, y entrevistó a 15 mientras respondían: muchas personas autistas interpretaron esas preguntas de otra manera. Límites: muestra en línea y pocas entrevistas; no ofrece todavía una herramienta adaptada. Ante un riesgo inmediato, contacte con servicios de emergencia.
sheet.en: If a professional uses a general suicide-risk questionnaire with an autistic adult, don't rely on the score alone. Ask directly in concrete words, allow time to answer, and check you both understand the question the same way, especially questions about whether they have told anyone they might act, or how likely they think a future attempt is. This study compared online answers from 188 autistic adults and 183 general-population adults, and interviewed 15 people while they answered; many autistic adults read those questions differently than intended. Limits: an online sample and few interviews, and no adapted tool exists yet. If there is immediate danger, contact emergency services.
sheet.sv: Om en yrkesperson använder ett allmänt frågeformulär om självmordstankar med en autistisk vuxen, lita inte enbart på poängen. Fråga direkt med konkreta ord, ge tid att svara och kontrollera att ni förstår frågan på samma sätt, särskilt frågor om personen berättat för någon om sina avsikter eller hur troligt ett framtida försök är. Studien jämförde svar på nätet från 188 autistiska vuxna och 183 vuxna i allmänbefolkningen, och intervjuade 15 personer medan de svarade; många autistiska vuxna tolkade frågorna annorlunda än avsett. Begränsningar: urval via nätet, få intervjuer och inget anpassat verktyg finns ännu. Vid akut fara, kontakta 112.

title: Differential mirror neuron system (MNS) activation during action observation with and without social-emotional components in autism: a meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies.
authors: Chan MMY, Han YMY
abstract: Background Impaired imitation has been found to be an important factor contributing to social communication deficits in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). It has been hypothesized that the neural correlate of imitation, the mirror neuron system (MNS), is dysfunctional in ASD, resulting in imitation impairment as one of the key behavioral manifestations in ASD. Previous MNS studies produced inconsistent results, leaving the debate of whether "broken" mirror neurons in ASD are unresolved. Methods This meta-analysis aimed to explore the differences in MNS activation patterns between typically developing (TD) and ASD individuals when they observe biological motions with or without social-emotional components. Effect size signed differential mapping (ES-SDM) was adopted to synthesize the available fMRI data. Results ES-SDM analysis revealed hyperactivation in the right inferior frontal gyrus and left supplementary motor area in ASD during observation of biological motions. Subgroup analysis of experiments involving the observation of stimuli with or without emotional component revealed hyperactivation in the left inferior parietal lobule and left supplementary motor during action observation without emotional components, whereas hyperactivation of the right inferior frontal gyrus was found during action observation with emotional components in ASD. Subgroup analyses of age showed hyperactivation of the bilateral inferior frontal gyrus in ASD adolescents, while hyperactivation in the right inferior frontal gyrus was noted in ASD adults. Meta-regression within ASD individuals indicated that the right cerebellum crus I activation increased with age, while the left inferior temporal gyrus activation decreased with age. Limitations This meta-analysis is limited in its generalization of the findings to individuals with ASD by the restricted age range, heterogeneous study sample, and the large within-group variation in MNS activation patterns during object observation. Furthermore, we only included action observation studies which might limit the generalization of our results to the imitation deficits in ASD. In addition, the relatively small sample size for individual studies might also potentially overestimate the effect sizes. Conclusion The MNS is impaired in ASD. The abnormal activation patterns were found to be modulated by the nature of stimuli and age, which might explain the contradictory results from earlier studies on the "broken mirror neuron" debate.

sheet.es: No hace falta cambiar nada mañana por este estudio. Si a tu hijo o hija autista le cuesta imitar gestos o expresiones, no significa que su cerebro esté «roto»: este trabajo sugiere que ciertas áreas cerebrales trabajan más, no menos, al observar movimientos, sobre todo con carga emocional. Puede ayudar dar tiempo, mostrar las acciones con calma y explicar con palabras lo que ocurre. Es un metaanálisis de estudios de resonancia magnética que comparó a adolescentes y adultos autistas y no autistas. Sus límites: muestras pequeñas y variadas, gran diferencia entre personas, y mide observación, no imitación ni vida diaria.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change tomorrow because of this study. If your autistic child finds it hard to copy gestures or expressions, it does not mean their brain is "broken": this work suggests some brain areas work harder, not less, when watching movement, especially emotional movement. Giving extra time, showing actions calmly and putting what is happening into words may help. This is a meta-analysis of brain-imaging (fMRI) studies comparing autistic and non-autistic adolescents and adults. Limits: small, mixed samples, large differences between individuals, and it measured watching actions, not imitation or everyday life.
sheet.sv: Ingenting behöver ändras i morgon på grund av den här studien. Om ditt autistiska barn tycker det är svårt att härma gester eller ansiktsuttryck betyder det inte att hjärnan är ”trasig”: studien tyder på att vissa hjärnområden arbetar mer, inte mindre, när man ser rörelser, särskilt känslomässiga. Det kan hjälpa att ge mer tid, visa handlingar lugnt och sätta ord på vad som händer. Det är en metaanalys av hjärnavbildningsstudier (fMRI) som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska tonåringar och vuxna. Begränsningar: små, blandade grupper, stora individuella skillnader, och den mätte att titta på handlingar, inte härmning eller vardagsliv.

title: The relationship between intolerance of uncertainty and anxiety in autism: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
authors: Jenkinson R, Milne E, Thompson A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract People who find it especially hard to cope with the unexpected or unknown are said to have an intolerance of uncertainty. Autistic individuals often report a preference for certainty and experience levels of anxiety that can interfere with their daily life. Understanding more about the link between the intolerance of uncertainty and anxiety in autistic people might lead to better treatments for anxiety being developed. Therefore, this work aimed to review previous research in order to explore this link. Twelve studies were found and their results were compared and contrasted. The autistic people who participated in the studies completed questionnaires that suggested a large number of them experienced very high levels of anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty. Of 10 studies that used relevant statistics, nine found a statistically significant link between anxiety and the intolerance of uncertainty. In general, the strength of the link was about the same as previous research found in people who did not have a diagnosis of autism. This might mean that interventions that aim to help people who are intolerant of uncertainty could be effective for autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas se angustia ante lo imprevisto, reducir la incertidumbre puede aliviar su ansiedad: anticipa cambios, usa agendas visuales y explica qué va a pasar y cuándo. También puede ayudar ensayar juntos, con calma y a su ritmo, pequeñas situaciones inciertas. Este metaanálisis reunió 12 estudios con personas autistas; en nueve de diez análisis relevantes, la intolerancia a la incertidumbre se relacionó con más ansiedad, de forma similar a personas no autistas. Sus límites: se basa en cuestionarios, muestra una relación pero no prueba causa, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support becomes distressed by the unexpected, reducing uncertainty may ease their anxiety: give advance notice of changes, use visual schedules, and explain what will happen and when. Gently practising small uncertain situations together, at their pace, may also help. This meta-analysis combined 12 studies with autistic participants; in nine of ten relevant analyses, intolerance of uncertainty was linked to higher anxiety, about as strongly as in non-autistic people. Limits: it relies on questionnaires, shows a link rather than cause, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar blir orolig av det oväntade kan mindre osäkerhet lindra ångesten: förvarna om förändringar, använd bildscheman och förklara vad som ska hända och när. Att lugnt öva på små osäkra situationer tillsammans, i personens egen takt, kan också hjälpa. Denna metaanalys sammanställde 12 studier med autistiska deltagare; i nio av tio relevanta analyser hängde svårigheter att tåla osäkerhet ihop med mer ångest, ungefär lika starkt som hos icke-autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den bygger på enkäter, visar samband men inte orsak, och varje person är unik.

title: Alexithymic and autistic traits: Relevance for comorbid depression and social phobia in adults with and without autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Albantakis L, Brandi ML, Zillekens IC, Henco L, Weindel L, Thaler H, Schliephake L, Timmermans B, Schilbach L
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Adults with autism often develop mental health problems such as depression and social phobia. The reasons for this are still unclear. Many studies found that alexithymia plays an important role in mental health problems like depression. People with alexithymia have difficulties identifying and describing their emotions. Almost every second person with autism has alexithymia. Therefore, we explored in this study whether alexithymia is linked to worse mental health in autistic people. We looked at two common diagnoses, depression and social phobia. We found that alexithymia increased symptoms of depression, while autistic traits increased symptoms of social phobia. Our results suggest that alexithymia and autistic traits can increase the risk of mental health problems. An early assessment could help prevent mental health problems and improve quality of life.

sheet.es: Si a una persona autista le cuesta reconocer o nombrar lo que siente (alexitimia), conviene estar atentos a señales de bajo ánimo que quizá no sepa expresar con palabras. Pueden ayudar herramientas visuales de emociones, preguntas concretas sobre el cuerpo (sueño, cansancio, apetito) y consultar pronto con profesionales si notáis cambios. La ansiedad social, en cambio, se relacionó más con los rasgos autistas, así que adaptar los entornos sociales también importa. Es un estudio con adultos autistas y no autistas que comparó cuestionarios. Muestra asociaciones, no causas, y los resultados pueden no aplicarse a cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person finds it hard to recognise or name their feelings (alexithymia), it helps to watch for signs of low mood they may not be able to put into words. Visual emotion tools, concrete questions about the body (sleep, tiredness, appetite) and checking in early with professionals when you notice changes can help. Social anxiety was linked more to autistic traits, so adapting social settings also matters. This study compared questionnaire answers from autistic and non-autistic adults. It shows associations, not causes, and the findings may not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att känna igen eller sätta ord på sina känslor (alexitymi) kan det vara bra att vara uppmärksam på tecken på nedstämdhet som hen kanske inte kan beskriva. Visuella känslostöd, konkreta frågor om kroppen (sömn, trötthet, aptit) och att tidigt kontakta vården vid förändringar kan hjälpa. Social ångest hängde mer ihop med autistiska drag, så att anpassa sociala miljöer spelar också roll. Studien jämförde enkätsvar från autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna. Den visar samband, inte orsaker, och resultaten passar inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: Autistic peer-to-peer information transfer is highly effective.
authors: Crompton CJ, Ropar D, Evans-Williams CV, Flynn EG, Fletcher-Watson S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Sharing information with other people relies on the ability to communicate well. Autism is defined clinically by deficits in social communication. It may therefore be expected that autistic people find it difficult to share information with other people. We wanted to find out whether this was the case, and whether it was different when autistic people were sharing information with other autistic people or with non-autistic people. We recruited nine groups, each with eight people. In three of the groups, everyone was autistic; in three of the groups, everyone was non-autistic; and three of the groups were mixed groups where half the group was autistic and half the group was non-autistic. We told one person in each group a story and asked them to share it with another person, and for that person to share it again and so on, until everyone in the group had heard the story. We then looked at how many details of the story had been shared at each stage. We found that autistic people share information with other autistic people as well as non-autistic people do with other non-autistic people. However, when there are mixed groups of autistic and non-autistic people, much less information is shared. Participants were also asked how they felt they had got on with the other person in the interaction. The people in the mixed groups also experienced lower rapport with the person they were sharing the story with. This finding is important as it shows that autistic people have the skills to share information well with one another and experience good rapport, and that there are selective problems when autistic and non-autistic people are interacting.

sheet.es: Si a veces la comunicación entre tú y una persona autista se atasca, no significa que a ella le falten habilidades: puede ser un desajuste entre estilos. Ayuda hablar de forma directa, preguntar cómo prefiere recibir la información y valorar el contacto con otras personas autistas, con quienes muchas se entienden con facilidad. En este estudio, 72 adultos en grupos autistas, no autistas y mixtos se pasaron una historia en cadena: los grupos autistas compartieron tanta información como los no autistas, y los mixtos perdieron más detalles y sintieron menos conexión. Es un estudio pequeño, con una sola tarea de laboratorio, y no describe a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If communication between you and an autistic person sometimes stalls, it does not mean they lack skills: it may be a mismatch between styles. It can help to speak directly, ask how they prefer to receive information, and value time with other autistic people, with whom many connect easily. In this study, 72 adults in autistic, non-autistic and mixed groups passed a story along a chain: autistic groups shared as much information as non-autistic groups, while mixed groups lost more details and felt less rapport. It is a small study using a single lab task, and it does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om kommunikationen mellan dig och en autistisk person ibland kör fast betyder det inte att hen saknar förmåga: det kan handla om olika kommunikationsstilar som inte möts. Det kan hjälpa att tala rakt, fråga hur hen helst vill få information och värdesätta kontakt med andra autistiska personer, som många förstår sig lätt på. I studien förde 72 vuxna i autistiska, icke-autistiska och blandade grupper en berättelse vidare i en kedja: autistiska grupper delade lika mycket information som icke-autistiska, medan blandade grupper tappade fler detaljer och kände mindre samhörighet. Studien är liten, bygger på en enda laboratorieuppgift och beskriver inte alla.

claim.es: Entre personas autistas la información fluye tan bien como entre no autistas; se pierde en los grupos mixtos.
claim.en: Information flows between autistic people as well as between non-autistic people; it breaks down in mixed groups.
claim.sv: Information flödar lika bra mellan autistiska personer som mellan icke-autistiska; den bryts i blandade grupper.

supports.es: Valorar a iguales autistas y autodefensores como un recurso.
supports.en: Valuing autistic peers and self-advocates as a resource.
supports.sv: Att värdera autistiska jämlikar och självförespråkare som en resurs.

doesNotSupport.es: Que las personas autistas carezcan de capacidad social.
doesNotSupport.en: That autistic people lack social ability.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att autistiska personer saknar social förmåga.

title: The Prevalence of Self-injurious Behaviour in Autism: A Meta-analytic Study.
authors: Steenfeldt-Kristensen C, Jones CA, Richards C
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Self-injurious behaviour is purportedly common in autism, but prevalence rates have not yet been synthesised meta-analytically. In the present study, data from 14,379 participants in thirty-seven papers were analysed to generate a pooled prevalence estimate of self-injury in autism of 42% (confidence intervals 0.38-0.47). Hand-hitting topography was the most common form of self-injury (23%), self-cutting topography the least common (3%). Sub-group analyses revealed no association between study quality, participant intellectual disability or age and overall prevalence rate of self-injury. However, females obtained higher prevalence rates than males (p = .013) and hair pulling and self-scratching were associated with intellectual disability (p = .008 and p = .002, respectively). The results confirm very high rates of self-injury in autism and highlight within group risk-markers.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista se golpea, se rasca o se tira del pelo, no estás solo: es frecuente y merece atención tranquila, no culpa. Observa cuándo ocurre (dolor, ruido, cansancio, frustración por no poder comunicar) y anótalo; esas pistas ayudan a reducir la causa y a hablar con profesionales. Las chicas pueden estar en mayor riesgo, así que no lo pases por alto en ellas. Evidencia: metaanálisis de 37 estudios con 14.379 personas autistas; estimó que alrededor del 42% se autolesiona, sobre todo golpeándose las manos o con las manos. Límites: los estudios definieron la autolesión de forma distinta y la cifra no predice lo que vivirá cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child hits, scratches or pulls their hair, you are not alone: it is common and deserves calm attention, not blame. Notice when it happens (pain, noise, tiredness, frustration at not being understood) and jot it down; these clues help ease the cause and support conversations with professionals. Girls may be at higher risk, so don't overlook it in them. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 37 studies with 14,379 autistic participants estimated that about 42% self-injure, most often hand-hitting. Limits: studies defined self-injury differently, and a group figure cannot predict any one person's experience.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn slår sig, river sig eller drar sig i håret är du inte ensam: det är vanligt och förtjänar lugn uppmärksamhet, inte skuld. Lägg märke till när det händer (smärta, ljud, trötthet, frustration över att inte bli förstådd) och anteckna det; ledtrådarna hjälper dig att minska orsaken och att prata med professionella. Flickor kan ha högre risk, så förbise inte detta hos dem. Evidens: en metaanalys av 37 studier med 14 379 autistiska deltagare uppskattade att cirka 42 % skadar sig själva, oftast genom att slå med handen. Begränsningar: studierna definierade självskada olika, och en gruppsiffra kan inte förutsäga en enskild persons upplevelse.

title: Dropping out and moving on: A qualitative study of autistic people's experiences of university.
authors: Cage E, Howes J
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Many autistic people now go to university, but many of them also drop out of their studies. In fact, it is believed that autistic people are at higher risk of dropping out, but little research has been done to understand why this is happening. This research used interviews to take an in-depth look at 14 autistic people's experiences of dropping out of university. All the things the participants talked about were examined closely by the researchers who identified common themes in what the participants discussed. The first set of themes captured some overarching issues faced by autistic people, such as difficulties with getting diagnosed, a lack of autism understanding, mental health challenges and feeling like an outsider. The next themes were organised within challenges faced at university, including a feeling of culture shock, becoming disengaged from one's studies, a lack of proactive support from their university and a feeling that dropping out became inevitable. Finally, there were themes about life after dropping out, which involved a sense that the experience at university had been traumatic and shameful, but they believed people had to do what is right for them. All of these themes suggest that universities need to be better at supporting autistic people when they first come to university, and that they should actively offer clear support throughout and try and make the university environment more accessible for everyone, to ensure more autistic people have a positive university experience.
