Om du oroar dig för ätande eller allmän hälsa, prata med barnets läkare innan du börjar med kosttillskott eller provtagning. Det är en metaanalys av 87 studier med 4 928 autistiska och 4 181 icke-autistiska barn. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, åldern påverkade resultaten och den kan inte visa orsak eller ännu användas för diagnos.

title: Emerging behavioral and neuroimaging biomarkers for early and accurate characterization of autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Hiremath CS, Sagar KJV, Yamini BK, Girimaji AS, Kumar R, Sravanti SL, Padmanabha H, Vykunta Raju KN, Kishore MT, Jacob P, Saini J, Bharath RD, Seshadri SP, Kumar M
abstract: The possibility of early treatment and a better outcome is the direct product of early identification and characterization of any pathological condition. Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impairment in social communication, restricted, and repetitive patterns of behavior. In recent times, various tools and methods have been developed for the early identification and characterization of ASD features as early as 6 months of age. Thorough and exhaustive research has been done to identify biomarkers in ASD using noninvasive neuroimaging and various molecular methods. By employing advanced assessment tools such as MRI and behavioral assessment methods for accurate characterization of the ASD features and may facilitate pre-emptive interventional and targeted therapy programs. However, the application of advanced quantitative MRI methods is still confined to investigational/laboratory settings, and the clinical implication of these imaging methods in personalized medicine is still in infancy. Longitudinal research studies in neurodevelopmental disorders are the need of the hour for accurate characterization of brain-behavioral changes that could be monitored over a period of time. These findings would be more reliable and consistent with translating into the clinics. This review article aims to focus on the recent advancement of early biomarkers for the characterization of ASD features at a younger age using behavioral and quantitative MRI methods.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa el desarrollo de tu bebé, puedes pedir una valoración del desarrollo sin esperar: algunas señales conductuales pueden observarse desde los primeros meses, y un apoyo temprano adaptado al niño suele ayudar a la familia. Las resonancias magnéticas (MRI) para detectar autismo todavía no son una prueba clínica; si alguien te las ofrece como diagnóstico, es razonable preguntar por la evidencia. Esta es una revisión sistemática que resume estudios sobre señales conductuales y de imagen cerebral en niños pequeños. Su límite: los métodos de imagen siguen en fase de investigación, faltan estudios que sigan a los niños durante años y los resultados no se aplican igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you have questions about your baby's development, you can ask for a developmental assessment without waiting: some behavioural signs can be noticed in the first months, and early support shaped around the child often helps the whole family. Brain scans (MRI) for identifying autism are not yet a clinical test; if someone offers one as a diagnosis, it is fair to ask about the evidence. This is a systematic review summarising studies on behavioural and brain-imaging markers in young children. Its limits: the imaging methods are still research tools, long-term studies following children over years are lacking, and findings do not apply the same way to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar över ditt barns utveckling kan du be om en utvecklingsbedömning utan att vänta: vissa beteendetecken kan märkas redan under de första månaderna, och tidigt stöd anpassat efter barnet hjälper ofta hela familjen. Hjärnröntgen (MR) för att identifiera autism är ännu inget kliniskt test; om någon erbjuder det som diagnos är det rimligt att fråga efter evidensen. Detta är en systematisk översikt som sammanfattar studier om beteende- och hjärnavbildningsmarkörer hos små barn. Begränsningar: avbildningsmetoderna är fortfarande forskningsverktyg, det saknas studier som följer barn under flera år, och resultaten gäller inte på samma sätt för varje person.

title: "I'm Proud to be a Little Bit Different": The Effects of Autistic Individuals' Perceptions of Autism and Autism Social Identity on Their Collective Self-esteem.
authors: Cooper R, Cooper K, Russell AJ, Smith LGE
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study aimed to identify the attributes that autistic people perceive as positively and negatively impacting on their identity and wellbeing. In Study 1, we recruited 140 autistic participants for an online survey. Participants completed autism social identification and collective self-esteem measures and listed attributes they associated with autism. In Study 2, we conducted focus groups with 15 autistic people to explore how positively they perceived the attributes of autism. Participants then discussed the autism attributes in relation to their own experiences and identity. We found a positive relationship between the number of positive attributes participants associated with autism, and their collective self-esteem, to the extent that they identified with other autistic people.

sheet.es: Hablar de las fortalezas y cualidades del autismo, y facilitar el contacto con otras personas autistas, puede apoyar una identidad más orgullosa. Mañana podrías nombrar algo concreto que valoras de cómo piensa o percibe tu familiar, y explorar con él o ella comunidades autistas, en línea o presenciales, si le interesan. Evidencia: una encuesta en línea con 140 personas autistas y grupos focales con 15; quienes asociaban más atributos positivos al autismo y se identificaban con otras personas autistas tenían mayor autoestima colectiva. Límites: es un estudio de correlación con adultos voluntarios; no demuestra causa ni aplica igual a todas las personas.
sheet.en: Talking about the strengths and qualities of autism, and making it easier to connect with other autistic people, may support a prouder sense of identity. Tomorrow you could name one specific thing you value about how your family member thinks or perceives, and explore autistic communities, online or in person, together if they are interested. Evidence: an online survey of 140 autistic people plus focus groups with 15; those who linked more positive attributes to autism and identified with other autistic people had higher collective self-esteem. Limits: this is correlational research with adult volunteers; it does not prove cause and will not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Att prata om styrkor och egenskaper i autism, och göra det lättare att träffa andra autistiska personer, kan stödja en stoltare identitet. I morgon kan du nämna något konkret du uppskattar i hur din närstående tänker eller uppfattar världen, och tillsammans utforska autistiska gemenskaper, på nätet eller på plats, om intresse finns. Evidens: en webbenkät med 140 autistiska personer samt fokusgrupper med 15; de som kopplade fler positiva egenskaper till autism och identifierade sig med andra autistiska personer hade högre kollektiv självkänsla. Begränsningar: studien visar samband hos frivilliga vuxna, inte orsak, och passar inte alla.

title: Emotional self-awareness in autism: A meta-analysis of group differences and developmental effects.
authors: Huggins CF, Donnan G, Cameron IM, Williams JH
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are thought to have difficulties with identifying and understanding their own emotions. This is referred to as emotional self-awareness. It is important to study emotional self-awareness as people who are more able to understand their own emotions, whether they are autistic or not, are more able to respond to them appropriately, as well as to identify them in other people. It has not yet been confirmed whether autistic people have difficulties with emotional self-awareness, or if any reported difficulties are actually due to the way in which emotional self-awareness is measured in autistic people. If these difficulties do exist, it is also not known when these difficulties emerge. In this research, we reviewed 47 existing studies that measured emotional self-awareness in autistic and non-autistic adults and children. We also compared studies that measured emotional self-awareness in different ways. We found that autistic adults did seem to have poorer emotional self-awareness compared to their neurotypical peers. However, this was not the case with autistic children of age 12 years and below. Instead, differences in emotional self-awareness only seemed to emerge during adolescence. Moreover, these difficulties seemed to increase with age. These results suggest that difficulties with emotional self-awareness may not be inherent in autism. Instead, they may emerge alongside the greater social and mental health difficulties that are experienced by many autistic people during adolescence. We therefore suggest that it is important to find out more about, and subsequently support, the emotional self-awareness difficulties that autistic adolescents may encounter.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un adolescente autista, puede ayudar ofrecer formas sencillas y sin presión de nombrar lo que siente: tarjetas de emociones, escalas del 1 al 5 o preguntar por sensaciones del cuerpo («¿tienes tensión, cansancio?»). La adolescencia puede ser una etapa clave para este apoyo, junto con atención a su bienestar social y emocional. La evidencia viene de un metaanálisis de 47 estudios con niños y adultos autistas y no autistas: las diferencias en reconocer las propias emociones no aparecieron antes de los 12 años, sino en la adolescencia, y aumentaban con la edad. Límites: los estudios midieron estas habilidades de maneras distintas y no muestran causas; cada persona es diferente.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic teenager, it may help to offer simple, pressure-free ways to name feelings: emotion cards, 1-to-5 scales, or asking about body sensations ("any tension, tiredness?"). Adolescence may be a key time for this support, alongside attention to social and emotional wellbeing. The evidence comes from a meta-analysis of 47 studies with autistic and non-autistic children and adults: differences in recognising one's own emotions did not appear at age 12 or younger, but emerged in adolescence and grew with age. Limits: studies measured these skills in different ways and cannot show causes; every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk tonåring kan det hjälpa att erbjuda enkla sätt utan press att sätta ord på känslor: känslokort, skalor från 1 till 5 eller frågor om kroppen ("känns det spänt, trött?"). Tonåren kan vara en viktig tid för sådant stöd, tillsammans med omsorg om socialt och psykiskt välmående. Underlaget är en metaanalys av 47 studier med autistiska och icke-autistiska barn och vuxna: skillnader i att känna igen egna känslor syntes inte hos barn upp till 12 år, utan uppstod i tonåren och ökade med åldern. Begränsningar: studierna mätte förmågan på olika sätt och kan inte visa orsaker; varje person är olik.

title: How do core autism traits and associated symptoms relate to quality of life? Findings from the Longitudinal European Autism Project.
authors: Oakley BF, Tillmann J, Ahmad J, Crawley D, San José Cáceres A, Holt R, Charman T, Banaschewski T, Buitelaar J, Simonoff E, Murphy D, Loth E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Previous studies suggest that some autistic individuals report lower satisfaction, or well-being, with different aspects of everyday life than those without autism. It is unclear whether this might be partly explained by symptoms of anxiety and/or depression, which affect at least 20%-50% of autistic people. In this study, we measured individual differences in well-being in 573 six to thirty-year-olds with and without a diagnosis of autism. We investigated whether individual differences in well-being were explained by autism traits (e.g. social-communication difficulties) and/or anxiety and depression symptoms. We showed that, though well-being was lower for some autistic individuals, compared to those without autism, many autistic individuals reported good well-being. Where well-being was reduced, this was particularly explained by depression symptoms, across all ages. For children/adolescents, anxiety and social-communication difficulties were also related to some aspects of well-being. Our study suggests that support and services for improving mental health, especially depression symptoms, may also improve broader outcomes for autistic people.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas parece menos satisfecha con su vida, vale la pena prestar atención a posibles señales de depresión (tristeza persistente, pérdida de interés, cansancio) y hablarlo con un profesional de salud mental. Muchas personas autistas tienen un buen bienestar; cuando es más bajo, la depresión fue lo que más lo explicó, y en niños y adolescentes también la ansiedad y las dificultades de comunicación social. Es un estudio europeo con 573 personas de 6 a 30 años, autistas y no autistas. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no describe la experiencia de cada persona.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support seems less satisfied with life, it is worth watching gently for possible signs of depression (lasting sadness, loss of interest, tiredness) and talking with a mental health professional. Many autistic people report good well-being; where it was lower, depression explained it most, and for children and teenagers anxiety and social-communication difficulties also mattered. This European study included 573 people aged 6 to 30, autistic and non-autistic. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, and does not describe every individual's experience.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar verkar mindre nöjd med livet kan det vara värt att varsamt uppmärksamma möjliga tecken på depression (ihållande nedstämdhet, minskat intresse, trötthet) och prata med en professionell inom psykisk hälsa. Många autistiska personer har god livskvalitet; där den var lägre förklarades det mest av depression, och hos barn och unga även av ångest och svårigheter med social kommunikation. Den europeiska studien omfattade 573 personer, 6–30 år, autistiska och icke-autistiska. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, och beskriver inte varje persons upplevelse.

title: Is social camouflaging associated with anxiety and depression in autistic adults?
authors: Hull L, Levy L, Lai MC, Petrides KV, Baron-Cohen S, Allison C, Smith P, Mandy W
abstract: Background There is inconsistent evidence for a clear pattern of association between 'camouflaging' (strategies used to mask and/or compensate for autism characteristics during social interactions) and mental health. Methods This study explored the relationship between self-reported camouflaging and generalised anxiety, depression, and social anxiety in a large sample of autistic adults and, for the first time, explored the moderating effect of gender, in an online survey. Results Overall, camouflaging was associated with greater symptoms of generalised anxiety, depression, and social anxiety, although only to a small extent beyond the contribution of autistic traits and age. Camouflaging more strongly predicted generalised and social anxiety than depression. No interaction between camouflaging and gender was found. Limitations These results cannot be generalised to autistic people with intellectual disability, or autistic children and young people. The sample did not include sufficient numbers of non-binary people to run separate analyses; therefore, it is possible that camouflaging impacts mental health differently in this population. Conclusions The findings suggest that camouflaging is a risk factor for mental health problems in autistic adults without intellectual disability, regardless of gender. We also identified levels of camouflaging at which risk of mental health problems is highest, suggesting clinicians should be particularly aware of mental health problems in those who score at or above these levels.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta pasa mucho tiempo ocultando o compensando sus rasgos autistas en situaciones sociales, conviene crear espacios donde no necesite hacerlo: momentos de descanso, entornos tranquilos y relaciones donde pueda ser como es. También vale la pena estar atento a señales de ansiedad o ánimo bajo y ofrecer apoyo sin presionar. La evidencia procede de una encuesta en línea con un grupo amplio de adultos autistas: el camuflaje se asoció con más ansiedad generalizada, ansiedad social y depresión, sin diferencias por género, aunque el efecto fue pequeño. No incluyó a niños, jóvenes ni personas con discapacidad intelectual, y hubo pocas personas no binarias; además, una encuesta no demuestra causa y efecto.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult spends a lot of energy masking or compensating for autistic traits in social situations, it helps to create spaces where they don't have to: recovery time, calm settings and relationships where they can simply be themselves. It's also worth gently noticing signs of anxiety or low mood and offering support without pressure. The evidence comes from an online survey of a large group of autistic adults: camouflaging was linked to more generalised anxiety, social anxiety and depression, regardless of gender, though the effect was small. It did not include children, young people or people with intellectual disability, had few non-binary participants, and a survey cannot show cause and effect.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen lägger mycket energi på att maskera eller kompensera för autistiska drag i sociala situationer kan det hjälpa att skapa utrymmen där det inte behövs: återhämtningstid, lugna miljöer och relationer där personen kan vara sig själv. Det är också klokt att varsamt uppmärksamma tecken på oro eller nedstämdhet och erbjuda stöd utan press. Underlaget är en webbenkät med en stor grupp autistiska vuxna: kamouflering hängde ihop med mer generaliserad ångest, social ångest och depression, oavsett kön, men sambandet var litet. Barn, unga och personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning ingick inte, få icke-binära deltog, och en enkät kan inte visa orsak och verkan.

title: Early Diagnostics and Early Intervention in Neurodevelopmental Disorders-Age-Dependent Challenges and Opportunities.
authors: Hadders-Algra M
abstract: This review discusses early diagnostics and early intervention in developmental disorders in the light of brain development. The best instruments for early detection of cerebral palsy (CP) with or without intellectual disability are neonatal magnetic resonance imaging, general movements assessment at 2-4 months and from 2-4 months onwards, the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination and Standardized Infant NeuroDevelopmental Assessment. Early detection of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is difficult; its first signs emerge at the end of the first year. Prediction with the Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers and Infant Toddler Checklist is possible to some extent and improves during the second year, especially in children at familial risk of ASD. Thus, prediction improves substantially when transient brain structures have been replaced by permanent circuitries. At around 3 months the cortical subplate has dissolved in primary motor and sensory cortices; around 12 months the cortical subplate in prefrontal and parieto-temporal cortices and cerebellar external granular layer have disappeared. This review stresses that families are pivotal in early intervention. It summarizes evidence on the effectiveness of early intervention in medically fragile neonates, infants at low to moderate risk, infants with or at high risk of CP and with or at high risk of ASD.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa el desarrollo de tu bebé, puedes anotar lo que observas (miradas, gestos, juego, movimiento) y comentarlo con el equipo de salud; las primeras señales de autismo suelen aparecer hacia el final del primer año y se ven con más claridad durante el segundo. Tu papel como familia es central: el apoyo temprano funciona mejor cuando se integra en la vida diaria. Se trata de una revisión narrativa que resume investigaciones sobre detección y apoyo temprano en autismo, parálisis cerebral y bebés con riesgo médico. Su límite: no aporta datos nuevos, las herramientas de cribado solo predicen en parte y cada niño se desarrolla a su ritmo.
sheet.en: If you have questions about your baby's development, you can jot down what you notice (eye contact, gestures, play, movement) and share it with your health team; early signs of autism usually appear near the end of the first year and become clearer during the second. Your role as a family is central: early support works best when it fits into everyday life. This is a narrative review summarising research on early detection and support in autism, cerebral palsy and medically fragile infants. Its limit: it adds no new data, screening checklists only partly predict outcomes, and every child develops at their own pace.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar över ditt barns utveckling kan du skriva ner vad du ser (blickkontakt, gester, lek, rörelser) och ta upp det med barnhälsovården; tidiga tecken på autism visar sig oftast mot slutet av första året och blir tydligare under det andra. Er roll som familj är central: tidigt stöd fungerar bäst när det passar in i vardagen. Detta är en översiktsartikel som sammanfattar forskning om tidig upptäckt och tidigt stöd vid autism, cerebral pares och medicinskt sköra spädbarn. Begränsning: den tillför inga nya data, screeningformulär förutsäger bara delvis och varje barn utvecklas i sin egen takt.

title: Genetic Testing in Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
authors: Savatt JM, Myers SM
abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders are the most prevalent chronic medical conditions encountered in pediatric primary care. In addition to identifying appropriate descriptive diagnoses and guiding families to evidence-based treatments and supports, comprehensive care for individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders includes a search for an underlying etiologic diagnosis, primarily through a genetic evaluation. Identification of an underlying genetic etiology can inform prognosis, clarify recurrence risk, shape clinical management, and direct patients and families to condition-specific resources and supports. Here we review the utility of genetic testing in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders and describe the three major testing modalities and their yields - chromosomal microarray, exome sequencing (with/without copy number variant calling), and FMR1 CGG repeat analysis for fragile X syndrome. Given the diagnostic yield of genetic testing and the potential for clinical and personal utility, there is consensus that genetic testing should be offered to all patients with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, and/or autism spectrum disorder. Despite this recommendation, data suggest that a minority of children with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability have undergone genetic testing. To address this gap in care, we describe a structured but flexible approach to facilitate integration of genetic testing into clinical practice across pediatric specialties and discuss future considerations for genetic testing in neurodevelopmental disorders to prepare pediatric providers to care for patients with such diagnoses today and tomorrow.

sheet.es: Puede preguntar al pediatra si a su hijo o hija le han ofrecido una evaluación genética. Para niños autistas, con retraso global del desarrollo o discapacidad intelectual, existe consenso en ofrecerla: a veces encuentra una causa que ayuda a entender la salud, el riesgo para futuros hermanos y el acceso a apoyos específicos. Hacerla es una decisión de la familia, no una obligación, y un resultado no cambia quién es su hijo. Esta revisión resume las pruebas principales (microarray, secuenciación del exoma y X frágil) y señala que pocos niños las reciben. Es una revisión narrativa, no un estudio nuevo; muchas pruebas no encuentran causa y el acceso varía según el país.
sheet.en: You can ask your child's paediatrician whether a genetic evaluation has been offered. For autistic children, and children with global developmental delay or intellectual disability, experts agree it should be offered: sometimes it finds a cause that helps with health planning, understanding chances for future siblings, and connecting to condition-specific support. Testing is a family choice, not a requirement, and a result does not change who your child is. This review summarises the main tests (chromosomal microarray, exome sequencing and fragile X testing) and notes that few children actually receive them. It is a narrative review, not new research; many tests find no cause, and access differs between countries.
sheet.sv: Du kan fråga barnets läkare om en genetisk utredning har erbjudits. För autistiska barn, och barn med global utvecklingsförsening eller intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, är experter eniga om att den bör erbjudas: ibland hittas en orsak som hjälper med hälsoplanering, förståelse av risken för framtida syskon och tillgång till riktat stöd. Att testa är familjens eget val, inget krav, och ett resultat förändrar inte vem ditt barn är. Översikten sammanfattar de viktigaste testerna (kromosomal mikroarray, exomsekvensering och fragilt X-test) och visar att få barn faktiskt får dem. Det är en narrativ översikt, ingen ny studie; många tester hittar ingen orsak och tillgången skiljer sig mellan länder.

title: Supporting Newly Identified or Diagnosed Autistic Adults: An Initial Evaluation of an Autistic-Led Programme.
authors: Crane L, Hearst C, Ashworth M, Davies J, Hill EL
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Sixteen adults (diagnosed or self-identified as autistic) participated in one of two iterations of a ten-week autistic-led programme, aimed at helping autistic adults learn more about autism within a peer group context. Motivations for taking part in the programme included a desire for: (1) exploration of autism; (2) empowerment; and (3) the development of practical strategies and coping mechanisms. Interviews were conducted upon completion of the programme and again 6 months later. Using thematic analysis, three themes were identified: (1) appreciation of the autistic-led nature of the programme; (2) unity in diversity; and (3) developing a positive, practical outlook on autism. These promising initial results highlight the value of autistic-led peer support for those recently diagnosed/identified as autistic.

sheet.es: Si tú o un adulto cercano acaba de descubrir o recibir la confirmación de que es autista, puede ayudar buscar un grupo de apoyo entre iguales dirigido por personas autistas. Allí es posible explorar qué significa ser autista, sentirse comprendido entre personas diversas y compartir estrategias prácticas para el día a día. En este estudio cualitativo, 16 adultos diagnosticados o autoidentificados como autistas participaron en un programa de diez semanas liderado por personas autistas y fueron entrevistados al terminar y seis meses después; valoraron el liderazgo autista y desarrollaron una visión más positiva. Es una evaluación inicial, con pocos participantes y sin grupo de comparación, así que no sirve para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you or an adult close to you has recently been diagnosed or has come to identify as autistic, it may help to look for a peer support group led by autistic people. Such a group can offer space to explore what being autistic means, feel understood among people with diverse experiences, and share practical everyday strategies. In this qualitative study, 16 diagnosed or self-identified autistic adults took part in a ten-week autistic-led programme and were interviewed at the end and six months later; they valued the autistic leadership and developed a more positive outlook. This is an early evaluation with few participants and no comparison group, so it will not fit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du eller en vuxen nära dig nyligen har fått en autismdiagnos eller börjat identifiera sig som autistisk kan det hjälpa att söka en kamratstödsgrupp som leds av autistiska personer. Där finns utrymme att utforska vad det innebär att vara autistisk, känna sig förstådd bland människor med olika erfarenheter och dela praktiska strategier för vardagen. I denna kvalitativa studie deltog 16 diagnostiserade eller självidentifierade autistiska vuxna i ett tioveckorsprogram lett av autistiska personer och intervjuades efteråt och sex månader senare; de uppskattade det autistiska ledarskapet och fick en mer positiv syn. Det är en tidig utvärdering med få deltagare och utan jämförelsegrupp, så den passar inte alla.

title: The importance and availability of adjustments to improve access for autistic adults who need mental and physical healthcare: findings from UK surveys.
authors: Brice S, Rodgers J, Ingham B, Mason D, Wilson C, Freeston M, Le Couteur A, Parr JR
abstract: Objectives To investigate autistic people's views on the importance and availability of adjustments to mental and physical healthcare provision. To explore whether specific categories of adjustments can be identified and to identify any differences in their importance and availability between mental and physical healthcare. Design Data from two studies, both employing a cross-sectional survey design. Setting UK-based autistic adults registered with the Adult Autism Spectrum Cohort-UK were contacted by post or online. In both studies, recruitment was staged over a 12-month period. Non-responders were sent a single reminder letter 2 weeks after initial contact. Participants 537 autistic adults completed a survey about mental health services (51% response rate), 407 completed the physical health survey (49% response rate). Within these samples, 221 participants completed both surveys. Primary outcome measures Each study developed a bespoke survey to explore participants' views on mental and physical health services, respectively. Both included an identical list of adjustments that participants rated based on importance and availability. Results Three factors of important adjustments were identified: sensory environment, clinical and service context, and clinician knowledge and communication. Adjustments across healthcare settings were widely rated as being important yet rarely available. One significant difference between the importance of adjustments available through mental and physical health services was identified. Participants reported that having access to a clinician who is willing to adapt their approach to suit the person's preferences was significantly more important for participants attending mental health settings (p=0.001). Conclusions Autistic people reported the limited availability of important adjustments in current healthcare provision. To address unmet need and tackle the health inequalities faced by autistic people attending physical and mental healthcare settings, healthcare providers should offer adjustments relating to the three identified factors. Future research should focus on identifying and addressing service provider barriers to implementation.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica o de salud mental, puede ayudar pedir ajustes concretos: un lugar tranquilo para esperar, luz o ruido reducidos, horarios claros, más tiempo, información por escrito y un profesional dispuesto a adaptar su forma de comunicarse. Tiene derecho a solicitarlos y a anotarlos en el historial. Este estudio usó dos encuestas en el Reino Unido con 537 y 407 adultos autistas; valoraron estos ajustes como importantes pero rara vez disponibles, y en salud mental destacaron especialmente un profesional flexible. Límites: participaron solo adultos de un registro británico, cerca de la mitad respondió y las encuestas reflejan opiniones, no resultados de salud; cada persona necesita ajustes distintos.
sheet.en: Before a medical or mental health appointment, it can help to ask for specific adjustments: a quiet place to wait, less light or noise, clear timings, longer appointments, written information, and a clinician willing to adapt how they communicate. You can request these and ask for them to be noted in the record. This study used two UK surveys of 537 and 407 autistic adults; they rated these adjustments as important but rarely available, and for mental health especially valued a flexible clinician. Limits: only adults from one UK registry took part, about half responded, and surveys capture views, not health outcomes; each person needs different adjustments.
sheet.sv: Inför ett besök i vården eller psykiatrin kan det hjälpa att be om konkreta anpassningar: en lugn plats att vänta på, mindre ljus eller ljud, tydliga tider, längre besök, skriftlig information och en behandlare som är villig att anpassa sitt sätt att kommunicera. Du kan begära detta och be att det antecknas i journalen. Studien bygger på två brittiska enkäter med 537 och 407 autistiska vuxna; de bedömde anpassningarna som viktiga men sällan tillgängliga, och inom psykiatrin värderades en flexibel behandlare särskilt högt. Begränsningar: bara vuxna från ett brittiskt register deltog, ungefär hälften svarade och enkäter visar åsikter, inte hälsoutfall; varje person behöver olika anpassningar.

title: Tackling healthcare access barriers for individuals with autism from diagnosis to adulthood.
authors: Malik-Soni N, Shaker A, Luck H, Mullin AE, Wiley RE, Lewis MES, Fuentes J, Frazier TW

title: Early Pandemic Experiences of Autistic Adults: Predictors of Psychological Distress.
authors: Bal VH, Wilkinson E, White LC, Law JK, SPARK Consortium, Feliciano P, Chung WK
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted lives around the world. Autistic adults are at higher risk for co-occurring medical and psychiatric conditions and may be more prone to difficulties adapting to pandemic-related changes and social distancing mandates and coping with ongoing uncertainties. On the other hand, the pandemic may lead to greater understanding and acceptance of accommodations in the broader community that may facilitate supports for autistic adults beyond the pandemic. To learn more about their early pandemic experiences, online surveys were sent to independent adults enrolled in the Simons Powering Autism Research Knowledge (SPARK). The first survey was open from March 30 to April 19, 2020; a follow-up survey sent to original responders was open from May 27 to June 6, yielding 396 participants with data for both surveys. We found that adults who were female, younger, had prior diagnoses of a mental health condition, personal COVID-19 experience (i.e., knowing someone who had symptoms or tested positive) or less frequent hope for the future reported the greatest negative impacts. Decrease in feelings of hopefulness over time predicted greater psychological distress at T2, accounting for T1 impact and distress levels and increases in total COVID-19 impact. Less perceived benefit of online services also predicted later distress. Although there tends to be a focus on coping with negative effects of the pandemic, mental health providers may consider approaches that focus on positives, such as fostering hope and understanding factors that facilitate benefit from online services. LAY SUMMARY: Autistic adults may be at risk for psychological distress during the COVID-19 pandemic. The current study suggests that autistic adults who were younger, female, had a mental health diagnosis before the pandemic and knew someone who showed symptoms or tested positive for COVID-19 reported more areas negatively impacted by COVID-19 and greater difficulty coping with those effects. Decreases in hope over time were associated with greater psychological distress. Less perceived benefit from online services also predicted distress 2 months later. These results suggest important areas to further explore as we develop supports for autistic adults during the pandemic.

sheet.es: En tiempos de crisis o cambios grandes, puede ayudar fijarse en la esperanza, no solo en los problemas: preguntar a la persona autista adulta qué la ilusiona, planear pequeñas cosas agradables y revisar juntos si los servicios en línea (terapia, grupos, trámites) le resultan realmente útiles o necesitan ajustes. Prestar atención especial si es más joven, mujer, ya tenía una condición de salud mental o alguien cercano enfermó. Evidencia: encuestas en línea a 396 personas autistas adultas e independientes de la cohorte SPARK, al inicio de la pandemia de COVID-19 (2020), con seguimiento a dos meses. Límites: datos autoinformados, periodo corto y participantes que no representan a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: During crises or big changes, it may help to focus on hope, not only on problems: ask the autistic adult what they look forward to, plan small enjoyable things, and check together whether online services (therapy, groups, appointments) actually work for them or need adjusting. Pay extra attention if they are younger, a woman, already had a mental health condition, or someone close fell ill. Evidence: online surveys of 396 independent autistic adults from the SPARK cohort early in the COVID-19 pandemic (2020), followed up two months later. Limits: self-reported data, a short time span, and participants who do not represent all autistic people.
sheet.sv: Vid kriser eller stora förändringar kan det hjälpa att fokusera på hopp, inte bara på problem: fråga den autistiska vuxna vad hen ser fram emot, planera små trevliga saker och undersök tillsammans om digitala tjänster (terapi, grupper, vårdbesök) faktiskt fungerar eller behöver anpassas. Var extra uppmärksam om personen är yngre, kvinna, redan hade en psykisk ohälsa eller om någon nära blev sjuk. Evidens: webbenkäter till 396 självständiga autistiska vuxna i SPARK-kohorten tidigt under covid-19-pandemin (2020), med uppföljning efter två månader. Begränsningar: självrapporterade data, kort tidsperiod och deltagare som inte representerar alla autistiska personer.

title: Early non-social behavioural indicators of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in siblings at elevated likelihood for ASD: a systematic review.
authors: Canu D, Van der Paelt S, Canal-Bedia R, Posada M, Vanvuchelen M, Roeyers H
abstract: We aimed at identifying early non-social behavioural indicators that predict later ASD. Likewise, we were interested in the moment in which non-social signs discriminate between children at elevated likelihood for ASD with a later diagnosis of ASD, and children at elevated likelihood for ASD with a typical developmental outcome. In addition, we intended to explore the developmental evolution of children's symptomatology over time. A systematic literature search was conducted for longitudinal studies on early non-social behavioural indicators among siblings at elevated likelihood for ASD. The following databases were searched: PUBMED, Web of Science, PsycINFO, CINAHL and EMBASE. The study identification process was conducted by two reviewers independently. Compared to siblings at elevated likelihood for ASD with a typical developmental outcome, siblings at elevated likelihood for ASD with later ASD show impairments in attention disengagement, in gross and fine motor development and characteristic restricted and repetitive interests and behaviours, starting at 12 months of age. Moreover, early attention disengagement exerts a predictive role towards a later ASD diagnosis, given that from 12 months siblings at elevated likelihood for ASD who will receive an independent ASD diagnosis towards 24-36 months present marked difficulties in disengaging in comparison with siblings at elevated likelihood for ASD that will not satisfy the criteria for an ASD diagnosis. The findings call for a more comprehensive vision on early indicators of ASD. Further research is needed to extend results to other behavioural domains.

sheet.es: Si tienes un bebé con un hermano o hermana autista, puede ser útil fijarte también en aspectos no sociales desde el primer año: cómo cambia la atención de un objeto a otro, cómo se mueve (gatear, agarrar, manipular) y si aparecen intereses o movimientos muy repetitivos. Si notas algo, coméntalo con calma con tu equipo de salud; observar no es diagnosticar. Esta revisión sistemática reunió estudios longitudinales con hermanos pequeños de niños autistas, seguidos hasta los 2-3 años. Sus límites: solo incluye familias con un hijo autista, los estudios varían en métodos y estas señales describen grupos, no predicen con certeza el desarrollo de cada niño.
sheet.en: If you have a baby whose older sibling is autistic, it can help to notice non-social things too from around the first birthday: how easily attention shifts from one thing to another, how the baby moves (crawling, grasping, handling objects), and whether very repetitive interests or movements appear. If something stands out, mention it calmly to your health team; noticing is not diagnosing. This systematic review gathered longitudinal studies following younger siblings of autistic children up to age 2-3. Its limits: it only covers families who already have an autistic child, the studies used different methods, and these signs describe groups rather than predicting any single child's path.
sheet.sv: Om du har en bebis med ett autistiskt äldre syskon kan det vara bra att även lägga märke till icke-sociala saker från ungefär ett års ålder: hur lätt uppmärksamheten flyttas från en sak till en annan, hur barnet rör sig (kryper, greppar, hanterar föremål) och om mycket upprepande intressen eller rörelser syns. Om något sticker ut, ta upp det lugnt med vården; att observera är inte att diagnostisera. Denna systematiska översikt samlade longitudinella studier som följde yngre syskon till autistiska barn upp till 2–3 års ålder. Begränsningar: den gäller bara familjer som redan har ett autistiskt barn, studierna använde olika metoder och tecknen beskriver grupper, inte enskilda barns utveckling.

title: Music Therapy for Children With Autistic Spectrum Disorder and/or Other Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Systematic Review.
authors: Mayer-Benarous H, Benarous X, Vonthron F, Cohen D
abstract: Background: Several studies have reported contradictory results regarding the benefits of music interventions in children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), including autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Methods: We performed a systematic review according to the PRISMA guidelines. We searched the Cochrane, PubMed and Medline databases from January 1970 to September 2020 to review all empirical findings, except case reports, measuring the effect of music therapy on youths with ASD, intellectual disability (ID), communication disorder (CD), developmental coordination disorder (DCD), specific learning disorder, and attention/deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Results: Thirty-nine studies ( N = 1,774 participants) were included in this review (ASD: n = 22; ID: n = 7; CD and dyslexia: n = 5; DCD: n = 0; ADHD: n = 5 studies). Two main music therapies were used: educational music therapy and improvisational music therapy. A positive effect of educational music therapy on patients with ASD was reported in most controlled studies (6/7), particularly in terms of speech production. A positive effect of improvisational music therapy was reported in most controlled studies (6/8), particularly in terms of social functioning. The subgroup of patients with both ASD and ID had a higher response rate. Data are lacking for children with other NDDs, although preliminary evidence appears encouraging for educational music therapy in children with dyslexia. Discussion: Improvisational music therapy in children with NDDs appears relevant for individuals with both ASD and ID. More research should be encouraged to explore whether oral and written language skills may improve after educational music therapy, as preliminary data are encouraging.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija le atrae la música, la musicoterapia puede ser una opción que valga la pena explorar: algunos niños autistas parecen comunicarse con más palabras o compartir más con otras personas a través de actividades musicales, sobre todo cuando se sigue su ritmo e intereses. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 39 estudios con 1.774 niños y adolescentes, 22 de ellos centrados en niños autistas; la mayoría de los estudios controlados mostró efectos positivos, especialmente en niños autistas con discapacidad intelectual. Como límite, muchos estudios eran pequeños y distintos entre sí, y los resultados no garantizan que funcione igual para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your child enjoys music, music therapy may be worth exploring: some autistic children seem to use more words or connect more with others through musical activities, especially when sessions follow their pace and interests. This systematic review gathered 39 studies with 1,774 children and teenagers, 22 of them focused on autistic children; most controlled studies reported positive effects, particularly for autistic children who also have an intellectual disability. As a limit, many studies were small and varied in methods, so the results cannot promise the same benefit for every child, and evidence for other neurodevelopmental conditions is still thin.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn tycker om musik kan musikterapi vara värt att utforska: en del autistiska barn verkar använda fler ord eller få mer kontakt med andra genom musikaliska aktiviteter, särskilt när sessionerna följer barnets tempo och intressen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 39 studier med 1 774 barn och ungdomar, varav 22 handlade om autistiska barn; de flesta kontrollerade studier visade positiva effekter, framför allt för autistiska barn som också har en intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. En begränsning är att många studier var små och olika i upplägg, så resultaten kan inte lova samma nytta för varje barn, och underlaget för andra diagnoser är fortfarande tunt.

title: Autistic Self-Advocacy and the Neurodiversity Movement: Implications for Autism Early Intervention Research and Practice.
authors: Leadbitter K, Buckle KL, Ellis C, Dekker M
abstract: The growth of autistic self-advocacy and the neurodiversity movement has brought about new ethical, theoretical and ideological debates within autism theory, research and practice. These debates have had genuine impact within some areas of autism research but their influence is less evident within early intervention research. In this paper, we argue that all autism intervention stakeholders need to understand and actively engage with the views of autistic people and with neurodiversity as a concept and movement. In so doing, intervention researchers and practitioners are required to move away from a normative agenda and pay diligence to environmental goodness-of-fit, autistic developmental trajectories, internal drivers and experiences, and autistic prioritized intervention targets. Autism intervention researchers must respond to these debates by reframing effectiveness, developing tools to measure autistic prioritized outcomes, and forming partnerships with autistic people. There is a pressing need for increased reflection and articulation around how intervention practices align with a neurodiversity framework and greater emphasis within intervention programmes on natural developmental processes, coping strategies, autonomy, and well-being.

sheet.es: Al elegir o revisar apoyos tempranos para tu hijo o hija, puedes preguntar: ¿este objetivo busca su bienestar, autonomía y estrategias para afrontar el día, o solo que parezca menos autista? Ajustar el entorno (ruido, rutinas, comunicación) puede ayudar tanto como cambiar a la persona, y respetar sus intereses y su ritmo de desarrollo es parte del apoyo. Las voces de personas autistas adultas son una guía valiosa. Este artículo es un análisis teórico y ético escrito por investigadores, que reúne debates del movimiento de la neurodiversidad y la autodefensa autista. Su límite: no presenta datos nuevos ni prueba qué intervención funciona mejor; ofrece un marco para reflexionar, no una regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: When choosing or reviewing early support for your child, you can ask: does this goal serve their well-being, autonomy and coping, or mainly aim to make them look less autistic? Adjusting the environment (noise, routines, communication) can help as much as changing the person, and respecting their interests and developmental pace is part of good support. Autistic adults' perspectives are a valuable guide. This paper is a theoretical and ethical analysis by researchers, drawing on debates from autistic self-advocacy and the neurodiversity movement. Its limit: it presents no new data and does not test which intervention works best; it offers a framework for reflection, not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: När du väljer eller ser över tidigt stöd för ditt barn kan du fråga: tjänar målet barnets välmående, självständighet och sätt att hantera vardagen, eller handlar det mest om att verka mindre autistisk? Att anpassa miljön (ljud, rutiner, kommunikation) kan hjälpa lika mycket som att förändra personen, och att respektera intressen och egen utvecklingstakt är en del av bra stöd. Autistiska vuxnas perspektiv är en värdefull vägledning. Artikeln är en teoretisk och etisk analys av forskare, byggd på debatter från autistisk självförespråkning och neurodiversitetsrörelsen. Begränsning: den redovisar inga nya data och prövar inte vilken insats som fungerar bäst; den ger en ram för eftertanke, inte en regel för varje familj.

title: An investigation of the diet, exercise, sleep, BMI, and health outcomes of autistic adults.
authors: Weir E, Allison C, Ong KK, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Studies of autistic children suggest that restricted eating, reduced physical activity, and sleep disorders are common; however, no studies attempt to broadly describe the diet, exercise, and sleep patterns of autistic adults or consider relationships between lifestyle behaviors and the widely reported increased risks of obesity and chronic conditions. To address this, the authors developed the largest study of lifestyle patterns of autistic adults and assessed their relationships to body mass index, health outcomes, and family history. Methods We administered an anonymized, online survey to n = 2386 adults (n = 1183 autistic) aged 16-90 years of age. We employed Fisher's exact tests and binomial logistic regression to describe diet, exercise, and sleep patterns; mediation of seizure disorders on sleep; body mass index (BMI); relationships of lifestyle factors to BMI, cardiovascular conditions, and diabetic conditions; and sex differences among autistic adults. Results Autistic adults, and particularly autistic females, exhibit unhealthy diet, exercise, and sleep patterns; they are also more likely to be underweight or obese. Limited sleep duration and high rates of sleep disturbances cannot be accounted for by epilepsy or seizure disorders. Lifestyle factors are positively related to higher risk of cardiovascular conditions among autistic males, even more than family history. Limitations Our sample may not be representative of all autistic and non-autistic people, as it primarily comprised individuals who are white, female, have a high school education or higher, and reside in the UK. Our sampling methods may also exclude some individuals on the autism spectrum, and particularly those with moderate to severe intellectual disability. This is a cross-sectional sample that can test for relationships between factors (e.g., lifestyle factors and health outcomes) but cannot assess the direction of these relationships. Conclusions Autistic adults are less likely to meet minimal health recommendations for diet, exercise, and sleep-and these unhealthy behaviors may relate to excess risk of cardiovascular conditions. Although the present study can only provide preliminary, correlational evidence, our findings suggest that diet, exercise, and sleep should be considered and further investigated as key targets for reducing the now widely reported and dramatically increased risks of health comorbidity and premature death among autistic individuals compared to others. Physicians should work cooperatively with patients to provide health education and develop individualized strategies for how to better manage challenges with diet, exercise, and sleep.

sheet.es: Vale la pena hablar con calma sobre alimentación, movimiento y sueño en la vida adulta autista, sin juicio y respetando preferencias sensoriales. Pequeños pasos ayudan: rutinas de sueño predecibles, actividades físicas que la persona disfrute y alimentos seguros ampliados poco a poco. Llevar estas notas a la consulta médica permite construir estrategias individuales junto al profesional. La evidencia viene de una encuesta en línea a 2386 adultos (1183 autistas), que encontró más dificultades de sueño, dieta y ejercicio, y relación con riesgo cardiovascular en hombres autistas. Límites: la mayoría eran mujeres blancas del Reino Unido, faltaron personas con discapacidad intelectual y el diseño no muestra causa y efecto.
sheet.en: It is worth talking calmly about food, movement and sleep in autistic adult life, without judgement and respecting sensory preferences. Small steps help: predictable sleep routines, physical activity the person actually enjoys, and safe foods expanded gradually. Bringing notes to medical appointments lets you build individual strategies together with the clinician. The evidence comes from an online survey of 2,386 adults (1,183 autistic), which found more difficulties with sleep, diet and exercise, linked to cardiovascular risk in autistic men. Limits: most participants were white women in the UK, people with intellectual disability were largely missing, and the design cannot show cause and effect.
sheet.sv: Det är värt att lugnt prata om mat, rörelse och sömn i det autistiska vuxenlivet, utan att döma och med respekt för sensoriska preferenser. Små steg hjälper: förutsägbara sömnrutiner, fysisk aktivitet som personen faktiskt tycker om och trygga livsmedel som utökas gradvis. Att ta med anteckningar till vården gör det lättare att skapa individuella strategier tillsammans. Underlaget är en webbenkät med 2 386 vuxna (1 183 autistiska), som visade fler svårigheter med sömn, kost och motion, kopplat till hjärt-kärlrisk hos autistiska män. Begränsningar: de flesta var vita kvinnor i Storbritannien, personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning saknades till stor del och studien kan inte visa orsak och verkan.

title: Intensive behavioural interventions based on applied behaviour analysis for young children with autism: An international collaborative individual participant data meta-analysis.
authors: Rodgers M, Simmonds M, Marshall D, Hodgson R, Stewart LA, Rai D, Wright K, Ben-Itzchak E, Eikeseth S, Eldevik S, Kovshoff H, Magiati I, Osborne LA, Reed P, Vivanti G, Zachor D, Couteur AL
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Early intensive applied behaviour analysis-based interventions are designed to support young autistic children's learning and development. Unfortunately, the available evidence about the effectiveness of these interventions remains unclear. Several reviews have focused on the published findings rather than contacting the authors to collect and analyse data about the individual participants in the original studies. Also, most of the studies were carried out by groups involved in delivering the interventions leading to the potential bias in interpreting the results. Our research team (supported by an international advisory group) carried out an independent individual patient data review by collecting the original participant data from the authors of the studies, to examine the effectiveness of these interventions. The results suggested that early intensive applied behaviour analysis-based interventions might lead to some changes in children's cognitive ability (intelligence quotient) and everyday life skills after 2 years, compared with standard treatments. However, all the studies had problems with the way they were designed. Also, few of the studies looked at outcomes that have been described as most important to autistic people or followed children beyond 2 years. We think that further systematic reviews of the existing evidence are unlikely to add to the findings of our review. Furthermore, we recommend that future research should investigate which types of supports and interventions are most effective for children and families, prioritising outcomes measures that are meaningful for the autism community and include, wherever possible, longer-term follow-up.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa intensivo basado en ABA para su hijo pequeño, puede preguntar con calma: ¿qué objetivos importan a mi hijo y a nuestra familia, cómo se medirá su bienestar y qué pasa si algo no le encaja? Esta revisión encontró que estos programas podrían producir algunos cambios en el CI y en habilidades de la vida diaria tras dos años, comparados con apoyos habituales. Es un metaanálisis independiente que reunió los datos individuales de niños autistas pequeños de varios estudios. Sus límites: todos los estudios tenían problemas de diseño, pocos midieron lo que las personas autistas consideran importante y casi ninguno siguió a los niños más allá de dos años.
sheet.en: If you are offered an intensive ABA-based programme for your young child, you can calmly ask: which goals matter to my child and our family, how will their wellbeing be measured, and what happens if something doesn't suit them? This review found these programmes might bring some changes in IQ and everyday living skills after two years, compared with usual support. It is an independent meta-analysis that gathered individual data on young autistic children from several studies. Its limits: every study had design problems, few measured outcomes autistic people say matter most, and almost none followed children beyond two years.
sheet.sv: Om ni erbjuds ett intensivt ABA-baserat program för ert lilla barn kan ni lugnt fråga: vilka mål är viktiga för mitt barn och vår familj, hur följs barnets välmående upp, och vad händer om något inte passar? Översikten fann att sådana program kanske kan ge vissa förändringar i IQ och vardagsfärdigheter efter två år, jämfört med vanligt stöd. Det är en oberoende metaanalys som samlade individuella data om små autistiska barn från flera studier. Begränsningar: alla studier hade brister i upplägget, få mätte det autistiska personer anser viktigast och nästan ingen följde barnen längre än två år.

title: What Do New Findings About Social Interaction in Autistic Adults Mean for Neurodevelopmental Research?
authors: Davis R, Crompton CJ
journal: Perspectives on psychological science : a journal of the Association for Psychological Science
abstract: Deficit-based accounts of social and communication abilities continue to dominate autism research. However, emerging findings suggest that this view may be overly simplistic and discount the two-way nature of interaction. Here we discuss the reconceptualization of social cognition to consider such difficulties as examples of bidirectional, multifaceted misattunement between autistic and nonautistic individuals. Aligned with progressive theoretical frameworks, emerging empirical research indicates that mismatches in communication styles can contribute to autistic social difficulties and the important role that nonautistic difficulties play. We highlight two areas of future research with the aim of providing empirical support for the views that the autistic community has proposed over the past 2 decades. We discuss the impact of such a paradigm shift on a number of levels, including how bridging the gap between different interaction styles can reduce stigma and increase understanding. Adopting such a framework will provide radical opportunities for transformative societal changes and education around inclusion.

sheet.es: Cuando una conversación no fluye, no asuma que el problema es solo de la persona autista. La comunicación va en dos direcciones: pruebe a ajustar su propio estilo, por ejemplo hablando de forma más directa, preguntando qué le resulta cómodo y aceptando otras formas de mostrar interés. Este artículo es una revisión teórica que reúne investigaciones recientes con adultos autistas y no autistas, y apoya lo que la comunidad autista lleva décadas diciendo: los malentendidos surgen de diferencias de estilo entre ambos lados. Su límite es que no aporta datos nuevos propios y propone líneas futuras; cada persona y cada relación son distintas.
sheet.en: When a conversation isn't flowing, don't assume the problem lies only with the autistic person. Communication goes both ways: try adjusting your own style, for example by speaking more directly, asking what feels comfortable, and accepting different ways of showing interest. This article is a theoretical review drawing on recent research with autistic and non-autistic adults, and it supports what the autistic community has said for decades: misunderstandings arise from differences in style on both sides. Its limit is that it offers no new data of its own and mainly proposes future research; every person and every relationship is different.
sheet.sv: När ett samtal inte flyter, anta inte att problemet bara ligger hos den autistiska personen. Kommunikation går åt båda hållen: prova att anpassa din egen stil, till exempel genom att tala mer rakt på sak, fråga vad som känns bekvämt och acceptera andra sätt att visa intresse. Artikeln är en teoretisk översikt som bygger på ny forskning med autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna, och den stöder det autistiska personer sagt i decennier: missförstånd uppstår ur stilskillnader på båda sidor. Begränsningen är att den inte har egna nya data och mest föreslår framtida forskning; varje person och relation är olika.

title: Mutual (Mis)understanding: Reframing Autistic Pragmatic "Impairments" Using Relevance Theory.
authors: Williams GL, Wharton T, Jagoe C
abstract: A central diagnostic and anecdotal feature of autism is difficulty with social communication . We take the position that communication is a two-way, intersubjective phenomenon-as described by the double empathy problem -and offer up relevance theory (a cognitive account of utterance interpretation) as a means of explaining such communication difficulties. Based on a set of proposed heuristics for successful and rapid interpretation of intended meaning, relevance theory positions communication as contingent on shared-and, importantly, mutually recognized-"relevance." Given that autistic and non-autistic people may have sometimes markedly different embodied experiences of the world, we argue that what is most salient to each interlocutor may be mismatched. Relevance theory would predict that where this salient information is not (mutually) recognized or adjusted for, mutual understanding may be more effortful to achieve. This paper presents the findings from a small-scale, linguistic ethnographic study of autistic communication featuring eight core autistic participants. Each core autistic participant engaged in three naturalistic conversations around the topic of loneliness with: (1) a familiar, chosen conversation partner; (2) a non-autistic stranger and (3) an autistic stranger. Relevance theory is utilized as a frame for the linguistic analysis of the interactions. Mutual understanding was unexpectedly high across all types of conversation pairings. In conversations involving two autistic participants, flow, rapport and intersubjective attunement were significantly increased and in three instances, autistic interlocutors appeared to experience improvements in their individual communicative competence contrasted with their other conversations. The findings have the potential to guide future thinking about how, in practical terms, communication between autistic and non-autistic people in both personal and public settings might be improved.

sheet.es: Cuando una conversación se atasca, no asumas que el problema está solo en la persona autista: puede que cada uno esté dando importancia a cosas distintas. Mañana, prueba a preguntar «¿qué es lo importante para ti aquí?», explica tu propia intención con claridad y valora los espacios donde tu familiar pueda hablar con otras personas autistas, donde la conversación puede fluir con más facilidad. Este estudio lingüístico analizó conversaciones naturales de ocho personas autistas con un conocido, un desconocido no autista y un desconocido autista; la comprensión mutua fue alta en todas, y mayor la sintonía entre personas autistas. Es una muestra muy pequeña y no se aplica a todas las personas.
sheet.en: When a conversation gets stuck, don't assume the problem lies only with the autistic person: each of you may be focusing on different things as important. Tomorrow, try asking "what matters most to you here?", state your own meaning clearly, and value spaces where your family member can talk with other autistic people, where conversation may flow more easily. This linguistic study analysed natural conversations of eight autistic people with a familiar partner, a non-autistic stranger and an autistic stranger; mutual understanding was high in all, and rapport was stronger between autistic people. The sample is very small, so it won't apply to every person.
sheet.sv: När ett samtal kör fast, anta inte att problemet bara ligger hos den autistiska personen: ni kanske tycker att olika saker är viktiga. I morgon kan du fråga ”vad är viktigast för dig här?”, säga tydligt vad du själv menar och värdesätta tillfällen där din närstående kan prata med andra autistiska personer, där samtalet ofta flyter lättare. Denna språkvetenskapliga studie analyserade naturliga samtal där åtta autistiska personer pratade med en bekant, en icke-autistisk främling och en autistisk främling; den ömsesidiga förståelsen var hög i alla, och samspelet starkast mellan autistiska personer. Urvalet är mycket litet och gäller inte alla.

title: Relationship between Autism Spectrum Disorder and Pesticides: A Systematic Review of Human and Preclinical Models.
authors: Biosca-Brull J, Pérez-Fernández C, Mora S, Carrillo B, Pinos H, Conejo NM, Collado P, Arias JL, Martín-Sánchez F, Sánchez-Santed F, Colomina MT
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex set of neurodevelopmental pathologies characterized by impoverished social and communicative abilities and stereotyped behaviors. Although its genetic basis is unquestionable, the involvement of environmental factors such as exposure to pesticides has also been proposed. Despite the systematic analyses of this relationship in humans, there are no specific reviews including both human and preclinical models. The present systematic review summarizes, analyzes, and discusses recent advances in preclinical and epidemiological studies. We included 45 human and 16 preclinical studies. These studies focused on Organophosphates (OP), Organochlorine (OC), Pyrethroid (PT), Neonicotinoid (NN), Carbamate (CM), and mixed exposures. Preclinical studies, where the OP Chlorpyrifos (CPF) compound is the one most studied, pointed to an association between gestational exposure and increased ASD-like behaviors, although the data are inconclusive with regard to other ages or pesticides. Studies in humans focused on prenatal exposure to OP and OC agents, and report cognitive and behavioral alterations related to ASD symptomatology. The results of both suggest that gestational exposure to certain OP agents could be linked to the clinical signs of ASD. Future experimental studies should focus on extending the analysis of ASD-like behaviors in preclinical models and include exposure patterns similar to those observed in human studies.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, este estudio no es motivo de culpa: el autismo tiene una base genética fuerte y nadie puede saber qué causó el autismo de un niño concreto. La revisión sugiere que la exposición durante el embarazo a algunos pesticidas organofosforados, como el clorpirifós, podría estar asociada a rasgos autistas; en la vida diaria, lavar frutas y verduras y evitar el uso de pesticidas en casa son medidas sensatas para toda la familia. Es una revisión sistemática de 45 estudios en humanos y 16 en animales. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas, los datos sobre otros pesticidas y edades no son concluyentes, y los estudios con animales no se trasladan directamente a las personas.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, this study is not a reason for guilt: autism has a strong genetic basis, and no one can know what led to any individual child being autistic. The review suggests that exposure during pregnancy to some organophosphate pesticides, such as chlorpyrifos, may be associated with autistic traits; day to day, washing fruit and vegetables and avoiding pesticide use at home are sensible steps for the whole family. It is a systematic review of 45 human and 16 animal studies. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, data on other pesticides and ages are inconclusive, and animal findings do not translate directly to people.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är den här studien ingen anledning till skuld: autism har en stark genetisk grund, och ingen kan veta vad som ledde till att ett enskilt barn är autistiskt. Översikten tyder på att exponering under graviditeten för vissa organofosfatbekämpningsmedel, som klorpyrifos, kan ha ett samband med autistiska drag; i vardagen är det klokt för hela familjen att skölja frukt och grönsaker och undvika bekämpningsmedel hemma. Det är en systematisk översikt av 45 studier på människor och 16 på djur. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, data om andra medel och åldrar är osäkra, och djurfynd går inte direkt att överföra till människor.

title: Telehealth and Autism Prior to and in the Age of COVID-19: A Systematic and Critical Review of the Last Decade.
authors: Ellison KS, Guidry J, Picou P, Adenuga P, Davis TE
journal: Clinical child and family psychology review

title: Visual Sensory Experiences From the Viewpoint of Autistic Adults.
authors: Parmar KR, Porter CS, Dickinson CM, Pelham J, Baimbridge P, Gowen E
abstract: Although previous research has investigated altered sensory reactivity in autistic individuals, there has been no specific focus on visual sensory experiences, particularly in adults. Using qualitative methods, this study aimed to characterize autistic visual sensory symptoms, contextualize their impact and document any associated coping strategies. A total of 18 autistic adults took part in four focus groups which involved questions around visual experiences, the impact of these on daily life, and strategies for their reduction. Transcripts of each session were thematically analyzed allocating six key themes. Participants described a range of visual hypersensitivities, including to light, motion, patterns and particular colors, which contributed to distraction and were frequently part of a wider multisensory issue. Such experiences had significant negative impacts on personal wellbeing and daily life with participants describing fatigue, stress and hindrances on day-to-day activities (e.g., travel and social activities). However, the degree of understanding that participants had about their visual experiences influenced their emotional response, with greater understanding reducing concern. Participants employed a variety of coping strategies to overcome visual sensory experiences but with varied success. Discussions also highlighted that there may be a poor public understanding of sensory issues in autism affecting how well autistic individuals are able manage their sensory symptoms. In summary, autistic adults expressed significant concern about their visual experiences and there is a need to improve understanding of visual experiences on a personal and public level as well as for developing potential support.

sheet.es: Pregunte a la persona autista qué le molesta visualmente: luz intensa, movimiento, patrones o ciertos colores. Ajustar la iluminación, permitir gafas de sol o gorra, reducir el desorden visual y planificar descansos antes de viajes o actividades sociales puede disminuir el cansancio y el estrés. Entender las propias reacciones visuales parecía reducir la preocupación, así que hablar de ello con calma ayuda. Las estrategias funcionan de forma distinta para cada persona; pruebe y observe. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con cuatro grupos focales de 18 adultos autistas que describieron sus experiencias. Límites: muestra pequeña, solo adultos y relatos personales, sin medir qué estrategias funcionan mejor.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person what bothers them visually: bright light, motion, patterns or certain colours. Adjusting lighting, allowing sunglasses or a cap, reducing visual clutter and planning breaks before travel or social activities may ease fatigue and stress. Understanding one's own visual reactions seemed to reduce worry, so talking about it calmly can help. Strategies work differently for each person; try things and notice what helps. Evidence: a qualitative study with four focus groups of 18 autistic adults describing their own experiences. Limits: a small sample, adults only, and personal accounts, without testing which strategies work best.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen vad som stör visuellt: starkt ljus, rörelse, mönster eller vissa färger. Att justera belysningen, tillåta solglasögon eller keps, minska visuellt rörigt och planera pauser inför resor eller sociala aktiviteter kan minska trötthet och stress. Att förstå sina egna visuella reaktioner verkade minska oron, så att lugnt prata om dem kan hjälpa. Strategier fungerar olika för olika personer; prova och se vad som hjälper. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie med fyra fokusgrupper där 18 autistiska vuxna beskrev sina erfarenheter. Begränsningar: litet urval, endast vuxna och egna berättelser, utan test av vilka strategier som fungerar bäst.

title: Development and validation of the suicidal behaviours questionnaire - autism spectrum conditions in a community sample of autistic, possibly autistic and non-autistic adults.
authors: Cassidy SA, Bradley L, Cogger-Ward H, Rodgers J
abstract: Background Autistic people and those with high autistic traits are at high risk of experiencing suicidality. Yet, there are no suicidality assessment tools developed or validated for these groups. Methods A widely used and validated suicidality assessment tool developed for the general population (SBQ-R), was adapted using feedback from autistic adults, to create the Suicidal Behaviours Questionnaire-Autism Spectrum Conditions (SBQ-ASC). The adapted tool was refined through nine interviews, and an online survey with 251 autistic adults, to establish clarity and relevance of the items. Subsequently, 308 autistic, 113 possibly autistic, and 268 non-autistic adults completed the adapted tool online, alongside self-report measures of autistic traits (AQ), camouflaging autistic traits (CAT-Q), depression (PHQ-9), anxiety (ASA-A), thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness (INQ-15), lifetime non-suicidal self-injury, and the original version of the suicidality assessment tool (SBQ-R). Analyses explored the appropriateness and measurement properties of the adapted tool between the groups. Results There was evidence in support of content validity, structural validity, internal consistency, convergent and divergent validity, test-retest validity, sensitivity and specificity (for distinguishing those with or without lifetime experience of suicide attempt), and hypothesis testing of the adapted tool (SBQ-ASC) in each group. The structure of the SBQ-ASC was equivalent between autistic and possibly autistic adults, regardless of gender, or use of visual aids to help quantify abstract rating scales. Limitations The samples involved in the development and validation of the adapted tool were largely female, and largely diagnosed as autistic in adulthood, which limits the generalisability of results to the wider autistic population. The SBQ-ASC has been developed for use in research and is not recommended to assess risk of future suicide attempts and/or self-harm. The SBQ-ASC has been designed with and for autistic and possibly autistic adults, and is not appropriate to compare to non-autistic adults given measurement differences between these groups. Conclusions The SBQ-ASC is a brief self-report suicidality assessment tool, developed and validated with and for autistic adults, without co-occurring intellectual disability. The SBQ-ASC is appropriate for use in research to identify suicidal thoughts and behaviours in autistic and possibly autistic people, and model associations with risk and protective factors.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa una persona autista adulta, puedes preguntarle directamente y con calma por pensamientos suicidas, usando palabras claras y concretas; preguntar no aumenta el riesgo y ayuda a que se sienta escuchada. Las preguntas generales pueden resultar ambiguas, por eso adultos autistas ayudaron a reformularlas. Este estudio adaptó un cuestionario con entrevistas y encuestas en línea a casi 700 adultos autistas, posiblemente autistas y no autistas, y mostró que funciona bien. Límites: la mayoría eran mujeres diagnosticadas en la adultez, sin discapacidad intelectual, y la herramienta es para investigación, no para predecir riesgo. Si hay peligro, contacta con servicios de emergencia o salud.
sheet.en: If you are worried about an autistic adult, you can ask directly and calmly about suicidal thoughts, using clear, concrete words; asking does not raise risk and helps the person feel heard. General questions can feel ambiguous, so autistic adults helped reword them. This study adapted a questionnaire through interviews and online surveys with nearly 700 autistic, possibly autistic and non-autistic adults, and found it measured well. Limits: most participants were women diagnosed in adulthood, without intellectual disability, and the tool is meant for research, not for predicting risk. If someone is in danger, contact emergency or health services.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för en autistisk vuxen kan du fråga direkt och lugnt om självmordstankar, med tydliga och konkreta ord; att fråga ökar inte risken och hjälper personen att känna sig lyssnad på. Allmänna frågor kan kännas tvetydiga, därför hjälpte autistiska vuxna till att formulera om dem. Studien anpassade ett frågeformulär genom intervjuer och webbenkäter med nästan 700 autistiska, möjligen autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna, och det fungerade väl. Begränsningar: de flesta var kvinnor diagnostiserade i vuxen ålder, utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, och verktyget är för forskning, inte för att förutsäga risk. Vid fara, kontakta akut- eller vårdtjänster.

title: International Expert Opinions and Recommendations on the Use of Melatonin in the Treatment of Insomnia and Circadian Sleep Disturbances in Adult Neuropsychiatric Disorders.
