authors: Scattoni ML, Micai M, Ciaramella A, Salvitti T, Fulceri F, Fatta LM, Poustka L, Diehm R, Iskrov G, Stefanov R, Guillon Q, Rogé B, Staines A, Sweeney MR, Boilson AM, Leósdóttir T, Saemundsen E, Moilane
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Research providing an evidence-base for autistic adult services is sparse. The Autism Spectrum Disorders in the European Union (ASDEU) network implemented an on-line survey to determine gaps in autistic adult diagnostic evaluation and post-diagnostic support services. More than 55% in all groups experienced most of the recommended features for diagnostic evaluation for autistic adults. In contrast, < 2% of adults or carers, and < 21% of professionals experienced each of the recommended features for post-diagnostic support. In contrast to 61% of professionals, only about 30% of autistic adults and carers had knowledge of good local services models for autism diagnosis in adulthood. There are major differences between good practice guidelines for diagnostic and post-diagnostic care for autistic adults, and what is actually experienced by services users and professionals.

sheet.es: Si tú o la persona a la que apoyas recibe un diagnóstico de autismo en la edad adulta, conviene preparar desde ya qué apoyo pedir después: el diagnóstico suele seguir las recomendaciones, pero el apoyo posterior a menudo falta. Puede ayudar preguntar directamente al servicio qué seguimiento ofrece, anotar necesidades concretas y buscar asociaciones de personas autistas o grupos locales. La evidencia procede de una encuesta en línea de la red europea ASDEU, respondida por adultos autistas, familiares y profesionales. Sus límites: las personas participantes se autoseleccionaron, los servicios varían mucho entre países y regiones, y una encuesta no mide la calidad real de cada servicio.
sheet.en: If you or the person you support receives an autism diagnosis in adulthood, it helps to plan now what support to ask for afterwards: diagnosis often follows guidelines, but post-diagnostic support is frequently missing. Consider asking the service directly what follow-up it offers, writing down concrete needs, and looking for autistic-led organisations or local peer groups. The evidence comes from an online survey by the European ASDEU network, answered by autistic adults, carers and professionals. Its limits: participants chose to take part, services vary widely between countries and regions, and a survey cannot measure the actual quality of each service.
sheet.sv: Om du eller personen du stöttar får en autismdiagnos i vuxen ålder kan det vara bra att redan nu planera vilket stöd ni ska be om efteråt: utredningen följer ofta riktlinjerna, men stödet efter diagnosen saknas ofta. Fråga gärna verksamheten direkt vilken uppföljning de erbjuder, skriv ner konkreta behov och sök upp autistiskt ledda organisationer eller lokala nätverk. Underlaget är en webbenkät från det europeiska nätverket ASDEU, besvarad av autistiska vuxna, anhöriga och yrkesverksamma. Begränsningar: deltagarna valde själva att svara, tjänsterna skiljer sig mycket mellan länder och regioner, och en enkät mäter inte varje verksamhets faktiska kvalitet.

title: An examination of active inference in autistic adults using immersive virtual reality.
authors: Arthur T, Harris D, Buckingham G, Brosnan M, Wilson M, Williams G, Vine S
abstract: The integration of prior expectations, sensory information, and environmental volatility is proposed to be atypical in Autism Spectrum Disorder, yet few studies have tested these predictive processes in active movement tasks. To address this gap in the research, we used an immersive virtual-reality racquetball paradigm to explore how visual sampling behaviours and movement kinematics are adjusted in relation to unexpected, uncertain, and volatile changes in environmental statistics. We found that prior expectations concerning ball 'bounciness' affected sensorimotor control in both autistic and neurotypical participants, with all individuals using prediction-driven gaze strategies to track the virtual ball. However, autistic participants showed substantial differences in visuomotor behaviour when environmental conditions were more volatile. Specifically, uncertainty-related performance difficulties in these conditions were accompanied by atypical movement kinematics and visual sampling responses. Results support proposals that autistic people overestimate the volatility of sensory environments, and suggest that context-sensitive differences in active inference could explain a range of movement-related difficulties in autism.

sheet.es: Si a tu familiar autista le cuestan las actividades de movimiento cuando las cosas cambian de forma impredecible (juegos de pelota, multitudes, reglas que varían), puede ayudar mantener algunas condiciones estables, avisar de los cambios y dar tiempo para adaptarse. No es falta de esfuerzo: su cerebro puede tratar el entorno como más cambiante de lo que es. En este estudio, adultos autistas y no autistas jugaron a un juego de raqueta en realidad virtual; todos anticipaban la pelota, pero los autistas mostraron más diferencias cuando las condiciones cambiaban mucho. Limitaciones: fue un grupo pequeño de adultos en un laboratorio, y los resultados no describen a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic family member finds movement activities harder when things change unpredictably (ball games, crowds, shifting rules), it may help to keep some conditions steady, announce changes, and allow time to adjust. This is not a lack of effort: their brain may treat the environment as more changeable than it is. In this study, autistic and non-autistic adults played a virtual-reality racquetball game; everyone anticipated the ball, but autistic players showed more differences in gaze and movement when conditions changed a lot. Limits: it was a small group of adults in a lab, and the findings do not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska familjemedlem tycker att rörelseaktiviteter blir svårare när saker ändras oförutsägbart (bollspel, folkmassor, regler som skiftar), kan det hjälpa att hålla vissa förhållanden stabila, förvarna om förändringar och ge tid att anpassa sig. Det handlar inte om bristande ansträngning: hjärnan kan uppfatta omgivningen som mer föränderlig än den är. I studien spelade autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna ett racketspel i virtuell verklighet; alla förutsåg bollen, men autistiska deltagare visade fler skillnader i blick och rörelse när förhållandena ändrades mycket. Begränsningar: en liten grupp vuxna i laboratorium, och resultaten beskriver inte varje person.

title: The Diagnosis of Autism: From Kanner to DSM-III to DSM-5 and Beyond.
authors: Rosen NE, Lord C, Volkmar FR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: In this paper we review the impact of DSM-III and its successors on the field of autism-both in terms of clinical work and research. We summarize the events leading up to the inclusion of autism as a "new" official diagnostic category in DSM-III, the subsequent revisions of the DSM, and the impact of the official recognition of autism on research. We discuss the uses of categorical vs. dimensional approaches and the continuing tensions around broad vs. narrow views of autism. We also note some areas of current controversy and directions for the future.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: si a tu hijo o a ti os dieron un diagnóstico con otro nombre (síndrome de Asperger, TGD), no significa que algo haya cambiado en la persona; cambiaron los manuales. Puedes pedir que te expliquen qué criterios se usaron y qué apoyos concretos se derivan, porque eso importa más que la etiqueta. Esta es una revisión histórica que repasa cómo el autismo pasó de Kanner al DSM-III y al DSM-5, y los debates entre visiones amplias y estrechas del autismo. Su límite: no recoge datos nuevos de participantes y refleja sobre todo la mirada clínica y de investigación, no necesariamente la experiencia de las personas autistas.
sheet.en: The practical point: if you or your child received a diagnosis under an older name (Asperger syndrome, PDD-NOS), the person hasn't changed; the manuals have. You can ask professionals which criteria were used and which concrete supports follow, since that matters more than the label itself. This is a historical review tracing how autism moved from Kanner's description through DSM-III to DSM-5, including debates about broad versus narrow definitions and categories versus dimensions. Its limit: it gathers no new data from participants and mainly reflects clinical and research perspectives, not necessarily the lived experience of autistic people.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: om du eller ditt barn fick en diagnos med ett äldre namn (Aspergers syndrom, autismliknande tillstånd) har personen inte förändrats; det är manualerna som har ändrats. Du kan fråga vilka kriterier som användes och vilket konkret stöd som följer, eftersom det betyder mer än själva etiketten. Detta är en historisk översikt som beskriver hur autism gick från Kanners beskrivning via DSM-III till DSM-5, och debatterna om breda kontra snäva definitioner samt kategorier kontra dimensioner. Begränsning: den samlar inga nya data från deltagare och speglar främst klinikers och forskares perspektiv, inte nödvändigtvis autistiska personers egna erfarenheter.

title: Adults with Autism: Changes in Understanding Since DSM-111.
authors: Howlin P
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Over the past four decades there have been significant advances in our understanding of autism, yet services for autistic adults continue to lag far behind those for children, and prospects for employment and independent living remain poor. Adult outcomes also vary widely and while cognitive and language abilities are important prognostic indicators, the influence of social, emotional, familial and many other factors remains uncertain. For this special issue marking the 40th anniversary of DSM-III, the present paper describes the changing perspectives of autism in adulthood that have occurred over this period, explores individual and wider environmental factors related to outcome, and suggests ways in which services need to be changed to improve the future for adults living with autism.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: los resultados en la adultez no están escritos de antemano. Además de las capacidades cognitivas y de lenguaje, influyen el entorno, el apoyo familiar, la salud emocional y el acceso a servicios. Mañana puedes empezar a planificar la transición a la vida adulta junto a la persona autista: preguntar qué quiere, anotar qué apoyos le funcionan y buscar servicios para adultos con tiempo, porque suelen ser escasos. Sobre la evidencia: es una revisión narrativa que resume cuatro décadas de investigación sobre adultos autistas desde el DSM-III. Límites: no aporta datos nuevos ni prueba intervenciones concretas, y refleja la perspectiva de sus autores.
sheet.en: The practical takeaway: adult outcomes are not fixed in advance. Alongside cognitive and language abilities, the environment, family support, emotional wellbeing and access to services all play a part. Tomorrow you could start planning the move into adulthood together with the autistic person: ask what they want, note which supports work for them, and look for adult services early, since they are often scarce. On the evidence: this is a narrative review summarising four decades of research on autistic adults since DSM-III. Its limits: it offers no new data, does not test specific interventions, and reflects the authors' own perspective.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: hur livet blir i vuxen ålder är inte bestämt på förhand. Utöver kognitiva och språkliga förmågor spelar miljö, stöd från familjen, emotionellt välmående och tillgång till stöd och service roll. I morgon kan du börja planera övergången till vuxenlivet tillsammans med den autistiska personen: fråga vad hen vill, anteckna vilket stöd som fungerar och sök vuxeninsatser i god tid, eftersom de ofta är få. Om evidensen: detta är en berättande översikt av fyra decenniers forskning om autistiska vuxna sedan DSM-III. Begränsningar: den ger inga nya data, prövar inga specifika insatser och speglar författarnas eget perspektiv.

title: Effects of Cognitive Training Programs on Executive Function in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Pasqualotto A, Mazzoni N, Bentenuto A, Mulè A, Benso F, Venuti P
abstract: Background Autism Spectrum Disorder is often associated with deficits in executive functions (EFs), which is contributing significantly to individuals with ASD's difficulties in conducting an independent life, particularly considering social skills. Technologies offer promising opportunities to structure EF intervention programs for children on the autistic spectrum. Methods This study aimed to review the effectiveness of randomized controlled trials or quasi-experimental studies of EF interventions delivered to children and young people (up to 23 years old) with a diagnosis of ASD. A special focus was dedicated to document the effectiveness of computerized and non-computerized cognitive training on (1) EFs and on (2) ASD symptomatology and social skills. Of 2601 studies retrieved, 19 fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Results Most of the interventions identified were effective in enhancing EFs and reducing symptoms in children and young people with ASD. Limited evidence is available on their generalization to untrained skills (i.e., social abilities) as well as long-term effects. Conclusions There is growing evidence for overall effectiveness of EF training, particularly when computerized. However, caution should be taken when interpreting these findings owing to methodological limitations, the minimal number of papers retrieved, and a small samples of included studies.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista disfruta de juegos o actividades que entrenan la planificación, la memoria de trabajo o la flexibilidad, pueden ser una opción razonable, sobre todo en formato digital. Mantén expectativas realistas: mejorar en el juego no siempre se traslada a la vida diaria o a la relación con otros, así que conviene practicar también esas habilidades en situaciones reales y siguiendo sus intereses. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 19 estudios con niños y jóvenes autistas de hasta 23 años, y la mayoría encontró mejoras en las funciones ejecutivas. Sus límites: pocos estudios, muestras pequeñas, debilidades metodológicas y escasos datos sobre efectos a largo plazo.
sheet.en: If your autistic child enjoys games or activities that train planning, working memory or flexibility, these can be a reasonable option, especially in computer-based form. Keep expectations realistic: getting better at the game does not always carry over into daily life or social situations, so it helps to also practise those skills in real settings, building on your child's interests. This systematic review gathered 19 studies of autistic children and young people up to 23 years old, and most found improvements in executive functions. Its limits: few studies, small samples, methodological weaknesses and little data on long-term effects.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn tycker om spel eller aktiviteter som tränar planering, arbetsminne eller flexibilitet kan de vara ett rimligt alternativ, särskilt i datorbaserad form. Ha realistiska förväntningar: att bli bättre på spelet överförs inte alltid till vardagen eller sociala situationer, så det hjälper att också öva de förmågorna i verkliga sammanhang och utgå från barnets intressen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 19 studier med autistiska barn och unga upp till 23 år, och de flesta fann förbättringar i exekutiva funktioner. Begränsningar: få studier, små urval, metodologiska svagheter och lite data om långsiktiga effekter.

title: Features of Mobile Apps for People with Autism in a Post COVID-19 Scenario: Current Status and Recommendations for Apps Using AI.
authors: Rehman IU, Sobnath D, Sobnath D, Nasralla MM, Winnett M, Anwar A, Asif W, Sherazi HHR
abstract: The new 'normal' defined during the COVID-19 pandemic has forced us to re-assess how people with special needs thrive in these unprecedented conditions, such as those with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). These changing/challenging conditions have instigated us to revisit the usage of telehealth services to improve the quality of life for people with ASD. This study aims to identify mobile applications that suit the needs of such individuals. This work focuses on identifying features of a number of highly-rated mobile applications (apps) that are designed to assist people with ASD, specifically those features that use Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. In this study, 250 mobile apps have been retrieved using keywords such as autism, autism AI, and autistic. Among 250 apps, 46 were identified after filtering out irrelevant apps based on defined elimination criteria such as ASD common users, medical staff, and non-medically trained people interacting with people with ASD. In order to review common functionalities and features, 25 apps were downloaded and analysed based on eye tracking, facial expression analysis, use of 3D cartoons, haptic feedback, engaging interface, text-to-speech, use of Applied Behaviour Analysis therapy, Augmentative and Alternative Communication techniques, among others were also deconstructed. As a result, software developers and healthcare professionals can consider the identified features in designing future support tools for autistic people. This study hypothesises that by studying these current features, further recommendations of how existing applications for ASD people could be enhanced using AI for (1) progress tracking, (2) personalised content delivery, (3) automated reasoning, (4) image recognition, and (5) Natural Language Processing (NLP). This paper follows the PRISMA methodology, which involves a set of recommendations for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

sheet.es: Si estás buscando una app para apoyar a tu hijo o hija autista, puedes fijarte en funciones concretas: comunicación aumentativa y alternativa (CAA), texto a voz, una interfaz clara y la posibilidad de adaptar el contenido a sus intereses y ritmo. Pruébala juntos unos días y observa si le resulta cómoda y útil, no solo si está bien valorada. Esta revisión analizó 250 apps de tiendas en línea y examinó a fondo 25. Evaluó las funciones que ofrecen, pero no midió si ayudan de verdad a las personas autistas. Tampoco recogió sus opiniones, así que tu observación y la de tu hijo siguen siendo clave.
sheet.en: If you are looking for an app to support your autistic child, look for concrete features: augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), text-to-speech, a clear interface, and content you can adapt to their interests and pace. Try it together for a few days and notice whether it feels comfortable and useful, not just whether it is highly rated. This review searched app stores, found 250 autism apps and examined 25 in detail. It described the features the apps offer but did not test whether they actually help autistic people. It also did not gather their views, so your own observations and your child's experience still matter most.
sheet.sv: Om du letar efter en app för att stötta ditt autistiska barn kan du titta efter konkreta funktioner: alternativ och kompletterande kommunikation (AKK), text-till-tal, ett tydligt gränssnitt och innehåll som går att anpassa efter barnets intressen och tempo. Prova appen tillsammans några dagar och märk om den känns bekväm och användbar, inte bara om den har höga betyg. Översikten sökte i appbutiker, hittade 250 autismappar och granskade 25 närmare. Den beskrev vilka funktioner apparna har, men testade inte om de faktiskt hjälper autistiska personer. Den samlade inte heller in deras synpunkter, så det som du och ditt barn själva märker väger fortfarande tyngst.

title: Prevalence of Autism Spectrum Disorder and Co-morbidities in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Bougeard C, Picarel-Blanchot F, Schmid R, Campbell R, Buitelaar J
abstract: Objective: Individuals with autism spectrum disorder often present somatic and/or psychiatric co-morbid disorders. The DSM-5 allows for consideration of additional diagnoses besides ASD and may have impacted the prevalence of co-morbidities as well as being limited in capturing the true differences in prevalence observed between males and females. We describe the prevalence of ASD and frequently observed co-morbidities in children and adolescents ( Methods: Two systematic literature reviews were conducted in PubMed and Embase for the period 2014-2019 and focusing on the prevalence of ASD and nine co-morbidities of interest based on their frequency and/or severity: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), anxiety, depressive disorders, epilepsy, intellectual disability (ID), sleep disorders, sight/hearing impairment/loss, and gastro-intestinal syndromes (GI). Results: Thirteen studies on prevalence of ASD and 33 on prevalence of co-morbidities were included. Prevalence of ASD was 1.70 and 1.85% in US children aged 4 and 8 years respectively, while prevalence in Europe ranged between 0.38 and 1.55%. Additionally, current evidence is supportive of a global increase in ASD prevalence over the past years. Substantial heterogeneity in prevalence of co-morbidities was observed: ADHD (0.00-86.00%), anxiety (0.00-82.20%), depressive disorders (0.00-74.80%), epilepsy (2.80-77.50%), ID (0.00-91.70%), sleep disorders (2.08-72.50%), sight/hearing impairment/loss (0.00-14.90%/0.00-4.90%), and GI syndromes (0.00-67.80%). Studies were heterogeneous in terms of design and method to estimate prevalence. Gender appears to represent a risk factor for co-morbid ADHD (higher in males) and epilepsy/seizure (higher in females) while age is also associated with ADHD and anxiety (increasing until adolescence). Conclusion: Our results provide a descriptive review of the prevalence of ASD and its co-morbidities in children and adolescents. These insights can be valuable for clinicians and parents/guardians of autistic children. Prevalence of ASD has increased over time while co-morbidities bring additional heterogeneity to the clinical presentation, which further advocates for personalized approaches to treatment and support. Having a clear understanding of the prevalence of ASD and its co-morbidities is important to raise awareness among stakeholders.

sheet.es: Muchos niños y adolescentes autistas tienen también otras condiciones, como TDAH, ansiedad, depresión, epilepsia, discapacidad intelectual, problemas de sueño, de vista u oído, o molestias digestivas. Si notas cambios en el sueño, la digestión, el ánimo o episodios extraños, vale la pena anotarlos y comentarlos con el equipo de salud, en lugar de atribuirlo todo al autismo. Cada persona tiene una combinación distinta, por eso el apoyo debe ser personalizado. Es una revisión sistemática de 46 estudios publicados entre 2014 y 2019 con niños y adolescentes. Sus límites: los estudios usaron métodos muy diferentes, por lo que las cifras varían enormemente y no predicen lo que vivirá tu hijo.
sheet.en: Many autistic children and teenagers also have other conditions, such as ADHD, anxiety, depression, epilepsy, intellectual disability, sleep difficulties, sight or hearing differences, or gut problems. If you notice changes in sleep, digestion, mood or unusual episodes, it helps to write them down and raise them with your health team, rather than assuming everything is 'just autism'. Each person has a different mix, so support should be personalised. This is a systematic review of 46 studies published between 2014 and 2019 involving children and adolescents. Its limits: the studies used very different methods, so the figures vary enormously and cannot predict what your child will experience.
sheet.sv: Många autistiska barn och tonåringar har också andra tillstånd, som adhd, ångest, depression, epilepsi, intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, sömnsvårigheter, syn- eller hörselnedsättning eller magbesvär. Om du märker förändringar i sömn, mage, humör eller ovanliga episoder kan det hjälpa att anteckna dem och ta upp dem med vården, i stället för att anta att allt beror på autismen. Varje person har sin egen kombination, så stödet behöver vara individuellt. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 46 studier publicerade 2014–2019 med barn och ungdomar. Begränsningar: studierna använde mycket olika metoder, så siffrorna varierar enormt och kan inte förutsäga hur det blir för just ditt barn.

title: The Role of Maternal Immune Activation in the Pathogenesis of Autism: A Review of the Evidence, Proposed Mechanisms and Implications for Treatment.
authors: Zawadzka A, Cieślik M, Adamczyk A
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disease that is characterized by a deficit in social interactions and communication, as well as repetitive and restrictive behaviors. Increasing lines of evidence suggest an important role for immune dysregulation and/or inflammation in the development of ASD. Recently, a relationship between inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction has been reported in the brain tissue of individuals with ASD. Some recent studies have also reported oxidative stress and mitochondrial abnormalities in animal models of maternal immune activation (MIA). This review is focused on the hypothesis that MIA induces microglial activation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, a deleterious trio in the brain that can lead to neuroinflammation and neurodevelopmental pathologies in offspring. Infection during pregnancy activates the mother's immune system to release proinflammatory cytokines, such as IL-6, TNF-α, and others. Furthermore, these cytokines can directly cross the placenta and enter the fetal circulation, or activate resident immune cells, resulting in an increased production of proinflammatory cytokines, including IL-6. Proinflammatory cytokines that cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB) may initiate a neuroinflammation cascade, starting with the activation of the microglia. Inflammatory processes induce oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction that, in turn, may exacerbate oxidative stress in a self-perpetuating vicious cycle that can lead to downstream abnormalities in brain development and behavior.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada práctico: esta revisión no ofrece pautas de apoyo ni tratamientos para su hijo o hija autista. Si usted se pregunta si una infección en el embarazo «causó» el autismo, puede soltar la culpa: el autismo tiene muchas influencias, sobre todo genéticas, y nadie hizo nada mal. Si tiene dudas sobre la salud física, hable con su equipo médico. Se trata de una revisión narrativa que reúne estudios, sobre todo en modelos animales, sobre cómo la activación inmune materna podría afectar el desarrollo cerebral. Su límite: describe hipótesis y mecanismos, no prueba causas en personas ni evalúa tratamientos.
sheet.en: Nothing practical changes tomorrow: this review offers no support strategies or treatments for your autistic child. If you wonder whether an infection during pregnancy "caused" autism, you can let go of blame: autism has many influences, mostly genetic, and no one did anything wrong. If you have concerns about physical health, talk with your healthcare team. This is a narrative review gathering studies, largely in animal models, on how maternal immune activation might affect brain development. Its limit: it describes hypotheses and mechanisms; it does not prove causes in people or test any treatment.
sheet.sv: Inget praktiskt ändras i morgon: översikten ger inga stödstrategier eller behandlingar för ditt autistiska barn. Om du undrar om en infektion under graviditeten "orsakade" autismen kan du släppa skulden: autism har många påverkansfaktorer, främst genetiska, och ingen har gjort något fel. Har du frågor om fysisk hälsa, prata med vården. Detta är en narrativ översikt som samlar studier, mest på djurmodeller, om hur moderns immunaktivering kan påverka hjärnans utveckling. Begränsning: den beskriver hypoteser och mekanismer, bevisar inte orsaker hos människor och prövar ingen behandling.

title: Role of phosphodiesterases in the pathophysiology of neurodevelopmental disorders.
authors: Delhaye S, Bardoni B
abstract: Phosphodiesterases (PDEs) are enzymes involved in the homeostasis of both cAMP and cGMP. They are members of a family of proteins that includes 11 subfamilies with different substrate specificities. Their main function is to catalyze the hydrolysis of cAMP, cGMP, or both. cAMP and cGMP are two key second messengers that modulate a wide array of intracellular processes and neurobehavioral functions, including memory and cognition. Even if these enzymes are present in all tissues, we focused on those PDEs that are expressed in the brain. We took into consideration genetic variants in patients affected by neurodevelopmental disorders, phenotypes of animal models, and pharmacological effects of PDE inhibitors, a class of drugs in rapid evolution and increasing application to brain disorders. Collectively, these data indicate the potential of PDE modulators to treat neurodevelopmental diseases characterized by learning and memory impairment, alteration of behaviors associated with depression, and deficits in social interaction. Indeed, clinical trials are in progress to treat patients with Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, depression, and autism spectrum disorders. Among the most recent results, the application of some PDE inhibitors (PDE2A, PDE3, PDE4/4D, and PDE10A) to treat neurodevelopmental diseases, including autism spectrum disorders and intellectual disability, is a significant advance, since no specific therapies are available for these disorders that have a large prevalence. In addition, to highlight the role of several PDEs in normal and pathological neurodevelopment, we focused here on the deregulation of cAMP and/or cGMP in Down Syndrome, Fragile X Syndrome, Rett Syndrome, and intellectual disability associated with the CC2D1A gene.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en casa: esta revisión trata sobre biología cerebral y posibles fármacos futuros, no sobre apoyos cotidianos. Si alguien le ofrece un 'tratamiento' basado en enzimas PDE, conviene hablarlo con el equipo médico antes de tomar decisiones y seguir apoyando lo que ya funciona: rutinas previsibles, comunicación accesible e intereses propios. Evidencia: es una revisión narrativa que reúne estudios genéticos, modelos animales y ensayos farmacológicos sobre autismo, síndrome X frágil, Rett, Down y discapacidad intelectual. Límites: gran parte procede de animales y ensayos en curso; no demuestra beneficios en personas autistas ni sirve como guía para nadie en particular.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change at home tomorrow: this review is about brain biology and possible future medicines, not everyday support. If anyone offers a 'treatment' based on PDE enzymes, talk it through with the medical team before deciding, and keep supporting what already works: predictable routines, accessible communication and the person's own interests. Evidence: this is a narrative review pulling together genetic findings, animal models and drug studies related to autism, Fragile X, Rett and Down syndromes and intellectual disability. Limits: much of the evidence comes from animals and unfinished trials; it does not show benefits for autistic people and is not guidance for any individual.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras hemma i morgon: denna översikt handlar om hjärnans biologi och möjliga framtida läkemedel, inte om vardagsstöd. Om någon erbjuder en 'behandling' baserad på PDE-enzymer, prata med vårdteamet innan ni bestämmer något, och fortsätt med det som redan fungerar: förutsägbara rutiner, tillgänglig kommunikation och personens egna intressen. Evidens: en narrativ översikt som samlar genetiska fynd, djurmodeller och läkemedelsstudier kring autism, fragilt X-, Rett- och Downs syndrom samt intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Begränsningar: mycket bygger på djurstudier och pågående prövningar; den visar ingen nytta för autistiska personer och är ingen vägledning för enskilda.

title: What I Wish You Knew: Insights on Burnout, Inertia, Meltdown, and Shutdown From Autistic Youth.
authors: Phung J, Penner M, Pirlot C, Welch C
abstract: Introduction: Burnout, inertia, meltdown, and shutdown (BIMS) have been identified as important parts of some autistic people's lives. This study builds on our previous work that offered early academic descriptions of these phenomena, based on the perspectives of autistic adults. Objectives: This study aimed to explore the unique knowledge and insights of eight autistic children and youth to extend and refine our earlier description of burnout, i nertia, and meltdown, with additional exploration of shutdown. We also aimed to explore how these youth cope with these phenomena and what others around them do that make things better or worse, with a hope to glean knowledge to design better supports. Methods: One-to-one interviews were conducted with eight children and youth, who shared their experience with BIMS. To match individual communication strengths of children and youth, we took a flexible approach to interviews, allowing for augmentative communication systems and use of visual images to support verbal interviews, as needed. We conducted a reflexive, inductive thematic analysis, using an iterative process of coding, collating, reviewing, and mapping themes. Findings: Our analysis has identified that these youth describe BIMS as a multi-faceted experience involving emotional, cognitive and physical components. Moreover, these multifaceted experiences are often misunderstood by neurotypical adults, which contributes to inadequate support in managing BIMS. Of the four experiences, these youth identified meltdowns as most common. Conclusion: By gaining first-hand perspectives, we have identified novel insights into BIMS and developed a more holistic understanding of these phenomena. These youths' descriptions of supportive strategies for BIMS stress the importance of compassion and collaboration from trusted adults. This new knowledge will provide a foundation for how to better support autistic children and youth. Further research is required to develop an understanding of BIMS, especially with respect to how it is experienced by children and youth. Future research should leverage the insights and experiential knowledge of autistic children and youth to co-design support tool(s) for BIMS.

sheet.es: Cuando su hijo o hija autista tenga un colapso (meltdown), se bloquee (shutdown), no pueda empezar o cambiar de tarea (inercia) o muestre agotamiento prolongado (burnout), no lo vea como desobediencia. Pruebe a bajar las exigencias, reducir el ruido y las palabras, quedarse cerca con calma y preguntar después qué le ayuda. Los jóvenes destacaron la compasión y el trabajo conjunto con adultos de confianza. Es un estudio cualitativo de entrevistas con ocho niños y jóvenes autistas, que podían usar comunicación aumentativa o imágenes. Sus limitaciones: la muestra es pequeña y las experiencias son personales, así que lo que sirve a uno puede no servir a otro.
sheet.en: When your autistic child has a meltdown, shuts down, struggles to start or switch tasks (inertia), or shows long-lasting exhaustion (burnout), try not to read it as defiance. Lower demands, reduce noise and talk, stay nearby calmly, and later ask together what helps. The young people stressed compassion and collaboration from trusted adults, and said meltdowns were the most common experience. This was a qualitative interview study with eight autistic children and youth, who could use augmentative communication or pictures. Its limits: the group was small and experiences are individual, so what helps one young person may not help another.
sheet.sv: När ditt autistiska barn får en meltdown, stänger av (shutdown), har svårt att komma igång eller byta aktivitet (inertia) eller visar långvarig utmattning (autistisk utbrändhet), försök att inte tolka det som trots. Sänk kraven, minska ljud och prat, var lugnt nära och fråga efteråt tillsammans vad som hjälper. Ungdomarna betonade medkänsla och samarbete med trygga vuxna, och meltdowns var det vanligaste. Studien är en kvalitativ intervjustudie med åtta autistiska barn och unga, som kunde använda alternativ kommunikation eller bilder. Begränsningar: gruppen var liten och upplevelser är individuella, så det som hjälper en person passar inte alla.

title: The meaning of significant mean group differences for biomarker discovery.
authors: Loth E, Ahmad J, Chatham C, López B, Carter B, Crawley D, Oakley B, Hayward H, Cooke J, San José Cáceres A, Bzdok D, Jones E, Charman T, Beckmann C, Bourgeron T, Toro R, Buitelaar J, Murphy D, Dumas G
abstract: Over the past decade, biomarker discovery has become a key goal in psychiatry to aid in the more reliable diagnosis and prognosis of heterogeneous psychiatric conditions and the development of tailored therapies. Nevertheless, the prevailing statistical approach is still the mean group comparison between "cases" and "controls," which tends to ignore within-group variability. In this educational article, we used empirical data simulations to investigate how effect size, sample size, and the shape of distributions impact the interpretation of mean group differences for biomarker discovery. We then applied these statistical criteria to evaluate biomarker discovery in one area of psychiatric research-autism research. Across the most influential areas of autism research, effect size estimates ranged from small (d = 0.21, anatomical structure) to medium (d = 0.36 electrophysiology, d = 0.5, eye-tracking) to large (d = 1.1 theory of mind). We show that in normal distributions, this translates to approximately 45% to 63% of cases performing within 1 standard deviation (SD) of the typical range, i.e., they do not have a deficit/atypicality in a statistical sense. For a measure to have diagnostic utility as defined by 80% sensitivity and 80% specificity, Cohen's d of 1.66 is required, with still 40% of cases falling within 1 SD. However, in both normal and nonnormal distributions, 1 (skewness) or 2 (platykurtic, bimodal) biologically plausible subgroups may exist despite small or even nonsignificant mean group differences. This conclusion drastically contrasts the way mean group differences are frequently reported. Over 95% of studies omitted the "on average" when summarising their findings in their abstracts ("autistic people have deficits in X"), which can be misleading as it implies that the group-level difference applies to all individuals in that group. We outline practical approaches and steps for researchers to explore mean group comparisons for the discovery of stratification biomarkers.

sheet.es: Cuando leas que «las personas autistas tienen déficits en X», recuerda que casi siempre significa «en promedio». Muchas personas autistas están dentro del rango típico en esa medida, así que un titular no describe a tu hijo, hija o a ti. Observa a la persona concreta: sus fortalezas y necesidades reales. Este es un artículo educativo que usó simulaciones de datos y revisó estudios influyentes de investigación sobre autismo (cerebro, electrofisiología, seguimiento ocular, teoría de la mente); entre el 45 % y el 63 % de las personas autistas puntuaban dentro del rango típico. Límite: es un análisis estadístico, no un estudio con participantes nuevos, y no ofrece pautas de apoyo directas.
sheet.en: When you read that "autistic people have deficits in X," remember it almost always means "on average." Many autistic people score within the typical range on that measure, so a headline does not describe your child or you. Look at the actual person: their real strengths and needs. This is an educational article that used data simulations and reviewed influential areas of autism research (brain structure, electrophysiology, eye-tracking, theory of mind); roughly 45% to 63% of autistic people scored within the typical range. Limit: it is a statistical analysis, not a study with new participants, and it offers no direct support strategies.
sheet.sv: När du läser att ”autistiska personer har brister i X”, kom ihåg att det nästan alltid betyder ”i genomsnitt”. Många autistiska personer ligger inom det typiska spannet på det måttet, så en rubrik beskriver inte ditt barn eller dig. Se till den faktiska personen: verkliga styrkor och behov. Detta är en pedagogisk artikel som använde datasimuleringar och granskade inflytelserika områden inom autismforskning (hjärnstruktur, elektrofysiologi, ögonrörelsemätning, theory of mind); ungefär 45–63 % av autistiska personer låg inom det typiska spannet. Begränsning: det är en statistisk analys, inte en studie med nya deltagare, och den ger inga direkta stödstrategier.

title: Barriers to Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Young Women and Girls: a Systematic Review.
authors: Lockwood Estrin G, Milner V, Spain D, Happé F, Colvert E
journal: Review journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: There is increased recognition that women and girls with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are underserved by the clinical criteria and processes required to receive a diagnosis. This mixed-methods systematic review aimed to identify key barriers to obtaining an ASD diagnosis in girls and young women under 21 years. Six themes were identified that focused on perceived gendered symptoms, namely behavioural problems, social and communication abilities, language, relationships, additional diagnoses/difficulties and restricted and repetitive behaviours and interests. Five themes were identified as (parental) perceived barriers to diagnosis, namely compensatory behaviours, parental concerns, others' perceptions, lack of information/resources and clinician bias. This review highlights the importance of enhancing widespread understanding and recognition of ASD presentation in females across development. PROSPERO Centre for Reviews and Dissemination (ID 2018 CRD42018087235). Supplementary information The online version of this article (10.1007/s40489-020-00225-8) contains supplementary material, which is available to authorized users.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña o joven y sospechas que podría ser autista, confía en lo que observas aunque otros no lo vean. Muchas chicas camuflan sus diferencias (imitan a otras, se esfuerzan por encajar) y se agotan después en casa. Anota ejemplos concretos —cansancio tras el colegio, intereses intensos, amistades difíciles— y llévalos a la consulta; si sientes que no te escuchan, puedes pedir otra opinión. Esta revisión sistemática reunió estudios cualitativos y cuantitativos sobre chicas y jóvenes menores de 21 años, sobre todo desde la perspectiva de las familias. Sus límites: se basa en percepciones parentales y estudios variados, y no todas las chicas viven estas barreras igual.
sheet.en: If you care for a girl or young woman you think may be autistic, trust what you notice even when others don't see it. Many girls mask their differences (copying peers, working hard to fit in) and then feel exhausted at home. Write down concrete examples—tiredness after school, intense interests, difficult friendships—and bring them to appointments; if you feel unheard, you can ask for a second opinion. This mixed-methods systematic review gathered studies on girls and young women under 21, largely from parents' perspectives. Its limits: it relies mainly on parental perceptions and varied studies, and not every girl meets these barriers in the same way.
sheet.sv: Om du har ansvar för en flicka eller ung kvinna som du tror kan vara autistisk, lita på det du ser även när andra inte gör det. Många flickor maskerar sina olikheter (härmar jämnåriga, anstränger sig för att passa in) och blir sedan utmattade hemma. Skriv ner konkreta exempel – trötthet efter skolan, intensiva intressen, svåra vänskaper – och ta med dem till besöket; känner du dig inte lyssnad på kan du be om en ny bedömning. Denna systematiska översikt med blandade metoder samlade studier om flickor och unga kvinnor under 21 år, främst utifrån föräldrars perspektiv. Begränsningar: den bygger mest på föräldrars upplevelser och skiftande studier, och alla flickor möter inte samma hinder.

title: A Systematic Review on the Impact of the Social Confinement on People with Autism Spectrum Disorder and Their Caregivers during the COVID-19 Pandemic.
authors: Alonso-Esteban Y, López-Ramón MF, Moreno-Campos V, Navarro-Pardo E, Alcantud-Marín F
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic had imposed a variety of containment measures on the general population for prolonged periods. Confinement has had, and still has, social, economic, educational, health, and psychological consequences on the entire population. Objective In this article, a systematic search has been performed based on studies carried out since the beginning of the pandemic, regarding the impact of these containment measures on the autism spectrum disorder (ASD) population and their caregivers. Method We consulted six databases (i.e., PubMed, Medline, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Science Direct) and selected ten studies that met the inclusion criteria. The chosen studies have been classified according to their theoretical focus, methodology, and target population. Results We found an increase in stress and a decrease in psychological well-being among individuals diagnosed with ASD (i.e., parents and caregivers). Additionally, in studies focused on children, youth, and adults with ASD diagnosis, the results are contradictory depending on variables such as age, ASD severity, or type of family structure. Conclusions The results show that the consequences of quarantine and social confinement are quite contradictory and depend on variables such as age, ASD severity, and family features.

sheet.es: Si una rutina cambia de golpe (cierres, enfermedad, vacaciones), cuida también tu propio descanso: el estrés de quienes cuidan aumentó claramente durante el confinamiento. Para la persona autista, observa cómo reacciona ella en concreto; a algunas les costó mucho, otras vivieron menos presión social. Ofrece previsibilidad, avisa de los cambios y busca apoyo para ti sin culpa. La evidencia procede de una revisión sistemática de diez estudios de 2020-2021 con personas autistas de distintas edades y sus familias. Sus límites: pocos estudios, métodos muy variados y resultados contradictorios según la edad, las necesidades de apoyo y la estructura familiar.
sheet.en: When routines change suddenly (lockdowns, illness, holidays), protect your own rest too: caregiver stress clearly rose during confinement. For the autistic person, watch how they in particular respond; some found it very hard, others experienced less social pressure. Offer predictability, give notice of changes, and seek support for yourself without guilt. The evidence comes from a systematic review of ten studies from 2020–2021 involving autistic children, youth and adults and their families. Its limits: few studies, very different methods, and contradictory results depending on age, support needs and family structure.
sheet.sv: När rutiner plötsligt förändras (nedstängning, sjukdom, lov) behöver du skydda din egen vila också: stressen hos anhöriga ökade tydligt under pandemins restriktioner. Lägg märke till hur just din autistiska person reagerar; för vissa var det mycket svårt, andra upplevde mindre socialt tryck. Erbjud förutsägbarhet, förvarna om förändringar och sök stöd för dig själv utan skuld. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av tio studier från 2020–2021 med autistiska barn, unga och vuxna samt deras familjer. Begränsningar: få studier, mycket olika metoder och motstridiga resultat beroende på ålder, stödbehov och familjesituation.

title: Effects of Creative Movement Therapies on Social Communication, Behavioral-Affective, Sensorimotor, Cognitive, and Functional Participation Skills of Individuals With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Amonkar N, Su WC, Bhat AN, Srinivasan SM
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder affecting multiple developmental domains including social communication, behavioral-affective, sensorimotor, and cognitive systems. There is growing evidence for the use of holistic, whole-body, Creative Movement Therapies (CMT) such as music, dance, yoga, theater, and martial arts in addressing the multisystem impairments in ASD. We conducted a comprehensive quantitative and qualitative review of the evidence to date on the effects of CMT on multiple systems in individuals with ASD. The strongest evidence, both in terms of quantity and quality, exists for music and martial arts-based interventions followed by yoga and theater, with very limited research on dance-based approaches. Our review of 72 studies ( N = 1,939 participants) across participants with ASD ranging from 3 to 65 years of age suggests that at present there is consistent evidence from high quality studies for small-to-large sized improvements in social communication skills following music and martial arts therapies and medium-to-large improvements in motor and cognitive skills following yoga and martial arts training, with insufficient evidence to date for gains in affective, sensory, and functional participation domains following CMT. Although promising, our review serves as a call for more rigorous high-quality research to assess the multisystem effects of CMT in ASD. Based on the existing literature, we discuss implications of our findings for autism researchers and also provide evidence-based guidelines for clinicians to incorporate CMT approaches in their plan of care for individuals with ASD.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o familiar autista le atrae la música, las artes marciales, el yoga o el teatro, puede valer la pena probar una actividad así, a su ritmo y respetando sus preferencias sensoriales. La música y las artes marciales se asociaron con mejoras en la comunicación social, y el yoga y las artes marciales con mejoras motoras y cognitivas. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 72 estudios con 1.939 personas autistas de 3 a 65 años. Sus límites: la calidad de los estudios varía, hay poca investigación sobre danza y no hay pruebas suficientes sobre bienestar emocional, sensorial o participación diaria. Lo que ayuda a una persona puede no ayudar a otra.
sheet.en: If your autistic child or family member enjoys music, martial arts, yoga or theatre, trying one of these activities may be worthwhile, at their own pace and with respect for their sensory preferences. Music and martial arts were linked to gains in social communication, and yoga and martial arts to gains in motor and thinking skills. This systematic review pooled 72 studies with 1,939 autistic people aged 3 to 65. Its limits: study quality varies, dance has barely been researched, and there is not enough evidence about emotional, sensory or everyday participation outcomes. What helps one person may not help another.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn eller din anhörige tycker om musik, kampsport, yoga eller teater kan det vara värt att prova en sådan aktivitet, i egen takt och med respekt för sensoriska behov. Musik och kampsport kopplades till förbättrad social kommunikation, och yoga och kampsport till förbättrad motorik och kognition. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 72 studier med 1 939 autistiska personer mellan 3 och 65 år. Begränsningar: studiernas kvalitet varierar, dans är knappt undersökt och det saknas tillräckliga belägg för effekter på känslor, sinnesintryck och vardagligt deltagande. Det som hjälper en person hjälper inte nödvändigtvis en annan.

title: The feasibility of low-intensity psychological therapy for depression co-occurring with autism in adults: The Autism Depression Trial (ADEPT) - a pilot randomised controlled trial.
authors: Russell A, Gaunt DM, Cooper K, Barton S, Horwood J, Kessler D, Metcalfe C, Ensum I, Ingham B, Parr JR, Rai D, Wiles N
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Low-intensity cognitive behaviour therapy including behavioural activation is an evidence-based treatment for depression, a condition frequently co-occurring with autism. The feasibility of adapting low-intensity cognitive behaviour therapy for depression to meet the needs of autistic adults via a randomised controlled trial was investigated. The adapted intervention (guided self-help) comprised materials for nine individual sessions with a low-intensity psychological therapist. Autistic adults (n = 70) with depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score ⩾10) recruited from National Health Service adult autism services and research cohorts were randomly allocated to guided self-help or treatment as usual. Outcomes at 10-, 16- and 24-weeks post-randomisation were blind to treatment group. Rates of retention in the study differed by treatment group with more participants attending follow-up in the guided self-help group than treatment as usual. The adapted intervention was well-received, 86% (n = 30/35) of participants attended the pre-defined 'dose' of five sessions of treatment and 71% (25/35) attended all treatment sessions. The findings of this pilot randomised controlled trial indicate that low-intensity cognitive behaviour therapy informed by behavioural activation can be successfully adapted to meet the needs of autistic people. Evaluation of the effectiveness of this intervention in a full scale randomised controlled trial is now warranted.

sheet.es: Si un adulto autista de tu entorno vive con depresión, puede valer la pena preguntar a su servicio de salud por una terapia guiada de baja intensidad adaptada al autismo, con materiales claros y sesiones individuales centradas en retomar actividades significativas. Este estudio piloto aleatorizado incluyó a 70 adultos autistas con depresión en el Reino Unido: la terapia adaptada de nueve sesiones fue bien recibida, y el 71 % asistió a todas las sesiones. Su límite es que solo comprobó si la terapia era viable y aceptable, no si reduce la depresión; hace falta un ensayo más grande, y cada persona puede necesitar algo distinto.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult in your life is living with depression, it may be worth asking their health service about low-intensity guided self-help adapted for autism, with clear materials and one-to-one sessions focused on gently returning to meaningful activities. This pilot randomised controlled trial included 70 autistic adults with depression in the UK: the adapted nine-session therapy was well received, and 71% attended every session. Its limit is that it only tested whether the therapy was feasible and acceptable, not whether it reduces depression; a larger trial is needed, and each person may need something different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen i din närhet lever med depression kan det vara värt att fråga vården om lågintensiv guidad självhjälp anpassad för autism, med tydligt material och enskilda samtal som fokuserar på att varsamt återuppta meningsfulla aktiviteter. Denna randomiserade pilotstudie omfattade 70 autistiska vuxna med depression i Storbritannien: den anpassade terapin med nio sessioner togs emot väl, och 71 % deltog i alla sessioner. Begränsningen är att studien bara undersökte om terapin var genomförbar och accepterad, inte om den minskar depression; en större studie behövs, och varje person kan behöva något annat.

title: The impact of COVID-19 on the mental health and wellbeing of caregivers of autistic children and youth: A scoping review.
authors: Lee V, Albaum C, Tablon Modica P, Ahmad F, Gorter JW, Khanlou N, McMorris C, Lai J, Harrison C, Hedley T, Johnston P, Putterman C, Spoelstra M, Weiss JA
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Caregivers and families of autistic people have experienced stress and increase in demands due to the COVID-19 pandemic that may have long-term negative consequences for both their own and their children's mental health. A scoping review was conducted to identify pandemic related demands experienced by caregivers and families of autistic children and youth. The review also consolidated information on coping strategies and parenting-related guidelines that have emerged to help parents meet these demands. Search strategies were approved by a research librarian and were conducted in peer-reviewed and gray literature databases between May 2020 and February 2021. Additional resources were solicited through author networks and social media. All articles were published between December 2019 and February 2021. Article summaries were charted, and a thematic analysis was conducted with confirmation of findings with our knowledge users. Twenty-three published articles and 14 pieces of gray literature were included in the review. The majority of articles characterized and highlighted the increase in demands on caregivers of autistic children and youth during the pandemic globally. Both quantitative and qualitative studies suggest that parents have experienced an increase in stress and mental health-related symptoms during lockdown measures. Findings suggest that families are employing coping strategies, but there no evidence-based supports were identified. The review highlighted the potential long-term impact of prolonged exposure to increasing demands on the mental health and wellbeing of caregivers and families of autistic people, and pointed to a need for the rapid development and evaluation of flexible and timely support programs. LAY SUMMARY: Caregivers and families of autistic children and youth have faced increased demands due to pandemic-related lockdown measures. We reviewed the literature to outline sources of stress, links to their influence on caregiver mental health, and if support programs have emerged to help them. Our findings suggest a number of demands have increased caregivers' risk to mental health challenges, and their potential impact on family wellbeing. Ongoing development of evidence-based supports of all families of autistic children and youth are needed.

sheet.es: Si la pandemia o cualquier cambio brusco de rutinas te ha dejado agotado, no es un fallo personal: muchas familias de niños y jóvenes autistas vivieron más estrés y más exigencias. Mañana puedes reservar un momento breve para ti, pedir ayuda concreta a alguien de confianza y hablar con tu centro de salud si notas ansiedad o tristeza persistentes. Tu bienestar también cuenta. Esta revisión exploratoria reunió 23 artículos publicados y 14 documentos de literatura gris (2019–2021) sobre cuidadores de todo el mundo. Sus límites: se hizo muy rápido, al inicio de la pandemia, con estudios variados, y no encontró apoyos con evidencia probada; cada familia vive su situación de forma distinta.
sheet.en: If the pandemic, or any sudden change in routines, has left you exhausted, it is not a personal failing: many families of autistic children and youth faced more stress and more demands. Tomorrow you could set aside a short moment for yourself, ask someone you trust for one concrete kind of help, and talk to your health centre if anxiety or low mood persists. Your wellbeing matters too. This scoping review gathered 23 published articles and 14 grey-literature pieces (2019–2021) about caregivers worldwide. Its limits: it was done quickly, early in the pandemic, with varied studies, and found no evidence-based supports yet; every family's experience is different.
sheet.sv: Om pandemin, eller andra plötsliga förändringar i rutinerna, har gjort dig utmattad är det inte ett personligt misslyckande: många familjer till autistiska barn och unga upplevde mer stress och fler krav. I morgon kan du avsätta en kort stund för dig själv, be någon du litar på om en konkret sorts hjälp och kontakta vårdcentralen om oro eller nedstämdhet håller i sig. Ditt välmående spelar också roll. Denna översikt (scoping review) samlade 23 publicerade artiklar och 14 texter ur grå litteratur (2019–2021) om omsorgsgivare i hela världen. Begränsningar: den gjordes snabbt, tidigt i pandemin, med varierande studier, och fann inga evidensbaserade stöd ännu; varje familjs upplevelse är olika.

title: The association between COVID-19, personal wellbeing, depression, and suicide risk factors in Australian autistic adults.
authors: Hedley D, Hayward SM, Denney K, Uljarević M, Uljarević M, Bury S, Sahin E, Brown CM, Clapperton A, Dissanayake C, Robinson J, Trollor J, Stokes MA
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has had a significant impact on the mental health and wellbeing of the world's population, with particularly negative effects on vulnerable populations, including autistic people. Although some consensus regarding specific impact on aspects of wellbeing and mental health in autism is starting to emerge, it is unclear whether the pandemic has increased suicide risk. The goals of this study were to examine (a) potential associations between COVID-19 impact and depression, personal wellbeing, and suicide risk factors in Australian autistic adults and (b) age and gender effects. The COVID-19 Impact Scale (CIS), Personal Wellbeing Index, Patient Health Questionnaire, and the Suicide Behavior Questionnaire, Revised (SBQ-R), were administered to 111 autistic adults aged 20 to 71 years during the second wave of the COVID-19 pandemic in Australia. COVID-19 impact showed small associations with poorer personal wellbeing (r = -0.224, p = 0.023, [-0.409, -0.016]) and higher depressive symptoms (r = 0.268, p = 0.006, [0.056, 0.445]) and was not associated with the SBQ-R suicide risk score (r = 0.081, p = 0.418, [-0.118, 0.264). No significant effects were identified for age. Although model results were similar for women and men, the strength of the associations between personal wellbeing and depression (z = -2.16, p = 0.015), and depression and SBQ-R suicide risk (z = 1.961, p = 0.025), were stronger in women than in men. Qualitative analysis of an open response question from the CIS suggested that the pandemic had both positive and negative impacts on participants. The COVID-19 pandemic has had a large impact on the mental health and wellbeing of the world's population, particularly vulnerable populations such as autistic people. It is not known if these impacts on mental health and wellbeing have increased suicide risk. Our findings suggest that the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic may be associated with poorer wellbeing and higher depression, but is not associated with suicide risk. Overall, autistic people reported both positive and negative impacts of the pandemic on their lives.

sheet.es: Cuando la rutina se rompe por una crisis grande, como una pandemia, vale la pena preguntar con calma a la persona autista adulta cómo se siente y qué le está costando más. Escuche también lo que mejoró: algunas personas vivieron cambios positivos, como menos exigencias sociales. Si nota tristeza persistente o pensamientos de muerte, busque apoyo profesional sin esperar. Evidencia: encuesta a 111 adultos autistas de 20 a 71 años en Australia; el impacto de la COVID-19 se asoció levemente con menor bienestar y más síntomas depresivos, pero no con el riesgo de suicidio. Límites: muestra pequeña, un solo momento y un solo país; no prueba causa ni vale igual para todos.
sheet.en: When a big disruption like a pandemic breaks routines, it helps to calmly ask the autistic adult in your life how they are feeling and what is hardest right now. Listen for what improved too: some people experienced positive changes, such as fewer social demands. If you notice lasting low mood or thoughts of death, seek professional support without waiting. Evidence: a survey of 111 autistic adults aged 20 to 71 in Australia found COVID-19 impact was slightly linked to lower wellbeing and more depressive symptoms, but not to suicide risk. Limits: small sample, one point in time and one country; it does not show cause and will not fit everyone.
sheet.sv: När en stor förändring, som en pandemi, rubbar rutinerna kan det hjälpa att lugnt fråga den autistiska vuxna hur hen mår och vad som känns svårast just nu. Lyssna också efter det som blev bättre: vissa upplevde positiva förändringar, till exempel färre sociala krav. Om du märker långvarig nedstämdhet eller tankar på döden, sök professionellt stöd utan att vänta. Evidens: en enkät med 111 autistiska vuxna, 20–71 år, i Australien visade att pandemins påverkan hade ett svagt samband med lägre välbefinnande och fler depressiva symtom, men inte med suicidrisk. Begränsningar: litet urval, ett enda mättillfälle och ett land; studien visar inte orsak och gäller inte alla.

title: Challenges Surrounding the Diagnosis of Autism in Children.
authors: Hus Y, Segal O
abstract: This comprehensive thematic review aims to highlight and familiarize readers with the challenges and pitfalls encountered in differential diagnosis of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) in children to facilitate the process of accurate identification by stakeholders. Accordingly, articles that best answer our questions and highlight our concerns were chosen from well-established publishers with prime peer reviewed journals. Included are studies showing alternate views of the issues so as to point readers to other possibilities. ASD, a complex dynamic biological-neurodevelopmental disorder, is underscored by its heterogeneous symptomology, severity, and phenotypes - all characterized by social communication deficits and presence of restricted interests and repetitive behaviours (RRBs), the core symptoms in ASD. Language and intellectual capacities do not form ASD core symptoms although vary considerably. Accurate identification is challenging as ASD is often enmeshed with other neurodevelopmental disorders, and medical comorbidities, a situation now recognized as the rule rather than the exception in child psychiatry and developmental medicine. ASD is a disorder with varying performance and severity of symptoms over time, including unexpected loss of early skills, and lost diagnosis in some children following treatment. The review reiterates the urgency in accurate diagnosis in face of the rapid rise in ASD prevalence globally, and risk-increase in delayed or denied treatment with undesirable life-long consequences for most of the affected children. In addition, a call for change is advised to circumvent the ethical dilemma posed by the present "deficit model" in ASD diagnosis. Here, ASD prevalence is presented first, followed by emphasis on importance of accurate early diagnosis, and challenges in its accomplishment due to flaws in diagnostic instruments and other contributing factors. Next follow the required criteria for accurate identification, and its difficulties attributed to comorbid conditions, gender differences, and socio-economic and cultural influences. The conclusion includes future directions and a take away message.

sheet.es: Si el proceso de evaluación de tu hijo o hija parece lento o confuso, no es culpa tuya: identificar el autismo en la infancia es realmente complejo. Puede ayudar anotar ejemplos concretos del día a día, mencionar otras condiciones de salud o del desarrollo, y preguntar cómo se tienen en cuenta el género, la cultura y el idioma. Pedir una segunda opinión es razonable. Esta es una revisión temática de estudios publicados que analiza las dificultades del diagnóstico y critica el enfoque basado en déficits. Sus límites: no es una revisión sistemática, los artículos se eligieron a criterio de los autores y no aporta datos nuevos ni pautas válidas para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your child's assessment feels slow or confusing, it is not your fault: recognising autism in childhood is genuinely complex. It can help to write down concrete everyday examples, mention any other health or developmental conditions, and ask how gender, culture and language are taken into account. Asking for a second opinion is reasonable. This is a thematic review of published studies that examines why diagnosis is difficult and questions the deficit-focused approach. Its limits: it is not a systematic review, the authors chose the articles themselves, and it offers no new data or guidance that fits every child.
sheet.sv: Om utredningen av ditt barn känns långsam eller förvirrande är det inte ditt fel: att känna igen autism hos barn är verkligen komplext. Det kan hjälpa att skriva ner konkreta exempel från vardagen, nämna andra hälso- eller utvecklingsrelaterade tillstånd och fråga hur kön, kultur och språk vägs in. Att be om en second opinion är rimligt. Detta är en tematisk översikt av publicerade studier som belyser varför diagnostik är svår och ifrågasätter det bristfokuserade synsättet. Begränsningar: det är ingen systematisk översikt, författarna valde själva artiklarna och den ger inga nya data eller råd som passar alla barn.

title: Childhood diagnoses in individuals identified as autistics in adulthood.
authors: Rødgaard EM, Jensen K, Miskowiak KW, Mottron L
abstract: Background Autism is a developmental condition, where symptoms are expected to occur in childhood, but a significant number of individuals are diagnosed with autism for the first time in adulthood. Here, we examine diagnoses given in childhood among individuals that are diagnosed with autism in adulthood, to investigate whether the late autism diagnosis might be explained by misdiagnosis in childhood or diagnostic overshadowing. Methods Through the Danish National Patient Registry, we identified individuals diagnosed with autism in adulthood (N = 2199), as well as a control sample with no records of an autism diagnosis (N = 460,798) and calculated how many had received different psychiatric or neurological diagnoses in childhood. Results We found that most childhood diagnoses were overrepresented in those with an adult autism diagnosis, and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, affective disorders, anxiety, and stress disorders were the most prevalent childhood conditions in this group. However, 69% of males and 61% of females with adult autism diagnoses were not found to have received any of the investigated diagnoses before 18 years of age, and most childhood diagnoses were given after the age of 12. Limitations Milder to moderate cases of psychiatric conditions that have been solely treated by family physicians or school psychologists may not be fully included in our dataset. The study is based on data from the Danish health care system, and further research is needed to assess whether the findings can be generalized to other countries. Conclusion A majority of those with an adult autism diagnosis had no records of having received any of the investigated diagnoses in childhood. In these cases, the late autism diagnosis is therefore unlikely to be explained by either misdiagnosis or overshadowing. This result is at odds with the prevailing notion that autistic symptoms tend to diminish with age. Therefore, further research is warranted to examine how and if early signs of autism may have manifested among these individuals, and how similar they are to autistic people diagnosed earlier in their development.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo, tu pareja o tú recibís un diagnóstico de autismo en la edad adulta, no significa que alguien "se equivocara" antes: muchas personas autistas pasan la infancia sin ningún diagnóstico. Si hubo diagnósticos previos como TDAH, ansiedad o estrés, conviene revisarlos con calma junto al nuevo, porque pueden coexistir. Este estudio de registros daneses comparó a 2.199 personas diagnosticadas de autismo en la adultez con más de 460.000 sin ese diagnóstico; entre el 61 % y el 69 % no tenía ningún diagnóstico psiquiátrico antes de los 18 años. Límite: solo incluye datos hospitalarios de Dinamarca, así que puede no reflejar la atención primaria o escolar ni otros países.
sheet.en: If your child, partner or you receive an autism diagnosis in adulthood, it does not mean someone "got it wrong" earlier: many autistic people go through childhood with no diagnosis at all. If there were earlier diagnoses such as ADHD, anxiety or stress, it can help to look at them calmly alongside the new one, since they can coexist. This Danish registry study compared 2,199 people diagnosed autistic as adults with over 460,000 people without that diagnosis; 61–69% had no psychiatric diagnosis before age 18. Limit: it uses only Danish hospital-level records, so it may miss care from family doctors or school psychologists and may not apply to other countries.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn, din partner eller du får en autismdiagnos i vuxen ålder betyder det inte att någon "gjorde fel" tidigare: många autistiska personer går igenom barndomen helt utan diagnos. Om det funnits tidigare diagnoser som adhd, ångest eller stress kan det hjälpa att lugnt se på dem tillsammans med den nya, eftersom de kan finnas samtidigt. Den här danska registerstudien jämförde 2 199 personer som fick autismdiagnos som vuxna med över 460 000 utan den diagnosen; 61–69 % hade ingen psykiatrisk diagnos före 18 års ålder. Begränsning: den bygger bara på danska specialistvårdsregister, så vård hos husläkare eller skolpsykolog kan saknas, och resultaten gäller kanske inte andra länder.

title: Self-reported parkinsonism features in older autistic adults: A descriptive study.
authors: Geurts HM, McQuaid GA, Begeer S, Wallace GL
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults without a suspected intellectual disability reported several motor features such as having tremors, and stiffness in one's legs which are considered to be part of a complex of motor features called parkinsonism. This so-called parkinsonism was remarkably prevalent in middle-aged and older autistic adults in two independent studies (Dutch study: 50-81 years, 183 males, 113 females, all adulthood diagnoses; the USA study: 50-83 years, 110 females, 109 males, majority adulthood diagnosis). Parkinsonism can be part of the progressive motor disease-Parkinson's disease. Therefore, it is important that future studies, including in-person neurological assessment, determine if (and if so, why) autistic adults who report these motor features are at increased risk for developing Parkinson's disease.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista mayor de 50 años, presta atención a cambios en el movimiento, como temblores, rigidez en las piernas o lentitud, y anótalos con calma. Llevar ese registro a una consulta médica puede ayudar a que se valore con cuidado, sin alarmarse. Dos estudios descriptivos independientes, en Países Bajos (296 personas) y en EE. UU. (219 personas) de 50 a 83 años, la mayoría diagnosticadas en la adultez y sin discapacidad intelectual sospechada, encontraron que estos rasgos autoinformados eran frecuentes. Sus límites: se basan en cuestionarios, sin exploración neurológica presencial, por lo que no muestran si existe mayor riesgo de párkinson ni sirven como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person over 50, notice changes in movement, such as tremors, stiffness in the legs or slowness, and calmly write them down. Bringing these notes to a health appointment can help them be checked carefully, without alarm. Two independent descriptive studies, in the Netherlands (296 people) and the USA (219 people) aged 50 to 83, mostly diagnosed in adulthood and without suspected intellectual disability, found these self-reported features were common. Limits: the findings come from questionnaires, not in-person neurological exams, so they do not show whether Parkinson's risk is higher and are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person över 50 år, lägg märke till förändringar i rörelser, som skakningar, stelhet i benen eller långsamhet, och skriv lugnt ner dem. Att ta med anteckningarna till ett vårdbesök kan hjälpa till att få dem bedömda noggrant, utan oro. Två oberoende beskrivande studier, i Nederländerna (296 personer) och USA (219 personer) i åldern 50–83 år, de flesta diagnostiserade i vuxen ålder och utan misstänkt intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, fann att dessa självrapporterade drag var vanliga. Begränsningar: resultaten bygger på enkäter, inte neurologisk undersökning på plats, så de visar inte om risken för Parkinsons sjukdom är högre och gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: Participatory autism research: Early career and established researchers' views and experiences.
authors: Pickard H, Pellicano E, den Houting J, Crane L
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract 'Participatory autism research' refers to ways of involving autistic people and their allies (e.g. family members) in making decisions about research. These decisions can include what research gets done, how it gets done and how research findings are used. While there is more and more interest in participatory autism research, we know little about how researchers at different stages of their careers use this approach. To find out more, we discussed these issues with 25 researchers. Fourteen of these were at an early stage of their careers, and 11 were more senior researchers. We spoke to people in individual interviews or in groups. We then used a technique called thematic analysis to analyse our data, which involved us looking for common topics or 'themes' discussed by our participants. What did we find? Our participants told us that participatory autism research was a flexible approach, meaning that autistic people can be involved in research in many different ways. While people viewed this flexibility in a positive way, it also caused some confusion about what does or does not 'count' as participatory research. Our participants also spoke about how important it was to build relationships with those involved in their research, but they also said it could be difficult to communicate well with diverse groups of people who may not have much experience of research. Finally, our participants said it was hard to do participatory research when there was not much time, funding or support available to researchers. In this article, we discuss these findings, focusing on what needs to change to ensure that autistic people and their allies are meaningfully involved in autism research.

sheet.es: Si te invitan a participar en un estudio sobre autismo, puedes preguntar cómo se tendrá en cuenta tu voz: si las personas autistas y sus familias ayudan a decidir qué se investiga, cómo se hace y cómo se usan los resultados. Tu experiencia es valiosa y puedes pedir una comunicación clara y accesible. Este estudio entrevistó, individualmente o en grupos, a 25 investigadores (14 al inicio de su carrera y 11 con más experiencia) sobre la investigación participativa. Sus límites: recoge solo la visión de investigadores, no la de personas autistas ni familias, y es un grupo pequeño.
sheet.en: If you are invited to take part in autism research, you can ask how your voice will count: whether autistic people and families help decide what is studied, how it is done and how findings are used. Your experience matters, and you can ask for clear, accessible communication. This qualitative study interviewed 25 researchers (14 early career, 11 established), individually or in groups, about participatory autism research.
