They described it as flexible but sometimes unclear, and limited by time and funding. Its limits: it reflects only researchers' views, not those of autistic people or families, and the group was small.
sheet.sv: Om du blir inbjuden att delta i autismforskning kan du fråga hur din röst kommer att räknas: om autistiska personer och familjer får vara med och bestämma vad som undersöks, hur det görs och hur resultaten används. Din erfarenhet är värdefull, och du kan be om tydlig och tillgänglig kommunikation. Denna kvalitativa studie intervjuade 25 forskare (14 i början av karriären, 11 erfarna), enskilt eller i grupp, om delaktighetsbaserad autismforskning. De beskrev den som flexibel men ibland otydlig, och begränsad av tid och pengar. Begränsningar: den speglar bara forskares syn, inte autistiska personers eller familjers, och gruppen var liten.

title: Face memory and face perception in autism.
authors: Stantić M, Ichijo E, Catmur C, Bird G
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract It is well known that some people with autism have difficulties recognizing faces. It is generally thought that this is not because autistic individuals cannot perceive faces, but because autistic individuals have greater problems than people without autism in remembering faces. Here, we worked with a group of autistic adults and a group of non-autistic adults to test their ability to perceive and remember faces. We also asked each person to report any difficulties that they have with recognizing faces in everyday life. We find that, as a group, people with autism have difficulties with both remembering and perceiving faces, and report more problems recognizing faces in everyday life. However, it is worth noting that we observed a wide range of scores in the group of people with autism, with some autistic participants scoring as well as the group of people without autism.

sheet.es: Si a una persona autista le cuesta reconocer caras, no es descuido ni desinterés: puede deberse tanto a cómo percibe los rostros como a cómo los recuerda. Mañana puedes presentarte por tu nombre al saludar, avisar quién va a venir y animar a usar pistas como la voz, la ropa o el contexto. Pregúntale cómo le va con las caras en su día a día. Evidencia: estudio que comparó a adultos autistas y no autistas en tareas de percepción y memoria de caras, junto con su experiencia cotidiana. Límites: solo participaron adultos y hubo mucha variación; algunas personas autistas puntuaron igual que el grupo no autista, así que no aplica a todos.
sheet.en: If an autistic person finds it hard to recognise faces, it is not carelessness or lack of interest: it may relate both to how faces are perceived and how they are remembered. Tomorrow, you could say your name when greeting, mention who is coming, and encourage using cues like voice, clothing or context. Ask how faces work for them in daily life. Evidence: a study comparing autistic and non-autistic adults on face perception and face memory tasks, plus their everyday experiences. Limits: only adults took part and scores varied widely; some autistic participants scored as well as the non-autistic group, so this does not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att känna igen ansikten handlar det inte om slarv eller ointresse: det kan hänga ihop både med hur ansikten uppfattas och hur de minns. I morgon kan du säga ditt namn när du hälsar, berätta vem som kommer och uppmuntra ledtrådar som röst, kläder eller sammanhang. Fråga hur ansikten fungerar för personen i vardagen. Evidens: en studie som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna i uppgifter om ansiktsuppfattning och ansiktsminne, samt deras vardagserfarenheter. Begränsningar: bara vuxna deltog och resultaten varierade mycket; vissa autistiska deltagare presterade lika bra som den icke-autistiska gruppen, så det gäller inte alla.

title: Objective and subjective psychosocial outcomes in adults with autism spectrum disorder: A 6-year longitudinal study.
authors: Scheeren AM, Buil JM, Howlin P, Bartels M, Begeer S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Previous research has shown that relatively few adults with autism have a paid job or live on their own. However, outcomes also vary a lot and may depend on many different factors. In this study, we examined the level of functioning and happiness of 917 adults with autism (425 men and 492 women) aged 18-65 years. Most of them were of average to high intellectual ability. Over 6 years, we measured whether they had a paid job, close friendships and lived on their own (i.e. their objective functioning). We also measured how happy they felt. Objectively, most autistic adults did fairly to very well. Those with better objective outcomes (e.g. those with paid work) also tended to be happier. Most adults improved in objective functioning and happiness over 6 years. Participants with a lower intellectual ability, more autism traits, mental health problems and younger age had poorer objective outcomes. Participants with more autism traits and mental health problems were less happy. Autistic men and women functioned at similar levels and were equally happy. We found important factors that predict a better (or worse) outcome for autistic adults. Overall, compared with some previous research, our findings give a more positive picture of the outcomes for autistic adults with average to high intellectual abilities.

sheet.es: Para muchas personas autistas adultas, la vida tiende a mejorar con los años: en este estudio, la mayoría avanzó en trabajo, amistades, vida independiente y felicidad en seis años. Cuidar la salud mental parece especialmente importante, porque se relacionó tanto con la felicidad como con la vida diaria; buscar apoyo temprano para la ansiedad o el ánimo puede marcar diferencia. Se trata de un estudio longitudinal con 917 adultos autistas de 18 a 65 años, hombres y mujeres, seguidos durante seis años. Límites: la mayoría tenía capacidad intelectual media o alta, así que los resultados no describen a todas las personas autistas, y mostrar asociaciones no prueba causas.
sheet.en: For many autistic adults, life tends to get better over time: in this study, most improved in work, friendships, independent living and happiness over six years. Looking after mental health seems especially important, as it was linked to both happiness and daily life; seeking support early for anxiety or low mood may make a real difference. This was a longitudinal study of 917 autistic adults aged 18 to 65, men and women, followed for six years. Limits: most participants had average to high intellectual ability, so the findings do not describe every autistic person, and associations do not prove causes.
sheet.sv: För många autistiska vuxna tenderar livet att bli bättre med tiden: i den här studien förbättrades de flesta när det gällde arbete, vänskap, eget boende och lycka under sex år. Att ta hand om den psykiska hälsan verkar särskilt viktigt, eftersom den hängde ihop med både lycka och vardagsliv; att tidigt söka stöd vid ångest eller nedstämdhet kan göra verklig skillnad. Det var en longitudinell studie med 917 autistiska vuxna, 18–65 år, män och kvinnor, som följdes i sex år. Begränsningar: de flesta hade genomsnittlig till hög intellektuell förmåga, så resultaten beskriver inte alla autistiska personer, och samband bevisar inte orsaker.

title: The Association between Parenting Stress, Positive Reappraisal Coping, and Quality of Life in Parents with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Children: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ni'matuzahroh, Suen MW, Ningrum V, Widayat, Yuniardi MS, Hasanati N, Wang JH
abstract: Parents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) children generally suffer from poor coping and an impaired quality of life (QoL). This systematic review investigates parenting stress, positive reappraisal coping, and QoL in parents with ASD children. A literature search was carried out for publications written in English on the selected investigation topics using five databases, namely, Scopus, PubMed, Wiley, ScienceDirect Online, and EBSCO. Only studies investigating or measuring parenting stress, positive reappraisal coping, and QoL in ASD were included. Our results indicate that parents with ASD children have high stress levels. This is associated with the ineffective use of coping strategies and a low QoL. Adaptive coping strategies are related to a higher QoL, whereas maladaptive coping techniques are related to a worse QoL. Positive reappraisal coping is negatively correlated to meaningfulness, and it is used by parents to change their daily routines in order to motivate themselves towards new and evolving goals in life. Finally, we found a significant negative correlation between parenting stress, positive reappraisal coping, and the QoL of parents with ASD children. Positive reappraisal coping as a strategy helps parents adapt to stress and was found to be a potential mediatory function between parental stress and QoL.

sheet.es: Su bienestar también importa. Cuando el día se complica, puede ayudar detenerse y buscar otra forma de ver la situación: qué salió bien, qué aprendió, qué pequeña meta nueva es posible. Esto no significa negar el cansancio, y pedir apoyo práctico sigue siendo válido. En esta revisión, este tipo de afrontamiento, llamado reevaluación positiva, se relacionó con menos estrés y mejor calidad de vida. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de estudios publicados en inglés con madres y padres de niños autistas. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no incluye la perspectiva de las personas autistas. Además, lo que ayuda a una familia puede no servir a otra.
sheet.en: Your wellbeing matters too. When a day gets hard, it can help to pause and look for another way to see the situation: what went well, what you learned, what small new goal is possible. This does not mean ignoring exhaustion, and asking for practical support is still valid. In this review, this kind of coping, called positive reappraisal, was linked to lower stress and better quality of life. It is a systematic review of English-language studies with parents of autistic children. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, and it does not include autistic people's own perspectives. What helps one family may not help another.
sheet.sv: Ditt eget välmående spelar också roll. När en dag blir tung kan det hjälpa att stanna upp och se situationen på ett annat sätt: vad gick bra, vad lärde du dig, vilket litet nytt mål är möjligt? Det betyder inte att du ska förneka tröttheten, och att be om praktiskt stöd är fortfarande rimligt. I översikten var den här typen av hantering, kallad positiv omvärdering, kopplad till mindre stress och bättre livskvalitet. Det är en systematisk översikt av engelskspråkiga studier med föräldrar till autistiska barn. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, och saknar autistiska personers egna perspektiv. Det som hjälper en familj passar inte alltid en annan.

title: Beyond Friendship: The Spectrum of Social Participation of Autistic Adults.
authors: Chan DV, Doran JD, Galobardi OD
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: Catatonia in autism spectrum disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Vaquerizo-Serrano J, Salazar De Pablo G, Singh J, Santosh P
journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
abstract: Background Catatonic features can appear in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs). There can be overlap in symptoms across catatonia and ASD. The overall aim of this review is to provide evidence for the presence of catatonic features in subjects with ASD. Methods A systematic literature search using the Web of Science database from inception to July 10, 2021 was conducted following PRISMA, MOOSE guidelines and the PROSPERO protocol. (CRD42021248615). Twelve studies with information about catatonia and ASD were reviewed. Data from a subset was used to conduct meta-analyses of the presence of catatonia in ASD. Results The systematic review included 12 studies, seven of which were used for the meta-analysis, comprising 969 individuals. The mean age was 21.25 (7.5) years. Two studies (16.6%) included only children and adolescents. A total of 70-100% were males. Our meta-analysis showed that 10.4% (5.8-18.0 95%CI) of individuals with ASD have catatonia. Motor disturbances were common in ASD subjects with catatonia. No differences were found in comorbidity. Several treatments have been used in ASD with catatonic features, including benzodiazepines, antipsychotics, and electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). The findings of the systematic review showed that ECT might help manage catatonic symptoms. Conclusions Different features of catatonia can exist in individuals with ASD and core symptoms of catatonia are reported in ASD. Longitudinal and longer-term studies are required to understand the relationship between catatonia and ASD, and the response of catatonic symptoms to treatment.

sheet.es: Si notas cambios nuevos en el movimiento de una persona autista —se queda inmóvil, tarda mucho en empezar acciones, adopta posturas fijas, habla mucho menos o deja de comer—, anota qué pasa y desde cuándo, y consúltalo pronto con un profesional sanitario. Estos cambios pueden indicar catatonia, que según este estudio aparece en alrededor de 1 de cada 10 personas autistas y tiene tratamiento. Es un metaanálisis de 12 estudios (7 combinados, 969 personas, edad media 21 años, mayoría hombres). Sus límites: pocos estudios, poca representación de niñas y mujeres, y faltan estudios a largo plazo sobre causas y tratamientos.
sheet.en: If you notice new changes in how an autistic person moves — freezing, great difficulty starting actions, holding fixed postures, speaking much less or stopping eating — write down what happens and since when, and raise it soon with a healthcare professional. Such changes can signal catatonia, which this study found in about 1 in 10 autistic people, and which can be treated. This is a meta-analysis of 12 studies (7 pooled, 969 people, average age 21, mostly male). Its limits: few studies, few girls and women included, and no long-term research yet on causes or how treatments work over time.
sheet.sv: Om du märker nya förändringar i hur en autistisk person rör sig – stelnar, har mycket svårt att komma igång, stannar i fasta positioner, pratar mycket mindre eller slutar äta – skriv ner vad som händer och sedan när, och ta upp det snart med vården. Sådana förändringar kan tyda på katatoni, som enligt studien förekommer hos ungefär 1 av 10 autistiska personer och som går att behandla. Det är en metaanalys av 12 studier (7 sammanslagna, 969 personer, medelålder 21 år, mest män). Begränsningar: få studier, få flickor och kvinnor, och långtidsstudier om orsaker och behandling saknas.

title: Autistic Adults May Be Erroneously Perceived as Deceptive and Lacking Credibility.
authors: Lim A, Young RL, Brewer N
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: We hypothesized that autistic adults may be erroneously judged as deceptive or lacking credibility due to demonstrating unexpected and atypical behaviors. Thirty autistic and 29 neurotypical individuals participated in video-recorded interviews, and we measured their demonstration of gaze aversion, repetitive body movements, literal interpretation of figurative language, poor reciprocity, and flat affect. Participants (N = 1410) viewed one of these videos and rated their perception of the individual's truthfulness or credibility. The hypothesis was partially supported, with autistic individuals perceived as more deceptive and less credible than neurotypical individuals when telling the truth. However, this relationship was not influenced by the presence of any of the target behaviors, but instead, by the individual's overall presentation.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista a una entrevista, una cita médica, una reunión escolar o un trámite legal, puede ayudar avisar con antelación de que su forma de comunicarse puede ser malinterpretada, y pedir que se valore lo que dice, no cómo lo dice. Preparar notas escritas o llevar a alguien de confianza también puede apoyar su voz. En este estudio, 30 adultos autistas y 29 no autistas fueron grabados en entrevistas, y 1410 personas valoraron su credibilidad: los autistas que decían la verdad fueron vistos como menos creíbles, por su presentación general y no por conductas concretas como evitar la mirada. Es un estudio con vídeos y pocos participantes grabados, así que no refleja todas las situaciones reales.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person at a job interview, medical visit, school meeting or legal process, it may help to explain in advance that their communication style can be misread, and to ask others to focus on what is said rather than how. Written notes or a trusted companion can also support their voice. In this study, 30 autistic and 29 non-autistic adults were video-recorded in interviews, and 1,410 viewers rated their credibility: autistic people telling the truth were seen as less credible, linked to their overall presentation rather than specific behaviours like avoiding eye contact. It used videos and a small number of recorded people, so it may not reflect every real-life situation.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person vid en anställningsintervju, ett läkarbesök, ett skolmöte eller en rättslig process kan det hjälpa att i förväg förklara att personens sätt att kommunicera kan misstolkas, och be andra fokusera på vad som sägs snarare än hur. Skriftliga anteckningar eller en betrodd person med kan också stärka personens röst. I studien filmades 30 autistiska och 29 icke-autistiska vuxna under intervjuer, och 1 410 personer bedömde deras trovärdighet: autistiska personer som talade sanning uppfattades som mindre trovärdiga, kopplat till helhetsintrycket snarare än enskilda beteenden som att undvika ögonkontakt. Studien byggde på filmer och få filmade deltagare, så den speglar inte alla verkliga situationer.

title: Understanding Camouflaging as a Response to Autism-Related Stigma: A Social Identity Theory Approach.
authors: Perry E, Mandy W, Hull L, Cage E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Camouflaging refers to strategies used by autistic people to mask or hide social difficulties. The current study draws on Social Identity Theory to examine the relationship between camouflaging and autism-related stigma, testing the hypothesis that camouflaging represents an individualistic strategy in response to stigma. Two hundred and twenty-three autistic adults completed an online survey measuring perceived autism-related stigma, individualistic and collective strategies, camouflaging and mental wellbeing. Results indicated that higher camouflaging was positively associated with autism-related stigma and both individualistic and collective strategy use. Autism-related stigma was associated with lower wellbeing however this relationship was not mediated by camouflaging. These findings demonstrate how stigma contributes to camouflaging and highlight the complexities of navigating autistic identity while still camouflaging.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo se esfuerza por «parecer» no autista, puede ser una respuesta al estigma que percibe, no una elección libre. Mañana puedes ofrecer espacios donde no tenga que disimular, hablar con naturalidad sobre la identidad autista y cuestionar comentarios estigmatizantes a su alrededor. Reducir el estigma en el entorno importa, porque se asoció con menor bienestar. Evidencia: encuesta en línea a 223 adultos autistas que midió estigma percibido, camuflaje, estrategias de afrontamiento y bienestar. Límites: es un estudio transversal y autoinformado, así que muestra asociaciones, no causas, y puede no reflejar a niños ni a quienes no respondieron encuestas en línea.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support works hard to 'pass' as non-autistic, this may be a response to stigma they sense, not a free preference. Tomorrow you can offer spaces where they don't need to mask, speak openly and positively about autistic identity, and challenge stigmatising remarks around them. Reducing stigma in the environment matters, since stigma was linked to lower wellbeing. Evidence: an online survey of 223 autistic adults measuring perceived stigma, camouflaging, coping strategies and wellbeing. Limits: it is cross-sectional and self-reported, so it shows associations rather than causes, and may not reflect children or people who don't take part in online surveys.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar anstränger sig för att verka icke-autistisk kan det vara ett svar på stigma hen upplever, inte ett fritt val. I morgon kan du erbjuda miljöer där hen inte behöver maskera, prata öppet och positivt om autistisk identitet och ifrågasätta stigmatiserande kommentarer omkring hen. Att minska stigma i omgivningen spelar roll, eftersom stigma hängde ihop med sämre välbefinnande. Evidens: en webbenkät med 223 autistiska vuxna som mätte upplevt stigma, kamouflering, strategier och välbefinnande. Begränsningar: studien är en tvärsnittsstudie med självskattning, så den visar samband snarare än orsaker och speglar kanske inte barn eller personer som inte svarar på webbenkäter.

title: Self-reported camouflaging behaviours used by autistic adults during everyday social interactions.
authors: Cook J, Crane L, Hull L, Bourne L, Mandy W
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Camouflaging can be thought of as the process through which autistic people modify their natural social behaviours to adapt to, cope within or influence the largely neurotypical (non-autistic) social world. Many autistic people experience negative reactions to their natural or intuitive social behaviours when interacting with non-autistic people. Over time, in response to these negative reactions, autistic people's social behaviour often changes. We refer to autistic people's changed behaviours as 'camouflaging behaviours'. Research exploring camouflaging behaviours is still at an early stage. This study investigated camouflaging behaviours used by autistic adults in everyday social interactions using a research method that was new to the field of autism. Specifically, 17 autistic adults were filmed taking part in a common everyday social situation - a conversation with a stranger. With the help of the video of this conversation, they then showed and described their camouflaging behaviours to a researcher. These autistic people identified and described a total of 38 different camouflaging behaviours. The detailed and specific information provided by autistic adults about camouflaging behaviours generated important new insights into the ways in which autistic people adapt to, cope within and influence the neurotypical (non-autistic) social world.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: muchas personas autistas ajustan su forma natural de interactuar (mirada, gestos, temas, tono) para encajar en entornos no autistas, a menudo por reacciones negativas previas. Puedes ofrecer espacios donde no haga falta camuflar: aceptar el contacto visual reducido, los movimientos propios o las pausas, y preguntar con curiosidad qué esfuerzos hace la persona en conversaciones. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo en el que 17 adultos autistas fueron grabados conversando con un desconocido y luego describieron, viendo el vídeo, 38 conductas de camuflaje distintas. Límites: muestra pequeña, una sola situación social y solo adultos que pueden describir su experiencia verbalmente; no se aplica igual a todas las personas.
sheet.en: The practical point: many autistic people adjust their natural ways of interacting (eye gaze, gestures, topics, tone) to fit non-autistic settings, often after negative reactions in the past. You can offer spaces where camouflaging isn't needed: accept less eye contact, personal movements or pauses, and ask with curiosity what effort conversations take for the person. Evidence: a qualitative study where 17 autistic adults were filmed talking with a stranger, then used the video to describe 38 different camouflaging behaviours. Limits: a small sample, one social situation, and only adults able to describe their experience in words; it won't apply the same way to everyone.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: många autistiska personer justerar sitt naturliga sätt att umgås (blick, gester, samtalsämnen, tonläge) för att passa in i icke-autistiska miljöer, ofta efter negativa reaktioner tidigare. Du kan erbjuda sammanhang där kamouflering inte behövs: acceptera mindre ögonkontakt, egna rörelser eller pauser, och fråga nyfiket vilka ansträngningar samtal kräver för personen. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie där 17 autistiska vuxna filmades i samtal med en främling och sedan, med hjälp av videon, beskrev 38 olika kamoufleringsbeteenden. Begränsningar: litet urval, en enda social situation och bara vuxna som kan beskriva sin upplevelse i ord; det gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

title: The Human Gut Microbiome as a Potential Factor in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Alharthi A, Alhazmi S, Alburae N, Bahieldin A
abstract: The high prevalence of gastrointestinal (GI) disorders among autism spectrum disorder (ASD) patients has prompted scientists to look into the gut microbiota as a putative trigger in ASD pathogenesis. Thus, many studies have linked the gut microbial dysbiosis that is frequently observed in ASD patients with the modulation of brain function and social behavior, but little is known about this connection and its contribution to the etiology of ASD. This present review highlights the potential role of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in autism. In particular, it focuses on how gut microbiota dysbiosis may impact gut permeability, immune function, and the microbial metabolites in autistic people. We further discuss recent findings supporting the possible role of the gut microbiome in initiating epigenetic modifications and consider the potential role of this pathway in influencing the severity of ASD. Lastly, we summarize recent updates in microbiota-targeted therapies such as probiotics, prebiotics, dietary supplements, fecal microbiota transplantation, and microbiota transfer therapy. The findings of this paper reveal new insights into possible therapeutic interventions that may be used to reduce and cure ASD-related symptoms. However, well-designed research studies using large sample sizes are still required in this area of study.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene molestias digestivas frecuentes (estreñimiento, diarrea, dolor de barriga), vale la pena tomarlas en serio y comentarlas con su médico: el malestar intestinal puede afectar al sueño, al ánimo y a la regulación. Lleva un registro sencillo de comidas, deposiciones y momentos difíciles. No hace falta cambiar la dieta ni probar probióticos o trasplantes fecales por tu cuenta. Esta revisión resume estudios sobre la relación entre microbiota intestinal, cerebro y autismo en personas autistas. Sus límites: reúne investigaciones pequeñas y variadas, no demuestra causa, y el autismo no es algo que deba 'curarse'.
sheet.en: If your autistic child often has gut discomfort (constipation, diarrhoea, tummy pain), take it seriously and raise it with their doctor: digestive pain can affect sleep, mood and regulation. Keep a simple log of meals, bowel movements and hard moments. There is no need to change their diet or try probiotics or faecal transplants on your own. This review summarises studies on links between gut microbes, the brain and autism in autistic people. Its limits: it pools small, varied studies, cannot show cause and effect, and autism itself is not something that needs a 'cure'.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn ofta har besvär med magen (förstoppning, diarré, magont) är det värt att ta det på allvar och ta upp det med läkaren: magsmärtor kan påverka sömn, humör och reglering. För en enkel logg över måltider, toalettbesök och svåra stunder. Du behöver inte ändra kosten eller prova probiotika eller faeces­transplantation på egen hand. Denna översikt sammanfattar studier om kopplingen mellan tarmbakterier, hjärnan och autism hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den bygger på små och olikartade studier, kan inte visa orsakssamband, och autism i sig är inget som behöver 'botas'.

title: Autism and chronic ill health: an observational study of symptoms and diagnoses of central sensitivity syndromes in autistic adults.
authors: Grant S, Norton S, Weiland RF, Scheeren AM, Begeer S, Hoekstra RA
abstract: Background Autistic adults, particularly women, are more likely to experience chronic ill health than the general population. Central sensitivity syndromes (CSS) are a group of related conditions that are thought to include an underlying sensitisation of the central nervous system; heightened sensory sensitivity is a common feature. Anecdotal evidence suggests autistic adults may be more prone to developing a CSS. This study aimed to investigate the occurrence of CSS diagnoses and symptoms in autistic adults, and to explore whether CSS symptoms were related to autistic traits, mental health, sensory sensitivity, or gender. Methods The full sample of participants included 973 autistic adults (410 men, 563 women, mean age = 44.6) registered at the Netherlands Autism Register, who completed questionnaires assessing autistic traits, sensory sensitivity, CSS, physical and mental health symptoms. The reliability and validity of the Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) in an autistic sample was established using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. Chi 2 analyses, independent t-tests, hierarchical regression and path analysis were used to analyse relationships between CSS symptoms, autistic traits, measures of mental health and wellbeing, sensory sensitivity, age and gender. Results 21% of participants reported one or more CSS diagnosis, and 60% scored at or above the clinical cut-off for a CSS. Autistic women were more likely to report a CSS diagnosis and experienced more CSS symptoms than men. Sensory sensitivity, anxiety, age and gender were significant predictors of CSS symptoms, with sensory sensitivity and anxiety fully mediating the relationship between autistic traits and CSS symptoms. Limitations Although this study included a large sample of autistic adults, we did not have a control group or a CSS only group. We also could not include a non-binary group due to lack of statistical power. Conclusions CSS diagnoses and symptoms appear to be very common in the autistic population. Increased awareness of an association between autism and central sensitisation should inform clinicians and guide diagnostic practice, particularly for women where CSS are common and autism under recognised.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta habla de dolor persistente, cansancio o molestias físicas que van y vienen, tómelo en serio y anótelo junto con su nivel de sensibilidad sensorial y ansiedad. Puede ayudar llevar ese registro a la consulta médica y mencionar que los síndromes de sensibilización central (como la fibromialgia) parecen frecuentes en personas autistas, sobre todo en mujeres. Reducir la carga sensorial y la ansiedad en el día a día puede ser un punto de partida. Evidencia: estudio con cuestionarios a 973 adultos autistas del Registro de Autismo de Países Bajos; el 21 % tenía un diagnóstico de este tipo. Límites: sin grupo de comparación no autista y sin datos de personas no binarias.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult mentions ongoing pain, fatigue or physical symptoms that come and go, take it seriously and note it alongside how sensory overload and anxiety are going. Bringing that record to a medical appointment, and mentioning that central sensitivity syndromes (such as fibromyalgia) seem common in autistic people, especially women, may help. Easing everyday sensory load and anxiety can be a reasonable starting point. Evidence: a questionnaire study of 973 autistic adults from the Netherlands Autism Register; 21% reported such a diagnosis. Limits: there was no non-autistic comparison group, and non-binary people could not be analysed separately.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen berättar om ihållande smärta, trötthet eller kroppsliga besvär som kommer och går, ta det på allvar och anteckna det tillsammans med hur sensorisk överbelastning och oro ser ut. Det kan hjälpa att ta med anteckningarna till vården och nämna att centrala sensitiseringssyndrom (som fibromyalgi) verkar vanliga hos autistiska personer, särskilt kvinnor. Att minska sensorisk belastning och oro i vardagen kan vara en rimlig början. Evidens: enkätstudie med 973 autistiska vuxna från Nederländernas autismregister; 21 % hade en sådan diagnos. Begränsningar: ingen icke-autistisk jämförelsegrupp, och icke-binära personer kunde inte analyseras separat.

title: Mortality in Persons With Autism Spectrum Disorder or Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Catalá-López F, Hutton B, Page MJ, Driver JA, Ridao M, Alonso-Arroyo A, Valencia A, Macías Saint-Gerons D, Tabarés-Seisdedos R
abstract: Importance Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are childhood-onset disorders that may persist into adulthood. Several studies have suggested that they may be associated with an increased risk of mortality; however, the results are inconsistent. Objective To assess the risk of mortality among persons with ASD or ADHD and their first-degree relatives. Data sources A search of MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and PsycINFO (published from inception to April 1, 2021) was supplemented by searching reference lists of the retrieved articles. Study selection Cohort and case-control studies that reported mortality rate ratios (RRs) in persons with ASD or ADHD and/or their first-degree relatives compared with the general population or those without ASD/ADHD were included. Data extraction and synthesis Screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed by at least 2 researchers independently. A random-effects model was used to meta-analyze individual studies and assessed heterogeneity (I2). Main outcomes and measures All-cause mortality in association with ASD or ADHD. Secondary outcome was cause-specific mortality. Results Twenty-seven studies were included, with a total of 642 260 individuals. All-cause mortality was found to be higher for persons with ASD (154 238 participants; 12 studies; RR, 2.37; 95% CI, 1.97-2.85; I2, 89%; moderate confidence) and persons with ADHD (396 488 participants; 8 studies; RR, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.13-4.02; I2, 98%; low confidence) than for the general population. Among persons with ASD, deaths from natural causes (4 studies; RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 2.06-7.01; I2, 96%; low confidence) and deaths from unnatural causes were increased (6 studies; RR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.49-4.18; I2, 95%; low confidence). Among persons with ADHD, deaths from natural causes were not significantly increased (4 studies; RR, 1.62; 95% CI, 0.89-2.96; I2, 88%; low confidence), but deaths from unnatural causes were higher than expected (10 studies; RR, 2.81; 95% CI, 1.73-4.55; I2, 92%; low confidence). Conclusions and relevance This systematic review and meta-analysis found that ASD and ADHD are associated with a significantly increased risk of mortality. Understanding the mechanisms of these associations may lead to targeted strategies to prevent avoidable deaths in high-risk groups. The substantial heterogeneity between studies should be explored further.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: cuidar la salud física y la seguridad es parte del apoyo diario. Mañana puedes revisar si hay controles médicos pendientes, anotar señales de dolor o malestar que quizá no se expresen con palabras, y repasar riesgos cotidianos como el agua, el tráfico o las salidas sin aviso. Si notas tristeza profunda o crisis, busca ayuda profesional pronto. La evidencia: es un metaanálisis de 27 estudios con más de 640 000 personas, que encontró mayor mortalidad en personas autistas y con TDAH frente a la población general. Límites: los estudios eran muy diferentes entre sí, la confianza es moderada o baja, y no explica causas ni predice nada sobre una persona concreta.
sheet.en: The practical point: looking after physical health and safety is part of everyday support. Tomorrow you might check for overdue medical appointments, note signs of pain or discomfort that may not be expressed in words, and review everyday risks such as water, traffic or leaving without notice. If you notice deep sadness or crisis, seek professional help early. The evidence: this meta-analysis of 27 studies with over 640,000 people found higher mortality among autistic people and people with ADHD compared with the general population. Limits: the studies varied widely, confidence is moderate to low, and it does not explain causes or predict anything about any individual person.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: att ta hand om fysisk hälsa och säkerhet är en del av vardagsstödet. I morgon kan du se över om några läkarbesök har blivit uppskjutna, notera tecken på smärta eller obehag som kanske inte uttrycks i ord, och gå igenom vardagsrisker som vatten, trafik eller att lämna hemmet utan att säga till. Om du märker djup nedstämdhet eller kris, sök professionell hjälp tidigt. Evidensen: en metaanalys av 27 studier med över 640 000 personer visade högre dödlighet bland autistiska personer och personer med ADHD jämfört med befolkningen i stort. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, tillförlitligheten är måttlig till låg, och resultaten förklarar inte orsaker eller förutsäger något om en enskild person.

title: GABAergic System Dysfunction in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Zhao H, Mao X, Zhu C, Zou X, Peng F, Yang W, Li B, Li G, Ge T, Cui R
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) refers to a series of neurodevelopmental diseases characterized by two hallmark symptoms, social communication deficits and repetitive behaviors. Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is one of the most important inhibitory neurotransmitters in the central nervous system (CNS). GABAergic inhibitory neurotransmission is critical for the regulation of brain rhythm and spontaneous neuronal activities during neurodevelopment. Genetic evidence has identified some variations of genes associated with the GABA system, indicating an abnormal excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) neurotransmission ratio implicated in the pathogenesis of ASD. However, the specific molecular mechanism by which GABA and GABAergic synaptic transmission affect ASD remains unclear. Transgenic technology enables translating genetic variations into rodent models to further investigate the structural and functional synaptic dysregulation related to ASD. In this review, we summarized evidence from human neuroimaging, postmortem, and genetic and pharmacological studies, and put emphasis on the GABAergic synaptic dysregulation and consequent E/I imbalance. We attempt to illuminate the pathophysiological role of structural and functional synaptic dysregulation in ASD and provide insights for future investigation.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no cambia lo que hace mañana: no ofrece un tratamiento ni una prueba nueva. Ayuda a entender que algunas personas autistas pueden tener un equilibrio distinto entre señales cerebrales que activan y que calman, lo que podría relacionarse con la sensibilidad sensorial. Si su familiar se satura con ruido o luz, seguir ofreciendo pausas, espacios tranquilos y previsibilidad sigue siendo razonable. Es una revisión narrativa que resume estudios de neuroimagen, tejido postmortem, genética, fármacos y modelos en roedores. Sus límites: los mecanismos siguen sin estar claros, gran parte proviene de animales y no describe a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: This review does not change what you do tomorrow: it offers no new treatment or test. It helps explain that some autistic people may have a different balance between brain signals that excite and those that calm, which might relate to sensory sensitivity. If your family member gets overwhelmed by noise or light, continuing to offer breaks, quiet spaces and predictability remains sensible. It is a narrative review summarising neuroimaging, postmortem, genetic, drug and rodent-model studies. Its limits: the mechanisms remain unclear, much evidence comes from animals, and it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ändrar inte vad du gör i morgon: den erbjuder ingen ny behandling eller test. Den hjälper till att förklara att vissa autistiska personer kan ha en annan balans mellan hjärnsignaler som aktiverar och som lugnar, vilket kan hänga ihop med sensorisk känslighet. Om din närstående blir överväldigad av ljud eller ljus är det fortsatt rimligt att erbjuda pauser, lugna platser och förutsägbarhet. Det är en narrativ översikt av studier med hjärnavbildning, vävnad efter döden, genetik, läkemedel och gnagarmodeller. Begränsningar: mekanismerna är fortfarande oklara, mycket bygger på djurstudier och den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Automatic Emotion Recognition in Children with Autism: A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Landowska A, Karpus A, Zawadzka T, Robins B, Erol Barkana D, Kose H, Zorcec T, Cummins N
abstract: The automatic emotion recognition domain brings new methods and technologies that might be used to enhance therapy of children with autism. The paper aims at the exploration of methods and tools used to recognize emotions in children. It presents a literature review study that was performed using a systematic approach and PRISMA methodology for reporting quantitative and qualitative results. Diverse observation channels and modalities are used in the analyzed studies, including facial expressions, prosody of speech, and physiological signals. Regarding representation models, the basic emotions are the most frequently recognized, especially happiness, fear, and sadness. Both single-channel and multichannel approaches are applied, with a preference for the first one. For multimodal recognition, early fusion was the most frequently applied. SVM and neural networks were the most popular for building classifiers. Qualitative analysis revealed important clues on participant group construction and the most common combinations of modalities and methods. All channels are reported to be prone to some disturbance, and as a result, information on a specific symptoms of emotions might be temporarily or permanently unavailable. The challenges of proper stimuli, labelling methods, and the creation of open datasets were also identified.

sheet.es: Por ahora, la mejor forma de entender cómo se siente tu hijo o hija autista sigue siendo conocerle: observa sus propias señales, pregúntale de la forma que le resulte cómoda y no des por hecho que su cara o su voz muestran lo que siente. Las herramientas automáticas que "leen" emociones aún están en investigación y no sustituyen tu conocimiento. Esta revisión sistemática analizó estudios que usaban expresiones faciales, voz y señales fisiológicas para reconocer emociones en niños autistas, sobre todo felicidad, miedo y tristeza. Sus límites: los datos son poco fiables por interferencias, faltan bases de datos abiertas y los métodos de etiquetado son discutibles.
sheet.en: For now, the best way to understand how your autistic child feels is still to know them: notice their own signals, ask in a way that works for them, and don't assume their face or voice shows what they feel. Automatic tools that "read" emotions are still at the research stage and don't replace your knowledge. This systematic review examined studies that used facial expressions, speech and physiological signals to recognise emotions in autistic children, mostly happiness, fear and sadness. Its limits: signals are often disrupted, open datasets are scarce, and the ways emotions were labelled remain uncertain.
sheet.sv: Just nu är det bästa sättet att förstå hur ditt autistiska barn mår fortfarande att känna barnet: lägg märke till barnets egna signaler, fråga på ett sätt som fungerar för hen och utgå inte från att ansikte eller röst visar vad hen känner. Automatiska verktyg som "läser av" känslor är fortfarande forskning och ersätter inte din kunskap. Denna systematiska översikt granskade studier som använde ansiktsuttryck, röst och fysiologiska signaler för att känna igen känslor hos autistiska barn, främst glädje, rädsla och ledsenhet. Begränsningar: signalerna störs ofta, öppna dataset saknas och sätten att märka känslor är osäkra.

title: Barriers to healthcare and self-reported adverse outcomes for autistic adults: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Doherty M, Neilson S, O'Sullivan J, Carravallah L, Johnson M, Cullen W, Shaw SCK
abstract: Objectives Autistic people experience poor physical and mental health along with reduced life expectancy compared with non-autistic people. Our aim was to identify self-reported barriers to primary care access by autistic adults compared with non-autistic adults and to link these barriers to self-reported adverse health consequences. Design Following consultation with the autistic community at an autistic conference, Autscape , we developed a self-report survey, which we administered online through social media platforms. Setting A 52-item, international, online survey. Participants 507 autistic adults and 157 non-autistic adults. Primary and secondary outcome measures Self-reported barriers to accessing healthcare and associated adverse health outcomes. Results Eighty per cent of autistic adults and 37% of non-autistic respondents reported difficulty visiting a general practitioner (GP). The highest-rated barriers by autistic adults were deciding if symptoms warrant a GP visit (72%), difficulty making appointments by telephone (62%), not feeling understood (56%), difficulty communicating with their doctor (53%) and the waiting room environment (51%). Autistic adults reported a preference for online or text-based appointment booking, facility to email in advance the reason for consultation, the first or last clinic appointment and a quiet place to wait. Self-reported adverse health outcomes experienced by autistic adults were associated with barriers to accessing healthcare. Adverse outcomes included untreated physical and mental health conditions, not attending specialist referral or screening programmes, requiring more extensive treatment or surgery due to late presentations and untreated potentially life-threatening conditions. There were no significant differences in difficulty attending, barriers experienced or adverse outcomes between formally diagnosed and self-identified autistic respondents. Conclusions Reduction of healthcare inequalities for autistic people requires that healthcare providers understand autistic perspectives, communication needs and sensory sensitivities. Adjustments for autism-specific needs are as necessary as ramps for wheelchair users.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta al médico de cabecera, puedes pedir ajustes concretos: reservar cita por internet o mensaje en lugar de por teléfono, enviar por correo antes el motivo de la consulta, solicitar la primera o la última cita del día y un lugar tranquilo para esperar. También puede ayudar decidir juntos, con calma, si un síntoma merece consulta. Estos ajustes son tan necesarios como una rampa. La evidencia procede de una encuesta internacional en línea, diseñada con la comunidad autista, con 507 adultos autistas y 157 no autistas. Sus límites: son datos autoinformados, de personas que usan redes sociales, y muestran asociaciones, no causas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult with GP visits, you can ask for concrete adjustments: booking online or by text instead of by phone, emailing the reason for the visit in advance, requesting the first or last appointment of the day, and a quiet place to wait. It can also help to calmly decide together whether a symptom is worth a visit. These adjustments are as necessary as a ramp. The evidence comes from an international online survey, designed with the autistic community, with 507 autistic and 157 non-autistic adults. Its limits: answers are self-reported, from people reached through social media, and show associations, not causes.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen vid läkarbesök kan du be om konkreta anpassningar: boka tid via nätet eller sms i stället för telefon, mejla orsaken till besöket i förväg, be om dagens första eller sista tid och en lugn plats att vänta på. Det kan också hjälpa att i lugn och ro tillsammans avgöra om ett symtom behöver ett besök. Sådana anpassningar är lika nödvändiga som en ramp. Underlaget är en internationell webbenkät, utformad tillsammans med autistiska personer, med 507 autistiska och 157 icke-autistiska vuxna. Begränsningar: svaren är självrapporterade, från personer som nåddes via sociala medier, och visar samband, inte orsaker.

title: Pharmacological and dietary-supplement treatments for autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
authors: Siafis S, Çıray O, Wu H, Schneider-Thoma J, Bighelli I, Krause M, Rodolico A, Ceraso A, Deste G, Huhn M, Fraguas D, San José Cáceres A, Mavridis D, Charman T, Murphy DG, Parellada M, Arango C, Leucht
abstract: Background There is still no approved medication for the core symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This network meta-analysis investigated pharmacological and dietary-supplement treatments for ASD. Methods We searched for randomized-controlled-trials (RCTs) with a minimum duration of seven days in ClinicalTrials.gov, EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, WHO-ICTRP (from inception up to July 8, 2018), CENTRAL and PubMed (up to November 3, 2021). The co-primary outcomes were core symptoms (social-communication difficulties-SCD, repetitive behaviors-RB, overall core symptoms-OCS) measured by validated scales and standardized-mean-differences (SMDs). Associated symptoms, e.g., irritability/aggression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms, dropouts and important side-effects, were investigated as secondary outcomes. Studies in children/adolescents and adults were analyzed separately in random-effects pairwise and network meta-analyses. Results We analyzed data for 41 drugs and 17 dietary-supplements, from 125 RCTs (n = 7450 participants) in children/adolescents and 18 RCTs (n = 1104) in adults. The following medications could improve at least one core symptom domain in comparison with placebo: aripiprazole (k = 6 studies in analysis, SCD: SMD = 0.27 95% CI [0.09, 0.44], RB: 0.48 [0.26, 0.70]), atomoxetine (k = 3, RB:0.49 [0.18, 0.80]), bumetanide (k = 4, RB: 0.35 [0.09, 0.62], OCS: 0.61 [0.31, 0.91]), and risperidone (k = 4, SCM: 0.31 [0.06, 0.55], RB: 0.60 [0.29, 0.90]; k = 3, OCS: 1.18 [0.75, 1.61]) in children/adolescents; fluoxetine (k = 1, RB: 1.20 [0.45, 1.96]), fluvoxamine (k = 1, RB: 1.04 [0.27, 1.81]), oxytocin (k = 6, RB:0.41 [0.16, 0.66]) and risperidone (k = 1, RB: 0.97 [0.21,1.74]) in adults. There were some indications of improvement by carnosine, haloperidol, folinic acid, guanfacine, omega-3-fatty-acids, probiotics, sulforaphane, tideglusib and valproate, yet imprecise and not robust. Confidence in these estimates was very low or low, except moderate for oxytocin. Medications differed substantially in improving associated symptoms, and in their side-effect profiles. Limitations Most of the studies were inadequately powered (sample sizes of 20-80 participants), with short duration (8-13 weeks), and about a third focused on associated symptoms. Networks were mainly star-shaped, and there were indications of reporting bias. There was no optimal rating scale measuring change in core symptoms. Conclusions Some medications could improve core symptoms, although this could be likely secondary to the improvement of associated symptoms. Evidence on their efficacy and safety is preliminary; therefore, routine prescription of medications for the core symptoms cannot be recommended. Trial registration PROSPERO-ID CRD42019125317.

sheet.es: Si alguien le ofrece un medicamento o suplemento para cambiar los rasgos centrales del autismo, puede pedir con calma que le expliquen qué objetivo concreto tiene, qué efectos secundarios vigilar y cómo se revisará. Hoy no existe ningún fármaco aprobado para ello, y esta revisión concluye que no se recomienda recetarlos de forma rutinaria con ese fin. Las decisiones sobre medicación corresponden siempre a su equipo médico. Es un metaanálisis en red de 143 ensayos aleatorizados con unos 7.450 niños y adolescentes y 1.104 adultos autistas. Sus límites: estudios pequeños y cortos (8-13 semanas), confianza baja o muy baja en casi todos los resultados y posible sesgo de publicación.
sheet.en: If someone suggests a medication or supplement to change core autistic traits, you can calmly ask what specific goal it has, which side effects to watch for, and how it will be reviewed. No medication is approved for this, and this review concludes that routine prescribing for that purpose cannot be recommended. Decisions about medication always belong with your medical team. It is a network meta-analysis of 143 randomised trials involving about 7,450 autistic children and adolescents and 1,104 autistic adults. Its limits: small, short studies (8-13 weeks), low or very low confidence in almost all findings, and signs of reporting bias.
sheet.sv: Om någon föreslår ett läkemedel eller kosttillskott för att förändra autistiska kärndrag kan du lugnt fråga vilket konkret mål det har, vilka biverkningar ni ska vara uppmärksamma på och hur det ska följas upp. Inget läkemedel är godkänt för detta, och översikten drar slutsatsen att rutinmässig förskrivning i det syftet inte kan rekommenderas. Beslut om läkemedel fattas alltid tillsammans med vården. Studien är en nätverksmetaanalys av 143 randomiserade studier med cirka 7 450 autistiska barn och ungdomar och 1 104 autistiska vuxna. Begränsningar: små och korta studier (8-13 veckor), låg eller mycket låg tillförlitlighet för nästan alla resultat och tecken på rapporteringsbias.

title: Behavioural and psychological features of PTEN mutations: a systematic review of the literature and meta-analysis of the prevalence of autism spectrum disorder characteristics.
authors: Cummings K, Watkins A, Jones C, Dias R, Welham A
abstract: Background Phosphatase and tensin homologue (PTEN) is a cancer suppressor gene. Constitutional mutations affecting this gene are associated with several conditions, collectively termed PTEN hamartoma tumour syndromes (PHTS). In addition to hamartomas, PTEN aberrations have been associated with a range of non-tumoural phenotypes such as macrocephaly, and research indicates possibly increased rates of developmental delay and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) for people with germline mutations affecting PTEN. Method A systematic review of literature reporting behavioural and psychological variables for people with constitutional PTEN mutations/PHTS was conducted using four databases. Following in-depth screening, 25 articles met the inclusion criteria and were used in the review. Fourteen papers reported the proportion of people with PTEN mutations/PTHS meeting criteria for or having characteristics of ASD and were thus used in a pooled prevalence meta-analysis. Results Meta-analysis using a random effects model estimated pooled prevalence of ASD characteristics at 25% (95% CI 16-33%), although this should be interpreted cautiously due to possible biases in existing literature. Intellectual disability and developmental delay (global, motor and speech and language) were also reported frequently. Emotional difficulties and impaired cognitive functioning in specific domains were noted but assessed/reported less frequently. Methods of assessment of psychological/behavioural factors varied widely (with retrospective examination of medical records common). Conclusions Existing research suggests approximately 25% of people with constitutional PTEN mutations may meet criteria for or have characteristics of ASD. Studies have also begun to establish a range of possible cognitive impairments in affected individuals, especially when ASD is also reported. However, further large-scale studies are needed to elucidate psychological/behavioural corollaries of this mutation, and how they may relate to physiological/physical characteristics.

sheet.es: Si una persona de tu familia tiene una variante en el gen PTEN (síndrome de tumor hamartoma PTEN), puede ser útil pedir una valoración del desarrollo, la comunicación y posibles rasgos autistas, además del seguimiento médico habitual. Saberlo pronto ayuda a ofrecer apoyos adaptados en casa y en la escuela. Esta revisión sistemática con metaanálisis reunió 25 estudios; en 14 de ellos, alrededor de una de cada cuatro personas con variantes en PTEN tenía rasgos o diagnóstico de autismo, y también se describieron con frecuencia retrasos del desarrollo y discapacidad intelectual. Sus límites: los estudios eran pequeños, usaban métodos de evaluación muy distintos (a menudo historiales médicos) y podrían sobrestimar la cifra. Cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If someone in your family has a PTEN gene variant (PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome), it may help to ask for an assessment of development, communication and possible autistic traits alongside routine medical follow-up. Knowing early makes it easier to set up fitting support at home and school. This systematic review and meta-analysis gathered 25 studies; in 14 of them, about one in four people with PTEN variants had autistic traits or an autism diagnosis, and developmental delay and intellectual disability were also often reported. Its limits: the studies were small, used very different assessment methods (often medical records) and may overestimate the figure. Every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om någon i din familj har en variant i PTEN-genen (PTEN-hamartomtumörsyndrom) kan det vara bra att be om en bedömning av utveckling, kommunikation och möjliga autistiska drag, vid sidan av den vanliga medicinska uppföljningen. Att veta tidigt gör det lättare att ordna passande stöd hemma och i skolan. Denna systematiska översikt med metaanalys samlade 25 studier; i 14 av dem hade ungefär var fjärde person med PTEN-varianter autistiska drag eller en autismdiagnos, och utvecklingsförsening och intellektuell funktionsnedsättning rapporterades också ofta. Begränsningar: studierna var små, använde mycket olika bedömningsmetoder (ofta journaler) och kan överskatta siffran. Varje person är unik.

title: Oxidative Stress in Autism Spectrum Disorder-Current Progress of Mechanisms and Biomarkers.
authors: Liu X, Lin J, Zhang H, Khan NU, Zhang J, Tang X, Cao X, Shen L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a type of neurodevelopmental disorder that has been diagnosed in an increasing number of children around the world. Existing data suggest that early diagnosis and intervention can improve ASD outcomes. However, the causes of ASD remain complex and unclear, and there are currently no clinical biomarkers for autism spectrum disorder. More mechanisms and biomarkers of autism have been found with the development of advanced technology such as mass spectrometry. Many recent studies have found a link between ASD and elevated oxidative stress, which may play a role in its development. ASD is caused by oxidative stress in several ways, including protein post-translational changes (e.g., carbonylation), abnormal metabolism (e.g., lipid peroxidation), and toxic buildup [e.g., reactive oxygen species (ROS)]. To detect elevated oxidative stress in ASD, various biomarkers have been developed and employed. This article summarizes recent studies about the mechanisms and biomarkers of oxidative stress. Potential biomarkers identified in this study could be used for early diagnosis and evaluation of ASD intervention, as well as to inform and target ASD pharmacological or nutritional treatment interventions.

sheet.es: Por ahora, esta investigación no cambia lo que hace mañana. Los análisis de estrés oxidativo no son una prueba para diagnosticar el autismo ni una guía para elegir suplementos o dietas. Si alguien le ofrece pruebas o productos «antioxidantes» como solución, es razonable consultarlo primero con el equipo de salud de su hijo o hija. Lo que ya sabe sobre sus necesidades, su descanso y su bienestar sigue siendo la mejor guía. Se trata de una revisión que resume estudios de laboratorio y biomarcadores en personas autistas, sobre todo niños. Su límite es importante: muestra asociaciones, no causas, y ninguno de estos biomarcadores está validado para uso clínico.
sheet.en: For now, this research does not change what you do tomorrow. Oxidative stress tests are not a way to diagnose autism, nor a guide for choosing supplements or diets. If someone offers you tests or 'antioxidant' products as a solution, it is reasonable to check with your child's health team first. What you already know about their needs, rest and wellbeing remains the best guide. This is a review summarising laboratory and biomarker studies in autistic people, mostly children. Its limit matters: it shows associations, not causes, and none of these biomarkers is validated for clinical use.
sheet.sv: Just nu ändrar den här forskningen inte vad du gör i morgon. Tester av oxidativ stress är inte ett sätt att ställa autismdiagnos och inte heller en vägledning för att välja kosttillskott eller dieter. Om någon erbjuder tester eller ”antioxidantprodukter” som en lösning är det rimligt att först prata med ditt barns vårdteam. Det du redan vet om barnets behov, vila och välmående är fortfarande den bästa vägledningen. Detta är en översikt som sammanfattar laboratorie- och biomarkörstudier hos autistiska personer, främst barn. Begränsningen är viktig: den visar samband, inte orsaker, och ingen av biomarkörerna är validerad för klinisk användning.

title: Repetitive Restricted Behaviors in Autism Spectrum Disorder: From Mechanism to Development of Therapeutics.
authors: Tian J, Gao X, Yang L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by deficits in social communication, social interaction, and repetitive restricted behaviors (RRBs). It is usually detected in early childhood. RRBs are behavioral patterns characterized by repetition, inflexibility, invariance, inappropriateness, and frequent lack of obvious function or specific purpose. To date, the classification of RRBs is contentious. Understanding the potential mechanisms of RRBs in children with ASD, such as neural connectivity disorders and abnormal immune functions, will contribute to finding new therapeutic targets. Although behavioral intervention remains the most effective and safe strategy for RRBs treatment, some promising drugs and new treatment options (e.g., supplementary and cell therapy) have shown positive effects on RRBs in recent studies. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of RRBs from mechanistic to therapeutic approaches and propose potential future directions in research on RRBs.

sheet.es: Las conductas repetitivas, como balancearse, alinear objetos o necesitar rutinas fijas, suelen cumplir una función para la persona autista: calmarse, organizarse o disfrutar. Mañana, en lugar de intentar eliminarlas, observa cuándo aparecen y qué necesidad podrían cubrir; interviene solo si causan daño o malestar real, y anticipa los cambios de rutina con calma. Esta revisión resume investigaciones sobre posibles mecanismos cerebrales e inmunitarios y sobre tratamientos, y señala que los apoyos conductuales son la opción más estudiada y segura. Sus límites: no es un estudio nuevo con participantes, usa un lenguaje centrado en déficits y las terapias emergentes que menciona aún no tienen pruebas sólidas.
sheet.en: Repetitive behaviours, like rocking, lining things up or needing fixed routines, often serve a purpose for an autistic person: calming, organising or simply enjoying. Tomorrow, instead of trying to stop them, notice when they happen and what need they might meet; step in only if they cause real harm or distress, and prepare for routine changes calmly. This review summarises research on possible brain and immune mechanisms and on treatments, noting that behavioural supports are the most studied and safest option. Its limits: it is not a new study with participants, it uses deficit-focused language, and the emerging therapies it mentions still lack solid evidence.
sheet.sv: Repetitiva beteenden, som att gunga, ställa saker på rad eller behöva fasta rutiner, fyller ofta en funktion för en autistisk person: att lugna sig, skapa ordning eller helt enkelt njuta. I morgon, i stället för att försöka stoppa dem, lägg märke till när de uppstår och vilket behov de kan möta; ingrip bara om de orsakar verklig skada eller stress, och förbered rutinändringar i lugn takt. Denna översikt sammanfattar forskning om möjliga hjärn- och immunmekanismer och behandlingar, och anger att beteendestöd är det mest studerade och säkraste alternativet. Begränsningar: det är ingen ny studie med deltagare, språket är bristfokuserat och de nya terapier som nämns saknar fortfarande starkt stöd.

title: The relevance of the interpersonal theory of suicide for predicting past-year and lifetime suicidality in autistic adults.
authors: Moseley RL, Gregory NJ, Smith P, Allison C, Cassidy S, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background While there are known risk factors for suicidality in autistic adults, these are often unconnected from theoretical frameworks that might explain why risk is elevated and guide clinical interventions. The present study investigated the relevance of constructs from the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide (ITS), including perceived burdensomeness, thwarted belongingness and acquired capability for suicide, and explored mechanisms through which certain risk factors (relationship status, age at diagnosis) might elevate suicide risk. Methods Autistic adults (n = 314) completed an online study including measures of depression, anxiety and constructs from the ITS. Linear and multinomial regression analysis disentangled contributions of ITS variables from effects of depression and anxiety for past-year suicide ideation, past-year and lifetime suicide attempts. Mediation analyses examined associations between risk factors and these suicide outcomes via mechanisms proposed by the ITS. Results Past-year suicide ideation was associated with burdensomeness, mental rehearsal of suicide plans (a facet of acquired capability), and depression. Greater feelings of burdensomeness, and reduced fear of death, marked out participants who had attempted suicide in comparison to those who had experienced suicide ideation in the past year. Relationship status was indirectly associated with past-year suicide ideation via the mediators of depression and burdensomeness, and was associated with past-year attempts via its effect on ideation. Age at diagnosis was unrelated to any variables. Limitations Cross-sectional research is insensitive to causality and temporal dynamics, which is likely why interaction hypotheses from the ITS were unsupported. Normative measures may be invalid in autistic samples. There was no control group. The autistic sample was unrepresentative of the whole population, particularly autistic people with intellectual disabilities, ethnic/racial minorities, and gender minorities. Conclusions Perceived burdensomeness and acquired capability appear potentially important to suicide in autistic people, and may mediate the effects of some risk factors. Future research should explore the temporal dynamics of suicide trajectories in longitudinal, prospective designs.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta cercana expresa que se siente una carga para los demás, tómalo en serio: pregunta con calma y directamente cómo está, recuérdale con hechos concretos lo que aporta y busca apoyo profesional si habla de planes o de no tener miedo a morir. Si hay riesgo inmediato, llama a emergencias. Es un estudio en línea con 314 adultos autistas, que relacionó sentirse una carga, ensayar mentalmente planes y la depresión con pensamientos suicidas recientes. Limitaciones: mide un solo momento, así que no prueba causas; no hubo grupo de comparación y apenas participaron personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual, de minorías étnicas o de género.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult close to you says they feel like a burden to others, take it seriously: ask calmly and directly how they are, remind them with concrete examples of what they bring, and seek professional support if they mention plans or no longer fearing death. If there is immediate danger, contact emergency services. This online study of 314 autistic adults linked feeling like a burden, mentally rehearsing plans and depression with recent suicidal thoughts. Limits: it captured one moment, so it cannot show causes; there was no comparison group, and few autistic people with intellectual disability, from ethnic minorities or gender minorities took part.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen nära dig säger att hen känner sig som en börda för andra, ta det på allvar: fråga lugnt och rakt hur hen mår, påminn med konkreta exempel om vad hen bidrar med och sök professionellt stöd om hen nämner planer eller att inte längre vara rädd för döden. Vid akut fara, ring 112. Denna onlinestudie med 314 autistiska vuxna kopplade känslan av att vara en börda, att mentalt öva på planer och depression till nyliga självmordstankar. Begränsningar: den mätte ett enda tillfälle och kan inte visa orsaker; det fanns ingen jämförelsegrupp och få autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, från etniska minoriteter eller könsminoriteter deltog.

title: Immune Dysregulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: What Do We Know about It?
authors: Robinson-Agramonte MLA, Noris García E, Fraga Guerra J, Vega Hurtado Y, Antonucci N, Semprún-Hernández N, Schultz S, Siniscalco D
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a group of complex multifactorial neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by a wide and variable set of neuropsychiatric symptoms, including deficits in social communication, narrow and restricted interests, and repetitive behavior. The immune hypothesis is considered to be a major factor contributing to autism pathogenesis, as well as a way to explain the differences of the clinical phenotypes and comorbidities influencing disease course and severity. Evidence highlights a link between immune dysfunction and behavioral traits in autism from several types of evidence found in both cerebrospinal fluid and peripheral blood and their utility to identify autistic subgroups with specific immunophenotypes; underlying behavioral symptoms are also shown. This review summarizes current insights into immune dysfunction in ASD, with particular reference to the impact of immunological factors related to the maternal influence of autism development; comorbidities influencing autism disease course and severity; and others factors with particular relevance, including obesity. Finally, we described main elements of similarities between immunopathology overlapping neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders, taking as examples autism and Parkinson Disease, respectively.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo tiene infecciones frecuentes, alergias, problemas digestivos o cambios en el peso, vale la pena anotarlos y comentarlos con su médico: la salud física puede influir en cómo se siente y se comporta cada día. No hace falta cambiar nada por tu cuenta; un registro sencillo de síntomas, sueño y estado de ánimo ayuda a que te escuchen. Esta es una revisión narrativa que resume estudios sobre el sistema inmunitario en personas autistas y en el embarazo. Sus límites: no presenta datos nuevos, mezcla estudios muy distintos y no ofrece pruebas ni tratamientos válidos para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support has frequent infections, allergies, gut problems or weight changes, it is worth noting them down and raising them with their doctor: physical health can affect how someone feels and acts day to day. You don't need to change anything on your own; a simple log of symptoms, sleep and mood helps you be heard. This is a narrative review summarising research on the immune system in autistic people and during pregnancy. Its limits: it adds no new data, combines very different studies, and offers no test or treatment that applies to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar ofta har infektioner, allergier, magbesvär eller viktförändringar är det värt att anteckna det och ta upp det med läkaren: kroppslig hälsa kan påverka hur någon mår och agerar i vardagen. Du behöver inte ändra något på egen hand; en enkel logg över symtom, sömn och humör hjälper dig att bli lyssnad på. Detta är en översiktsartikel som sammanfattar forskning om immunsystemet hos autistiska personer och under graviditet. Begränsningar: den tillför inga nya data, blandar mycket olika studier och erbjuder inget test eller behandling som gäller alla.

title: Environmental exposures associated with elevated risk for autism spectrum disorder may augment the burden of deleterious de novo mutations among probands.
authors: Pugsley K, Scherer SW, Bellgrove MA, Hawi Z
abstract: Although the full aetiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is unknown, familial and twin studies demonstrate high heritability of 60-90%, indicating a predominant role of genetics in the development of the disorder. The genetic architecture of ASD consists of a complex array of rare and common variants of all classes of genetic variation usually acting additively to augment individual risk. The relative contribution of heredity in ASD persists despite selective pressures against the classic autistic phenotype; a phenomenon thought to be explained, in part, by the incidence of spontaneous (or de novo) mutations. Notably, environmental exposures attributed as salient risk factors for ASD may play a causal role in the emergence of deleterious de novo variations, with several ASD-associated agents having significant mutagenic potential. To explore this hypothesis, this review article assesses published epidemiological data with evidence derived from assays of mutagenicity, both in vivo and in vitro, to determine the likely role such agents may play in augmenting the genetic liability in ASD. Broadly, these exposures were observed to elicit genomic alterations through one or a combination of: (1) direct interaction with genetic material; (2) impaired DNA repair; or (3) oxidative DNA damage. However, the direct contribution of these factors to the ASD phenotype cannot be determined without further analysis. The development of comprehensive prospective birth cohorts in combination with genome sequencing is essential to forming a causal, mechanistic account of de novo mutations in ASD that links exposure, genotypic alterations, and phenotypic consequences.

sheet.es: Para el día a día, este estudio no cambia nada: no hay ninguna acción nueva que tomar ni motivo para buscar culpas. Ser autista está ligado sobre todo a la genética, y nada de lo que hizo o dejó de hacer una familia se señala aquí como causa. Es una revisión que reúne estudios epidemiológicos y de laboratorio para plantear una idea: algunas exposiciones ambientales podrían favorecer cambios genéticos nuevos (de novo) asociados al autismo. Su límite es claro: es una hipótesis, no una prueba; los propios autores dicen que hacen falta grandes estudios de seguimiento desde el nacimiento con secuenciación genética para saber si esta relación es real.
sheet.en: For everyday life, this study changes nothing: there is no new action to take and no reason to look for blame. Being autistic is linked mainly to genetics, and nothing a family did or didn't do is identified here as a cause. This is a review that brings together epidemiological and laboratory studies to propose an idea: some environmental exposures might encourage new (de novo) genetic changes associated with autism. Its limit is clear: it is a hypothesis, not proof; the authors themselves say large birth cohort studies with genome sequencing are needed to know whether this link is real.
sheet.sv: I vardagen ändrar den här studien ingenting: det finns ingen ny åtgärd att vidta och ingen anledning att leta efter skuld. Att vara autistisk hänger främst ihop med genetik, och inget en familj gjort eller inte gjort pekas här ut som orsak. Det är en översikt som samlar epidemiologiska studier och laboratoriestudier för att lägga fram en idé: vissa miljöexponeringar skulle kunna bidra till nya (de novo) genetiska förändringar kopplade till autism. Begränsningen är tydlig: det är en hypotes, inte ett bevis; författarna skriver själva att stora födelsekohorter med gensekvensering behövs för att veta om sambandet är verkligt.

title: "A Group of Fellow Travellers Who Understand": Interviews With Autistic People About Post-diagnostic Peer Support in Adulthood.
authors: Crompton CJ, Hallett S, McAuliffe C, Stanfield AC, Fletcher-Watson S
abstract: Receiving a diagnosis of autism in adulthood can be a life changing event, impacting identity, relationships, and mental health. A lack of post-diagnostic support has been highlighted by autistic adults, their allies, clinicians, and service providers. It can be a source of distress for autistic adults, reinforcing feelings of social isolation and rejection. Peer support could be a cost-effective, flexible, and sustainable model to provide community-based support for autistic adults. However, there is little research on the value of peer support, despite calls from the autistic community. This qualitative study explored autistic experiences and needs post-diagnosis, identifying specific ways that peer support may benefit them, and exploring the limitations of peer support. Twelve autistic adults who had all received an autism diagnosis in adulthood completed a semi-structured interview focussing on the diagnostic experience, post-diagnostic support needed and provided, engagement with the autistic community, and post-diagnostic peer support. Thematic analysis of interview transcripts resulted in four themes: (1) Mismatch in support needed and provided; (2) Community connection; (3) Flexible and personalised support; and (4) Sustainability. Participants indicated that peer support may be a useful mechanism to support autistic adults' post-diagnosis and offers unique opportunities not available through other support channels. Though informal peer support exists, it could be more sustainable and effective if well-supported and funded.

sheet.es: Si tú o alguien cercano recibe un diagnóstico de autismo en la adultez, puede ayudar buscar contacto con otras personas autistas: grupos locales, asociaciones o comunidades en línea. Muchas personas encuentran allí comprensión, información práctica y una sensación de pertenencia que los servicios formales a menudo no ofrecen. Conviene que el apoyo sea flexible: cada persona elige el ritmo, el formato (presencial, escrito, en línea) y cuánto participa. Es un estudio cualitativo basado en entrevistas con doce adultos autistas diagnosticados en la adultez. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño, describe experiencias y no mide resultados, y lo que sirvió a estas personas puede no servir a todas.
