sheet.en: If you or someone close to you is diagnosed autistic as an adult, it may help to look for contact with other autistic people: local groups, autistic-led organisations or online communities. Many people find understanding, practical tips and a sense of belonging there that formal services often don't provide. Support works best when it is flexible: each person chooses the pace, the format (in person, written, online) and how much to take part. This is a qualitative interview study with twelve autistic adults diagnosed in adulthood. Its limits: the group is small, it describes experiences rather than measuring outcomes, and what helped these people may not suit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du eller någon nära dig får en autismdiagnos i vuxen ålder kan det hjälpa att söka kontakt med andra autistiska personer: lokala grupper, föreningar som drivs av autistiska personer eller nätgemenskaper. Många hittar där förståelse, praktiska tips och en känsla av tillhörighet som vården ofta inte erbjuder. Stödet fungerar bäst när det är flexibelt: varje person väljer takt, form (på plats, skriftligt, digitalt) och hur mycket hen vill delta. Det här är en kvalitativ intervjustudie med tolv autistiska vuxna som fått diagnos i vuxen ålder. Begränsningar: gruppen är liten, studien beskriver upplevelser snarare än mäter effekter, och det som hjälpte dessa personer passar inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: Avoiding Ableist Language: Suggestions for Autism Researchers.
authors: Bottema-Beutel K, Kapp SK, Lester JN, Sasson NJ, Hand BN
abstract: In this commentary, we describe how language used to communicate about autism within much of autism research can reflect and perpetuate ableist ideologies (i.e., beliefs and practices that discriminate against people with disabilities), whether or not researchers intend to have such effects. Drawing largely from autistic scholarship on this subject, along with research and theory from disability studies and discourse analysis, we define ableism and its realization in linguistic practices, provide a historical overview of ableist language used to describe autism, and review calls from autistic researchers and laypeople to adopt alternative ways of speaking and writing. Finally, we provide several specific avenues to aid autism researchers in reflecting on and adjusting their language choices. Lay summary Why is this topic important?: In the past, autism research has mostly been conducted by nonautistic people, and researchers have described autism as something bad that should be fixed. Describing autism in this way has negative effects on how society views and treats autistic people and may even negatively affect how autistic people view themselves. Despite recent positive changes in how researchers write and speak about autism, "ableist" language is still used. Ableist language refers to language that assumes disabled people are inferior to nondisabled people. What is the purpose of this article?: We wrote this article to describe how ableism influences the way autism is often described in research. We also give autism researchers strategies for avoiding ableist language in their future work. What is the perspective of the authors?: We believe that ableism is a "system of discrimination," which means that it influences how people talk about and perceive autism whether or not they are aware of it, and regardless of whether or not they actually believe that autistic people are inferior to nonautistic people. We also believe that language choices are part of what perpetuates this system. Because of this, researchers need to take special care to determine whether their language choices reflect ableism and take steps to use language that is not ableist. What is already known about this topic?: Autistic adults (including researchers and nonresearchers) have been writing and speaking about ableist language for several decades, but nonautistic autism researchers may not be aware of this work. We have compiled this material and summarized it for autism researchers. What do the authors recommend?: We recommend that researchers understand what ableism is, reflect on the language they use in their written and spoken work, and use nonableist language alternatives to describe autism and autistic people. For example, many autistic people find terms such as "special interests" and "special needs" patronizing; these terms could be replaced with "focused interests" and descriptions of autistic people's specific needs. Medicalized/deficit language such as "at risk for autism" should be replaced by more neutral terms such as "increased likelihood of autism." Finally, ways of speaking about autism that are not restricted to particular terms but still contribute to marginalization, such as discussion about the "economic burden of autism," should be replaced with discourses that center the impacts of social arrangements on autistic people. How will these recommendations help autistic people now or in the future?: Language is a powerful means for shaping how people view autism. If researchers take steps to avoid ableist language, researchers, service providers, and society at large may become more accepting and accommodating of autistic people.

sheet.es: Mañana puede revisar cómo habla de su familiar autista, en casa y con profesionales: cambie «intereses especiales» por «intereses intensos», nombre necesidades concretas en lugar de «necesidades especiales» y evite hablar del autismo como una carga. Si un informe usa lenguaje de déficit, puede pedir con calma otras palabras. Las palabras influyen en cómo la persona se ve a sí misma. Este artículo es un comentario, no un experimento: reúne décadas de escritos de personas autistas y estudios sobre discapacidad. Su límite es que no mide efectos directos, y cada persona puede preferir términos distintos; pregúntele a la suya.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, you could notice how you talk about your autistic family member, at home and with professionals: try "focused interests" instead of "special interests," name specific needs rather than "special needs," and avoid describing autism as a burden. If a report uses deficit language, you can calmly ask for different words. Language shapes how a person sees themselves. This article is a commentary, not an experiment: it gathers decades of writing by autistic people plus disability studies research. Its limit is that it does not measure direct effects, and individuals may prefer different terms, so ask the person you support.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du lägga märke till hur du pratar om din autistiska närstående, hemma och med personal: säg "fokuserade intressen" i stället för "specialintressen", beskriv konkreta behov i stället för "särskilda behov" och undvik att tala om autism som en börda. Om ett utlåtande använder bristspråk kan du lugnt be om andra ord. Språk påverkar hur en person ser på sig själv. Artikeln är en kommentar, inte ett experiment: den samlar decennier av texter från autistiska personer och funktionshinderforskning. Begränsningen är att den inte mäter direkta effekter, och personer kan föredra olika ord, så fråga den du stöttar.

claim.es: El lenguaje que usamos sobre el autismo importa: términos como 'conducta desafiante' o 'bajo funcionamiento' estigmatizan.
claim.en: The words we use about autism matter: terms like 'challenging behaviour' or 'low functioning' stigmatise.
claim.sv: Orden vi använder om autism spelar roll: uttryck som 'utmanande beteende' eller 'lågfungerande' stigmatiserar.

supports.es: Describir qué pasó y qué ayudó, sin etiquetar a la persona.
supports.en: Describing what happened and what helped, not labelling the person.
supports.sv: Att beskriva vad som hände och vad som hjälpte, inte att etikettera personen.

doesNotSupport.es: Que todos deban usar las mismas palabras; las preferencias varían y hay que preguntarlas.
doesNotSupport.en: That everyone must use identical words; preferences vary and should be asked.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att alla måste använda samma ord; preferenser varierar och bör efterfrågas.

title: Experiences of Sensory Overload and Communication Barriers by Autistic Adults in Health Care Settings.
authors: Strömberg M, Liman L, Bang P, Igelström K
abstract: Background Autistic adults have an elevated risk of many health problems compared with the general population, making health care access extra critical. Unfortunately, autistic people often find health care settings quite aversive, and many medical providers report feeling unsure about how to interact with autistic patients. We aimed at characterizing specific challenges regarding sensory experiences and communicative barriers in health care settings. Methods We recruited adults to complete an anonymous online questionnaire on the topic of improving health care experiences for everyone. The questions covered demographics, sensory experiences in medical settings, and communication with health care providers. We quantified the associations between autism diagnosis and experiences of sensory discomfort and communication barriers in health care settings. We also did a qualitative analysis of text responses to questions on how to improve sensory environments and communication with providers. Results Swedish adults (62 autistic and 36 nonautistic) participated in the study. The cohort was well educated, and autistic participants received their autism diagnosis late in life (median age 36 years, range 13-57). Compared with nonautistic participants, autistic participants reported greater discomfort with background sound levels in health care settings and felt more misunderstood by health care providers. Thematic analyses showed that auditory stimuli and proximity to other people were particularly bothersome for autistic participants, causing stress or avoidance and affecting the ability to interact with providers. Providers contributed to communication barriers by failing to recognize the need for individualized information, especially when respondents' difficulties were not visible or taken seriously. Participants requested greater clarity and supplementary written information. Providers also misunderstood autistic adults' body language or eye contact patterns, as they interpreted their clients through the lens of neurotypical expectations. Conclusions Our results extend previous research by emphasizing sensory aspects of health care settings and suggesting specific and reasonable adaptations. The results also highlight how the provider's implicit expectations of nonverbal communication caused misinterpretations of autistic people who were socially skilled but did not use typical body language. Based on the data, we suggest specific adaptations, many of which may also benefit nonautistic people.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar pedir una sala de espera tranquila o esperar fuera, solicitar información por escrito y explicar al personal que la falta de contacto visual o un lenguaje corporal distinto no significa desinterés ni que todo esté bien. En este estudio, los adultos autistas señalaron el ruido de fondo y la cercanía de otras personas como especialmente estresantes, y se sintieron más incomprendidos por los profesionales. Se trata de una encuesta anónima en línea con 62 adultos autistas y 36 no autistas en Suecia. Sus límites: muestra pequeña, muy formada y con diagnóstico tardío, por lo que no representa a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to ask for a quiet waiting space or to wait outside, request written information, and tell staff that little eye contact or different body language does not mean disinterest or that everything is fine. In this study, autistic adults described background noise and being close to other people as especially stressful, and felt more misunderstood by providers. It was an anonymous online survey of 62 autistic and 36 non-autistic adults in Sweden. Its limits: a small, highly educated sample, mostly diagnosed late in life, so it does not represent every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Inför ett vårdbesök kan det hjälpa att be om ett lugnt väntrum eller att få vänta utanför, be om skriftlig information och berätta för personalen att lite ögonkontakt eller annorlunda kroppsspråk inte betyder ointresse eller att allt är bra. I studien beskrev autistiska vuxna bakgrundsljud och närhet till andra människor som särskilt stressande, och de kände sig oftare missförstådda av vårdpersonal. Det var en anonym webbenkät med 62 autistiska och 36 icke-autistiska vuxna i Sverige. Begränsningar: urvalet var litet, högutbildat och fick oftast diagnos sent i livet, så resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Autistic Adults' Experiences of Camouflaging and Its Perceived Impact on Mental Health.
authors: Bradley L, Shaw R, Baron-Cohen S, Cassidy S
abstract: Background: Camouflaging (also referred to as "masking") is a commonly reported strategy used by autistic adults in everyday life to help them cope in social situations. Autistic adults report that camouflaging can have a devastating effect on mental health and well-being, yet little is known about the lived experiences of camouflaging and its impact. Methods: We designed an online survey in partnership with autistic adults, to explore the experiences of camouflaging and its impact on mental health. Participants self-reported the lifetime experience of camouflaging, where they camouflaged the frequency and length of time spent camouflaging. Four open questions allowed participants to elaborate their answers to the closed questions on frequency and length of time, and subsequently any positive and negative aspects of their experience of camouflaging. Two hundred seventy-seven autistic adults who self-reported a diagnosis of an autism spectrum condition (128 female, 78 male) or self-identified as autistic (56 female, 15 male) were included in the analysis of qualitative responses to the open-ended questions. Findings: We thematically analyzed participant answers from the open questions. Three main themes emerged. First, "dangers of camouflaging" described how the amount of time spent camouflaging led to exhaustion, isolation, poor mental and physical health, loss of identity and acceptance of self, others' unreal perceptions and expectations, and delayed diagnosis. Second, "positive aspects of camouflaging" included greater access to social spaces, and protection from harm. Camouflaging was, therefore, seen as necessary to survive in a world designed for the neurotypical majority. Third, autistic adults described being diagnosed and accepted for who they are as reasons for "why I don't need to camouflage like I used to." Conclusions: Time spent camouflaging is what seems to be most damaging for the participants' mental health. The main reason reported for needing to spend so much time camouflaging is society's lack of awareness and acceptance of autism. Lay summary Why is this study being done?: Many autistic adults report that they need to camouflage their autistic behaviors to help them "fit in" and cope in social situations with non-autistic people. This is because society is not as aware and accepting of autistic people as it needs to be. We also know that for most autistic adults camouflaging is exhausting and damaging for their mental health. This study is important, because researchers have not studied camouflaging enough to know what it is like for autistic adults to camouflage in their everyday lives and to understand the impact that camouflaging has on their mental health. What was the purpose of this study?: We wanted to ask autistic adults about their positive and negative experiences of camouflaging. This is important because it will help professionals better understand why autistic adults camouflage, and better support the mental health needs of autistic adults. This increased understanding may also help society become more aware and accepting of autism. If this happens, autistic adults will not need to camouflage as much. Not having to camouflage as much could also help prevent and reduce mental health problems in autistic adults. What did we do?: We asked autistic adults with a clinical diagnosis and those who self-identify as autistic to complete an online survey. The survey asked questions about mental health, self-injury, suicidal thoughts, and suicidal behaviors. One part of the survey asked questions about camouflaging. If research participants said they camouflaged or masked their autistic characteristics to cope with social situations, they would then be asked about when and why they camouflage, and about the positive and negative consequences of camouflaging. What did we find?: We found that autistic people confirmed that they camouflage because of a lack of awareness and acceptance of autism in society. We also found that both autistic males and females camouflage. Although some autistic adults said that "everyone" camouflages, they thought that autistic people spent much more time than non-autistic people camouflaging in their everyday lives. Spending lots of time camouflaging was what was most damaging for autistic adults' mental health. Although most autistic adults thought that camouflaging was damaging to their mental health, some thought that it helped them too. How will knowing this help autistic adults?: Our results suggest that it is important to reduce pressure to camouflage. This could help prevent high rates of mental health problems in autistic people. Our results suggest that this can be achieved if wider society becomes more aware and accepting of autistic people. Our results also suggest that reducing pressure to camouflage could benefit everyone in society.

sheet.es: Mañana puedes ofrecer espacios donde la persona autista no tenga que aparentar: deja que se mueva, hable o se retire a su manera, y planifica tiempo de descanso después de situaciones sociales largas. Según este estudio, lo que más desgasta es la cantidad de tiempo que se pasa camuflándose, y la aceptación ayuda a necesitarlo menos. Aun así, algunas personas sienten que camuflarse las protege, así que conviene preguntar y no imponer. Se trata de una encuesta en línea diseñada junto con personas autistas, con 277 adultos autistas, con diagnóstico o autoidentificados. Sus límites: son respuestas escritas y autoinformadas, de personas que eligieron participar, y no incluye a niños.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, you can offer spaces where the autistic person doesn't have to pretend: let them move, talk or step away in their own way, and plan recovery time after long social situations. In this study, what wore people down most was how much time they spent camouflaging, and being accepted helped them need it less. Some people still felt camouflaging protected them, so ask rather than insist. This was an online survey designed together with autistic people, answered by 277 autistic adults, diagnosed or self-identified. Its limits: answers were written and self-reported by people who chose to take part, and children were not included.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du erbjuda sammanhang där den autistiska personen slipper låtsas: låt hen röra sig, prata eller dra sig undan på sitt sätt, och planera återhämtning efter långa sociala situationer. I den här studien var det mängden tid som gick åt till att kamouflera som tärde mest, och att bli accepterad gjorde att behovet minskade. Vissa upplevde ändå att kamouflering skyddade dem, så fråga hellre än att kräva. Det var en webbenkät utformad tillsammans med autistiska personer, besvarad av 277 autistiska vuxna med diagnos eller självidentifierade. Begränsningar: svaren var skriftliga och självrapporterade från personer som valde att delta, och barn ingick inte.

title: Investigating Markers of Rapport in Autistic and Nonautistic Interactions.
authors: Rifai OM, Fletcher-Watson S, Jiménez-Sánchez L, Crompton CJ
abstract: Background Autism is considered to entail a social impairment whereby autistic people experience difficulty interpreting others' mental states. However, recent research has shown that nonautistic people also have difficulty understanding the mental states of autistic people. This mismatch of understanding may explain lower rapport in interactions between autistic and nonautistic people. As mental states can be expressed externally through socially normed signals, it is important to investigate the role of such signals in autistic, nonautistic, and mixed interactions. This study explores variability in two social signals between autistic, nonautistic, and mixed interactions, and how their use may affect rapport within interactions. Methods Videos from a previous study of autistic, nonautistic, and mixed pair interactions in a diffusion chain context in which participants were aware of others' diagnostic status were video coded for mutual gaze and backchanneling as candidate indicators of interactional rapport. Results Although use of mutual gaze and backchanneling was lower in mixed pairs than in nonautistic pairs, corresponding to lower ratings of interactional rapport, less backchanneling in autistic pairs of both nonverbal and verbal subtypes corresponded to higher ratings of rapport. Conclusions We observed differences in the use of candidate rapport markers between autistic, mixed, and nonautistic interactions, which did not map onto patterns of rapport scores, suggesting differences in reliance on these cues between autistic and nonautistic people. These results suggest that visible markers of rapport may vary by neurotype or pairing and give clues to inform future investigations of autistic interaction.

sheet.es: Mañana, no juzgues la conexión solo por el contacto visual o los gestos de escucha como asentir o decir «ajá». Entre personas autistas, menos de estas señales coincidió con más sintonía. Pregunta directamente cómo va la conversación y acepta otras formas de mostrar interés. Si eres no autista, recuerda que el malentendido va en ambas direcciones. Evidencia: se analizaron vídeos de parejas autistas, no autistas y mixtas que se pasaban información, codificando mirada mutua y señales de escucha. Límites: grupo pequeño de adultos en una tarea de laboratorio, sabiendo el diagnóstico del otro; puede no reflejar la vida diaria ni a cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, don't judge connection only by eye contact or listening signals like nodding or saying "mm-hm". Between autistic people, fewer of these signals went with stronger rapport. Ask directly how the conversation feels and welcome other ways of showing interest. If you are nonautistic, remember that misunderstanding runs both ways. Evidence: researchers coded videos of autistic, nonautistic and mixed pairs passing on information, looking at mutual gaze and listening signals. Limits: a small group of adults in a lab task who knew each other's diagnosis; results may not reflect everyday life or every person.
sheet.sv: I morgon, bedöm inte kontakt bara utifrån ögonkontakt eller lyssnarsignaler som nickar eller "mm". Mellan autistiska personer hängde färre sådana signaler ihop med bättre samspel. Fråga direkt hur samtalet känns och välkomna andra sätt att visa intresse. Om du inte är autistisk, kom ihåg att missförstånd går åt båda håll. Evidens: forskare kodade videor av autistiska, icke-autistiska och blandade par som förde vidare information, med fokus på ömsesidig blick och lyssnarsignaler. Begränsningar: en liten grupp vuxna i en laboratorieuppgift som kände till varandras diagnos; resultaten speglar kanske inte vardagen eller varje person.

title: The Cerebellar Involvement in Autism Spectrum Disorders: From the Social Brain to Mouse Models.
authors: Mapelli L, Soda T, D'Angelo E, Prestori F
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are pervasive neurodevelopmental disorders that include a variety of forms and clinical phenotypes. This heterogeneity complicates the clinical and experimental approaches to ASD etiology and pathophysiology. To date, a unifying theory of these diseases is still missing. Nevertheless, the intense work of researchers and clinicians in the last decades has identified some ASD hallmarks and the primary brain areas involved. Not surprisingly, the areas that are part of the so-called "social brain", and those strictly connected to them, were found to be crucial, such as the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, limbic system, and dopaminergic pathways. With the recent acknowledgment of the cerebellar contribution to cognitive functions and the social brain, its involvement in ASD has become unmistakable, though its extent is still to be elucidated. In most cases, significant advances were made possible by recent technological developments in structural/functional assessment of the human brain and by using mouse models of ASD. Mouse models are an invaluable tool to get insights into the molecular and cellular counterparts of the disease, acting on the specific genetic background generating ASD-like phenotype. Given the multifaceted nature of ASD and related studies, it is often difficult to navigate the literature and limit the huge content to specific questions. This review fulfills the need for an organized, clear, and state-of-the-art perspective on cerebellar involvement in ASD, from its connections to the social brain areas (which are the primary sites of ASD impairments) to the use of monogenic mouse models.

sheet.es: No hay nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana: esta investigación busca entender mejor el cerebro, no ofrece técnicas ni tratamientos. Puede ayudar saber que el cerebelo, conocido por la coordinación del movimiento, también participa en el pensamiento y la vida social, lo que quizá explique por qué algunas personas autistas viven de forma conectada el movimiento, la sensorialidad y la comunicación. Sigue observando qué le funciona a tu familiar. Se trata de una revisión de la literatura que reúne estudios de imágenes cerebrales en humanos y de modelos de ratón. Sus límites: no aporta datos nuevos, gran parte procede de ratones y no se aplica directamente a ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change tomorrow morning: this research aims to understand the brain, not to offer techniques or treatments. It may help to know that the cerebellum, known for coordinating movement, also plays a part in thinking and social life, which might partly explain why some autistic people experience movement, senses and communication as closely linked. Keep noticing what works for your family member. This is a literature review bringing together human brain-imaging studies and mouse-model research. Its limits: it adds no new data, much of the evidence comes from mice, and it does not apply directly to any individual person.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras i morgon bitti: forskningen handlar om att förstå hjärnan, inte om metoder eller behandlingar. Det kan vara bra att veta att lillhjärnan, känd för att samordna rörelser, också deltar i tänkande och socialt samspel. Det kan delvis förklara varför vissa autistiska personer upplever rörelse, sinnen och kommunikation som nära sammankopplade. Fortsätt lägga märke till vad som fungerar för din närstående. Detta är en litteraturöversikt som sammanfattar studier av hjärnavbildning hos människor och forskning på möss. Begränsningar: den tillför inga nya data, mycket bygger på möss och den gäller inte direkt för någon enskild person.

title: Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Leader G, Abberton C, Cunningham S, Gilmartin K, Grudzien M, Higgins E, Joshi L, Whelan S, Mannion A
abstract: This systematic review aims to offer an updated understanding of the relationship between gastrointestinal symptoms (GIS) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in children and adolescents. The databases PsycINFO, Medline, Cinahl, and ERIC were searched using keywords, and relevant literature was hand-searched. Papers ( n = 3319) were systematically screened and deemed eligible if they were empirical studies published in English since 2014 and measured the GIS of individuals with ASD who were under 18 years old. Thirty studies were included in the final review. The study findings were synthesized under eight themes, including the prevalence and nature of GIS and their relationship with developmental regression, language and communication, ASD severity, challenging behavior, comorbid psychopathology, sleep problems, and sensory issues. The review found that GIS were common and that there was contradictory evidence concerning their relationship with co-occurring conditions. It also identified evidence of some causal relationships that support the existence of the gut-immune-brain pathways. Future research needs to use large prospective designs and objective and standardized GIS measurements to provide a nuanced understanding of GIS in the context of ASD.

sheet.es: Los problemas digestivos, como estreñimiento, diarrea o dolor de barriga, son frecuentes en niños y adolescentes autistas y merecen atención. Si notas cambios en el sueño, la irritabilidad o la sensibilidad sensorial, considera si podría haber malestar intestinal, sobre todo si tu hijo o hija tiene dificultades para expresar dolor. Anotar comidas, deposiciones y señales de incomodidad puede ayudar a conversar con el equipo de salud. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 30 estudios publicados desde 2014 con menores de 18 años. Sus límites: los resultados sobre la relación con el sueño, la conducta o la comunicación fueron contradictorios, y muchos estudios usaron mediciones poco estandarizadas.
sheet.en: Digestive issues such as constipation, diarrhoea or tummy pain are common in autistic children and teenagers and deserve attention. If you notice changes in sleep, irritability or sensory sensitivity, consider whether gut discomfort might be involved, especially if your child finds it hard to communicate pain. Keeping simple notes on meals, bowel movements and signs of discomfort can support conversations with your healthcare team. This systematic review brought together 30 studies published since 2014 involving people under 18. Its limits: findings on links with sleep, behaviour or communication were contradictory, and many studies used measurements that were not standardised.
sheet.sv: Magbesvär som förstoppning, diarré eller ont i magen är vanliga hos autistiska barn och tonåringar och förtjänar uppmärksamhet. Om du märker förändringar i sömn, irritabilitet eller sensorisk känslighet kan det vara värt att fundera på om magen besvärar, särskilt om ditt barn har svårt att uttrycka smärta. Enkla anteckningar om måltider, toalettbesök och tecken på obehag kan underlätta samtal med vården. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 30 studier publicerade sedan 2014 med deltagare under 18 år. Begränsningar: resultaten om samband med sömn, beteende och kommunikation var motstridiga, och många studier använde mätmetoder som inte var standardiserade.

title: The lived experience of gender dysphoria in autistic adults: An interpretative phenomenological analysis.
authors: Cooper K, Mandy W, Butler C, Russell A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are more likely to be transgender, which means having a gender identity different to one's sex assigned at birth. Some transgender people experience distress about their gender and sex assigned at birth not matching which is called gender dysphoria. Research has focused on finding out why autistic people are more likely to have gender dysphoria, and less on what the experience of gender dysphoria is like for autistic people. We interviewed 21 autistic adults about their experience of incongruence between their gender identity and sex assigned at birth, and any associated distress. We carefully read the transcripts of the interviews, focusing on how participants understood their experiences. We found a range of themes from the interviews. Participants were distressed because their bodies did not match their gender identities. Participants told us they had to work hard to understand themselves and who they were, and to manage having multiple different needs such as mental health needs. It was upsetting for participants to experience discrimination because of being autistic and/or transgender. Some participants said it was more difficult to get transgender healthcare as an autistic person. Some participants thought being autistic had helped them understand their gender identity more than non-autistic people. Other participants found it was challenging to be both autistic and transgender. For example, most participants wanted to change their bodies to match their gender identity, but some participants were nervous about making changes to themselves and their routine due to being autistic. We conclude that autism can in some ways be helpful and other ways contribute to challenges for transgender autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista cercana habla de su identidad de género, escúchela sin cuestionar que su autismo invalide lo que siente. Puede necesitar tiempo para entenderse, apoyo con su salud mental y ayuda práctica para gestionar cambios y rutinas si decide hacer una transición. Esté atento a la discriminación que pueda vivir y acompáñela cuando busque atención sanitaria, que a veces resulta más difícil para personas autistas. Este estudio cualitativo entrevistó en profundidad a 21 adultos autistas con experiencias de disforia de género. Al ser un grupo pequeño y basado en entrevistas, describe vivencias diversas, no reglas que se apliquen a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person close to you talks about their gender identity, listen without assuming their autism makes their feelings less valid. They may need time to understand themselves, support with mental health, and practical help managing changes and routines if they choose to transition. Watch for discrimination they may face, and offer to accompany them when seeking healthcare, which can be harder to access as an autistic person. This qualitative study interviewed 21 autistic adults in depth about their experiences of gender dysphoria. Because it is a small, interview-based group, it describes varied experiences rather than rules that apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person nära dig pratar om sin könsidentitet, lyssna utan att anta att autismen gör känslorna mindre giltiga. Personen kan behöva tid att förstå sig själv, stöd för psykisk hälsa och praktisk hjälp med förändringar och rutiner om hen väljer att transitionera. Var uppmärksam på diskriminering hen kan möta, och erbjud att följa med i kontakter med vården, som kan vara svårare att få tillgång till som autistisk. Denna kvalitativa studie intervjuade 21 autistiska vuxna på djupet om deras erfarenheter av könsdysfori. Eftersom gruppen är liten och bygger på intervjuer beskriver den olika upplevelser, inte regler som gäller alla.

title: Examining the Relationship Between Sleep Quality, Social Functioning, and Behavior Problems in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Whelan S, Mannion A, Madden A, Berger F, Costello R, Ghadiri S, Leader G
abstract: Over forty percent of autistic children experience poor sleep quality, and social interaction difficulties are a core characteristic of autism. However, the relationship between sleep quality and social functioning and behavior remains poorly understood. This systematic review examined the evidence concerning the impact of sleep quality on the social functioning and behavior problems in autistic children and adolescents. It also identified key related factors and evaluated how this issue has been researched to date. Seven key journals were hand-searched and five databases were systematically searched, using keywords. Titles and abstracts of 4123 items were screened against eligibility criteria by two researchers. Relevant studies were retained if they were peer-reviewed empirical papers, published in English between 2000 and 2021. Then, the full text of 97 papers was screened and if they met the eligibility criteria, their reference lists were hand-searched. Forty-six studies were included in the final review. Data were systematically extracted and two authors critically appraised the strengths and weaknesses of studies using Critical Appraisal Skills Programme tools. Key themes were identified, because a meta-analysis was not possible due to the studies' heterogeneity. The review identified that sleep quality and social functioning are associated with one another and there is a small amount of evidence that a bi-directional causal relationship may exist. Evidence suggests that several nights of suboptimal sleep duration and a lack of deep continuous sleep negatively impact externalizing and internalizing behavior. Sleep quality is also reduced by anxiety and sensory sensitivity. However, longitudinal studies with larger samples are needed to establish causality. Future research needs to examine confounding factors and to develop consensus regarding best-practice processes for the objective measurement of sleep with autistic children. Additional research also needs to further examine the consequences of poor sleep quality on internalizing behavior, and the impact of socio-cultural practices.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista ha dormido mal varias noches, es razonable esperar más irritabilidad, tristeza o retraimiento al día siguiente, y ajustar las exigencias sociales. Observar qué afecta al sueño, como la ansiedad o la sensibilidad sensorial (luz, ruido, texturas), puede orientar cambios suaves en la rutina nocturna. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 46 estudios con niños y adolescentes autistas y encontró que sueño y vida social están relacionados, quizá en ambas direcciones. Sus límites: los estudios eran muy distintos entre sí, faltan seguimientos largos con muestras grandes y no se puede afirmar causa y efecto ni aplicarlo igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has slept poorly for several nights, it is reasonable to expect more irritability, sadness or withdrawal the next day, and to lighten social demands. Noticing what disrupts sleep, such as anxiety or sensory sensitivity (light, noise, textures), can guide gentle changes to the bedtime routine. This systematic review brought together 46 studies of autistic children and adolescents and found that sleep and social life are linked, possibly in both directions. Its limits: the studies differed widely, long-term studies with larger groups are lacking, and cause and effect cannot be confirmed or applied the same way to every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har sovit dåligt flera nätter är det rimligt att räkna med mer irritation, nedstämdhet eller tillbakadragenhet dagen efter, och att minska sociala krav. Att lägga märke till vad som stör sömnen, till exempel oro eller sensorisk känslighet (ljus, ljud, texturer), kan vägleda varsamma ändringar i kvällsrutinen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 46 studier med autistiska barn och ungdomar och fann att sömn och socialt liv hänger ihop, kanske i båda riktningarna. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, långa uppföljningar med större grupper saknas och orsak och verkan kan inte fastställas eller gälla lika för alla.

title: Evidence That Nine Autistic Women Out of Ten Have Been Victims of Sexual Violence.
authors: Cazalis F, Reyes E, Leduc S, Gourion D
abstract: Background Research indicates that sexual violence affects about 30% of women in the general population and between two to three times as much for autistic women. Materials and methods We investigated prevalence of sexual abuse, autistic traits and a range of symptoms, using an online survey addressed to the women of the French autistic community ( n = 225). We assessed victimization through an open question and through a specific questionnaire, derived from the Sexual Experiences Survey-Short Form Victimization. Results Both case identification methods yielded high figures: 68.9% victimization (open question) compared to 88.4% (standardized questionnaire). Two thirds of the victims were very young when they were first assaulted: among 199 victims, 135 were aged 18 or below and 112 participants were aged 15 or below. 75% of participants included in our study reported several aggressions. Analyses indicate that primo-victimization was highly correlated to revictimization and that being young increased that risk. Young victims were also at higher risk of developing post-traumatic stress disorder. A third of the victims reported the assault. 25% of those were able to file a complaint ( n = 12) and/or receive care ( n = 13). For the remainder 75%, reporting did not lead to action. Discussion Those findings indicate a very large proportion of victims of sexual assault among autistic women, consistently with previous research. The World Health Organization states unambiguously that sexual violence is systemic and that vulnerable individuals are preferably targeted by offenders. We therefore postulate that it would be erroneous to consider that victimization of autistic women is mainly due to autism. On the contrary, autism seems to be just a vulnerability factor. Some authors propose that educating potential victims to better protect themselves would help preventing abuse. We reviewed this proposition in the light of our results and found it to be impossible to apply since more than half of the victims were below or at the age of consent. Literature about sexual violence is discussed. Large-scale prevention programs proposed by World Health Organization and the Center for Disease Control aim at cultural changes in order to diminish gender inequality, that they identify as the very root of sexual violence.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una chica o mujer autista, crea desde hoy espacios tranquilos donde pueda contar cosas difíciles sin ser juzgada, y créela si lo hace. La responsabilidad es de los agresores y de los adultos que protegen, no de ella: enseñarle a «protegerse» no basta, sobre todo en la infancia. Si comparte algo, busca apoyo especializado y acompáñala en la denuncia. Evidencia: encuesta en línea con 225 mujeres de la comunidad autista francesa; casi nueve de cada diez describieron violencia sexual, a menudo antes de los 18 años. Límites: participación voluntaria por internet, sin grupo de comparación, así que las cifras pueden no representar a todas las mujeres autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic girl or woman, start building calm, regular moments where she can share difficult things without judgement, and believe her if she does. Responsibility lies with perpetrators and with protective adults, not with her: teaching her to 'protect herself' is not enough, especially in childhood. If she discloses something, seek specialist support and stand by her if she reports it. Evidence: an online survey of 225 women from the French autistic community; nearly nine in ten described sexual violence, often before age 18. Limits: voluntary online participation and no comparison group, so the figures may not reflect all autistic women.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk flicka eller kvinna, skapa redan i dag lugna, återkommande stunder där hon kan berätta svåra saker utan att dömas, och tro på henne om hon gör det. Ansvaret ligger hos förövarna och hos skyddande vuxna, inte hos henne: att lära henne ”skydda sig själv” räcker inte, särskilt i barndomen. Om hon berättar något, sök specialiserat stöd och stå vid hennes sida om hon anmäler. Evidens: en webbenkät med 225 kvinnor i den franska autistiska gemenskapen; nästan nio av tio beskrev sexuellt våld, ofta före 18 års ålder. Begränsningar: frivilligt deltagande via internet och ingen jämförelsegrupp, så siffrorna speglar kanske inte alla autistiska kvinnor.

title: Vitamin D: Before, during and after Pregnancy: Effect on Neonates and Children.
authors: Mansur JL, Oliveri B, Giacoia E, Fusaro D, Costanzo PR
abstract: A worldwide high prevalence of vitamin D (VD) deficiency has become of growing concern because of potential adverse effects on human health, including pregnant women and their offsprings. Beyond its classical function as a regulator of calcium and phosphate metabolism, together with its fundamental role in bone health in every stage of life, its deficiency has been associated to multiple adverse health effects. The classic effects of VD deficiency in pregnancy and neonates have been late hypocalcemia and nutritional rickets. Nevertheless, recent studies have linked VD to fertility and 25(OH)D with several clinical conditions in pregnancy: preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, higher incidence of cesarean section and preterm birth, while in infants, the clinical conditions are low birth weight, lower bone mass and possible relationship with the development of such diseases as bronchiolitis, asthma, type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis and autism included as VD non-classical actions. The supplementation with Vitamin D and achievement of optimal levels reduce maternal-fetal and newborn complications. Supplementation in children with VD deficiency reduces the risk of respiratory infections and possibly autoimmune diseases and autism. This review emphasizes the roles of Vitamin D deficiency and the consequences of intervention from preconception to infancy.

sheet.es: Si estás embarazada, planeas un embarazo o cuidas a un bebé, puede ser útil preguntar en tu centro de salud si conviene revisar los niveles de vitamina D; la decisión sobre suplementos corresponde al equipo sanitario. No hace falta cambiar nada en la rutina de un niño autista por este estudio: el autismo es una forma de ser, no algo que se deba a una falta de nutrientes. Se trata de una revisión narrativa que resume estudios sobre embarazo, recién nacidos e infancia. Sus límites: la relación con el autismo se basa en asociaciones, no demuestra causa y no se aplica igual a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy or caring for a baby, it may help to ask your health centre whether checking vitamin D levels makes sense; any decision about supplements belongs with your healthcare team. There is no need to change anything in an autistic child's routine because of this paper: autism is a way of being, not something caused simply by a missing nutrient. This is a narrative review summarising studies on pregnancy, newborns and childhood. Its limits: the link with autism rests on associations, does not prove cause, and does not apply equally to every family.
sheet.sv: Om du är gravid, planerar en graviditet eller tar hand om en bebis kan det vara bra att fråga vårdcentralen eller mödravården om det är rimligt att kontrollera D-vitaminnivåer; beslut om tillskott fattas tillsammans med vården. Du behöver inte ändra något i ett autistiskt barns vardag på grund av den här artikeln: autism är ett sätt att vara, inte något som bara beror på brist på ett näringsämne. Det är en översiktsartikel som sammanfattar studier om graviditet, nyfödda och barndom. Begränsningar: kopplingen till autism bygger på samband, bevisar inte orsak och gäller inte lika för alla familjer.

title: An Update on Psychopharmacological Treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Aishworiya R, Valica T, Hagerman R, Restrepo B
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
abstract: While behavioral interventions remain the mainstay of treatment of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), several potential targeted treatments addressing the underlying neurophysiology of ASD have emerged in the last few years. These are promising for the potential to, in future, become part of the mainstay treatment in addressing the core symptoms of ASD. Although it is likely that the development of future targeted treatments will be influenced by the underlying heterogeneity in etiology, associated genetic mechanisms influencing ASD are likely to be the first targets of treatments and even gene therapy in the future for ASD. In this article, we provide a review of current psychopharmacological treatment in ASD including those used to address common comorbidities of the condition and upcoming new targeted approaches in autism management. Medications including metformin, arbaclofen, cannabidiol, oxytocin, bumetanide, lovastatin, trofinetide, and dietary supplements including sulforophane and N-acetylcysteine are discussed. Commonly used medications to address the comorbidities associated with ASD including atypical antipsychotics, serotoninergic agents, alpha-2 agonists, and stimulant medications are also reviewed. Targeted treatments in Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most common genetic disorder leading to ASD, provide a model for new treatments that may be helpful for other forms of ASD.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas por medicamentos o suplementos que circulan en internet (como cannabidiol, oxitocina o bumetanida), lleva tus preguntas concretas al equipo médico en lugar de probarlos por tu cuenta. Muchos siguen en investigación. Los fármacos actuales suelen usarse para condiciones que acompañan al autismo, como ansiedad, dificultades de atención o sueño, no para cambiar a la persona autista. Observa y anota qué le resulta difícil a tu hijo o hija y qué le ayuda; eso guía mejor cualquier conversación. Esta es una revisión narrativa de estudios sobre fármacos y tratamientos dirigidos, incluido el síndrome X frágil. No aporta datos nuevos y muchos tratamientos tienen evidencia temprana o mixta.
sheet.en: If you are wondering about medications or supplements discussed online (such as cannabidiol, oxytocin or bumetanide), bring your specific questions to your medical team rather than trying them on your own. Many are still being researched. Current medications are mostly used for conditions that can come alongside autism, such as anxiety, attention or sleep difficulties, not to change who an autistic person is. Noting what feels hard for your child and what helps will guide any conversation better. This is a narrative review of studies on medications and targeted treatments, including Fragile X syndrome. It adds no new data, and evidence for many treatments is early or mixed.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar över läkemedel eller kosttillskott som diskuteras på nätet (till exempel cannabidiol, oxytocin eller bumetanid), ta med dina konkreta frågor till vårdteamet i stället för att prova på egen hand. Många är fortfarande under forskning. Dagens läkemedel används främst för tillstånd som kan finnas vid sidan av autism, som ångest, uppmärksamhets- eller sömnsvårigheter, inte för att förändra vem en autistisk person är. Att anteckna vad som är svårt för ditt barn och vad som hjälper gör samtalet mer givande. Detta är en narrativ översikt av studier om läkemedel och riktade behandlingar, bland annat vid fragilt X-syndrom. Den tillför inga nya data, och evidensen för många behandlingar är tidig eller blandad.

title: Autistic adults have poorer quality healthcare and worse health based on self-report data.
authors: Weir E, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Recent research suggests that autistic individuals have shorter lifespans and experience worse health (greater health burden) than non-autistic individuals. Small, qualitative studies suggest that autistic adults also experience poor self-reported healthcare quality. Methods An anonymized, cross-sectional, self-report questionnaire was administered to n = 4158 individuals. The study assessed prevalence of chronic health conditions, healthcare quality, differences in overall health inequality score, and effects of the coronavirus pandemic on healthcare quality. We used Fisher's exact tests, binomial logistic regression, and predictive machine learning tools, as appropriate. Results The final sample included n = 2649 participants (n = 1285 autistic) aged 16-96 years. Autistic adults reported lower quality healthcare than non-autistic adults across 50/51 items, including poorer access to healthcare and poorer communication, alongside increased anxiety, sensory sensitivity, system-level problems, shutdowns, and meltdowns. Differences between groups were stark: aggregated health inequality scores predicted autism diagnosis, even after stratifying by sex. Autistic adults were also more likely to have chronic health conditions than non-autistic adults. There were no significant differences in healthcare quality for autistic adults before and during the pandemic, although they received relatively poorer quality healthcare than non-autistic adults across both periods. Limitations The study's sampling methods are not likely to capture the perspectives of all autistic individuals, especially those with intellectual disability. Both the autistic and control samples are biased towards UK residents, white individuals, those assigned female at birth, and those who completed an undergraduate degree or higher education. As such, these results may limit their generalizability to other groups. Finally, these results relate to self-reported differences in healthcare quality between autistic and non-autistic adults. The observed group differences may in part reflect differences in perception and communication rather than differences in actual healthcare quality. Conclusions Autistic adults are more likely to have chronic health conditions alongside self-reported lower quality healthcare than others. Health inequalities between these groups are widespread and dramatic; unfortunately, they existed before and have persisted after the onset of the coronavirus pandemic.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta al médico, puede ayudar preparar juntos la cita: escribir antes los síntomas y preguntas, pedir citas a primera hora o en salas tranquilas, solicitar comunicación por escrito y avisar de necesidades sensoriales. Vale la pena revisar con calma su salud general, porque los problemas crónicos pueden pasar desapercibidos. Este estudio fue un cuestionario anónimo con 2649 adultos (1285 autistas), que describieron peor acceso, peor comunicación y más ansiedad y crisis en la atención sanitaria. Sus límites: son datos autoinformados, la mayoría eran mujeres británicas, blancas y con estudios universitarios, y apenas incluyó a personas con discapacidad intelectual.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult with healthcare, it can help to prepare appointments together: write down symptoms and questions beforehand, ask for early or quiet appointments, request written communication, and share sensory needs with staff. It is also worth calmly keeping an eye on overall health, since long-term conditions can be missed. This study was an anonymous questionnaire answered by 2,649 adults (1,285 autistic), who reported poorer access, poorer communication, and more anxiety, shutdowns and meltdowns around healthcare. Its limits: the data are self-reported, most participants were UK-based, white, female and university-educated, and few people with intellectual disability took part.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen i vården kan det hjälpa att förbereda besöken tillsammans: skriv ner symtom och frågor i förväg, be om tidiga eller lugna tider, be om skriftlig information och berätta om sensoriska behov. Det är också klokt att lugnt hålla koll på den allmänna hälsan, eftersom långvariga besvär kan missas. Studien var en anonym enkät med 2 649 vuxna (1 285 autistiska), som rapporterade sämre tillgång, sämre kommunikation och mer ångest, shutdowns och meltdowns i vården. Begränsningar: svaren är självrapporterade, de flesta var brittiska, vita kvinnor med universitetsutbildning, och få personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning deltog.

title: Genetics of glutamate and its receptors in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Nisar S, Bhat AA, Masoodi T, Hashem S, Akhtar S, Ali TA, Amjad S, Chawla S, Bagga P, Frenneaux MP, Reddy R, Fakhro K, Haris M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental impairment characterized by deficits in social interaction skills, impaired communication, and repetitive and restricted behaviors that are thought to be due to altered neurotransmission processes. The amino acid glutamate is an essential excitatory neurotransmitter in the human brain that regulates cognitive functions such as learning and memory, which are usually impaired in ASD. Over the last several years, increasing evidence from genetics, neuroimaging, protein expression, and animal model studies supporting the notion of altered glutamate metabolism has heightened the interest in evaluating glutamatergic dysfunction in ASD. Numerous pharmacological, behavioral, and imaging studies have demonstrated the imbalance in excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmitters, thus revealing the involvement of the glutamatergic system in ASD pathology. Here, we review the effects of genetic alterations on glutamate and its receptors in ASD and the role of non-invasive imaging modalities in detecting these changes. We also highlight the potential therapeutic targets associated with impaired glutamatergic pathways.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en el día a día: esta revisión trata de biología básica, no de pautas de crianza. Saber que el glutamato, un mensajero químico del cerebro, puede funcionar de forma distinta en algunas personas autistas ayuda a entender que las diferencias en percepción, aprendizaje o regulación tienen una base neurológica, no son falta de voluntad. Desconfía de productos o dietas que prometan «corregir el glutamato». Es una revisión narrativa que reúne estudios genéticos, de imagen cerebral y con animales. Su límite: no evalúa apoyos concretos, gran parte de la evidencia viene de modelos animales y no describe a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change tomorrow morning: this review is about basic biology, not parenting guidance. Knowing that glutamate, a chemical messenger in the brain, may work differently in some autistic people can help you see that differences in perception, learning or regulation have a neurological basis, not a lack of effort. Be cautious about products or diets claiming to "fix glutamate". This is a narrative review bringing together genetic, brain imaging and animal studies. Its limit: it does not test any practical support, much of the evidence comes from animal models, and it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras i morgon bitti: översikten handlar om grundläggande biologi, inte om råd i vardagen. Att glutamat, en kemisk budbärare i hjärnan, kan fungera annorlunda hos en del autistiska personer kan hjälpa dig se att skillnader i perception, inlärning eller reglering har en neurologisk grund och inte handlar om bristande vilja. Var försiktig med produkter eller dieter som lovar att "rätta till glutamatet". Det är en narrativ översikt som samlar genetiska studier, hjärnavbildning och djurstudier. Begränsning: den prövar inget konkret stöd, mycket bygger på djurmodeller och den beskriver inte varje autistisk person.

title: Sex Differences in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Diagnostic, Neurobiological, and Behavioral Features.
authors: Napolitano A, Schiavi S, La Rosa P, Rossi-Espagnet MC, Petrillo S, Bottino F, Tagliente E, Longo D, Lupi E, Casula L, Valeri G, Piemonte F, Trezza V, Vicari S
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder with a worldwide prevalence of about 1%, characterized by impairments in social interaction, communication, repetitive patterns of behaviors, and can be associated with hyper- or hypo-reactivity of sensory stimulation and cognitive disability. ASD comorbid features include internalizing and externalizing symptoms such as anxiety, depression, hyperactivity, and attention problems. The precise etiology of ASD is still unknown and it is undoubted that the disorder is linked to some extent to both genetic and environmental factors. It is also well-documented and known that one of the most striking and consistent finding in ASD is the higher prevalence in males compared to females, with around 70% of ASD cases described being males. The present review looked into the most significant studies that attempted to investigate differences in ASD males and females thus trying to shade some light on the peculiar characteristics of this prevalence in terms of diagnosis, imaging, major autistic-like behavior and sex-dependent uniqueness. The study also discussed sex differences found in animal models of ASD, to provide a possible explanation of the neurological mechanisms underpinning the different presentation of autistic symptoms in males and females.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña o mujer que podría ser autista, ten en cuenta que su autismo puede verse distinto: a veces menos evidente, con más camuflaje social, intereses que parecen «típicos» o más ansiedad interna. Si algo te preocupa, anota ejemplos concretos del día a día y compártelos con profesionales que conozcan estas diferencias. Esta revisión resume estudios sobre diferencias entre hombres y mujeres autistas en diagnóstico, imágenes cerebrales y comportamiento, incluidos modelos animales. Sus límites: no es un estudio nuevo con participantes, mezcla investigaciones muy diversas, usa un enfoque binario de sexo y no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support a girl or woman who might be autistic, keep in mind that her autism may look different: sometimes less obvious, with more social camouflaging, interests that seem 'typical', or more inner anxiety. If something concerns you, note concrete everyday examples and share them with professionals familiar with these differences. This review summarises studies on differences between autistic males and females in diagnosis, brain imaging and behaviour, including animal models. Its limits: it is not a new study with participants, it combines very varied research, it uses a binary view of sex, and it does not describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en flicka eller kvinna som kanske är autistisk, tänk på att hennes autism kan se annorlunda ut: ibland mindre tydlig, med mer socialt kamouflage, intressen som verkar ”typiska” eller mer inre oro. Om något bekymrar dig, skriv ner konkreta vardagsexempel och dela dem med yrkespersoner som känner till dessa skillnader. Denna översikt sammanfattar studier om skillnader mellan autistiska män och kvinnor i diagnos, hjärnavbildning och beteende, inklusive djurmodeller. Begränsningar: det är ingen ny studie med deltagare, den blandar mycket olika forskning, utgår från en binär syn på kön och beskriver inte varje individ.

title: Sleep, Sensory Integration/Processing, and Autism: A Scoping Review.
authors: Lane SJ, Leão MA, Spielmann V
abstract: The prevalence of sleep dysfunction is considerably higher in the autistic population than in the non-autistic. Similarly, the incidence of sensory reactivity differences in autism exceeds that in the neurotypical population. The basis of sleep disorders in autism is multifactorial, but sensory integration/processing concerns may play a role. Research that investigates this interplay for autistic individuals is limited but vital. In this scoping review, we examined literature addressing the following research question: What is the relationship between sleep and sensory integration/processing in autism? We included articles if they were peer-reviewed, English or Spanish, purposefully addressed sensory integration/processing differences, were sleep focused and included autism as the primary diagnosis or population. Articles were excluded if the language was not English or Spanish, research was conducted with animals, they were non-peer-reviewed, the primary population was not autistic, the sensory focus reflected a specific sensorineural loss (e.g., blindness, or deafness), there was not a clear inclusion of sensory integration/processing or sleep. We searched six databases and included all citations from the inception of each database through June 2021. The search strategy identified 397 documents that were reduced to 24 included articles after exclusion criteria were applied. The majority of studies we identified characterized the relation between sleep and sensory integration/processing differences in autism. Investigators found multiple sleep concerns such as bedtime resistance, sleep anxiety, delayed sleep onset, night awaking, and short sleep duration in autistic individuals. Identified sensory concerns focused on reactivity, finding hyper- and hypo-reactivity as well as sensory seeking across sensory domains. Co-existence of sleep concerns and sensory integration/processing differences was frequently reported. Few intervention studies showed a clear sensory focus; those that did emphasized pressure, movement, touch, and individual sensory preferences/needs. Swimming programs and massage showed promising results. No studies were of high quality. At a minimum, there is a co-existence of sensory reactivity differences and sleep concerns in autistic children, and possibly autistic adults. The relationship between poor sleep and sensory integration/processing differences is complex and multi-faceted, requiring additional research. Interventions that purposefully include a central sensory component have not been well studied in autistic children or adults. Overall studies with greater rigor and purposeful use of sensation and sensorimotor supports as a component of intervention are needed. This study was not funded.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija autista le cuesta dormirse o se despierta de noche, vale la pena mirar el entorno sensorial: luz, ruido, texturas de pijama y sábanas, temperatura. Observa qué le calma (presión firme, movimiento, tacto, un masaje suave) y qué le activa, y ajusta la rutina de la tarde según sus preferencias. Algunas familias notan ayuda con actividades como la natación durante el día. Esta revisión de alcance reunió 24 estudios, sobre todo con niños autistas, que a menudo encontraron dificultades de sueño y diferencias sensoriales juntas. Ningún estudio era de alta calidad y hay pocas pruebas sobre intervenciones, así que se trata de ideas para probar con calma, no de reglas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child struggles to fall asleep or wakes at night, it may help to look at the sensory side of bedtime: light, noise, pyjama and bedding textures, temperature. Notice what calms them (firm pressure, movement, touch, gentle massage) and what winds them up, and shape the evening routine around their own preferences. Some families find daytime activities like swimming helpful. This scoping review gathered 24 studies, mostly with autistic children, which often found sleep difficulties and sensory differences occurring together. None of the studies were high quality and evidence on interventions is thin, so treat these as ideas to try gently, not rules for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har svårt att somna eller vaknar på natten kan det vara värt att se över sinnesintrycken vid läggdags: ljus, ljud, pyjamasens och sängklädernas material, temperatur. Lägg märke till vad som lugnar (fast tryck, rörelse, beröring, mjuk massage) och vad som väcker upp, och forma kvällsrutinen efter barnets egna preferenser. Vissa familjer upplever att aktiviteter som simning under dagen hjälper. Den här översikten samlade 24 studier, mest med autistiska barn, som ofta fann sömnsvårigheter och sensoriska skillnader samtidigt. Ingen studie höll hög kvalitet och underlaget om insatser är tunt, så se det som idéer att pröva varsamt, inte regler för alla.

title: Population-Based Psychiatric Comorbidity in Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis.
authors: Mutluer T, Aslan Genç H, Özcan Morey A, Yapici Eser H, Ertinmaz B, Can M, Munir K
abstract: Psychiatric comorbidity in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a subject of critical scientific importance, affecting the quality of life, prognosis, and functional outcomes. The prevalence of psychiatric disorders vary considerably according to variables such as index subject characteristics, study setting, sampling frame, diagnostic methods used, as well as country of geographic origin. To date, most studies comprise clinical or treatment referral samples in tertiary care or subjects enrolled in clinical trials and genetic cohort collections. Such samples carry the potential for overestimation of both the frequency and severity of psychiatric comorbidity. A systematic literature search was performed using PubMed and Web of Science databases restricted to population-based study publications in the English between May 1, 2015, and May 31, 2020. A comprehensive keyword list was generated to investigate co-occurrence of psychiatric disorders in children and adolescents with ASD. A wide range of DSM-5 based disorders such as anxiety, mood, ADHD, intellectual disability/intellectual developmental disorder, eating/feeding, gender dysphoria and sleep-wake disorders were assessed. Initial search revealed a total of 1674 articles after removal of duplicates. Two independent researchers conducted a parallel-blinded screening process to identify the eligible studies based on titles and abstracts; 39 studies were analyzed in the current review. The main findings show prevalence estimates of 22.9% (95% CI: 17.7- 29.2) for intellectual disability; 26.2% (22-31) for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder; 11.1% (8.6-14.1) for anxiety disorders; 19.7% (11.9-30.7) for sleep disorders; 7% (5.2- 9.3) for disruptive disorders; 2% (1.3- 3.1) for bipolar disorders; 2.7% (1.8- 4.2) for depression; 1.8% (0.4-8.7) for obsessive-compulsive disorder; and 0.6% (0.3-1.1) for psychosis. Psychiatric comorbidity in population-based studies is lower than in clinical and referred samples. However, our results also indicate that the frequency of psychiatric comorbidity in children and adolescents with ASD in the population context is considerable, without the influence of referral bias implicit in clinical and treatment samples. There is a need for better targeted diagnostic tools to detect psychiatric comorbidity in children and youth in future population-based studies, as an essential component in providing care as well as new insights into the nature and mechanisms of its underlying associations. Systematic review registration [https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/], identifier [CRD42021234464].

sheet.es: Muchos niños y adolescentes autistas viven también con otras condiciones, como TDAH (alrededor de 1 de cada 4), discapacidad intelectual, dificultades de sueño (cerca de 1 de cada 5) o ansiedad. Si notas cambios en el sueño, la atención o el ánimo, vale la pena anotarlos y comentarlos con el equipo de salud, sin asumir que "todo es por el autismo". Este metaanálisis reunió 39 estudios poblacionales (2015-2020) con niños y jóvenes autistas de la comunidad general, no solo de clínicas. Limitaciones: los estudios usaron métodos y países distintos, solo se incluyeron publicaciones en inglés, y las cifras son promedios que no predicen lo que vivirá tu hijo o hija.
sheet.en: Many autistic children and teens also live with other conditions, such as ADHD (about 1 in 4), intellectual disability, sleep difficulties (around 1 in 5) or anxiety. If you notice changes in sleep, attention or mood, it is worth writing them down and raising them with your health team, rather than assuming "it's just the autism". This meta-analysis pooled 39 population-based studies (2015-2020) of autistic children and young people from the general community, not only clinic samples. Limits: the studies used different methods and countries, only English-language papers were included, and the figures are averages that cannot predict your own child's experience.
sheet.sv: Många autistiska barn och tonåringar har också andra tillstånd, till exempel ADHD (ungefär 1 av 4), intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, sömnsvårigheter (omkring 1 av 5) eller ångest. Om du märker förändringar i sömn, uppmärksamhet eller humör kan det vara bra att skriva ner dem och ta upp dem med vården, i stället för att anta att "det bara är autismen". Denna metaanalys sammanställde 39 befolkningsbaserade studier (2015–2020) med autistiska barn och unga ur den allmänna befolkningen, inte bara klinikgrupper. Begränsningar: studierna använde olika metoder och kom från olika länder, bara engelskspråkiga artiklar togs med, och siffrorna är genomsnitt som inte förutsäger just ditt barns situation.

title: Reconsidering animal models used to study autism spectrum disorder: Current state and optimizing future.
authors: Silverman JL, Thurm A, Ethridge SB, Soller MM, Petkova SP, Abel T, Bauman MD, Brodkin ES, Harony-Nicolas H, Wöhr M, Halladay A
abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID), are pervasive, often lifelong disorders, lacking evidence-based interventions for core symptoms. With no established biological markers, diagnoses are defined by behavioral criteria. Thus, preclinical in vivo animal models of NDDs must be optimally utilized. For this reason, experts in the field of behavioral neuroscience convened a workshop with the goals of reviewing current behavioral studies, reports, and assessments in rodent models. Goals included: (a) identifying the maximal utility and limitations of behavior in animal models with construct validity; (b) providing recommendations for phenotyping animal models; and (c) guidelines on how in vivo models should be used and reported reliably and rigorously while acknowledging their limitations. We concluded by recommending minimal criteria for reporting in manuscripts going forward. The workshop elucidated a consensus of potential solutions to several problems, including revisiting claims made about animal model links to ASD (and related conditions). Specific conclusions included: mice (or other rodent or preclinical models) are models of the neurodevelopmental insult, not specifically any disorder (e.g., ASD); a model that perfectly recapitulates a disorder such as ASD is untenable; and greater attention needs be given to validation of behavioral testing methods, data analysis, and critical interpretation.

sheet.es: Si lees titulares que dicen que un ratón «tiene autismo» o que un hallazgo en animales explica a tu hijo o hija, puedes tomarlos con calma: esta revisión concluye que los roedores modelan cambios biológicos en el desarrollo, no el autismo en sí, y que ningún animal puede reproducir la experiencia autista. Para decisiones diarias, sigue guiándote por lo que la persona autista comunica y necesita. Se trata de una revisión de consenso de expertos en neurociencia del comportamiento, basada en estudios con roedores. Su límite: no estudió a personas ni ofrece apoyos prácticos; orienta sobre cómo investigar e informar mejor.
sheet.en: If you see headlines claiming a mouse "has autism" or that an animal finding explains your child, you can read them calmly: this review concludes that rodents model biological changes in development, not autism itself, and that no animal can recreate autistic experience. For everyday decisions, keep following what the autistic person communicates and needs. This is a consensus review from a workshop of behavioural neuroscience experts, drawing on rodent studies. Its limit: it did not study people or offer practical supports; it guides how research should be done and reported more carefully.
sheet.sv: Om du ser rubriker om att en mus "har autism" eller att ett djurfynd förklarar ditt barn kan du läsa dem lugnt: den här översikten konstaterar att gnagare modellerar biologiska förändringar i utvecklingen, inte autism i sig, och att inget djur kan återskapa autistisk upplevelse. I vardagens beslut, fortsätt utgå från vad den autistiska personen kommunicerar och behöver. Det är en konsensusöversikt från en workshop med experter inom beteendeneurovetenskap, baserad på studier av gnagare. Begränsning: den studerade inga människor och ger inget praktiskt stöd; den vägleder hur forskning bör göras och rapporteras noggrannare.

title: In Our Own Words: The Complex Sensory Experiences of Autistic Adults.
authors: MacLennan K, O'Brien S, Tavassoli T
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic adults commonly experience sensory reactivity differences. Sensory hyperreactivity is frequently researched, whilst hyporeactivity and seeking, and experiences across domains, e.g., vision, are often neglected. Therefore, we aimed to understand more about the sensory experiences of autistic adults. We conducted a mixed-methods study, co-produced with stakeholders; recruiting 49 autistic adults who completed an online survey. Firstly, quantitative results and content analysis enhanced our understanding of sensory input/contexts associated with sensory hyperreactivity, hyporeactivity, and seeking across modalities. Secondly, thematic analysis developed themes relating to 'Outcomes', 'Control', 'Tolerance and management', and 'The role of other people', informing a theoretical model of sensory reactivity differences in autistic adults. These findings have implications for support services and improving quality of life for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Pregunte a la persona autista qué sensaciones le abruman, cuáles apenas nota y cuáles busca porque le hacen bien; las tres cosas pueden darse a la vez y cambiar según el lugar y el día. Ofrezca control: poder salir, bajar la luz o usar auriculares. Su actitud también cuenta: comprender sin juzgar facilita la tolerancia. Es un estudio de métodos mixtos, diseñado junto a personas implicadas, con una encuesta en línea a 49 adultos autistas que describieron sus experiencias con sus propias palabras. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña, solo incluye a quienes podían responder en línea y no se aplica igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person which sensations overwhelm them, which they barely notice, and which they seek out because they feel good; all three can exist together and shift with place and day. Offer control: a way to leave, dimmer lights, headphones. Your attitude matters too: understanding without judgement makes things easier to tolerate. This was a mixed-methods study, co-produced with stakeholders, using an online survey of 49 autistic adults who described their experiences in their own words. Limits: the sample is small, includes only people able to respond online, and the findings will not fit every person the same way.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen vilka sinnesintryck som blir för mycket, vilka hen knappt märker och vilka hen söker för att de känns bra; alla tre kan finnas samtidigt och variera med plats och dag. Erbjud kontroll: möjlighet att gå undan, dämpat ljus, hörlurar. Ditt bemötande spelar också roll: förståelse utan dömande gör det lättare att hantera. Studien använde blandade metoder, togs fram tillsammans med berörda och byggde på en webbenkät där 49 autistiska vuxna beskrev sina upplevelser med egna ord. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet, omfattar bara de som kunde svara digitalt, och resultaten passar inte alla på samma sätt.

title: The use of social robots with children and young people on the autism spectrum: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kouroupa A, Laws KR, Irvine K, Mengoni SE, Baird A, Sharma S
abstract: Background Robot-mediated interventions show promise in supporting the development of children on the autism spectrum. Objectives In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we summarize key features of available evidence on robot-interventions for children and young people on the autism spectrum aged up to 18 years old, as well as consider their efficacy for specific domains of learning.
