Data sources PubMed, Scopus, EBSCOhost, Google Scholar, Cochrane Library, ACM Digital Library, and IEEE Xplore. Grey literature was also searched using PsycExtra, OpenGrey, British Library EThOS, and the British Library Catalogue. Databases were searched from inception until April (6th) 2021. Synthesis methods Searches undertaken across seven databases yielded 2145 articles. Forty studies met our review inclusion criteria of which 17 were randomized control trials. The methodological quality of studies was conducted with the Quality Assessment Tool for Quantitative Studies. A narrative synthesis summarised the findings. A meta-analysis was conducted with 12 RCTs. Results Most interventions used humanoid (67%) robotic platforms, were predominantly based in clinics (37%) followed home, schools and laboratory (17% respectively) environments and targeted at improving social and communication skills (77%). Focusing on the most common outcomes, a random effects meta-analysis of RCTs showed that robot-mediated interventions significantly improved social functioning (g = 0.35 [95%CI 0.09 to 0.61; k = 7). By contrast, robots did not improve emotional (g = 0.63 [95%CI -1.43 to 2.69]; k = 2) or motor outcomes (g = -0.10 [95%CI -1.08 to 0.89]; k = 3), but the numbers of trials were very small. Meta-regression revealed that age accounted for almost one-third of the variance in effect sizes, with greater benefits being found in younger children. Conclusions Overall, our findings support the use of robot-mediated interventions for autistic children and youth, and we propose several recommendations for future research to aid learning and enhance implementation in everyday settings. Prospero registration Our methods were preregistered in the PROSPERO database (CRD42019148981).

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija muestra interés por la tecnología, un robot social usado en terapia o en la escuela podría ser una forma más predecible y cómoda de practicar la interacción, sobre todo en edades tempranas. No es imprescindible: observa si lo disfruta y respeta su ritmo y sus formas propias de comunicarse. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 40 estudios con niños y jóvenes autistas de hasta 18 años; un metaanálisis de 12 ensayos aleatorizados encontró una mejora moderada en lo social, mayor en los más pequeños. Sus límites: pocos ensayos, muestras pequeñas y casi ningún dato sobre emociones, motricidad o la vida cotidiana fuera de la clínica.
sheet.en: If your child is drawn to technology, a social robot used in therapy or at school might offer a more predictable, comfortable way to practise interaction, especially for younger children. It is not essential: notice whether they enjoy it, and respect their pace and their own ways of communicating. This systematic review pooled 40 studies with autistic children and young people up to 18; a meta-analysis of 12 randomised trials found a modest benefit for social outcomes, larger in younger children. Its limits: few trials, small samples, and very little evidence on emotional or motor outcomes or on everyday life outside clinics.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn dras till teknik kan en social robot i terapi eller skola vara ett mer förutsägbart och bekvämt sätt att öva samspel, särskilt för yngre barn. Det är inget måste: lägg märke till om barnet tycker om det, och respektera barnets tempo och egna sätt att kommunicera. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 40 studier med autistiska barn och unga upp till 18 år; en metaanalys av 12 randomiserade studier visade en måttlig förbättring av sociala förmågor, större hos yngre barn. Begränsningar: få studier, små grupper och mycket lite kunskap om känslor, motorik eller vardagen utanför kliniken.

title: The global prevalence of autism spectrum disorder: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Salari N, Rasoulpoor S, Rasoulpoor S, Shohaimi S, Jafarpour S, Abdoli N, Khaledi-Paveh B, Mohammadi M
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is one of the serious developmental disorders that is usually diagnosed below the age of three years. Although the severity of the disease's symptoms varies from patient to patient, the ability to communicate with others is affected in all forms of ASD. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of ASD in high-risk groups by continent. Methods The present study was conducted by systematic review and meta-analysis from 2008 to July 2021. Databases such as Science Direct, PubMed, Scopus, SID, Magiran, Web of Science (WoS), and Google Scholar from 2008 to July 2021 were searched to find related studies. Data were analysed using Comprehensive Meta-Analysis software (Version 2). Results A total of 74 studies with 30,212,757 participants were included in this study. The prevalence of ASD in the world was 0.6% (95% confidence interval: 0.4-1%). Subgroup analyses indicated that the prevalence of ASD in Asia, America, Europe, Africa and Australia was 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1-1), 1% (95% CI: 0.8-1.1), 0.5% (95% CI: 0.2-1), 1% (95% CI: 0.3-3.1), 1.7% (95% CI: 0.5-6.1) respectively. Conclusion ASD imposes a heavy health burden on communities around the world. Early detection of ASD can reduce the incidence of developmental disorders and improve patients' communication skills. Therefore, health policymakers need to be aware of the prevalence and increasing trend of ASD to implement appropriate planning and interventions to reduce its consequences.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija es autista, no estáis solos: este análisis estima que alrededor de 6 de cada 1.000 personas en el mundo son autistas, con cifras distintas según el continente. Puede ayudarte a pedir apoyos con calma: el autismo es frecuente y los servicios deberían estar preparados. Si notas diferencias en la comunicación o el desarrollo, consultar pronto puede abrir puertas a apoyos útiles. Se trata de un metaanálisis de 74 estudios publicados entre 2008 y 2021, con más de 30 millones de participantes. Sus límites: los estudios usaron métodos muy diferentes, las cifras regionales son inciertas y el lenguaje del artículo trata el autismo como enfermedad, algo que no refleja la experiencia de muchas personas autistas.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic, you are not alone: this analysis estimates that about 6 in every 1,000 people worldwide are autistic, with figures varying by continent. It can help you ask for support calmly: autism is common, and services should be ready for it. If you notice differences in communication or development, seeking an assessment early can open the door to useful support. This is a meta-analysis of 74 studies published between 2008 and 2021, covering over 30 million participants. Its limits: the studies used very different methods, regional figures are uncertain, and the paper frames autism as a disease, which does not reflect many autistic people's experience.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt är ni inte ensamma: den här analysen uppskattar att ungefär 6 av 1 000 människor i världen är autistiska, med olika siffror beroende på kontinent. Det kan hjälpa dig att lugnt be om stöd: autism är vanligt och verksamheter borde vara förberedda. Om du märker skillnader i kommunikation eller utveckling kan en tidig utredning öppna dörrar till användbart stöd. Detta är en metaanalys av 74 studier publicerade 2008–2021, med över 30 miljoner deltagare. Begränsningar: studierna använde mycket olika metoder, de regionala siffrorna är osäkra och artikeln beskriver autism som en sjukdom, vilket inte speglar många autistiska personers erfarenhet.

title: Signalling pathways in autism spectrum disorder: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
authors: Jiang CC, Lin LS, Long S, Ke XY, Fukunaga K, Lu YM, Han F
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a prevalent and complex neurodevelopmental disorder which has strong genetic basis. Despite the rapidly rising incidence of autism, little is known about its aetiology, risk factors, and disease progression. There are currently neither validated biomarkers for diagnostic screening nor specific medication for autism. Over the last two decades, there have been remarkable advances in genetics, with hundreds of genes identified and validated as being associated with a high risk for autism. The convergence of neuroscience methods is becoming more widely recognized for its significance in elucidating the pathological mechanisms of autism. Efforts have been devoted to exploring the behavioural functions, key pathological mechanisms and potential treatments of autism. Here, as we highlight in this review, emerging evidence shows that signal transduction molecular events are involved in pathological processes such as transcription, translation, synaptic transmission, epigenetics and immunoinflammatory responses. This involvement has important implications for the discovery of precise molecular targets for autism. Moreover, we review recent insights into the mechanisms and clinical implications of signal transduction in autism from molecular, cellular, neural circuit, and neurobehavioural aspects. Finally, the challenges and future perspectives are discussed with regard to novel strategies predicated on the biological features of autism.

sheet.es: Para mañana, nada cambia en la vida diaria: esta revisión trata de biología básica, no de pautas de apoyo. Si alguien le ofrece un «tratamiento dirigido» basado en genes o vías moleculares del autismo, conviene preguntar con calma qué pruebas reales tiene en personas, porque hoy no existe un medicamento específico ni un biomarcador validado para el autismo. Lo útil sigue siendo observar qué ayuda a su familiar y respetar su forma de ser. Se trata de una revisión narrativa de estudios genéticos, celulares y en animales, sin participantes propios. Su límite: gran parte proviene de laboratorio y modelos animales, y no muestra beneficios prácticos comprobados en personas autistas.
sheet.en: For tomorrow, nothing changes in daily life: this review is about basic biology, not support strategies. If someone offers a "targeted treatment" based on autism genes or molecular pathways, it is reasonable to calmly ask what real evidence exists in people, because there is currently no specific medication or validated biomarker for autism. What remains useful is noticing what helps your family member and respecting who they are. This is a narrative review of genetic, cellular and animal research, with no participants of its own. Its limit: much of the work comes from laboratories and animal models, and it shows no proven practical benefits for autistic people.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon förändras ingenting i vardagen: den här översikten handlar om grundläggande biologi, inte om stödstrategier. Om någon erbjuder en ”riktad behandling” baserad på autismgener eller molekylära signalvägar är det rimligt att lugnt fråga vilka verkliga belägg som finns hos människor, eftersom det i dag inte finns något specifikt läkemedel eller validerad biomarkör för autism. Det som fortfarande hjälper är att märka vad som fungerar för din närstående och respektera hen som person. Detta är en narrativ översikt av genetisk, cellulär och djurbaserad forskning, utan egna deltagare. Begränsning: mycket bygger på laboratorie- och djurmodeller och visar inga bevisade praktiska fördelar för autistiska personer.

title: Camouflaging Intent, First Impressions, and Age of ASC Diagnosis in Autistic Men and Women.
authors: Belcher HL, Morein-Zamir S, Mandy W, Ford RM
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Camouflaging of autistic traits may make autism harder to diagnose. The current study evaluated the relations between camouflaging intent, first impressions, and age of autism diagnosis. Participants comprised autistic and non-autistic adults (n = 80, 50% female) who completed the Camouflaging of Autistic Traits Questionnaire. They were later video-recorded having a conversation with a person unaware of their diagnostic status. Ten-second clips from half these videos were later shown to 127 non-autistic peers, who rated their first impressions of each participant. Results showed that autistic participants were rated more poorly on first impressions, males were rated less favourably than females, and male raters were particularly harsh in their evaluations of autistic males. Camouflaging intent did not predict first impressions but better first impressions were linked with a later age of diagnosis.

sheet.es: Si a una persona autista, sobre todo una mujer, se la percibe «bien» en un primer encuentro, eso no significa que no necesite apoyo ni evaluación. Las impresiones rápidas favorables pueden retrasar el diagnóstico; vale la pena escuchar cómo la persona describe su propia experiencia, más allá de cómo parece por fuera. También conviene recordar que los juicios rápidos de otras personas reflejan sus prejuicios, no el valor de nadie. Evidencia: estudio con 80 adultos autistas y no autistas, cuyos vídeos breves fueron valorados por 127 personas no autistas. Límites: muestra pequeña, clips de diez segundos y una sola conversación; no se aplica igual a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person, especially a woman, comes across as 'fine' at a first meeting, that does not mean they need no support or assessment. Favourable quick impressions may delay diagnosis, so it helps to listen to how the person describes their own experience, not just how they appear. It is also worth remembering that others' snap judgements reflect their biases, not anyone's worth. Evidence: a study of 80 autistic and non-autistic adults whose short video clips were rated by 127 non-autistic peers. Limits: small sample, ten-second clips and a single conversation; it does not apply the same way to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person, särskilt en kvinna, verkar ”klara sig bra” vid ett första möte betyder det inte att hen inte behöver stöd eller utredning. Positiva snabba intryck kan fördröja diagnos, så lyssna på hur personen själv beskriver sin upplevelse, inte bara hur hen verkar utåt. Kom också ihåg att andras snabba omdömen speglar deras fördomar, inte någons värde. Evidens: en studie med 80 autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna vars korta videoklipp bedömdes av 127 icke-autistiska jämnåriga. Begränsningar: litet urval, tiosekundersklipp och ett enda samtal; resultaten gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

title: Autism Through the Ages: A Mixed Methods Approach to Understanding How Age and Age of Diagnosis Affect Quality of Life.
authors: Atherton G, Edisbury E, Piovesan A, Cross L
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: A significant proportion of autistic adults today were not diagnosed until later in life, a group referred to as the 'lost generation,' which may affect mental health. In Study 1 we explored quality of life and autistic trait levels in 420 autistic and TD adults, and in Study 2 we explored the experiences of 8 autistic adults diagnosed as adults. We found that autistic adults had lower quality of life outcomes and higher autistic trait levels which related to age of diagnosis, and qualitative findings indicated that while adults were empowered by their new diagnosis, they still require specialized supports. Our findings are discussed, emphasizing future directions and implications for the current care system in place for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si usted acompaña a un adulto que recibió su diagnóstico de autismo tarde, el diagnóstico puede traer alivio y una nueva comprensión de sí mismo, pero no sustituye a los apoyos. Mañana puede preguntarle con calma qué le resulta difícil ahora y qué ayudas concretas (salud mental, trabajo, vida diaria) le gustaría buscar. En este estudio, 420 adultos autistas y no autistas respondieron cuestionarios, y 8 adultos diagnosticados en la adultez compartieron sus experiencias en entrevistas; un diagnóstico más tardío se relacionó con menor calidad de vida. Es un estudio transversal con un grupo cualitativo pequeño: muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no describe la experiencia de cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an adult who was diagnosed as autistic later in life, the diagnosis may bring relief and a new understanding of themselves, but it does not replace support. Tomorrow you could calmly ask what feels hard right now and which concrete help (mental health, work, daily life) they would like to look for. In this study, 420 autistic and non-autistic adults completed questionnaires, and 8 adults diagnosed in adulthood shared their experiences in interviews; a later diagnosis was linked to lower quality of life. It is a cross-sectional study with a small qualitative group: it shows associations, not causes, and does not describe every person's experience.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en vuxen som fick sin autismdiagnos sent i livet kan diagnosen ge lättnad och en ny förståelse av sig själv, men den ersätter inte stöd. I morgon kan du lugnt fråga vad som känns svårt just nu och vilken konkret hjälp (psykisk hälsa, arbete, vardag) personen vill söka. I studien besvarade 420 autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna enkäter, och 8 vuxna som fått diagnos i vuxen ålder berättade om sina erfarenheter i intervjuer; senare diagnos hängde ihop med lägre livskvalitet. Det är en tvärsnittsstudie med en liten kvalitativ grupp: den visar samband, inte orsaker, och beskriver inte alla personers upplevelser.

title: Annual Research Review: Shifting from 'normal science' to neurodiversity in autism science.
authors: Pellicano E, den Houting J
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Since its initial description, the concept of autism has been firmly rooted within the conventional medical paradigm of child psychiatry. Increasingly, there have been calls from the autistic community and, more recently, nonautistic researchers, to rethink the way in which autism science is framed and conducted. Neurodiversity, where autism is seen as one form of variation within a diversity of minds, has been proposed as a potential alternative paradigm. In this review, we concentrate on three major challenges to the conventional medical paradigm - an overfocus on deficits, an emphasis on the individual as opposed to their broader context and a narrowness of perspective - each of which necessarily constrains what we can know about autism and how we are able to know it. We then outline the ways in which fundamental elements of the neurodiversity paradigm can potentially help researchers respond to the medical model's limitations. We conclude by considering the implications of a shift towards the neurodiversity paradigm for autism science.

sheet.es: Una idea práctica para mañana: además de fijarte en lo que a tu hijo o familiar le cuesta, anota también sus fortalezas, intereses y qué cambios en el entorno (ruido, horarios, expectativas) le ayudan. Pregúntale, de la forma que mejor comunique, qué necesita. Esta revisión de investigación, escrita con participación de personas autistas, analiza cómo la ciencia del autismo se ha centrado demasiado en déficits, en el individuo y en una sola perspectiva, y propone el paradigma de la neurodiversidad. Es un artículo de reflexión, no un estudio con participantes ni datos nuevos, así que no ofrece técnicas probadas que funcionen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: A practical idea for tomorrow: alongside noticing what is hard for your child or family member, also write down their strengths, interests and which changes in their surroundings (noise, routines, expectations) help them. Ask them, in whatever way they communicate best, what they need. This research review, written with involvement of autistic people, examines how autism science has focused too much on deficits, on the individual rather than their context, and on a narrow perspective, and it proposes the neurodiversity paradigm instead. It is a reflective paper, not a study with participants or new data, so it does not offer tested techniques that work for every person.
sheet.sv: En praktisk idé för i morgon: lägg märke till vad som är svårt för ditt barn eller din närstående, men skriv också ner styrkor, intressen och vilka förändringar i omgivningen (ljud, rutiner, förväntningar) som hjälper. Fråga personen, på det sätt hen kommunicerar bäst, vad hen behöver. Den här forskningsöversikten, skriven med medverkan av autistiska personer, granskar hur autismforskningen fokuserat för mycket på brister, på individen snarare än sammanhanget och på ett snävt perspektiv, och föreslår neurodiversitetsparadigmet. Det är en reflekterande artikel, inte en studie med deltagare eller nya data, så den ger inga beprövade metoder som passar alla.

title: Parallel age-related cognitive effects in autism: A cross-sectional replication study.
authors: Torenvliet C, Groenman AP, Radhoe TA, Agelink van Rentergem JA, Van der Putten WJ, Geurts HM
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Findings on age-related cognitive effects in autism in adulthood are inconsistent across studies. As these studies substantially differ in their methodology, replication studies are needed. In this replication study frequentist (i.e., null-hypothesis significance testing), and Bayesian statistics were used to investigate the hypothesis that in autistic adults compared to non-autistic adults mostly parallel, but also protective age-related cognitive effects can be observed. Participants were 88 autistic adults, and 88 non-autistic matched comparisons (age range: 30-89 years, mean age: 55 years). Cognitive measures were administered on the following six domains: verbal memory, visual memory, working memory, Theory of Mind (ToM), verbal fluency, and processing speed, and self-reported cognitive failures. Non-autistic adults outperformed autistic adults on ToM, verbal fluency, and verbal memory, but only the first two were confirmed with Bayesian replication analyses. Also, more cognitive failures were reported by autistic adults. No interactions between group and age were observed, suggesting a parallel age-related effect on all cognitive domains. In sum, previously observed difficulties in ToM and verbal fluency were replicated which seem to persist at older age. Previously reported parallel age-related cognitive patterns were replicated, yet no evidence for protective age-related patterns was found. LAY SUMMARY: We investigated whether our previous findings on cognitive aging in autism could be confirmed in a new study measuring the cognitive effects of age in autistic and non-autistic adults. As expected, tasks that younger autistic adults had difficulties with (theory of mind, fluency) were also difficult for older autistic adults, and the effect of age itself was similar in autistic and non-autistic adults. Unexpectedly, we observed no protective effects (less cognitive aging) in autism.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta o mayor, este estudio sugiere que el envejecimiento cognitivo suele seguir un ritmo parecido al de personas no autistas: no hay señales de un deterioro más rápido. Algunas diferencias, como en tareas de comprensión de lo que piensan otros o de fluidez verbal, pueden mantenerse con la edad, así que conviene seguir ofreciendo tiempo extra, instrucciones claras y apoyos escritos. Tomarse en serio los despistes cotidianos que la persona describe también ayuda. Fue un estudio transversal de replicación con 88 adultos autistas y 88 no autistas de 30 a 89 años. Limitación: midió a cada persona una sola vez, por lo que no sigue cambios individuales a lo largo del tiempo.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult who is getting older, this study suggests cognitive ageing tends to follow a similar pace to non-autistic people, with no sign of faster decline. Some differences, such as in tasks about understanding others' thoughts or verbal fluency, may persist with age, so continuing to offer extra time, clear instructions and written supports makes sense. Taking the everyday slips the person describes seriously also helps. This was a cross-sectional replication study with 88 autistic and 88 non-autistic adults aged 30 to 89. Limitation: each person was measured only once, so it cannot track how individuals change over time.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen som blir äldre tyder studien på att det kognitiva åldrandet ofta sker i liknande takt som hos icke-autistiska personer, utan tecken på snabbare försämring. Vissa skillnader, till exempel i uppgifter om att förstå andras tankar eller verbalt flöde, kan finnas kvar med åldern, så det är klokt att fortsätta ge extra tid, tydliga instruktioner och skriftligt stöd. Att ta personens egna beskrivningar av vardagliga missar på allvar hjälper också. Det var en tvärsnittsstudie som upprepade tidigare forskning, med 88 autistiska och 88 icke-autistiska vuxna i åldern 30–89 år. Begränsning: varje person mättes bara en gång, så förändringar hos individen över tid följdes inte.

title: Global prevalence of autism: A systematic review update.
authors: Zeidan J, Fombonne E, Scorah J, Ibrahim A, Durkin MS, Saxena S, Yusuf A, Shih A, Elsabbagh M
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Prevalence estimates of autism are essential for informing public policy, raising awareness, and developing research priorities. Using a systematic review, we synthesized estimates of the prevalence of autism worldwide. We examined factors accounting for variability in estimates and critically reviewed evidence relevant for hypotheses about biological or social determinants (viz., biological sex, sociodemographic status, ethnicity/race, and nativity) potentially modifying prevalence estimates of autism. We performed the search in November 2021 within Medline for studies estimating autism prevalence, published since our last systematic review in 2012. Data were extracted by two independent researchers. Since 2012, 99 estimates from 71 studies were published indicating a global autism prevalence that ranges within and across regions, with a median prevalence of 100/10,000 (range: 1.09/10,000 to 436.0/10,000). The median male-to-female ratio was 4.2. The median percentage of autism cases with co-occurring intellectual disability was 33.0%. Estimates varied, likely reflecting complex and dynamic interactions between patterns of community awareness, service capacity, help seeking, and sociodemographic factors. A limitation of this review is that synthesizing methodological features precludes a quality appraisal of studies. Our findings reveal an increase in measured autism prevalence globally, reflecting the combined effects of multiple factors including the increase in community awareness and public health response globally, progress in case identification and definition, and an increase in community capacity. Hypotheses linking factors that increase the likelihood of developing autism with variations in prevalence will require research with large, representative samples and comparable autism diagnostic criteria and case-finding methods in diverse world regions over time. LAY SUMMARY: We reviewed studies of the prevalence of autism worldwide, considering the impact of geographic, ethnic, and socioeconomic factors on prevalence estimates. Approximately 1/100 children are diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder around the world. Prevalence estimates increased over time and varied greatly within and across sociodemographic groups. These findings reflect changes in the definition of autism and differences in the methodology and contexts of prevalence studies.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija es autista, no estáis solos: alrededor de 1 de cada 100 niños en el mundo recibe un diagnóstico de autismo. Que hoy se identifique a más personas refleja sobre todo más conciencia social, mejores servicios y definiciones más amplias, no una «epidemia». Las niñas pueden pasar más desapercibidas, así que vale la pena confiar en lo que observas y pedir orientación cuando lo necesites. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 99 estimaciones de 71 estudios publicados entre 2012 y 2021 en distintas regiones del mundo. Como límite, no evaluó la calidad de cada estudio, y las cifras varían mucho según el país y el método usado.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic, you are not alone: around 1 in 100 children worldwide receive an autism diagnosis. The rise in numbers mainly reflects greater awareness, better services and broader definitions, not an "epidemic". Autistic girls may be noticed less often, so it is worth trusting what you observe and asking for support when you need it. This systematic review brought together 99 estimates from 71 studies published between 2012 and 2021 across many world regions. Its limit: it did not appraise the quality of each study, and figures vary widely by country and by the methods used.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt är ni inte ensamma: ungefär 1 av 100 barn i världen får en autismdiagnos. Att fler identifieras i dag beror främst på ökad medvetenhet, bättre tjänster och bredare definitioner, inte på en ”epidemi”. Autistiska flickor uppmärksammas ofta mer sällan, så lita på det du ser och be om stöd när du behöver det. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 99 skattningar från 71 studier publicerade 2012–2021 i många delar av världen. En begränsning är att studiernas kvalitet inte bedömdes, och siffrorna skiljer sig mycket mellan länder och metoder.

title: Factors influencing oral health behaviours, access and delivery of dental care for autistic children and adolescents: A mixed-methods systematic review.
authors: Erwin J, Paisi M, Neill S, Burns L, Vassallo I, Nelder A, Facenfield J, Devalia U, Vassallo T, Witton R
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
abstract: Background Autistic children and young people (CYP) experience oral health (OH) inequalities. They are at high risk of dental disease and show significant levels of unmet need in relation to OH and access to dental care. Aim This study aimed to gather evidence on the factors that influence OH behaviours, access to and delivery of dental care for autistic CYP. Design This was a mixed-methods narrative systematic review. Data sources Embase, Web of Science, Dentistry & Oral Sciences Source, MEDLINE, Psychinfo, Scopus, CINAHL, SocINDEX and grey literature were the data sources for this study. Review methods A systematic search was conducted for qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods research studies from countries with a High Development Index that related to OH behaviours, access to and delivery of dental care for autistic CYP. Results were analysed using narrative synthesis. Results From 59 eligible studies, 9 themes were generated: (1) affordability and accessibility; (2) autism-related factors and cognitive or motor skill differences; (3) the dental environment; (4) managing CYP's behaviour; (5) responding and adapting to the needs of the autistic CYP and their parent/carer; (6) attitude of dental health professionals (DHPs) towards autistic CYP and their parents/carers; (7) knowledge of how to care for and support CYP's OH; (8) empowerment of parents/carers and collaboration with DHPs; and (9) communication and building rapport. Conclusion The adoption of healthy OH behaviours and access to dental care by autistic CYP is impacted by a range of factors including those intrinsically related to a diagnosis of autism, for example, communication and those often associated with autism, for example, sensory sensitivities. Access to better OH and dental care can be facilitated by responding to the individual needs of autistic CYP through accommodation, education and adaptation. This necessitates greater awareness and knowledge of autism amongst DHPs and the provision of appropriate services. More methodologically robust intervention studies are needed to identify effective ways to support autistic CYP in achieving good OH and access to dental care. Patient and public contribution The review protocol was developed with members of the project patient and public involvement group who provided the autistic voice, contributing to the interpretation of the review findings and writing of the manuscript.

sheet.es: Antes de la próxima cita dental, puede ser útil llamar a la clínica para contar lo que ayuda a su hijo o hija: luces más suaves, esperar menos, explicar cada paso, pausas o visitas previas para conocer el lugar. En casa, el cepillado puede adaptarse a la sensibilidad sensorial y a las habilidades motoras, sin forzar. Buscar profesionales que escuchen y colaboren con la familia marca diferencia. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 59 estudios de países con alto desarrollo, con niños y adolescentes autistas, familias y dentistas, e incluyó voces autistas en su elaboración. Su límite: pocos estudios prueban qué intervenciones funcionan realmente, y cada persona necesita ajustes propios.
sheet.en: Before the next dental appointment, it can help to call the clinic and share what works for your child: softer lighting, shorter waits, explaining each step, breaks, or a visit beforehand to get familiar with the space. At home, toothbrushing can be adapted to sensory sensitivities and motor skills rather than forced. Finding dental staff who listen and work with you as a partner makes a real difference. This systematic review brought together 59 studies from high-income countries involving autistic children and teens, families and dental professionals, with autistic people helping shape it. Its limit: few studies test which supports actually work, and each young person needs their own adjustments.
sheet.sv: Inför nästa tandläkarbesök kan det hjälpa att ringa kliniken och berätta vad som fungerar för ditt barn: dämpat ljus, kortare väntan, att varje steg förklaras, pauser eller ett besök i förväg för att bekanta sig med miljön. Hemma kan tandborstningen anpassas efter sensorisk känslighet och motorik i stället för att tvingas fram. Tandvårdspersonal som lyssnar och samarbetar med familjen gör stor skillnad. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 59 studier från höginkomstländer med autistiska barn och unga, föräldrar och tandvårdspersonal, och autistiska personer deltog i arbetet. Begränsning: få studier testar vilka insatser som faktiskt fungerar, och varje ung person behöver egna anpassningar.

title: The Impact of Autism Spectrum Disorder on Parents in Arab Countries: A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Alkhateeb JM, Hadidi MS, Mounzer W
abstract: Background Having a child with autism spectrum disorder can have significant psychological effects on parents. This systematic review summarizes the current state of literature underscoring the impact of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) on parents in Arab countries. Methods A systematic search of seven databases (PubMed, Scopus, ProQuest, Google Scholar, ERIC, Academic Search Complete, and PsycINFO) was performed, which identified 24 studies (20 quantitative studies and four qualitative studies) that included 3,299 parents or caregivers of children with ASD. These studies were conducted in 10 Arab countries (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Egypt, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Emirates, Palestine, Qatar, and Lebanon). Results The majority of the included studies found that ASD has a significant negative impact on the mental health and wellbeing of Arab parents. It was found that parents of children with ASD have a poor quality of life (QoL) and an increased risk of psychological disorders. These findings were in contrast to findings of parents of typically developing children and children with other developmental disorders. Challenges faced by parents of children with ASD were associated with several child- and parent-related factors. The most common coping strategy used by parents was religious coping. Conclusion The impact of ASD on parents has only recently gained traction among researchers in Arab countries. Despite several knowledge gaps, published studies have provided useful information outlining the impact of ASD on parents in some of these countries. Further research comprising larger random samples and using varied research and data-collection methods is required to understand the multifaceted challenges experienced by parents raising children with ASD in Arab countries.

sheet.es: Si usted cuida a un niño autista, su propio bienestar también importa: buscar apoyo para usted no es egoísmo. Hablar con otros padres, con su comunidad de fe si le ayuda, o con un profesional puede aliviar la carga diaria. Muchas familias encuentran fuerza en la fe y en redes cercanas. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 24 estudios con 3.299 padres y cuidadores de 10 países árabes, y encontró más estrés y menor calidad de vida que en otros padres, a menudo ligados a la falta de apoyos. Sus límites: la mayoría de los estudios eran pequeños y no aleatorios, y midieron la carga de los padres, no el valor de sus hijos.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, your own wellbeing matters too: seeking support for yourself is not selfish. Talking with other parents, your faith community if that helps you, or a professional can ease the daily load. Many families draw strength from faith and close networks. This systematic review gathered 24 studies with 3,299 parents and caregivers in 10 Arab countries and found higher stress and lower quality of life than among other parents, often linked to gaps in support. Its limits: most studies were small and non-random, and they measured parents' strain, not the worth of their children.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn spelar ditt eget mående också roll: att söka stöd för dig själv är inte själviskt. Att prata med andra föräldrar, med ditt trossamfund om det hjälper dig, eller med en professionell kan lätta den dagliga bördan. Många familjer hämtar kraft ur tro och nära nätverk. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 24 studier med 3 299 föräldrar och vårdnadshavare i 10 arabiska länder och fann mer stress och lägre livskvalitet än hos andra föräldrar, ofta kopplat till brist på stöd. Begränsningar: de flesta studier var små och inte slumpmässiga, och de mätte föräldrarnas belastning, inte barnens värde.

title: Exploring the impact of adolescent cognitive inflexibility on emotional and behavioural problems experienced by autistic adults.
authors: Hollocks MJ, Charman T, Baird G, Lord C, Pickles A, Simonoff E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people experience high levels of co-occurring mental health difficulties. To develop more effective treatments, a greater understanding of the thinking processes that may lead to these difficulties is needed. Cognitive inflexibility, defined as a rigid pattern of thoughts and subsequently behaviours, is one possible thinking trait which has previously been associated with both co-occurring mental health difficulties but also other features of autism such as restricted and repetitive behaviours. Restricted and repetitive behaviours include repetitive movements, ritualistic behaviours, and/or highly focused interests. This study investigates the relationship between, cognitive inflexibility, measured using neuropsychological tasks, and emotional and behavioural problems across adolescence and early adulthood. Eighty-one autistic people who were recruited to be representative of the wider autism population were assessed at 16 and 23 years on measures of emotional and behavioural problems, with cognitive inflexibility, restricted and repetitive behaviours and verbal intelligence measured at 16 years. We used statistical modelling to investigate the relationship between cognitive inflexibility and emotional and behavioural symptoms at both timepoints while accounting for the possible relationship with restricted and repetitive behaviours and verbal intelligence quotient. Our results suggest that cognitive inflexibility may be an important factor associated with emotional difficulties across adolescence and early adulthood. This suggests that developing intervention approaches targeting cognitive inflexibility may be an important step in improving the mental health of those with autism.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija adolescente autista vive con mucha dificultad los cambios de plan o las formas nuevas de pensar algo, conviene prestar atención a cómo se siente emocionalmente, no solo a su conducta. Anticipar cambios, ofrecer apoyos visuales y practicar juntos alternativas pequeñas y seguras puede ayudar, respetando siempre sus intereses y rutinas. Este estudio siguió a 81 personas autistas, representativas de la población autista, a los 16 y 23 años, y encontró que la inflexibilidad cognitiva en la adolescencia se asociaba con más dificultades emocionales después. Es una asociación, no prueba causa, la muestra es pequeña y no se aplica igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic teenager finds changes of plan or new ways of thinking about something very hard, it is worth paying attention to how they feel emotionally, not only to what they do. Giving warning before changes, using visual supports and gently practising small, safe alternatives together may help, while respecting their interests and routines. This study followed 81 autistic people, recruited to reflect the wider autistic population, at ages 16 and 23, and found that cognitive inflexibility in adolescence was linked to more emotional difficulties later. It shows a link, not a cause, the group was small, and it does not apply the same way to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska tonåring har mycket svårt med ändrade planer eller nya sätt att tänka kring något kan det vara klokt att uppmärksamma hur hen mår känslomässigt, inte bara vad hen gör. Att förvarna om förändringar, använda bildstöd och tillsammans lugnt öva på små, trygga alternativ kan hjälpa, med respekt för hens intressen och rutiner. Studien följde 81 autistiska personer, valda för att spegla den bredare autistiska befolkningen, vid 16 och 23 års ålder och fann att kognitiv oflexibilitet i tonåren hängde ihop med fler känslomässiga svårigheter senare. Det är ett samband, inte ett orsaksbevis, gruppen var liten och resultatet gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

title: A qualitative exploration of autistic mothers' experiences II: Childbirth and postnatal experiences.
authors: Hampton S, Man J, Allison C, Aydin E, Baron-Cohen S, Holt R
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Very little research has looked at how autistic people experience childbirth and the first few months of parenthood. We interviewed 21 autistic and 25 non-autistic women 2-3 months after their baby was born, to find out how they experienced giving birth and being a parent. Some autistic participants found sensory aspects of giving birth difficult, such as noise and being touched. They also wanted healthcare professionals to give them clear information while giving birth. Participants sometimes thought that healthcare professionals did not know enough about autism. Autistic and non-autistic participants both found parenthood difficult at times and autistic parents sometimes had extra difficulties, such as with planning and organising. Autistic participants also felt good at understanding their baby's needs. This research suggests that autistic people would benefit from changes to childbirth and postnatal healthcare such as being communicated with more clearly. It also indicates that healthcare professionals should receive more training about autism.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que va a dar a luz o acaba de hacerlo, puede ayudar preparar juntos un plan sensorial (menos ruido, avisar antes de tocar) y pedir al personal sanitario información clara y paso a paso. En el posparto, el apoyo práctico con la planificación y la organización puede aliviar mucho, reconociendo también que muchas madres autistas entienden bien las necesidades de su bebé. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 21 mujeres autistas y 25 no autistas, dos o tres meses después del parto. Sus límites: pocas participantes, solo mujeres y en un país, así que las experiencias no se aplican a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who is about to give birth or has just done so, it may help to plan sensory needs together (less noise, asking before touching) and to ask healthcare staff for clear, step-by-step information. After the birth, practical help with planning and organising can make a real difference, while recognising that many autistic mothers feel skilled at understanding their baby's needs. This is a qualitative study interviewing 21 autistic and 25 non-autistic women two to three months after birth. Its limits: a small group, only women, in one setting, so these experiences will not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som ska föda eller nyss har fött kan det hjälpa att tillsammans planera för sinnesintryck (mindre ljud, fråga innan beröring) och be vårdpersonalen om tydlig information steg för steg. Efter förlossningen kan praktisk hjälp med planering och organisering göra stor skillnad, samtidigt som många autistiska mammor känner att de är bra på att förstå sitt barns behov. Det är en kvalitativ studie där 21 autistiska och 25 icke-autistiska kvinnor intervjuades två till tre månader efter förlossningen. Begränsningar: få deltagare, bara kvinnor och en miljö, så erfarenheterna gäller inte alla.

title: A blind spot in mental healthcare? Psychotherapists lack education and expertise for the support of adults on the autism spectrum.
authors: Lipinski S, Boegl K, Blanke ES, Suenkel U, Dziobek I
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Most autistic adults experience mental health problems. There is a great demand for psychotherapeutic support that addresses the specific needs of autistic individuals. However, people with autism encounter difficulties trying to access diagnostic and therapeutic services. This study was conducted by a participatory autism research group: a group in which autistic individuals and scientists collaborate. The group developed a questionnaire for psychotherapists in Germany to assess their knowledge about autism. Psychotherapists also rated their ability to diagnose and treat autistic patients without intellectual disability, and patients with other psychological diagnoses. Many of the 498 psychotherapists that responded reported little knowledge and outdated beliefs about autism, as well as little training on treating patients with autism. Their expertise about other psychological conditions was more comprehensive. However, many psychotherapists were interested in professional training on autism. Those with more knowledge were also more open to treating autistic patients. In conclusion, psychotherapists' lack of knowledge and expertise seem to be a major barrier for adults with autism to receiving helpful psychotherapeutic support. The results demonstrate the need for an advancement in autism education during psychotherapists' training and in continuous education.

sheet.es: Si buscas psicoterapia para un adulto autista, es razonable preguntar al terapeuta, antes de empezar, qué formación y experiencia tiene en autismo y cómo adaptaría las sesiones. Llevar información breve sobre las necesidades de la persona puede ayudar, y cambiar de profesional si no hay comprensión es legítimo. Este estudio, diseñado por un grupo participativo de personas autistas e investigadores, encuestó a 498 psicoterapeutas en Alemania: muchos tenían poco conocimiento, ideas desactualizadas y escasa formación en autismo, aunque muchos querían aprender. Sus límites: se basa en autoevaluaciones de quienes quisieron responder, en un solo país, y no mide la calidad real de la atención.
sheet.en: If you are looking for psychotherapy for an autistic adult, it is reasonable to ask a therapist, before starting, what training and experience they have with autism and how they would adapt sessions. Bringing brief notes on the person's needs can help, and changing professionals if understanding is lacking is legitimate. This study, designed by a participatory group of autistic people and researchers, surveyed 498 psychotherapists in Germany: many reported little knowledge, outdated beliefs and limited autism training, though many wanted to learn more. Its limits: it relies on self-ratings from those who chose to respond, in one country, and does not measure actual quality of care.
sheet.sv: Om du söker psykoterapi för en autistisk vuxen är det rimligt att innan start fråga terapeuten vilken utbildning och erfarenhet hen har av autism och hur sessionerna skulle anpassas. Att ta med korta anteckningar om personens behov kan hjälpa, och det är helt okej att byta behandlare om förståelsen saknas. Studien, utformad av en deltagande grupp av autistiska personer och forskare, var en enkät till 498 psykoterapeuter i Tyskland: många rapporterade lite kunskap, föråldrade föreställningar och begränsad autismutbildning, men många ville lära sig mer. Begränsningar: den bygger på självskattningar från dem som valde att svara, i ett enda land, och mäter inte vårdens faktiska kvalitet.

title: The Current View on the Paradox of Pain in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Bogdanova OV, Bogdanov VB, Pizano A, Bouvard M, Cazalets JR, Mellen N, Amestoy A
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder, which affects 1 in 44 children and may cause severe disabilities. Besides socio-communicational difficulties and repetitive behaviors, ASD also presents as atypical sensorimotor function and pain reactivity. While chronic pain is a frequent co-morbidity in autism, pain management in this population is often insufficient because of difficulties in pain evaluation, worsening their prognosis and perhaps driving higher mortality rates. Previous observations have tended to oversimplify the experience of pain in autism as being insensitive to painful stimuli. Various findings in the past 15 years have challenged and complicated this dogma. However, a relatively small number of studies investigates the physiological correlates of pain reactivity in ASD. We explore the possibility that atypical pain perception in people with ASD is mediated by alterations in pain perception, transmission, expression and modulation, and through interactions between these processes. These complex interactions may account for the great variability and sometimes contradictory findings from the studies. A growing body of evidence is challenging the idea of alterations in pain processing in ASD due to a single factor, and calls for an integrative view. We propose a model of the pain cycle that includes the interplay between the molecular and neurophysiological pathways of pain processing and it conscious appraisal that may interfere with pain reactivity and coping in autism. The role of social factors in pain-induced response is also discussed. Pain assessment in clinical care is mostly based on subjective rather than objective measures. This review clarifies the strong need for a consistent methodology, and describes innovative tools to cope with the heterogeneity of pain expression in ASD, enabling individualized assessment. Multiple measures, including self-reporting, informant reporting, clinician-assessed, and purely physiological metrics may provide more consistent results. An integrative view on the regulation of the pain cycle offers a more robust framework to characterize the experience of pain in autism.

sheet.es: No des por hecho que una persona autista no siente dolor porque no lo muestre de la forma esperada. El dolor puede expresarse de maneras distintas: cambios en el sueño, en la comida, en los movimientos, retirada o más inquietud. Conviene observar qué es habitual en tu familiar, anotar cambios y compartir esa información con el equipo sanitario, junto con lo que la propia persona pueda comunicar por cualquier medio. Se trata de una revisión narrativa que reúne estudios de unos 15 años sobre percepción y expresión del dolor en el autismo. Su límite: no aporta datos nuevos y los estudios existentes son pocos y con resultados variables, así que cada persona es diferente.
sheet.en: Don't assume an autistic person feels no pain just because they don't show it in the expected way. Pain may appear differently: changes in sleep, eating, movement, withdrawal or extra restlessness. It helps to know what is usual for your family member, note changes, and share this with health professionals, alongside whatever the person themselves can communicate in any form. This is a narrative review bringing together about 15 years of research on how autistic people perceive and express pain. Its limit: it offers no new data, and existing studies are few and show varied, sometimes contradictory results, so every person differs.
sheet.sv: Utgå inte från att en autistisk person inte känner smärta bara för att den inte visas på förväntat sätt. Smärta kan märkas på andra sätt: förändrad sömn, aptit eller rörelser, tillbakadragenhet eller ökad oro. Det hjälper att känna till vad som är vanligt för din närstående, anteckna förändringar och dela det med vården, tillsammans med det personen själv kan förmedla på valfritt sätt. Detta är en översiktsartikel som samlar cirka 15 års forskning om hur autistiska personer upplever och uttrycker smärta. Begränsning: den ger inga nya data, och de studier som finns är få med varierande, ibland motsägelsefulla resultat, så varje person är olik.

claim.es: La vieja idea de 'indiferencia al dolor' en autismo es errónea: el dolor se expresa de forma atípica y a menudo se pasa por alto.
claim.en: The old idea of 'pain indifference' in autism is wrong: pain is expressed atypically and often missed.
claim.sv: Den gamla idén om 'smärtokänslighet' vid autism är fel: smärta uttrycks annorlunda och missas ofta.

supports.es: Tratar un cambio de conducta como posible señal de dolor que merece comprobarse.
supports.en: Treating a change in behaviour as a possible pain signal worth checking.
supports.sv: Att se en beteendeförändring som en möjlig smärtsignal värd att kontrollera.

doesNotSupport.es: Que cuidadores o cámaras puedan medir el dolor; el dolor sigue siendo una hipótesis que se comprueba con sanidad.
doesNotSupport.en: That caregivers or cameras can measure pain; pain remains a hypothesis to check with healthcare.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att vårdgivare eller kameror kan mäta smärta; smärta förblir en hypotes att kontrollera med vården.

title: Autistic adults' views and experiences of requesting and receiving workplace adjustments in the UK.
authors: Davies J, Heasman B, Livesey A, Walker A, Pellicano E, Remington A
abstract: This article examines 181 autistic adults' views toward, and experiences of, requesting and receiving workplace adjustments in the UK. Using an online survey, we collected both qualitative and quantitative data relating to individuals' experiences. While the majority of participants perceived workplace adjustments to be important, many were not receiving them. Analysis of open-ended text responses highlighted specific challenges that autistic people face in requesting and receiving adjustments. Specifically, participants felt the onus fell on them to (1) identify their need for adjustments; (2) establish the specific adjustments that would be beneficial and (3) request adjustments from their employer. Yet, they reported struggling with this process. Participants also highlighted a range of social and organisational barriers to the successful implementation of workplace adjustments. Unsurprisingly, the lack of successfully implemented adjustments had far-reaching impacts on participants' wellbeing as well as the choices they made about their future employment. These findings highlight the need for employers to take a more active role in the identification and implementation of workplace adjustments, as well as a need for more understanding and inclusive working environments that truly allow autistic employees to thrive in the workplace.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que trabaja, puedes ayudarle a identificar qué cambios le facilitarían el día (luz, ruido, horarios, instrucciones por escrito) y a preparar juntos la petición a la empresa, si ella lo desea. No debería cargar sola con todo el proceso: es razonable esperar que el empleador participe activamente. Este estudio fue una encuesta en línea a 181 adultos autistas en el Reino Unido; la mayoría valoraba las adaptaciones, pero muchas no las recibían, y eso afectaba su bienestar y sus decisiones laborales. Sus límites: participaron voluntariamente personas con acceso a internet, en un solo país, y las experiencias pueden no reflejar las de todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who works, you can help them notice which changes would make the day easier (lighting, noise, schedules, written instructions) and prepare a request to their employer together, if they want that. They shouldn't have to carry the whole process alone: it is reasonable to expect employers to take an active part. This study was an online survey of 181 autistic adults in the UK; most valued workplace adjustments, but many weren't receiving them, which affected their wellbeing and job choices. Its limits: participants volunteered online, all in one country, so their experiences may not reflect every autistic person's.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som arbetar kan ni tillsammans fundera på vilka anpassningar som skulle göra dagen lättare (ljus, ljud, arbetstider, skriftliga instruktioner) och förbereda en begäran till arbetsgivaren, om personen vill det. Hen ska inte behöva bära hela processen själv: det är rimligt att arbetsgivaren tar en aktiv roll. Studien var en webbenkät med 181 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien; de flesta tyckte att anpassningar var viktiga, men många fick dem inte, vilket påverkade välmående och framtida jobbval. Begränsningar: deltagarna anmälde sig frivilligt via nätet i ett enda land, så erfarenheterna gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla autistiska personer.

title: Psychometric validation of a brief self-report measure of misophonia symptoms and functional impairment: The duke-vanderbilt misophonia screening questionnaire.
authors: Williams ZJ, Cascio CJ, Woynaroski TG
abstract: Misophonia is a newly described disorder of sound tolerance characterized by strong negative emotional reactions to specific "trigger" sounds, resulting in significant distress, pathological avoidance, and impairment in daily life. Research on misophonia is still in its infancy, and most existing psychometric tools for assessing misophonia symptoms have not been extensively validated. The purpose of the current study was to introduce and psychometrically validate the duke-vanderbilt Misophonia Screening Questionnaire (DVMSQ), a novel self-report measure of misophonia symptoms that can be used to determine misophonia "caseness" in clinical and research settings. Employing large online samples of general population adults ( n = 1403) and adults on the autism spectrum ( n = 936), we rigorously evaluated the internal structure, reliability, validity, and measurement invariance of the DVMSQ. Results indicated that 17 of the 20 original DVMSQ items fit well to a bifactor structure with one "general misophonia" factor and four specific factors (anger/aggression, distress/avoidance, impairment, and global impact). DVMSQ total and subscale scores were highly reliable in both general population and autistic adult samples, and the measure was found to be approximately invariant across age, sex, education level, and autism status. DVMSQ total scores also correlated strongly with another measure of misophonia symptoms (Duke Misophonia Questionnaire-Symptom Scale), with correlations between these two measures being significantly stronger than correlations between the DVMSQ and scales measuring other types of sound intolerance (Inventory of Hyperacusis Symptoms [General Loudness subscale] and DSM-5 Severity Measure for Specific Phobia [modified for phonophobia]). Additionally, DVMSQ items were used to operationalize diagnostic criteria for misophonia derived from the Revised Amsterdam Criteria, which were further updated to reflect a recent consensus definition of misophonia (published after the development of the DVMSQ). Using the new DVMSQ algorithm, 7.3% of general population adults and 35.5% of autistic adults met criteria for clinically significant misophonia. Although additional work is needed to further investigate the psychometric properties of the DVMSQ and validate its theory-based screening algorithm using best-estimate clinical diagnoses, this novel measure represents a potentially useful tool to screen for misophonia and quantify symptom severity and impairment in both autistic adults and the general population.

sheet.es: Si a una persona autista ciertos sonidos concretos (masticar, respirar, teclear) le provocan enfado, angustia o ganas de huir, tómelo en serio: puede ser misofonía, algo frecuente y real. Pregúntele qué sonidos le afectan, acuerden juntos opciones como auriculares, música de fondo o comer en otro espacio, y evite insistir en que «se acostumbre». Este estudio validó un cuestionario breve de autoinforme con 1.403 adultos de población general y 936 adultos autistas en línea; el 35,5 % de los adultos autistas cumplía criterios de misofonía significativa, frente al 7,3 % del resto. Límites: muestras en línea, solo adultos y sin confirmación mediante evaluación clínica; el cuestionario sirve para detectar, no para diagnosticar.
sheet.en: If an autistic person reacts to specific sounds (chewing, breathing, typing) with anger, distress or an urge to escape, take it seriously: it may be misophonia, which is common and real. Ask which sounds affect them, agree together on options like headphones, background music or eating in another room, and avoid pushing them to “get used to it.” This study validated a brief self-report questionnaire with 1,403 general-population adults and 936 autistic adults online; 35.5% of autistic adults met criteria for significant misophonia, versus 7.3% of others. Limits: online samples, adults only, and no confirmation through clinical assessment; the questionnaire screens, it does not diagnose.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person reagerar på vissa specifika ljud (tuggande, andning, tangentknatter) med ilska, obehag eller vilja att fly, ta det på allvar: det kan vara misofoni, som är vanligt och verkligt. Fråga vilka ljud som påverkar, kom gemensamt överens om lösningar som hörlurar, bakgrundsmusik eller att äta i ett annat rum, och undvik att kräva att personen ska ”vänja sig”. Studien validerade ett kort självskattningsformulär med 1 403 vuxna ur befolkningen och 936 autistiska vuxna online; 35,5 % av de autistiska vuxna uppfyllde kriterier för betydande misofoni, jämfört med 7,3 % av övriga. Begränsningar: onlineurval, endast vuxna och ingen bekräftelse genom klinisk bedömning; formuläret är för screening, inte diagnos.

title: Role of Gut Microbiome in Autism Spectrum Disorder and Its Therapeutic Regulation.
authors: Taniya MA, Chung HJ, Al Mamun A, Alam S, Aziz MA, Emon NU, Islam MM, Hong SS, Podder BR, Ara Mimi A, Aktar Suchi S, Xiao J
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurological disorder that affects normal brain development. The recent finding of the microbiota-gut-brain axis indicates the bidirectional connection between our gut and brain, demonstrating that gut microbiota can influence many neurological disorders such as autism. Most autistic patients suffer from gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms. Many studies have shown that early colonization, mode of delivery, and antibiotic usage significantly affect the gut microbiome and the onset of autism. Microbial fermentation of plant-based fiber can produce different types of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) that may have a beneficial or detrimental effect on the gut and neurological development of autistic patients. Several comprehensive studies of the gut microbiome and microbiota-gut-brain axis help to understand the mechanism that leads to the onset of neurological disorders and find possible treatments for autism. This review integrates the findings of recent years on the gut microbiota and ASD association, mainly focusing on the characterization of specific microbiota that leads to ASD and addressing potential therapeutic interventions to restore a healthy balance of gut microbiome composition that can treat autism-associated symptoms.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene molestias digestivas frecuentes (dolor de barriga, estreñimiento, diarrea), merece la pena tomarlas en serio y comentarlas con su equipo de salud: pueden afectar al sueño, al ánimo y al bienestar diario. Llevar un diario sencillo de comidas, deposiciones y momentos de malestar puede ayudar en la consulta. Evita cambiar la dieta o dar suplementos por tu cuenta. Se trata de una revisión que resume estudios recientes sobre la microbiota intestinal y el autismo, no de un ensayo con participantes propios. Sus límites: la mayoría de las relaciones descritas son asociaciones, muchas provienen de estudios pequeños o con animales, y ningún tratamiento microbiano está probado para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child often has gut discomfort (tummy pain, constipation, diarrhoea), it is worth taking it seriously and raising it with their health team: it can affect sleep, mood and everyday wellbeing. Keeping a simple diary of meals, bowel movements and moments of distress can help at appointments. Avoid changing their diet or giving supplements on your own. This is a review summarising recent research on gut bacteria and autism, not a trial with its own participants. Its limits: most links described are associations, many come from small or animal studies, and no microbiome-based treatment has been shown to work for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn ofta har besvär med magen (ont i magen, förstoppning, diarré) är det värt att ta det på allvar och ta upp det med vården: det kan påverka sömn, humör och vardagens välmående. En enkel dagbok över måltider, toalettbesök och stunder av obehag kan underlätta vid besöket. Undvik att själv ändra kosten eller ge kosttillskott. Detta är en översikt som sammanfattar ny forskning om tarmbakterier och autism, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Begränsningar: de flesta samband är just samband, många bygger på små studier eller djurstudier, och ingen tarmfloraterapi har visats fungera för alla.

title: Misinformation About COVID-19 Vaccines on Social Media: Rapid Review.
authors: Skafle I, Nordahl-Hansen A, Quintana DS, Wynn R, Gabarron E
abstract: Background The development of COVID-19 vaccines has been crucial in fighting the pandemic. However, misinformation about the COVID-19 pandemic and vaccines is spread on social media platforms at a rate that has made the World Health Organization coin the phrase infodemic. False claims about adverse vaccine side effects, such as vaccines being the cause of autism, were already considered a threat to global health before the outbreak of COVID-19. Objective We aimed to synthesize the existing research on misinformation about COVID-19 vaccines spread on social media platforms and its effects. The secondary aim was to gain insight and gather knowledge about whether misinformation about autism and COVID-19 vaccines is being spread on social media platforms. Methods We performed a literature search on September 9, 2021, and searched PubMed, PsycINFO, ERIC, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and the Cochrane COVID-19 Study Register. We included publications in peer-reviewed journals that fulfilled the following criteria: original empirical studies, studies that assessed social media and misinformation, and studies about COVID-19 vaccines. Thematic analysis was used to identify the patterns (themes) of misinformation. Narrative qualitative synthesis was undertaken with the guidance of the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 Statement and the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis reporting guideline. The risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal tool. Ratings of the certainty of evidence were based on recommendations from the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation Working Group. Results The search yielded 757 records, with 45 articles selected for this review. We identified 3 main themes of misinformation: medical misinformation, vaccine development, and conspiracies. Twitter was the most studied social media platform, followed by Facebook, YouTube, and Instagram. A vast majority of studies were from industrialized Western countries. We identified 19 studies in which the effect of social media misinformation on vaccine hesitancy was measured or discussed. These studies implied that the misinformation spread on social media had a negative effect on vaccine hesitancy and uptake. Only 1 study contained misinformation about autism as a side effect of COVID-19 vaccines. Conclusions To prevent these misconceptions from taking hold, health authorities should openly address and discuss these false claims with both cultural and religious awareness in mind. Our review showed that there is a need to examine the effect of social media misinformation on vaccine hesitancy with a more robust experimental design. Furthermore, this review also demonstrated that more studies are needed from the Global South and on social media platforms other than the major platforms such as Twitter and Facebook. Trial registration PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews CRD42021277524; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD42021277524. International registered report identifier (irrid) RR2-10.31219/osf.io/tyevj.

sheet.es: Si en redes sociales ve afirmaciones de que las vacunas contra la COVID-19 causan autismo, puede tomarlas con calma: esta revisión encontró que esa idea apenas aparecía, y la afirmación de que las vacunas causan autismo ya se consideraba falsa antes de la pandemia. Ante una duda sobre vacunas, conviene consultar fuentes sanitarias oficiales o a su profesional de salud, y compartir solo información verificada. La evidencia procede de una revisión rápida sistemática de 45 estudios sobre desinformación en Twitter, Facebook, YouTube e Instagram. Sus límites: casi todos los estudios eran de países occidentales industrializados, se centraban en pocas plataformas y pocos usaban diseños experimentales sólidos.
sheet.en: If you see claims on social media that COVID-19 vaccines cause autism, you can take them calmly: this review found that idea appeared only rarely, and the claim that vaccines cause autism was already considered false before the pandemic. When you have questions about vaccines, it helps to check official health sources or talk with your health professional, and to share only verified information. The evidence comes from a rapid systematic review of 45 studies on misinformation across Twitter, Facebook, YouTube and Instagram. Its limits: most studies came from industrialized Western countries, focused on a few major platforms, and few used robust experimental designs.
sheet.sv: Om du ser påståenden i sociala medier om att covid-19-vaccin orsakar autism kan du ta det med ro: den här översikten fann att den idén förekom mycket sällan, och påståendet att vaccin orsakar autism ansågs falskt redan före pandemin. Har du frågor om vaccin kan du vända dig till officiella hälsokällor eller din vårdkontakt, och dela bara kontrollerad information. Underlaget är en snabb systematisk översikt av 45 studier om desinformation på Twitter, Facebook, YouTube och Instagram. Begränsningar: de flesta studier kom från industrialiserade västländer, gällde några få stora plattformar och få hade robust experimentell design.

title: Five Ways Providers Can Improve Mental Healthcare for Autistic Adults: A Review of Mental Healthcare Use, Barriers to Care, and Evidence-Based Recommendations.
authors: Gilmore D, Longo A, Krantz M, Radford D, Hand BN

title: A capabilities approach to understanding and supporting autistic adulthood.
authors: Pellicano E, Fatima U, Hall G, Heyworth M, Lawson W, Lilley R, Mahony J, Stears M

title: Applied Behavior Analysis in Children and Youth with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Scoping Review.
authors: Gitimoghaddam M, Chichkine N, McArthur L, Sangha SS, Symington V
abstract: This manuscript provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of applied behavior analysis (ABA) on children and youth with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Seven online databases and identified systematic reviews were searched for published, peer-reviewed, English-language studies examining the impact of ABA on health outcomes. Measured outcomes were classified into eight categories: cognitive, language, social/communication, problem behavior, adaptive behavior, emotional, autism symptoms, and quality of life (QoL) outcomes. Improvements were observed across seven of the eight outcome measures. There were no included studies that measured subject QoL. Moreover, of 770 included study records, only 32 (4%) assessed ABA impact, had a comparison to a control or other intervention, and did not rely on mastery of specific skills to mark improvement. Results reinforce the need for large-scale prospective studies that compare ABA with other non-ABA interventions and include measurements of subject QoL to provide policy makers with valuable information on the impacts of ABA and other existing and emerging interventions. Supplementary information The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40614-022-00338-x.

sheet.es: Si te ofrecen ABA para tu hijo o hija, puedes preguntar con calma: ¿cómo sabremos si mejora su bienestar y calidad de vida, no solo si domina habilidades concretas? Observa si disfruta, si se respeta su forma de comunicarse y si puede decir que no. Esta revisión de alcance analizó 770 estudios sobre ABA en niños, niñas y jóvenes autistas; muchos informaron mejoras en lenguaje, adaptación o conducta. Sus límites son importantes: ningún estudio midió la calidad de vida y solo el 4 % comparó ABA con otra intervención sin basarse en el dominio de habilidades específicas. Cada niño es distinto.
sheet.en: If ABA is offered for your child, it is fair to calmly ask: how will we know whether their wellbeing and quality of life improve, not just whether they master specific skills? Notice whether they seem to enjoy it, whether their way of communicating is respected, and whether they can say no. This scoping review looked at 770 studies of ABA with autistic children and youth; many reported gains in language, adaptive skills or behaviour. Its limits matter: no study measured quality of life, and only 4% compared ABA with another approach without relying on skill mastery. Every child is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn erbjuds ABA är det rimligt att lugnt fråga: hur ska vi veta om barnets välmående och livskvalitet blir bättre, inte bara om hen klarar specifika färdigheter? Lägg märke till om barnet verkar trivas, om hens sätt att kommunicera respekteras och om hen kan säga nej. Denna kartläggande översikt gick igenom 770 studier om ABA för autistiska barn och unga; många rapporterade framsteg i språk, vardagsfärdigheter eller beteende. Begränsningarna är viktiga: ingen studie mätte livskvalitet, och bara 4 % jämförde ABA med ett annat stöd utan att mäta enbart inlärda färdigheter. Varje barn är unikt.

title: The impact of early stages of COVID-19 on the mental health of autistic adults in the United Kingdom: A longitudinal mixed-methods study.
authors: Bundy R, Mandy W, Crane L, Belcher H, Belcher H, Bourne L, Brede J, Hull L, Brinkert J, Cook J
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, high levels of depression, anxiety and stress have been reported in the general population. However, much less has been reported about the impact of COVID-19 on the mental health of autistic people. What we did: In the present study, we investigated how the mental health of autistic adults in the United Kingdom changed during the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. In total, 133 participants completed an online survey at two different time points. Of the 133 participants, 70 completed the survey at the first time point just before the onset of the national lockdown. This allowed us to look at changes in their mental health, from before the lockdown to 10 to 15 weeks during lockdown. All participants (133) told us about their experiences of the pandemic. What we found: While many autistic adults told us that their mental health worsened, people's experience varied. For some autistic adults, aspects of mental health (e.g. anxiety, stress) actually improved. Participants also described social changes that had occurred, at home and in the outside world. They described feelings of uncertainty during the pandemic, and discussed how the pandemic had affected some of their previous coping strategies. Participants also told us about their difficulties in accessing healthcare services and food during the early stages of the pandemic. In our article, we discuss these findings and focus on what needs to change to ensure that autistic people are better supported as the pandemic continues.

sheet.es: Cuando la rutina cambia de golpe, pregunte a la persona autista adulta cómo le está afectando en lugar de suponerlo: para algunas el estrés aumenta, y para otras disminuye al haber menos exigencias sociales. Ayude a revisar qué estrategias de afrontamiento siguen funcionando, a reducir la incertidumbre con información clara y a planificar el acceso a la atención sanitaria y a la comida. Este estudio combinó encuestas en línea en dos momentos con relatos de 133 adultos autistas del Reino Unido, 70 de ellos antes y durante el confinamiento de 2020. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña y en línea, se centra en un solo país y abarca solo las primeras semanas de la pandemia.
sheet.en: When routines change suddenly, ask the autistic adult how it is affecting them rather than assuming: for some, stress rises, while for others it eases because there are fewer social demands. Help them review which coping strategies still work, reduce uncertainty with clear information, and plan ahead for access to healthcare and food. This study combined online surveys at two time points with personal accounts from 133 autistic adults in the UK, 70 of whom answered both before and during the 2020 lockdown. Its limits: the sample is small and recruited online, it covers a single country, and it only spans the early weeks of the pandemic.
sheet.sv: När rutiner plötsligt förändras, fråga den autistiska vuxna hur det påverkar dem i stället för att anta: för vissa ökar stressen, för andra minskar den när de sociala kraven blir färre. Hjälp till att se över vilka copingstrategier som fortfarande fungerar, minska osäkerheten med tydlig information och planera i förväg för tillgång till vård och mat. Studien kombinerade onlineenkäter vid två tillfällen med berättelser från 133 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien, varav 70 svarade både före och under nedstängningen 2020. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet och rekryterat online, studien gäller ett enda land och täcker bara pandemins första veckor.
