title: The Mediating Effects of Alexithymia, Intolerance of Uncertainty, and Anxiety on the Relationship Between Sensory Processing Differences and Restricted and Repetitive Behaviours in Autistic Adults.
authors: Moore HL, Brice S, Powell L, Ingham B, Freeston M, Parr JR, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Distress caused by sensory processing differences for autistic individuals may be reduced by repetitive behaviours (RRB), including repetitive motor (RMB) and insistence on sameness (ISB) behaviours. Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) and anxiety mediate the relationship between sensory processing and RRB in autistic children. We replicated this model in autistic adults, extending it to include alexithymia. Serial mediation, using data from 426 autistic adults, identified significant direct effects from sensory processing to RMB and ISB, and indirect effects through alexithymia-IU-anxiety for RMB, and IU alone, and alexithymia-IU for ISB. Different mechanisms may underpin RMB and ISB. Alexithymia alongside, IU and anxiety, should be considered when understanding the relationship between sensory processing and RRB, and when offering interventions to support autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta repite movimientos o necesita que las cosas sigan igual, puede ser una forma de manejar el malestar sensorial, la incertidumbre o la ansiedad. Mañana puedes reducir sorpresas (avisar cambios, explicar planes), cuidar el entorno sensorial y ayudar con calma a poner nombre a lo que siente, sin intentar eliminar esas conductas. Es un estudio con cuestionarios a 426 adultos autistas, que encontró vínculos entre diferencias sensoriales, dificultad para identificar emociones (alexitimia), intolerancia a la incertidumbre, ansiedad y conductas repetitivas. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones en un solo momento, no causas, y quizá no refleje a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult repeats movements or needs things to stay the same, this may be a way of coping with sensory distress, uncertainty or anxiety. Tomorrow you could reduce surprises (flag changes, explain plans), adjust the sensory environment, and calmly help put words to feelings, rather than trying to stop these behaviours. This was a questionnaire study with 426 autistic adults, linking sensory differences, difficulty identifying emotions (alexithymia), intolerance of uncertainty, anxiety and repetitive behaviours. Its limits: it shows associations at one point in time, not causes, and may not reflect every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen upprepar rörelser eller behöver att saker förblir som de är kan det vara ett sätt att hantera sensoriskt obehag, osäkerhet eller oro. I morgon kan du minska överraskningar (förvarna om ändringar, förklara planer), anpassa den sensoriska miljön och lugnt hjälpa till att sätta ord på känslor, i stället för att försöka stoppa beteendena. Det här var en enkätstudie med 426 autistiska vuxna som kopplade samman sensoriska skillnader, svårt att identifiera känslor (alexitymi), intolerans mot osäkerhet, ångest och repetitiva beteenden. Begränsningar: den visar samband vid ett tillfälle, inte orsaker, och speglar kanske inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Autism and anorexia nervosa: Longitudinal prediction of eating disorder outcomes.
authors: Leppanen J, Sedgewick F, Halls D, Tchanturia K
abstract: Background Recently, elevated levels of autistic features and autism diagnoses have been reported among people with anorexia nervosa (AN). In clinical settings high levels of autistic features have been linked to more complex, highly comorbid illness presentation and poorer treatment outcome. This study aimed to examine whether autistic features predict AN symptom profile in long term. Methods Altogether 118 women with lived experience of AN completed two autism assessments at time 1, the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) and the short version of the Autism Quotient (AQ10). Measures assessing AN symptom profile, including eating disorders symptoms, anxiety, depression, OCD symptoms, and Body Mass Index (BMI), were also recorded. The symptom profile measures were administered again 6 months and 2 years later. We conducted two analyses to examine the extent to which the ADOS and AQ10 scores predicted broad AN symptom profile at each three time points. Results Overall, high levels of autistic features were consistently associated with worse psychological symptoms, but not BMI, across all time points. Both the analysis using baseline ADOS scores and self-reported AQ10 scores showed similar pattern. Conclusion The present findings consolidate previously reported associations between autistic features and worse psychological outcome among people with AN. The findings also suggest that self-report measures may be sufficient for assessing the impact of autistic features on illness outcome among people with AN. Importantly, the study highlights the need for development and further investigation of neurodiversity accommodations in the treatment of AN.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista que vive con anorexia, puede ser útil pedir al equipo de tratamiento que adapte la atención a su forma de procesar el mundo: necesidades sensoriales con la comida, rutinas previsibles y comunicación clara. Más rasgos autistas se asociaron con más ansiedad, depresión y síntomas alimentarios, aunque no con el peso, así que un peso estable no siempre significa bienestar. La evidencia procede de un estudio de seguimiento durante dos años con 118 mujeres con experiencia de anorexia. Sus límites: solo participaron mujeres, muestra una asociación y no una causa, y no probó qué adaptaciones funcionan mejor.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person living with anorexia, it may help to ask the treatment team to adapt care to how they experience the world: sensory needs around food, predictable routines and clear communication. More autistic traits were linked to more anxiety, depression and eating-disorder symptoms, but not to weight, so stable weight does not always mean wellbeing. The evidence comes from a two-year follow-up study of 118 women with lived experience of anorexia. Its limits: only women took part, it shows an association rather than a cause, and it did not test which adaptations work best.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som lever med anorexi kan det hjälpa att be behandlingsteamet anpassa vården efter hur personen upplever världen: sensoriska behov kring mat, förutsägbara rutiner och tydlig kommunikation. Fler autistiska drag hängde ihop med mer ångest, depression och ätstörningssymtom, men inte med vikt, så en stabil vikt betyder inte alltid att personen mår bra. Underlaget är en uppföljningsstudie under två år med 118 kvinnor med egen erfarenhet av anorexi. Begränsningar: bara kvinnor deltog, studien visar samband och inte orsak, och den prövade inte vilka anpassningar som fungerar bäst.

title: Problematic eating behaviours of autistic women-A scoping review.
authors: Schröder SS, Danner UN, Spek AA, van Elburg AA
journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
abstract: Aim Eating and feeding behaviours of autistic individuals and related consequences have been mainly investigated in autistic children or in autistic adults with intellectual disabilities. Behaviours such as food selectivity or food neophobia have been shown to persist into adolescence and adulthood and are associated with aversive consequences. However, much less is known about the eating behaviours of autistic adults without intellectual disabilities, especially those of women. By means of a scoping review, we aim to assess the extent of the scientific literature on what is known about the eating behaviours of these women and the possible consequences of such eating behaviour. Method Medline, Cochrane, PubMed and PsycInfo databases were searched according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Results Five studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in this review. Autistic women not only reported high levels of eating behaviour frequently seen in autism spectrum disorders (ASD), but also high levels of disordered eating behaviour, similar to that of women with eating disorders. Conclusions Autistic women seem to exhibit high levels of eating behaviour frequently seen in ASD as well as disordered eating behaviour. Future research needs to shed light on what underlies these problematic eating behaviours, in order to help to adapt current treatment modalities to meet the unique needs of these women.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una mujer autista adulta, conviene mirar su relación con la comida con curiosidad y sin juicio: la selectividad alimentaria o el rechazo a alimentos nuevos pueden convivir con patrones parecidos a los trastornos alimentarios. Puedes preguntarle con calma qué texturas, rutinas o situaciones le resultan difíciles y, si te preocupa, buscar juntas un profesional que conozca el autismo. Esta revisión exploratoria reunió cinco estudios con mujeres autistas adultas sin discapacidad intelectual. Son pocos estudios, no explican las causas y no describen a todas las mujeres autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult woman, it helps to look at her relationship with food with curiosity, not judgement: food selectivity or avoiding new foods can sit alongside patterns similar to eating disorders. You might calmly ask which textures, routines or situations feel hard and, if you are worried, look together for a professional who understands autism. This scoping review brought together five studies with autistic adult women without intellectual disability. There are very few studies, they do not explain causes, and they do not describe every autistic woman.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en vuxen autistisk kvinna kan det hjälpa att se på hennes förhållande till mat med nyfikenhet, inte dömande: selektivt ätande eller att undvika ny mat kan finnas samtidigt som mönster som liknar ätstörningar. Fråga lugnt vilka konsistenser, rutiner eller situationer som känns svåra och, om du är orolig, sök tillsammans en vårdgivare som förstår autism. Denna kartläggande översikt samlade fem studier med vuxna autistiska kvinnor utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Studierna är få, förklarar inte orsaker och beskriver inte alla autistiska kvinnor.

title: Increased perceived stress is negatively associated with activities of daily living and subjective quality of life in younger, middle, and older autistic adults.
authors: McQuaid GA, Weiss CH, Said AJ, Pelphrey KA, Lee NR, Wallace GL
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Few studies have examined self-reported perceived stress in autistic adults. Existing studies have included relatively small, predominantly male samples and have not included older autistic adults. Using a large autistic sample (N = 713), enriched for individuals designated female at birth (59.3%), and spanning younger, middle, and older adulthood, we examined perceived stress and its associations with independence in activities of daily living and subjective quality of life (QoL). Perceived stress for autistic adults designated male or female at birth was compared to their same birth-sex counterparts in a general population sample. In addition, within the autistic sample, effects of sex designated at birth, age, and their interaction were examined. Regression modeling examined associations between perceived stress and independence in activities of daily living and domains of subjective QoL in autistic adults, after controlling for age, sex designated at birth, and household income. Autistic adults reported significantly greater perceived stress than a general population comparison sample. Relative to autistic adults designated male at birth, those designated female at birth demonstrated significantly elevated perceived stress. Perceived stress contributed significantly to all regression models, with greater perceived stress associated with less independence in activities of daily living, and poorer subjective QoL across all domains-Physical, Psychological, Social, Environment, and Autism-related QoL. Findings are contextualized within the literature documenting that autistic individuals experience elevated underemployment and unemployment, heightened rates of adverse life events, and increased exposure to minority stress. LAY SUMMARY: This study looked at self-reported perceived stress in a large sample of autistic adults. Autistic adults reported more perceived stress than non-autistic adults. Autistic individuals designated female at birth reported higher stress than autistic individuals designated male at birth. In autistic adults, greater perceived stress is related to less independence in activities of daily living and poorer subjective quality of life.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta parece tener más dificultades con las tareas diarias, vale la pena preguntar con calma por su nivel de estrés, sin suponer pérdida de capacidades. Reducir presiones concretas (ruido, cambios imprevistos, exigencias sociales, preocupaciones económicas) y ofrecer apoyo práctico puede dar más margen para la vida diaria y el bienestar. Las mujeres autistas, en este estudio, refirieron más estrés y merecen especial atención. Evidencia: estudio con 713 adultos autistas jóvenes, de mediana edad y mayores, comparados con población general mediante cuestionarios. Límites: muestra asociación, no causa, y se basa en autoinformes; no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult seems to struggle more with daily tasks, it is worth gently asking about stress rather than assuming lost abilities. Easing concrete pressures (noise, unexpected changes, social demands, money worries) and offering practical support may free up energy for daily life and wellbeing. Autistic women in this study reported more stress and may need particular attention. Evidence: a questionnaire study of 713 younger, middle-aged and older autistic adults, compared with a general population sample. Limits: it shows an association, not cause and effect, relies on self-report, and does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen verkar få svårare med vardagssysslor kan det vara klokt att lugnt fråga om stress, i stället för att anta att förmågor gått förlorade. Att minska konkreta påfrestningar (ljud, oväntade förändringar, sociala krav, ekonomisk oro) och ge praktiskt stöd kan frigöra kraft till vardag och välmående. Autistiska kvinnor rapporterade mer stress i studien och kan behöva särskild uppmärksamhet. Evidens: enkätstudie med 713 yngre, medelålders och äldre autistiska vuxna, jämförda med ett urval ur befolkningen. Begränsningar: den visar ett samband, inte orsak, bygger på självskattning och beskriver inte varje person.

title: Sensory processing and eating behaviours in autism: A systematic review.
authors: Nimbley E, Golds L, Sharpe H, Gillespie-Smith K, Duffy F
journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to assess the relationship between sensory processing and a broad range of eating behaviours across the lifespan. Methods Five electronic databases of published and unpublished quantitative studies were systematically searched, evaluated for risk of bias and synthesised according to identified eating outcomes. Results Across 25 studies, there was consistent evidence of a relationship between sensory processing and a range of eating behaviours. There was early evidence for the particular role of taste/smell sensitivities, as well as hypersensitivities, although future research is needed looking at different sensory patterns and modalities. There was also tentative evidence to suggest this relationship extends across development. Discussion Study findings are discussed in relation to implications for sensory-based eating and feeding interventions and the development of eating disorders. Methodological and conceptual limitations are discussed and suggestions for future research are made to address these limitations. A broader investigation of multi-sensory issues and clearly defined eating behaviours, including disordered eating in clinically diagnosed samples, will allow for a more comprehensive and robust understanding of the relationship between sensory processing and eating behaviours in autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista come pocos alimentos o rechaza algunos, puede ayudar fijarse en lo sensorial: sabor, olor, textura o temperatura. Mañana puedes observar con calma qué características comparten los alimentos que acepta y ofrecer opciones parecidas sin presión, respetando sus señales. Las sensibilidades sensoriales son reales, no caprichos. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 25 estudios cuantitativos con personas autistas de distintas edades y encontró una relación constante entre el procesamiento sensorial y la forma de comer, especialmente con la sensibilidad al sabor y al olor. Sus límites: los estudios eran variados, algunas conclusiones son preliminares y no muestran qué apoyos funcionan para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person eats a narrow range of foods or refuses some, it can help to look at the sensory side: taste, smell, texture or temperature. Tomorrow you could calmly notice what the foods they accept have in common and offer similar options without pressure, respecting their signals. Sensory sensitivities are real, not fussiness. This systematic review pooled 25 quantitative studies of autistic people across ages and found a consistent link between sensory processing and eating, especially taste and smell sensitivity. Its limits: the studies varied widely, some findings are tentative, and it does not show which supports work for each individual.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person äter ett fåtal livsmedel eller vägrar vissa kan det hjälpa att titta på det sensoriska: smak, lukt, konsistens eller temperatur. I morgon kan du lugnt lägga märke till vad maten som accepteras har gemensamt och erbjuda liknande alternativ utan press, med respekt för personens signaler. Sensorisk känslighet är verklig, inte kräsenhet. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 25 kvantitativa studier med autistiska personer i olika åldrar och fann ett genomgående samband mellan sensorisk bearbetning och ätande, särskilt känslighet för smak och lukt. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, vissa resultat är preliminära och visar inte vilket stöd som fungerar för varje person.

title: Atypical structural connectivity of language networks in autism spectrum disorder: A meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging studies.
authors: Li M, Wang Y, Tachibana M, Rahman S, Kagitani-Shimono K
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often show pervasive and complex language impairments that are closely associated with aberrant structural connectivity of language networks. However, the characteristics of white matter connectivity in ASD have remained inconclusive in previous diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) studies. The current meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively elucidate the abnormality in language-related white matter connectivity in individuals with ASD. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Medline databases to identify relevant studies. The standardized mean difference was calculated to measure the pooled difference in DTI metrics in each tract between the ASD and typically developing (TD) groups. The moderating effects of age, sex, language ability, and symptom severity were investigated using subgroup and meta-regression analysis. Thirty-three DTI studies involving 831 individuals with ASD and 836 TD controls were included in the meta-analysis. ASD subjects showed significantly lower fractional anisotropy or higher mean diffusivity across language-associated tracts than TD controls. These abnormalities tended to be more prominent in the left language networks than in the right. In addition, children with ASD exhibit more pronounced and pervasive disturbances in white matter connectivity than adults. These results support the under-connectivity hypothesis and demonstrate the widespread abnormal microstructure of language-related tracts in patients with ASD. Otherwise, white matter abnormalities in the autistic brain could vary depending on the developmental stage and hemisphere. LAY SUMMARY: This meta-analysis explored abnormalities in white matter connectivity in language networks of individuals with ASD. Significantly reduced white matter integrity was found in all language-associated tracts in subjects with ASD compared with TD controls. In addition, structural disturbances of language networks in the autistic brain exhibit a leftward tendency, and more prominent abnormalities are observed in younger people with ASD than in adults.

sheet.es: Esta investigación no cambia lo que hace mañana: describe diferencias en el cerebro, no ofrece una intervención. Si su hijo o hija autista se comunica de otra forma, eso puede tener una base biológica real, no es falta de esfuerzo. Respete todas las formas de comunicación (gestos, imágenes, dispositivos, palabras) y dé tiempo extra para procesar el lenguaje. Las diferencias fueron mayores en niños que en adultos, lo que sugiere que el cerebro sigue desarrollándose. Es un metaanálisis de 33 estudios de imagen cerebral con 831 personas autistas y 836 no autistas. Límites: muestra promedios de grupo, no predice cómo se comunicará una persona concreta y no mide la comunicación cotidiana.
sheet.en: This research doesn't change what you do tomorrow: it describes brain differences, not an intervention. If your autistic child communicates differently, that may have a real biological basis; it is not a lack of effort. Respect every form of communication (gestures, pictures, devices, speech) and allow extra time to process language. Differences were larger in children than in adults, suggesting the brain keeps developing over time. This is a meta-analysis of 33 brain imaging studies with 831 autistic and 836 non-autistic people. Limits: it shows group averages, cannot predict how any one person will communicate, and did not measure everyday communication.
sheet.sv: Den här forskningen ändrar inte vad du gör i morgon: den beskriver skillnader i hjärnan, inte en insats. Om ditt autistiska barn kommunicerar annorlunda kan det ha en verklig biologisk grund; det handlar inte om bristande ansträngning. Respektera alla sätt att kommunicera (gester, bilder, hjälpmedel, tal) och ge extra tid att bearbeta språk. Skillnaderna var större hos barn än hos vuxna, vilket tyder på att hjärnan fortsätter utvecklas. Det är en metaanalys av 33 hjärnavbildningsstudier med 831 autistiska och 836 icke-autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den visar gruppgenomsnitt, kan inte förutsäga hur en enskild person kommunicerar och mätte inte vardaglig kommunikation.

title: Virtual and Augmented Reality in Social Skills Interventions for Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Scoping Review.
authors: Dechsling A, Orm S, Kalandadze T, Sütterlin S, Øien RA, Shic F, Nordahl-Hansen A
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: In the last decade, there has been an increase in publications on technology-based interventions for autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Virtual reality based assessments and intervention tools are promising and have shown to be acceptable amongst individuals with ASD. This scoping review reports on 49 studies utilizing virtual reality and augmented reality technology in social skills interventions for individuals with ASD. The included studies mostly targeted children and adolescents, but few targeted very young children or adults. Our findings show that the mode number of participants with ASD is low, and that female participants are underrepresented. Our review suggests that there is need for studies that apply virtual and augmented realty with more rigorous designs involving established and evidenced-based intervention strategies.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija autista le atrae la tecnología, la realidad virtual o aumentada puede ser una forma aceptable y cómoda de practicar situaciones sociales, siempre que respete sus intereses y su ritmo, y no sustituya el apoyo de personas de confianza. Pregunta a profesionales en qué estrategia basada en evidencia se apoya cualquier programa antes de probarlo. Esta revisión de alcance reunió 49 estudios, sobre todo con niños, niñas y adolescentes; hubo pocos con niños muy pequeños o personas adultas. Sus límites: los estudios eran pequeños, participaron pocas chicas y mujeres, y los diseños eran poco rigurosos, así que aún no sabemos con certeza qué funciona ni para quién.
sheet.en: If your autistic child enjoys technology, virtual or augmented reality may be an acceptable, comfortable way to practise social situations, as long as it follows their interests and pace and doesn't replace support from trusted people. Before trying any programme, ask professionals which evidence-based strategy it builds on. This scoping review gathered 49 studies, mostly with children and teenagers; very few included very young children or adults. Its limits: most studies were small, girls and women were underrepresented, and designs were not very rigorous, so we don't yet know clearly what works, or for whom.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn tycker om teknik kan virtuell eller förstärkt verklighet vara ett godtagbart och bekvämt sätt att öva sociala situationer, så länge det utgår från barnets intressen och tempo och inte ersätter stöd från trygga personer. Fråga yrkespersoner vilken evidensbaserad metod ett program bygger på innan ni provar det. Denna kartläggande översikt samlade 49 studier, främst med barn och tonåringar; få gällde mycket små barn eller vuxna. Begränsningar: studierna var oftast små, flickor och kvinnor var underrepresenterade och upplägget var inte särskilt rigoröst, så vi vet ännu inte säkert vad som fungerar eller för vem.

title: Patterns in reporting and participant inclusion related to race and ethnicity in autism intervention literature: Data from a large-scale systematic review of evidence-based practices.
authors: Steinbrenner JR, McIntyre N, Rentschler LF, Pearson JN, Luelmo P, Jaramillo ME, Boyd BA, Wong C, Nowell SW, Odom SL, Hume KA
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Researchers who study autism-related interventions do a poor job reporting data related to the race and ethnicity of autistic individuals who participate in their studies, and of those who do report these data, the participants are overwhelmingly White. This is problematic for many reasons, as we know little about how interventions are meeting the needs of culturally and linguistically diverse populations, and we assume that interventions are effective for all when they have been developed and validated primarily with and for White children. This study examined the reporting patterns of autism intervention researchers whose work was included in a large-scale systematic review of the intervention literature published between 1990 and 2017. We found that only 25% of studies (out of 1,013 included in the review) included data related to the race and ethnicity of their participants, with minimal change in reporting patterns across the years. In studies with reported data, White participants had the highest rate of participation, with a large gap between the next highest rates of participation among Hispanic/Latino, Black, and Asian participants. Other race and ethnicity groups had very low representation. This study includes additional analyses which examine how the reporting patterns and the inclusion of racially and ethnically diverse participants varies across study types, interventions, and outcome areas. Reporting this data is merely a starting point to begin to address the many disparities in autism-related healthcare, education, and research practices, and this article includes broader implications and next steps to ensure the field becomes more equitable and inclusive.

sheet.es: Si su familia no es blanca o habla otro idioma en casa, es razonable preguntar a los profesionales si una intervención se ha probado con niños y familias como la suya, y pedir que se adapte a su cultura y lengua. Su conocimiento de su hijo y de su comunidad es información valiosa. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 1.013 estudios sobre intervenciones en autismo publicados entre 1990 y 2017: solo el 25 % informó la raza o etnia de los participantes, y la mayoría eran blancos. Limitación: muestra quién participó, no si las intervenciones funcionan peor en otros grupos, y los datos provienen sobre todo de un contexto estadounidense.
sheet.en: If your family is not White or speaks another language at home, it is reasonable to ask professionals whether an intervention has been tested with children and families like yours, and to request that it be adapted to your culture and language. Your knowledge of your child and your community is valuable information. This systematic review examined 1,013 autism intervention studies published between 1990 and 2017: only 25% reported participants' race or ethnicity, and most participants were White. Limitation: it shows who took part, not whether interventions work less well for other groups, and the data come largely from a US context.
sheet.sv: Om er familj inte är vit eller talar ett annat språk hemma är det rimligt att fråga yrkesverksamma om en insats har prövats med barn och familjer som er, och att be om att den anpassas till er kultur och ert språk. Din kunskap om ditt barn och er gemenskap är värdefull information. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 1 013 studier om insatser för autistiska personer, publicerade 1990–2017: bara 25 % redovisade deltagarnas etnicitet, och de flesta deltagarna var vita. Begränsning: den visar vilka som deltog, inte om insatserna fungerar sämre för andra grupper, och underlaget kommer främst från USA.

title: Loneliness in autistic adults: A systematic review.
authors: Grace K, Remington A, Lloyd-Evans B, Davies J, Crane L
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Recently, researchers have been interested in how autistic people experience loneliness. Yet, most of this research has focused on loneliness in autistic children and young people. We present the results of a systematic review on loneliness in autistic adults. A systematic review is a rigorous way of searching for all existing research on a topic and summarizing the findings about specific questions. We searched for all research published on this topic until 9 April 2021. We found 34 articles that investigated loneliness in autistic adults. This research showed that (1) there is fairly little research that has involved directly asking autistic adults about their first-hand experiences of loneliness (e.g. what loneliness feels like for them); (2) few research studies have used loneliness questionnaires specifically developed for autistic adults (this was attempted in just one research study); (3) collective loneliness (i.e. loneliness associated with how much an autistic person feels they 'fit in' to society) seems important to autistic adults but has not been investigated as commonly as other aspects of loneliness (e.g. loneliness associated with romantic relationships or friendships); (4) things that might increase loneliness in autistic adults include anxiety and depression, and a lack of autism understanding and acceptance, for example; and (5) things that might reduce loneliness in autistic adults include having relationships and self-acceptance, for example. In our article, we discuss the kinds of future research on loneliness in autistic adults that might be useful.

sheet.es: Pregunte a la persona autista adulta qué significa la soledad para ella, en lugar de suponerlo. Además de amistades o pareja, puede pesar sentirse fuera de lugar en la sociedad. Ayudan las relaciones elegidas, la autoaceptación y entornos que comprendan y acepten el autismo; la ansiedad, la depresión y la falta de comprensión pueden aumentarla. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 34 estudios sobre soledad en adultos autistas publicados hasta abril de 2021. Su límite: pocos estudios preguntaron directamente a adultos autistas por su experiencia y casi ninguno usó cuestionarios diseñados para ellos, así que los hallazgos son orientativos y no se aplican igual a todas las personas.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic adult in your life what loneliness means to them, rather than assuming. Beyond friendships or romance, feeling that you don't 'fit in' to society can matter a lot. Chosen relationships, self-acceptance and settings that understand and accept autism may help; anxiety, depression and lack of understanding may deepen loneliness. This systematic review brought together 34 studies on loneliness in autistic adults published up to April 2021. Its limit: few studies directly asked autistic adults about their own experience, and almost none used questionnaires designed for them, so the findings are a guide, not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska vuxna i ditt liv vad ensamhet betyder för just hen, i stället för att anta. Utöver vänskap eller kärlek kan känslan av att inte passa in i samhället väga tungt. Valda relationer, självacceptans och miljöer som förstår och accepterar autism kan hjälpa; ångest, depression och bristande förståelse kan öka ensamheten. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 34 studier om ensamhet hos autistiska vuxna publicerade fram till april 2021. Begränsning: få studier frågade autistiska vuxna direkt om deras egen upplevelse och nästan inga använde frågeformulär utformade för dem, så resultaten är vägledande och gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

title: 'It's being a part of a grand tradition, a grand counter-culture which involves communities': A qualitative investigation of autistic community connectedness.
authors: Botha M, Dibb B, Frost DM
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract A sense of being connected to other autistic people has been reported anecdotally. Friendships and connectedness may be important to autistic people and beneficial for their wellbeing. Our research aimed to understand the autistic community by interviewing 20 autistic people about their experiences of being connected to other autistic people. Participants were interviewed in person, over video, using a text-based software to type or over email. Participants detailed three parts of autistic community connectedness: a sense of belonging, social connection with autistic friends and political connectedness. The friendships autistic people had with one another were deemed to be very important to participants because it gave them confidence, provided companionship and made them happy. Some participants did not experience connectedness to the autistic community. These participants also found autism to be less important to their identity and had fewer positive feelings about being autistic. This research is important as it raises awareness that community connectedness is viewed as important to this group. It is possible that community connectedness may help protect the mental health of autistic people when they face stigma or negative life experiences in society.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista a la que acompañas lo desea, puede valer la pena ayudarle a encontrar a otras personas autistas: grupos locales, foros en línea, espacios dirigidos por autistas. Para muchas personas, estas amistades aportan pertenencia, compañía, confianza y alegría. Respeta su ritmo y su forma preferida de comunicarse; no todas las personas autistas sienten esta conexión, y eso también es válido. Este estudio cualitativo entrevistó a 20 personas autistas en persona, por vídeo, por texto o por correo electrónico. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño, describe experiencias y no demuestra que la comunidad mejore la salud mental de cada persona.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support wants it, it may be worth helping them find other autistic people: local groups, online forums, autistic-led spaces. For many, these friendships bring belonging, companionship, confidence and happiness. Follow their pace and preferred way of communicating; not every autistic person feels this connection, and that is valid too. This qualitative study interviewed 20 autistic people in person, over video, through typed text or by email. Its limits: the group is small, it describes experiences, and it does not prove that community connection improves mental health for every person.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar vill det kan det vara värt att hjälpa hen att hitta andra autistiska personer: lokala grupper, nätforum, autistledda sammanhang. För många ger sådana vänskaper tillhörighet, sällskap, självförtroende och glädje. Följ personens takt och föredragna sätt att kommunicera; alla autistiska personer känner inte denna gemenskap, och det är också helt okej. Denna kvalitativa studie intervjuade 20 autistiska personer på plats, via video, via skriven text eller e-post. Begränsningar: gruppen är liten, studien beskriver upplevelser och visar inte att gemenskap förbättrar den psykiska hälsan för varje person.

title: Exploring potential sources of childhood trauma: A qualitative study with autistic adults and caregivers.
authors: Kerns CM, Lankenau S, Shattuck PT, Robins DL, Newschaffer CJ, Berkowitz SJ
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract The stressors autistic individuals encounter and experience as traumatic may vary from those not on the spectrum and typically measured. We conducted in-depth interviews with autistic adults and caregivers of children and adults on the spectrum to identify potential sources of trauma for autistic individuals and evaluate the ability of a standard trauma measure to capture those experiences. Fourteen autistic adults and 15 caregivers with varied backgrounds, clinical profiles, and histories of adversity were interviewed. Participants also completed standard measures of autism, traumatic exposures, and stress. Interviews were analyzed to record both traditional sources of trauma, for comparison with the standard measure, and distinct sources, described as traumatic only in the narratives of participants. Participants described varied experiences as traumatic. Whereas some reflected traditional traumas (e.g. maltreatment) and forms of social marginalization, others reflected conflicts between autistic characteristics and the environment (e.g. sensory trauma). All adults and most caregivers described sources of trauma in interviews not reported on the standard measure. Results have implications for assessing traumatic events in autism and for understanding their contribution to the mental health of this group.

sheet.es: Algo que para otras personas parece pequeño (un ruido intenso, cambios bruscos, exclusión social o ser forzado a tolerar sensaciones) puede vivirse como traumático por una persona autista. Mañana, puedes preguntar con calma qué experiencias le resultaron difíciles, creer su relato aunque no encaje en las listas habituales y reducir las cargas sensoriales evitables. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 14 adultos autistas y 15 cuidadores; casi todos describieron fuentes de trauma que un cuestionario estándar no recogía. Límites: la muestra es pequeña, no mide causas ni frecuencias y cada persona vive estas experiencias de forma distinta.
sheet.en: Things that seem minor to others, such as intense noise, sudden changes, social exclusion or being made to endure certain sensations, can be experienced as traumatic by an autistic person. Tomorrow, you might calmly ask which experiences felt hard, believe their account even if it doesn't fit usual checklists, and reduce avoidable sensory strain. This qualitative study interviewed 14 autistic adults and 15 caregivers; nearly all described sources of trauma that a standard trauma questionnaire missed. Limits: the sample is small, it doesn't measure causes or how common these experiences are, and each person experiences them differently.
sheet.sv: Sådant som verkar litet för andra, till exempel starkt ljud, plötsliga förändringar, social utestängning eller att tvingas stå ut med vissa sinnesintryck, kan upplevas som traumatiskt av en autistisk person. I morgon kan du lugnt fråga vilka upplevelser som varit svåra, tro på berättelsen även om den inte passar vanliga checklistor och minska onödig sensorisk belastning. Studien är kvalitativ med intervjuer med 14 autistiska vuxna och 15 anhöriga; nästan alla beskrev traumakällor som ett standardformulär missade. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet, studien mäter inte orsaker eller hur vanligt det är, och varje person upplever detta olika.

title: Autistic adults' experiences of diagnostic disclosure in the workplace: Decision-making and factors associated with outcomes.
authors: Romualdez AM, Walker Z, Remington A
abstract: Autistic individuals often struggle to find and maintain employment. This may be because many workplaces are not suited to autistic individuals' needs. Among other difficulties, many autistic employees experience distracting or disruptive sensory environments, lack of flexibility in work hours, and unclear communication from colleagues. One possible way of mitigating these difficulties is for employees to disclose their diagnosis at work. While disclosure may increase understanding and acceptance from colleagues, it can also lead to discrimination and stigma in the workplace. Research has shown that disclosure outcomes are often mixed, but it is unclear what factors are associated with either positive or negative outcomes of disclosure for autistic people. This study aimed to identify these factors and explore the reasons why autistic employees choose to disclose or to keep their diagnosis private. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 24 clinically-diagnosed autistic adults (12 male and 12 female) who were currently, or had been, employed in the UK (mean age = 45.7 years). Through thematic analysis, we identified three main themes under experiences of disclosure: 1) A preference for keeping my diagnosis private; 2) The importance of disclosure in the workplace; and 3) Disclosure has mixed outcomes. We also identified three factors associated with disclosure outcomes: understanding of autism, adaptations, and organisational culture. These results have implications for improving inclusive practices on both the individual and organisational level to ensure more positive disclosure experiences for autistic employees.

sheet.es: Decidir si contar el diagnóstico en el trabajo es una elección personal, sin respuesta correcta única. Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, puedes ayudarle a valorar: ¿cuánto se entiende el autismo en ese lugar?, ¿hay disposición a hacer ajustes (ruido, horarios flexibles, instrucciones claras)?, ¿cómo es la cultura de la organización? Estos tres factores se asociaron con mejores o peores resultados. Respetar también la decisión de mantenerlo en privado. Evidencia: entrevistas con 24 adultos autistas diagnosticados (12 hombres, 12 mujeres, edad media 46 años) con empleo actual o pasado en Reino Unido. Límites: muestra pequeña y de un solo país; describe experiencias, no prueba qué estrategia funciona para cada persona.
sheet.en: Deciding whether to disclose a diagnosis at work is a personal choice with no single right answer. If you support an autistic adult, you can help them weigh: how well is autism understood in that workplace? Is there willingness to make adaptations (noise, flexible hours, clear instructions)? What is the organisational culture like? These three factors were linked to better or worse outcomes. Respect a decision to keep it private, too. Evidence: interviews with 24 clinically diagnosed autistic adults (12 men, 12 women, average age 46) currently or previously employed in the UK. Limits: a small, single-country sample; it describes experiences rather than proving which approach works for every person.
sheet.sv: Att berätta om sin diagnos på jobbet är ett personligt val utan ett enda rätt svar. Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan ni tillsammans fundera på: hur väl förstås autism på arbetsplatsen? Finns vilja att göra anpassningar (ljud, flexibla tider, tydliga instruktioner)? Hur ser organisationens kultur ut? Dessa tre faktorer hängde ihop med bättre eller sämre utfall. Respektera också beslutet att hålla diagnosen privat. Evidens: intervjuer med 24 kliniskt diagnostiserade autistiska vuxna (12 män, 12 kvinnor, medelålder 46 år) som arbetade eller hade arbetat i Storbritannien. Begränsningar: litet urval från ett land; studien beskriver erfarenheter och visar inte vilket sätt som fungerar för varje person.

title: Play-based interventions to support social and communication development in autistic children aged 2-8 years: A scoping review.
authors: Gibson JL, Pritchard E, de Lemos C
abstract: Background and aims Play is used by practitioners from across disciplinary backgrounds as a natural and enjoyable context for providing intervention and support in early childhood. In the case of autism interventions, many therapies are based on the association between social play and the development of social skills, language development, and communication skills, as these are often particular areas of challenge for autistic children. However, play is a wide-ranging concept and the extant literature on play-based interventions is large and heterogeneous. This means it is challenging for practitioners and families to navigate the evidence base and make choices about differing intervention strategies. This review aims to provide a comprehensive map of the research on this topic and to develop a conceptual framework to inform clinical decision-making. Methods An initial stakeholder consultation confirmed the relevance of the topic to practitioners and autistic people. A scoping review methodology (preregistered) was used to identify relevant literature. We systematically searched seven databases to find peer-reviewed primary intervention studies of play-based approaches targeting language, social and communication outcomes for autistic children aged 2-8 years. We then summarised the literature using narrative synthesis and Evidence Gap Maps (EGMs). The literature was summarised according to a range of characteristics, including study design, population characteristics, agent of intervention and outcomes measured, among others. These summaries were then used to develop a framework for some key considerations for practitioners appraising play-based approaches. Results 388 studies met inclusion criteria. Approximately 21% of studies were RCTs, and over 50% had ≤10 participants. Over 45% of studies reported multiple relevant outcomes, with social play skills being the most common single intervention target. Girls and minority background groups are under-represented. A range of intervention types were identified, and some high-level categorisations are proposed. Main contribution: On the basis of the evidence synthesis we suggest important dimensions for appraisal of play-based interventions, including the role of play within an intervention (as a context, a key developmental mechanism, or a component of a larger approach), the underpinning philosophy (e.g. behaviourist or developmental), and the role of the practitioner (providing parent feedback, 1:1 intervention, group facilitation). Conclusions The wide range of approaches uncovered by this review is a testament to the wonderful diversity inherent to both play and autism. However, research could usefully focus on consolidating the evidence base for existing approaches, rather than aiming for further diversification. Implications: The conceptual framework proposed in this review can help practitioners appraise the literature and aid their advice to families when making shared intervention decisions.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa basado en el juego para su hijo o hija, puede hacer tres preguntas sencillas: ¿el juego es solo el contexto o la herramienta principal?, ¿el enfoque es conductual o del desarrollo?, ¿quién lo aplica: usted con apoyo del profesional, una sesión individual o un grupo? Elija lo que respete cómo juega y disfruta su niño o niña. Esta revisión de alcance reunió 388 estudios sobre niños autistas de 2 a 8 años. Sus límites: solo un 21 % eran ensayos controlados, más de la mitad tenía diez participantes o menos, y las niñas y las minorías estaban poco representadas.
sheet.en: If you are offered a play-based programme for your child, you can ask three simple questions: is play just the setting or the main tool? Is the approach behavioural or developmental? Who delivers it: you with coaching from a practitioner, one-to-one sessions, or a group? Choose what respects how your child already plays and enjoys themselves. This scoping review mapped 388 studies of play-based approaches for autistic children aged 2–8. Its limits: only about 21% were randomised trials, over half had ten or fewer participants, and girls and minority groups were under-represented.
sheet.sv: Om ni erbjuds ett lekbaserat stöd för ert barn kan ni ställa tre enkla frågor: Är leken bara sammanhanget eller själva verktyget? Bygger metoden på beteendeteori eller utvecklingsteori? Vem genomför den: ni själva med handledning, en behandlare enskilt eller i grupp? Välj det som respekterar hur ert barn redan leker och har roligt. Denna kartläggande översikt samlade 388 studier om lekbaserade insatser för autistiska barn mellan 2 och 8 år. Begränsningar: bara cirka 21 % var randomiserade studier, över hälften hade tio deltagare eller färre, och flickor samt minoritetsgrupper var underrepresenterade.

title: "Autism research is in crisis": A mixed method study of researcher's constructions of autistic people and autism research.
authors: Botha M, Cage E
abstract: Introduction While not all autism research is ableism, autism researchers can be ableist, including by talking about autistic people in sub-human terms (dehumanization), treating autistic people like objects (objectification), and making othering statements which set autistic people apart from non-autistic people, and below in status (stigmatization). Method This mixed-method study aimed to investigate how autism researchers construct autistic people and autism research, and to investigate whether including autistic people more in research relates to lower ableism in narratives about autistic people. We used a survey with autism researchers ( N = 195) asking five open-ended questions about autism and autism research, as well as demographics, career length, contact with autistic people (familial and non-familial) and degree to which researchers involve autistic people in their research. We used content analysis to categorize narratives used by autism researchers and cues for ableism (dehumanization, objectification, and stigmatization). We then used binary-logistic regression to identify whether narrative or higher inclusion of autistic people predicted fewer ableist cues, controlling for career length and connections to autistic people. Results and discussion Using medicalized narratives of autism predicted higher odds of ableist cues compared to employing social model or neutral embodiment narratives. Greater inclusion of autistic people in research predicted significantly lower odds of ableist cues, while controlling for other contact with autistic people and career length. Next, we used reflexive thematic analysis to analyze researcher's perceptions of autistic people and autism research. Narratives reflected core ideological disagreements of the field, such as whether researchers consider autism to be an intrinsic barrier to a good life, and whether researchers prioritize research which tackles "autism" versus barriers to societal inclusion for autistic people. Instrumentality (a form of objectification) was key to whether researchers considered a person to have social value with emphasis revolving around intellectual ability and independence. Lastly, language seemed to act as a tool of normalization of violence. Researchers relied on an amorphous idea of "autism" when talking about prevention or eradication, potentially because it sounds more palatable than talking about preventing "autistic people," despite autism only existing within the context of autistic people.

sheet.es: Al leer sobre autismo o elegir servicios y estudios, puede ayudar fijarse en el lenguaje: ¿habla de la persona autista con respeto, o solo de «déficits» y «curar el autismo»? Merece la pena preguntar si los investigadores o profesionales incluyen a personas autistas en sus decisiones; ese tipo de inclusión se asoció con un lenguaje menos capacitista. Se trata de una encuesta con preguntas abiertas a 195 investigadores en autismo, analizada con métodos cualitativos y estadísticos. Sus límites: refleja lo que escribieron los investigadores que quisieron participar, muestra asociaciones y no causas, y no mide directamente cómo afecta esto a las familias.
sheet.en: When reading about autism or choosing services and studies, it can help to notice the language: does it speak about autistic people with respect, or only about "deficits" and "curing autism"? It is worth asking whether researchers or professionals involve autistic people in their decisions; that kind of inclusion was linked to less ableist language. This was a survey with open-ended questions answered by 195 autism researchers, analysed with qualitative and statistical methods. Its limits: it reflects what volunteering researchers wrote, it shows associations rather than causes, and it does not directly measure effects on families.
sheet.sv: När du läser om autism eller väljer insatser och studier kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till språket: talar det om autistiska personer med respekt, eller bara om "brister" och att "bota autism"? Det är värt att fråga om forskare eller yrkespersoner involverar autistiska personer i sina beslut; sådan delaktighet hängde ihop med mindre funkofobiskt språk. Studien var en enkät med öppna frågor till 195 autismforskare, analyserad med kvalitativa och statistiska metoder. Begränsningar: den speglar vad forskare som valde att delta skrev, visar samband snarare än orsaker och mäter inte direkt hur detta påverkar familjer.

title: Mental health and social difficulties of late-diagnosed autistic children, across childhood and adolescence.
authors: Mandy W, Midouhas E, Hosozawa M, Cable N, Sacker A, Flouri E
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background Autism can be diagnosed from 2 years of age, although most autistic people receive their diagnosis later than this after they have started education. Research is required to understand why some autistic children are diagnosed late, and the level and nature of unmet need prior to diagnosis for late-diagnosed children. Methods We examined trajectories of emotional, behavioural and social difficulties (EBSDs) across childhood and adolescence, comparing 'earlier-diagnosed' (diagnosed 7 years or younger) with 'late-diagnosed' (diagnosed between 8 and 14 years) autistic children. Data were from the Millennium Cohort Study, a population-based UK birth cohort. EBSDs were measured using the parent-report Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, at 3, 5, 7, 11 and 14 years. We used Growth Curve Modelling to investigate levels and rates of change in these difficulties, and to compare earlier- (n = 146) and late-diagnosed (n = 284) autistic children. Results Aged 5, earlier-diagnosed autistic children had more emotional (i.e., internalising), conduct, hyperactivity and social difficulties; although clinical difficulties in these areas were nevertheless common in late-diagnosed children. There was a faster annual increase in scores for all domains for late-diagnosed children, and by age 14 years, they had higher levels of EBSDs. These results persisted when we ran adjusted models, to account for the late-diagnosed group having higher rates of late-diagnosed attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder, higher IQ, a higher proportion of females and older and more educated mothers. Conclusions Emotional, behavioural and social difficulties are associated with, and may influence, the timing of autism diagnosis. Late-diagnosed autistic children often have high levels of mental health and social difficulties prior to their autism diagnosis, and tend to develop even more severe problems as they enter adolescence.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija recibió el diagnóstico de autismo tarde, o aún no lo tiene, presta atención temprana a señales de ansiedad, tristeza o dificultades con amistades, sobre todo al acercarse la adolescencia. No hace falta esperar al diagnóstico para pedir apoyo en la escuela o en salud mental, ni para ajustar rutinas y expectativas en casa. Este estudio siguió a 430 niños y niñas autistas de una gran cohorte británica, con cuestionarios de las familias entre los 3 y los 14 años; quienes fueron diagnosticados tarde mostraron dificultades crecientes. Límites: solo informaron los padres y no se escuchó a los propios jóvenes, y no se aplica igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your child was diagnosed autistic later, or has no diagnosis yet, notice early signs of anxiety, low mood or friendship difficulties, especially as adolescence approaches. You do not need to wait for a diagnosis to ask for support at school or from mental health services, or to adjust routines and expectations at home. This study followed 430 autistic children from a large UK birth cohort, using parent questionnaires from age 3 to 14; those diagnosed later showed difficulties that grew faster over time. Limits: only parents reported, the young people themselves were not asked, and the pattern will not fit every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn fick sin autismdiagnos sent, eller ännu inte har någon, var uppmärksam tidigt på tecken på oro, nedstämdhet eller svårigheter med kompisar, särskilt inför tonåren. Du behöver inte vänta på en diagnos för att be om stöd i skolan eller från psykiatrin, eller för att anpassa rutiner och förväntningar hemma. Studien följde 430 autistiska barn i en stor brittisk födelsekohort, med föräldraenkäter från 3 till 14 års ålder; de som fick diagnos sent fick svårigheter som ökade snabbare. Begränsningar: bara föräldrar svarade, ungdomarna själva tillfrågades inte, och mönstret gäller inte alla barn.

title: Reexamining empathy in autism: Empathic disequilibrium as a novel predictor of autism diagnosis and autistic traits.
authors: Shalev I, Warrier V, Greenberg DM, Smith P, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S, Eran A, Uzefovsky F
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: A large body of research showed that autistic people have intact emotional (affective) empathy alongside reduced cognitive empathy. However, there are mixed findings and these call for a more subtle understanding of empathy in autism. Empathic disequilibrium refers to the imbalance between emotional and cognitive empathy and is associated with a higher number of autistic traits in the typical population. Here we examined whether empathic disequilibrium predicts both the number of autistic traits and autism diagnosis. In a large sample of autistic (N = 1905) and typical individuals (N = 3009), we examined empathic disequilibrium and empathy as predictors of autistic traits and autism diagnosis, using a polynomial regression with response surface analysis. Empathy and autistic traits were measured using validated self-report questionnaires. Both empathic disequilibrium and empathy predicted linearly and non-linearly autism diagnosis and autistic traits. Specifically, a tendency towards higher emotional than cognitive empathy (empathic disequilibrium towards emotional empathy) predicted both autism diagnosis and the social domain of autistic traits, while higher cognitive than emotional empathy was associated with the non-social domain of autism. Empathic disequilibrium was also more prominent in autistic females. This study provides evidence that beyond empathy as was measured thus far, empathic disequilibrium offers a novel analytical approach for examining the role of empathy. Empathic disequilibrium allows for a more nuanced understanding of the links between empathy and autism. LAY SUMMARY: Many autistic individuals report feelings of excessive empathy, yet their experience is not reflected by most of the current literature, typically suggesting that autism is characterized by intact emotional and reduced cognitive empathy. To fill this gap, we looked at both ends of the imbalance between these components, termed empathic disequilibrium. We show that, like empathy, empathic disequilibrium is related to autism diagnosis and traits, and thus may provide a more nuanced understanding of empathy and its link with autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a su cargo parece afectarse mucho por las emociones de otros pero le cuesta saber qué piensan, puede que no le falte empatía: quizá siente demasiado. Mañana, valide esa intensidad, ofrezca pausas tras situaciones emocionales y ayude a nombrar lo que pasa sin exigir que «lea» a los demás. Evidencia: estudio con cuestionarios de autoinforme en 1905 personas autistas y 3009 no autistas; un desequilibrio hacia más empatía emocional que cognitiva se asoció con el diagnóstico, y fue más marcado en mujeres autistas. Límites: solo autoinforme, diseño transversal; no describe a cada persona ni sirve para diagnosticar.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support seems deeply affected by others' feelings yet finds it hard to work out what they think, it may not be a lack of empathy: they may feel too much. Tomorrow, validate that intensity, offer breaks after emotional moments, and help name what is happening without demanding they 'read' people. Evidence: a self-report questionnaire study of 1,905 autistic and 3,009 non-autistic adults; an imbalance toward more emotional than cognitive empathy was linked to autism, especially in autistic women. Limits: self-report only, one point in time; it does not describe every person and cannot be used to diagnose.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar verkar starkt påverkad av andras känslor men har svårt att förstå vad de tänker, kanske det inte handlar om brist på empati: hen kanske känner för mycket. I morgon kan du bekräfta den intensiteten, erbjuda pauser efter känslomässiga situationer och hjälpa till att sätta ord på vad som händer, utan krav på att ”läsa av” andra. Evidens: en enkätstudie med självskattning hos 1 905 autistiska och 3 009 icke-autistiska personer; obalans mot mer emotionell än kognitiv empati kopplades till autism, tydligast hos autistiska kvinnor. Begränsningar: endast självskattning vid ett tillfälle; gäller inte alla och kan inte användas för diagnos.

title: Exclusion of females in autism research: Empirical evidence for a "leaky" recruitment-to-research pipeline.
authors: D'Mello AM, Frosch IR, Li CE, Cardinaux AL, Gabrieli JDE
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by challenges in social communication and the presence of repetitive behaviors or restricted interests. Notably, males are four times as likely as females to be diagnosed with autism. Despite efforts to increase representation and characterization of autistic females, research studies consistently enroll small samples of females, or exclude females altogether. Importantly, researchers often rely on standardized measures to confirm diagnosis prior to enrollment in research studies. We retrospectively analyzed the effects of one such measure (Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, ADOS) on research inclusion/exclusion rates by sex in autistic adults, all of whom had a preexisting community diagnosis of autism (n = 145, 95 male, 50 female). Using the ADOS as a confirmatory diagnostic measure resulted in the exclusion of autistic females at a rate over 2.5 times higher than that of autistic males. We compared sex ratios in our sample to those in other large, publically available datasets that rely either on community diagnosis (6 datasets, total n = 42,209) or standardized assessments (2 datasets, total n = 214) to determine eligibility of participants for research. Reliance on community diagnosis rather than confirmatory diagnostic assessments resulted in significantly more equal sex ratios. These results provide evidence for a "leaky" recruitment-to-research pipeline for females in autism research. LAY SUMMARY: Despite efforts to increase the representation of autistic females in research, studies consistently enroll small samples of females or exclude females altogether. We find that despite making up almost 50% of the initially recruited sample based upon self-report of community diagnosis, autistic females are disproportonately excluded from research participation as a result of commonly used autism diagnostic measures. In our sample, and several other publically available datasets, reliance on community diagnosis resulted in significantly more equal sex ratios.

sheet.es: Si tú o la persona que acompañas sois mujeres o chicas autistas y un estudio o una evaluación no «confirma» el autismo, eso no invalida su experiencia ni su diagnóstico. Las herramientas estándar pueden pasar por alto cómo se manifiesta el autismo en muchas mujeres. Al participar en investigaciones, conviene preguntar qué pruebas usan y llevar informes previos. Evidencia: estudio retrospectivo con 145 adultos autistas ya diagnosticados (50 mujeres); la prueba ADOS excluyó a las mujeres 2,5 veces más que a los hombres, y se comparó con bases de datos de más de 42.000 personas. Límites: una sola muestra pequeña y analizada a posteriori; no estudia otras identidades de género ni cada caso individual.
sheet.en: If you or the person you support is an autistic woman or girl and a study or assessment does not "confirm" autism, that does not cancel her experience or her existing diagnosis. Standard tools can miss how autism shows up in many women. When joining research, it helps to ask which measures are used and to bring earlier reports. Evidence: a retrospective study of 145 autistic adults with community diagnoses (50 women); the ADOS excluded women over 2.5 times more often than men, compared with datasets of over 42,000 people. Limits: one small sample analysed after the fact; it does not cover other gender identities or every individual.
sheet.sv: Om du eller personen du stöttar är en autistisk kvinna eller flicka och en studie eller bedömning inte "bekräftar" autism, betyder det inte att hennes erfarenhet eller tidigare diagnos är fel. Standardiserade verktyg kan missa hur autism visar sig hos många kvinnor. Vid deltagande i forskning kan det hjälpa att fråga vilka mått som används och ta med tidigare utlåtanden. Evidens: en retrospektiv studie av 145 autistiska vuxna med befintlig diagnos (50 kvinnor); ADOS uteslöt kvinnor över 2,5 gånger oftare än män, jämfört med dataset med över 42 000 personer. Begränsningar: ett litet urval analyserat i efterhand; andra könsidentiteter och enskilda fall belyses inte.

title: Social support and links to quality of life among middle-aged and older autistic adults.
authors: Charlton RA, McQuaid GA, Wallace GL
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Social support can take many forms, such as practical help, time spent socially with others, or the satisfaction with personal relationships. Social support is known to affect quality of life (QoL) in both non-autistic older and autistic young adults. QoL reflects how satisfied an individual is with their life either overall or in a certain area. We know little about middle-aged and older autistic adults' experiences of social support or QoL. In this study, 388 adults aged 40-83 years old, completed online questionnaires asking about background such as age and sex, depression and anxiety symptoms, QoL (physical, psychological, social, environmental, and autism-specific), and different types of social support. Even after taking into account background, depression, and anxiety, social support was important for individuals' QoL. To our knowledge this is the first paper to examine the relationship between social support and QoL in middle-aged and older autistic adults. Improving social support may have a significant impact on the QoL of older autistic adults. Future studies should examine whether age-related changes in social support (size, content, and arrangement of social networks) that are common in non-autistic aging, also occur among older autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista de mediana edad o mayor, vale la pena preguntarle qué tipo de apoyo le sirve: ayuda práctica, tiempo compartido a su ritmo o relaciones de confianza. No se trata de más contacto social, sino del que ella valora. Pequeños gestos regulares, como ayudar con un trámite o un encuentro tranquilo, pueden sumar a su calidad de vida. En este estudio, 388 adultos autistas de 40 a 83 años respondieron cuestionarios en línea; el apoyo social se relacionó con mejor calidad de vida incluso considerando ansiedad y depresión. Límites: es una foto en un momento dado, no prueba causa y efecto, y la muestra en línea no representa a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in midlife or later, it is worth asking which kinds of support actually help them: practical help, time together on their terms, or trusted relationships. The goal is not more socialising, but the kind they value. Small, regular gestures, like help with paperwork or a calm visit, may add to their quality of life. In this study, 388 autistic adults aged 40 to 83 completed online questionnaires; social support was linked to better quality of life even after accounting for anxiety and depression. Limits: it is a single snapshot, cannot show cause and effect, and an online sample does not represent every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i medelåldern eller äldre kan det vara värt att fråga vilket stöd som faktiskt hjälper: praktisk hjälp, tid tillsammans på personens villkor eller nära relationer. Målet är inte mer umgänge, utan den sortens kontakt personen själv värdesätter. Små, regelbundna insatser, som hjälp med pappersarbete eller ett lugnt besök, kan bidra till livskvaliteten. I studien besvarade 388 autistiska vuxna mellan 40 och 83 år enkäter på nätet; socialt stöd hängde ihop med bättre livskvalitet även när ångest och depression räknats in. Begränsningar: det är en ögonblicksbild som inte visar orsak och verkan, och ett nätbaserat urval representerar inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Benefits and harms of interventions to improve anxiety, depression, and other mental health outcomes for autistic people: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
authors: Linden A, Best L, Elise F, Roberts D, Branagan A, Tay YBE, Crane L, Cusack J, Davidson B, Davidson I, Hearst C, Mandy W, Rai D, Smith E, Gurusamy K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Nearly three out of four autistic people experience mental health problems such as stress, anxiety or depression. The research already done does not guide us on how best to prevent or treat mental health problems for autistic people. Our aim was to look at the benefits and harms of different interventions on mental health outcomes in autistic people. We searched all the published randomised controlled trials (RCTs) about interventions for mental health conditions in autistic people until 17 October 2020. We also searched for RCTs that were not published in peer-reviewed journals. These were obtained from registers of clinical trials online. We then combined the information from all these trials using advanced statistical methods to analyse how good the interventions are. Seventy-one studies (3630 participants) provided information for this research. The studies reported how participants were responding to the intervention for only a short period of time. The trials did not report which interventions worked for people with intellectual disability. In people without intellectual disability, some forms of cognitive behavioural therapy and mindfulness therapy may be helpful. However, further research is necessary. Many trials used medications to target core features of autism rather than targeting mental health conditions, but these medications did not help autistic people. Until we have more evidence, treatment of mental health conditions in autistic people should follow the evidence available for non-autistic people. We plan to widely disseminate the findings to healthcare professionals through medical journals and conferences and contact other groups representing autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo vive con ansiedad, estrés o tristeza persistente, vale la pena preguntar a su equipo de salud por terapias adaptadas, como la terapia cognitivo-conductual o el mindfulness, que pueden ayudar a algunas personas autistas sin discapacidad intelectual. Mientras haya poca evidencia específica, los profesionales pueden apoyarse en lo que funciona para la población general, ajustándolo a cada persona. Es un metaanálisis de 71 ensayos aleatorizados con 3630 personas autistas. Sus límites: los estudios siguieron a los participantes poco tiempo y no aportan datos sobre qué funciona para personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support lives with anxiety, stress or ongoing low mood, it is worth asking their health team about adapted therapies, such as cognitive behavioural therapy or mindfulness, which may help some autistic people without intellectual disability. While autism-specific evidence is limited, professionals can draw on what works for the general population, adjusted to the individual. This is a meta-analysis of 71 randomised trials including 3,630 autistic people. Its limits: participants were followed only for a short time, and the trials give no information on what works for autistic people with intellectual disability.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar lever med ångest, stress eller långvarig nedstämdhet kan det vara värt att fråga vården om anpassade terapier, till exempel kognitiv beteendeterapi eller mindfulness, som kan hjälpa en del autistiska personer utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Så länge autismspecifik kunskap är begränsad kan vården utgå från det som fungerar för befolkningen i stort, anpassat efter personen. Detta är en metaanalys av 71 randomiserade studier med 3 630 autistiska deltagare. Begränsningar: deltagarna följdes bara under kort tid, och studierna säger inget om vad som fungerar för autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Autistic Adults: a Scoping Review.
authors: Scheeren AM, Crane L, Heyworth M, Pellicano E
abstract: Purpose of review The COVID-19 pandemic and its associated restrictions have had a significant impact on people's everyday lives, including the lives of Autistic adults. We aimed to (a) synthesise all papers currently published on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on autistic adults and (b) identify lessons for the care and support of Autistic adults in pandemic and post-pandemic times. Recent findings Fifty-five papers met the inclusion criteria. Most studies focused on the pandemic's impact on the wellbeing of Autistic adults. Several studies focused on the use of (telehealth) services or the risk of COVID-19 infection/hospitalisation. Summary Autistic adults were significantly impacted by the pandemic, both directly as indicated by higher COVID-19 infection and hospitalisation rates, but also indirectly due to severe service disruptions and social restrictions. Even though there were large differences observed both between as well as within individuals in terms of the negative/positive effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, most studies reported a negative effect on Autistic adults' mental health. We draw several lessons from this review for the future care and support of Autistic adults, all of which must be underpinned by participatory research methods, that is, where Autistic community members are actively involved in setting research questions, testing the acceptability of the methods and interpreting and disseminating the results. Supplementary information The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40474-023-00268-6.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, conviene tener un plan para cuando se interrumpan rutinas o servicios: saber qué apoyos pueden seguir a distancia, mantener contacto regular y preguntarle qué cambios le resultan más difíciles o, a veces, más llevaderos. Durante la pandemia, muchas personas autistas adultas vieron afectada su salud mental, aunque las experiencias variaron mucho. Esta revisión de alcance reunió 55 estudios sobre adultos autistas, con mayor riesgo de infección y hospitalización y fuertes cortes en servicios. Sus límites: los estudios eran muy distintos entre sí y las autoras piden más investigación con participación activa de la comunidad autista.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it helps to plan ahead for times when routines or services are disrupted: know which supports can continue remotely, keep regular contact, and ask which changes feel hardest, or sometimes easier. During the pandemic, many autistic adults experienced a toll on their mental health, though experiences varied widely. This scoping review brought together 55 studies on autistic adults, also finding higher infection and hospitalisation rates and severe service disruptions. Its limits: the studies differed a lot in methods, and the authors call for more research where autistic community members are actively involved.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att planera för tider när rutiner eller stöd avbryts: ta reda på vilket stöd som kan fortsätta på distans, håll regelbunden kontakt och fråga vilka förändringar som känns svårast, eller ibland lättare. Under pandemin påverkades den psykiska hälsan negativt för många autistiska vuxna, men upplevelserna skilde sig mycket åt. Denna översikt samlade 55 studier om autistiska vuxna och fann även högre risk för smitta och sjukhusvård samt stora avbrott i stödinsatser. Begränsningar: studierna var mycket olika, och författarna efterlyser mer forskning där autistiska personer deltar aktivt.

title: Sex differences in predictors and outcomes of camouflaging: Comparing diagnosed autistic, high autistic trait and low autistic trait young adults.
authors: Milner V, Mandy W, Happé F, Colvert E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Many autistic people use strategies that help them adapt in social situations and hide behaviours that may seem different to non-autistic individuals - this is called camouflaging.
